place_lore.nirncraft.abahs_landing.hook: A salt-white harbour town on the Hew's Bane coast, ringed by net-lofts and watched by a lighthouse whose lamp has been seen to drift on foggy nights.
place_lore.nirncraft.abahs_landing.landi:
^NOTICE TO ALL MASTERS AND MATES
^All vessels are to moor at the Landing quay or the harbour mole only. No vessel is to moor to any light, pier, cask or float that is not on the harbour chart. Vessels that do so are not the harbour's responsibility, nor, in all honesty, its friend.

^The Net-Loft Guild reminds masters that old Karim knows the sound of every mooring in the bay and will gladly tell you if yours is wrong. He will not tell you twice. He is, after all, a very old man, and the fog is in no hurry.
place_lore.nirncraft.abahs_landing.rumou: At the Landing they say a pier moves in the fog, and that the harbour has two kinds of captain: those who have tied up to it, and those who are lying about it.

place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_lodge.hel:
Sigvar,
I came up from Raven Rock with your winter boots and found the door open and the fire cold. I am leaving the boots by the hearth. I am leaving this letter on the table, where you will see it when you come home. I will come back every Loredas until you do. Do not make me come every Loredas forever. Your Helga.

A second sheet beneath the first, the ink fresher: Fourth Loredas. The boots are gone from the hearth. The door was shut from outside. There were wolf tracks all round the lodge, and one set of a man's bare feet, going toward Frostmoon Crag. Sigvar, if that was you, why did you not knock?
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_lodge.hoo: A hunting lodge below Hvitkald Peak, its door hanging open and its larder untouched. The hunter who lived here walked out one full moon and did not come back as himself.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_lodge.rum: The Abandoned Lodge belonged to a hunter called Sigvar. Good shot, bad temper. Went out under the full moon chasing a white wolf toward Frostmoon Crag and never came home. His wife's still waiting in Raven Rock.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_lodge.sig:
#12th of Frostfall
A white wolf took the doe off my line again, right under my nose, and looked back at me as it went. Not like a wolf looks. Like a man looks when he's won at dice.

#14th of Frostfall
Followed its tracks to Frostmoon Crag. More tracks there than I could count. Some wolf, some man, some that start as one and end as the other. Went home and drank. Have not told Helga.

#15th of Frostfall
Full moon tonight. I am going back. My ring from Helga is on the thong around my neck, where it always is. If I do not come home, she should have it back. I keep thinking about the white wolf's eyes. They looked like they knew me.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_prison.ho: A gutted stone prison tower on the hills west of Fort Amol, abandoned since a fever swept its cells, though lamps still burn behind the bars on certain nights.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_prison.ru: The Abandoned Prison's not as abandoned as you'd think. Lamps in the cells, and the Lost Knife boys carry crates up there and come back without them.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_prison.sk: Folio #25 (1202, 124): Field inspection recorded for Abandoned Prison within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #25 for abandoned_prison: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Abandoned Prison are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_prison.sm: Up from Lost Knife Hideout this month: 6 crates of Fort Amol grain (the garrison will never count), 2 casks of Brandy-Mug cider, 1 crate of Imperial arrows bought off the camp quartermaster, no questions asked.
Kept here because no Stormcloak will set foot in a fever-house, and no Imperial knows it's here. The old lamps make a fine excuse. Folk think it's ghosts. Let them.
Reminder: stop the new boys whispering to the warden's bones. It is bad for discipline.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_prison.wa:
#4E 188, Sun's Dusk
To the Jarl of Windhelm. Fever in cells four through nine. The healer from Fort Amol will not come. The prisoners beg for water and I have none to spare that is clean.

#Later
I have opened the cells. Let the Jarl hang me for it. Better they run and die in the snow than die in here like rats in a barrel. Some of them thanked me. Most of them only ran.

#Later still
I am staying. Someone has to keep the lamps lit, in case any of them come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_shack.fre:
This shack is spoken for.
The rope is new. The candles are new. The lock on the door was oiled two days ago. None of this concerns you.

If you are a traveller sheltering from the fog, rest, and go in the morning, and forget the way here. If you are curious, be less curious. Curious people in Hjaalmarch have a way of being found in the reeds.
There is no signature on this note. There never is.
Do not move the candles. Do not take the rope. Do not, under any circumstances, lie down on the floor by the hearth and wait to see who comes. Someone always comes.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_shack.hoo: A rotting shack in the marsh west of Ustengrav, its roof sagging and its windows boarded. A marsh witch lived here once. Someone has swept the floor since.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_shack.rum: That old shack in the marsh? A witch lived there when I was a girl. She sold love charms and cures for warts, and folk said she buried her husbands under the floorboards. Somebody's been fixing the door lately. Not a witch, I hope.
place_lore.nirncraft.abandoned_shack.wit:
For warts: rub with a split nightshade and bury it where three paths meet. 1 septim.
For a cough: deathbell steeped in mead. No. Deathbell in nothing. Stop selling the deathbell cure, Aud. 2 septims, and an apology to the widow Ragna.

For love: a lock of hair, a drop of blood, a jar of mudcrab chitin and a full moon. 10 septims. Has never worked. They keep coming back for it.
For a husband who will not leave: a strong rope, a calm hand. Price to be discussed in person, and only in the dark.

place_lore.nirncraft.adasooms_gate.gate_:
#BY ORDER OF THE GATE
No one passes. No one is expected. No one has been sent. If a messenger is seen, he is to be asked politely for his name, and then, politely, to turn around.
A later soldier has pencilled: 'We have been here eleven hundred years. I am not sure who is expecting us to still be here. I am not sure who has stopped. We are very good at it.'
place_lore.nirncraft.adasooms_gate.hook: A great iron gate in a mountain pass of Kamal, held by a garrison of Ka Po' Tun veterans who have forgotten which side they were guarding.
place_lore.nirncraft.adasooms_gate.rumou: Adasoom's Gate has never been breached. It has also never been opened, which a keen scholar will tell you is the same thing.

place_lore.nirncraft.aetherian_archive.h: A giant sealed library sphere half out of the sand, its surface covered in turning glyph-rings.
place_lore.nirncraft.aetherian_archive.r: The great sphere's rings turn at dusk, always to the same heading. Scholars come to watch and write nothing down.
place_lore.nirncraft.aetherian_archive.w: Panel the First: the climbers. Panel the Last: a stair to nowhere, and a figure who steps off it. The panels foretell the stair, not the fall. Whoever stands where the last panel stands will choose whether the stair is an ending or a door. The roll does not know.

place_lore.nirncraft.ahaleb_necropolis.h: A mid-size necropolis with a long bridge hall over a pit, a hidden oasis chamber of palms under skylights and a final stair of golden doors.
place_lore.nirncraft.ahaleb_necropolis.r: Ahaleb has a garden underneath that glows green at noon, if you stand on the right dune.
place_lore.nirncraft.ahaleb_necropolis.w: I do not remember coming. I remember a contract, a palm, and a glass of water. I tend. The dead are warm. The bloom is gold and very beautiful, and when I touch it I feel my name loosening. I think this is how the gardens keep their gardeners. I must remember my name. Hadiya. Hadiya. Hadiya.

place_lore.nirncraft.alchemists_shack.al: Vampire dust, acquired at great expense from a hunter who would not say where he found it, though his boots were thick with the red clay of Haemar's Shame. Combined with mountain flower and nightshade it produces a tonic of truly remarkable effect upon the endurance.

Third trial on myself. Sleep no longer necessary. Daylight uncomfortable. Garlic intolerable. I note these as side effects and not as symptoms, because symptoms would imply an illness, and I am perfectly well. I am only very, very thirsty, and nothing in the shack seems to help.
place_lore.nirncraft.alchemists_shack.ho: A tumbledown shack on the eastern edge of Falkreath Hold where an alchemist once worked in peace. The cauldron is cold, the door hangs loose, and the ingredients have been arranged with unsettling care.
place_lore.nirncraft.alchemists_shack.ru: The alchemist out on the Rift border had the best frost salts in the south. Then he got interested in vampire dust, and you know how that ends.
place_lore.nirncraft.alchemists_shack.sk: Folio #3 (819, 1217): Field inspection recorded for Alchemists Shack within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #3 for alchemists_shack: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Alchemists Shack are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.alchemists_shack.un:
To Elgrim in Riften,
Cancel the garlic. Cancel the holy water. Increase the order of salts by half and add six bottles of the darkest wine you have. Payment on delivery. Deliver after dusk, please. Not before. I am unwell in the mornings. Do not knock. Simply leave the crate at the door and walk away without looking back. Thank you, old friend.

P.S. Elgrim, if you are curious, I have found a better use for the vampire dust than I first imagined. Come and see. Come at night. Bring Hafjorg; I have missed her. I have missed everyone, lately. It is lonely out here, and I am so very hungry for company.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_sotha.hook: A huge ancient Velothi shrine fortress with dusky green stone, great doors and a sunken lower temple of a long-silent god.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_sotha.rumour: Ald Sotha's lower rooms flood and drain on a schedule. Some say a clerk's bell rings down there.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_sotha.web.p0: HERE THE WAITING ARE KEPT. Whoever comes in faith shall be remembered, whoever comes in doubt shall be counted. Take a token, leave a token. The quiet house does not close.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_velothi.hook: A harbour village of one temple and many boat-houses along a bay where the water goes grey from fallen ash.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_velothi.rumour: Ald Velothi hasn't put a boat out at night in months. They say the dreamers wade into the bay and stand there till dawn.
place_lore.nirncraft.ald_velothi.web.p0: Watch rotates to the bay at dusk. DO NOT wake a standing sleeper. If one reaches the temple wall, tie a ribbon to the wrist; in the morning, count the ribbons. Last night: nineteen. We carried three back. Two of the three still ask which way is the mountain.

place_lore.nirncraft.aldhaven_harbor.hoo: A small harbour on the Iliac Bay's shore with a heavy chain across the mouth and a tidal slip for night barges.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldhaven_harbor.rum: A barge with no cargo but dust slips out of Aldhaven every ninth night and comes back lighter.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldhaven_harbor.web: Ninth night. Manifest: stone dust, chisels, one priest. Departed the chain at the ninth bell. Returned the third. No priest. No dust. Fresh-cut chips on the deck. I was paid to open the chain and asked to forget. I have not forgotten. The priest wore a Wayrest-sealed ring.

place_lore.nirncraft.aldruhn.gazetteer.p:
#The Council and the town
Councilor Brara Redoran sits in the Skar and counts honour like debt. Captain Rolfa Skar-Guard keeps the gate and explains rules slowly. Brarmin the egg-miner knows the tunnels under the town and does not whistle. Tevra Dren the apothecary sells marshmerrow and, she says, no poisons. Durgul Ash-Born duels for hire and insists he is no assassin.

#Inns and secrets
The Rat in the Pot has a pot and no rat. There was a rat; it is on the sign, and has recently been given a very small crown. The Ald Skar Inn's smith, Velan Arethi, will replace any chitin plate he did not break. The shell hums three notes on certain nights. The third is wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldruhn.hook: The Redoran city of the Ashlands, built in and around the shell of a giant emperor crab, where ash storms rattle the shutters and Daedric shrines stand within sight of the councillors' windows.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldruhn.rumour: Ald'ruhn's Redoran to the bone: duty, honour, and a dry cough. If you're headed north of town, mind the Nocturnal stones; the Bal Molagmer meet there, and they don't like strangers seeing their faces.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldruhn.skar_letter:
Garyn,
You write that Cyrodiil is green and wet and that nobody coughs. I am happy for you. Here the ash is so thick this year we eat it in our bread and call it pepper.

Your sister has joined the Redoran Guard. She says she is protecting the house. She is protecting a wall. But she is good at it, and the wall is still standing, and so is she.
Come home when your service ends. Bring Imperial tea. Do not bring an Imperial wife, your father is too old for the argument.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldruhn.storm_watch:
#Night watch, Skyrim gate
Storm began at the first hour. Visibility nil. Three knocks at the gate at the second hour. Did not open, per standing order. No footprints in the morning. The ash covers footprints. That is the official explanation.

Second item. A Telvanni mouth arrived at dusk, asked the road to the Hermaeus Mora stones west of the city, and was given it, as the road is public. He has not returned. Councillor Sarethi asks whether we are obliged to look for him. Councillor Venim asks whether we are obliged to stop looking if we find him.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldunz.hook: At place.nirncraft.aldunz, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the dune-seas and qanat-fed oases of the Alik'r Desert, where Crown oasis-lords, nomad matrons, and the Ash'abah enforce the sacred Well-Oaths.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldunz.rumour: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.aldunz report signs of Kykos dust-witches, Withered Hand tomb-defilers, and Anthotis crypt-drinkers operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.aldunz.v8_lore_aldu:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.aldunz

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.aldunz. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.aldunz

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the dune-seas and qanat-fed oases of the Alik'r Desert, where Crown oasis-lords, nomad matrons, and the Ash'abah enforce the sacred Well-Oaths. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.aldunz have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by Kykos dust-witches, Withered Hand tomb-defilers, and Anthotis crypt-drinkers. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

place_lore.nirncraft.alftand.brelas_note: Brelas Indarys, assistant to Quaestor Vesk

Day 3 in the glacier. The Quaestor's instructions are to sketch the resonator coils in the upper halls and come home. The Quaestor's instructions did not account for the treasure-hunters who got here first, two of whom are now fighting over a bag of Dwemer cogs.
Day 5. The hunters are dead. I did not see what did it; I heard it. A long click, then a hiss of steam. I have hidden in a pipe gallery with my sketches and half a loaf.

Day 7. Found the great coil. It hums when I touch it, a note the Quaestor will weep to hear. I have taken the small regulating rod; it fits in my satchel. Something down below has started clicking again. If I do not return, my notes go to Aurelian Vesk at the College. He will pretend he is not worried. He will be.
place_lore.nirncraft.alftand.expedition_:
Rope, 200 ft. Picks, 6. Lamp oil, 4 jugs. Skooma, 2 bottles (J'zhar's, do not touch).
Personnel: Sulla (leader), J'zhar, Umana, Sond, Endrast, Valie. Pay: equal shares of all salvage, leader takes double.
Revised: Sond took the sled and ran in the night. Valie fell in the crevasse. Pay: equal shares among the living. Revised again: whoever is left, take everything and run.

^Scrawled on the back
Umana's gone too. J'zhar says it was the cold. J'zhar keeps going down to the lower halls alone and coming back with his paws full of brass. I do not think I trust J'zhar. I do not think J'zhar trusts me either.
place_lore.nirncraft.alftand.hook: A Dwemer city half-swallowed by a glacier in the hills of Winterhold. An expedition dug its way inside last year; the glacier is still deciding whether to let them out.
place_lore.nirncraft.alftand.rumour: Alftand's under the ice. There was a whole camp of treasure-hunters out there. Now there's a camp, and no hunters.
place_lore.nirncraft.alftand.sk4_note_19: Folio #20 (927, -1345): Field inspection recorded for Alftand within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #20 for alftand: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Alftand are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor.hook: The white capital of the Summerset Isles and the heart of the Aldmeri Dominion, a city of perfect towers and perfect manners, where the Thalmor govern, the Sapiarchs teach, and everyone is watched.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor.porters_lett: Ondarion, porter of the Lower Quay

Brother,
They took Aunt Elerie's daughter away last week. The child was born with a crooked spine and the Directorate's genealogists came to the house with their measuring rods. They were very polite. They always are. They said the family's 'line' would be reviewed. Aunt Elerie said she would rather lose the line than the girl.

So she has lost the line. They are both gone, out to the old Namira shrine west of the city where the cast-outs live, the crooked and the scarred and the ones whose ears are the wrong shape. I took them bread at night. Do not tell Father. He would report me, and then he would weep, and he would do both sincerely.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor.rumour: Alinor is the most beautiful city in Tamriel. Everybody says so. Everybody has to. There's a Justiciar on every corner taking notes on who doesn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor.thalmor_proc:
^CONCERNING THE SHRINES OF THE OUTER HILLS
The Directorate notes with displeasure that the old Daedric shrines in the hills about Alinor continue to receive visitors. These shrines predate the Dominion and are preserved solely as historical curiosities, in the manner of a ruin or a scar.

Citizens of good lineage do not visit scars. Any citizen found at a Daedric shrine after sunset will be presumed to be engaged in research, and will be invited to explain that research to a Justiciar. The invitation may not be declined. The Directorate thanks the citizens of Alinor for their continued and unanimous loyalty.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor.tirenwe_lett: Lorekeeper Tirenwe of the Crystal Tower Annex

Dear Colleague,
You ask why I still keep the memorial roll of the Oblivion Crisis when the Directorate prefers that we celebrate the Dominion's founding instead. Because I was a child in this city when the gates opened. Because I watched the hills north of Alinor burn while the Daedra walked up from the Destroyer's old shrine as if it were a doorway they had always owned.

And because, my friend, someone has begun leaving offerings at that shrine again. Fresh ones. I have reported this to the Justiciars, who thanked me and did nothing, which in my experience means either that they know, or that they do not wish to. I am too old to climb hills. I am looking for someone who is not.
place_lore.nirncraft.alinor_royal_palace:
#PROTOCOL
Bow when the sun is above the left-hand arch. Bow lower when it is above the right. If the sun is behind a cloud, bow as though it were not. Do not speak of the Queen's sister. Do not speak of the Queen's other sister. Do not mention that there are two.

A courtier's marginal note: 'There are, of course, three. The third has not been spoken of since the winter before the Great War. The Chancellor has asked that her name be omitted from this protocol, and from every other.'
The royal palace of Alinor on its terrace of white quartz, a stack of arches and prism-roofed halls where the Dominion's Queen holds court beneath the Crystal Tower.

The Palace has three hundred rooms and the Queen uses six. The rest are kept in exquisite order, for no one, by servants who do not know why. It is the greatest compliment the court knows how to pay a ghost.
place_lore.nirncraft.allmaker_beast_ston: The All-Maker's Beast Stone, a short walk west of Thirsk Mead Hall. Skaal hunters touch it before a hunt. Lately, the beasts themselves have been coming to it and standing very still.
A Thirsk hunter told me he saw a bear, a wolf and a horker standing at the Beast Stone side by side, just staring at it. Not fighting. Staring. Then they all walked away north together.

Three mornings running I have found tracks of many beasts circling the Beast Stone and not one of them hunting another. Rabbit beside wolf, wolf beside bear. On the third morning I waited. They came at dusk, stood around the stone like folk at a funeral, and left in the same direction: toward the Temple of Miraak. I did not follow. Brenna says I should tell the Skaal. The Skaal already know. They just look at me and say the stone is sick.
place_lore.nirncraft.allmaker_earth_ston: Sergeant, as ordered, I watched the Earth Stone from the ridge from dusk until dawn. Fourteen townsfolk arrived after midnight, some barefoot, all silent. I recognised Ilvi Sadrano, the smith's apprentice, and two of the Company miners. They worked without speaking, setting stone on stone, as neatly as masons.

When I went down to turn Ilvi home, she looked at me and smiled and said: we are nearly done. Then she went back to work. At first light they all simply stopped and walked back to town, and when I asked them at the gate what they had been doing, every one of them said they had been asleep. I believe them. I do not know what to report.
The All-Maker's Earth Stone, west of Raven Rock, where sleepwalkers from the town have built a strange shrine around the ancient pillar without knowing they did it.
The sleepwalkers go to the Earth Stone, carry rocks, build walls, and come home with no memory of it. Every morning the shrine is a little taller.
The All-Maker's Sun Stone, on the ash plain north of Tel Mithryn. The Skaal greet the dawn here. Telvanni spies watch the road to Ashfallow Citadel from its shadow.
There's a Telvanni apprentice who spends all day sitting in the shade of the Sun Stone with a spyglass, looking at Ashfallow Citadel. Says it's research. Looks like spying to me.

To the master's steward. From the Sun Stone, fourth day. The renegade Seryne Dralas walks the walls of Ashfallow Citadel at dawn and dusk. I have counted seven ash creatures in her yard; today there were nine. They face south toward Raven Rock and do not move. Her hired guards appear nervous, which I consider sensible of them.

Additional: the Sun Stone itself is unwell. The Skaal who come to greet the sunrise here touch it and pull their hands away as if it burned. At night I hear stone grinding against stone, but there is nobody here except me. I would like to be relieved. I would like to be relieved quite soon.
place_lore.nirncraft.allmaker_tree_stone: The All-Maker's Tree Stone, standing just north of the Temple of Miraak. The Skaal bring it the first green of spring; something else has been bringing it a shadow.
The Tree Stone is right next to the Temple of Miraak. Skaal say that was never a coincidence, and that the stone's been fighting the temple for a thousand years. And losing, lately.

A strip of bark tied to the base of the stone, with Skaal runes burned into it: For the Tree Stone, from the children of Brandvar's hearth. A sprig of pine, the first of the season, though the season is late. The roots of the trees near the temple have turned black this year. We do not know why. We have brought our sprig anyway. Even a sick stone needs its offering.

On the reverse: The pine we left last spring has turned grey, though no frost could touch it here. The temple stones grow a little higher every night. The Tree Stone is the oldest thing on this hill, older than the temple, and it is tired.
place_lore.nirncraft.allmaker_water_ston: One of the six stones of the All-Maker, raised by the Skaal in the island's west. The Skaal come to it for the blessing of the sea and the rivers. Lately they come to it frightened.
The Water Stone's sick, the Skaal say. Some kind of wall's grown up around it overnight. My cousin heard chanting from there, and he says nobody was chanting.

~All-Maker, who gave the fish its river and the river its sea,
~Who froze the sea to give the Skaal a road,
~Keep the water moving, that it may not grow bitter;
~Keep us moving, that we may not grow bitter.
~The stone is cold tonight, and something sits beside it
~Who is not you. Do not let it drink.

Beneath the verse a Skaal fisher has cut: Three nights ago, the stream that runs by the stone flowed backward for an hour. I put my hand in it and it was warm. Storn says the stone is sick. I say it is frightened.
place_lore.nirncraft.allmaker_wind_stone: The All-Maker's Wind Stone, on the high ground west of the Skaal village. The Skaal say the wind carries their prayers from here. Lately it carries a voice they do not know.
The Skaal won't go near the Wind Stone any more. They say the wind speaks there, and it's not the All-Maker speaking.

~Wind of the north, carry our words,
~Over the ice to the All-Maker's ear.
~Wind of the north, carry our dead,
~Over the sea where the stars are near.

Scratched underneath by a younger hand: The wind is wrong this winter. It blows from the stone and not toward it. When I put my hand on the stone I heard someone say my name, and then say that I would be useful. I did not tell Storn. I am telling the stone instead. Stone, tell the All-Maker.
place_lore.nirncraft.altar_of_thrond.hoo: A weathered stone altar between Mount Moesring and the Temple of Miraak, older than the Skaal. Offerings left here vanish overnight, and no one admits to taking them.
place_lore.nirncraft.altar_of_thrond.rum: Leave something at the Altar of Thrond and it's gone by morning. Skaal say Thrond takes it. Raven Rock folk say rieklings. My coin's on rieklings.
place_lore.nirncraft.altar_of_thrond.thr:
Old Nordic letters, half eaten by ash and frost, with a translation scratched beneath by some visitor: To Thrond, who stood between the island and the dragon-masked ones and would not kneel. Bring him salt, bread, and a true word. He was the last who said no.
Below, in a different hand, fresh: The masked ones have been here. They left nothing. They broke the bread. The altar is not happy.
And lower, carved deliberately by a Skaal hand: We brought new bread. Thrond, forgive the breakers. They follow one who knelt to everyone and everything, and he will kneel to them in the end.
place_lore.nirncraft.alten_meerhleel.hoo: A tidy canal-town east of Lilmoth, every house with a lantern in the window, one of them lit for a man who never came home.
place_lore.nirncraft.alten_meerhleel.rum: A widow in Alten Meerhleel keeps a lantern in the window for her husband, who went out in the reed-boats and was never found. The Dripping Reed says the reeds have been whispering his way home.
place_lore.nirncraft.alten_meerhleel.wid:
#To whoever the reeds speak to
My husband Jorun poled out on the fourth day of Rain's Hand and did not come back. I have lit the lantern each night since. If he is lost, tell him the way is east, then left, then east again. If he is gone, tell him the lantern is still lit.
place_lore.nirncraft.amol.hook: A small, wind-hardened hamlet on the southern snow-road where carters rest their horses before climbing into the high drifts of Winterhold.
place_lore.nirncraft.amol.rumour: The folk at Amol hamlet keep their chimneys smoking day and night; it's the last warm hearth before the road climbs into the ice.
Six coal-sledges from Whistling Mine and two scholars' wagons bound for the College sheltered in our stable-yard during yesterday's whiteout. We keep forty loaves of barley-bread and a kettle of mutton broth on the crane for anyone who makes it over the ridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancestor_glade.chil:
~Grandmother is a white moth now,
~She lives where the big tree grows,
~She lands on my hand and she does not bite,
~And she still smells a bit like a rose.

Written in large, careful letters, with a moth drawn in the corner and coloured with something yellow, perhaps pollen.
On the other side of the bark, in an adult's hand: 'My daughter wrote this the week we buried her grandmother. We stood at the water an hour, and one white moth came and sat on her hand. I do not know if it was my mother. I know my daughter stopped crying. That is enough.'
place_lore.nirncraft.ancestor_glade.hook: A hidden glade in the forest south of Falkreath where the moths glow like souls and an ancient tree stands at the heart of still water. Families come here to remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancestor_glade.mour: It is the custom in Falkreath, older than the Hall of the Dead, for a family to visit the glade in the first month after a burial. They bring no gifts. They speak no prayers aloud. They stand at the water until the moths come, and they go home when the moths go.

I am a priest of Arkay, and I am obliged to say the soul goes to Aetherius and not into a moth. I am also a man who has stood at that water after burying a friend. I do not argue with the custom. I bring a lantern, so the old ones can find the path home in the dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancestor_glade.rumo: My mother took me to the Ancestor Glade when Father died. You stand by the water, and the moths come. She said each one was someone we'd lost. I counted eleven and I cried at all of them.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancestor_glade.sk4_: Folio #35 (-525, 1404): Field inspection recorded for Ancestor Glade within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #35 for ancestor_glade: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Ancestor Glade are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancients_ascent.gri:
#3rd of Frostfall
Everyone in Falkreath has seen the dragon go over. Nobody has seen where it lands. I have. It roosts on Ancient's Ascent, south of Bonechill Passage, and it eats the elk I would otherwise be selling.

#4th of Frostfall
Halfway up. The rocks are melted smooth in places like candle wax. Bones everywhere, old and new, sheep and horse and some I do not want to name. The beast calls itself something when it lands. Sahlokvir, I think. It sounds like a name you would give a storm.

#5th of Frostfall
It saw me. It spoke to me. I do not know the words but I know mockery when I hear it. Going higher. If I can put an arrow in its eye while it sleeps, they will sing about Grimvar in Dead Man's Drink for a hundred years.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancients_ascent.hoo: A wind-scoured summit in the southern Jerall range where a dragon has made its nest among the bones of older dragons. Smoke rises from it at dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancients_ascent.leg: Patrol of the southern road, Falkreath camp. Proceeded as far as Bloodlet Throne. Observed a dragon of dun colour rising from the peak called Ancient's Ascent. Beast circled the patrol twice and departed without attacking.

I do not believe it was afraid of us. I believe it was choosing. Recommend no patrol go nearer than the Bonechill Passage until the Legion sends something heavier than eight spears. Recommend this be read by someone who will do something about it.

Endorsed below by the camp captain: 'Received. Forwarded to the Legate. The Legate replies that the Legion is not equipped to fight dragons and that the matter is for the Jarl. The Jarl replies that the matter is for the Legion. The dragon has not replied, and has eaten another horse.'
place_lore.nirncraft.ancients_ascent.rum: Hunter called Grimvar went up Ancient's Ascent to see the dragon for himself. We found his bow halfway down the mountain. Charred to the grip.
place_lore.nirncraft.ancients_ascent.sk4: Folio #36 (-339, 1454): Field inspection recorded for Ancients Ascent within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #36 for ancients_ascent: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Ancients Ascent are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.anequina_aqueduct.h: A long arched aqueduct carrying cold mountain water across a gorge, so old that the water on its top is a different colour from the water at its feet.
place_lore.nirncraft.anequina_aqueduct.m:
^BUILT BY A HUNDRED PAWS.
^FINISHED BY ONE, WHO CARVED THIS MARK AND DID NOT STAY.
Lower down, in a modern chisel: 'The one who finished it was not a mason. The mason fell, and she took his tools. Her name is on no stone. Her arch is the one that has never leaked.'
place_lore.nirncraft.anequina_aqueduct.r: The aqueduct has one more arch than its builders ever planned. The extra arch is at the middle, and the sand under it is always wet.
place_lore.nirncraft.angarvunde.angarvun:
^Here sleeps the Warden of Angarvunde
^who held the pass for forty winters
^and asked no thanks but this:
^that no hand should lift his blade.

Someone has scratched an arrow beneath the last line, pointing down a side passage. Under it, in fresh soot: 'Orc went this way. Did not come back this way.'

The stone of the lid is cracked along one edge where something heavy struck it, very recently, and there is dark blood dried on the floor beneath it. Further down the side passage the soot arrow points to, the flagstones are scattered with draugr bones, broken in a way no Nord weapon breaks them: crushed, as if by a hammer swung by someone who was very angry and very strong.
place_lore.nirncraft.angarvunde.durz_mar:
Day one. Nord dead walk here. Slow. I break three. Easy.
Day two. More dead. Not easy. Arm bleeds. Tusk-charm from Gula keeps me. She carved it from our father's tusk. I touch it, I fight better.

Day three. Big dead one in the deep hall. Blue eyes. Shouts. Wall fell on me. Charm cord snapped. Lost it in the dark.
Day four. Cannot find charm. Cannot find way out. Gula, you were right. Do not tell chief you were right. Tell chief I was brave.
place_lore.nirncraft.angarvunde.hook: A vast Nord barrow in the woods south-west of Lake Honrich, its catacombs said to guard a dead war-leader and the wealth of his clan. An Orc of Largashbur went in nine days ago.
place_lore.nirncraft.angarvunde.rumour: An Orc lad from Largashbur walked into Angarvunde bold as a bull. His sister's been sitting at the mill road every evening since, sharpening a spear.
place_lore.nirncraft.angarvunde.sk4_note: Folio #26 (1485, 1423): Field inspection recorded for Angarvunde within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #26 for angarvunde: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Angarvunde are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.angas_mill.hook: A timber mill on a cold lake in the southern Pale, worked by a handful of stubborn folk who would rather fell pines than pay tribute to anyone.
place_lore.nirncraft.angas_mill.mill_led:
#Hearthfire
Logs felled: 60. Planks dressed: 112. Sold to Windhelm: 40. Sold to Dawnstar: 30. 'Given' to Fort Kastav: 40. Remaining for our own roofs: 2.
Two planks. I'll patch the roof with the bandits' own arrows if this goes on.

Aeri says pay and keep our heads down. Aeri says the Jarl's men won't come so far south. Aeri is probably right. I hate it when she's right.
If a sellsword passes this way, I'll pay what I can. The saw is worth more than the planks.
place_lore.nirncraft.angas_mill.rumour: Anga's Mill does good timber, but lately half of it goes up the road to Fort Kastav, and it isn't the Jarl who's taking it.
place_lore.nirncraft.angas_mill.tribute_:
To the mill folk.
The road from your lake to anywhere worth selling timber goes past my walls. That makes it my road. Twenty planks every Loredas, cut and dressed, and a cask of whatever your woman brews.

Last week you sent eighteen planks and no cask. I counted. My boys counted. My boys can count to twenty when it matters.
Next time it's your saw I take, then your boat, then your thumbs. Fort Kastav has stood five hundred years and it'll stand long after your mill rots.
Grelka
place_lore.nirncraft.angis_camp.falkreat:
Dear Angi,
I am eleven and a good shot already. I hit the crow on the graveyard gate twice (it lived both times). Father says you might teach me if I ask politely and stop climbing on things. I am asking politely.

I could carry your water and clean your arrows. I would not talk much. I would try not to talk much. Father says I should mention I am not afraid of anything, but that is not true anymore since I went in the cairn, so I will not say it. Please write back. Thorvi of Falkreath.
place_lore.nirncraft.angis_camp.hook: A secluded camp in the hills south of Falkreath, ringed with archery targets. A young huntress lives here alone and teaches the bow to those who earn her trust.
place_lore.nirncraft.angis_camp.rumour: There's a girl lives alone in the hills south of town, Angi. Best shot in the hold, they say. Doesn't like visitors. Likes arrows that hit the middle.
place_lore.nirncraft.angis_camp.sk4_note: Folio #37 (-737, 1546): Field inspection recorded for Angis Camp within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #37 for angis_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Angis Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.angis_camp.target_t:
Notches cut neatly into the side of a target post:
Morning: 30 shafts, 27 in the red. Wind from the east.
Noon: 30 shafts, 29 in the red. No wind.
Dusk: 30 shafts, moving target (rabbit, by accident), 1 in the red. Rabbit escaped.
Note to self: the rabbit was faster than the wind. Practise rabbits.

Lower on the post, cut more deeply: 'Mother and Father taught me to shoot here. Thirty shafts a day, every day, until it is not a thing you do but a thing you are. I still shoot thirty. Some days I think they would be proud. Some days I think they would tell me to come down from the hills and live.'
place_lore.nirncraft.anises_cabin.anise_:
For a visitor who asks too many questions:
One cup honey, one cup flour, a pinch of nightshade (only a pinch, dear, we want them to forget, not to stop).
Bake until golden. Serve warm with a smile.
For a visitor who will not stop asking: see the other recipe, in the cellar, under the loose stone.

On the back, in the same spidery script: 'Sweet rolls for the Riverwood boy, the one who brings the wood. No nightshade. He is polite, and he is useful, and one must keep a few useful people about who remember where they have been. Mostly.'
place_lore.nirncraft.anises_cabin.hook: A lonely cabin in the hills below Bleak Falls Barrow, home to an old woman who keeps to herself and keeps her cellar locked.
place_lore.nirncraft.anises_cabin.riverw: I do not like to speak ill of the old woman in the cabin by the Guardian Stones. She has always been polite. But my nephew went to sell her firewood on Turdas and came back three hours later with no memory of the afternoon and a taste of cinnamon in his mouth.

He had been paid in full. He had also been paid for wood he did not bring. I would like someone sensible to go and ask her, very politely, what exactly she keeps in the cellar, and why there are crows on her roof in every season, including those when crows have gone south.
place_lore.nirncraft.anises_cabin.rumour: Old Anise lives up past the Guardian Stones. Kind enough, gives out sweet rolls. But my dog won't go within a mile of her cellar, and that dog's afraid of nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.anises_cabin.sk4_no: Folio #15 (-304, 716): Field inspection recorded for Anises Cabin within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.ansilvund.barrow_li:
Old runes, deep-cut, in a hand that pressed hard:
'Hrodvald lies here, who drove the elves from the warm valleys. His guard lies with him. They sleep sworn. They wake sworn. Whoever wakes them is their lord until the oath is broken, and the oath is broken only by the blade that sealed it.'

Beneath, scratched fresh: 'Feldir thinks that makes him lord. Feldir has not read the part about the blade. The blade hangs on the eldest of the guard, and the guard does not sleep as deeply as the master.'
place_lore.nirncraft.ansilvund.cell_jour:
#12th of Last Seed
The outer seals broken. The barrow's lord is named on every lintel: Hrodvald Iron-Breath, who took this valley from the snow elves and was buried with his oath-guard around him.

#2nd of Hearthfire
Venkar at Cragwallow Slope has stopped trading us bodies. Without fresh vessels we must wake the old ones. Hrodvald's guard stir at the sound of his name. Hrodvald himself has not.

#Frostfall
We have found the inner chamber. Master Feldir says three more nights of chanting. I counted the guard and counted us. They are more. I have not said so to Master Feldir.
place_lore.nirncraft.ansilvund.hook: An old Nord barrow in the south-eastern hills, opened by a cell of necromancers who believe its sleeping chieftain can be woken, and who are very close to being right.
place_lore.nirncraft.ansilvund.lover_let:
Helga,
You were right. I am not cut out for this. I joined because Master Feldir promised me a way to bring back Mother. Now I spend every night chanting at a corpse in a crown and he has stopped mentioning Mother at all.

If I come home in spring, marry me. If I don't, marry the smith's boy; he has nice teeth and no interest in the dead.
Sister Thyra counts the oath-guard every night and goes pale. I have started counting the steps to the outer door instead. There are two hundred and twelve. I could run them in the dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.ansilvund.rumour: Robed folk came to Ansilvund in Last Seed with mule-loads of salt and books. Since then the hunters say the barrow sighs at night, like something stretching after a long sleep.

place_lore.nirncraft.anvil.company_manif: Purser of the East Empire Company

#Inbound from Senchal, 2nd of Hearthfire
80 casks of rum, sealed. 60 bolts of Elsweyr cotton. 4 crates 'medicinal herbs', Senchal port-stamp, not opened per instruction from the Factor.
1 Khajiit passenger, name given as 'no one in particular', paid in gold, disembarked before inspection.

Note for the Factor: the medicinal herbs smell exactly like moon sugar. I have not opened them. I would like that recorded twice. I have also not seen the Khajiit since. I would like that recorded too, in case it matters later.
place_lore.nirncraft.anvil.hook: A Gold Coast port of white walls and red roofs, where East Empire Company ships unload, pirates drink in the same taverns as the sailors they rob, and the old lighthouse watches the Abecean Sea.
place_lore.nirncraft.anvil.rumour: Anvil's lovely if you like fish and gossip. The Company's hiring sailors and nobody's signing. The last crew that sailed for Stros M'Kai came back three hands short and wouldn't say why.
#Turdas
Oil low. Ordered more. The Company says it will send oil when it sends wages, which is to say at the second coming of Tiber Septim.
A widow climbed the stair at dusk. The lamp guttered, as they say it does. I stood with her until it steadied.

#Fredas
She came again. She says her husband was mate on the Jolly Pocket, taken by the new pirate captain, the one who spares Kvatch flags. She says the captain is Kvatch-born and hates Anvil for taking her mother's house. If true, half the town owes that woman something and the other half owes her more.

place_lore.nirncraft.arboretum.hook: A great domed glasshouse where the Empire grows a specimen of every tree it has ever conquered, and a few that conquered it.
place_lore.nirncraft.arboretum.rumour: The Arboretum's oldest tree is meant to be a cutting of the Eldergleam-grove stock, brought south by Alessia. Ask the Archivist about it and you will be there until dinner.
place_lore.nirncraft.arboretum.seedling_:
^ACCESSIONS, LAST QUARTER
^No. 3114: Silverbirch scion, Nobles District donation, thriving.
^No. 3115: Fire-cedar, Valenwood stock, dying; the Archivist will not hear of it.
^No. 3116: a bulb of unknown origin, delivered by a barge-woman who gave no name. It has bloomed twice. The flowers are blue and warm to the touch.
Query for the next committee: if a flower is warm, is it a flower? I have asked three alchemists and a priest of Dibella. The priest said yes. The alchemists said send it back.
place_lore.nirncraft.arcwind_point.hook: A ruined dragon shrine on a rocky height in the far south-west of the Rift. A great green-scaled dragon has claimed it and burns anything that climbs its stair.
place_lore.nirncraft.arcwind_point.rumou: Arcwind Point's got a dragon on it now. Legion scouts went up to look and came back with their eyebrows gone. Two of them came back, anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.arcwind_point.scout:
Legate,
Three of us went to observe the dragon at Arcwind Point as ordered. Observation completed. The dragon also observed us. Marcus did not survive the observation.

The beast nests on the old stone platform at the summit. It has scales the colour of birch moss and it hunts the deer herds south of Autumnwatch Tower every third day, returning at dusk.

Recommendation: someone kills it. Recommendation: that someone is not me. I am requesting transfer to a posting with fewer dragons.
place_lore.nirncraft.arcwind_point.sk4_n: Folio #29 (747, 1460): Field inspection recorded for Arcwind Point within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #29 for arcwind_point: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Arcwind Point are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.arcwind_point.word_:
A rubbing taken from the curved wall near the summit, in the angular claw-script of the old dragon tongue. Beside it, a pilgrim from Ivarstead has written:

'The Greybeards say these walls remember the words of the dead. I touched it and heard a wind with no air in it. I don't know what I heard. I know I won't come back.'
place_lore.nirncraft.arenthia.caravan_no:
^THIS ONE SEEKS GUARDS
Ri'zahd's caravan leaves for Rimmen at the new moon with moon-sugar, silk and many very fine carpets. Ri'zahd pays well. Ri'zahd pays better if no carpets go missing, as they did last time near the shadowed shrine north-west of town.

Ri'zahd knows who took them. Ri'zahd knows the thieves leave a share for the Night Mistress at that stone. Ri'zahd has also left a share at that stone, a larger one, so that the Mistress may think twice before favouring the thieves again. Ri'zahd is not proud. Ri'zahd is practical.
place_lore.nirncraft.arenthia.hook: A border town of Reaper's March where Bosmer and Khajiit trade, quarrel and drink together beneath stone walls older than either people's memory, and lately where nobody sleeps soundly.
place_lore.nirncraft.arenthia.innkeeper_: Shazah, keeper of the Two Moons Inn

To the Moon-Priest of Rawl'kha,
Shazah writes because no one in Arenthia will listen. Every night this month the sleepers come down out of the houses and walk north, toward the old stones of Vaermina beyond the walls. Bosmer and Khajiit alike, eyes shut, smiling. In the morning they remember nothing but a woman with a purple lantern.

Shazah's own cub walked last night. Shazah followed. There is a Bosmer woman at the shrine who calls herself the Lantern-Bearer, and she sits with a basket and the sleepers drop their dreams into it like fruit. Please send a priest. Or send someone with claws. Shazah does not much care which.
place_lore.nirncraft.arenthia.rumour: Arenthia used to be a good town for a quiet drink. Now half of it walks the streets at night with its eyes shut. Shazah at the inn says it's the dreams. Shazah's eyes have gone very dark.

Every funeral cart coming down the road stops at Arkay's Wayside Altar to leave a sprig of snowberry before entering the town gates.

Folio #63 (-1280, 1640): Field inspection recorded for Arkay Wayside Altar within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Let the traveler who passes beneath these pines pause a moment and trim the lantern wick. Four seasons turn upon the wheel, and every road in Skyrim comes at last to the quiet earth.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthamz.dwemer_r:
A charcoal rubbing on fine paper, with a translation pencilled beneath in a cramped hand:
'Let the hall be struck and the deep listen. What answers is ours. What does not answer is to be made to answer.'
Below, the translator has added: 'Uncertain of the final verb. It may also read: to be made silent.'

On the reverse, in Pell's hand: 'Took this rubbing from the lintel of the singing hall. The machines did not stir while I worked, which I attribute to my having first hummed the fourth harmonic very softly. Note for any successor: hum low, move slowly, and under no circumstances whistle.'
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthamz.hook: A Dwemer ruin in the gorge below Dushnikh Yal, where the stone still hums with a note no living singer can hold. Scholars come for the sound; the machines keep most of them.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthamz.orc_lett:
Milk-drinker,
Your friend with the trumpet did not come back up. We waited three days because the chief said it was polite. Then we went down as far as the brass men let us and brought back what was left. His bones are in a sack at our gate. His lens is not. The brass men keep it in the singing hall.

Do not send another one. If you must send another one, send one who can swing an axe and does not talk so much. We are tired of the singing. When the stone sings loud the forge goes cold and the iron will not take an edge.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthamz.rumour: Orcs at Dushnikh Yal say the ruin under their mountain sings at night. A scholar went down last spring to measure the song. They sent his bones back up with his notes.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthamz.scholar_: Magister Avidius Pell, College of Winterhold (Associate)

Being a preliminary account of the tonal phenomena of Arkngthamz, with remarks.
The so-called singing of the ruin is not, as the Orcs of Dushnikh Yal insist, the voice of trapped Dwemer spirits (1). It is a sustained resonance produced by the great tuning apparatus in the lower halls, which I have heard but not yet seen.

(1) The Orcs also insisted I should not go down. I note this objection for completeness.
I have fitted my Tonal Lens, a ground crystal of my own design, to the brass ear-trumpet and can now hear the fourth harmonic distinctly. The machines appear to wake when the harmonic rises. I have left the lens in the lower chamber for a night's measurement and shall retrieve it at first light.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthand.hook: A Dwemer city-hall of cranking bronze with giant gear-halls, steam vents and a centrifuge chamber at the core.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthand.rumour: Arkngthand still turns, one revolution an hour. Locals say there is someone in the middle of it, waiting.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthand.thread.p: Dial two: Arkngthand, centrifuge side. Same figure as the first, same hand, same tick. I was told the dials were calibrated to local time. They are not. They are calibrated to each other. One hand moves, they all move. One dial stops, they all stop. This is a signal, not a clock.
place_lore.nirncraft.arkngthand.web.p0: ATTENDANT, SEAT UNTIL RETURN. The masters will come back by the third turn of the age. If they do not, the Attendant is released. If they do, the Attendant will answer for the delay.
place_lore.nirncraft.artaeum.fisherman_a: I write this down because no one in the tavern believes me. On the night of the 3rd of Hearthfire I was out past the western shoals in the fog, and the fog opened like a door. There was an island, green and gentle, with orchards and a white tower, and bells ringing so softly I felt them more than heard them.

A woman in a grey robe stood on the shore and looked straight at me. She did not wave. She simply nodded, as if I had arrived exactly when expected, and then the fog closed and I was alone with my nets. My nets were full. They had been empty before. I have never caught fish like those before or since. They tasted of time.
place_lore.nirncraft.artaeum.hook: The misty isle of the Psijic Order, which appears off the Summerset coast only when the monks of the Old Ways wish to be found. Sailors who have seen it rarely agree on what they saw.
place_lore.nirncraft.artaeum.psijic_apho:
^Cut into a white stone on the shore, in a hand that is very old and very patient
The Old Ways are not a door. They are the wall in which the door is set.
What the Altmer call purity, we call stillness. What the Thalmor call order, we call a cage that has not yet noticed it is a cage.

Time is a river that remembers its banks. Do not try to swim against it. Do not try to drink all of it. Sit on the bank, and wait, and you will see everything you have lost come floating by.
If you are reading this, you were invited. Do not be proud of it. So was the fish.
place_lore.nirncraft.artaeum.rumour: My father saw Artaeum once, through the fog off Alinor: a white tower and an old man waving. Next morning, nothing but sea. He never fished that water again. Said it felt like he'd been interrupted.
place_lore.nirncraft.aryon_plantation.ba:
#Whoever finds this
I left on the night of the fire. My mother was in the house. I was twenty. I have been twenty ever since. The ring is hers. The deed is ours. If you are from the Row, tell the keeper I am sorry, and that I have not forgotten where she is.
place_lore.nirncraft.aryon_plantation.ho: A weathered plantation on the road to Necrom, its saltrice fields slack and its manor house shuttered for forty years.
place_lore.nirncraft.aryon_plantation.ru: A man sleeps in the barn at the old Aryon farm, they say, with a half-burned deed in one fist and a ring on his thumb he will not take off, not even to wash.

place_lore.nirncraft.ashfallow_citadel.d:
Ma,
The wizard pays well. Better than the mine at Raven Rock, better than fishing. The work is standing on a wall and watching for Telvanni.
The things she makes walk the yard at night. They do not sleep. They do not eat. They stand by the gate and look south toward Raven Rock, all of them, the same way, like dogs that smell supper.
I am going to leave before she makes enough of them to need us gone. If I do not come, burn this, and do not tell Pa what I was doing here. Tell him I was fishing. Jorund.
place_lore.nirncraft.ashfallow_citadel.h: A walled Telvanni citadel in the ash wastes east of Kagrumez, held by a renegade wizard who quarrelled with Neloth. She has found a way to make the ash itself stand up and serve.
place_lore.nirncraft.ashfallow_citadel.r: Ashfallow Citadel's got a new mistress. Telvanni, cast out of Tel Mithryn. They say she can raise ash spawn the way a farmer raises guar. And she's not raising them to plough.
place_lore.nirncraft.ashfallow_citadel.s: Neloth said the ash spawn are a nuisance to be swept from doorsteps. Neloth is old and lazy and has never asked what the ash remembers. I have. It remembers being people. It remembers the Red Year. It remembers a great deal of anger, and anger can be shaped.

Progress: seven risen, all obedient. A heart-stone of compressed ash at the core of each gives them purpose. I need more ash. Raven Rock has a great deal of it, swept into piles every morning by the Redoran fools. When I have thirty, I will go and collect it. When I have a hundred, I will go and collect Tel Mithryn.
Personal: Neloth's spies watch from the Sun Stone. Let them watch. Let them tell him. I want him to know it was me.

Needed from the Ramshackle Trading Post: salt fish, 30. Sujamma, 4 bottles, the good kind, not the kind Burzol waters. Soul gems, any size, as many as he has. Lamp oil. New lock for the south gate. Tell Burzol the Mistress will pay at the end of the month. Tell Burzol not to ask about the end of the month.

Underneath, scrawled by a guard: Burzol says no more credit until the Mistress pays for the last lot. The Mistress says Burzol will be paid in ash. I do not think she was joking, and I do not think he knows what that means.

place_lore.nirncraft.autumnshade_clearin: A quiet clearing in the gold birch woods north-west of Riften, where the leaves lie so deep you sink to the ankle. Hunters say it's a place the forest spirits come to rest.

Ingun,
I'll wait in the clearing until the moon's over the tallest birch. If you come, we'll go to Windhelm and never see a Black-Briar again. If you don't, I'll know your mother won, and I'll go anyway, and I'll write to you every month and burn every letter.

The leaves are very deep tonight. It's cold. Something big moved in the trees just now and then stopped. I'm sure it was a deer. Please come.
Autumnshade Clearing's the prettiest spot in the Rift. Also the quietest. No birds sing there, have you noticed? My mother said that's where the spriggans sleep.

Folio #41 (2114, 1143): Field inspection recorded for Autumnshade Clearing within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #41 for autumnshade_clearing: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Autumnshade Clearing are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Carved into a birch at the edge of the clearing, a hand with five fingers spread, the old woodcutters' sign for 'do not cut here'. Beneath it, a newer note pinned with a nail:

'Heartwood Mill men: do NOT take timber from this clearing again. Remember what happened to Ottar's uncle. The trees remember too.'

Woodcutters in the Rift tell of a Heartwood man who felled three birches in this clearing to fill a Black-Briar order in a hurry. The next morning the stumps had grown back as thorn, and the man was found at the edge of the clearing with his own axe in his hand and moss in his mouth. The mill has kept to the far side of the woods ever since. Spriggans, folk say, do not forget a wrong, and they do not care whose order it was.
place_lore.nirncraft.autumnwatch_poacher: A birch-bark shelter hidden in the golden foliage below the southern towers, where poachers dry venison and black-bear pelts.
The game-wardens in Riften have been looking for the Autumnwatch Poacher Blind all season, but the birch woods hide the smoke too well.

place_lore.nirncraft.autumnwatch_tower.h: A ruined Nord watchtower in the birch woods south of Ivarstead. Dragons have been seen circling it since the mounds began to open.
place_lore.nirncraft.autumnwatch_tower.r: There's a dragon been circling Autumnwatch Tower like it's waiting for something. Froki says it's waiting for its friend to wake.

place_lore.nirncraft.autumnwatch_tower.t:
#14th of Frostfall
The Legion pays me three septims a week to sit in this tower and shout if I see Stormcloaks. I have not seen any Stormcloaks.

I have seen a dragon. It came over the trees at dawn, black against the sun, and circled twice and went north to where the burial mound is. I shouted. Nobody heard.

#16th of Frostfall
Two now. One green, from the direction of Arcwind Point. One black, from the mound. They spoke to each other in the air. Thunder that had words in it.

I'm leaving. Three septims a week is not enough to be the fellow they speak about next.
place_lore.nirncraft.avanchnzel.expediti: Lucan Varro, of the Imperial Geographical Society

#17th of Sun's Height
Avanchnzel at last. Six of us, four mules, and one Orc guide who left the moment we lit the first lamp. The machinery here still breathes. I have never been so happy in my life.

#2nd of Last Seed
Found a small bronze key that hums at a single pitch when held near the larger engines. I am calling it the resonance key. The engines quiet when it hums. I believe it was a kind of master command. Petronia thinks I am being romantic.

#9th of Last Seed
Petronia is dead. The large guardian in the lower hall woke when I took the key past it. The key does not quiet that one. That one, I think, was built to guard the key. I am hiding. If this book is found, the key must not go back to the Society. It must go into the lake.
place_lore.nirncraft.avanchnzel.hook: A sprawling Dwemer ruin in the southern hills near Largashbur. An Imperial scholarly expedition went in last summer and sent back only one letter.
place_lore.nirncraft.avanchnzel.petronia:
Dear Livia,
You'd hate it here: no baths, no wine and nowhere to sit that isn't brass. You would love the light, though. The Dwemer pipes glow faintly, as if the whole city were remembering a fire it can't quite recall.

Lucan is besotted with a key. Men and their keys. I'll be home by Hearthfire, I promise, with a crate of cogs for your boy and a story for you.
place_lore.nirncraft.avanchnzel.rumour: Some fancy Imperials went into the Dwemer ruin by Largashbur with mules and ledgers and a lot of bright ideas. The Orcs say the mules came out. Nobody else.

place_lore.nirncraft.baandari_caravan_st: A ring of wagons and a ring of fires beside the Rimmen road, where Baandari traders mend axles, trade songs and keep the only route book that every clan agrees on.

#THE SHORT WAY TO RIMMEN
Wells: Qasari, good; Seri, brackish; Thamokha, salt. Do not camp at Thamokha. A caravan once did, and rose with a very strange hunger.
Price of safe passage past Nekha: three coins, one song, and the polite refusal to ask who is paying whom. Do not carry more than you can sing.
The Baandari say the road is a living thing, and they have only borrowed it. They return it each evening, with interest, by way of a song.

place_lore.nirncraft.baira.baira_travell:
#Baira, the night before the long road.
Rasul, I will not say what is in the bag, but I will say that the watch at the Spice Gate has doubled. They stopped three of my camels and asked about a leather bag with red stitching. I said I knew nothing. I know nothing. I carried nothing.

If your man comes through Baira, tell him the well is dry on the east side and the goats are in a mood. Tell him the way is open, and the shade returns at the third hour. He will know what I mean. If not, I have sent him a camel.
place_lore.nirncraft.baira.hook: A small caravan-village south of Rihad, famed for its well, its goats and a cheese that a Rihad merchant once said was worth the trip.
place_lore.nirncraft.baira.rumour: Baira is where the caravans from Rihad rest the night before the desert. It has one well, one inn, and one cheese, and each is better than it has any right to be.

place_lore.nirncraft.balmora.gazetteer.p:
#The people of the river
Factor Dron Hlaalu keeps the Council Manor and the river with equal care. Nilena Vandas is a freight consultant on the south bank and will tell you she has never held anything for anyone. Hesta Girith the apothecary sells poultices and, on quieter days, apologies. Rilvo Aleth of the Legion watches the high bridge and will tell you to keep to the left.

#Eating, drinking and being cheated
Eight Plates serves eight plates a night; the ninth guest goes hungry. It is a policy, not a shortage. South Wall Cornerclub has rules about singing before sundown and cheating after; everything between is a negotiation. The silt strider called Dowager has been known to sit on caches of silk. Do not tell her she is brave.
place_lore.nirncraft.balmora.hook: The Hlaalu town on the Odai river, where silt striders groan at the port, the Camonna Tong owns half the doors, and sleepers have begun to walk out of the ash at night toward the Vaermina stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.balmora.rumour: Balmora's all business, bad business mostly. Ask Fevyn Andalor about her brother. She'll tell you about the ash-sleepers, and about the Vaermina stones north-east, and she'll cry, and she'll ask you for help.
place_lore.nirncraft.balmora.sleepwalker:
#Night of the 2nd
Drals got up at the second hour and walked to the door with his eyes open. I said his name. He said 'the Mother is singing'. Our mother is twelve years in the ground.

#Night of the 5th
Tied him to the bed. Woke to find the rope bitten through and the door open. Found him at the edge of town at dawn, facing north-east, toward the Vaermina stones, standing in a ring of others. All sleeping. All smiling.
#Night of the 6th
I am going to ask the outlanders at the Council Club. One of them might be mad enough to walk up there.
place_lore.nirncraft.balmora.tong_warnin:
OUTLANDER,
This house was sold to you by a Hlaalu clerk who did not ask us. We are asking now. You have until the next Tirdas to sell it back to its rightful buyer for the price you paid, less the cost of our trouble.

If you are wondering who we are, ask the Imperial who had the house before you. You will find him in the Odai, a little downstream. Bring a pole.
This is a courtesy. The Tong is courteous once.

place_lore.nirncraft.bannermist_tower.ho: A ruined Nordic tower in the misty woods west of Falkreath, once a signal post and now a lookout for the bandits of Knifepoint Ridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.bannermist_tower.lo:
Third night up here. Mist so thick I can't see the lamp at Knifepoint Ridge, so how is Hjolfrid supposed to see mine?
Rats in the stair. Wind in the arrow slits. Somebody's grave right under the tower, the old stones say, and on the second night something knocked on the floor from below. Three times. Not the code for anything.
I want to go back to the camp.

Fourth night. The knocking came again, and the floor stones were warm when I put my hand on them. There's an old name carved over the cellar arch, mostly worn: something-mist. Banner? I am not paid enough to sit over somebody's grave.
place_lore.nirncraft.bannermist_tower.ru: On clear nights you see lamps blink in Bannermist Tower, short and long, like someone talking. Next morning there's always a cart missing on the mill road.
place_lore.nirncraft.bannermist_tower.si:
One long: cart on the mill road, heading for Falkreath.
Two long: cart heading for Half-Moon Mill.
One long, one short: guards with it. Let it pass.
Three short: Legion patrol. Everybody get down.
All dark: something's wrong at the tower. Hjolfrid sends three to look.

Lamp code for the gang only. Learn it, then burn this.
If you didn't burn this, Hjolfrid will burn you. Finnvid, I'm talking to you. You've had this list three weeks and you still signal 'Legion' for every hay cart.
The lamp stays in the tower top. Nobody takes it to camp. Without the lamp, the ridge is blind, and a blind gang is a hanged gang.
place_lore.nirncraft.bannermist_tower.sk: Folio #20 (-1223, 867): Field inspection recorded for Bannermist Tower within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #20 for bannermist_tower: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Bannermist Tower are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.bards_leap_summit.b: ~I came up here with a broken heart,
~A broken lute, and a Briarheart's dart.
~I dropped my ring where the white water pours,
~Then I followed it down. The pool is yours.
^Below, smaller: The ring was Ingrith's. She married a merchant in Markarth. If you find it in the pool beneath the falls, keep it. I'm done with it. - the Leaper

Further down the rock, in a different and steadier hand: I watched him jump. He came up laughing in the pool with blood on his lip, and he sang the whole walk back to Markarth and never once stammered. Some of the Bards' College folk think the falls themselves are blessed. I think a man who survives that has nothing left to be nervous about.
place_lore.nirncraft.bards_leap_summit.h: A waterfall plunging from the cliffs by Lost Valley Redoubt, named for a bard who leapt from its top and lived to sing about it, or so the bards insist.
place_lore.nirncraft.bards_leap_summit.r: Bards say if you leap from the top of Bard's Leap and live, you'll never be tongue-tied again. Bards also say a lot of things.

place_lore.nirncraft.battle_born_farm.fo:
Master Olfrid,
The wheat is in, forty sacks, two more than last year. The Legion quartermaster took twelve without paying, as promised. He gave me a paper with a seal on it. I have put the paper in the strongbox. I don't know what else to do with paper.

The Gray-Mane boy was seen at the north fence again, looking at the barn. I don't think he meant harm, but I set the dogs loose that night anyway.

Also, the hands want to know if they are expected to fight if the Stormcloaks come down from their camp past the river. I told them a Battle-Born never runs. They asked if that went for hired men too. Please advise. Hrongar.
place_lore.nirncraft.battle_born_farm.ho: The Battle-Born clan's own farmland east of Whiterun, with Imperial colours flying over the barn. Its hands talk loudly of loyalty and quietly of the grain levy.
place_lore.nirncraft.battle_born_farm.ru: Old Olfrid Battle-Born doesn't plough a single furrow himself, but he'll tell you to your face whose farm it is. His foreman Hrongar does the work and takes the blame.

place_lore.nirncraft.benirus_manor.hook: A fine house on the Anvil cliffs, abandoned within living memory, whose shutters bang at night with the rhythm of a heartbeat.
place_lore.nirncraft.benirus_manor.manor:
^INVENTORY OF BENIRUS MANOR, taken at the instance of the Count's Receiver
^Sixteen chairs, two repairable. One harpsichord, silent. One portrait of a lady in green, the eyes unaccountably wet. One barrel of pickled herring, labelled in a childish hand as "for the Ghosts."
Remark of the notary: the herring was eaten, and the barrel has been refilled, since. I did not see by whom. I did not look. I left a copper by the door and was not robbed on the way home.
place_lore.nirncraft.benirus_manor.rumou: Gull the harbour-gull is said to nest on the Benirus roof. Sailors say the gull is the manor's last tenant and the only one who pays rent.
place_lore.nirncraft.benkongerike.barrow: A partial rubbing, taken in charcoal and much smudged. The script is old Nordic, cruder than mainland work. My reading: Here lie the sworn of the first landing, who came over the ice from Skyrim and found the island already spoken for. The rest, I think, lists who spoke for it and how many they had to kill. The door below is cut with a dragon's head, its mouth sealed with iron. I did not try the door. I have more sense than skalds.
place_lore.nirncraft.benkongerike.hook: A Nordic barrow sunk into the snow north of the Headwaters of Harstrad. The Skaal call it the House That Coughs, for the wind that blows out of its door, and they will not camp in its sight.
place_lore.nirncraft.benkongerike.rumour: Benkongerike? A Thirsk skald went in there last moon to sing the dead to sleep. Said they deserved a song. The dead didn't agree, apparently.
place_lore.nirncraft.benkongerike.skald_:
~Sleep, old jarls, in your house of stone,
~The ships are burnt and the songs are gone.
~I bring you one, a little late:
~Lie down, lie down, and shut the gate.

Orm's hand, on the back, much shakier: They do not want lullabies. They want the names of the men who buried them, and I do not know the names. The one in the iron crown keeps asking. I have started making names up. He knows.

The last lines are barely legible: He has stopped asking. He has started singing. He has a better voice than I do, which is the cruellest thing of all. If any Thirsk folk find this, tell Brenna I owed her for two casks, and tell her I am sorry.

place_lore.nirncraft.bilegulch_mine.exil:
Mother,
We are not dead. That is the news. Father still thinks leaving the stronghold was the right thing and he still will not say why. The iron here is good and the hills are full of Nords who pay for it with sour faces.

There is a troll in the deep shaft now. It took my leg below the knee. I have made a new one from pine and it is better than the old one in some ways, it does not get cold. Do not come. Do not worry. Both are useless, I know. Your son, Ugrak.
place_lore.nirncraft.bilegulch_mine.hook: An Orcish mine in the western hills, worked by exiles from the strongholds who dig iron and fight anyone who comes to look at it. Something in the lower shaft fights them back.
place_lore.nirncraft.bilegulch_mine.ore_:
Sun's Height: 32 loads iron. 4 loads to Falkreath smith for salt and arrows. Rest kept.
Last Seed: 28 loads. Ugrak's leg broken. Lower shaft cracked into a cave.
Hearthfire: 9 loads. Lower shaft closed. Old Blackhide lives in the crack now, the troll with the white scar. Took Ugrak's other leg. Took Old Mother Bilek's pick, the founder's pick, from where it hung by the shaft.

That pick dug the first stone of this mine. Without it hanging there we are not a clan, only orcs in a hole. Any who brings it back eats at our fire and is not an outsider. I write that here so no one may say later I did not.
place_lore.nirncraft.bilegulch_mine.rumo: Orcs at Bilegulch Mine sell good iron cheap, if you can get them to talk to you. They lost their founder's pick to something down the deep shaft, and they don't speak of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.bilegulch_mine.sk4_: Folio #9 (-1555, 521): Field inspection recorded for Bilegulch Mine within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #9 for bilegulch_mine: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Bilegulch Mine are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
An arched stone pack-bridge spanning a leaf-strewn ravine in the heart of the Rift's golden birch woods.
Keep your hand on your purse when crossing Birch Basin Bridge; highwaymen love to wait under the stone arch.

Folio #62 (880, 1800): Field inspection recorded for Birch Basin Bridge within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #62 for birch_basin_bridge: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Birch Basin Bridge are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Cleared a brushwood barricade from the northern approach of the bridge at dawn and drove three cutpurses into the bracken. Carters hauling mead from Riften should travel in pairs until the autumn fair is over.
place_lore.nirncraft.black_briar_lodge.g:
My name is Corvus Tullian, clerk of the Imperial customs at Riften. I counted the crates going in and out of Lost Prospect Mine and they don't match the ore tallies. I said so to the wrong person.

If I am not on the Imperial rolls next spring, someone should look in the mine. There's no ore in those crates. Never was.
place_lore.nirncraft.black_briar_lodge.h: A hunting lodge in the eastern woods that belongs to the Black-Briar family. Its doors are always locked, its guards are always awake, and the wagons that leave it at night never carry game.
place_lore.nirncraft.black_briar_lodge.l:
The guest arriving on the 20th is to be fed, watered and kept from the windows. He is not to be harmed. He is also not to leave. If he asks why, tell him the roads are unsafe. That is true.

The cellar crates from Lost Prospect go to the meadery by the lake road, not the Greenwall road. I will not pay Brannoc's toll on my own goods.
Burn this when read. I mean it, Hrolfdir. The last keeper did not burn his, and you are the new keeper.
place_lore.nirncraft.black_briar_lodge.r: Black-Briar Lodge? I'd not go knocking. The Briar sends people up there who are never seen in Riften again. Some of them are guests. Some aren't.
place_lore.nirncraft.black_briar_lodge.s: Folio #12 (2824, 1428): Field inspection recorded for Black Briar Lodge within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.black_lacquer_pagod:
#THE BELLS
First tier: Patience, which rings at dawn. Second: Doubt, which rings at noon. Third: Resolve, which has not rung in a hundred years. Fourth through sixth: lost. Seventh: Return, which rings only for the one who returns.
Pencilled below: 'The seventh rang last night. Nobody had returned. I went up with a lamp. The bell was still swinging. On the floor, a single wet footprint, small and bare, pointing inward.'
A seven-tiered pagoda of black lacquer on a bluff of the Tsaesci coast, whose eaves are hung with bells that ring only when no one is near to hear.
The Black Lacquer Pagoda is said to have an eighth tier, above the roof, that is only visible at dusk, and which is used by someone who has never come down.
