Morning: Gunnhild on the stairs. Afternoon: Bersi on the stairs. Night: whoever lost at dice.
NOBODY goes past the second hall. Not for loot, not on a dare. Arvid went past the second hall. Ask Arvid how that went. You can't. That's the point.
Food runs to Riverwood on Tirdas and Fredas. Don't use the main road, use the goat path past Anise's cabin. And leave the old woman alone, she gives me the shivers.

One more thing. Arvid's letter for his sister is in the chest by the fire. Somebody take it down to Riverwood next food run and leave it at her door. Don't knock, don't explain. Just leave it. We're bandits, not animals.
An ancient Nord temple crowning the peak above Riverwood, its stone arches visible for miles. Grave robbers, bandits and worse have all tried their luck on its stairs.

Dagny,
I know you said not to. I know. But the bandits at the top have got careless and half of them are drinking, and there is a door inside that nobody has opened, with rings of stone on it and animals carved where the keyhole ought to be. Where there is a fancy door there is treasure behind it.

I am writing this from the first hall. It is cold and there are skeevers and the dead are laid out in rows on the shelves like loaves at the market. I will be home before the Riverwood mill stops turning. Put the kettle on. Do not tell Mother. Arvid.
Every summer some fool from Riverwood climbs to Bleak Falls Barrow to get rich. The last one sent his sister a letter from the top. That's the last she heard of him.

place_lore.nirncraft.bleakcoast_cave.hoo: A cave in the sea cliffs east of the College where a great white sabre cat makes its den. Winterhold's best hunter went after it at Frostfall and did not return.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakcoast_cave.hun:
#1st of Frostfall
Tracked her again. White coat, white as fresh snow, one ear torn. Biggest cat I have seen in forty winters of hunting. She took three of Ranmir's goats and a dog. The Jarl will pay ten septims a tooth.

#4th of Frostfall
Found her den in the cliff cave by the sea. Bones everywhere: seals, horkers, a man's boot with the foot still in it. She was not home. I left my mark on the wall and went back for more arrows.

#5th of Frostfall
Going in tonight with my grandfather's bow, Frostsinger. If I do not come back, the bow stays with me. Let whoever kills her have it.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakcoast_cave.rum: Bleakcoast Cave belongs to the white cat now. Old Grunnar went in with his bow and the cat came out wearing his hat. Well, near enough.

place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_basin.gia: Watched the basin from the rocks for three days. Two giants, one old, one young. Four mammoths. One cow, ours, Brindle, standing by the fire like she was born there.

The young giant scratches Brindle behind the ears every morning. The old one milks the mammoths and gives the young one the first bowl. They are kinder to each other than half the families in Whiterun.

I still want my cow back. But I don't want to fight for her. There must be another way. Giants like cheese, the old herders say. Maybe a trade.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_basin.hoo: A wide stony basin west of Whiterun where giants herd their mammoths beside a smouldering fire. They want to be left alone, and they mostly are.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_basin.rum: Giants at Bleakwind Basin. Leave them be and they'll leave you be. Unless you're a cow from Pelagia Farm, apparently. Ask Gunnvor over there about it.

place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_bluff.gue:
Scratched on hide with a burnt twig:
The Rorikstead peddler. Soft. For the pot.
The Orc from Dushnikh Yal. Hard. For the briar.
The Nord girl with the moonstone ring from Soljund's Sinkhole. Pretty. For the trade to Blind Cliff Cave.
The old man from Lund's Hut. Stringy. Let him go, nobody wants him.
Under the list: Lund's man went home and told the others. Good. Let them know the bluff is ours. Let them be afraid on the road to Rorikstead.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_bluff.hoo: A windswept rise crowned with a Forsworn tower, where a hagraven keeps a garden of thorns and a cage full of what she calls guests.
place_lore.nirncraft.bleakwind_bluff.rum: Wind never stops on Bleakwind Bluff. You'd think that'd blow the stink of the crone's pot away. It doesn't.

place_lore.nirncraft.blind_cliff_cave.ai: My mother sold me to Ulvra Ash-Tongue for a briar. She thinks it is an honour. On the dark of the moon they will do the becoming and I will not be Aiwen anymore.

I have woven this into my ribbon and thrown it out the smoke hole. If the wind is kind, someone will find it near the Lover Stone, where my Nord boy used to wait for me. Tell him not to come. Tell anyone else to come with fire. The crone keeps the rite-knife on her belt. Without it there is no becoming.
place_lore.nirncraft.blind_cliff_cave.be:
The ash from a willing heart. The feather from an old mother. The knife that was bathed in the Karth when the moon was drowned.
She must not be willing in the mouth. She must be willing in the blood. The girl Aiwen is unwilling in the mouth and that is better, her anger feeds the feathers.
After the becoming, take her to Dead Crone Rock to learn the songs. The sisters there will teach her to sing a Nord off a cliff.
place_lore.nirncraft.blind_cliff_cave.ho: A cave in the cliffs south of Karthwasten, where the hagravens of the Reach perform their darkest rite: turning a living woman into one of their own.
place_lore.nirncraft.blind_cliff_cave.ru: Blind Cliff Cave belongs to the crones. They take Reachwomen in there and what comes out has feathers. Don't you look at me like that, it's true.
place_lore.nirncraft.blind_cliff_cave.sk: Folio #28 (-2563, -491): Field inspection recorded for Blind Cliff Cave within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.blizzard_rest.hook: A giant camp on the open snowfields of the Pale, close enough to Heljarchen Hall that the new homesteaders can hear the mammoths grumbling at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.blizzard_rest.lorei:
Steward,
Poachers are cutting tusks off the mammoths at Blizzard Rest and the giants are coming down to the road looking for whoever did it. Yesterday one of them sat on my fence. It is no longer a fence.

Hang the poachers or pay for my fence, I do not mind which. Preferably both.
V. Loreius

^Postscript
Also, one of the giants has taken to leaving a mammoth's tooth on my doorstep every morning. I do not know whether this is an apology or a threat. My wife says it is a courtship. I would like the Steward's opinion on all three possibilities, in writing.
place_lore.nirncraft.blizzard_rest.poach: Wanted: mammoth tusk, whole, unbroken, at least six feet. Price: two hundred septims per pair, delivered to the back door of the alchemist's in Windhelm. No questions asked. No answers given.

Advice from the buyer: the herd at Blizzard Rest has an old cow with the best ivory in the Pale. The giants are slow in the cold. Strike at dawn, cut fast, run downhill.
^Scrawled beneath in another hand: Erik tried it. Erik is now part of the snowfield.
place_lore.nirncraft.blizzard_rest.rumou: The giants at Blizzard Rest are calm enough if you leave their mammoths be. The trouble is, somebody hasn't been leaving their mammoths be.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloated_mans_grotto:
~Father of the chase, I came with bow strung,
~I came with knife sharp, I came alone.
~If I am the hunter, guide my arrow.
~If I am the hunted, let me run well.

Cut into a gnarled root beside the pool, the letters small and neat in the Bosmeri style, with a single dried bloodstain at the end of the last line.
Beneath the carving someone has hung a small bundle of feathers and a wolf's tooth on a string. Hunters who know the grotto say a Bosmer comes every Hearthfire to add one tooth to the string. Nobody has asked what happens when the string is full.
A secluded grotto north of Lake Ilinalta, lush and warm and strangely silent, where hunters of men and beasts alike come to settle old scores.

#12th of Frostfall
Tracked the great wolf up from the lake for two days. Prints twice the size of my hand, and they changed partway, the claws going long and the heel coming down like a man's. I have followed many beasts. I have never followed one that changed its mind about what it was.

#13th of Frostfall
The trail ends in the grotto. It is warm in here, green and wet, and the pool is very still. Something has been feeding. The bones are cracked for marrow. I hear breathing in the ferns and it is patient. I am going to stop writing now and nock an arrow. Hircine, if this is your hunt, at least let it be a fair one.
Bloated Man's Grotto? Pretty place. Got its name from what the hunters found floating in the pool the first time anyone went in. Werewolves, some say. Worse, say others.

place_lore.nirncraft.bloodlet_throne.cap:
Wife,
We never reached the glade. They took us on the road below the fortress, at dusk, with no more noise than wind. There are perhaps a dozen of them. The one they call Lady Arnvor is the oldest, and she likes to talk. She has asked me what I miss most, three nights running, and written down my answers.

If this reaches Falkreath, give it to Bailiff Eirik. Tell him the cells are under the great hall, and that the creatures sleep in the eastern tower from dawn until the sun is well down. Tell him to come by day. Tell our son I was not afraid. That is a lie. Tell him anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodlet_throne.cou:
By the will of Lady Arnvor:
No kill on the road within sight of Falkreath's walls. The town must think it is wolves.
No kill of Legion soldiers by more than one in a season. The Legion counts.
The Stormcloaks may pass freely. They are good for the war, and the war is good for us: graves are dug faster than anyone can watch them.

Postscript, in the same elegant hand: 'The Lady reminds her court that the Dawnguard has a fort in the Rift and long memories. Let Haemar's Shame take their attention. We are patient. We will outlast the war, the Dawnguard, and the Empire, if we are careful with our appetites.'
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodlet_throne.hoo: A grim fortress on the high pass south of Falkreath, held by a vampire court that takes its tithe in blood from the travellers of the Pale Pass road.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodlet_throne.rum: Bloodlet Throne. They don't rob you, the ones up there. They count you. They count everyone who uses that road, and every so often, the count comes up short.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodlet_throne.tit:
Tithe for the season of Hearthfire, taken from the Pale Pass road:
One carter of Helgen, a refugee, fed upon.
Two pilgrims bound for the Ancestor Glade, kept.
One Legion courier, kept. His dispatches burned unread.
The miller's boy from the Half-Moon road, fed upon and returned, for kindness costs little and buys silence.

To the master of Haemar's Shame: our offer stands. You have the Rift's thin, sour blood. We have Falkreath's, sweet with pine and grief. Trade with us, or do not. But do not lecture us about the Dawnguard. The Dawnguard is far away, and we are very old.

place_lore.nirncraft.bloodskal_barrow.ho: A Nordic barrow north of Raven Rock, cut with red-stained stone. Grave robbers have been digging there by torchlight, and Raven Rock's own ancestral urns have started turning up in their sacks.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodskal_barrow.re: To the Councilor. Five urns are missing from the ancestral tomb, one of them from your own family's niche. The thieves came through the drainage cut on the west wall. Tracks lead north toward Bloodskal Barrow. I recommend that we send a party of four. I recognise that we do not have four to spare, and that the Bulwark comes first. I will therefore ask outsiders, and I will keep the matter quiet, as you will wish. Indaram.

Appended in the Councilor's own hand: Do what you think best, Sergeant. Bring my grandmother home. I will not ask how. I will not ask who. I will ask only that she be home before the Feast of the Dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodskal_barrow.ro:
From the town tomb: four urns, decent glaze, one cracked. Sell to the Khajiit at the docks, who will sell to some fool in Cyrodiil who thinks Dunmer ashes are a cure for gout.
One urn of the Morvayn line, silver-banded. Keep that one apart. The Councilor's family will pay to get it back quietly, and pay more to keep it quiet.

From the barrow itself: copper, bronze, rotten furs, two Nord swords, one of them good. The rest of the deep rooms are sealed with a red stone door that won't open for any lever we've found. Henrik says it hums. Henrik is drunk. Leave the deep rooms alone.
place_lore.nirncraft.bloodskal_barrow.ru: Grave robbers at Bloodskal Barrow. The Guard says they've been stealing urns out of our own tomb in town and stashing them in the barrow before shipping out. Stealing a Dunmer's ancestors. There's no lower thing.
place_lore.nirncraft.bogmother.hook: A fetid root-cave and hag-lair where a mother-of-bog spawns, with walls of knotted root and a dripping ceiling.
place_lore.nirncraft.bogmother.rumour: Something big has been laying in the swamp lately. The hunters won't go past the bend.
place_lore.nirncraft.bogmother.web.p0: Do not go near the bend. Her spawn come in clutches of nine now, where it was three. She is enraged, and she has cause. Whoever put the pipe through her ceiling should be fed to the next clutch. I will not go in. I have children.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonechill_passage.h: An icy cave in the Jerall foothills where the cold never lifts, even in high summer. Bears den in its mouth and older things sleep deeper in the ice.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonechill_passage.m:
Scratched into the frozen stone near the deepest point, in angular old runes:
'We dug for the frost-iron that sings when struck. The mountain struck back. Here lie Harek, Ingjald and Thorgest. The cold keeps us. Do not wake us with your fire.'
The ice before the marks is melted in a hand-sized patch, as if someone has recently pressed a torch to it.

To one side, in a newer, shakier hand: 'Somebody has been here with a torch. The ice is weeping. If you lit that torch, put it out and go. The one with his eyes open moved his hand. I saw it. I am Bodvar Frost-Ear and I do not lie about ice.'
place_lore.nirncraft.bonechill_passage.r: Bonechill Passage keeps meat fresh all year, so the trappers say. Keeps other things fresh too. Ask the one who found the man frozen standing up.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonechill_passage.s: Folio #34 (-275, 1325): Field inspection recorded for Bonechill Passage within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.bonechill_passage.t:
#Evening Star
The bear sow is back in the outer cave with two cubs. I will set my lines further in, past the ice fall, where nothing lives.
#Next day
I was wrong about nothing living past the ice fall. There is a man in the ice. Standing. Old Nord armour, pick in his hand, eyes open. He must have been there since the Merethic, by the look of the steel.

#Later
I could swear his eyes were turned toward the left when I came, and to the right when I left. I am not a fanciful man. I am leaving my traps. They can have them.

place_lore.nirncraft.bonestrewn_crest.ad:
#18th of Frostfall
Camped below Bonestrewn Crest with Arvel and the twins. The giants at Steamcrag say a dragon came in Hearthfire and took the crest for its own. They call it a word I cannot spell. Arvel says it sounded like 'Sahqovul'. Arvel is guessing.

#19th of Frostfall
We went up at dawn. The dragon was asleep on a bed of mammoth tusks. Arvel said we could take it sleeping. The twins agreed. I agreed. We were all very brave at dawn.

#19th, later
Arvel is ash. The twins ran. My leg is broken and I am writing this under a mammoth's ribcage. It knows I am here. It is waiting until it is hungry.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonestrewn_crest.ho: A wind-scoured crest south of Witchmist Grove littered with the cracked bones of mammoths and men, where a dragon has made its roost and the giants no longer dare to graze.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonestrewn_crest.ru: You can see the bones on Bonestrewn Crest from the Darkwater road. Mammoth ribs, mostly. Some that aren't. And something big circling up there at dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.bonestrewn_crest.sh: Deep gouges in the boulder at the crest's peak, too regular to be accident. Someone who knew the dragon tongue has scratched a translation beside them in charcoal:

'I am Sahqovul. The crest is mine. The bones are my count. Come and be counted.'

Beneath, in a different hand: 'Thirty-one tallies. I have stopped adding to them. There is no room.'

And at the very bottom, scratched with a broken arrowhead: 'Arvel, the twins, and me. Make it thirty-four. If anyone kills it, cut one more mark, for us.'

place_lore.nirncraft.boulderfall_cave.ap:
#16th of Frostfall
The Magister says the dead feel nothing. I believed her until tonight, when the drowned man from Riften opened his eyes on the table and looked at me. Not at her. At me.

#17th of Frostfall
I could leave. The road to Riften is a day's walk. But the Magister keeps my name in her ledger and my lock of hair in her box, and she says that means wherever I go, she'll find me. I don't think she's lying. I wish I'd stayed in the Ratway.
place_lore.nirncraft.boulderfall_cave.co:
#Received, Frostfall
From the Riften supplier, by cart via the lake road: three adult males (drowned, fresh), one adult female (fever, poor), one child (refused, returned with a rebuke).
Paid: 150 septims and a lesser soul gem, filled.

The supplier is a junior attendant at the Hall of the Dead who thinks Arkay will not notice. Arkay notices. That is rather the point of the exercise.

Sister Hrolfa at Ruunvald is to receive the strongest frames. The rest stay here for study. Note: the Shor's Stone men will not stop asking after their own. Discourage the asking.
place_lore.nirncraft.boulderfall_cave.ho: A cave in the boulder-strewn hills west of Fort Greenwall where the snow lingers into spring. Necromancers have made it a workshop, and corpses go in by the cartload.
place_lore.nirncraft.boulderfall_cave.ru: Grave robbers, I heard. Up by Boulderfall. Someone's buying bodies from the Hall of the Dead in Riften, and it's not for burying.
place_lore.nirncraft.boulderfall_cave.sk: Folio #37 (1999, 969): Field inspection recorded for Boulderfall Cave within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #37 for boulderfall_cave: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Boulderfall Cave are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

place_lore.nirncraft.brandy_mug_farm.hoo: A small farm on the road south of Windhelm, owned by a pair of friends who started it on a bet and have kept it going on stubbornness and very strong drink.
place_lore.nirncraft.brandy_mug_farm.req:
To whoever reads complaints in that great cold Palace,
On the 6th of Frostfall a patrol of your men came through and requisitioned four casks of our cider, two hams, and a wheel of goat cheese 'in the name of Skyrim'. I asked which part of Skyrim. They said the hungry part.

I am loyal to Ulfric. I am also loyal to my ledger, and my ledger is starving. If the Jarl wishes to fight the Empire on my cider, the Jarl may pay for my cider. 60 septims will do. 80 if he wants me to stop writing these.
^Bolfrida, who is not leaving this alone
place_lore.nirncraft.brandy_mug_farm.rum: Brandy-Mug Farm? They brew a cider out there that'll take the frost out of your toes and the sense out of your head. Stormcloaks keep 'buying' it without paying.

place_lore.nirncraft.bravil.hook: A river town of leaning shacks and skooma dens around the statue of the Lucky Old Lady, where the Niben's fog hides smugglers, dream-sellers and the shrines of madness and ruin just beyond the walls.
place_lore.nirncraft.bravil.old_lady_pra:
~Old Lady, Lucky Lady, turn your face my way,
~Keep my hull above the water, keep the watch at bay,
~Keep my boy from Senchal sugar, keep my man from dice,
~And if you can't keep both of them, at least keep one of them twice.

Old Lady, it's me again. You turned east last night and the river men are betting that means a flood. I've put my last two drakes on 'no flood'. If you could see your way to staying dry, I'd light you a candle every Loredas till I die, and I've never once lied to you, except about the candles.
place_lore.nirncraft.bravil.rumour: Bravil's no worse than any river town, it's just more honest about it. If you hear a fellow by the bridge selling sleep, keep walking. If you hear one selling buttons, walk faster.
place_lore.nirncraft.bravil.watch_report: Patrol to the Dagon shrine at dusk, as ordered. Nine persons in red hoods, keeping a fire. One woman giving a sermon about 'the world unmade and made honest'. They called her Cassia. They did not appear to fear us. We appeared to fear them, which I regret.

On the way back we passed the Mad God's stones and found a soup tureen full of buttons on the altar. Constable Vibia took a button. Constable Vibia now speaks only in rhyme. I am requesting hazard pay, a priest, and a new constable.

place_lore.nirncraft.brinewater_grotto.h: A sea cave in the cliffs north of Solitude, its mouth hidden at high tide. Wreckers signal from it on moonless nights, and the cargo of drowned ships finds its way inside.
place_lore.nirncraft.brinewater_grotto.r: Brinewater Grotto? Smugglers have used it since my grandfather's day. But smugglers wait for ships to come to them. This new lot makes the ships come.
place_lore.nirncraft.brinewater_grotto.s:
MARCUS OF THE SILVER GULL
WE STRUCK ON THE 9TH. SIX OF US CAME ASHORE. THEY WERE WAITING ON THE ROCKS WITH CLUBS. I AM THE LAST. THEY SAY THEY WILL SELL ME TO VARO TO ROW HIS BOATS.

IF YOU READ THIS, TELL MY WIFE IN THE SOLITUDE DOCK HOUSES I DID NOT DROWN. TELL HER IT WAS NOT THE SEA. TELL THE COMPANY IT WAS NOT THE SEA.
THE OLD LAMP MAN IS IN THE BACK CAVE WITH ME NOW. HE SAYS HIS BRASS GLASS IS IN HROAR'S CHEST. HE SAYS IF ANYONE COMES WE ARE TO SHOUT. WE WILL SHOUT.

Signals from the grotto mouth:
Three short, one long: lamp is dark, ships may come in.
Two long: Company boat on the water, everyone below.
One lantern swung in a circle: Varo's men at Broken Oar to row out for the haul.

Watches: Ingrid and the Khajiit at the mouth, Sven on the cliff path, me with the haul. Nobody touches the wine from the Silver Gull. It's sold already, to a man in Solitude who doesn't like his casks opened.
The old lightkeeper came sniffing yesterday with a hammer. He's in the back cave now with a sore head and a good view of his own lens. Keep him alive. A dead keeper means a new keeper, and a new keeper might not scare.
place_lore.nirncraft.bristleback_cave.bo: Painted in red ochre by some passing hunter: SOWS WITH YOUNG INSIDE. They will not run. They will not stop. If you hear grunting, you are already too close. Rolf's sledge is at the bottom of the gully if anyone wants it. Rolf does not.

Underneath, in charcoal, a second hand: Rolf went in on the twelfth of Evening Star with a torch and a boar-spear and his best hides on his back. He always said the hides were worth it. If you find a fur pack with a red thong on it, it was his. Leave it. The sows have made a nest of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.bristleback_cave.ho: A cave in the northwestern hills where the island's bristlebacks den through the worst of the winter. A trapper made it his larder; the boars have made him part of theirs.
place_lore.nirncraft.bristleback_cave.ru: Bristleback Cave? Old Rolf Hide-Seller set his snares there every winter. Third winter running he came back with a full sledge. This winter the sledge came back alone.
place_lore.nirncraft.bristleback_cave.tr:
#Sun's Dusk
Snares set along the gully, twelve of them. Two bristlebacks taken, good hides, bad tempers. Sold the tusks to the miners at Broken Tusk Mine, who think it is funny to hang them over their door. Funny until the rieklings came for the tusks too.

#Evening Star
Something has been at the snares before me. Not a boar. Not a bear. It ate the bait, the boar, and the snare, and left the stake chewed to splinters. I am going deeper to see what it is. The hides are worth it. The hides are always worth it, until they aren't.
place_lore.nirncraft.brodir_grove.appren:
For the master's preparation, gather at Brodir Grove:
Bark from the eldest tree, three palms' width. Sap, one phial. Moss from the north face, as much as will fill a pouch.
The master says the spriggans will not mind. The master has not been to Brodir Grove in thirty years. Bring a fire spell. Bring two. If the trees start singing, do not stop to listen, it is not a compliment.
At the bottom, in a hurried hand: Gathered the bark. The eldest tree screamed. Ran. Left the sickle. Left one boot. If the master wants the moss, the master can come and get it himself.
place_lore.nirncraft.brodir_grove.hook: A grove of ancient trees in the ash wastes north of Raven Rock, one of the few green places left in the south. The spriggans here have grown restless since Telvanni gatherers came with sickles.
place_lore.nirncraft.brodir_grove.rumour: Brodir Grove used to be a nice place for a picnic. Then some Telvanni apprentices came cutting bark for their master's potions, and now the trees walk.
place_lore.nirncraft.brodir_grove.skaal_: A twist of birch bark tucked into the roots of the eldest tree, with a few dried berries and a lock of hair. The words cut in the bark: Grandmother Tree, forgive the sickle-men. They do not know the All-Maker made you before he made them. We have brought you water from the Headwaters of Harstrad and a song. Be patient with them. Be patient with us. We will be gone before you are.

Tied with the bark, a twist of red wool and a second strip, more recent: The Telvanni sickle-man came back. He left his own offering this time: a phial of good wine and a note in his tongue. We cannot read it, but the tree let him go, so it must have been an apology.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_fang_cave.ho: A cave mouth like a snapped tooth in the hills west of Whiterun. Travellers on the road nearby have been vanishing at dusk, and the Vigilants of Stendarr have taken an interest.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_fang_cave.ru: Broken Fang Cave. Folk who camp near it wake up tired and pale, if they wake up at all. A Vigilant came asking about it last week, all grey robes and grim looks.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_fang_cave.sk: Folio #38 (-1121, 119): Field inspection recorded for Broken Fang Cave within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #38 for broken_fang_cave: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Broken Fang Cave are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_fang_cave.tr:
#Morndas
Camped by the road near a cave shaped like a broken tooth. A kind man in a fine coat shared his fire and asked a great many questions about who would be expecting me in Whiterun. Nobody, I told him. He smiled at that.

#Tirdas
So tired. Slept until noon and woke with a sore neck. The kind man is still here. He says I should rest another day. His fire never seems to need wood.
#Middas
I cannot remember Tirdas night. There are two small marks on my neck. I think I should leave. I think I should leave now.
Brother,
The captain won't send men to the Hollow. Says it's out of our way, says the Briar would rather we kept to the city. You know what that means as well as I do.

I'm going on my own on my day off. If I don't come back, don't come after me. Mother's buried one son to this hold already. Get out of the guard, Torbjorn. Get out of Riften. There's nothing left here worth guarding.

#The Wall, as of Frostfall
14 iron. 3 steel. 1 Imperial with the red plume still on it. 2 Stormcloak, with blue paint. 1 Riften guard, purple, with a big dent over the left eye where I got him.

The Riften one's my favourite. He begged and then he stopped begging and swung at me, which I respect. His brother's in the guard too. I hope he comes. I've left a nail for him.
Rule of the Hollow: whoever brings in a new helm drinks first. Whoever loses theirs, goes on the wall.
A cave in the south-eastern hills that the bandits inside have decorated with the helmets of everyone they have killed. The walls are getting crowded.
Broken Helm Hollow, they call it, on account of all the helmets they nail up. My cousin's in the Riften guard. His brother's helm is up there. He knows the dent in it.

Folio #47 (2723, 1617): Field inspection recorded for Broken Helm Hollow within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #47 for broken_helm_hollow: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Broken Helm Hollow are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_limb_camp.ca: A low cairn of river stones beside the giants' pool, too small for a man, and on its top stone a mammoth's milk-tooth set in a hollow, surrounded by handprints in red clay: one large hand, pressed again and again, as though someone had not known how to stop.
Around the cairn the snow is trodden flat in a perfect circle, as if something enormous has walked around it every night since.
Wedged between two stones, half-hidden, lies a broken spear-shaft with a Mixwater Mill timber-brand burned into the wood, and a twist of rope of the kind the mill's carters use to lash their loads.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_limb_camp.ho: A giants' camp on the hills south of Mixwater Mill, where a one-tusked giant has started smashing log carts on the river road, and the mill wants it dead without saying why.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_limb_camp.po:
Brother,
You owe me five septims. I told you we would get a mammoth before you got a wife. Gralfr, Hroald and I took a calf by the Broken Limb pools on the 12th of Frostfall. Gralfr says the tusks will sell in Windhelm for more than a season's timber.
The big one with the single tusk came roaring after us, but we were across the river before it reached the bank. It stood in the water and howled. Gralfr laughed at it.
Two days later it found the river road. I am not laughing now. Gralfr says we tell nobody about the calf. Gralfr says a bounty is cheaper than the truth.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_limb_camp.ru: The giant at Broken Limb Camp's been smashing carts. Gralfr at the mill put a bounty on it. Funny, though: it never touched a cart in ten years before Frostfall.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_limb_camp.sk: Folio #24 (1457, 109): Field inspection recorded for Broken Limb Camp within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #24 for broken_limb_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Broken Limb Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_oar_grotto.h: A smugglers' den on the far northern shore, where a stolen ship lies moored inside the sea cave. Captain Varo's crew buys what the wreckers steal and sails it where the Company can't follow.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_oar_grotto.r: Rhosen Varo was a Company captain once. Then the Company docked his pay for a lost cargo, and now he takes every cargo he can find to even the account.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_oar_grotto.s:
Silver Gull wine, 18 casks: sold to the A. in Solitude at 40 the cask. Our share 480.
Raw ebony, Orphan's Tear salvage, 6 bars: held. Too easy to trace.
Skooma, Dainty Sload, 20 crates: buyer in Dawnstar, buyer in Windhelm, half to the Riften men. Pending.

Bribes this quarter: dock clerk 60, gate guard 15, the keeper of the Castle Dour keys 100 and a cask.
We have more coin than we have ever had, and the men are restless. Rich crews want to go home. I told them: one more season. One more season is what my old captain told me, the year the Company took everything.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_oar_grotto.v:
Lads,
The Sload's twenty crates come ashore the next dark night. Brinewater rows them to us, we pay Hroar his third and not a copper more. If he complains, remind him who owns the only ship on this coast that can outrun a Company cutter.

Nobody fights the Legion. Nobody fights the Thalmor. We are businessmen, and dead businessmen pay no shares. If a Company boat finds us, you surrender, you weep, you name Hroar. I'll have you out of the Castle Dour cells in a week; the clerk who keeps the keys drinks our wine.
And somebody feed the rowers from the Silver Gull. They're no use to me starved.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_tower_redoub:
Cut deep into the wood with a stone knife, in rough Tamrielic so that Nord captives can read it:
THIS TOWER WAS REACH BEFORE IT WAS NORD. IT WILL BE REACH AFTER.
KAELIN THORN-CHEST SITS HERE. HIS HEART IS IN A HAGRAVEN'S JAR AT DEEPWOOD. KILL HIM AND HE STANDS UP AGAIN, ASK THE NORDS WHO TRIED.

Below, in charcoal, in a different and shakier hand:
I tried. He stood up again. But he was slower the second time. Aim for the briar. - H.

A shattered Nordic fort in the middle Reach, its broken tower crowned with Forsworn totems. The Briarheart who rules it keeps Nord captives, and the miners of Karthwasten hear their names shouted from the walls.

Bergljot, if this ever reaches you. I am not a prisoner anymore, not the way you think. The Reachwoman who brought me water when I was in the cage is called Mairi. Her father died in Cidhna for a theft the Silver-Bloods made up.

I have seen what they are fighting for, and I have seen what we dig for, and I know who gets fat on it. I am not coming back to swing a pick for Thonar Silver-Blood's coin purse. Tell Mother I am alive. Tell her I am sorry. Do not send anyone. I mean it, sister. Do not send anyone.
The Forsworn at Broken Tower Redoubt took Bergljot's brother. They yell his name from the ridge at night just to watch Karthwasten flinch.

place_lore.nirncraft.broken_tusk_mine.fo:
#Frostfall
Iron, 40 measures. Silver, 6. One seam of black ice at the bottom gallery, which the Skaal say is stalhrim and is not ours to cut. Left it alone. Wages paid in full.
#Sun's Dusk
Iron, 22 measures. Rieklings seen on the ridge three times. Posted a watch.

#Evening Star
Rieklings in the bottom gallery. Fifteen at least. They came up through a crack we did not know was there. Torvi lost a finger. We ran. The claim stone with the Jarl's seal is still in the strongbox in the bottom gallery, and without it the Company will say the mine is anyone's. Whoever brings it back gets a share of the first year's iron.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_tusk_mine.ho: A Nord mine in the northwestern hills, named for the bristleback tusk nailed over its entrance. The miners fled when the rieklings came for the tusk, and stayed fled when the rieklings stayed.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_tusk_mine.ri: Scratched into the side of an ore cart, with pictures where the rieklings did not know the letters: Tusk, one (picture of tusk, very proud). Boots, four. Mead, none, angry face. Pick, six. Nord, zero, then crossed out and made into one, then crossed out again and made into zero. Pictures of the chief sitting on the cart and the other rieklings pushing. It appears to be a list of the mine's riches as the new owners understand them.

At the very bottom, beside a picture of a horker with a crown, someone has added a single Nordic word in a neat miner's hand: Hrefna. Whether it was the foreman herself, insulted at being left off, nobody has asked.
place_lore.nirncraft.broken_tusk_mine.ru: Broken Tusk Mine paid well until the rieklings moved in. Foreman Hrefna says they've built a throne out of ore carts. She wants it back. The mine, not the throne.
place_lore.nirncraft.bronze_water_cave.h: A cave by a coppery pool east of Nightgate Inn, home to a family of cave bears. The pool takes its colour from Dwemer metal washed down from the ruins above.
place_lore.nirncraft.bronze_water_cave.r: Bronze Water Cave? Bears. Just bears. Lots of bears. The water tastes of pennies, too.
place_lore.nirncraft.bronze_water_cave.t: Bronze Water: three bears this season, a sow and two yearlings, plus the old male who comes and goes. Do not set snares near the pool. The bears drink there at dusk and they do not like surprises.

Odd thing: the water is green-bronze because of Dwemer scrap washed down from the Great Lift. I found a cog the size of a shield at the bottom. The College would pay for it, maybe. If I can find a way to drag it out without being eaten.
Going north to the Driftshade hills next week to trap wolves. Better pelts up there.
place_lore.nirncraft.brood_cavern.alchem:
To gather in Brood Cavern:
Frostbite venom, 6 sacs (the paler the better).
Spider eggs, 12, unbroken.
Webbing, two good handfuls, for the wizard in Morthal, who will not say what for.

Annotation, written lower and shakier:
Have 4 sacs and 9 eggs. The mother is in the deepest chamber, white as frost and the size of a cart. She has my satchel. I dropped it climbing out of her web. My notes are in it, two years of them, every recipe. I am not going back. I am also not sleeping. If someone braver kills her and brings that satchel to me at Morthal, I will pay what I have, which is not much, and teach them what I know, which is a great deal.
place_lore.nirncraft.brood_cavern.hook: A web-choked cave in the hills south of Morthal where frostbite spiders breed in their hundreds. Alchemists pay well for what is inside, and widows pay for what the alchemists leave behind.
place_lore.nirncraft.brood_cavern.orothe:
To the Orotheim lads:
We agreed. You take the Rorikstead road, we take the cave. Stay out of Brood Cavern. The venom's ours to sell.

^Written beneath in another hand:
You can have it. We came to take the cave back and found the last lot of you hanging in the webs like washing. Our chief says no road toll in Skyrim is worth that. Keep your venom. Keep your spiders. Keep your faces, while you still have them.
There's a Dunmer alchemist's bag in there too, by the big white one. Anyone who wants it can fetch it. We don't.
place_lore.nirncraft.brood_cavern.rumour: Brood Cavern's full of spiders, big as dogs and some bigger. Alchemists go in for venom sacs. A lad from Morthal went for Falion and came back without his hair. Turned white overnight.
place_lore.nirncraft.brucas_leap_redoubt:
If you read this you are in the cage too, or you are the one who opens it. If you are in the cage: do not eat what they bring on the third day. If you are the one who opens it: the key is not on the chief, he is too clever. It is under the drum.
Gunnar of Karthwasten. Here since Second Seed. Still here.

Below that, a second hand, older and shakier:
Gunnar is gone. They took him on the third day. I did not eat what they brought. I am still here. The drum is by the falls, and the falls are loud enough to cover the sound of a key turning. If I get out I am going home to Karthwasten and never coming back past the river.
A Forsworn hideout built around a waterfall on the upper Karth, where the river leaps a cliff and the Reachmen watch every boat and bridge below.

Kept by the watcher at the falls, in the Reach tongue scratched with a thorn. Translated loosely: Four Nord boats down the river this moon. One carried silver. The silver went into the water when we struck. Let the river carry Nord silver to the sea. Let the sea choke on it.

Orc hunters passed by the west path, from Mor Khazgur. We did not strike. Orcs bleed and keep coming. The briar is not cheap, it is not to be spent on Orcs.
The Nords build their camp at Liar's Retreat way, blue cloaks. Let them. Blue cloaks or red cloaks, both stole the Reach.
That waterfall at Bruca's Leap? The Forsworn have a camp in it. You can hear the drums from the river, under the roar.

place_lore.nirncraft.bruma.chapel_notice: Brother Aurel, Chapel of the Nine

^By Order of the Countess
This house is the Chapel of the Eight Divines. Petitions to the Ninth are not to be spoken, written or left in the offering box. Petitions so left will be burned unread by the priest, for the protection of the petitioner.

To the faithful, from Brother Aurel: I burn them unread. I do. But some of you write very large, and the fire is slow, and Talos forgive me, I have learned the names of half your dead this winter.
And to whoever keeps leaving wolf-pelts on the altar: the Countess knows. Stop.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma.hook: A Nord town on the roof of Cyrodiil, all steep slate and woodsmoke, where the Pale Pass trade runs north and the Daedric stones in the nearby hills are busier than the chapel.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma.iron_ledger.p:
#Second Seed
40 iron bars, for Falkreath. Paid in fur.
12 crates 'salt fish', for Helgen. Not fish.
3 crossbows, broken down, for 'the cousin'. Paid in Stormcloak silver. Melt it before spending.

#Mid Year
Toll at the Pass went up again. Legion sergeant wants a cask of mead a week to look the other way. Cheaper than silver and he can't spend it in the Imperial City.
Note: Kjeld says the road past the Molag Bal stones is bad. Three carters gone this season. Send the wagons the long way, and never at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma.rumour: Bruma folk are Nords at heart and Imperials on paper. The paper's getting thin, if you take my meaning. Mind what you say about Ulfric in the Countess's hearing.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma_caverns.chand:
#Bruma, the second of Frostfall
To the Collector of Candles, Imperial City,
Sir, the beeswax you sent is mostly paraffin. My customers are Nords at heart, and a Nord can smell a cheat at forty paces. Three of them have told me so in language I would rather not set down.

Further, one black candle was found at the mouth of the caverns last week, still lit, with no trace of who carried it. I have my suspicions. I will not write them. I will say only that the Legion's courier does not pass this way as often as he should, and that the new Captain looks at the mountain as though it owed her money.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma_caverns.hook: A split in the Jerall foothills where Bruma's old smugglers hid from the Legion, and where something is said to hide from them.
place_lore.nirncraft.bruma_caverns.rumou: The caverns drain into the creek that turns the Mountain Smithy's wheel. Every winter the water runs red for a night. Brandt Ironsled says it is iron in the stone. Brandt Ironsled does not go up there.

place_lore.nirncraft.bthardamz.afflicted:
Written in something that is not quite paint:
THE TASKMASTER SEES THE ORDER IN THE MACHINE. THE DEEP FOLK SERVED NO ONE, SO THEY WERE ERASED. WE SERVE. WE ARE NOT ERASED. ROT IS ORDER. ROT IS ORDER.
Below it, small and frantic: Whoever wrote that came past my hiding place three times. They smell like a sickroom. I don't think they're scholars. F.

And under that, scratched with a stylus in a neat scholar's hand: Third pass today. One of them stopped by my pipe and sniffed, then walked on. Either they cannot smell a living man over their own sickness, or the Taskmaster's servants have no orders concerning lanky Bretons. I shall try not to give them any reason to write some.
place_lore.nirncraft.bthardamz.fennick_n: Fennick Aulus, assistant to Ancilia Varro

#Day 1
Mistress says copy the gate glyphs and come back. Easy. Copied the gate in a morning. But the door was open. Who leaves a Dwemer door open? Nobody leaves a Dwemer door open. I'll just look.

#Day 3
The spiders don't notice me if I stay still and hum. Discovered this by accident. The Lexicon fits the slot by the great hall door perfectly, which is surely meaningful.

#Day 6
The big one woke when the Lexicon turned in the slot. Steam everywhere. I've hidden in a pipe room with no food and a very sore ankle. The Lexicon is still in the slot by the great hall. Mistress will kill me. If the centurion doesn't first.
place_lore.nirncraft.bthardamz.hook: A sprawling Dwemer ruin in the northwest Reach, whose halls echo with the hiss of steam and the clatter of machines still guarding their makers' secrets.
place_lore.nirncraft.bthardamz.rumour: Some Breton scholar's assistant went into Bthardamz with a lexicon and never came out. His mistress in Markarth is offering good coin for the book. Not so much for the Breton.

Goatherds in the northern hills warm their hands by the Bthardamz Surface Vent in winter, though they run if the brass valves start clanking.

place_lore.nirncraft.bujolds_retreat.buj: To whoever lives here after me: I built this house to be away from Thirsk and its quarrels. It is a good house. The roof does not leak and the hearth draws well. Treat it kindly. If you are a quarreller yourself, go back to Thirsk. If you are worse than a quarreller, the house will know, and so will the Skaal, and so will I, wherever I have gone.

The ink is old, and beneath it a reaver has drawn a rude picture of a woman with a bucket on her head. Underneath that, in yet another hand, very small: The hearth does draw well. The roof does not leak. I am sorry, Bujold. I would leave if I could.
place_lore.nirncraft.bujolds_retreat.hoo: A Nord homestead on the eastern coast, abandoned by the family who built it and taken over by reavers. They raid the Skaal sledges and sell what they steal on the docks at Raven Rock.
place_lore.nirncraft.bujolds_retreat.rea:
Listen, you sea-lice. The Skaal don't fight. That's the beauty of it. They pray at you and walk off. So we take what we like off their sledges, and nobody in Raven Rock asks where the furs came from.
The mask stays here. Some Telvanni at Tel Mithryn will pay forty drakes for anything the Skaal think is holy. I'll sell it myself. Anyone who tries to sell it first gets to swim to Windhelm.

Watch the north path toward Gyldenhul Barrow. If a Skaal comes with a spear, run. If anyone else comes with a spear, kill them. If anyone comes with an axe and a hammer and a look in their eye, wake me up first.
place_lore.nirncraft.bujolds_retreat.rum: Reavers at Bujold's Retreat stole a Skaal hunting mask older than my village. The Skaal won't fight for it. Not their way, they say. I'd fight for my grandfather's face.

place_lore.nirncraft.camlorn.dawn_sermon: Brother Hugues of the Dawn Chapel

Points for Sundas: Camlorn remembers the year its dead would not stay buried. Our grandfathers did not drive them out with prayers to the Eight alone. Some of them walked to the bright stone south-east of the walls and asked a Lady of Light for help, and they got it.

Must not say that from the pulpit. The Vigilants are in town. Say instead: light is light, wherever it is lit. Say: the dead deserve rest and the living deserve courage. Say nothing of the knights who still kneel at that stone at sunrise. They know who they are.
place_lore.nirncraft.camlorn.hook: A proud Breton city of high walls and old ghosts in northern Glenumbra. Its merchants grow rich at a suspicious pace, and its priests of the dawn hunt what walks after dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.camlorn.merchant_le:
#Accounts for Sun's Height, 4E 201
Salt from Daggerfall, 60 barrels: 480 septims. Wine sold to the Camlorn garrison: 1,120 septims. Repairs to the warehouse roof: 35 septims. Profit beyond all reasonable expectation, for the fourth month running.

Paid to the gentleman with the dog, at the stones east of the city: nothing yet.
Owed to the gentleman with the dog: one thing I do not value.
The dog says I will know what it is when it is gone. I asked if he meant the horse. The dog laughed. I did not know dogs could laugh. Lisette has stopped singing in the mornings. I am sure it is a cold.
place_lore.nirncraft.camlorn.rumour: Camlorn folk will tell you their city's haunted. Then they'll tell you which ghost, and what it wants, and how much the walk costs.

place_lore.nirncraft.castle_karstaag_rui: The ice-bound ruin of the frost giant Karstaag's hall, slain in the last age. Something has taken up his throne, and the cold coming off it can be felt from Mortrag Peak.

#14th of Evening Star
Camped below Mortrag Peak. The old Skaal story says Karstaag's bones lie in the castle with a crown of ice still on his skull. A crown of ice that never melts is worth a fortune to the right mage in Tel Mithryn.

#16th of Evening Star
The bones are not here. Something larger than a man dragged them deeper, and there are fresh tracks: wide, three-toed, with frost blooming in every print. Not Karstaag. His get, maybe. The Skaal say giants of the ice have long memories and longer children.

#17th
It sat on the old throne and watched me. It did not attack. I think it wanted me to leave something. My fingers do not work any more. Whoever finds this: the crown shard is in its fist.
The giant Karstaag died two hundred years ago, they say. So why are there giant tracks in the snow outside his castle, big as a cart and fresh as this morning?

Carved in the Skaal manner, with a frost-giant's hand cut beneath the words:
This was the hall of the cold king. He fell. His blood did not. Do not bring fire here, for the ice remembers burning. Do not take, for the ice remembers taking. Whoever sits the cold throne now is no friend to the All-Maker's children.

Beneath the giant hand, a second carving, newer and shallower: Eirik Snow-Born went past this stone in Evening Star seeking the crown of ice. We told him the crown is not a thing to be sold. He said everything is a thing to be sold. The stone is still here. Eirik is not.

place_lore.nirncraft.castle_volkihar.fer: TRAVELLER: the boat leaves when it leaves. Do not ring the bell after dark. Do not ring it twice. Do not ask the boatman his name; he has forgotten it, and it upsets him to be reminded.

If you have been invited to the castle, you will know. If you have not been invited, turn round and walk back to Solitude, and be grateful you have a long walk and a short memory. The castle remembers everyone.
The fishermen of Dragon Bridge have lost eleven people to that island since my father's time. Not one body has ever washed ashore. The sea gives back everything, sooner or later. It does not give back these.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_volkihar.hoo: A black castle on an island off the far north-west coast, wrapped in fog under a reddened sky. Sailors steer wide of it, and the ferryman at Icewater Jetty asks no questions of his passengers.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_volkihar.rum: Don't go asking about the castle in the fog. The ferryman at the Icewater Jetty takes people over. He never takes anyone back. He says they don't want to come back. He says it like it's a comfort.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_volkihar.thr:
~Mara, I was a fisherwife at Dragon Bridge.
~I was a mother of two, and I sang at the harvest.
~I am writing it down because I am forgetting.

~They feed from me on Morndas and on Fredas.
~On the other days I clean the great hall and do not look at the windows.
~If you cannot free me, Mara, then let me keep my children's names.
~Asta. Leif. Asta. Leif. Asta.

~The lord of the castle says that memory is a kindness he allows us.
~I do not want his kindness. I want my kitchen with the smoke in it.
~I want the bridge and the river and my mother's bad singing.
~If anyone finds this, go to Dragon Bridge and tell them Sigga did not drown.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_wayrest.dess:
#To whomever finds this,
If this card has come to you, you are in a room you ought not to be, and I admire the effort. I will not call the guard. I will say only that the third drawer is not what it seems, and the fourth is exactly what it seems, and the fifth has a rat in it. Be kind to the rat.

If you are a thief, take the silver and leave the ledgers. If you are a spy, take the ledgers, but replace them with forgeries; they will not be read. If you are an honest person, I am sorry, and I hope the rat is well.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_wayrest.hook: The twin-towered seat of the Duchess of Wayrest, a keep of pale stone and green banners whose cellars are said to be older than its cathedral.
place_lore.nirncraft.castle_wayrest.rumo: The Chamberlain keeps two sets of keys: one for the rooms the Duchess has seen, and one for those she has not. He is said to be quite scrupulous about the second set.
place_lore.nirncraft.cath_bedraud.hook: A knight's crypt under a ruined chapel with long vaulted aisles of effigies, a bone-lined crypt and a hollow font.
place_lore.nirncraft.cath_bedraud.rumour: In Cath Bedraud the knights' stone faces all look one way: toward a niche that has been plastered shut.
place_lore.nirncraft.cath_bedraud.web.p0: HE WHO WAS NOT COUNTED LIES HERE UNDER A BORROWED NAME. Seven he stood beside and an eighth he stood above. Let the chisel rest. Let the plaster crack. Let the heirs be found.
place_lore.nirncraft.cathedral_of_webs.h: A crystal vault wrapped in giant spider-silk, shafts of light through white webs onto lecterns of woven thread.
place_lore.nirncraft.cathedral_of_webs.r: The Cathedral of Webs is a place of reading. The spiders sit very still.
place_lore.nirncraft.cathedral_of_webs.w: I came to rescue a book and stayed to hear it read. The spiders do not eat us; they eat nothing but silk and light. They weave the words so they will not be lost. If I stop reading, they stop weaving. I have not stopped. I think I have been reading for a hundred days. I am quite happy.
place_lore.nirncraft.celinmbek.hook: At place.nirncraft.celinmbek, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the rain-soaked moors and ancient cairns of Glenumbra, where Camlorn's cathedral clergy and the Beldama Wyrd keep uneasy watch over the barrow-dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.celinmbek.rumour: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.celinmbek report signs of moorland werewolf packs, barrow-wights, and Llugwych blood-courtiers operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.

As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.celinmbek

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the rain-soaked moors and ancient cairns of Glenumbra, where Camlorn's cathedral clergy and the Beldama Wyrd keep uneasy watch over the barrow-dead. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.celinmbek have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by moorland werewolf packs, barrow-wights, and Llugwych blood-courtiers. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.
place_lore.nirncraft.cheydinhal.hook: A Nibenese town of tall timber houses and a canal, half full of Dunmer who came over the Valus Mountains after the Red Year and never went home, because there was no home to go to.
place_lore.nirncraft.cheydinhal.letter_h:
Aunt Vedila,
We are in Cheydinhal. The Imperials are cold but they leave us be, which is more than the ash did. Father works the canal locks. Mother does not speak since Kragenmoor.

There is a shrine to Nocturnal west of the town where some of our people go at night. Father says the Temple would not approve. Mother went last week. She came back and slept for the first time in a year. I don't know who to thank.
If the roads open, tell me if the house still stands. Tell me even if it doesn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.cheydinhal.refugee_:
#Arrivals, Rain's Hand
The Sarano family, six, from Kragenmoor. Two burned, one blind. Bunks four to nine.
A silt-strider herder, no name given, from Balmora. Brought the strider's harness and nothing else. Says the beast died crossing the Valus and he carried the harness for luck.

#Arrivals, Second Seed
One Ordinator, out of armour, refusing to give his name. Prays at the canal at dawn and dusk. The children are afraid of him. I am not. I have seen what he is afraid of.
Note to the Count's steward: we need blankets more than prayers. Send blankets. I will supply the prayers myself.
place_lore.nirncraft.cheydinhal.rumour: Cheydinhal's Dunmer now, more or less. Good neighbours, mostly, if you don't mind ash-yam stew in every kitchen. Just don't buy the empty house by the east wall, whatever price they ask.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillfurrow_farm.al:
#First Seed
Planted cabbage and leek in the north field. Frost late, as ever. Lost a row.
#Rain's Hand
Wolves at the fence twice. Shot one. The other stood and watched me like it was counting.

#Second Seed
Men camped past the east hedge. Clean armour, silver on the buckles, polishing their blades by the fire every night. They asked if I'd seen any big dogs. I said only wolves. One of them laughed and said, 'Wolves. Yes.'

I keep the shutters barred now. Whatever they are hunting, I'd rather not be in the way.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillfurrow_farm.ho: A lonely farm east of Whiterun where the cabbages grow fat and the farmers grow nervous. Silver-armoured strangers have been seen at the edge of the fields.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillfurrow_farm.ru: Chillfurrow's had a bad season. There was a pelt-trader killed out there, and folk say the killers wore silver. Now nobody wants to buy pelts in Whiterun at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillfurrow_farm.sk: Folio #12 (185, 45): Field inspection recorded for Chillfurrow Farm within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #12 for chillfurrow_farm: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Chillfurrow Farm are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillwind_depths.ba: FROM THE LADS AT CLIFFSIDE: DON'T GO DOWN.

We used the top of this cave to keep our stores cool. Then the stores started going missing. Then Hrodgar went missing. Then we found Hrodgar, what the chaurus left of him, laid out at the second turning like a gift. We moved our stores back to the Retreat. We'd move further if we could. Down there the dark has ears, and it hunts by them.
If you must go down, wrap your boots in fur and don't talk. They can't see a torch, but they can hear you swearing at the cold.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillwind_depths.ho: A frozen cave in the hills between Haafingar and the Reach that runs down into Falmer warrens. Trappers set their lines at its mouth for the white foxes. Some lines are pulled in from below.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillwind_depths.or:
#14th of Frostfall
White fox in the snare, chewed loose, ran down into the Depths. Brannoc went after it with a torch, laughing. Said it was worth six septims and he wasn't leaving six septims to the dark.

#15th of Frostfall
Brannoc has not come up. I heard him shout once, far down, and then a clicking like a hundred beetles.
#17th of Frostfall
I've been to the second turning with a torch. There are blind elves down there, with bows. Their leader wears a mask of chitin and carries Brannoc's brass compass on a thong, like a trophy. I can't go further alone. Somebody. Please. Even if it's only to bring back the compass.
place_lore.nirncraft.chillwind_depths.ru: Chillwind Depths? Good furs at the mouth, bad things at the bottom. Orla the trapper's partner went in after a fox that ran down the hole. She's been sitting by the entrance three days, waiting.

place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol.creditors.p:
#Those I owed, as of First Seed
Gallus the wool-factor, 300. Dead, fell from his roof.
Widow Marcia Plautia, 85. Dead, choked at table.
Tertia of the Grey Mare, 40. Dead, kicked by her own mule.
Caius the cobbler, 12 drakes and a pair of boots. Dead. I didn't even mind about the boots.

Still living: my sister Livilla, 6 drakes, lent to me at Mother's grave so I could buy the flowers.
I said the words at the stones. 'Let what I owe be settled.' I meant paid. I meant paid. Livilla, if you read this, go to Skingrad. Go now. Don't lend anyone anything.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol.guild_board:
^CONTRACTS OPEN
Goblins in the hills west of the North Country road. Twenty drakes the ear, proof required, no ears from the same goblin.
Escort wanted for a wool cart to Skingrad. Driver is deaf; shout.

Investigation wanted, discreetly: the beggars of Chorrol walk south to the Namira stones every new moon. Two have not come back. The Countess wants to know why, and she does not want to know loudly.
Refused contracts: anything involving the Clavicus Vile shrine. The Guildmaster says she's done paying funerals for clever men.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol.hook: A Colovian market town built around a great oak, home to the Fighters Guild hall and to more quarrels over cattle, debts and inheritance than any court in the Empire can untangle.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol.rumour: Chorrol's honest, mostly. But there's a fellow here who wished his debts away at the Clavicus Vile stones south of town, and now every man he owed is in the ground. Talk to Ostorius, if you've the stomach.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol_milegate.ho: A little milestone fort on the Chorrol road, long since out of the Legion's hands, where the road sign still says Chorrol, 4 miles, and means it.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol_milegate.mi:
^LOGBOOK, CHORROL MILEGATE
^Fourteenth of Rain's Hand: three wagons, one cart, a lame mule. All accounted for.
^Fifteenth: four wagons. One, I did not see arrive. It had no driver. It had a full load of barrels and a note in the back that said "for the Count, when he calls." I did not open the barrels.

^Sixteenth: five wagons. The extra wagon has come again. The barrels are heavier today. The note now reads "for the Count, now." I have moved the patrol to the north wall. If anyone finds this, do not send a replacement. The wagon will not need a driver.
place_lore.nirncraft.chorrol_milegate.ru: The Chorrol milegate is a good place to stop. It has no inn, no priest, and no guard. It does have a very old well that never runs dry, and a curious habit of guests leaving early.
place_lore.nirncraft.city_of_ash.hook: A burned Ayleid city with ash-choked terraces, melted crystal lamps and a scorched grand cistern.
place_lore.nirncraft.city_of_ash.rumour: The City of Ash is quiet. The ash holds the shape of people who sat down and did not get up.
The City of Ash was the worst. I lit the lamp and every ash-figure on the terraces turned its head. One said a word. I have not repeated it since. The cabal's youngest has gone pale. We have one stone left and a Tower to face. I would give a great deal for a quieter instrument to play.
place_lore.nirncraft.city_of_ash.web.p0: ~Our lords put out the lamps and wept,~and wept, and fed the fire.~The trees took us, the trees have kept~the ash of our desire.~We lean, we lean, we lean for home,~for stone that has no tire.
place_lore.nirncraft.clearpine_pond.angl:
THIS POND IS FISHED BY FENRIC OF DRAGON BRIDGE AND HAS BEEN SINCE BEFORE YOU WERE BORN.
Take a trout if you are hungry. Take two if you are very hungry. Take three and I will know.

Do not cut the old pine on the east bank; it is older than the bridge. Do not swim. The pond is deeper than it looks and the bottom is soft.
And if you are one of the Pinemoon lot, I saw you burying something by the stump on the north shore. I did not touch it. I want that understood, by you and by whatever gods are listening.
place_lore.nirncraft.clearpine_pond.hook: A still green pond among old pines north of Dragon Bridge, where a lone angler used to camp. Something besides trout has been hidden at the water's edge.
place_lore.nirncraft.clearpine_pond.rumo: Old Fenric fished Clearpine Pond every summer until the bandits from Pinemoon chased him off. He says the pond's haunted now. He says it with a funny look, like someone who knows exactly what's haunting it.
place_lore.nirncraft.clearspring_tarn.ho: A clear mountain pool high in the northern Rift, so still that hunters swear they can see the stars in it at noon. Something drinks there at night that leaves no tracks.
place_lore.nirncraft.clearspring_tarn.ru: The water at Clearspring Tarn's sweet enough to cure a hangover, they say. But don't camp there. My uncle did. Said he woke up with the frost on him in the shape of a hand.

place_lore.nirncraft.clearspring_tarn.ta:
~I came to the tarn with a heart full of stones,
~I left with my heart and the stones in the water.
~Drink if you're thirsty, but don't drink alone,
~For the tarn keeps a little of every man's daughter.

Cut below, in a rougher hand: Ingrid, 4E 188. Come home.

The verse is old, the bark grown thick around the letters, but the name beneath it is fresher. Hunters from Shor's Stone say a girl called Ingrid walked up to the tarn in the autumn of 188 to fetch water for her sick mother and was never seen again. Her father carved the line and came back every year until he could no longer climb. Some say the frost-hand on sleeping travellers is hers, still trying to wake someone to take her home.
place_lore.nirncraft.cliffside_retreat.h:
#2nd of Rain's Hand
The goats have found the path down to the river again. Fetched them back. Saw smoke from Liar's Retreat. Bandits, or the Stormcloaks' new camp. Neither one buys goat cheese.

#9th of Rain's Hand
Dug the cellar deeper. The rock gives way to old worked stone, carved by someone, not Dwemer, not Nord. Found a little iron key in a niche, no lock to fit it.

#20th of Rain's Hand
Strange men came asking for the key. Robes under their cloaks, red as fresh meat. I said I had no key. They said they'd come back. I believe them. Buried the key where the goats won't dig.
A lonely cabin perched on the cliffs east of the Karth gorge, with a cellar dug deeper than any honest hermit needs.
place_lore.nirncraft.cliffside_retreat.r: Old cabin up on the cliff by Liar's Retreat. Hermit who lived there never came to market, but he always had coin. Makes you wonder where from.

The Blades' cliff keep above the cloud line, with banners, wind and a rope bridge over the whole Jerall range.
The Cloud Ruler cloister has a row of bells that don't ring, and a woman in grey who polishes them.

We hold the seven. Four are in the high rooms, three are lost or stolen, the one at Frostcrag was sold to a wizard who wanted it as a curiosity. A wizard! If the seal opens, it will not be a cloud-keep that answers. Fetch the Frostcrag bell and I will trust you with the rest.
place_lore.nirncraft.cloudrest.balcony_r:
#THE COUNT
Seventeen thousand, four hundred and eleven. Entered on the first of every month. The count is not an accounting, it is a courtesy. Every pane is a person, once, a mason who laid it. I call them by their panes.

A different ink, a later hand: 'It is seventeen thousand, four hundred and ten. I have counted it four times. I do not like to write it. A pane that was there is not there. The floor is not lonely. The floor is not anything. I should like to be sure.'
place_lore.nirncraft.cloudrest.hook: A palace-city cantilevered over the cliff with balconies of glass over a restless sea, a long causeway and no walls at all. The sky itself is the defence.
place_lore.nirncraft.cloudrest.rumour: Cloudrest has never been besieged. No one knows how you would begin. The few who tried reportedly looked down, and went home.

place_lore.nirncraft.college_of_psijics_: The ruined seaside college of the Psijic Order on Artaeum, where broken arches and half-open doors lead into halls that are sometimes here and sometimes elsewhere.

#RULE THE FIRST
Do not hurry; the day will arrive. Rule the second: Do not say what you have not yet thought. Rule the third: if a door is open that was closed, close it, and wait to see whether it was you who opened it. Rule the fourth: you are not late.
On the back, in pencil, in a very young hand: 'I have been late for three years and the rule says I am not. I am beginning to understand that the Psijics are not strict, only very, very patient.'
The Psijics say the college is not ruined. It is simply between versions. They promise it will be rebuilt as soon as they decide which of the two they prefer.
place_lore.nirncraft.college_of_winterho:
Things I am no longer permitted to do, by order of the Master-Wizard:
1. Summon a familiar in the Arcanaeum.
2. Summon a familiar near the Arcanaeum.
3. Attempt to 'just look' at the thing in the Midden.
4. Go to the Skytemple Ruins at night, alone or otherwise.
5. Borrow Quaestor Vesk's Dwemer cog to prop the window open.

6. Light the hearth with Destruction magic. (In my defence it was cold.)
7. Tell the Winterhold innkeeper we are boiling the sea. He believed me and now the Jarl believes it too.
8. Mention the Collapse at supper.
Things I am still permitted to do: study. Apparently.
The College of Winterhold stands on its broken bridge above the sea, the last great building of the old city. Mages come from every province, and not all of them leave.
The College? They let anyone in who can light a candle without a flint. The ones who can't get out again, mostly.

Folio #3 (1529, -1886): Field inspection recorded for College Of Winterhold within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #3 for college_of_winterhold: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing College Of Winterhold are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

To the Arch-Mage, with respect and some urgency.
It is my considered opinion (1) that the Dwemer ruins of the Pale, namely Alftand, Raldbthar and Irkngthand, together with their Great Lifts, form a single engineered system rather than three independent settlements, and that this College has been negligent (2) in failing to survey it.

(1) Considered over eleven years, four expeditions and one regrettable frostbitten toe.
(2) I use the word advisedly. See my previous memoranda of 4E 196, 198 and 199, none of which received a reply.

I propose to begin at Raldbthar, whose upper halls are the least disturbed by treasure-hunters. I request funds for two assistants, a sled, and a quantity of lamp oil. My last assistant, young Brelas, has not returned from Alftand, and I would rather not discuss it.
A. Vesk, Quaestor of Antiquities (unofficial)
place_lore.nirncraft.colosseum_of_the_ol:
#TONIGHT
A contest of Illusion, no blood, no blows, no applause. The victor shall be the one who persuades the other that the other has already won. The loser shall be the one who believes it. The audience shall be asked to leave quietly.

Scrawled: 'I do not know who won. I know that I left feeling triumphant, and woke at dawn on the steps with no memory of the evening and a very strong sense that someone had enjoyed themselves at my expense.'
A ruined ring arena of pale stone on Artaeum's coast, where the old Psijic champions once fought with arts rather than steel, and where the sand still remembers every bout.
The Colosseum has no gate. It has a door that appears when you stop looking for it, and the sand inside always bears the print of a shoe that is slightly too small.
place_lore.nirncraft.coral_tower_of_thra: A tower of living coral in a sea of plague, with rooms of pulsing polyps, bright pink and poison green and a spiral reef stair.
The tower in the plague sea has grown a fathom this year. The folk of Thras say it is thinking.

The tower breathes. I did not believe it, but there it is: each room expands and contracts. The heart is down below, a thing like a lung the size of a house. It is not ill. It is not mad. It is simply patient, and it wants to be larger. It does not know there is a fleet. It does not know there is a shore. It only knows 'more'.

place_lore.nirncraft.corinthe.canal_chal:
^DO NOT MOOR HERE AFTER MIDNIGHT
^The third bridge sings. It does not like to be answered. If it asks you a question, say that you are not from Corinthe and that you will pay the toll on the way back.
#HIVES OF THE GARDEN CATHEDRAL
Hive One: Old Mother. Calm, golden, tolerates priests. Hive Seven: Quiet Seven. Sulks in winter, forgives in spring. Hive Eleven: Eleven-Without-Sting. Honey of surprising sweetness, but bees of surprising rudeness.
Report to the Bell on any hive that falls silent. A silent hive is not a dead hive; it is a hive that has decided something. Learn what, before anyone opens the lid.
place_lore.nirncraft.corinthe.hook: A green river city of canal bridges and terraced gardens, where bees outnumber citizens and a garden-roofed cathedral hums with three hundred hives.
place_lore.nirncraft.corinthe.rumour: People forget Elsweyr has rivers. Corinthe does not let them. Every window in the city has a box of flowers, and every flower has a bee that has opinions about the neighbours.
place_lore.nirncraft.corpselight_stead.h: A damp pine-shadowed steading near the eastern barrow-ridges, named for the pale marsh-candles that drift over the moss at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.corpselight_stead.r: Nobody envies the family at Corpselight Stead; between the old cairns above them and the spriggans in the hollow, they sleep with iron bars on the shutters.
place_lore.nirncraft.corpselight_stead.s: Folio #49 (-980, 1520): Field inspection recorded for Corpselight Stead within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.corpselight_stead.w: Kept the pitch-pots lit along the dry-stone wall all through the dark of the moon. When the rain stops, a pale green glimmer hangs over the path toward Halldir's Cairn, and the hounds whimper under the porch until sunrise.
place_lore.nirncraft.crabbers_shanty.cra:
#Sun's Dusk
Sold forty crabs to the Imperial camp. Kept the shells for the garden. Kept the coin in the usual place. Nobody knows the usual place but me and the crabs, and the crabs are not talking.

#Evening Star
Cough is worse. Can't stand long in the cold water. If I don't see spring, whoever reads this can have the purse. It's under the third trap from the door, the one with the blue rope, buried an arm deep in the shingle by the water.

Mind the big crab. I named him Jarl. He bites.
place_lore.nirncraft.crabbers_shanty.gor:
DON'T TAKE THE GORGE ROAD WEST. Robbers in the gorge with a toll-chain across the water and bows on the cliffs. They took my boat, my nets and my good knife.

If you must go to the Reach, go by the high path past Orotheim and keep your torch low. If you see a man in a red hood waving at you from the rocks, he is not friendly. He is counting you.

Signed with a crab's claw scratched in the wood. Grisvar, probably.
place_lore.nirncraft.crabbers_shanty.hoo: A leaning shack on a stony riverbank in the far west of the hold, ringed with old crab traps. Its owner died years ago, but the crabs never left, and neither did his savings.
place_lore.nirncraft.crabbers_shanty.rum: There was an old crabber out west, past Rorikstead, who never spent a coin in his life. When he died, nobody found a single septim in his shack. Folk say the mudcrabs are guarding it.
place_lore.nirncraft.cracked_tusk_keep.b: Nobody opens the east cellar. I don't care what you hear. The buyer who paid us to sit on what's in there pays more than every cart we've ever robbed, and he says if the door opens before he comes back, we'll all end up as something worse than dead.

He has a red cloak and a voice like a cracked bell and he said a name I won't write down. Watch the road from Halldir's Cairn and from the ruins on the north road. If anyone comes asking about an old sword hilt, they've come for what's in the cellar. Kill them first and ask second.
place_lore.nirncraft.cracked_tusk_keep.c: Told by the last of clan Gol-Tusk

My grandfather's grandfather built this keep with stone dragged from the river and blood from his own hands. The chief of that day broke a tusk biting through the chain of a Nord slaver, and so the keep was named, and the broken tusk was set in iron above the gate.

We held the keep against bandits, Nords, a bear the size of a cart, and two hard winters. We did not hold it against hunger. The last of us left for Orsinium when I was a boy. Whoever lives here now, know that the walls remember who built them, and the walls are patient.
place_lore.nirncraft.cracked_tusk_keep.h: A stone keep in the southwestern woods built by an Orc clan generations ago and named for a broken tusk on its gate. Bandits hold it now, and they guard more than coin.
place_lore.nirncraft.cracked_tusk_keep.r: Cracked Tusk Keep's held by a crew who don't drink in Falkreath and don't sell their loot there either. My cousin swears they've got a locked room even they don't open.

In ochre on the flat stone at the tower's foot, in the Reach tongue, copied and translated by a wandering scholar:
Child of the Reach, here is the rock your mothers lay on. Be as hard. Here is the wind your fathers breathed. Be as free. Here is the river below. Be as patient. It cut this valley with nothing but time.

The scholar adds: The Forsworn who now hold the tower still bring infants here at the turn of the year, under guard. A sentry let me copy this on the condition that I wrote it truly. I believe I have.
A broken stone tower on a crag near Bard's Leap, its base worn smooth by ages of Reachfolk mothers who came to lay their newborns on the rock for a blessing.
The Reachfolk used to bring their babies to the Cradle Stone for luck. The Forsworn hold it now. Not much luck to go round these days.

To the chief at Lost Valley. The crones there want the Cradle Stone for their rites. They want to bury briar here. I say no. The Cradle is for the living. Send me ten more spears and I will keep saying no.
The falls are loud this year. Something in Gloomreach is singing under the rock at night. Not Falmer. Falmer do not sing.

Below, a reply in a crone's spidery marks: Ten spears is ten spears less for the Nords. You will have three. And the briar will be buried where the briar is wanted. The Cradle is old, sentry, and old things serve the strong. Count your three spears and be grateful I do not count you.
