place_lore.nirncraft.cradlecrush_rock.gi: There are no letters on the great stone, only shapes worn deep by many hands: a large hand and a small one, over and over, pressed side by side into the rock until it took their outline.
A Nord has cut beneath, more recently: 'Counted forty-one pairs. My grandfather counted thirty-nine. They are still adding to it.'

And lower still, in a hasty, frightened hand: 'Wolf-tracks all round the stone last full moon, and one set that started as a wolf's and ended as a man's bare feet, going east toward the river and Mixwater Mill. The giants would not come near them. Neither will I.'
place_lore.nirncraft.cradlecrush_rock.ho: A giants' camp on a bare crag at the western edge of Eastmarch, where a great flat stone is said to have been the cradle of the first giant child, and where wolves run that are not always wolves.
place_lore.nirncraft.cradlecrush_rock.hu:
Captain Silver-Wrist,
Followed the beast's trail from the wolf-kill at Cradlecrush Rock to the river and lost it at the water. Found the same print, a man's foot halfway to a paw, outside the sawyers' bunkhouse at Mixwater Mill.

The giants did not interfere. One of them watched me the whole time from beside its stone, and when I went too near the stone it lifted its club, not to strike, only to show me. I took the hint. I recommend we all take it.
Bring the chains to Gallows Rock. I will point out our man.
place_lore.nirncraft.cradlecrush_rock.ru: The giants at Cradlecrush Rock are the old kind, quiet unless you near the stone. It's the woods below the rock I'd mind. Something there bites, and the bitten don't stay men.
place_lore.nirncraft.cradlecrush_rock.sk: Folio #21 (1150, -32): Field inspection recorded for Cradlecrush Rock within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.cragslane_cavern.ad:
Sister,
I need four hundred septims and I cannot tell you why. I can tell you that the Khajiit at Cragslane are patient people, and that patience has an end, and that I have found the end of it.
I only meant to watch one fight. Then I only meant to win back what I lost on it. Then there was the sugar, which only meant to help me sleep. Everything only meant one thing.
Do not tell Father. Do send the money. Do not come here yourself, whatever happens.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragslane_cavern.ho: A cavern in the south-eastern hills where a skooma ring runs a wolf-fighting pit for gamblers from Windhelm and Riften, and where losing bettors are fed to the winners.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragslane_cavern.pi:
#Frostfall
Fight the first: Greyjaw against the Ansilvund bitch. Greyjaw. 140 septims staked, 90 to the house.
Fight the second: Greyjaw against two of the Mixwater mutts. Greyjaw. 210 staked, 160 to the house.
Debts: the Windhelm Shatter-Shield cousin owes 400 and has stopped coming. Send the boys to remind him. The Riften man owes 120 in moon sugar. Accept it; we will sell it again at Stony Creek.
This one notes: Greyjaw is tired. A tired wolf loses. A losing wolf is dinner for the next one. This one does not like that, but this one likes going hungry less.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragslane_cavern.ru: Rich fellows from Windhelm go down to Cragslane Cavern to watch wolves tear each other apart. Some of those rich fellows come back poorer. Some don't come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragwallow_slope.ap:
To the cell at Ansilvund,
Master Venkar has stopped sending you bodies because he has started keeping them. He talks to them. He calls the widow 'mother'. I came here to learn a craft, not to watch a man build himself a family from the Kynesgrove graveyard.
If you still want what you were promised, come and take it. I will leave the lower gate unbarred on the night of the next new moon. I ask only that you take me with you when you go.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragwallow_slope.ho: A cairn-pocked slope south of Narzulbur where a necromancer has made a workshop of the old burial caves, and where the dead of Kynesgrove have been going missing.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragwallow_slope.ne:
#On the warmth of Eastmarch soil
Bodies buried near Kynesgrove keep astonishingly well. The heat of the ground rises through the grave and slows the rot, so that a man three months dead is as useful as one three days. Kyne, it seems, is a friend to my art.

#Specimens to date
Thrunvar of Kynesgrove: strong back, good for hauling. The widow Asta: frail, but her hands are steady. Two from the Ansilvund cell, traded for a pouch of grave-salts. The cell asks too many questions about what I intend.

#Intent
An army that does not need to eat, sleep or be paid. Ulfric would understand. Ulfric would say no, of course, but he would understand.
place_lore.nirncraft.cragwallow_slope.ru: Lanterns on Cragwallow Slope at night, and the Kynesgrove graves dug up by morning. Somebody up there is collecting, and it isn't flowers.

place_lore.nirncraft.cronvangr_cave.hook: A cave in the hills between Mixwater Mill and the dragon mound, where a nest of vampires drains the trappers' snares and, lately, the lovers of Mara's Eye Pond.
place_lore.nirncraft.cronvangr_cave.rumo: Don't walk the Cronvangr hills after dark. A Dunmer lady with lovely manners lives in that cave, and everyone she invites to supper ends up on the menu.
place_lore.nirncraft.cronvangr_cave.sk4_: Folio #20 (1585, -34): Field inspection recorded for Cronvangr Cave within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.cronvangr_cave.thra:
Ottar,
If you got away, do not come back for me. She is old and she is patient and she laughs when the others are cruel. She says I am to be kept for a special night.

If you must come back, bring a priest and bring fire and bring someone who is not in love with me, because love makes a man slow and she is very fast.
I still have the ring. I have kept it in my mouth so they would not take it. I am wearing it now. I am still sworn.
place_lore.nirncraft.cronvangr_cave.vamp:
#For the Frostfall table
Foxes from the riverside traps: adequate for the thralls, no more.
The trapper himself: fled to Kynesgrove. Pity. Lean men keep well.
Two lovers from Mara's Eye Pond, taken mid-vow: exquisite. The girl first. The boy ran, which was rude of him.

#For Sun's Dusk
Something from Mixwater Mill. Sawyers have a wonderful vigour. Perhaps the brother of the one the silver hunters took; grief sweetens the blood.
Mind the giants of Broken Limb Camp. They do not taste of anything but they hit very hard, and Venreth has not yet grown back his arm.

place_lore.nirncraft.crystal_tower_summe: A needle of crystal, many times taller than anything else on the isle, glowing faintly at night with a light that does not seem to come from the sun or the moons.

They say the Tower does not cast a shadow. Look on a clear noon and you will see it does not, though the sun is above it. The Altmer say this is a trick of the angle. The angle, they add, is very hard to find.

^HERE THE ANCESTORS PLANTED A SEED OF LIGHT.
^HERE THE LIGHT GREW A SPINE OF CRYSTAL.
^HERE THE SPINE REACHES UPWARD, AND NO FURTHER.
A tourist's scratch below it: 'It reaches further than the guides admit. I measured it. The shadow of the top fell in the sea, at noon, at a distance of two miles. Nobody believes me.'
place_lore.nirncraft.crystaldrift_cave.h: A cave of glittering ice in the southern hills, where the walls shine blue even in the dark. A thief once hid his take there, and the ice has been keeping it ever since.
place_lore.nirncraft.crystaldrift_cave.r: Crystaldrift Cave's colder than Maven's heart. Pretty, though. They say a thief from the Ratway hid a whole purse in there and froze to death going back for it.
place_lore.nirncraft.crystaldrift_cave.s: Folio #51 (2239, 1782): Field inspection recorded for Crystaldrift Cave within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #51 for crystaldrift_cave: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Crystaldrift Cave are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.crystaldrift_cave.t:
Hid the Goldenglow job's take where nobody will ever look. Crystaldrift, outside, round the west side of the hill. Twenty paces or so from the cave mouth there's a boulder with a crack in it shaped like a lightning bolt. Under that.

Gold ring, old setting. Don't sell it in Riften, they'll know it. Take it to Windhelm. And don't go into the cave itself. Ice spiders. Big ones. You hate spiders, Svari. Remember that you hate spiders.

place_lore.nirncraft.daggerfall.courtier:
#Daggerfall, Turdas the 6th of Frostfall
Cousin,
You asked whether the court is quiet. It is never quiet. It is only well-mannered. This season the talk is all of young lords riding north past the Boethiah stones before dawn, swords on their hips and nothing in their saddlebags. They come back with sharper faces and fewer friends.

Sir Corwin's brother died in a duel last week over a borrowed horse. A borrowed horse! The seconds swear it was fairly fought. The seconds both wear new rings. I have begun to keep a list, and I do not like the shape it is taking.
Burn this. I mean it this time.
Y.
place_lore.nirncraft.daggerfall.hook: The oldest of the Breton crowns, a grey city of towers on the Glenumbra coast where the Knights of the Dragon keep their vigils and every courtier keeps a knife behind the smile.
place_lore.nirncraft.daggerfall.masque_h:
^You are bidden, sweet stranger,
^to the Revel of the Ninth Mask,
^upon the first night of the dark moon,
^at the stones west of the city where the Lord of Revels keeps his chair.
Come masked. Come thirsty. Leave your name with your coachman, for you will not need it until morning, and perhaps not then.
On the back, scribbled: 'Aubin, don't you dare. Your mother will skin me. -- G.' And beneath that, in another hand: 'She'll never know.'
place_lore.nirncraft.daggerfall.rumour: Daggerfall's court runs on whispers. You can buy a secret on the morning tide and sell it back to the same lady by supper, at a profit.
place_lore.nirncraft.daggerfall_outlaws_: A cellar beneath the Guild Span's tollhouse where those with unpaid tolls wait out the Guild's patience.
The cellar under the Guild Span is dry in winter and flooded in summer. The smugglers who use it say the river keeps its own schedule.

^Scratched and chalked on the cellar wall, in forty hands:
"Paid in full, 4E 184. Paid again, 4E 188. Paid thrice, 4E 193, and still I cross."
"The Madam is lawful. The Madam is thorough. The Madam is a perfectly tuned bell, and nobody asks who tuned her."
"If you are reading this, you owe nothing. Nobody does. The bridge is a hole, and the hole is a coin, and the coin is a bridge. Cross, and say nothing, and do not count."
place_lore.nirncraft.dainty_sload.captai: No one goes ashore. No one signals the shore. If a Company boat comes alongside, you are a grain ship waiting on a buyer and you are bored about it. Yawn if you must.

When the lighthouse goes dark, the Broken Oar boats will come for the first twenty crates. Count them twice. The last time, Varo's men counted nineteen and swore it was twenty, and I am not paying for the pleasure of being robbed.
Anyone found talking to the Saltmane boy about anything other than rope will be put ashore at Orphan's Tear. Without a boat.
place_lore.nirncraft.dainty_sload.deckha:
To whoever finds this, and I pray it is not the captain:
The crates in the lower hold are marked as Cyrodilic brandy. They are not brandy. They are skooma, forty crates of it, bound for the buyers who meet the Broken Oar boats north of the lighthouse.

The true manifest is kept in the captain's sea chest, written in her own hand, with the names of the Solitude men who paid for it. I have seen one of those names on the East Empire Company's own ledgers.
I signed on to haul grain. I have a daughter in Dragon Bridge. If I go to the Company, the captain will know it was me. If I don't, the stuff goes ashore and kills somebody's daughter. So I am writing it down instead, like a coward, and hiding it where a braver man might look.
place_lore.nirncraft.dainty_sload.hook: A trim merchant ship anchored under Solitude's cliffs, its papers in perfect order. Too perfect: the harbour folk say her hold smells of moon sugar.
place_lore.nirncraft.dainty_sload.rumour: The Dainty Sload has been anchored out there a month without unloading a single crate. Merchant ships don't sit still unless the merchandise doesn't want to be seen.

place_lore.nirncraft.damphall_mine.hook: A Raven Rock mine in the western hills, abandoned after a seam of hot water broke through the lower galleries. The steam brought up more than water: the ash itself has started walking there.
place_lore.nirncraft.damphall_mine.miner: Scratched with the point of a pick, in Dunmeri: Ash is the bones of our grandmothers, my mother said. Then why are our grandmothers trying to kill us? Under it, another hand: Because we dug them up without asking. Under that, a third: Because we didn't pay them. Ha. Under that, nothing more, and a long scorch-mark across the wood.

At the very bottom, almost hidden by soot, in a careful hand: Rels Llarys owes me two weeks. Rels Llarys owes all of us. If anyone ever brings the payroll out, tell my wife on the docks that I did not run first.
place_lore.nirncraft.damphall_mine.rumou: Damphall Mine was a good dig until the water came up boiling. Now the miners say there's ash spawn in the lower galleries, climbing out of the steam like it's birthing them.
place_lore.nirncraft.damphall_mine.shift:
#Turdas, 9th of Sun's Dusk
Water broke through at the third gallery at mid-shift. Scalding. Two men burned, no deaths. Pumps cannot keep up. Withdrew to the second gallery.
#Fredas, 10th
Something moved in the steam. Not a man. Grey, crusted, burning at the joints. It walked straight out of the water as if the water had made it. Then another.

#Loredas, 11th
Mine closed by my order. The payroll chest is still in the overseer's alcove in the lower gallery: one hundred and twelve drakes owed to eleven miners who have families on the Raven Rock docks. I am not going back for it. I am ashamed to write that. If anyone else goes, take the payroll to Sergeant Indaram, who will see it fairly paid.
place_lore.nirncraft.dark_brotherhood_sa: A hidden cellar sanctuary under a nondescript house on the Gold Coast, with a small crypt-warren, a communal hall and a locked inner coffin-room.
A house on the Gold Coast road has no windows and a smoke-hole that smells of fish. People cross the street.

Target: Father Aldric Merenth of Kvatch. Fee: unpaid, client cannot be found. Note: the priest asked us to hold his last letter until the Candle came for it. No one has. File under unfinished. Do not open the coffin.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkfall_cave.durz_:
Bear went left. Blood on the left. I follow.
Pale ones here. Many. They do not see, they listen. Walk on moss, not stone.
Bear dead. Something else ate it first. The pale ones took the meat and they took my bow.

Hiding. Leg bad. If Bashnag comes, brother, my tusk-string is around my neck still. Take it back to the stronghold so they hang it by the fire and not on some pale one's wall.
The wind blows up from below, warm. Warm. In this cold. What is down there?
place_lore.nirncraft.darkfall_cave.falme:
These knotted hide strips were found on a crude altar of chaurus shell. A scholar of Markarth might read them. To the untrained eye they show a crude circle of figures with long ears bowing to a larger figure, and below them a sun, crossed out with a slash of dried blood.
Tied to the bottom is a scrap of Nord cloth, red, the kind the Orcs of Mor Khazgur trade for at Markarth.

Beside the altar, half-buried in guano, a broken Orcish arrow with red fletching lies pointed toward a passage that slopes steeply downward. The air from that passage is warm, and smells faintly of grass, which is impossible this far under the mountain. Someone has scratched a tusk-mark into the stone above it.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkfall_cave.hook: A black cleft in the Druadach Mountains that breathes cold air even in summer. Falmer hunt its upper passages, and the Orcs of Mor Khazgur say something far older waits at the bottom.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkfall_cave.rumou: Darkfall Cave goes down further than any map. Orc hunter went in after a wounded bear and nobody's seen him since. Bear neither.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkfall_cave.sk4_n: Folio #12 (-2765, -1267): Field inspection recorded for Darkfall Cave within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.darklight_tower.hag:
Little Snow-Shod girl wants the bad men gone. Bad men from the Briar who come about the debt. Gnarlmother can do it. Gnarlmother asks so little.

A lock of the mother's hair. A tooth from the father. A song from the girl, sung into a bottle. Then the bad men never come again, and the farm is safe, and the family belongs to Gnarlmother a little bit, which is no bad thing.
Scratched below in a crabbed hand: She hasn't brought them. Send the crows. Children forget, but crows don't let them.
place_lore.nirncraft.darklight_tower.hoo: A tall, dark tower in the southern hills of the Rift, home to hagravens who trade in hair, teeth and promises. Farm children have been seen walking towards it in their sleep.
place_lore.nirncraft.darklight_tower.rum: Hagravens in Darklight Tower. The Snow-Shod girl says one talked to her in the bottom field. Asgeir's sleeping in the barn with his axe now.
place_lore.nirncraft.darklight_tower.sk4: Folio #49 (2052, 1722): Field inspection recorded for Darklight Tower within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #49 for darklight_tower: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Darklight Tower are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.darklight_tower.wit:
Traveller,
The tower above you is home to a hagraven called the Gnarlmother and her brood. Do not trade with her. Do not speak to her crows. Do not give her anything that has been part of you, not even a hair from your comb.

I came here from Stendarr's Beacon to cleanse this place. I failed. If you are stronger than I was, aim for her before her spells take hold. Stendarr's mercy on you.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkshade.alchemist: Darkshade, third visit. Nirnroot in abundance along the inner pool, a full dozen plants singing so loudly I could find them with my eyes shut. Glowing mushrooms the size of a shield. A single deathbell where no deathbell should grow, in warm damp ground. Remarkable.

The spriggans tolerated me on the first two visits. Today one followed me from the entrance to the pool and back, close enough that I could hear the wood of it creak. I believe the old one at the back of the cave, the one with antlers like a dead oak, has decided I owe it something. I left my journal behind when I ran. All my receipts are in it.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkshade.hook: A green-lit cavern near the river below Valtheim Towers, thick with rare herbs and guarded by spriggans who resent every root a stranger pulls.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkshade.rumour: There's an alchemist used to swear by the herbs in Darkshade. Went in for nirnroot one spring. Came out with moss growing in his beard and no memory of the way home.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkshade.sk4_note_: Folio #2 (982, -88): Field inspection recorded for Darkshade within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #2 for darkshade: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Darkshade are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkshade.valtheim_: To whoever's on the riverside watch: stop sending the new ones into that cave for herbs. Two went in from Valtheim Towers this month and the one that came back won't stop picking bark out of his skin. If you want potions, rob a merchant like an honest bandit. Spriggans don't carry coin and they don't stay dead.

And another thing. The brothers say if anyone else goes in that cave without asking, they can stay in it. We have enough trouble keeping the Whiterun guards off the bridge without growing a forest in the barracks. Anyone wants healing, there's a priestess in Whiterun who takes coin and doesn't ask where you got it.
#Hearthfire, 4E 201
2nd: 6 loads iron, 1 gold, to Windhelm by the east road. Arrived.
9th: 5 loads iron, 2 gold. Cart overturned near Mistwatch, driver beaten, gold gone. Iron left in the ditch, too heavy to bother with.
16th: sent two loads only, with Eirik and a spear. Arrived.

#Frostfall, 4E 201
1st: 4 loads iron, 3 gold, with Eirik. Eirik came home on foot with an arrow in his shoulder. Gold gone.
They know when the gold goes out. They never take the iron. Someone is telling them, or someone is watching from that tower.
Whoever reads this: I will pay for the tally sheet those thieves keep. I want to know which of my neighbours is selling us.
A mining hamlet where the Darkwater river is forded below the Goldenrock Mine, the last stop before the pass into the Rift and a favourite place for ore carts to go missing.

The hunter Orgnar Bent-Bow went to Snapleg Cave on the 5th of Frostfall to fetch back his hound and his grandfather's horn. The hound came home. Orgnar did not. The horn was heard blowing from the cave three nights after.

There is a hagraven in that hole and she has taken to calling men in with their own things. If you hear a horn in the hills below Darkwater Pass, do not answer it. If you are fool enough to go in, bring fire and bring the horn back to his widow.
Darkwater Crossing's carts have been robbed three times this season, always between the ford and Mistwatch. Strange luck, that. Very regular luck.

Folio #3 (1595, 421): Field inspection recorded for Darkwater Crossing within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.darkwater_ford_camp: A fortified timber ford-post on the Darkwater River where scouts watch the southern crossing and tally ore wagons coming up from the gorge.
The pickets at Darkwater Ford have been stopping every mule-cart since the bridge planks loosened in the thaw.

Keep two lanterns burning on the north bank whenever the river mist rises. Every ore wagon out of Darkwater Crossing must show a stamped tally-stick before crossing the shallows, and any rider coming down from the Rift hills without hold colors is to be turned back before nightfall.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkwater_pass.hook: A cold cavern that tunnels under the mountains between the Rift and Eastmarch, used as a shortcut by the desperate. The Falmer use it too.
place_lore.nirncraft.darkwater_pass.rumo: Folk from Darkwater Crossing use the pass when the road's snowed in. They used to. Now they go the long way and don't say why.

place_lore.nirncraft.darkwater_pass.surv:
#11th of Frostfall
Commissioned by the Darkwater Crossing mine to chart the pass for a cart road. I have my lodestone, my chain and my courage. The first two are reliable.

#12th of Frostfall
There are tracks in the mud that are not animal and not quite man. Bare feet, long toes. Some of the side passages have been walled up with chitin and bone.

#12th, deeper
They took the lodestone. Snatched it from my belt in the dark. I heard them chattering over it. It's a black stone in a brass cage, worth more than my house. Without it the survey's worthless, and so am I. I'm going back in for it.

place_lore.nirncraft.dawnbreak.hook: A hamlet on a sea bluff where the dawn bell rings at midnight, and no one has been seen to pull the rope.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnbreak.rumour: The bell at Dawnbreak is the only one in Summerset that is never late. It is simply early, by about six hours, and has been since the first day of spring.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnbreak.sexton_lo:
#Eleventh night
The bell rang three times. I was awake. I saw the rope move, slowly, as if drawn by a very slow person. I called out. The rope paused, and I could have sworn it was apologetic. Then it went on.

Twelfth night. I left a candle on the sill, and a cup of milk. In the morning the milk was gone, and the candle was lit, and a very small knot had been tied in the rope. A sailor's knot. I have taken it down and put it on the shelf.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnstar.dream_diar:
#Morndas, 3rd of Frostfall
Dreamed of the door again. Black stone, cold handle, a smell like burnt honey. Woke with my hand out in front of me, gripping nothing.

#Turdas, 6th of Frostfall
Asked at the docks. Ingrith dreamed it too. So did the blacksmith's boy, and the Khajiit who sells skooma to the miners when the guards aren't looking. We have stopped pretending it's the herring.

#Sundas, 9th of Frostfall
A stranger at the inn is selling sachets of dried nightshade and salt 'to keep the dreamer from the door'. Five septims each. Half the town bought one. I bought two. Dreamed of the door anyway, and this time it was ajar.

#Middas, 12th of Frostfall
My husband says we should go to the temple on the hill and ask. I told him if he goes up that hill I'll break his oars. Some doors you leave shut.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnstar.hook: A harbour and mining town on the frozen northern coast, where the boats bring in fish, the mines bring up iron and quicksilver, and nobody has slept soundly in weeks.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnstar.mine_ledge:
#Last Seed, 4E 201
Ore raised: 41 loads iron, 6 loads quicksilver.
Shipped to Solitude: 33 loads iron, 4 quicksilver.
Difference: 8 loads iron, 2 quicksilver. Gone between the pit and the boats.

Leif says snow-slides. Leif says sleds tip. Leif bought his wife a silver brooch last Fredas.
Men are falling asleep at the face, too. Two cuts from dropped picks this week, one broken foot. Every one of them says the same thing: they dreamed so hard they never rested.
If this keeps up the Jarl will have no iron to sell and I will have no miners to dig it.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnstar.rumour: Dawnstar's a good town, honest work in the mines and on the boats. Just don't ask anyone how they slept. They'll either cry or hit you.
place_lore.nirncraft.dawnstar.sk4_note_2: Folio #3 (174, -1801): Field inspection recorded for Dawnstar within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.dead_crone_rock.cli:
#28th of Sun's Height
Made the climb from the Hag Rock side. The wall of the dead at the top is real, carved with dragon claws. I put my hand on it and the stone was warm. One of the words shone, I swear it, and my head filled with a sound like a crowd running.

#29th
The crones found me. One of them laughed and said the Nords who made the wall were too frightened to read it. I'm hiding in the old tower. Heard a lute being played below. No bard alive would come here. So who's playing?
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_crone_rock.cro: ~Come up, come up, the climb is long,
~And sweeter at the top the song.
~We'll sing your name, we'll sing your bones,
~We'll sing you into the cold stones.
^Found on a Nord shield, the bearer's name scratched off. Someone took the trouble to scratch it off.

On the shield's inner face, scratched by its owner before the end:
They sing every night. They sing my name now. I never told them my name. Climbed up for the wall and the words on it. Should have stayed down by Hag Rock with the bard and his drum. If you are reading this you climbed too. Go back down.
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_crone_rock.hoo: A ruined Nordic fortress on a sheer crag south of Markarth, held by hagravens and their servants. An ancient word wall stands on the heights beside it.
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_crone_rock.rum: Climb Dead Crone Rock and the crones up there will sing for you. Last thing you'll ever hear, mind, but very pretty.
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_crone_rock.sk4: Folio #41 (-3176, 185): Field inspection recorded for Dead Crone Rock within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.dead_mens_respite.f:
#Rain's Hand
My nets came up near the barrow with a bone flute tangled in them. Old work, Nord, with tiny wolves carved down the side. I played a note on it. Three nights now I've heard something answering from the barrow mound. The same note, back, slower.

#Second Seed
The lads at Robber's Gorge laugh at me. They won't go near the barrow either, mind. I put the flute back by the door and said sorry out loud, like a fool.

Whoever's in there, they like music. Don't take any. Don't play any. Leave them their song.
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_mens_respite.h: An old barrow in the wet hills near Morthal, its door half-sunk in bog-moss. The dead here are said to be restless over a song that was never finished.
place_lore.nirncraft.dead_mens_respite.r:
~Rest you here who sang too loud,
~rest you here who sang too long,
~the bog is deep, the mist a shroud,
~and the dead are keeping the end of the song.

Under the verse, in another hand, newer: 'They are keeping it for someone. I hope it isn't me.'

The door post is half sunk in moss and the barrow mound behind it is wet and green. Fishermen from Crabber's Shanty leave small things at the door: a bone hook, a scrap of song written on bark, a cup of mead with a dead moth floating in it. Hunters from as far as Orotheim say that on still nights the barrow hums, a low steady note, as if someone inside were tuning an instrument and waiting for the others to join.
The bards of Solitude go misty-eyed over Dead Men's Respite. I'd be more interested in the treasure, myself. Mind you, a cousin of mine went for the treasure and came back singing.
A Dwemer bridge of bronze and stone spanning a gorge in the northern Reach. It has not rusted in four thousand years, and the hum in its pillars has never stopped.
Put your ear to the pillars at Deep Folk Crossing and you'll hear it humming. My uncle swore it hummed louder the night before the Markarth Incident.
Ancilia Varro, of the Markarth Dwemer studies

The pillar glyphs at this crossing are not decoration, whatever my esteemed colleague in Understone Keep says. They are a route marker. Note the repeated sigil of three arcs, which I have also seen at the gates of Bthardamz, to the south.

Note the second sigil, which appears ONLY here and at Bthardamz: a closed eye. My working translation is 'the deep that listens'. I have sent my assistant Fennick to Bthardamz to copy the gate in full. He promised me ten days. It has been twenty.
(Footnote: if anyone finds a lanky Breton with ink on his face and a Dwemer lexicon he swore he'd return, please send him to me in Markarth.)

place_lore.nirncraft.deepscorn_hollow.ho: A coastal cave with a drowned lower level, a moon-lit sink-hole and a bone-white hall that shows different rooms at different tides.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepscorn_hollow.ru: The Hollow's caves flood and empty twice a day. Folk say a candle burns down there that never goes out.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepscorn_hollow.we: They took us in because we could say where the Candle's keepers lived. We said. Now they ask for the one name I will not give: my brother's. He kept the book of the night the Gate opened. I tell them nothing. The tide is out. I light the candle.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepwood_redoubt.br:
The briar wants a young heart, a heart that has not yet been afraid. The Nord child is afraid now, he will not do. Keep him for the pot or the trade, whichever.
Next moon we try the Orc girl from Mor Khazgur's hunting grounds. Orcs are born angry. Anger is near to courage.

Madanach's people at Druadach send word: no more taking near the river roads, the Nords grow bold. Madanach is in a cell in Cidhna and gives orders like a king. I give orders like a mother. We will see whose children grow.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepwood_redoubt.fa:
To whoever finds this. I could not get past the second gate. My arm is broken and I can hear them singing below.
My son Toki is ten winters old. He has red hair and a whistle carved like a hawk that he will not stop blowing, gods help him. The Forsworn took him from the timber camp near Dragon Bridge Overlook on the 4th of Hearthfire.

The old one with the feathers looked at him the way a butcher looks at a lamb. Her name, I heard the others call it, is Ungrid. If you are stronger than me, go down. If he is alive, bring him out. If he is not, bring me the whistle so I know.
I'll wait at the mill at Dragon Bridge as long as I live. That may not be long.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepwood_redoubt.ho: A Forsworn stronghold carved into an old Nord barrow in the northern Reach. The hagravens who rule it take children from the Karth valley, and none have been given back.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepwood_redoubt.ru: A woodcutter from Dragon Bridge lost his boy to the Forsworn. They took him up to Deepwood Redoubt. The crones there like them young, they say.
place_lore.nirncraft.deepwood_redoubt.sk: Folio #11 (-2423, -1390): Field inspection recorded for Deepwood Redoubt within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.dimhollow_crypt.dig: Engaged: six strong backs to clear the entrance of the crypt north of the Lord Stone. Pay: one septim a day, double for the inner chambers. Employer: the pale gentleman. Payment in gold, in advance. Questions: none permitted.

Foreman's own note: the pale gentleman only visits after dark and never eats with us. He made us stop when we reached a great stone door with a ring of carvings on it, and paid us off on the spot. Three of the lads went back to see what was behind the door. I haven't seen them since.
place_lore.nirncraft.dimhollow_crypt.hoo: An ancient crypt beneath the hills of the southern Pale, recently broken open from the outside. The Vigilants of Stendarr are very interested in whatever was sealed below.
place_lore.nirncraft.dimhollow_crypt.rum: Dimhollow Crypt was quiet for a thousand years. Then a crew of strangers with a lot of digging tools turned up. Haven't seen any of them come back down the hill.
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_acropolis.c:
#THE EASTERN ROW
First: Patient. Second: Oath-Keeper. Third: He Who Waits at Windows. Fourth: Second-Best. Fifth: Wise. Sixth: Quarrel. Seventh: the one that fell, without a name; nobody agreed.
In the margin: 'I tried to read the plinths. Every second one is blank. The scholars say the names have worn away. The columns say otherwise. The columns say they were never given.'
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_acropolis.h: A ruined hilltop acropolis of white columns and fallen architraves, once the seat of the great Direnni clan, now home to a private collection and a very quiet wind.
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_acropolis.r: Every column at the Acropolis was named. Walk among them and a ghost will tell you which. Walk between them at dusk and the ghosts have a joke they have been rehearsing for four thousand years.
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_tower.hook: A tall white elven tower on an island, the old Direnni seat, with a spiral stair and a crystal lens at the summit.
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_tower.rumou: The old white tower of the Direnni stands on its island and a light burns in its lens-room every night. No one has been seen to climb the stair.
place_lore.nirncraft.direnni_tower.web.p: I made the giant to weep for her because I could not. She would have laughed. Now the sea comes through the giant's eyes and the isle sinks by an inch. I cannot stop it; I cannot bear the silence of a still cheek. Forgive an old man. Let the pump close when I am gone.

place_lore.nirncraft.dokrin_monastery.ho: A forest monastery where the monks have been singing the same hymn for three days, and are afraid to stop.
place_lore.nirncraft.dokrin_monastery.hy:
~Rise, O voice, in the morning wood,
~sing what is, and sing what could,
~sing the sap and sing the root,
~sing the bough and sing the fruit.
The hymn has forty verses and an unwritten forty-first. The monks agree that no one should sing the forty-first. They disagree about why.
place_lore.nirncraft.dokrin_monastery.ru: The monks of Dokrin are a quiet order. That is why the hymn is so loud. It is the loudest thing they have ever done.
place_lore.nirncraft.doomcrag.hook: A black spire on a crag with spiral wards, a library of bound books and a roof with a storm engine.
place_lore.nirncraft.doomcrag.rumour: The Doomcrag library has a ledger of names, and the necromancer reads it every night.
place_lore.nirncraft.doomcrag.web.author: Hestrel Doom
place_lore.nirncraft.doomcrag.web.p0: I, Hestrel of the Crag, hereby supply to the Host of the Supper the register of the grieving of Rivenspire, with notes. In return I receive one tome of my choosing, and the Host's solemn word that I shall never be asked to attend. Signed, in my own best hand and a little fear.

place_lore.nirncraft.drabul.hook: An Orcish outpost in the Valenwood forest, a stockade of log and stone in a tense truce with the Bosmer neighbours who cannot tell whether the Orcs are guests or guards.
place_lore.nirncraft.drabul.rumour: Drabul is the only place in Valenwood where a Bosmer will eat at an Orc's table. They do not speak of it. They bring their own knives.
^ORC AND BOSMER MAY SHARE THIS GROUND.
^NEITHER MAY CUT A TREE THAT THE OTHER HAS NAMED.
^NEITHER MAY LEAVE A FEAST BEFORE THE OTHER HAS TASTED.
Scratched below with a knife: 'The Orcs have named every tree. The Bosmer have tasted every feast. Neither side has noticed this is exactly what the stone asked.'

place_lore.nirncraft.draggin_tale_inn.ho: An inn with a giant draconian tail over the door, a long common room and a back room where the families meet.
place_lore.nirncraft.draggin_tale_inn.ru: The Draggin Tale's back room is shut every fifth spring while twelve families draw lots.
place_lore.nirncraft.draggin_tale_inn.we: Aman, Bahrad, Cassim, Dalila, Emre, Farouk, Ghassan, Hadiya, Idris, Jabari, Karim, Layla. Each has sent a child on the fifth-year ship at least once. The lots are carved prows. This year's prow is white. I have drawn it for sixty years and never drawn mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_bridge.hook: A lumber town around an ancient stone bridge over the Karth, its arch carved with the heads of dragons. Every road to Solitude from the south crosses here, and every traveller is watched.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_bridge.ocula: Traffic over the bridge, week ending 21st of Frostfall: forty-one travellers. Of note: one Thalmor courier, eastbound, papers in order, manner insufferable. Two Khajiit traders, westbound, one with a cart whose axle sat too low for the cargo declared. Searched. Moon sugar. Confiscated. Traders released after donation.

The widow Hulda continues to watch the road each evening. One son with the Stormcloaks in the hills, one gone up to Volskygge after barrow treasure. She is not a threat. Recommend we leave her be. Recommend, privately, that someone go and look for the younger boy.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_bridge.rumou: Dragon Bridge is a quiet town with a loud bridge. Everyone crosses it, and everyone's noticed. Those Imperial agents at the outpost write down the colour of your horse.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_bridge.taver:
WANTED: strong backs for the lumber mill. Pay fair. Must not be afraid of saws, heights, or the foreman's wife.
LOST: one grey goat, answers to Hilde, last seen eating a Legion banner. Return to Faida. Banner not required.

FOR SALE: one good boat, little used. Owner gone to the war and won't need it. Ask Hulda.
NOTICE: travellers crossing the bridge after dark will be asked their business by agents of the Penitus Oculatus. Answer politely. Answer truthfully. Answer quickly.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_bridge_overl: A bandit camp on the cliffs above the road south of Dragon Bridge. Its occupants call it a toll house, and the carters who pay call it something else.

Morndas: Snorri on the ledge, Kjeld at the fire.
Tirdas: Kjeld on the ledge, Snorri at the fire. Snorri, if I find you asleep up there again I will roll you off it myself.
From the ledge you can see Chillwind Depths to the south. If anything comes up out of there, any of those pale things, you ring the pan and you run. Do NOT go and look. Asvald went and looked.

Asvald came back two days later without his boots, his sword or most of his wits. He keeps saying the pale ones 'ate the light'. The chief says to give him a ledge of his own, far away from the fire, and to keep him off the wine. We've kept him off the wine. Not sure that's helping.
Pay the toll at the Overlook or lose the cart, that's the rule on the north road now. Hrodvar's lot took the whole Karthwasten payroll last week.

Addendum #13 for dragon_bridge_overlook: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Dragon Bridge Overlook are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

#Hearthfire, 4E 201
Timber wagon from Dragon Bridge: 15 septims and a cask of mead. Paid without fuss. Good folk.
Pilgrim to the Shrine to Peryite: nothing. Sick as a dog, didn't want to touch him.
Silver-Blood wagon: tried to run the road. Did not run the road.

Karthwasten payroll chest: 312 septims, plus the ledger and a letter from the clerk. Keep the chest locked, I mean to ransom the ledger back to the miners. They need it to prove what the Silver-Bloods owe them.
Note to the lads: Legion patrols from the Reach camp have been up the road twice. Next time, we let them pass. We're bandits, not idiots.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_graveyard_of: A valley floor of enormous ribcages, white as salt under a low sky, with a path of vertebrae winding between them.
The valley of ribs groans at dusk. The Akaviri say it is the dragons turning over in their sleep.

~We came to die where the north wind breathes,~we came to lie where the ice-flower seethes.~Rib by rib and wing by wing,~we left our names to the silent thing.~If you would wake us, bring the four.~If you would sleep, then close the door.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_angas_: An ancient dragon burial mound in the hills north-west of Anga's Mill, older than any hold, its stones blackened as though something has stirred beneath them.
The mound above Anga's Mill was always just a hump in the snow. Now the snow won't settle on it. Melts as fast as it falls.

Folio #2 (1279, -744): Field inspection recorded for Dragon Mound Angas Mill within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #2 for dragon_mound_angas_mill: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Dragon Mound Angas Mill are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
My grandfather's grandfather was told by his grandfather that the Tongues of old buried a dragon here with its name cut into a stone, and the name was the only thing that kept it down.

On the 3rd of Frostfall the stone with the name split clean in two. I heard it from Anga's Mill like a tree coming down. Since then the snow will not lie on the mound, and the ravens that roosted on it have gone to the mill roof instead. Cut your wood somewhere else this winter.
^Brynjolf the Cutter, of Anga's Mill
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_autumn: An ancient dragon burial mound in the birch woods west of Autumnshade Clearing. The stone cap over it has been cracked across.
Hrelga Dawnmoor, Keeper of the Temple of Mara

#Second mound, Autumnshade, entered by a hired hand
The cap-stone is split from end to end, but the mound is not open. Not yet. My hired man put his ear to the crack and came back pale. He says the earth inside is warm, and that it hums.

I have left an offering to Mara and one to Akatosh, for whichever of them is listening. I have also left a note for the Jarl's steward. I expect the offerings to be the more useful of the two.

The third mound, below Lost Tongue Overlook, is next.
The mound by Autumnshade's cracked open, they say. My husband walked past it and swears he heard breathing underneath. Big breathing.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_bilegu: Ennis Hollowgate, assistant to Calvus Aterius

#27th of Hearthfire
Arrived at the Bilegulch mound. The stone cap is thrown outward, not dug inward; Master Calvus was right. The bones in the pit are gone. Scorch marks on the rim, as though something breathed fire on its way out.

#28th of Hearthfire
Three draugr walk the rim at dusk. They do not attack. They watch the sky. I think they are waiting for their master to return. I have hidden my satchel with the survey drawings in the rocks by the pit and will go down to the orcs for help. Should have gone yesterday.
A burial mound of the Dragon War on the slopes above Bilegulch Mine, split open from within. Draugr have been seen walking around it at dusk, as though on guard.
The orcs at Bilegulch say the old mound up the hill cracked open one night with a sound like a mountain coughing. Now there's dead men standing around it, waiting.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_bonest: A dragon burial mound on the ridge west of Bonestrewn Crest, its stone lid long since cracked, perhaps the very bed from which the crest's dragon rose.
That old mound by Bonestrewn Crest's empty. Lid's off. And there's a dragon roosting next door. I'm no scholar, but I can add.
The lid stone has not been broken from outside. The fractures radiate outward from the centre, as though pushed. Within: no bones, a great deal of ash, and claw marks on the inner walls.
Length of the hollow: sixty-one feet. Wingspan, by inference: considerable. Direction of departure, by scorch marks on the heather: east, toward Bonestrewn Crest, a hundred and twenty paces away.
I have stopped measuring. I recommend that whoever reads this also stop measuring, put away their quill, and walk west at a steady, unremarkable pace.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_dead_m: A dragon burial mound in the cold hills of the Hjaalmarch border, close by a haunted barrow. Two kinds of dead sleep here, and neither sleeps soundly.

Atli came in soaked and shaking and drank four meads before he would say a word. Then he said: the mound by Dead Men's Respite is open. The lid-stone is lying on its side in the snow, and there's a hole beneath like a well, going down into dark, and the air coming up out of it smells like a forge.
He swears he heard breathing. He swears something below said a word that made his ears bleed. He showed me his ears. They had bled. I gave him a fifth mead for free, and I don't do that.
Up near Dead Men's Respite there's a mound with a stone on top like a lid. Hunters say the stone's been knocked aside. Hunters say a lot of things. But they don't hunt up there any more.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_elders:
THE SEVEN CLANS OF THE MARSH LAID THE STORM-WING HERE.
THEY PAID HIM THE BLOOD OF THEIR ELDERS FOR SEVEN YEARS, AND IN THE EIGHTH THEY PAID HIM IN IRON.

HIS PERCH IS ON THE PEAK TO THE SOUTH, WHERE THE ELDERS BLED.
IF THE MOUND IS EVER EMPTY, LOOK THERE.
^Below, freshly scratched:
It's empty. The earth is thrown outward, not inward, in a ring as wide as a longhouse. Grima the herder has lost eleven head this season. Tell the Jarl. Tell the guards. Tell anyone with a bow and more courage than sense.
A dragon burial mound on the hill road south of Morthal, below Eldersblood Peak. The old marsh clans buried their storm-wing here, and the storm-wing may not have wanted to stay.
That mound on the road south of Morthal is empty now. Something dug its way out from underneath, the guards say. Dug out, mind you, not in. Then it flew up to Eldersblood Peak to sulk.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_evergr:
The Evergreen mound. Cap stone shattered outward. Burial pit empty to the bedrock. The surrounding pines are scorched on the side facing the pit but green on the far side, indicating a blast of heat from within (1).
(1) My colleagues in Cyrodiil will say I am credulous. My colleagues in Cyrodiil have not stood here.

This makes the third open mound in Falkreath Hold. I intend to compare the Evergreen mound to those near Sunderstone Gorge and Bilegulch Mine. If all three opened in the same season, then something is going from mound to mound, waking what lies inside. The local word for it is dragon. I have stopped laughing at the local word.
An ancient dragon burial mound in the pines near Evergreen Grove, its stone broken open from below. The spriggans of the grove will not go near it.
Even the spriggans keep clear of that mound by the grove. Calvus at the inn pays a septim for every rumour about it. I've given him four. Three were true.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_frokis: An ancient dragon burial mound in the woods north of Froki's Shack. Its earth has been thrown open from beneath, and nothing grows on the spoil.
Hrelga Dawnmoor, Keeper of the Temple of Mara

#First mound, near Froki's Shack, 15th of Frostfall
Opened from within. Spoil thrown outward six paces. No bones in the pit, which my old texts say is how a dragon rises: the bones are gone because they have been worn again.

The Temple asked me to count. I am counting. There are two more mounds in the Rift that I know of: one at Autumnshade Clearing, west of Riften, and one below Lost Tongue Overlook in the south. If you are braver than a temple keeper, go and see whether they are open too, and tell me in Riften. I would rather know.
Froki says the mound by his shack opened up on its own. I'd say he's mad, but my brother saw the hole, and he's not mad. He's just quieter now.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_glacia: An ancient dragon burial mound on the frozen northern coast, beyond the Glacial Cave. The Skaal shunned it for centuries; this winter the earth over it has split open.
The dragon mound past the Glacial Cave is open. Empty. A Skaal hunter saw the wings go up out of it at night, black against the aurora.

I was hunting seal on the ice when the ground shook. I saw a man in a mask standing on the mound, though there are no men out here, and he spoke, and the mound answered. Bones came up out of the earth and put on flesh as I watched. Then it flew north, and the man in the mask was gone, and I ran all the way to the village. Storn listened and said nothing for a long time, and then he went to the stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_greens:
To Irileth, Housecarl to the Jarl:
Investigated the stone mound near Greenspring Hollow as ordered. It is open. Not dug. Opened from beneath, the stones thrown outward as far as a bowshot. The pit is empty, its walls scorched black. Something left this place on its own.

The shepherds say a figure in a dark mask stood on the mound before it opened, and spoke words they did not know, and that the ground answered. I record this because they all say it, not because I believe it.

Recommend a watch on the mound and an extra guard at the Western Watchtower. Ottar.
A dragon burial mound in the western hills, its stones split open from within. Whatever slept here has woken and flown, and the earth still smells of fire.
The old burial mound near Greenspring Hollow cracked open like an egg. Shepherds heard a roar that night they say they'll never forget. Now there's nothing there but a hole and bones.
Copied the claw-script from the fallen stones at the mound's edge. Three marks repeated, the same three I saw at the mound near Shimmermist Cave. If my master is right, they are a name.

If they are a name, then each mound held a single dragon, buried under its own name like a Nord under his barrow-stone. And if each is now empty, then each name is flying somewhere over Skyrim tonight. I will not mention this to the Jarl until my master tells me to. I would rather he heard it from someone with a better title.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_greywa: A dragon burial mound in the southern hills below Greywater Grotto, torn open from within. The shepherds who saw it happen still will not speak of the night.
A shepherd south of Helgen saw that mound open. Said the ground shook, the stone flew, and something rose out of it and flew south toward Ancient's Ascent. He doesn't keep sheep anymore.
Taken down by the Falkreath steward's clerk

Account of Arnulf, shepherd, given at the Jarl's longhouse.
He states that on the night of the 2nd of Hearthfire a great black dragon flew low over his pasture and circled the old mound below Greywater Grotto. It spoke words that shook the stones. The mound split, and from it rose a second, smaller beast, dun-coloured and stinking of old earth.

The black one flew north. The dun one flew south and settled on Ancient's Ascent, where it has stayed. The shepherd requests the hold compensate him for eleven sheep. The steward has noted that the hold does not compensate for dragons. The shepherd has noted that he would like to see the steward tell the dragon that.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_harmug: Brother Valmund, of the Returning Wing
Brothers, the masters return. The mound at Dragontooth Crater is empty. The mound at the Lover Stone is empty. The dragon priests of old were not fools, they were wise, and we shall be wise again.

This mound has not yet opened. The master inside sleeps deeper than the rest. We shall wake him with blood and chanting, and when he rises, he will remember who knelt first.
Bring the shepherds from Karthwasten. Bring the goats if you cannot find shepherds. The master is not particular, or so I hope.
A dragon burial mound in the high hills north of Harmugstahl. Robed figures have been seen chanting over its broken stones by moonlight.
Folks in Karthwasten have seen robed men chanting at the old mound north of Harmugstahl. Dragon worshippers, in this day and age. Nothing good ever came of praying to something with teeth.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_kagrum: A dragon burial mound in the ash hills east of Kagrumez. The Telvanni once studied it and the Skaal once avoided it. Now there is nothing in it at all.
The dragon mound near Kagrumez is a hole in the ground now. Some say a Telvanni dug it up for research. Others say something climbed out by itself.

The mound east of Kagrumez is open from within; the earth is thrown outward, not dug inward. Depth of the hollow: nine paces. Length: twenty-two. No bones. Scorching on the north lip, consistent with dragon fire. I have consulted the Skaal, who were unhelpful, and the master, who was less helpful still and asked whether I had finished my work at Kagrumez yet. I had not. I went back to Kagrumez. One does not argue with an empty grave of that size.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_karths: A broken dragon burial mound on the slopes below the Karthspire. Whatever slept inside it has already risen, and the scorched earth around it has not yet regrown.

Dear cousin in Whiterun,
You laughed at me when I wrote about dragons. Laugh at this: on the 14th of Second Seed, the mound below Karthspire split open like an egg. A huge black dragon circled above it, shouting down into the earth, and then a second dragon dug its way up out of the ground and they both flew off toward Sky Haven.

Pa says the Forsworn at Karthspire Camp were so frightened they came down to the mine and asked to shelter with us. We let them. They slept in the lower gallery. They've gone now. The dragon hasn't come back. Neither has my good sense.
The mound below Karthspire burst open in the spring. Miners at Soljund's Sinkhole saw a dragon fly out of it like a hawk from a box. Haven't slept well since.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_kynesg: An ancient dragon burial mound on the ridge east of Kynesgrove, its great stones overlooking the village like a sleeping beast's spine.

From the oldest days, the families of Kynesgrove have kept a custom at the mound: on the first day of First Seed, each household brings a cup of spring water and pours it out on the highest stone, for Kyne, who wept the springs.
The children are told that the water keeps the dragon cool and drowsy. The adults say it is only a custom. The adults also never miss it.
This year, for the first time in my keeping, the water hissed as it touched the stone and rose as steam. I have not told the village. I have only begun to pour twice as much.
The mound above Kynesgrove's been there longer than Windhelm. The miners say on still nights the ground hums from the mound to the mine. I've felt it. Through my boots.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_lost_t: A dragon burial mound in the hills below Lost Tongue Overlook. The ground around it is scorched black in a perfect circle.
Hrelga Dawnmoor, Keeper of the Temple of Mara

#Third mound, below Lost Tongue Overlook
The ground is scorched in a ring twenty paces across. The mound itself is whole, but at its crown sits a great split, and from the split a thin smoke rises without any fire beneath it.

Three mounds: one open, one cracked, one smoking. I am not a scholar, only a keeper of candles. But I know what a pot looks like before it boils.

I shall write to the Jarl. I shall write to Whiterun, where they say a dragon was killed this year. And I shall pray, because there is nothing else that a keeper of candles is good for.
The mound below Lost Tongue's burnt round like someone drew a circle in fire. I don't know if something went in or came out. Either way, I'm not going.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_meekos: A grassy burial mound south of the Solitude Sawmill, ringed by old stones. The Nords of the Dragon War buried something here, and it may not have stayed buried.
There's a mound in the hills below the sawmill that the old men call a dragon's grave. Nonsense, of course. Though the grass on it doesn't grow, and the crows won't land.

MOVE YOUR FLOCK.
Three nights ago the ground on the mound shook like a horse shaking off flies. My ewes ran half the way to the sawmill.

This morning the big stone on top had moved a hand's width toward the north. Nothing moves that stone. My grandfather said the old Nords put a dragon under it in the war with the dragons, and that the stone is the lid. I always laughed. I'm not laughing. Graze somewhere else.
I've told the foreman at the sawmill and the Stormcloaks camped in the hills, since they were nearer than the Legion. The sawmill laughed. The Stormcloaks didn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_mzulft:
#1st of Hearthfire
Curious: Dwemer brass fittings and a broken digging-arm embedded in the slope of an ancient Nord burial mound below Mzulft. The arm points into the mound, as if the Dwemer dug toward it.

The digging stopped abruptly. The arm is bent backward, as though it struck something harder than itself. I have found three scorched Dwemer bolts in the turf and a gouge in the brass four fingers wide.
Hypothesis: the Dwemer dug for something here and found a dragon. Recommendation to myself: do not do what the Dwemer did. Go to Mzulft instead. Bertrand will laugh at the irony.
A dragon burial mound on the steaming slopes south-west of Mzulft, half-buried in old Dwemer rubble, as though the deep folk once tried to dig it out and thought better of it.
There's a dragon mound by Mzulft with Dwemer gears in the dirt around it. Scholars argue over why. I reckon even the Dwemer knew better than to wake one.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_pale_i: An ancient dragon burial mound near the Legion camp on the western Pale coast. It steams in the frost, and the soldiers have stopped joking about it.

To Quartermaster Ostorian.
Night picket at the old mound. Third night running it has steamed in the frost. Last night two figures in old Nord armour stood on the top of it until dawn, facing the sky, motionless. When the sun came up they walked down into the ground. Through it, I mean.
The men are frightened. I am not frightened, sir. I am merely recommending that somebody with more experience of the dead than a Legion picket look at it before something comes out of it with wings.
The mound south of the Legion camp has been steaming like a kettle. Old graves don't steam. Not unless something under them is warm.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_roriks: An ancient dragon burial mound on the plains north-west of Rorikstead. Farmers plough around it in a wide circle, and their grandfathers did the same.
PLOUGH NO NEARER THAN THIS STONE.

My grandfather put this stone here and his grandfather put the one before it. They say the old Nords buried a dragon under the mound and set a ward on it, and that a plough-blade would break the ward like a knife through a seal. I don't know if that's true. I know the mound steams on frosty mornings now, which it never used to, and I know my horse won't pass this stone. I'm trusting the horse.
There's a mound west of Rorikstead we never plough. Grandfather said it was a dragon's grave. I always thought he meant it as a joke. Lately the ground there's been warm.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_shimme:
Court Wizard,
You asked to be told of any old stone mounds that look disturbed. There is one on the hill above Shimmermist Cave. I passed it on the 11th and the capstone was in place. I passed it on the 13th and it lay thirty paces down the slope, broken in two.

Inside, a pit, and scorch marks, and a great rib bone as long as my bow. I took a splinter of it for you, as you asked, wrapped in my spare scarf. You owe me a scarf.

The Falmer from the cave below were out on the hill in daylight, all of them facing the empty mound. I did not stay to see why. Hedda.
A ring of ancient stones on a hill above Shimmermist Cave, marking a dragon's grave. The ring has been cracked, and the grass inside will not grow back.
There's an old mound above Shimmermist Cave. Hunters say the stones sing in the wind now, where they never did before. Some of the bones inside are big as a man.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_sunder: Sunderstone mound. Diameter of pit: nineteen paces. Depth: four men. Cap stone thrown thirty paces to the northeast. Same pattern as Evergreen. The skeleton is gone and so are the grave goods, if there were any.

Master Calvus wants Bilegulch done by the end of the month. It is a day's walk west, past the orc mine, and the orcs throw rocks at anyone who comes near. I have bought a jar of honey to give them. I am told Orcs like honey. I am told a great many things.
A Dragon War burial mound on the high ground north of Sunderstone Gorge, its pit empty and its rim blackened. Scholars come, measure it, and leave in a hurry.
Somebody's been camping by the old mound north of Sunderstone. Breton fellow, ink on his fingers. Haven't seen him in a while. Hope he moved on.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_the_lo: An ancient dragon burial mound in the hills between the Lover Stone and the Legion's camp. Its stones have been pushed outward from within.
The legionaries at the Reach camp won't stand watch facing that mound to the south. Say it moved. Say something climbed out of it. They're soldiers, not poets, so maybe it's true.

Sir, I was on night watch on the 9th of Frostfall. At the third bell the ground to the south shook. I saw the stones of the burial mound fly apart and something large rise out of it, black against the stars.

It flew north over the camp. It did not attack. It did not need to. I have been told to write that I saw a large bird. I saw a large bird, sir. A large bird that roared in words I could feel in my teeth. Request a transfer to Cyrodiil, sir.

place_lore.nirncraft.dragon_mound_witchm: Things that are true about the mound: The goats will not eat there. The mist from Witchmist Grove comes up the slope and sits on it like a hat. On cold mornings there is no frost on it, only wet.
Things Grandfather says are true about the mound: Something is sleeping inside with its name in its mouth. If you say the name you wake it. Nobody knows the name. That is the point.
I put my ear to it once. It was warm. I did not hear anything. Grandfather says that is because it was holding its breath.
A dragon burial mound on the slopes north-west of Witchmist Grove, where the mist of the springs gathers thickest and the old folk of Kynesgrove will not let their goats graze.
The goats won't go near the mound above Witchmist Grove. Goats'll eat a boot. They won't eat the grass on that mound. Tells you something.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragonstar.arena_od:
^ODDS OF THE SEVEN, THIS SEASON
^Pit, first bout: even.
^Pit, second: seven to five on the bandits.
^Pit, third: three to one against the bears.
^Ring, first: Brakka, two to one.
^Ring, second: Zenda, even; do not bet on Zenda.
^Star, first: the Unbeaten, ten to one against.
^The seventh bout has no odds. It is not listed. It is not spoken of. If you are told to bet on it, bet nothing, and leave the arena by the south gate. It is a very old rule of the house.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragonstar.hook: A crossroads of fighters and gamblers under the arena's great stone star, where everyone is a bettor and nobody is ever sure what they have bet on.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragonstar.rumour: In Dragonstar a man will take any bet. Ask him the odds on a stranger and he will give you three. He will have a fourth for himself.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena.ho: At place.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the star-carved Nede plateaus and border canyons of Craglorn between Elinhir, Belkarth, and Dragonstar Arena.
place_lore.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena.ru: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena report signs of Scaled Court serpent-cultists, fixed-bout arena brokers, and Skyreach blood-exarchs operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the star-carved Nede plateaus and border canyons of Craglorn between Elinhir, Belkarth, and Dragonstar Arena. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.dragonstar_arena have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by Scaled Court serpent-cultists, fixed-bout arena brokers, and Skyreach blood-exarchs. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.
A crater blasted into the Reach highlands, its rim jagged like a broken jaw. A dragon has made its lair on the scorched stone, and the hunters of Karthwasten no longer go north.

#14th of Frostfall
Watched it from the rim all morning. Grey-green scales, a notch out of the left wing. It sleeps in the middle of the crater with its head toward Harmugstahl. The miners at Karthwasten call it the Goat-Thief. The Greybeards would call it something else, I suppose.

#15th of Frostfall
Went closer. It woke. It spoke. I do not know the words but I felt them in my teeth, like the hum at Deep Folk Crossing. Burned my bow arm. I'm writing this left-handed.

#16th of Frostfall
I cannot climb the rim with this arm. If you read this, kill it. Aim under the jaw, where the scales are thin. I put an arrow there before it burned me and it bled.
There's a dragon roosting at Dragontooth Crater, plain as day. Comes down on the Karthwasten goats every few days. Somebody ought to do something, and by somebody I mean not me.

place_lore.nirncraft.drajkmyr_fishery.ru: The fishers at Drajkmyr burn bog-myrtle in their smokehouses just to keep the marsh-wisps from drifting into the nets.
place_lore.nirncraft.drajkmyr_fishery.wa: Twenty baskets of river-betty and nine crates of salted mudcrab claws loaded onto the flat-bottomed punt for Morthal market. Do not set eel-lines past the third reed-channel toward High Gate; the water there smells of old bronze and grave-linen.

place_lore.nirncraft.drelas_cottage.arca:
Drelas,
It has been five months. I lent you my good alembic, the Breton glass one with the silver stopper, and my copy of the Ingredients of the Tundra, because you said you would return both by Midyear. It is now Hearthfire.

I have asked politely twice. The courier who brought my second letter came back with singed eyebrows and refused to go again. I am not a patient woman, but I am a fair one. Send them back, or I will send someone who is neither patient nor fair.

Arcadia, Arcadia's Cauldron, Whiterun.
place_lore.nirncraft.drelas_cottage.drel: Third binding. The atronach answered faster tonight. I think it likes the cottage. It certainly likes the smell of Arcadia's alembic heating, which is why I have not returned it. Her glass holds the heat better than anything I own.

The Nords in Whiterun call me a witch. Good. Witches are left alone. The last courier fled when the atronach so much as looked at him, which saves me writing replies.

Note: the summoning circle must be redrawn every third night in salt and fire salts mixed. If the circle fails, so does the leash. Do not let the circle fail.
place_lore.nirncraft.drelas_cottage.hook: A neat little cottage in the western hills, smelling of brimstone and lavender. The Dunmer mage who lives there does not welcome visitors, and her fire atronach welcomes them even less.
place_lore.nirncraft.drelas_cottage.rumo: There's a Dunmer witch in a cottage out west. Arcadia lent her an alembic and a book of recipes, and got a scorched letter back telling her to come and collect them herself.

place_lore.nirncraft.driftshade_refuge.c:
My name is Aldis and I am not a beast. I am a trapper from Nightgate. They found wolf fur in my pack and said that was proof enough.
I have counted nineteen days by the light under the door. The man in the next cell changed on the eleventh night. He was a beast after all. I am not. I am not. I am not.
If you read this, tell my mother at Nightgate Inn I was not what they said.
place_lore.nirncraft.driftshade_refuge.h: An old stone refuge in the snows of the southern Winterhold hills. Hunters of a different kind have moved in, and the howls at night come from inside the walls.
place_lore.nirncraft.driftshade_refuge.r: Driftshade Refuge has been taken over by men with silver blades. They say they hunt beasts. They don't seem to care who they hurt doing it.
place_lore.nirncraft.driftshade_refuge.s:
Brothers,
The refuge is ours and the dogs know it. Every one we take alive goes to the cellar. Every one we take dead goes on the wall. Their kind is a sickness and we are the cure.

Watch the roads to Fort Fellhammer and Snowpoint Beacon. Strangers who ask too many questions about the cellar are either beasts in man-skin or friends of beasts. Either way, silver works on both.
No mercy. No bargains. No howling back.
Krev's addendum: the trapper we took at Nightgate swears he's no beast. Keep him anyway. If he's honest, the full moon will tell us. If he's lying, the full moon will tell us faster.

Post double sentries on the western scree where the briar-hearts prowl after moonset. No foraging parties are to go below the tree-line in groups smaller than six, and all silver taken from intercepted wagons goes straight to the war-chest.
place_lore.nirncraft.druadach_redoubt.he:
Brought in from the raid at the Karthwasten road: three. Arrow in the thigh, axe in the shoulder, one who will not wake.
From Broken Tower: one, Nord sword cut. He laughs about it. Let him laugh, it is good for the blood.
Needed from the woods: snowberries, nightshade for the one who will not wake, if he does not wake by the moon's end.
To any Reachman who reads: Druadach is not for war. Do not bring the hearts of Nords to these fires. Bring them to Deepwood and to the crones, who want such things. Here we keep only our own alive.
place_lore.nirncraft.druadach_redoubt.ho: A cave in the Druadach range that has sheltered Reachmen since before the Nords had a word for them. Its fires are where the Forsworn come to mend, mourn and plan.
place_lore.nirncraft.druadach_redoubt.ru: Druadach Redoubt is the Forsworn's home hearth. Every Briarheart that ever raided a farm went there to have his wounds sewn up.

place_lore.nirncraft.dune.fortune_card.p:
#THE WELL
A card of a woman kneeling at a well, a coin held out in her paw. On the back, scratched in a quick hand: 'Whoever draws this at the Wheel will be thirsty before the third night. Go by Nevoe, not by Temar. The Temar water has a man standing in it.'
In the margin, in a different ink: 'Do not tell Khir. He does not believe in cards. He believes in knots, and knots have not once told him anything useful.'
place_lore.nirncraft.dune.hook: A caravan crossroads shaped like a wheel: eight lanes of striped tents around a round market, camel pens at the rim, and a city that always seems about to leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.dune.rumour: Dune has eight lanes, but on the Wheel they count seven, and never explain why. Ask a camel-driver about the eighth and watch her change the subject to water.
place_lore.nirncraft.dune.toll_notice.p0:
^BY THE WHEEL, FOR THE WHEEL
^Each cart pays a copper at the hub, no more, no less. Carts that are late, early or unnamed shall be counted twice.
place_lore.nirncraft.dune.toll_notice.p1: Camel-drivers are reminded that the Eighth Lane is not a shortcut. It is not a lane. It does not appear on any map, and persons found using it shall be fined, and then thanked, in that order.

place_lore.nirncraft.dushnikh_yal.hook: An Orc stronghold in a mountain bowl south of Markarth, built around a smithy and a mine and a code older than Skyrim. Outsiders are tolerated if useful, and remembered if not.
place_lore.nirncraft.dushnikh_yal.malaca:
Malacath, keeper of the sworn word, the broken and the scorned.
I do not ask you for mercy. You do not have any to give.
I ask for a strong arm and a long memory, so that I remember every Nord who called us beasts at the Markarth gate, and so that my sons remember it after me.
And if there is a little mercy left over, Furious One, let the snow come late this year. The goats are thin.
place_lore.nirncraft.dushnikh_yal.rumour: Dushnikh Yal pays honest coin for honest work. Steal from them once and you'll find out what Malacath does with oathbreakers.
place_lore.nirncraft.dushnikh_yal.sk4_no: Folio #7 (-2623, 243): Field inspection recorded for Dushnikh Yal within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.dushnikh_yal.wives_:
Orichalcum from our own mine: 12 ingots. Good.
Iron traded from Markarth: 20 ingots. Bad iron, Nord iron, full of slag. Bring back the same factor and I take his ear.
Charcoal: low. Send the young ones to the woods past Reachwind Eyrie, not the woods by Arkngthamz. Not after last time.

Murbol wants to go after the grave-robbers at Reachwater Rock who sold him a cursed axe. Chief says it is his own honour to mend. I say Murbol is too proud to ask for help and too stubborn to die. One of those will end first.

place_lore.nirncraft.dusk.hook: A crescent harbour city under pale dunes, lilac in the evening, with a tall lantern tower and low pastel houses that never seem quite awake before dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.dusk.lamp_rota.p0:
#LIGHTING ORDER
Lantern Tower first, then the quay, then the south wall in order, east to west. The last lamp, the south one, is lit with a separate match, struck with the left hand. Do not ask why. Say nothing while it is lit. Do not look at it when it goes out.
place_lore.nirncraft.dusk.lamp_rota.p1: Below, in a child's hand: 'Grandfather lit it every night and never said who for. I think it was for Grandmother, who went out on the Seventh, and who said she would come back by lantern.'
place_lore.nirncraft.dusk.rumour: Everything in Dusk is a little off-colour. Not ill; just late. The bread, the sails, the sun: they all arrive an hour behind the rest of Tamriel and are quietly offended when it is mentioned.
place_lore.nirncraft.duskglow_crevice.co:
If someone from Dunstad finds this: the case is under me. I kept hold of it. They dragged me down here alive and I kept hold of it the whole way.
They do not speak but they understand each other. They pass things hand to hand in the dark. They have a priest with a staff of chaurus shell, and they keep looking at me the way you look at a meal.
Tell my sister in Bruma I was not a coward. Tell the commander I want my nine septims from Felix.
place_lore.nirncraft.duskglow_crevice.ho: A crack in the earth in the southern Pale where a warm, sickly glow rises from below. The Falmer who live there have been raiding further from home than ever.
place_lore.nirncraft.duskglow_crevice.ru: There's a glow in the cliffs at Duskglow, like a lantern behind a curtain. That's Falmer fungus. Where you see it, they're watching you.
place_lore.nirncraft.duskglow_crevice.sk: Folio #15 (415, -1059): Field inspection recorded for Duskglow Crevice within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.
