place_lore.nirncraft.dustmans_cairn.hamv:
Brother,
The ones from the cairn came to Hamvir's Rest again asking for a guide. I told them I know nothing of the cairn. They paid me anyway and asked what the Companions of Whiterun look like, how many there are, where they drink. I told them the Bannered Mare. Maybe I shouldn't have.
The stew is still bad here. The view is still good. Come visit when the roads are safe, which is never.

Postscript: Last night one of them came back from the cairn alone and bleeding, shouting about a wolf that walked on two legs and wore a woman's face. His friends hushed him and paid for the room in silver. I've hidden the silver under the floor. It feels like the kind of coin somebody comes back for.
place_lore.nirncraft.dustmans_cairn.hook: A Nordic barrow on the plains west of Whiterun, near Hamvir's Rest. Its draugr guard a fragment of an old and famous blade, and armed strangers have been seen going down its steps.
place_lore.nirncraft.dustmans_cairn.rumo: Dustman's Cairn? Bad place. Lately men in silver-trimmed armour have been seen going in. Werewolf hunters, my brother says. Hunting what, in a tomb?
place_lore.nirncraft.dustmans_cairn.sk4_: Folio #3 (-592, -407): Field inspection recorded for Dustmans Cairn within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #3 for dustmans_cairn: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Dustmans Cairn are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.dustmans_cairn.surv: Dustman's Cairn lies on the old boundary between Whiterun Hold and the Reach, which means both Jarls claim it and neither wants to pay to have it guarded. Entrance faces east. Steps descend steeply. Air smells of grave-dust and, oddly, fresh wolf.

Saw armed men in mismatched steel enter at dusk. They wore silver hand badges. When I asked their business, the tall one said, 'Hunting dogs.' I do not keep dogs, and I left.
Recommend the barrow be marked on hold maps as dangerous and left well alone, by order of both Jarls, which they will never agree on.

place_lore.nirncraft.east_empire_company: The ledger-house of the Company in Ebonheart, where silk, steel and sugar pass through the same polite door.

#Re: the parrot
The bird repeats: 'Four hundred and twelve. Silk. Pay at dusk. Do not tell the Factor.' I have asked the clerks. They know nothing. The bird knows everything and is not forthcoming.

Please: no one is to teach it further phrases until we have identified its former owner.
A Company parrot in the customs yard has been repeating a sum for three days: four hundred and twelve, in a Hlaalu accent. Nobody knows if it is a price, a ransom or a lottery.
place_lore.nirncraft.eastmarch_imperial_:
#7th of Frostfall, 4E 201
Camp holds. Rebel patrols probe the north perimeter every third night and withdraw. Morale fair, rations poor. The hot springs keep the men from freezing; they also make the camp smell like a boiled egg.

Supply: two wagons of arrows and salt pork lost this month at the Stony Creek ford, eighty paces from our own pickets. Not rebels. Bandits from the cave south of camp, who know our schedule better than our sergeants do.

I cannot spare a cohort to clear one cave. I can spare coin to anyone who will. Recommend a reward be posted at the camp gate for the head of their chief, a Redguard who calls herself Nazira the Ford-Keeper.
A Legion war camp pitched in the hot-spring hills south-east of Mzulft, deep in Ulfric's own hold, its soldiers watching Windhelm's roads and very much unwelcome.
There's a Legion camp past Mzulft, cheeky as you like, right on Ulfric's doorstep. The Stormcloaks say they'll burn it out by spring. They said that last spring too.

Dear Mother,
You asked what Skyrim is like. It is like Cheydinhal if Cheydinhal had been sat on by a mountain and then set on fire underneath. The ground steams. The rivers are warm. The people are not.
We are camped near a Dwemer ruin called Mzulft. Old Decius says there are blind elves in it who eat men. Old Decius says many things, but I have noticed he sleeps with his sword these days.
Do not worry. Tell Father I polish my boots every morning. Tell Julia I have not met anyone. Tell yourself I will be home for Midyear, and I will try to make it true.
place_lore.nirncraft.ebonheart.dock_ledg:
#Arrivals, Last Seed
The Abecean Rose from Anvil: wine, salt, and an inspector from the Company's head office. Inspector given the best room and the worst figures we could find, so as to set expectations.

#Departures, Last Seed
The Ondusi Gull for Windhelm: kwama eggs, saltrice, three crates of 'Telvanni pottery'. The pottery hums. Passengers: two Orc masons for the Malacath festival, one widow, one Bosmer who would not stop asking whether the ship was haunted. It is not. That we know of.
place_lore.nirncraft.ebonheart.garrison_: Tribune Marcus Salvo, Legion of Morrowind

To the Legate at Cyrodiil:
Strength this quarter: one hundred and twelve, of whom nineteen are sick, eleven are Dunmer levies who answer to their Houses before me, and four are, frankly, too old to hold a spear upright.

The Argonians patrol their bank of the border openly now. They wave. I have ordered my men not to wave back. My men wave back.
I repeat my request for two cohorts. I would accept one. I would accept a single competent sergeant. I would accept a letter telling me that anyone in the Imperial City remembers Ebonheart is still ours.
place_lore.nirncraft.ebonheart.gazetteer:
#Garrison and Company
Legate Corvus Pello wants order and a name by evening. Chaplain Loris hears the garrison's confessions, which are short. Felmin Rothal at the Company Hall will discuss margins openly; it is the only thing the Company does not hide. Guardsman Tolan Veyl keeps the south gate and an eye on his mother's medicine.

#The Quarter and its fixers
Aryn the Informer stands lower than anyone else and charges for the view. Marga Ironhand's Bastion's Heel serves two kinds of beer; ask for the one the garrison pretends it does not drink. Three guards salute a stone in the ash-flowers each dusk. Nobody has mentioned it to the Legate.
place_lore.nirncraft.ebonheart.hook: An old Imperial fortress-port on the Stonefalls coast, black-walled and salt-stained, where the East Empire Company and the Legion hang on in Morrowind with fewer men every year.
place_lore.nirncraft.ebonheart.rumour: Ebonheart's all Legion and Company, which these days means half a garrison and a lot of unpaid ledgers. Go to the docks if you want work. Go to the Sanguine stones south-east if you want a party.

place_lore.nirncraft.eight_plates.hook: A Hlaalu stew-house on the river road, famous for exactly eight plates a night and the one guest who is never served.
place_lore.nirncraft.eight_plates.plate_:
#By order of the house
Eight plates a night. Never nine. The ninth guest is welcomed, seated and talked to, and told that the stew has run out. It is a policy, not a shortage. Anyone found sharing their bowl with the ninth guest will be thanked, quietly, and asked to speak of it to nobody.

If a girl in a grey cloak asks, she is a regular. She is to be served first, and charged nothing, and never asked her name.
place_lore.nirncraft.eight_plates.rumour: Eight Plates will not serve a ninth, no matter the coin. Folk say a grey-cloaked girl sits at the end of the bench each night, and the keeper leaves out a ninth plate she will not touch.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_hollow.hook: The great hollow at the root of the Elden Tree, where the market sprawls between arched roots and the sap-lanterns burn amber in the green dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_hollow.root_m:
#RATES
Sap-lantern wick, a copper. Bark-tea, two. A night in the hollow-inn, six, with the tree's blessing, nine, without. Meat, any, fresh: one silver. Meat, aged, a quarter silver and a note of apology to the cook.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_hollow.rumour: Everyone in Elden Hollow looks up when they speak. It is a courtesy to the tree, and has become a habit, and has made the Hollow the best place in Valenwood to pick a pocket.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_root.hook: The living capital of Valenwood, built in the boughs of a single colossal graht-oak, where the Silvenar speaks for the Bosmer, the Spinners tell their tales, and Thalmor Justiciars listen to both.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_root.meat_man:
Grandson,
You write from Alinor that the Altmer eat greens and grains and call us savages for eating only meat. Tell them that Y'ffre sang the forest into shape and asked only that we not harm it. Tell them we keep that promise every day, with every meal, and that they cannot say as much for their promises to anyone.

Tell them also, very politely, that the Meat Mandate allows a Bosmer to eat an enemy fallen in battle within three days. Then smile, and show your teeth. That usually ends the dinner. Come home for the Felling Moon festival. I am making jerked boar with redberry wine sauce, and I will not tell you whose recipe it was.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_root.rumour: Elden Root's lovely from below and lovelier from above. Just don't say anything about the Thalmor on the high walks. The wind carries. So do the Justiciars.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_root.spinners: Told by a Spinner of Elden Root, set down by a Breton listener

Before there were Bosmer there were only the hungry and the hunted, and Y'ffre could not tell which was which. So the Storyteller made a bargain with the Huntsman: the forest would be his hunting ground, and the people his hounds, and in return the hounds would never become the hunted, so long as they kept the Pact.

The Huntsman's stone stands north-west of the great tree to this day. The Bosmer hunters leave the first kill of the year there, and say the old words. The Spinner who told me this tale laughed when I asked whether the Huntsman ever broke his side of the bargain. 'He never has,' she said. 'We have. And then he came hunting.'
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_root.thalmor_: First Emissary Lirinwe, for the Aldmeri Dominion

^ORDINANCE CONCERNING OBSERVANCES OF A DAEDRIC CHARACTER
The Dominion respects the customs of its Bosmeri subjects, including the Green Pact, which it has never sought to amend. The Dominion does not, however, extend that respect to the worship of Daedric Princes, which is an affront to the Aldmeri inheritance and an ongoing embarrassment.

Accordingly, the shrine north of the city, where certain persons gather to petition the Taskmaster for cures, is placed under observation. Names of petitioners will be recorded. No arrests are contemplated at present. Citizens are reminded that 'at present' is a precise phrase, and that the Dominion uses language precisely.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_tree.hook: The great tree itself, seen from the whole province, with a glow at its crown at night and a trunk wide enough to hold a city in its bark.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_tree.rumour: People say the Elden Tree has never dropped a leaf. People who live under it say it has, and that you do not want to find it, because it is shaped like a hand.
place_lore.nirncraft.elden_tree.sap_char:
^TREE OF ALL ROOTS, KEEP US.
^TREE OF ALL BOUGHS, HOLD US.
^TREE OF ALL LEAVES, FORGIVE US OUR FIRES, OUR AXES AND OUR HUNGER.
Below the carving, a child has scratched a small, very round face, with the words: 'Thank you for not minding.'
place_lore.nirncraft.eldergleam_sanctuar:
~Before the elves, before the men,
~Before the Dwemer sang below,
~The Gleam stood tall in Kyne's green glen
~And drank the springs and let them flow.

~And if you come with fire or blade
~To take a bough to warm your hall,
~The path you walked will fail and fade,
~And you will find no home at all.
A hidden cave north of Darkwater Crossing that opens onto a sunlit hollow and the Eldergleam itself, the oldest tree in Skyrim, tended by pilgrims and guarded by its spriggans.

Written by many hands in one leather-bound book chained to a root:
'Came from Bravil to see it. Wept. Not ashamed.' - Junia
'Asked it to heal my son's lungs. Will write when I know.' - Hrodmar of Darkwater Crossing

'Son is well. I walked back here barefoot to say so. Feet are not well. Worth it.' - Hrodmar
'The spriggans watched me the whole time. One of them touched my hair. I have never felt so carefully examined.' - an anonymous Bosmer
'To whoever brought an axe in here on the 4th of Frostfall: we found what was left of you, and buried it at the cave mouth, which is more than the tree would have done.' - the keepers
Pilgrims walk all the way from Cyrodiil to touch the Eldergleam. Just don't let them see you with an axe anywhere near the hollow. The spriggans don't take kindly to it, and neither do the pilgrims.

place_lore.nirncraft.eldersblood_peak.he:
#Hearthfire
Lost the brindle cow. Found only the bell, up near Eldersblood. The ground there is scorched in a circle wider than our longhouse.

#Frostfall
Watched it from the Cold Rock Pass. Grey as storm cloud, with a scar across one eye. It sits on the old stone ring at the summit at dawn and roars, and then it flies over the marsh, slow, like a man walking his fields. Like it owns them.
#Later in Frostfall
I've lost eleven head. I have nothing left to lose but the farm and my sons. My sons want to go up with spears. I have forbidden it. I am writing this so that if they go anyway, someone knows where they went.
place_lore.nirncraft.eldersblood_peak.ho: A storm-battered peak above the marshes, crowned with an ancient dragon perch. A great dragon has claimed it, and the cattle of half of Hjaalmarch have learned to fear the sky.
place_lore.nirncraft.eldersblood_peak.ri:
THE BLOOD OF THE ELDERS WAS SPILLED HERE TO FEED THE STORM-WING.
SEVEN ELDERS OF THE MARSH CLANS, ONE FOR EACH SEASON THE STORM-WING SPARED THEM.

THE STORM-WING SLEEPS BENEATH THE MOUND.
WHEN HE WAKES, HE WILL WANT THE OLD PRICE.
LET THE MARSH CLANS REMEMBER WHAT THEY PAID, AND PAY IT IN IRON INSTEAD.
THE IRON WAS PAID ON THE EIGHTH YEAR, AT THE POINT OF A HUNDRED SPEARS, AND THE STORM-WING FELL. BUT DRAGONS DO NOT DIE AS MEN DIE. THEY WAIT.
place_lore.nirncraft.eldersblood_peak.ru: There's a dragon on Eldersblood Peak, sure as I'm standing here. Takes a cow a week. The Jarl's sent word to Solitude, and Solitude's sent word back: it's a Hjaalmarch dragon, Hjaalmarch can deal with it.
place_lore.nirncraft.elinhir.astronomer_: Magister Hadiya Sel-Nur, Keeper of the Lenses

#To the Lord Warden of Elinhir, 23rd of Last Seed
My lord, for the third time: the great lens of the Serpent Tower has been stolen. It was ground by Yokudan glassmakers before the Crossing. It cannot be replaced, and without it we cannot chart the Serpent's movement through the Craglorn sky this winter.

The thieves were seen heading south toward the shrine of the Night Mistress beyond the city. Everyone in Elinhir knows the thieves' crews of Craglorn make their offerings there. Everyone, it appears, except the Watch. If the Watch will not fetch it back, I will pay whoever does. I will pay handsomely. I will even stop complaining, for a season.
place_lore.nirncraft.elinhir.caravan_not:
^TO ALL DROVERS ON THE WAYREST ROAD
Do not water your beasts at the springs north of the city below the spiked shrine. Two caravans have found the water hot as a kettle and red as a wound, and a third has not been found at all.

The Ansei of the Crowns rode up last week and came back silent. They have asked the Lord Warden for fire-wards and twenty more swords. Until the springs run clear, take the long road by Bangkorai. It costs three days. It is cheaper than a funeral.
place_lore.nirncraft.elinhir.hook: A city of mages and star-watchers on the edge of Craglorn, whose towers hold observatories older than the Empire and whose scholars argue, very loudly, about what the constellations are about to do.
place_lore.nirncraft.elinhir.rumour: Elinhir's mages say the Craglorn stars move when nobody's looking. Then they all stay up looking. Nobody in that city has slept properly in a hundred years.

place_lore.nirncraft.embershard_mine.for:
To Lucan Valerius at the Riverwood Trader, to be posted for the men,
We were paid for the season the day before they came. Twelve of us, two hundred and forty septims, in the iron chest in my office past the smelter. The bandits came over the ridge from the Guardian Stones at dawn and we ran with nothing but our picks.

The leader is a man called Skarn Two-Pick, who used to dig for us and was let go for drinking. He knows every shaft. He knows where the chest is. If any sword-arm passing through Riverwood will get our pay back, the men will gladly give a share of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.embershard_mine.hoo: An iron mine in the hills between Riverwood and the Guardian Stones, taken over by bandits who now dig its ore and sell it to anyone with gold.
place_lore.nirncraft.embershard_mine.rum: The miners of Embershard got run out by bandits last spring. They're still owed their wages, and the bandits are sitting on the paychest.
place_lore.nirncraft.embershard_mine.sk4: Folio #18 (-184, 792): Field inspection recorded for Embershard Mine within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.embershard_mine.ska:
Ore goes out on Middas to the buyer at the Guardian Stones. Not Riverwood, not Whiterun, they know the Embershard mark. Grind it off first.
The paychest stays in my room till the Fredas share-out. Anyone who touches it before Fredas loses a finger, and you know I keep count.
And stop dropping the lift on the lower shaft. That's how the old crew lost Bjorn and I didn't steal this mine to dig your graves in it.

P.S. The old crew's foreman wrote to Riverwood begging for a sellsword. If anybody comes up the path with a sword and a sense of justice, give them the lower shaft. It's always wet down there and nobody'll hear.

place_lore.nirncraft.evergreen_grove.dru:
~In the grove where the pine-mother sings,
~Every root is a promise she keeps,
~Lay down axe, lay down blade, lay down rings,
~Walk soft where the green lady sleeps.

A slate tablet with the verse scratched in a careful, old-fashioned hand, propped against a stump that has begun to sprout new branches.
Below the verse, a smaller line: 'Written by one who cut here once and was forgiven. The grove does not forgive twice.' The stump the tablet rests against has the marks of an old axe, and from those marks new green shoots are growing.
place_lore.nirncraft.evergreen_grove.hoo: A sunlit grove hidden in the pines south of Lake Ilinalta, where the trees grow strangely tall and spriggans tend them like a garden. Nothing that dies there stays dead for long.
place_lore.nirncraft.evergreen_grove.lum: To all cutters working for Half-Moon Mill: no timber is to be taken from the grove south of the lake, whatever the size of the trees. I know they are tall. I know they are straight. Three men tried last autumn. One axe is still in the trunk of the big pine and the tree has grown around it to the haft. The men did not come back. Cut on the north shore.
The notice is nailed to a pine at the edge of the grove. Someone has nailed a second scrap beneath it, in a ragged hand: 'Went in anyway. Big pine said no. Left my axe. Not going back for it. Ulf.'
place_lore.nirncraft.evergreen_grove.rum: There's a grove past the mill where it's always spring. Lovely, if you like being watched by trees. My grandfather said Kynareth sleeps there. My grandmother said, don't wake her.
place_lore.nirncraft.evergreen_grove.sk4: Folio #21 (-1124, 958): Field inspection recorded for Evergreen Grove within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #21 for evergreen_grove: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Evergreen Grove are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

place_lore.nirncraft.evermor.barge_ledge: Down the river, Last Seed: oak, 30 loads. Barley, 12. One coffin for Wayrest, paid in advance, very heavy, no flowers. Up the river: salt, cloth, two priests of Stendarr who were sick over the rail the whole way.

Note to self: stop putting in at the landing below the Namira stones. Third time the beggars there have offered to buy what's in the barrels without asking what it is. Last time they asked for the coffin. Didn't like the way they asked. Didn't like the way they smiled when I said no.
place_lore.nirncraft.evermor.hook: A quiet river city on the Bjoulsae, where barges carry timber and grain to the bay and the king's huntsmen ride out each autumn into woods that have their own opinions about who hunts whom.
place_lore.nirncraft.evermor.huntmaster_:
^THE AUTUMN HUNT IS SUSPENDED
By order of the Huntmaster, no party is to ride south-west of the Bjoulsae beyond the old lodge until further notice. Three hounds and a beater have been lost on the far side of the ridge, near the stones of the Huntsman Prince. The beater was found. The hounds were not.

Hunters are reminded that the prints in the mud by the ford are not a bear's, whatever the tavern says. Any man who has been bitten by any beast this season is to present himself at the lodge, quietly, and will not be punished. Any man who hides such a bite will be.
place_lore.nirncraft.evermor.rumour: Evermor's a sleepy place. Nothing happens. Well, nothing except the hunting lodge, and nobody there talks about the hunting lodge.

place_lore.nirncraft.fahlbtharz.dwemer_p:
A thin brass plate, with a scholar's translation pinned to it: Pressure is maintained so that the guardian is maintained. The guardian is maintained so that pressure is maintained. Do not disturb the regulator without the consent of the Tonal Assembly.
The scholar's marginal note: The Tonal Assembly has not met in four thousand years. I believe we may consider its consent lapsed.

A further scribble in another hand, likely the prospector Decimus Vello: Nerano, if your translation is correct, removing the regulator stops the guardian. If it is wrong, removing the regulator angers the guardian. Kindly be correct.
place_lore.nirncraft.fahlbtharz.hook: A Dwemer ruin west of Mount Moesring whose steam pipes have hissed without pause for four thousand years. A Company prospector went in for the boilers' brass and came out with burns and a theory.
place_lore.nirncraft.fahlbtharz.prospect: Decimus Vello, East Empire Company prospector

#2nd of Frostfall
The pipes run hot through the whole upper hall. Every valve I have found is set to the same mark. The Dwemer did not leave this place running by accident; they left it running on purpose. Whatever needs this much steam is still waiting for it.

#4th of Frostfall
Found the regulator: a brass heart the size of a ram's skull, fitted into the central pipe. It hums. When I touched it the whole ruin shuddered and something big stood up in the lower hall. Steam came out of its joints. It looked at me. I left.

#5th of Frostfall
The regulator would buy me out of my Company contract twice over. It is guarded by a centurion that the steam keeps warm and awake. Need a fighter. Will try Raven Rock. Will try anyone.
place_lore.nirncraft.fahlbtharz.rumour: Fahlbtharz breathes. You can see the steam from the pass on a cold morning. A Company man went in, came out scalded, went back in. Must be some theory.

place_lore.nirncraft.faldars_tooth.falda: Faldar was a Nord captain of the Second Era who held this knoll against a Dunmer raiding party for nine days with eleven men and a broken tooth. When the raiders asked him to surrender, he spat the tooth at their leader's feet and said he'd sooner give them the rest one at a time.

The fort they built on the spot was named for that tooth. It held for two hundred years. Then the Black-Briars of an older day bought the land, sold the stones and let it rot. Faldar, they say, still walks the wall at night, spitting at the bandits.
place_lore.nirncraft.faldars_tooth.hook: A ruined fort on a rocky knoll west of Goldenglow, home to the Ashwood Knives, a bandit band who paint birch leaves on their faces and rob the western road.
place_lore.nirncraft.faldars_tooth.ottar:
Knives,
The western road is ours. Heartwood Mill pays or burns. Goldenglow's mercenaries we leave alone, for now; they've more swords than sense. The Watch at Treva's thinks the mill is theirs. Show them it isn't.

Anyone wearing a Black-Briar thorn is to be let past with a bow and a smile. Brannoc at Greenwall tells me that's the price of breathing in the Rift. I don't like it, but I like breathing.

And whoever let that mill brat follow us halfway home last week owes me a pair of boots. His were too small for anyone.
place_lore.nirncraft.faldars_tooth.rumou: The Ashwood Knives hole up in Faldar's Tooth. Ottar Ashwood's their chief. Mean as a sabre cat with a sore tooth and twice as fond of meat.
place_lore.nirncraft.faldars_tooth.sk4_n: Folio #45 (1996, 1347): Field inspection recorded for Faldars Tooth within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #45 for faldars_tooth: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Faldars Tooth are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti.cartograp: Aurelia Venn, of the Imperial Geographical Society

Dear Society,
I regret to inform you that my survey of Malabal Tor is again incomplete, because the principal landmark has again moved. The Bosmer assure me Falinesti is 'sleeping', and that it only turned over. A city turning over in its sleep is not something one can usefully put on a map.

I have charted what I could. Note in particular the thorn-grove east of the city, where the Bosmer will not go. There is a shrine to Molag Bal at its heart and the trees there grow bent, as though something heavy were pressing down on the canopy. My guide refused to enter. When I asked why, he showed me the chains wound into the roots.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti.hook: The walking city of Valenwood, a graht-oak so vast it once strolled from season to season across the forest. Its rootkeepers swear it has begun to stir again, and cartographers weep.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti.rootkeepe:
^Where the Walking Tree has stood, as remembered by the Rootkeepers
Summer of the Red Moon: the banks of the Xylo, where it drank for three years and the river ran low. Winter of the Many Arrows: deep in Malabal Tor, where it hid from the Colovian armies. This year: here, where it has stood longer than any keeper living remembers.

The tree has begun to hum at night, as it did in the old songs before a walk. The young say it is the wind. The old say it is restless because of the felling east of Elden Root. If the Walking Tree walks again, the keepers will go with it, and the Thalmor tax-collectors may chase us through the canopy for as long as they like.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti.rumour: Falinesti's rooted in Malabal Tor this year. Or it was last week. Check before you send a letter. My cousin addressed one there and it came back from Greenshade, slightly chewed.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti_autumn_si:
#COUNT OF ACORNS
First week: four thousand and eleven. Second week: six thousand, three hundred. By Last Seed: eleven thousand, give or take a squirrel. One acorn, uncounted, buried by the stream; I marked it with a white stone, and the stone has wandered four paces since.
The Autumn site of the walking city: a hill of copper and flame-red leaves where the city settles each year, and where the forest drops its acorns with a sound like soft rain.
The city likes the autumn site best. Nobody says so. But the roots go in deeper, there, and come out slower, and the Tenders say it is reluctant to leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti_spring_si: The Spring site of the walking city: a ring of pale new boughs and a meadow of white blossom, where the city arrives each year in a wash of petals and leaves quietly in the dusk.

^HERE THE CITY ARRIVED, FOR THE ONE HUNDRED AND FORTIETH SPRING.
^HERE IT WILL ARRIVE AGAIN, AND AGAIN.
^BE PATIENT. THE ROOTS ARE SLOW, BUT THEY KNOW THE WAY.
On the day the city leaves, the blossoms close. On the day it arrives, they open. In between, the meadow is just a meadow, and the pilgrims sit in it and are quiet.
place_lore.nirncraft.falinesti_winter_si: Pilgrims say the prayer is sung once at sundown and once at dawn, very low, so the frost does not hear it and take offence. A tin cup of warm cider is left on the rock beside the verse, for whoever the prayer is meant for.
The Winter site of the walking city: a high stony shelf in the Grahtwood hills where the city stands bare and still, hung with frost and icicle-lanterns.
Everyone says the city sleeps in winter. The Tenders say it does not sleep. It listens, very hard, for the sound of spring walking.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath.bounty_no: By order of Jarl Siddgeir, Falkreath

^BY ORDER OF THE JARL OF FALKREATH

The band of outlaws keeping camp upon Knifepoint Ridge, west of this town, has robbed four wagons on the Half-Moon road since Midyear and murdered the carter Bolli and his son.

Their leader is a Nord woman calling herself Hjolfrid Ashpine, tall, with a burn scar down the left side of her jaw. The hold will pay a fair purse for proof of her death, delivered to Bailiff Eirik at the Jarl's longhouse.

The Jarl reminds all that the hold guard is fully occupied with the defence of the town and cannot spare men for the hills.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath.gravedigg:
#Hearthfire, 4E 201
3rd: Old Vigdis, north row. Deep, as she asked.
5th: Two Legion lads from the west camp. Their captain paid in good silver.
9th: Child of the cooper. Small box. Runil said the rites twice.

#Plots found open
11th: Hrofar the tanner. Earth thrown back, shroud cut, his silver ring gone.
14th: The cooper's child. Nothing taken that I can see. Body gone.
19th: Widow Asgerd. Body gone.
Boot prints in the frost, heading northwest along the old road toward the Roadside Ruins.

Told the Jarl's steward. He told me to dig the holes deeper. I have dug for twenty years and I have never had to dig a hole deep enough to keep a body from walking out of it. Someone is taking them, and I will find out who.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath.hook: The hold capital of Falkreath, a timber town under the tall pines whose graveyard is larger than its market. Lately the dead there have not been resting easily.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath.letter_to:
Gaius,
The girls ask every night if you are close enough to see Falkreath's chimneys from your camp. I tell them yes, and that you wave. Do not make a liar of me. The camp is only a day's walk west, past the mill road. If your centurion gives you a single free Sundas, come home.

The Stormcloaks have a camp of their own beyond Helgen now. Dengeir talks about them in the inn as though they were his own sons, and the Jarl pretends not to hear. Half the town would turn their coats for a sack of flour. I am frightened, my love. Stay alive. Stay fed. Write.
Thora
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath.rumour: More dead than living in Falkreath, they say, and now someone's digging the dead up again. Ask Ingrid at the graveyard. She's the one who has to fill the holes.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath_imperial_: A Legion field camp in the western woods of Falkreath, watching the roads to the Reach and the hold's capital. The soldiers are bored, cold and waiting for orders that matter.
Legate Fasendil, Legion command in Falkreath Hold

Captain,
The Jarl of Falkreath remains loyal to the Empire in word. In deed he does nothing, which in present circumstances amounts to the same thing. The former jarl, Dengeir of Stuhn, does not hide his sympathy for Ulfric. You will not act against him without orders.

Maintain patrols on the road to Half-Moon Mill and the Reach border. Report any Stormcloak movement from their camp near Helgen. Do not engage the bandits at Knifepoint Ridge unless they attack Legion supply: the hold may deal with its own outlaws. Keep the men out of the Falkreath inn. Their debts there are becoming a diplomatic matter.
The Legion camp west of here buys meat and pays on time, I'll say that for them. But their captain looks at Falkreath like a man measuring a fence he means to jump.

Folio #14 (-1394, 700): Field inspection recorded for Falkreath Imperial Camp within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #14 for falkreath_imperial_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Falkreath Imperial Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Thora,
Yes, I can see the chimneys, if I climb the pine behind the quartermaster's tent, which I am not supposed to do. I wave every evening. Tell the girls a centurion caught me at it and I said I was checking for Stormcloaks. He gave me latrine duty for a week. Worth it.
No free Sundas until Sun's Dusk. They say we may march east soon, toward the Stormcloak camp past Helgen. If we do, I will come through Falkreath on the way, even if I have to
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath_stormcloa: Commander of the Falkreath Stormcloak Camp

Soldiers of Skyrim,
This camp holds the road between Helgen and the south. The Empire made Helgen a gallows for our Jarl; Talos and a dragon made it a grave for them instead. We will not waste that gift.

Our friend in Falkreath, the old jarl, says the town will open its gates if it is given a reason. Our task is to be that reason, quietly. No raids. No burned farms. Buy your bread at Falkreath and pay double. When Siddgeir falls, let the people remember who paid fairly and who sent soldiers to eat their stores.

Brothers,
My nephew sits in my hall and thinks the chair makes him a jarl. The guard is underpaid and the walls are worse. Half the hold remembers who kept the peace before he was out of swaddling.

The Legion camp in the west woods has sixty men, no more. Their captain is sick of Siddgeir's mead and sicker of his promises. When you come, come by the east road past Peak's Shade Tower, where the watch is thinnest. I will see that the gate is slow to close.
A Stormcloak war camp hidden in the hills east of Helgen, watching the Pale Pass road and waiting for Falkreath to choose a side.
The Stormcloaks camped past Helgen send a man to Falkreath every week to drink with old Dengeir. He comes back sober. Dengeir doesn't.

place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath_watch_mou: A circular earthen tumulus ringed by leaning headstones on the hill above Falkreath's timber palisade.
Guard-sentries on the north gate say the frost melts off Falkreath Watch Mound days before the rest of the hillside thaws.

Folio #59 (-1360, 1400): Field inspection recorded for Falkreath Watch Mound within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #59 for falkreath_watch_mound: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Falkreath Watch Mound are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Do not pasture sheep inside the stone curb of the upper mound. Last week the turf in the center sank two spans, and the masonry beneath the sod is laid in the massive interlocking wedge-stones of the dragon cult.
place_lore.nirncraft.falkreath_watchtowe: A ruined stone watchtower on the road north of Falkreath. The hold guard abandoned it years ago; at night, a green lantern passes beneath it on the way to the old ruins.

To the watch at the north tower: by command of the Jarl, the tower is to be manned until the bandit trouble on the Half-Moon road is ended.
Below, in another hand, much later: 'Trouble not ended. Men recalled to Falkreath to guard the Jarl's new mead hall. Tower abandoned. Gods help the carters.'

Pinned under the orders is a later scrap: 'Squatter seen in the tower, Hearthfire. Harmless drifter. Left on his own. He reported a green lantern on the north road at midnight and a man with a handcart. The captain says to ignore drunkards. The captain does not walk the north road at midnight.'
Nobody mans the old watchtower anymore. Which is a pity, because somebody walks past it every few nights carrying a green lamp, and it'd be nice to know who.

#9th of Hearthfire
Dry floor, good walls, nobody to say be off. Best bed since Markarth.
#14th of Hearthfire
Man with a green lantern went by below at midnight, pulling a handcart. Something under a sheet on the cart. Something shaped like a sleeping person, only too still. He went toward the Roadside Ruins.

#19th of Hearthfire
He went by again with the cart. This time the thing under the sheet sat up halfway and he patted it on the head like a dog and it lay back down.
I am leaving in the morning. Markarth had its faults but in Markarth the dead stay on their side of the street.

place_lore.nirncraft.fallowstone_cave.ex:
#8th of Frostfall
Two trolls in the first cavern. I waited until they slept and crept past. Their snoring is like rockfall. I'd rather a dragon. A dragon at least you see coming.

#9th of Frostfall
Beyond the trolls the cave opens into a grotto with a waterfall falling from a crack in the roof, and moss on everything, and a light like dawn though there's no sun. I sat by the pool for an hour and forgot to be afraid.

There are stone markers at the far end, very old. Someone tended this place once. I'm going back to Riften for a lantern and a friend. Not necessarily in that order.
place_lore.nirncraft.fallowstone_cave.ho: A deep cave in the eastern hills above Riften, where trolls lair in the outer halls and old stories say a forgotten shrine waits beyond them.
place_lore.nirncraft.fallowstone_cave.ru: Fallowstone Cave's full of trolls, and past the trolls, the old folk say, there's something older. Nobody goes far enough to check.

place_lore.nirncraft.fellglow_keep.acoly:
Sister Hildrun,
You will be angry, and you will be right. I left the Temple of Kynareth without leave. I came to Fellglow because they promised me what the Temple never could: an answer. They said they can call back the dead, and my mother has been dead since Sun's Dawn.

I have seen what they do now. It is not my mother they call. It is something that wears the shape of the dead and smiles wrongly. They have locked the lower cells and I hear voices there. I would leave, but they watch me.

If this reaches you, do not send the guard. They will not come. Send someone who can get me out. Alvi.
place_lore.nirncraft.fellglow_keep.hook: An old Imperial keep in the hills north-east of Whiterun, abandoned by the Legion and taken by renegade mages. Lights burn in its windows, and the farms nearby have lost more than sheep.
place_lore.nirncraft.fellglow_keep.keep_:
The thralls in the lower cells are to be fed every second day. More than that is waste. Less than that makes them useless for the work.

The new acolyte from Whiterun is talented but squeamish. Keep him from the cells. Keep him from the front gate. If he asks about his mother, tell him we are close.

Supplies due: grave dust from the Ritual Stone, where Moriva's circle is working; salt; two more bodies, fresh. The farms east of the river have been watchful lately. Send the collectors further out.

We do not answer the College's letters. We do not answer anyone's letters.
place_lore.nirncraft.fellglow_keep.rumou: Fellglow Keep is full of mages the College threw out. They pay farmhands to fetch them things, and some of those farmhands don't come back. A young acolyte from the temple went there too. Sister Hildrun is beside herself.

place_lore.nirncraft.fields_of_kummu.hoo: A green flat of old standing shrines in ash grass, each carved with a face that looks toward the lagoon.
place_lore.nirncraft.fields_of_kummu.rum: The Kummu shrines are tended by clerks nobody has met. They keep a ledger of tokens left and tokens never taken.
place_lore.nirncraft.fields_of_kummu.web: Faces tended: 31. Tokens collected: 388. Tokens waiting: 1,904. Procedure: return tokens to the Sunken House at Ald Sotha, where the canton's keepers will file them. If a pilgrim asks for their token, tell them it is being kept safe. Do not tell them where.

place_lore.nirncraft.firsthold.customs_r:
#11th of Frostfall, 4E 201
The Breton carrack 'Fair Winifred' has been refused entry and towed to the quarantine anchorage. Three of her crew present the grey blisters. In accordance with the Directorate's orders, the crew may not land. In accordance with nature, they are dying.

It is reported that some of the anchorage's sick are rowing ashore by night to the Peryite shrine north-west of the town, to beg the Taskmaster for what our healers will not give. I have not ordered them stopped. I would like this report to record that I have not ordered them stopped. I would like it to record also that I have a family, and that they live in Firsthold.
place_lore.nirncraft.firsthold.hook: The oldest port of Auridon, a white-walled harbour where every ship from the mainland must anchor under the eyes of the Thalmor before it may continue to the Summerset Isle.
place_lore.nirncraft.firsthold.informant:
Esteemed Justiciars,
The thief who calls herself the Moth has robbed the house of Magistrate Caladwe again. Jewels, a ledger, and the Magistrate's ceremonial circlet. I have seen her at the Nocturnal shrine west of the town at dusk, a slight figure, an Altmer by her height, and dressed like a scholar.

I believe she hides her takings near the shrine, for she goes there laden and comes back light. I ask in return only that my son's application to the Sapiarchs be looked upon kindly. I am told that loyalty is its own reward. I am also told that it is not the only one.
place_lore.nirncraft.firsthold.rumour: Every ship bound for Alinor stops at Firsthold first. Customs searches your cargo, your crew and your conscience. Somebody called the Moth has been searching their strongboxes in return.

place_lore.nirncraft.folgunthur.hook: An old Nord barrow sunk into the marsh south of Solitude, its lower halls half-flooded. A scholar's apprentice went down to copy its carvings and has not come up.
place_lore.nirncraft.folgunthur.junia_jo: Junia Fulvia, apprentice to Verulus Agrippa

#1st day
The upper halls are dry. I have copied eleven panels. Master Verulus says the claw-door here was made by the same carvers as the one at Ustengrav; I think he is wrong, but I will not tell him until I can prove it.

#3rd day
Water in the lower halls is waist-deep and colder than anything I have felt. Something moved in it. Not a fish.
#4th day
The dead here are awake. I am safe in an alcove with the tablet I came for: a stone rubbing of the Folgunthur lineage, every name in the barrow. It is wonderful. I cannot get out. Please, somebody, tell Master Verulus I proved him wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.folgunthur.rumour: Folgunthur's mostly underwater these days, and what isn't underwater is under something worse. Some young woman from Solitude went in with a lantern and a stack of paper. Brave, or daft.
place_lore.nirncraft.folgunthur.verulus_:
Junia,
You will copy the lineage tablet in the lower hall(1). You will not touch the dead(2). You will not remove anything from the barrow except paper you have brought into it(3). You will be back in Solitude by Turdas, because I have promised the Jarl's steward a lecture and cannot give it without your notes(4).

(1) Exactly. Not your impression of it.
(2) They object.
(3) The Legion is touchy about grave goods, and so are the graves.
(4) Also because I would be sorry if you did not come back. I am putting that in a footnote so you do not make a fuss about it.

place_lore.nirncraft.forebears_holdout.a:
To the hunters of the Crown:
The traitor Nasim at-Rayan and his household are believed to shelter in the hills between Solitude and the Reach. Ask in Dragon Bridge after Redguards buying salt. Ask at the sawmill after Redguards selling pelts.

Bring him back alive if the Nords make it easy; dead if they make it hard. Do not harm the children. The Crown is not cruel. Do not let the Nords see you work. The Nords are cruel, and they do not love us either.
place_lore.nirncraft.forebears_holdout.f:
#Sun's Dusk, 4E 200
We came north because the Crowns of Hammerfell said our family helped the Dominion. We did not. We helped the Forebears hold Hammerfell when the Empire would not. That is a different thing, though the Alik'r do not care to know it.

#Rain's Hand, 4E 201
The cave is cold but it is ours. Layla has learned to set snares. My son asks why we cannot live in Solitude like other people. I tell him that in Solitude everyone sees you, and here only the deer do.
#Frostfall
Hooded riders on the ridge above Dragon Bridge Overlook. They wear the sand-coloured cloaks. They have found the Overlook. Next they will find us.
place_lore.nirncraft.forebears_holdout.h: A hidden cave in the wild hills south of Haafingar where a family of Redguard Forebears hides from the Alik'r warriors who hunt them. They trust no one. Can you blame them?
place_lore.nirncraft.forebears_holdout.r: There's Redguards hiding somewhere in the hills south of the sawmill. Proper Hammerfell folk, scimitars and all. And there's other Redguards hunting them. Don't ask me which lot are the good ones.
place_lore.nirncraft.forelhost.hook: A Dragon Cult monastery carved into the mountain south-east of Riften, where the last priests of the Cult chose death over surrender. A temple keeper in Riften wants to know how the siege really ended.
place_lore.nirncraft.forelhost.rumour: Forelhost's been sealed since the First Era. Only fools and scholars go there, and the fools at least come back sooner.
place_lore.nirncraft.forelhost.siege_cap: Captain Hroald of the Rift Muster, First Era

#Day thirty of the siege
The monks have not shown a face on the walls for three days. Our scouts say there is no smoke from their chimneys. The men are restless. We have eaten the last of the horses.

#Day thirty-two
We broke the gate at dawn. They are dead, all of them, at their tables, cups by their hands. Poison. Every one of them smiling. I have ordered the halls sealed.

#Day thirty-three
We did not find the High Priest. I took his door-signet, a ring of bronze with a dragon's head, to prove to the King that we entered. I will leave it in the lower hall, with my men's names cut beside it. Let whoever finds it tell the world we did not run.
place_lore.nirncraft.forelhost.sk4_note_: Folio #48 (2609, 1681): Field inspection recorded for Forelhost within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #48 for forelhost: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Forelhost are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.forelhost.temple_re:
To any brave soul who reads this,
The Temple of Mara in Riften keeps a roll of the dead of the Siege of Forelhost. It ends with a captain named Hroald, and beside his name an old priest wrote: 'signet left within'.

If the signet is still there, I would like it brought to the Temple, so the names of his men can be read aloud at the Hearthfire vigil. Mara is the goddess of love, and love remembers. Bring a strong sword. The Cult never forgave anyone for anything.
place_lore.nirncraft.forsaken_cave.hook: A Nordic barrow sunk into a hillside east of Nightgate Inn. A Stormcloak deserter fled into it with his company's banner, and the dead within were glad of the company.
place_lore.nirncraft.forsaken_cave.kolbe: I took the banner so they'd chase me instead of killing me. That was the plan. My cousin's in the Legion, at Fort Dunstad. If I march on Dunstad with Ulfric, I'll be the one that kills him. I won't. I can't.

The draugr don't care about Ulfric or Tullius. One of them wears a crown and stares at me from his throne when I sleep. I've wedged the banner in the wall behind his chair so at least he can't sit on it. I'm hungry. I'm cold. I'm still not sorry.
place_lore.nirncraft.forsaken_cave.rumou: A Stormcloak lad ran off from the camp south of here with their war banner. Last anyone saw, he was heading into Forsaken Cave. Bad choice.
place_lore.nirncraft.forsaken_cave.serge:
To all soldiers of the Pale camp.
Kolbeinn Rime-Hand has deserted his post and taken the company banner, the bear-and-axe sewn by the women of Windhelm. I want the banner back. I do not much care about Kolbeinn, though I would like a word with him.
Tracks lead to Forsaken Cave. I will not send good soldiers into a draugr hole after one bad one. If any sellsword returns the banner to this camp, I will pay in coin and say no more about it.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_amol.bandit_bo:
Ysolde,
You said a fort was too big for us. I say a fort is just a cave somebody bothered to stack. We've got walls, a well, sealed stores of salt beef, and a blue banner with a bear on it that I'm using as a blanket.

Send the rest of the boys up from Lost Knife Hideout. With the Stormcloaks off in Windhelm and the Legion stuck behind Darkwater Pass, nobody's coming for Fort Amol before the thaw. We'll be lords by Morning Star.
P.S. The bear banner smells of old men. Bring a new blanket.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_amol.hook: A Stormcloak fort guarding the western road to Darkwater Pass, stripped of its garrison to reinforce Windhelm, and quietly taken over by the cutthroats of Lost Knife Hideout.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_amol.rumour: Ulfric pulled the soldiers out of Fort Amol for Windhelm and didn't leave so much as a dog. Now there's smoke from the towers again, and it isn't blue cloaks lighting it.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_amol.sk4_note_: Folio #28 (1276, 245): Field inspection recorded for Fort Amol within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.fort_amol.withdrawa:
To the Captain of Fort Amol, from Galmar Stone-Fist, by the hand of his clerk:
You will withdraw your full garrison to Windhelm by the 1st of Frostfall. Leave the fort's stores sealed. Leave the regimental standard in the commander's chest; it is too old to carry and too proud to burn.

Should the Legion advance from Darkwater Pass, the fort is to be considered lost and retaken later. Should bandits advance on it, the fort is to be considered beneath our notice until spring.
^For Skyrim.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_dunstad.comman:
To General Tullius, Solitude.
Courier Anvari left this fort on the 10th of Frostfall carrying your dispatches for the Winterhold camp, including the troop dispositions for the Pale. He did not arrive. His horse came back alone, lame, with frost on its saddle and blood on its flank.

A trapper reports tracks leaving the road toward Duskglow Crevice, where the Falmer nest. If those dispatches fall into Stormcloak hands we lose the Pale. If they fall into Falmer hands we merely lose a courier. I would prefer to lose neither.
I have no men to spare. I am posting a reward for the dispatch case.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_dunstad.fort_g:
Rufio's rules: no drinking on watch, no dicing on watch, no sleeping on watch, no sitting on watch, no breathing too loudly on watch.
Dunstad's rules: the snow wins, the wind wins, the Falmer win if you go east, and the cook wins every argument.
Under it, freshly: Anvari owes me nine septims. Somebody find him.

Carved deeper, older: Garrison of 4E 174 was here. We held this fort against the snow, the Reachmen, the bandits and our own sergeant. Whoever reads this is now part of a long, cold, grumbling tradition. Welcome.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_dunstad.hook: A Legion fort in the snows of the southern Pale, holding the road between Dawnstar and the rest of Skyrim. A courier left it three days ago with dispatches and never reached the coast.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_dunstad.rumour: Fort Dunstad's commander is in a foul mood. One of his couriers took the east road with the dispatch case and vanished near the Falmer caves.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_dunstad.sk4_no: Folio #14 (145, -1096): Field inspection recorded for Fort Dunstad within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.fort_fellhammer.fen:
#Frostfall
Bought: six Dwemer cogs from the Alftand diggers (the ones that are left). Paid 40, will sell for 200 to the mage at the College who asks no questions.
Bought: a temple bell, small, bronze, green with sea-rot, from the wreck-divers off Winterhold. They say it came up from the drowned temple. Paid 15.

Bought: one wedding band, silver, from Kjeld at Frostmere. Did not buy, he wanted too much.
Note: a Winterhold woman has been asking about the bell all over town. Somebody wants it badly. Price is now 300.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_fellhammer.for: Waymark 22: Fort Fellhammer. Built in the Second Era to guard the old Fellhammer mine, whose silver paid for half the fort. The silver ran out, the miners left, and the garrison was withdrawn to Fort Dunstad.

Since then it has passed from Legion to bandits to Legion and back to bandits so often that the locals simply call whoever is inside 'the Fellhammer lot'. The mine below is flooded and full of ice. Do not shelter here without an escort.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_fellhammer.hoo: A ruined fort on a ridge above an abandoned mine in the hills where the Pale meets Winterhold. Bandits use it as a fence's warehouse for anything stolen in the north.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_fellhammer.rum: Fort Fellhammer's a market now. A bandit market. If something goes missing in Winterhold, it turns up in Fellhammer before the week is out.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_fellhammer.sk4: Folio #23 (366, -1242): Field inspection recorded for Fort Fellhammer within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #23 for fort_fellhammer: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Fort Fellhammer are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_frostmoth.gaiu:
Aulus,
I am in the old fort. Our great-grandfather's name is cut into the wall of the inner hall with the others. I read it aloud, and something in the dark answered with the muster call.

They are still here, brother. Bones in rusted plate, standing to. The standard is in the inner hall, where the reports say it was. I tried to take it, and the officer's shade stood up from his chair and put himself between me and it. I am hurt. I will try again at dawn. If I do not come back, the standard should go home, and so should they. Gaius.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_frostmoth.hook: The broken shell of an Imperial Legion fort on the southern coast, shattered when Red Mountain burst. Its legionaries never left their posts, and on ash-heavy nights they still stand to.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_frostmoth.last:
#Morning report, 4E 5
Present and fit: thirty-one. Sick: four. The sky over Vvardenfell has turned the colour of an old bruise. The fishermen say the sea is warm. The Captain has ordered that the standard be kept in the inner hall and the men stand to at the walls.

#Evening report
Ash falling like snow, hot. The shore is burning. The ships cannot put out. The Captain says the Legion does not leave its posts without orders, and we have no orders, because no ship can reach us to bring them. Present and fit: thirty-one. We will stand to. The standard will not fall while one of us is standing.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_frostmoth.redo: The fort's walls are sound on the seaward side only. Ash spawn are often seen in the courtyard, drawn, the old Guard say, to the Imperial dead the way the ash is drawn to anything that burned. The Councilor has decided that the fort is not Redoran business. Imperials who wish to visit their dead may do so at their own risk. We have warned them. We have warned them several times.

Added later: An Imperial named Gaius Vettrius passed the Bulwark in Frostfall, bound for the fort. He was warned. He showed us his family's Legion ring and said his great-grandfather was still on duty. The watch laughed. Nobody is laughing now.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_frostmoth.rumo: Fort Frostmoth died the day the mountain blew. The legionaries were at their posts and stayed there. Old Aulus Vettrius at Raven Rock says his brother went in to fetch the cohort's standard home and hasn't been seen since.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greenwall.hook: A squat stone fort on the road north of Riften, held by bandits who charge a toll on every cart that passes. Every cart, that is, except the Black-Briars'.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greenwall.pris:
To whoever finds this,
I'm a carter from Shor's Stone and I couldn't pay the twelve. They've kept me in the cellar a week to work it off, hauling barrels.

The barrels go out on the Black-Briar wagons. They aren't mead. They're too heavy for mead and they slosh wrong. If you find Brannoc's book you'll find what's in them, I'd wager. Get me out first, if you please.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greenwall.rumo: Brannoc Tollhand runs Fort Greenwall like a customs house. Twelve septims a cart. And the Black-Briar wagons roll through without paying a copper. Funny how the guard never comes.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greenwall.sk4_: Folio #38 (2349, 1030): Field inspection recorded for Fort Greenwall within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #38 for fort_greenwall: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Fort Greenwall are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greenwall.toll:
Twelve a cart. Five a horse. One a head on foot, unless they're carrying something worth taking, then whatever they're carrying.

NOBODY touches a wagon with the Briar seal. You see a black thorn painted on the tailboard, you wave and smile. You don't look in the back. You don't wonder what's in the back.

The toll book stays in my strongbox. Everything's in that book, every coin in and every coin out, who paid and who got paid. That's my insurance. The day the Lady decides I'm more trouble than I'm worth, the book goes to the Jarl. She knows it. That's why I'm still breathing.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greymoor.hook: An old stone fort west of Whiterun, long empty of Legion soldiers and now crawling with silver-clad hunters of beasts. Beneath its walls lies an older secret the hunters know nothing of.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greymoor.payma: Optio Gratian Sabe, paymaster of Fort Greymoor

To the Legate at Solitude,
The garrison is ordered to withdraw from Greymoor on the 2nd. We have no wagon for the pay chest. The road is thick with bandits who know exactly what a pay chest looks like.

I have therefore buried it, as regulations permit in time of danger. It lies outside the walls, thirty paces from the south-west tower, under a flat stone marked with the eagle of the Legion. The men's back pay for two months: one hundred and sixty septims and the garrison's silver ring of service.

I shall return for it with an escort. If I do not return, let it go to whoever serves the Empire best. Gratian Sabe.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greymoor.rumou: Fort Greymoor's held by the Silver Hand now. They say they hunt werewolves. They hunt anyone they don't like the look of. Old soldiers swear the last Legion paymaster buried the garrison's wages out there before the fort fell.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greymoor.silve: Watch rota for the walls. Two on the north rampart, two at the gate, one in the south-west tower. The tower is the worst post. The wolves howl under it every night. Not those wolves. Ordinary wolves. I think.

Anyone who sees a Companion on the road is to report it at once. Anyone who sees a Companion and does nothing will answer to me. The beasts of Jorrvaskr think the plains belong to them. We will teach them otherwise.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_greymoor.sk4_n: Folio #34 (-533, 16): Field inspection recorded for Fort Greymoor within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #34 for fort_greymoor: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Fort Greymoor are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_hraggstad.cast:
Commander,
The rebel camp south of the Statue to Meridia is not to be assaulted at this time. It is more useful to us watched than scattered. Its messengers ride east toward Hjaalmarch; note their routes and their numbers.

Pay particular attention to any Haafingar-born men in that camp. Families in Dragon Bridge and Solitude with sons in rebel blue are to be listed, not harassed. A list is a better weapon than a gallows; it lasts longer and makes less noise.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_hraggstad.hook: A Legion stronghold guarding the western approach to Solitude. The garrison is stretched thin between Stormcloak scouts, bandits on the Dragon Bridge road and a paymaster who keeps being robbed.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_hraggstad.quar:
To the Legate, Castle Dour.
On the 6th of Frostfall the payroll wagon for this fort was taken on the road two miles north-west of Dragon Bridge. Driver and two escorts killed. One escort survived by playing dead in a ditch. He reports eight attackers, wearing pine sprigs in their caps, who fled toward Pinemoon Cave.

The strongbox held four hundred and twenty septims and the Legion seal. I cannot send men after it; every spare blade is watching the Stormcloak camp near Meridia's statue. I respectfully request that the payroll travel with more than three guards. I respectfully request that someone respectfully read my requests.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_hraggstad.recr:
Mother,
The fort is cold, the porridge is colder, and I am now an expert at marching to the end of a cliff and back. The sergeant says I have a soldier's feet. I think that is a compliment.

We have not been paid in two months. The officers say it is the bandits. The older soldiers say the officers say that about everything. Last night a Nord in our cohort said he had a cousin in the Stormcloak camp and that they get paid in mead and glory. Then he looked at me to see if I would tell. I did not. I do not know if that makes me a good friend or a bad soldier.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_hraggstad.rumo: Fort Hraggstad lost its payroll again, down near Pinemoon. Third time this year. The lads are saying the Emperor pays in excuses now.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_kastav.grelka_:
#Frostfall
Toll from sleds on the Windhelm road: 112 septims, 3 sacks of flour, 1 goat (eaten).
Timber from Anga's Mill: 18 planks. Short by two. Sent the reminder.
Prisoners held for ransom: a Dawnstar ore-merchant's son (his father is haggling, the cheapskate).

Note: the Stormcloak camp to the east sniffs about. Pay their scouts in mead and they forget they saw us. The Legion is further off and stupider.
Note: build a proper gate before the snows. Lady of Kastav needs a proper gate.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_kastav.hook: An old fort on a ridge in the southern hills of Winterhold, held by a bandit chief who calls herself a lady and taxes the road like one.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_kastav.lookout:
To whoever's on the wall.
Watch the road south to Anga's Mill and north toward Stillborn Cave. If anything with a sword comes up the road, light the brazier and ring the pot. If anything comes up the road that is bigger than a horse, do not ring the pot. Just hide.

Anyone caught sleeping goes on the wall with no cloak for a night. Anyone caught dreaming of black doors and talking about it can do the same. I've had enough of that nonsense from the Dawnstar recruits.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_kastav.rumour: Grelka Iron-Jaw runs Fort Kastav. She takes a toll from every sled on the road and a tithe from Anga's Mill. The Jarl's too far away to care.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_neugrad.hook: A stone fort in the southern hills of Falkreath, abandoned by the Legion and seized by deserters who call themselves free soldiers. Rumour says the Legion's last payroll is still in its cellar.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_neugrad.prison:
Scratched into the stone of a cell door:
'Pell, legionary. Would not go with Broadshield. Locked up for it. Day eleven. They feed me when they remember. If the Legion ever comes back, the coffer is under the third flagstone from the cellar stair, and the Captain sleeps with the key round his neck.'

Below, scratched later and fainter: 'Day nineteen. Heard them talking. Broadshield means to sell the road to the Stormcloaks and the coffer to whoever comes first. If you're Legion, come soon. If you're not Legion, come anyway. I'm not fussy anymore.'
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_neugrad.quarte:
To the Legate at Falkreath.
Per orders, Fort Neugrad is evacuated as of this day, the 3rd of Last Seed, 4E 201. Stores have been carried to the Falkreath camp. The garrison payroll, eight hundred septims in a sealed iron coffer, remains in the fort cellar under guard of Captain Ulfgar Broadshield and six men, to follow on the morrow.

I note for the record my objection to leaving the coffer with Captain Broadshield, whose debts at the dice I have mentioned in two previous reports. I was overruled. I would like it written down that I was overruled.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_neugrad.rumour: Fort Neugrad's full of Legion deserters turned bandit. Their captain was the one who was meant to take the payroll back to Falkreath when they pulled out. Funny how it never arrived.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_neugrad.ulfgar: Ulfgar Broadshield, Captain of the Free Company

We are not deserters. The Legion left Fort Neugrad and we stayed in it. That makes it ours.
The coffer stays sealed in the cellar until the war's done and nobody's looking for it. Anyone who tries the lock answers to me.

No raids on Helgen's ruins, the scavengers there are ours to tax, not rob. No fighting the Stormcloaks to the north. They've offered good coin if we hold the road against the Legion when the time comes, and I mean to take it. A soldier's loyalty belongs to whoever pays him. The Empire stopped paying the day it left us here.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_snowhawk.hallg: Sten is gone. Ofrid is walking but he isn't Ofrid. She keeps me in the cage because I still cry and she likes to write down how long it lasts.

If Thorvar sends anyone, tell them she sleeps by day in the old commander's room and keeps her book under her pillow. Tell them to burn Ofrid properly. He'd want that. He was always cold.
And tell Thorvar it wasn't his fault for sending us. He told us to look and come back. We looked too long. Tell my mother in Morthal I was brave, even if I wasn't, and that I'm sorry about the shutters.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_snowhawk.hook: An old Imperial fort in the marsh west of Morthal, long abandoned and lately reoccupied. Not by the Legion. The Jarl's patrol went to look and did not come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_snowhawk.legio:
FORT SNOWHAWK
RAISED BY THE THIRD LEGION IN THE REIGN OF THE SEPTIMS
TO GUARD THE MARCHES OF HJAALMARCH AND THE ROAD TO SOLITUDE.

^Beneath, scratched with a knife:
Garrison withdrawn 4E 176. Last man out, Decanus Hollis, who would like it known that the roof leaks, the cellar floods, and something in the peat under the north wall knocks at night. Good riddance.
^And beneath that, in a neat new hand:
The knocking is the marsh dead, Decanus, and they were only asking to be let in. I have let them in. Vigdis.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_snowhawk.rumou: Fort Snowhawk was the Legion's once, then nobody's, and now there's smoke from it at night and a smell like burnt hair. Three guards went to see. Thorvar at Highmoon Hall hasn't slept since.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_snowhawk.vigdi: The marsh preserves. That is the whole of my discovery, and it took me eleven years. Bodies drawn from the Hjaalmarch peat after a century are softer than those from a dry tomb after a month. The marsh is the finest embalmer in Tamriel and it charges nothing.

Three fresh subjects arrived on their own, in Morthal livery, asking what we were doing. I have shown them. Two are already useful. The third, Hallgerd, still has enough of herself to weep, which interests me.
If the Jarl sends more, I will be grateful. If she sends the wizard Falion, I will leave by the back way; I am ambitious, not foolish.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_sungard.desert:
#Sun's Height, 4E 201
The Legion forgets its forts faster than it forgets its debts. Sungard was given up after the Markarth business. I, Vatrius Hollow, once optio of the Fourth Cohort, have taken it back for the Empire. The Empire does not know. The Empire will not be told.

#Last Seed
Taxed the road from the Bilegulch Mine: 80 septims and a cart of iron. The Orcs did not like it. The Orcs can complain to the Emperor.
The cohort's eagle standard hangs in the hall. As long as it hangs there, we are not deserters. We are a garrison. It is important to the men to believe this. It is important to me.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_sungard.hook: A Nordic fort on the eastern edge of the Reach, abandoned by the Legion and claimed by deserters who still wear its colours and still collect its taxes.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_sungard.mercha:
My Jarl,
The 'Legion' at Fort Sungard charged me 30 septims to pass a road the Empire paid for. When I asked for a receipt, the commander gave me one, written very neatly, signed 'Vatrius Hollow, Commander, Sungard Garrison, on behalf of His Imperial Majesty'.
I took it to the Legion camp near Bthardamz. The tribune laughed for a long time, then stopped, and asked me which way the fort was.

The Jarl's steward has written across the bottom: Forwarded to the Legion. The Legion replies that Fort Sungard is not a Legion fort and Vatrius Hollow is not a Legion officer, and that they would be very grateful if someone would remove the eagle standard from his hall before anyone in Solitude hears of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_sungard.rumour: Fort Sungard's got Legion banners and Legion armour, but don't let that fool you. Those are deserters, and they tax the road worse than any Jarl.
place_lore.nirncraft.fort_sungard.sk4_no: Folio #66 (-1466, 270): Field inspection recorded for Fort Sungard within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #66 for fort_sungard: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Fort Sungard are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
A crumbling Nordic watchpost south of Karthwasten, marked by four stone skulls that stare out over the Reach. Treasure maps to it are sold cheap in every inn west of Whiterun.

4E 176. The city has fallen back to Ulfric's militia and the Forsworn are scattering into the hills. I am not taking the cohort's pay chest down to Markarth through that. Buried it under the skull that faces the sunset, at the old lookout. Will return for it with an escort.
If I do not return, the gold belongs to the Emperor. Which is to say it belongs to whoever is first with a spade.

Second page, the ink badly run:
The chest holds the cohort's pay, an officer's sword, and my own savings, eleven years of them. If my wife in Bruma ever reads this, I am sorry. I told you the Reach would be quiet. I told you the Nords and the Reachmen had made their peace. I was wrong about everything, my love, except you.
Bought a map to Four Skull Lookout from a smooth-talking fellow by the river. Forty septims. Wife says it's fake. Wife is usually right. Still, though.

To the next fool with Ottar's map: I dug under the east skull, the north skull and the south skull. Nothing but roots and a dead skeever. I am too tired and too angry to do the west one. Liar's Retreat earned its name.
- Arngrim of Dragon Bridge, out forty septims and a good shovel
Beneath, in another hand: The draugr in here don't care about maps, by the way. Bring something sharp. - B.

And beneath both, in a third hand, very small: It is always the last place you'd look, isn't it. West skull. I would have dug it myself but I heard the draugr wake and I am not paid enough. Nobody is paid enough for draugr.

place_lore.nirncraft.frokis_shack.froki_:
#Frostfall
Birch gold. Lake cold. The elk walk north early. The wolves sleep in the day and howl in the night, which is wrong.

The mound north of here has opened. Not dug, opened, from inside. The earth is pushed up and outward like a flower. The birds won't land on it.

Kyne, I have kept your woods sixty years and never asked for anything. I ask for this: let whatever crawled out of that mound fly the other way.

Kept a tally of the elk. Kept a tally of the bears. Didn't think I'd need a tally of dragons. Two, so far, over Autumnwatch.
place_lore.nirncraft.frokis_shack.hook: A lonely hunting shack in the deep woods south of the lake, home to an old hermit who talks to the animals and claims they talk back.
place_lore.nirncraft.frokis_shack.rumour: Old Froki lives out past the dragon mound, by himself. He knows every wolf in the Rift by name. Says the wolves have been frightened lately. Says something big's waking up.

place_lore.nirncraft.frossel.hook: A riekling den in a sea cave on the north shore, stinking of horker fat and stolen mead. Its chief carries a spear that once hung in Thirsk Mead Hall.
place_lore.nirncraft.frossel.riekling_sc: A rough set of drawings, described here by whoever found them: a small blue figure holding a very long spear above its head. Many small figures bowing. A large hairy figure, clearly a Nord, lying flat with crosses for eyes. A mead barrel drawn with great love and detail. Last, the long spear stuck into the ground beside a fire, with the small figure asleep against it, and a horker standing guard. The horker has been given a crown.
On the back of the hide, someone from Thirsk has added in charcoal: The big hairy figure is Gunnar, I think. He is not dead. He will be annoyed to see this.
place_lore.nirncraft.frossel.rumour: Frossel is where the rieklings go to sleep off our mead. Their chief has a spear twice as long as he is and a temper twice as long as that.
place_lore.nirncraft.frossel.thirsk_hunt: Watched Frossel for two days from the rocks above Haknir's Shoal. Count: twenty rieklings, more when the boats come back. Two bristlebacks that they ride. One chief, Kruk Gnaw-Tooth, who carries the Spear of Thirsk and never puts it down, not even to eat.

They are not stupid. They post a watcher on the cliff and change him at dusk. They are afraid of fire and of loud singing, which we discovered by accident. Tell Brenna: go at dusk, go loud, and go with more than three. I went with three. I am the only one writing.
place_lore.nirncraft.frost_throne_of_kam: A throne-hall of ice and iron with a giant ice throne in a hall of ice pagodas.
The throne of Kamal is cold even in summer. The frost-warden has not blinked in a thousand years.

THE EIGHTH PIECE SITS HERE: THE ARM THAT HELD THE SCEPTRE. He who sets the ring, the crown, the sceptre and the sword in their places makes the king whole, and the king will rise, and the king will remember who he was. There is no one left who remembers who he was. This is the mercy.
FOUR COURTS, FOUR QUARTERS, ONE SEAL. Whoever joins them keeps the valley shut. Whoever breaks them opens it. It is the warden's duty to ask which you choose, and to remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostbreak_fortress: At place.nirncraft.frostbreak_fortress, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the granite peaks and iron-smelting valleys of Wrothgar, split between the rebuilt halls of Orsinium and the Malacath-sworn strongholds.

Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.frostbreak_fortress report signs of clanless mountain raiders, Daughters of Wroth frost-hags, and Lyrezi peak-vampires operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.

Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.frostbreak_fortress

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.frostbreak_fortress. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

place_lore.nirncraft.frostcrag_spire.hoo: A single obsidian spire on a rock in a cold sea, with no stairs: only a levitation or boat to the door and a storm-room at the top.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostcrag_spire.rum: The Spire sings in storm weather. Fishermen say it hums the same note as the old priory bell.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostcrag_spire.web: You ask me to give up the best bell I have ever heard, to men in grey who say a door will open. Doors have been opening in my head for forty years and I rather like the draught. Bring me a better note and we will talk.
