place_lore.nirncraft.frostflow_lighthous: A lighthouse on the rocks of the Winterhold coast. Its lamp has been dark for nine nights, and ships are feeling their way blind along the ice.

#2nd of Frostfall
Took up the post. The last keeper's family is gone, and the Jarl's steward was very quiet about how. Lamp works. Lens is cracked but serviceable. There is a cellar door nailed shut. I have left it nailed.

#11th of Frostfall
Scratching under the floor at night. Rats, I said. Rats do not click.

#14th of Frostfall
The cellar door was open this morning, nails on the floor. The lens was gone from the lamp. I followed the wet tracks down into the rock. There are tunnels under this lighthouse that go a long way into the dark. I am going down with a lantern and an axe. The ships need that lens.
Frostflow's gone dark. The new keeper Winterhold hired didn't last a season. Last ship that tried the coast at night is in pieces off the point.
Captain Hjolfrid of the Sea Squall

To whoever is supposed to be keeping the Frostflow light.
On the night of the 15th my ship came within a rope's length of the rocks below your tower. Your lamp was DARK. I lost a boat, two barrels of salt and very nearly my temper, which I am now losing in writing.

If your light is not burning when I return from Dawnstar, I will come ashore myself and kindle it with your furniture.
Hjolfrid

^Postscript
I am told the keeper went missing. I do not care. Find another keeper. Find a goat that can work a flint. I have a hold full of Windhelm salt and a crew who would like to see their wives again.

place_lore.nirncraft.frostflow_stead.hoo: A bleak coastal out-stead below the northern glacier cliffs where hardy sheep and salt-cured horker meat are kept behind drift-walls.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostflow_stead.rum: Travelers along the ice coast say the lamps at Frostflow Stead haven't been trimmed in a week, and strange clicking sounds come from the cellar.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostflow_stead.war: Built the snow-wall another two feet higher around the sheepfold to keep the sea-gales off the ewes. Something keeps scratching underneath the flagstone floor of the main house at night, like iron picks working through the glacial ice.

place_lore.nirncraft.frostmere_crypt.gan:
1. Old graves first. They don't scream.
2. Fresh graves only if the ring is gold. Silver's not worth the shovel-work.
3. Nobody goes past the iron door at the back. I heard what's behind it humming and I don't want to meet it.

4. The old man keeps leaving notes about his wife's ring. I'm keeping it. Call it rent.
5. Anybody who goes soft and wants to give rings back can give their share back too.
6. The woman in the lake behind the crypt is not real. Stop talking about her. Stop going down to look. Haldor went to look and now Haldor sits by the water all night with a face like milk.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmere_crypt.hoo: A crypt in the wooded hills of the southern Pale, where a gang of grave-robbers has moved in among the Nord dead. They've started stealing from fresh graves, too.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmere_crypt.rum: There's a crew in Frostmere Crypt pulling rings off the dead. Not just the old dead. My neighbour's wife was buried a month ago with her wedding band. Last week the grave was open.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmere_crypt.sk4: Folio #12 (-152, -1246): Field inspection recorded for Frostmere Crypt within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.frostmere_crypt.wid:
To the robbers at Frostmere Crypt, if any of you can read.
You opened my wife Gerdir's grave on the 9th of Frostfall and took the ring I put on her finger thirty years ago. It is a plain silver band. It is worth perhaps twenty septims to you. It is worth everything I have left to me.

I will pay you forty for it. I will leave the coin under the cairn by the crypt road and ask no questions. If you will not sell it, then I pray Arkay finds you before I do.
Sigvald
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmoon_crag.hook: A crag in the highlands west of the Altar of Thrond where wolves that are not wolves gather under the full moon. The hunting lodge downhill has been empty since the night they gathered for its keeper.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmoon_crag.hunt: Painted on a flat stone below the crag in red earth, a Skaal warning of the kind they leave for each other: Moon-beasts here. Do not hunt alone. Do not hunt at night. If one of them speaks to you, do not answer. If one of them speaks to you in the voice of someone you knew, run, and do not look back to see whose face it is wearing.

Beneath the red marks, someone has scratched a name: Sigvar. Then a line through it, not quite finished, as though whoever began it could not decide whether a man who runs with the pack is dead or only gone.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmoon_crag.pack: Scratched into a pine by something with claws, and then, more carefully, by something with a knife: The Hunt does not end. The moon calls and we answer. The man from the lodge answered. He did not want to, at first. Now he runs at the head of the pack and does not remember his own name. We call him Grey Brother. He keeps a ring on a thong around his throat and growls at anyone who looks at it.
place_lore.nirncraft.frostmoon_crag.rumo: Don't camp near Frostmoon Crag. The Skaal say Hircine's children run there under the full moon. The fellow who kept the Abandoned Lodge used to laugh at that story.

place_lore.nirncraft.frykte_peak.cairn_n: Climbed in two days from the Headwaters of Harstrad. Built this cairn on the third. On a clear morning I counted: the ice of Castle Karstaag, the tusks of the Broken Tusk hills, the black barrow of Benkongerike, and the sea beyond Haknir's Shoal. And on the next rock, so close I could see the scales, a dragon asleep on Saering's Watch. I did not finish my count. Add a stone if you came up here and lived. There are four stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.frykte_peak.hook: A wind-scoured summit beside Saering's Watch, named by the Skaal for fear. From its top you can see the whole frozen north, and the dragon that circles it.
place_lore.nirncraft.frykte_peak.rumour: Frykte means fear in the old Skaal tongue. My grandfather said they named it after the first man who climbed it and saw what was sitting on the next peak over.

place_lore.nirncraft.gallows_rock.hook: A ruined fort on a crag west of Mixwater Mill where Windhelm's old jarls hanged traitors, now held by grim hunters in silver-buckled leathers who keep a prisoner in chains.
place_lore.nirncraft.gallows_rock.hunt_c:
#2nd of Frostfall
Took the sawyer Ulmir at Mixwater Mill without trouble. His brother made a noise. Brothers always do. We were gone before the guard was sent for.

#6th of Frostfall
Ulmir swears he is no beast. They all swear. We keep him in silver and wait for the moon. If he is clean, we let him walk home and apologise for the inconvenience. We have never once had to apologise.

#9th of Frostfall
The moon came. We have not had to apologise. Two of my men are dead and the chains held, barely. When the brother comes, and he will come, we kill whatever comes with him.
place_lore.nirncraft.gallows_rock.rumour: There's screaming from Gallows Rock some nights, and howling other nights. The men up there say they hunt beasts. I've never heard of a beast with a brother in Mixwater.
place_lore.nirncraft.gallows_rock.sk4_no: Folio #16 (1279, -211): Field inspection recorded for Gallows Rock within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.gallows_rock.ulmir_:
Torvar,
They let me write this because they want me to say it. So I will say it, and I will say it to you, because you are the only one it matters to.

Two winters ago, in the woods by Cradlecrush Rock, something bit me and I lived. Since then there have been nights I do not remember, and mornings I have washed blood off my hands in the river before you woke. I told myself it was deer. It was mostly deer.
Do not come for me. If you do come, do not open the chains on a full moon. Take the ring Father gave me, and remember me as I was in the daylight.
place_lore.nirncraft.garden_of_the_sacre:
#THE SEVENTH BED
Seven hyacinths for the seven winds, spaced one-point-six paces apart. Three roses for the three sisters, each one a hand-span taller than the last. One fern in the centre, placed by moonlight, and not watered by anyone who has seen it do something unusual.

The fern is not mentioned in the original plan. It arrived on its own the winter before I took the post. It has never wilted. It has never grown. It is the only thing in the garden that has refused to be counted.
A terraced garden in Shimmerene where every bed, path and fountain has been laid out according to a sacred ratio, so that the whole place hums when the wind is right.
The gardeners of the Sacred Numbers never prune by eye. They prune by arithmetic. The flowers, by all accounts, resent it, and bloom in perfectly regular, perfectly sulky rows.

place_lore.nirncraft.gate_of_alma_ruma.h: A worn Alessian gate of white stone with a scroll-temple annex leaning against its flank, still ringed by a dry processional road.
place_lore.nirncraft.gate_of_alma_ruma.r: The Alma Ruma annex has a ledger of names and the old priest there weeps when anyone asks to see the page that was cut out.
place_lore.nirncraft.gate_of_alma_ruma.w: Struck through: 11. Unstruck: 4,208. The page that held the Nibenay vintners was cut out in the year of my predecessor's death and the wine-house of Thalaras never answered my letters. I have kept the register open. The dead are not finished.
place_lore.nirncraft.gateway_inn.hook: A Sadrith Mora inn whose windows show somewhere different each hour, which the Magisters call a resonance and the keeper calls a nuisance.
place_lore.nirncraft.gateway_inn.room_lo:
#Window observations, this month
Room 3: lagoon, lagoon, a fungal grove, a bored Magister waving.
Room 6: the same fungal grove, larger.
Room 9: lagoon, Isles, a field of white flowers, and a woman in a green shawl who points west and a little down.

Guests are not to be charged for the view. Nor for the ghost.
place_lore.nirncraft.gateway_inn.rumour: Room nine's window showed a lagoon on Monday, the Ascadian Isles on Tuesday, and last night, a woman in a green shawl, waving at someone who never checked in.

place_lore.nirncraft.geirmunds_hall.eydi:
~Kynareth, keeper of the wind on the water,
~you gave the lake its fish and you gave me my husband.
~You kept one. Give me back the other.

Arne wore a net-weight of carved soapstone on a cord, a fish with a hole for an eye. I made it for him. If you find it, bring it to Ivarstead. I'll stand at the dock every night until somebody does.
place_lore.nirncraft.geirmunds_hall.hook: A sunken Nord hall on an island in Lake Geir, east of Ivarstead, said to hold the tomb of an ancient archmage's hunter. The lake around it has a reputation for swallowing boats.
place_lore.nirncraft.geirmunds_hall.rumo: Nobody fishes near Geirmund's Hall if they can help it. Eydis's husband did. The lake gave back his boat, upside down. It kept him.
place_lore.nirncraft.geirmunds_hall.scho: Aurenia Calvo, of the College of Winterhold

#Lake Geir, 21st of Hearthfire
The local tradition that the hall belongs to one 'Geirmund' is, as usual with Rift peasantry, half right. The burial is unquestionably of the Gauldur period (cf. my own monograph, chapter four, which nobody has read).

#Same day, later
The lower chambers are flooded and something moves in the flooding. The fisherman who rowed me here, a pleasant man named Arne, went to fetch the boat and has not returned. I am writing this by the light of my last candle. I shall finish chapter five in here if I must.

place_lore.nirncraft.ghostfence_morrowin: A long wall of shimmering ghost-light enclosing the mountain, broken at gate-posts and humming at a pitch just below hearing.
The ghostfence has a gap you can see only at dusk, shaped like a person. It moves.

I have measured the fall for nine years. The ash falls where there are people with something to forget: a city of refugees, a mining colony, a village that fled. It is not random. It is drawn. If you wish to know what the volcano is saying, follow the wind and listen to what the ash does when it lands.

THE FENCE HAS A WALKER. Do not go through at dusk, do not carry a lantern through, do not follow the sleepers. The breach is a mile from the gate-posts and growing. Every night a little closer to the crater. Report to the Temple at once. They have not answered the last six.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.gazetteer.p0:
#Water, grain, law
Well-Keeper Dusk measures the Basin Well each dusk and each dawn and trusts nobody's plumb-line. Granary-Mother Seshi knows each person's debts by their pockets. Watcher Tamtam has watched for rain for eleven years. Magistrate Lucia Verrus keeps the courthouse and will not discuss the goat.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.gazetteer.p1:
#Inn and clay
The Stable Steed feeds the guar first; it is economics, not discrimination. Nesa Clay-Hand makes pots and one very ugly, much-loved idol. Twyllbek ruins hold a lead tube with the grant to the Eastern Cut. It belongs to the road.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.guild_reward: Reward offered for the recovery of the field journal of Adrienne Lirrian, Associate of the Guild, who travelled to the Daedric monument of Hermaeus Mora west of Stormhold to study the alleged intertwining of a Hist root with the monument's stone.

Associate Lirrian is presumed lost. Her assistant, Kassus, returned to Gideon, briefly, and then left again in the night for the shrine, reciting what we believe to be page numbers. If he is found, do not argue with him. He knows things now that do not bear arguing with. Bring the journal. Bring Kassus too, if he still answers to his name.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.hook: A former Imperial plantation town on the edge of the Black Marsh, its grand houses gutted by vines and Saxhleel salvagers, its Mages Guild chapter clinging on with a handful of stubborn scholars.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.plantation_l:
#Saltrice harvest, 4E 172
Hands in debt-service: 61. Hands escaped: 4. Hands returned: 0. Hands that the King's envoy calls 'free subjects of Argonia': 61. I have written to the Governor. There is no Governor.

#Last entry
The hands did not riot. They did not burn the house. They simply put down their tools at noon, all together, and walked into the marsh. The envoy came at dusk and read me a paper. I am leaving for Leyawiin tonight. Let the vines have the ballroom. They were always better dancers than my wife.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon.rumour: Gideon's quiet these days, except for the stone-cutters. The Mages Guild there lost a scholar at the Mora stones near Stormhold, and the Guildmaster's offering a reward for her journal.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon_courthouse.d:
#Cases pending
The water of the Eastern Cut: two farmers, two forgeries. The goat matter: closed, reopened, closed. The granary valve: referred to the well-keeper. The guar of the Stable Steed: ruled a wanderer, not a thief.

Magistrate Verrus notes that she is delighted to rule whenever the facts are short and the law is shorter.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon_courthouse.h: The clay courthouse of Gideon, where the Magistrate rules with the sun in her eyes and a goat in her past.
place_lore.nirncraft.gideon_courthouse.r: Two farmers dispute the Eastern Cut and both hold forged deeds. The Magistrate has read them and will not rule for a lie. She wants the original grant.

place_lore.nirncraft.gjukars_monument.ho: A weathered monument on the windswept plains north-west of Whiterun, raised to a war-leader called Gjukar and the shield-brothers who fell with him. On still nights, some say, the battle is still being fought.
place_lore.nirncraft.gjukars_monument.mo:
GJUKAR AND HIS SHIELD-BROTHERS STOOD HERE.
THEY DID NOT ASK HOW MANY CAME AGAINST THEM.
THEY ASKED ONLY WHERE TO STAND.

LET THE GRASS GROW HIGH OVER THEM.
LET THE WIND SAY THEIR NAMES.
TRAVELLER, IF YOU STAND HERE, STAND STRAIGHT.
^Scratched beneath, newer:
Saw them last Middas from the Legion camp. Lined up. Ready. Shields locked, though there was no one coming at them. One of them, the big one at the front with the braided beard, looked straight at me. He nodded, like one soldier to another, and then they were mist. I've stood straighter since.
place_lore.nirncraft.gjukars_monument.ru: Gjukar's Monument? Old soldiers' stone, out on the plains. Legion camp's nearby. The sentries swear they hear swords at night where there's no one. They keep the fires big.
place_lore.nirncraft.gjukars_monument.sk: Folio #4 (-1302, 32): Field inspection recorded for Gjukars Monument within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.glacial_cave.appren: Hjalmar was here. Tied three days. They took the cutting pick my master gave me; it has his mark on the haft, a hand and a hammer. If I do not come back, whoever reads this, take the pick to Aevar Stone-Ear in the Skaal Village. Tell him I did not teach them the words. Tell him the ice is crying.

Lower down, smaller, as if written later by a colder hand: They argue at night about the words. Torvar says there are no words, only Skaal tricks. Bjorn is not so sure. The white thing in the deep ice came closer tonight. It stood over me and did not touch me. I think it knows who taught me.
place_lore.nirncraft.glacial_cave.hook: A cave of blue ice in the far north, veined with stalhrim. The Skaal cut it with prayers and patience. The men who took the cave this winter cut it with neither.
place_lore.nirncraft.glacial_cave.rumour: Aevar Stone-Ear, the Skaal smith, sent his apprentice to the Glacial Cave to cut stalhrim the proper way. Boy found smugglers there instead, and the ice spirits are angry.
place_lore.nirncraft.glacial_cave.smuggl:
Slabs cut: 14. Slabs cracked in the cutting: 9. The stuff fights the chisel like it's alive.
Buyer in Windhelm pays 300 a slab if it reaches him whole. The Skaal boy we caught says it never reaches anyone whole without the words. I said he can teach us the words or he can stay tied up. He's chosen to stay tied up. Stubborn little seal.

Something walks in the deep ice now. White, see-through, cold enough to stop your heart from across the cave. Bjorn says it's a wraith, come because we cut without asking. Bjorn also says we should let the boy go. Bjorn's getting a smaller share.

place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoor_memorial.h: A weathered obelisk on the Bjoulsae shore, carved with the names of boatmen drowned between the founding of Evermor and the last great flood.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoor_memorial.m:
^Left on the plinth beneath a flat stone:
"I have cut four hundred and twelve names. The last was my own son's. I am to cut mine when it is time. I have the chisel ready, and the stone, and the dates. Only the final mark is left, and I will not carve it until I am sure."

"There is a space at the bottom, a hand's width, with nothing in it. People say the lake will fill it. I think the lake fills it every year and I merely keep it clean. If you are reading this, I hope you are not a boatman. If you are, stay on land awhile. The lake is a great reader of obelisks."
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoor_memorial.r: The names on the Glenmoor Memorial are re-cut every year by an old woman who is nobody's kin. She says the lake asked her.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoril_coven.cov:
A long thigh bone, polished, with letters burned along its length:
'Take only what is offered. Offer only what is asked. Keep the hunters' heads for the Lord of the Chase. Keep the rest for ourselves.'
A ring of tiny crow feathers is bound to one end with red thread.

Scratched along the shaft of the bone, much smaller, as if added later: 'The Hunter's beasts come seeking a cure for the blood. Sell it dear. Some pay with silver. Some pay with sons. A few pay with a promise to come back, and those are the best payment of all, for they always do.'
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoril_coven.hoo: A cave in the western Falkreath hills where a coven of witches meets under the pines. Those who come asking favours of them pay in strange coin.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoril_coven.rum: The Glenmoril witches don't bother the town. That's what worries me. Witches that leave you alone are waiting for something.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoril_coven.sk4: Folio #17 (-1563, 761): Field inspection recorded for Glenmoril Coven within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #17 for glenmoril_coven: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Glenmoril Coven are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenmoril_coven.vil:
To the wise women in the hill,
You told me to write it down so it would bind. Here it is. In exchange for my son's fever breaking, I give you the first thing he loses in his life that he cannot find again. You said it would be a small thing. A button, a tooth, a dream.

His fever broke on Middas. He is well. Last night he could not remember his father's face, and his father has been dead only a year. Was that the price? Is it paid? I am frightened to come and ask in case asking costs more.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenpoint.hook: A small salt-and-fishing harbour on the western tip of Glenumbra, where honest men sell salt at the same price to everyone and nobody quite believes it.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenpoint.pan_notic:
^NOTICE
^Salt is sold at the pans at a fixed price, in sealed crates, on market days only. No salt is to be carried from the pans after dusk. No salt is to be carried to the pans at any hour. Any crate arriving by water will be treated as a bad omen and a crime, in that order.

^By order of the Reeve: the tide-tables are to be posted at the quay each dawn. Anyone who tampers with them will be fined. Anyone who corrects them will be thanked, and told to stop. This town has always been small. It intends to remain honest.
place_lore.nirncraft.glenpoint.rumour: In Glenpoint the salt is salted twice. The first time for taste, and the second for luck, which the Reeve says is also a kind of tax.

place_lore.nirncraft.gloombound_mine.dus:
Chalked on a timber prop at the mouth of the east drift, where the Orc miners of Narzulbur leave word for the next shift, in big blunt letters:
BROKE THROUGH. CAVE BEYOND. WARM. SMELLS OF ROT AND VINEGAR. BRING MORE OIL. DO NOT TELL CHIEF YET. WANT TO SEE IT FIRST.

Lower down, smaller:
CLICKING IN THE DARK. LANTERN GOES DIM AT THE CRACK. NOT AFRAID. GOING IN.

At the bottom, scratched with a pick-point, barely legible:
PALE THINGS. EYES SEWN SHUT. THEY HEAR YOUR HEART. TELL MOGDURZ
place_lore.nirncraft.gloombound_mine.hoo: Narzulbur's ebony mine, a black throat in the hillside where the Orcs dig the finest ore in Eastmarch, and where the deepest drift has started swallowing miners.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloombound_mine.ore:
#Hearthfire
East drift: 3 bars ebony, 1 good vein. West drift: 2 bars. Bad air in the low cut, two men sick.
#Frostfall, first week
East drift: 4 bars and a breakthrough into old rock. Strange smell. Miners grumbling.

#Frostfall, second week
East drift: 0 bars. Lantern-oil missing. Dushgar's pick found by the crack, handle chewed.
#Frostfall, third week
East drift closed by order of the chief. Nobody argued, and that is the most frightening line in this book.
Mogdurz came to the drift mouth every night this week and stood there with an axe. Nobody argued with that either.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloombound_mine.rum: Gloombound's the richest hole in Eastmarch and the Orcs guard it like their own teeth. They've stopped working the east drift, though, and an Orc doesn't scare easy.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloombound_mine.sk4: Folio #17 (2220, -200): Field inspection recorded for Gloombound Mine within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.gloomreach.falmer_g:
On the walls of the deepest grotto someone, likely Sinnoc, has copied the Falmer scratchings in chalk to understand them. They show rows of mushrooms, carefully counted. Then a figure holding a staff over them. Then the figure feeding something to the mushrooms: something with arms and legs.
Under the drawing, in Sinnoc's hand: Oh. That's what the soil is.

Further along the wall the chalk lines grow shaky. Sinnoc has drawn the Falmer gardener again, larger, with something around its neck, a cord strung with what might be teeth. Beside it he has written: He wears the gatherers he catches. I can see a Nord ring on that cord. I am going back for my satchel and then I am leaving.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloomreach.gatherer: Master Lisbet, the spores are everything I promised. Glowing caps the size of a shield. I've filled one satchel already and I'm going deeper for the blue ones, the kind you said cure a fever in a night.

Should I not come back, the satchel is hidden behind the second falls, under a flat stone with a chalk mark. You paid me in advance, so you're owed it, dead or alive. I'm a lot of things, master, but I'm not a cheat.
The Falmer are tending these things like a farmer tends his beans. I think there is one who does nothing else. They call him something that sounds like a hiss.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloomreach.hook: A cave in the southeastern Reach where glowing fungus lights the walls in green and blue, and the Falmer tend their gardens in the dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloomreach.rumour: There's mushrooms down in Gloomreach that glow like moons. Alchemists'll pay a fortune for them. The pale folk who farm them don't sell.
place_lore.nirncraft.gloomreach.sk4_note: Folio #43 (-1904, 278): Field inspection recorded for Gloomreach within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.gnaar_mok.hook: A muddy swamp town raised on stilts with a mangrove market and a landing for silt striders.
place_lore.nirncraft.gnaar_mok.rumour: A stall in the Gnaar Mok market sells receipts and nothing else. Someone's always buying.
place_lore.nirncraft.gnaar_mok.thread.p0: THE CRESCENT LEDGER KEEPS ITS DEBTORS. THE DEBTORS KEEP THEIR YEARS. If you open this box you will know each name on it, and each name owes you. Be a creditor or a liberator. The swamp does not tell you which is easier.
place_lore.nirncraft.gnaar_mok.web.p0: I, the undersigned courier, agree to deliver parcels of brass to the Balmora cellar without opening them, listening to them, or answering when they speak. The master pays on delivery. The master will explain, in due time, what the guest requires.
place_lore.nirncraft.goats_head_oasis.ho: A well-oasis with palms and a half-buried statue of a goat, its horns visible above the sand.
place_lore.nirncraft.goats_head_oasis.ru: The Goat's Head well is an inch lower every season, and the goat statue is half-buried now.
place_lore.nirncraft.goats_head_oasis.we: Count nine paces from the left horn at dawn, dig under the shadow's tip. The first well was capped when the city's king drew the sand about his shoulders. Below it, a shaft. Below the shaft, a tithe. Bring water or bring no one.
place_lore.nirncraft.golden_gryphon_garr: A tiny turret-room above a tavern in Alinor, said to be the oldest gryphon-rider's garret in the city, hung with feathers, saddles and a single very worn flying helm.

#THEY LIVED HERE
Dalwe, who flew too high. Oren, who flew too low. Mirimel, who flew exactly as she should and still did not return. Calindor, who is the only one who came back, and he does not talk about it.

At the bottom, in a fresh hand: 'I took the room for the view. It is a very good view. It looks out, over the harbour, to a headland where a lantern is lit every evening. I have not asked who lights it. I think it is for us.'
The garret has been let to a different rider each decade, and every one of them was lost over the sea. The rent is very low. People take it anyway, for the view.
place_lore.nirncraft.goldenglow_estate.h:
#Frostfall, 4E 201
Hives standing: 46. Hives lost to wet rot: 3. Hives lost to a bear that swam the channel: 1 (bear also lost, the guards saw to it).
Honey to Black-Briar Meadery: 19 casks. Wax to the Temple of Mara for candles: 4 crates. Wax sold to Snow-Shod Farm on credit: 1 crate. Do not tell the master.

Personal note: I found a jar of our honey in a Ratway den last week, cut with something red. It smelled of berries and rot. Whoever is selling the Redwater stuff is using Goldenglow honey to sweeten it. I'd like to know who is buying from us twice.
An island honey farm on Lake Honrich whose hives supply the Black-Briar Meadery. Its owner pays mercenaries to guard bees, which tells you how much honey is worth in the Rift.
place_lore.nirncraft.goldenglow_estate.r: Goldenglow's honey is the only reason Black-Briar mead tastes like anything. The owner keeps hired swords on the island. Over bees. Bees!

place_lore.nirncraft.grave_singers_lodge: A lodge of singers on a hummock in the delta, hung with reed-chimes, with a single long table of seven empty chairs.
The singers' lodge has seven chairs and three singers. The other four have taken the lord's coin.

~Down the delta, down the water,~sing the sons and sing the daughters.~Past the reeds and past the flood,~to the teeth that drink the blood.~Lay them where the tide is slow.~Sing them home. We'll sing them so.

place_lore.nirncraft.graywinter_watch.ho: A cold cave east of Whiterun, close by the Ritual Stone, where a troll has made its den among the bones of its meals. Hunters have stopped taking the eastern trails.
place_lore.nirncraft.graywinter_watch.hu: TROLL. Big, grey, three eyes, one of them blinded by my first arrow. It heals faster than I can shoot. I put six arrows in it and it pulled them out and ate the shafts.

It took Gerd's hound and my good bow and it took the bounty notice the Jarl's steward nailed by the Battle-Born Farm road. The bounty still stands: 100 septims for the troll's head at the gate of Whiterun.

Bring fire. Bring friends. Bring more fire. Ulfgar.
place_lore.nirncraft.graywinter_watch.ru: Graywinter Watch has a troll in it, a big frost-grey one. It took a mammoth calf from the giants last month, which tells you how hungry it is. Don't go in without fire.
place_lore.nirncraft.graywinter_watch.sk: Folio #33 (475, -79): Field inspection recorded for Graywinter Watch within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #33 for graywinter_watch: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Graywinter Watch are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_bazaar.hook: An arcaded covered street of forty stalls under the temple's shadow, where every purchase is the first sale after the theft.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_bazaar.rumour: Mistress Hlaren's guild stall stamps contracts. One came through last week for forty crates of lamp-oil whose route runs, in the margin, beneath the bazaar itself.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_bazaar.stall_:
#By arcade
First arcade: spice, tea, dried fish, honey-cake. Second arcade: lamp-oil, ink, rope, lenses. Third arcade: cloth, buttons, ribbon, cheerful lies. Fourth arcade: what the third arcade does not stock.

#By rule
Nothing sold here is stolen. Everything sold here was stolen once. It is the first sale that matters. Report any theft of the second sort to the guild stall. It will be written down.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_lift_at_alfta: A Dwemer lift shaft in the hills near Nightgate Inn that plunges straight down into the dark. The brass still gleams, and the gears still turn when nobody is touching them.
There's a Dwemer lift east of Nightgate. Goes down further than anybody's ever dropped a stone and heard it land.

Folio #16 (961, -997): Field inspection recorded for Great Lift At Alftand within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #16 for great_lift_at_alftand: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Great Lift At Alftand are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

The lift descends at a rate I estimate (1) to be some twenty feet per breath, for a duration of three hundred and forty breaths. I did not ride it. I timed a lantern on a rope until the rope ran out, then timed it with a falling stone until I heard nothing at all.

(1) I note for the record that my apprentice, the excellent Brelas, offered to ride it and I forbade him. I sent him to Alftand instead. In hindsight I am not certain this was the safer choice.
Conclusion: the lift connects the northern ruins to something vast beneath the Pale. I recommend further study by someone more expendable than myself.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_lift_at_mzinc: A great Dwemer lift standing alone in the snowy hills south of Mzinchaleft. It descends to the buried dark beneath Skyrim, and something down there is still sending it back up.
There's a brass tower south of Mzinchaleft that hums and clanks on its own. Shepherd up there says it goes down, and down, and down, and sometimes something comes up in it.
The brass tower went down at dusk and came up at dawn. Nobody in it. Third time this month.

When the door opens there's a warm wind from below that smells of mushrooms and old metal. My dogs won't go near it. Last night the door opened and something small and blue and glowing floated out, drifted round the sheep, and went back down. The sheep didn't mind. I minded. I'm moving the flock to Stonehills.
Sigrun at the mine says the Dwemer roads under Mzinchaleft run all the way down to this lift. If her brother's still alive down there, maybe he'll come up in it one morning. I'll keep an eye on it for her. From a distance.
place_lore.nirncraft.great_lift_at_raldb: A Dwemer lift by the ruins of Raldbthar, its brass housing poking out of the snow. Quaestor Vesk believes it is one end of a vast hidden road beneath the Pale.
The brass tower near Raldbthar hums at night. College folk come out and listen to it like it's a bard. Strange people, mages.
The lift at Raldbthar hums at a pitch identical, within the limits of my tuning fork, to the lift at Alftand (1). This cannot be coincidence. The Dwemer did not build in coincidences.

(1) My tuning fork is of Dwemer make, purchased in Markarth at ruinous expense. I am told the fence who sold it now lives at Fort Fellhammer. I do not wish to know how he came by it.
Hypothesis: both lifts descend to a single great cavern. Proposal: find it. Precondition: find a brave assistant, now that Brelas is gone.
place_lore.nirncraft.green_eye_ruins.hoo: A ring of green-stained stones in the marsh where an herbalist's tent still stands, a journal still open inside it.
place_lore.nirncraft.green_eye_ruins.jou:
#Day ninety-one
Found it. A grey root, a white flower, three nights' steeping. It works on the mud-fever. I have tried it on myself. I am bitten. It was a small bite. I will finish this page and then the next.

#Day ninety-two
If anyone finds this: tell them I was not afraid. Tell Mother the lilies were never meant to be anything but white.
place_lore.nirncraft.green_eye_ruins.rum: A Soulrest daughter went into the marsh three years ago to find a cure and never came back. Her family keeps her lantern lit in the window and will not bury what they have not lost.
A green, sheltered hollow in the western hills, fed by warm springs and watched over by a spriggan. Poachers have moved in, and the hollow is growing angry.

#9th of Last Seed
Greenspring has a keeper. A spriggan, old and patient. I hunted here every autumn and it never troubled me, because I took one deer and said a word to Kynareth for it. That was the bargain, and we both kept it.

#20th of Last Seed
Three men have made camp in the hollow. They set snares on every trail and leave the carcasses to rot for the pelts. The spriggan has stopped being patient. Last night the trees closed the path behind me.

It is not the spriggan that needs killing. It is the men. But the men have bows, and I am one hunter.

~Kynareth of the wind and leaf,
~Take this one life and spare my grief.
~I took no more than I could eat,
~I left the fawn upon her feet.

~Keep the hollow green and wild,
~Keep the keeper reconciled,
~And if I break the bargain made,
~Let me lie in your green shade.

Carved smaller, at the foot of the tree, newer and deeper: 'The poachers cut this bark for kindling and laughed at the words. Three of them went into the thicket after a wounded doe that night. Two came back. The keeper does not forgive greed, and neither, I think, does She.'
Greenspring Hollow used to be the place to hunt elk. Now the trees there move when you're not looking. Some fools set up camp to trap the spriggan's deer, and the hollow's been wild ever since.

place_lore.nirncraft.greywater_grotto.he: White cap grows thickest in Greywater, by the warm spring at the back, where the steam keeps the frost off. Worth three times what it fetches up in Riverwood, because no one else will go.

The spiders sleep in the heat of the day, curled up in the high webs. Walk soft along the left wall, under the overhang, and they do not wake. That was how it was for twenty years.
This year there is a new one. Bigger. The colour of old snow, with a sac on her back the size of a churn. She does not sleep. I am leaving my satchel in the dry cleft and going out light. Will come back for it.
place_lore.nirncraft.greywater_grotto.ho: A spider-choked grotto in the hills south of Helgen, where a hot spring keeps the webs warm and the frostbite spiders fat. A herbalist went in after the rare mushrooms that grow by the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.greywater_grotto.ru: Old Ragnhild the herb-wife went into Greywater Grotto for her white caps. Swore she knew a path the spiders didn't. Turns out they knew it too.
place_lore.nirncraft.greywater_grotto.sk: Folio #33 (-77, 1314): Field inspection recorded for Greywater Grotto within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #33 for greywater_grotto: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Greywater Grotto are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.greywater_grotto.we:
A strip of linen with letters daubed in what might be soot:
SATCHEL IN CLEFT. LEFT WALL. TAKE IT TO BRYNJA AT HALF-MOON MILL. NOT FOR ME, FOR HER SICK BOY. WHITE CAP BOILED IN MILK. THREE DAYS.
The rest of the linen has been bound into the web, carefully, as if the spider meant to keep it.

The spider has spun a careful spiral around the linen, layer upon layer, the way she wraps her prey. A little further along the same web hangs a herb-wife's shawl, faded blue, embroidered with a sprig of lavender at each corner.

place_lore.nirncraft.gryphon_aerie.hook: A cliff nest of enormous gryphons high above the Summerset coast, where the great birds of the Dominion's riders roost between patrols.
place_lore.nirncraft.gryphon_aerie.rider:
#ON THE LEDGE TODAY
Stormbrow: cross. Willowfeather: sulking. Brass: asleep, do not wake. Old Mother: out hunting, leave her perch. The new one: unnamed, nipped Dalwe, do not leave sweetmeats near.

Beneath, in a rider's scrawl: 'The new one has not been named because it has not decided. It has watched every rider that came to the ledge. It has made no choice. Which is, to Calindor's mind, the most intelligent thing a gryphon has done in a hundred years.'
place_lore.nirncraft.gryphon_aerie.rumou: Every gryphon in the aerie has a name and a temper, and the riders say the temper is the better guide. A rider who cannot tell a sulking gryphon from a cross one does not last the season.

place_lore.nirncraft.guldun_rock.caravan: Note to self: at the bend near Guldun Rock, do not stop. Do not stop to fix a wheel. Do not stop to relieve oneself. The giants consider the bend theirs, and they have opinions about wheels.

Second note to self: the toll at Valtheim Towers, just north, is now higher than the profit of the trip. J'datharr suggests the eastern pass next time, through the Rift. Ahkari says no. Ahkari is the boss. J'datharr will write it down anyway, so that later J'datharr can say he said so.
place_lore.nirncraft.guldun_rock.hook: A giant camp on a rocky hill east of Whiterun, beside the river road. Caravans give it a wide berth, and the giants watch every wagon go by as if counting the cheeses inside.
place_lore.nirncraft.guldun_rock.rumour: Guldun Rock's giants are touchy. A Khajiit caravan cut too close and lost a wagon of salt. The giants licked it clean, they say. Every grain.

place_lore.nirncraft.gyldenhul_barrow.br:
Aunt Yrsa,
You said the old proving was done with. You said nobody has to walk into Gyldenhul any more. But the old men still talk about who went in and who came back, and they never talk about me. I am taking Father's spear. The one with the seal-tooth on the shaft.

If I come back you can be angry at me. If I do not come back, do not send anyone after me who does not want to go. I mean that. The All-Maker gives and takes, and I would rather be taken than be nothing. Brandr.
place_lore.nirncraft.gyldenhul_barrow.ho: A Nordic tomb on the eastern shore, a short walk from the Skaal village. Young Skaal hunters once went down its stairs to prove themselves. Lately they go down and do not come back up.
place_lore.nirncraft.gyldenhul_barrow.pr: On the wall of the stair, generations of Skaal marks: a hand, a spear, a name, cut by the young hunters who came down and walked out again. The oldest are worn almost smooth. The newest is a single spear-mark with a seal tooth drawn beside it and no name yet, as if the carver meant to finish it on the way out. Further down the stair the marks stop. Something has scraped the wall clean.

Below the last marks, at the turn of the stair, a crude warning has been chalked by some Skaal elder: The proving is ended. Go home. If you will not go home, go with two companions and a torch, and come back by dusk, or your mother will cut your name on this wall herself.
place_lore.nirncraft.gyldenhul_barrow.ru: Brandr, Yrsa's nephew, went into Gyldenhul Barrow to prove he was a man. The Skaal don't make their boys do that any more. He did it anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.haafingar_stormcloa: Office of the Jarl of Eastmarch

To the commander of the Haafingar camp:
You are not to engage Fort Hraggstad. You are to be seen. Every night your fires burn on that hill is a night General Tullius keeps men in Solitude who might otherwise march on Whiterun.

Recruit quietly among the Haafingar Nords. Pay in coin where you can and in promises where you can't. Send word of Thalmor traffic on the embassy road; the Jarl takes a particular interest in where the elves take our people.
Under no circumstances let the men visit family in Dragon Bridge. The Penitus Oculatus are there, and they are patient.

A Stormcloak war camp hidden in the hills between Dragon Bridge and the Statue to Meridia, a dagger held at Solitude's back. Some of its soldiers are Haafingar boys, a long way from home and a short walk from their mothers.

Mother,
I can see the smoke from our chimney from the ridge where I stand watch. I could walk home in an afternoon. I won't, because the sergeant would call it desertion, and because I'd never get my nerve back to leave again.

I'm not sorry I joined. Skyrim should be ruled by Skyrim. But I'm sorry I left the way I did, shouting, with Eirik standing in the door. Tell him he's the man of the house now. Tell him not to do anything stupid.
I keep starting this letter and not sending it. If a friend finds it, carry it to Hulda by the bridge. She'll want it even if she throws it in the fire.
The rebels camp so close to Dragon Bridge you can smell their cookfires. Half the village has a cousin up there. The other half has a cousin in the Legion. Makes for a quiet tavern.

place_lore.nirncraft.haemars_shame.haema:
Cut deep into the rock at the entrance, old and weathered:
'Haemar went in to pray for one more good winter. He got a thousand winters and no summers. Do not ask the shrine for anything you would not want forever.'
Below, in fresher letters: 'Went in anyway. Was worth it. - H.'

Further down, scratched faintly as if with a fingernail: 'The statue grins. It asks what you want. It does not ask what you will give. That part comes later.' The rock beneath is stained darker than the rest, in a line, as if someone sat here a long time and wept.
place_lore.nirncraft.haemars_shame.hook: A cave in the far eastern hills of Falkreath where a hunter once turned to a forbidden shrine and was rewarded with fangs. Vampires keep his shame warm now.
place_lore.nirncraft.haemars_shame.rumou: Haemar's Shame. Named for a man who made a bargain he regretted. They say there's still a shrine down there that answers whoever asks, if they can get past the ones with teeth.
place_lore.nirncraft.haemars_shame.sk4_n: Folio #30 (553, 1173): Field inspection recorded for Haemars Shame within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.haemars_shame.vampi:
#Frostfall
Two new thralls from the Rift road, a cartwright and his wife. The wife bites back, which is amusing. The master says keep them separate so they have something to beg for.
#Sun's Dusk
Visitors from the south, from a fortress they call the Bloodlet Throne. They want to trade thralls. They say Falkreath folk are sweeter than Riftfolk on account of all the pine.

The master refused. He says the Throne is greedy and will bring the Dawnguard down on all of us. Then he went down to the old shrine and talked to the statue for an hour. He always comes back from the statue in a worse temper.

place_lore.nirncraft.hag_rock_redoubt.dr:
On the frame of a broken Forsworn drum, in the Reach tongue: Beat once for the hunters' return. Beat twice for the briar. Beat thrice for the Nords at the gate.
The crone took the Nord bard's drum as a prize after the raid on the Markarth road. She says its sound is sweet. We say it is a Nord sound and wakes the dead in Dead Crone Rock across the valley.
Below: The crone does not care. She likes waking them.
place_lore.nirncraft.hag_rock_redoubt.ho: A Forsworn camp clustered on a rock in the hills south of Markarth, ruled by a hagraven and fortified with bone and briar. Bards say a thorn-sword lies at its heart.
place_lore.nirncraft.hag_rock_redoubt.ma:
By order of Jarl Igmund. A bounty of 200 septims is offered for the hagraven of Hag Rock Redoubt, who has led raids on the stables, the Salvius farm and the road to Purewater Run.
Proof of the deed: her head, or her staff, or failing both, the testimony of two sober witnesses. Sober witnesses have proven hard to find in Markarth this year.

Scrawled across the bottom by some wag at the Silver-Blood Inn: Two sober witnesses can be had at the inn for 10 septims each, sober guaranteed until noon. And beneath, in another hand: The crone's staff is made of a Nord's thighbone. Bring that back and you won't need witnesses. You'll need a priest.
place_lore.nirncraft.hag_rock_redoubt.ru: Hag Rock's not a place you visit, it's a place you get dragged to. The crone there grows a sword out of a briar, they say. Bloodthorn, the songs call it.

place_lore.nirncraft.haknirs_shoal.hook: The rotting wreck of Haknir Death-Brand's ship, caught on the rocks of the north shore. His crew swore to sail with him past death, and the tide has never quite let them stop rowing.
place_lore.nirncraft.haknirs_shoal.rumou: Haknir's Shoal. Don't go there at night. I mean it. My father heard the oars once, and a voice calling the stroke, and there was no boat on the water at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.haknirs_shoal.salva: I took the purser's coin from the Death-Brand's hold before the oarsmen woke. Too heavy to swim back with. Buried it on Horker Island, east of the barrow, under the flat stone the old bull horker sleeps on, about twenty paces north of the island's middle. If the bull is still there, wait for him to go fishing. He always goes fishing at noon. I will come back for it in spring. If I do not, it was never mine anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.haknirs_shoal.ships:
^Sworn on the brand-iron
Every man who signs below shares the take in eight parts: two to the captain, one to the mate, one to the brand-iron's keeping, four among the oars.
No man leaves the oar while the captain lives. No man leaves the oar when the captain dies. The brand-iron keeps the oath, and the oath keeps the oars.

Thirty-one marks follow, some names, some only crosses. At the bottom, in a different hand, scrawled later: The iron is still in the captain's chest. As long as it is there, they row. Somebody take it out and throw it in a fire. Please.
place_lore.nirncraft.hakoshae.hook: A small hamlet that grew around a ring of upright moonstones. Tomb-guardians live in low houses in the circle's shadow, and pilgrims come for the night the moons stand together.
place_lore.nirncraft.hakoshae.keeper_rul:
^SWEEP AT DAWN. WALK SUNWISE. DO NOT STAND IN THE CENTRE.
^LET NO ONE COUNT THE STONES.
^IF YOU HEAR YOUR NAME, DO NOT ANSWER UNTIL IT HAS BEEN SAID THREE TIMES.
place_lore.nirncraft.hakoshae.pilgrim_lo:
#My second lap
Rimmen to Hakoshae, four days. The road is longer when you are no longer trying to finish. I find that I enjoy it more now that I have no idea where I am going. At the Shrine of the Crescent I met a bandit who gave me his hat.

Hamza says I should stop. I tell him I have not started. I think this is a joke. I think he thinks it is a lie. Tomorrow I shall go to the Temple of the Hidden Moon and see what the moons are keeping hidden.
place_lore.nirncraft.hakoshae.rumour: In Hakoshae they say the ring is not stones at all. It is a crowd, patient, that has been standing a thousand years waiting for a late friend.

place_lore.nirncraft.half_moon_mill.fish:
#Morndas, Hearthfire
Good catch on the east shore. Two salmon, one fat as a priest.
#Middas
Rowed toward the drowned fort to try the deep water. Line went slack. Water so cold my hand ached through the glove.

#Fredas
Went back. Saw a light under the water by the old tower of Ilinalta's Deep. Not a reflection. It moved. Then it went out, all at once, as if someone below had pinched a candle.
#Loredas
Not going back. Brynja laughed at me. Let her laugh.
place_lore.nirncraft.half_moon_mill.hook: A lumber mill on the shore of Lake Ilinalta, where the saw never stops between thaw and first snow. The lake beside it is quiet, perhaps too quiet.
place_lore.nirncraft.half_moon_mill.mill:
#Frostfall, 4E 201
To Falkreath, for the Jarl's new stable: 40 planks, pine. Paid 120 septims, after argument.
To the Legion camp west of here: 60 stakes, sharpened. Paid 200 by a quartermaster who did not smile once.
To the Stormcloak camp east of Helgen: 60 stakes, sharpened. Paid 210.

Wagon to Falkreath robbed on the road below Knifepoint Ridge. Lost 30 planks, one ox, and Ulf's good boots. Ulf unhurt but furious.
Note to self: if both armies are buying stakes, the war is coming here. Raise the price.
place_lore.nirncraft.half_moon_mill.rumo: Brynja at Half-Moon Mill keeps a wreath of pine on her door all year. For her mother, she says, who loved the Lady Stone out on the lake.

place_lore.nirncraft.hall_of_the_ansei.a:
#ON LISTENING TO A BLADE
A sword is a voice, and a voice has a meaning. Do not draw it to be heard. Draw it to hear. When the edge sings, it is not for you. It is for the one who held it before.
Many have asked what the blade says. I tell them: it says nothing, and that is the lesson. A voice that says nothing is a voice that is waiting for you to speak.
place_lore.nirncraft.hall_of_the_ansei.h: A white hall of arches and long cloisters on a Yokudan island, where the Ansei, the sword-saints of the old continent, once sat in silence to listen to their blades.
place_lore.nirncraft.hall_of_the_ansei.r: The Hall has no roof. The Ansei said they preferred the sky. The sky has returned the compliment, and has not rained on it in a thousand years.
place_lore.nirncraft.hall_of_the_lunar_c:
^1. THE CHALLENGE IS OPEN TO ANY WHO WALK UNARMED INTO THE HALL AND WALK OUT ARMED.
^2. NO CHAMPION MAY BE A PRINCE'S SON, NEPHEW, OR PRIVATE ASSASSIN.
^3. THE PILLAR SHALL BE CARVED BY THE LOSER.
At the foot, a late addition in small letters: '4. Nobody has ever asked what happens if there is no loser. The Pillar-Warden would prefer not to find out.'
A long hall of pillars in Rimmen, each cut with the name of a champion of the Midyear challenge. One pillar at the far end has been left blank, and no one has dared to carve it.
A hundred and twelve pillars, a hundred and eleven names. The blank one is for the champion that no one has met. People say she is already in the hall, and has been for a thousand years.
place_lore.nirncraft.hall_of_the_vigilan: A lodge in the snows of the southern Pale where the Vigilants of Stendarr train to hunt Daedra, vampires and witches. Its doors are open to the faithful and closed to everyone else.
The Vigilants keep a hall out in the snow. Hard men and women in grey. They'll pray over you, then ask whether you've been sleeping well.

Folio #13 (3, -1184): Field inspection recorded for Hall Of The Vigilant within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #13 for hall_of_the_vigilant: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Hall Of The Vigilant are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

~Stendarr, steady my hand when the dark is near,
~Let me not mistake the frightened for the foe,
~Let me not mistake the foe for the frightened,
~And when I fall, let me fall facing the door.
^Written under it in chalk: Sister Hrefna's version adds a line about cold soup, which we will not reproduce here.

^Taught to every novice of the Hall on their first night
The vow is spoken at dusk, facing the door, with a hand on the cold iron of the hall's own lock. It reminds us that the work is not hatred. A Vigilant who hates is only one more thing in the dark that must be watched.

Patrols, this fortnight:
Dawnstar road: Vigilant Tolan and Vigilant Hrefna. Watch for those afflicted by the nightmare plague. Do not let them climb the hill to the temple.
Dimhollow and Frostmere crypts: Vigilant Asgeir. Report bats in daylight, open graves, pale strangers.

Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon: Nobody. It is quiet. Quiet is how it begins.
Supplies: we are short of silver and holy water. Request both from the temple in Windhelm. Request also that someone stop the Dawnstar fishwives sending us their nightmares in writing.
place_lore.nirncraft.halldirs_cairn.dare:
Written in charcoal on a scrap of plank, in several childish hands:
TOUCH THE GRAVEYARD GATE AT MIDNIGHT - Ari did it
STEAL A SWEETROLL FROM THE INN - Thorvi did it
STAY IN THE WATCHTOWER TILL DARK - nobody
GO IN HALLDIR'S CAIRN AND COME OUT WITH SOMETHING - Thorvi said he would.
Underneath, in smaller letters: 'Thorvi came out. He came out WITHOUT something. That doesn't count.'

Underneath the dares, in a different, more grown-up hand: 'No more dares. Thorvi's father says if he catches any of you near that cairn again he'll build you each a very small coffin, and he's the only carpenter in town, so he can.'
place_lore.nirncraft.halldirs_cairn.hall: Halldir was a sorcerer of the old Nord kind, who learned his craft from the Dragon Priests and then refused to serve them. He could stand in three places at once, it was said, and argue with himself and win. When he died his followers built the cairn in a single night and placed him in it still talking.

The cairn's warden was a draugr bound to keep Halldir in, not others out. It takes trinkets from those who trespass, the tale goes, and wears them as a reminder of what it guards against. A warden with no trinkets is a warden that has done its work. A warden wearing many is one that has grown careless.
place_lore.nirncraft.halldirs_cairn.hook: A sealed burial cairn in the hills south of Falkreath, raised over a mage who would not stay buried. A carpenter's boy went in on a dare and came out with nightmares.
place_lore.nirncraft.halldirs_cairn.rumo: Bersi's lad went into Halldir's Cairn on a dare from the other boys. Came back pale as milk and hasn't slept since. Says a dead man is wearing his mother's pendant.
place_lore.nirncraft.halldirs_cairn.thor:
I write down what my son says in his sleep, because Sister Hilde asked me to.
'Three of him, Father. Three of the old man, and they all talked at once, and I couldn't tell which was real. Then the big one in the iron mask took Mother's pendant off my neck and put it on its own, and it went back to stand by the door.'
Signy's pendant. The one with the little hammer of Zenithar. He took it for courage. I would give my workshop to have it back on his neck and the nightmares gone.

place_lore.nirncraft.halls_of_colossus.h: A Dwemer hall of colossal machines with too-large doors and a giant half-assembled construct whose chest is cracked.
place_lore.nirncraft.halls_of_colossus.r: The Halls of Colossus drip at night. The sugar-folk say the meadow grows from its tears.
place_lore.nirncraft.halls_of_colossus.t: The seventh dial is under the great machine's ribs. It has turned three-quarters. It is the nearest to its mark of any I have seen. The colossus is a clock-weight for it. Whatever will come, it will come when the dial and the colossus agree. I have left the dial alone, and I have left the colossus alone, and I have left.
place_lore.nirncraft.halls_of_colossus.w: UNFINISHED. DO NOT DRAIN. The cold-water must not touch the meadow-soil, for the soil is the colossus's keeper. Close the chest. Do not wake the chest. Do not wake the colossus.
place_lore.nirncraft.halls_of_fabricatio: A conveyor-and-forge hall with long assembly lines of half-built animunculi and a forge-pit finale, hammer sounds echoing in foundry glow.
Hammer-sounds in the Halls of Fabrication again. The machines are making something, but they never finish.

All lines run. All parts accounted for, save one: the Attendant's thumb. Without the thumb the Attendant cannot sign, and without the signature the Attendant cannot be released. Hold station until it returns. We will hold station.
place_lore.nirncraft.halset_rest.halset_:
^A prayer scratched on a shell and left at the foot of the shrine:
"Let the sea be kind to my boat, and let the boat be kind to my back. Let the water bring what it takes, in the end, and let it take only what I would not miss."

"If this shell is found by a stranger, take it. If you hear in it the sea saying something, that is a gift, and you should say thank you aloud. It is a very old custom. It will not hurt you. It might do something else."
place_lore.nirncraft.halset_rest.hook: A lonely headland shrine north of Taneth, where fishermen leave small shells and sailors say the sea comes close to listen.
place_lore.nirncraft.halset_rest.rumour: At Halset Rest the tide comes in and goes out without wetting the steps. Pilgrims call it a courtesy. The old Pearl-Diver says it is just the way the water is.
Listen, all of you, because I won't say it twice.
The ore goes to the fence at Swindler's Den every second Loredas. Not to Whiterun, not to the smith in Riverwood, not to your cousin. Anyone caught skimming loses the hand he skimmed with.

The good stuff, the pale ore from the deep end, does NOT go to the fence. It goes to Silent Moons Camp, to Hrodna and her forge. She says it takes the moonlight better than any steel she's seen.

The miners we took from Loreius Farm stay chained. Feed them. Dead men don't dig. Brattvar.
A bandit camp built around a choked-off mine north of Whiterun. The stream that once ran past it has been dammed with rubble, and the bandits are digging for something they won't name.

Ulf of Loreius Farm. Taken 3rd of Sun's Height.
Asbjorn, also of Loreius. Taken same day.
We dig. We dig. The big one with the stone hand counts the sacks every night and beats whoever is short.

If anyone reads this, tell Vantus Loreius that his men did not run away. We were taken on the road to Whitewatch Tower. Tell him to send someone. Tell him we are still alive. Tell him to hurry.

And tell my mother in Whiterun that I said my prayers. Ulf.

Bandits at Halted Stream have been working that old mine day and night. Iron, some say. Others say they found a vein of something brighter, and that's why they've started killing anyone who gets close.

place_lore.nirncraft.hamvirs_rest.hamvir:
^HAMVIR THE PATIENT
^CHIEF OF THE WESTERN HILLS

He waited forty winters for the raiders from the Reach to tire of raiding. They tired first. Lay his axe across his knees, that he may wait once more, until the end of all waiting.

Beneath, in a rougher hand, scratched with a knife point long after the barrow was sealed: 'We came for the axe. We were told he was only bones. He is not only bones. Skeggi, I am sorry. If anyone reads this, leave the axe where it lies. Whatever it is worth, it is not worth what he does to you for touching it.'
place_lore.nirncraft.hamvirs_rest.hook: A small sunken tomb in the western hills, where a forgotten chieftain was laid to rest with his favourite axe. Grave-robbers have been at the entrance, and something below didn't like it.
place_lore.nirncraft.hamvirs_rest.robber:
Plan for Hamvir's Rest:
Go in at dusk. Dustman's Cairn is close, so if the Companions are about, wait. Skeggi carries the rope, I carry the bag. Hamvir's axe is in the last room, the old woman in Rorikstead says. Bronze-headed, silver wire on the haft. Worth a hundred to the right buyer, three hundred to the wrong one.

Later, hand shaking:
Skeggi is still in there. Hamvir is not resting. He sat up when we touched the axe and said something in the old tongue and the others got up too. I ran. Gods forgive me, I ran. If anyone goes in, put him down and bring Skeggi's body out. I'll pay what I have.
place_lore.nirncraft.hamvirs_rest.rumour: Hamvir's Rest is near the Companions' old cairn. Couple of grave-robbers went in last month bragging about axes and silver. One came out. He doesn't brag any more.

place_lore.nirncraft.harmugstahl.breedin: Ostrel Vane, formerly of the College of Winterhold

Day 61. Specimen IV (the large female) has consumed the Karthwasten shepherd entirely. Growth after feeding: a third of a hand-span along the leg. Remarkable. The College would never fund this, which is why the College will never know.

Day 64. The binding glyph holds the specimens docile only within the walls of Harmugstahl. When I tried to walk Specimen IV to Dragontooth Crater to test the effect of dragon presence, she turned on me, and I lost two fingers and a good cloak.
Day 70. Visitors expected. Some sellsword the miners sent. I shall extend my hospitality. Specimen IV has not eaten in four days.
place_lore.nirncraft.harmugstahl.hook: A ruined Nordic fort east of the Druadach peaks, taken over by a solitary mage. Travellers who take shelter there are not seen again, and the spiders have grown very large.
place_lore.nirncraft.harmugstahl.rumour: Some wizard's holed up in Harmugstahl breeding spiders. Big as a cart. I'm not saying the man is mad. I'm saying I'm not going to check.
place_lore.nirncraft.harmugstahl.shepher:
Teit of Karthwasten, if anyone asks. The mage said he would pay for sheep and pay well. I brought him six. He paid in gold, then asked if I would like to see what the sheep were for.
I am writing this in the room he locked me in. I can hear them moving in the walls. If you find this, the mage is called Vane. He wears a College ring on a hand with two fingers missing. Stop him. Please tell my wife at Karthwasten I did not run off. Tell her I was a fool, but I did not run off.

place_lore.nirncraft.hatching_pools.hook: A ring of warm pools in Stormhold's lowland, each steaming faintly with a clutch in a nest of reeds.
place_lore.nirncraft.hatching_pools.rumo: The hatching pools are cooler. The steam goes south in a thread, and the keepers follow it with their eyes.
Pool one: 88 degrees, was 90. Pool two: 87, was 89. Steam goes south. I followed it to the wall of Lilmoth and lost it among the market stalls. I do not think the market is the thief. I think the thief is further. The steam is a thread, and a thread may be followed.
place_lore.nirncraft.hatchlings_crown.ho: A hill crowned with a ring of egg-shaped stones near Lilmoth, each carved with a notch-count of warmth.
place_lore.nirncraft.hatchlings_crown.ru: The egg-stones of the crown measure the warmth of the pools. The last cut is the deepest anyone has seen.
place_lore.nirncraft.hatchlings_crown.we: Count at dawn: 92 degrees. Last year: 94. The year before: 96. The eggs hatch pale now, and some do not hatch. A degree each year for ten years. I have asked the Hist-sages. They say the heat has been called elsewhere, and nobody called it. I have a strong suspicion. I will not say it aloud.

place_lore.nirncraft.hawia_egg_mine.pump:
#Pump tally
Twelve cisterns drawn in the dry month, sold to the plantation. Three more drawn in the wet. The Clerk says it is for the tithe. The tithe does not need a saw-cut in the wall under the canton, or a brass wheel unbolted from the gate.

I am leaving this book in the mine. Whoever finds it, please tell the Warden.
place_lore.nirncraft.hawia_egg_mine.rumo: The Hawia egg mine floods in a way no mine should: from below. The foremen say the sea is pushing; the canton wardens say the sea has had help.

place_lore.nirncraft.headwaters_of_harst: A clearing where hot springs bubble up through the snow and feed the river Harstrad. Hunters come to warm their bones; so do the beasts that hunt the hunters.

Two sets of initials cut deep into the bark, H and S, inside a heart that someone has tried to make look like a horker. Below, newer: S came here every Midyear for ten years. This Midyear H came alone. She sat in the warm water and sang his song, and a bear sat on the far bank and listened, and neither bothered the other. Some things the All-Maker allows.

Lower still, in a child's careful letters: My grandmother is S. She says H. still comes to the water in her dreams, and that the bear is still listening. She says if I ever marry, I must bring my husband here first and make him sing. I do not think I will marry. The water is too warm to leave.
The Headwaters are the only warm place north of Thirsk. Lovely for a soak. Keep your spear near the bank, though: the bears think so too.
place_lore.nirncraft.heartwood_mill.hook: A sawmill on the western reaches of Lake Honrich, cutting the Rift's golden birch into planks for Riften's docks and the Black-Briar meadery. The road past it belongs to the Ashwood Knives now.
place_lore.nirncraft.heartwood_mill.mill:
Heartwood Mill is to supply forty planks of seasoned birch and twelve oak staves for new fermenting vats, delivered to the Black-Briar Meadery no later than the 30th of Frostfall.

Price as agreed: one hundred and sixty septims. Less sixty for the late delivery in Hearthfire. Less twenty for the warped stave. Less ten for my patience.
Written in the margin by the mill's owner: Seventy septims for forty planks. I'd sooner feed them to the lake. But you don't say no to a Black-Briar, not if you want the mill standing in spring.
place_lore.nirncraft.heartwood_mill.robb:
Leif, age twelve, says: five of them, birch leaves painted on their faces in ash. The big one had a knife with a bone handle and laughed the whole time. They took the planks, the mule and Leif's boots.

They went off east, up the old track toward Faldar's Tooth. Leif followed a little way, barefoot, because he wanted his boots back. He says the big one is called Ottar and the others are afraid of him.
place_lore.nirncraft.heartwood_mill.rumo: Heartwood Mill's had its wagons robbed twice this month. Third time, the mill hands say, they'll go up to Faldar's Tooth with saws and settle it themselves.

place_lore.nirncraft.helas_folly.cache_s: Plate is ashore. From the bow, walk the line of the bowsprit toward the land. Count thirty paces past the last ice ridge. Where the rocks make a crooked doorway, dig on the sheltered side. I wrapped it in the spare mainsail and weighted it with the ship's bell, so you will hear it if your spade strikes true.

Sven and Orm have not come back. I think the ice opened under them. Whoever finds this: the plate was meant for a man in Winterhold who never paid a fair price in his life. Spend it better than he would have.
Tell my mother I was right about the route. Just wrong about the weather.
place_lore.nirncraft.helas_folly.hela_lo:
#Evening Star, 4E 199
Everyone said a ship cannot run north of Dawnstar in winter. Everyone has always been wrong about me. Cargo: Cyrodilic brandy, forty casks, and a strongbox of silver plate for a buyer in Winterhold. We will be a month ahead of every trader in the north.

#Three days later
Ice. On both sides now. The men have stopped laughing at the name I gave her.

#Later still
We are frozen fast. I have sent Sven and Orm across the ice for help from Winterhold. They will be back in two days. Three at most.

#No date
I have hidden the plate ashore where the ice cannot take it. If you read this and I am dead, it is yours. I only ask that you drink one cask of the brandy in my name.
place_lore.nirncraft.helas_folly.hook: A trading ship frozen into the pack ice off the Winterhold coast, her name carved proudly on the stern and her hold still half full of something her crew died for.
place_lore.nirncraft.helas_folly.rumour: Hela's Folly was a merchant's dream: north through the ice to beat the spring traders. The ice won. The merchant's still aboard, they say.
place_lore.nirncraft.helas_folly.sk4_not: Folio #5 (496, -2094): Field inspection recorded for Helas Folly within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.helgen.hook: What remains of Helgen, the walled town on the Pale Pass road that burned in a single afternoon when a black dragon fell on it. Looters and scavengers pick at the bones now.
place_lore.nirncraft.helgen.looters_list:
Worth taking:
Keep armoury - melted, mostly. Some arrowheads good.
Inn cellar - three barrels, one not smashed. MEAD.
Smithy by the north gate - anvil too heavy, but the strongbox under the floor is still there, I heard it rattle. Need a bar to lift the stones.

Not worth it:
The tower. Roof came down. Smell is bad.
Anything near the chopping block.

Karl says we bring the take to South Skybound Watch and sit tight till the Legion stops sending patrols. If you're reading this and you're not Karl, keep your hands off our pile.
place_lore.nirncraft.helgen.rumour: Ylva over in Riverwood walked out of Helgen with nothing but the dress she was wearing. Her father didn't walk out at all. She still asks every traveller about his house.
place_lore.nirncraft.helgen.sk4_note_1.p: Folio #2 (-24, 1143): Field inspection recorded for Helgen within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.helgen.unsent_lette:
#16th of Last Seed
Ylva,
The Legion has the whole town on edge. They say they caught Ulfric himself on the road and mean to try him here tomorrow, though nobody expects a trial. Stay in Riverwood with your aunt until it is done. I don't want you on the road while soldiers are this nervous.

I put your mother's ring and the money for your wedding in the box under the forge floor, the same place as always. If anything should happen, you know where it is. Nothing will happen. I am only an old man who writes too many letters. Your loving father.
place_lore.nirncraft.helgen_border_outpo: A charred timber barricade and watch-post outside the ruined gates of Helgen where patrols monitor looters and road traffic.
The sentries at Helgen Border Outpost still dig melted arrowheads out of the ditch whenever they mend the ditch-stakes.

Folio #53 (-1600, 1560): Field inspection recorded for Helgen Border Outpost within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #53 for helgen_border_outpost: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Helgen Border Outpost are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Addendum #83 for helgen_border_outpost: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Helgen Border Outpost are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

The smoke inside Helgen's keep has finally died down to cold ash, but scavengers from the southern hills slip over the broken wall every night. We have staked the main road approach and posted two bowmen to watch the mountain trail toward Pale Pass.
place_lore.nirncraft.heljarchen.hook: A homestead plot on the high plateau of the Pale, with a view across the snowfields to the giant camps. Whoever builds here will need thick walls and a thicker skin.
place_lore.nirncraft.heljarchen.rumour: The Jarl of Dawnstar is selling the land at Heljarchen to anyone with gold and a death wish. Lovely view, mind you. Mostly of giants.
place_lore.nirncraft.heljarchen.sk4_note: Folio #6 (184, -730): Field inspection recorded for Heljarchen within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.
