place_lore.nirncraft.heljarchen.surveyor:
To the Steward of Dawnstar.
I have walked the bounds of the Heljarchen plot as instructed. Ground: firm under the snow, good for footings. Water: a spring a short way north, frozen three months of the year. Timber: none nearby; it must be hauled. Stone: plenty, most of it in the way.

Neighbours: giants at Blizzard Rest, a short stroll east. They watched me work for an afternoon and did not interfere, though one of the mammoths ate my measuring cord.
Recommendation: sell it to someone tough, and charge them extra for the view.
Ormar
place_lore.nirncraft.helstrom.black_pool:
^Here we sank the chains
In the year the mountain burned we went north. We went to the houses where our grandparents were kept. We did not take gold. We took the chains, every one we could find, and we brought them home, and we gave them to the water.

The water turned black and has stayed black. The elders say it is the chains rusting. The young say it is the water refusing to forget. Both are true. Any Saxhleel may come here and drop a stone for an ancestor who wore iron. The pool is very full of stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.helstrom.border_rep: Walks-Ahead, Warden of the Northern Paths

Written down by the Lukiul scribe from the knots, as spoken:
Seven nights past, the paths by the noisy stones north of town. Footprints of Dunmer boots, heavy, as if carrying. Two of our hunters, Neeta-Lei and Old Breathes-Slow, did not come home from the egg-pools.

At the Molag Bal stones, a fire. Voices in Dunmeri. A chain, new iron, on the ground. Walks-Ahead says: this is not raiding. Raiders take and run. This is someone who means to stay. The Warden asks the Shadowscales for help. The Shadowscales say they are busy. The Warden asks anyone with a spear.
#Who lifts what
Rebuilder Pa-Dar wants to know why the ninth stair stops at the sky. Mason Noo measures twice and still apologises to the stone. Elder Teeba remembers where the stairs led and has told no one. Kessa Rope-Walker sells rope, pitch and plumb, and will not discuss the bridge.

#Beds and a stair
The Broken Ring's roof is new and its walls are old. The rope-walks sway; the long one has won a week's pay for a nameless stranger. The ninth stair needs a black wedge from a jar marked with a spiral. It is in the mason's old yard.
place_lore.nirncraft.helstrom.hook: A Saxhleel border town on the edge of the Shadowfen, closest of all Argonian towns to Morrowind, where the old chains of the slave years lie at the bottom of a black pool and the warriors never quite put down their spears.
place_lore.nirncraft.helstrom.rumour: Helstrom's touchy about Dunmer. Fair enough, really. If you've got grey skin, smile a lot and don't talk about Necrom. And stay off the paths to the shrines north of town.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_gate_ruins.cul:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
Through this gate the faithful climbed to bow before the winged lords. The priest who keeps the gate does not sleep, does not eat, and does not forget a single name.

Bring him your names, pilgrim, and he will keep them. Bring him your breath, and he will keep that too.
^A later scratch, in Tamrielic: WE SHOULD HAVE LISTENED

^Pencilled beside the copy, in Surveyor Calvo's hand
The translator at the College assures me this is merely ceremonial language and the gate-priest a figure of speech. I note, however, that the translator declined my invitation to accompany us.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_gate_ruins.hoo: A Nordic ruin crowning a hill above the marshes of the western Pale, where an old dragon cult kept its high gate. Imperial surveyors went in last Hearthfire to map it.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_gate_ruins.rum: The Legion sent mapmakers into High Gate Ruins. The mapmakers sent back one letter. After that, nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_gate_ruins.sur:
#7th of Hearthfire
Arrived at High Gate with two chainmen and a mule. The entrance faces east, toward the old Pale Imperial Camp. Excellent condition. The stonework is finer than anything in Bruma.

#8th of Hearthfire
The lower halls are full of burial niches, and the niches are full. Marcus insists one of the dead turned its head as we passed. I have told Marcus that the dead do not turn their heads and that he is to keep holding the chain.

#9th of Hearthfire
Marcus and the mule are gone. The chain is still here, cut. I have the survey satchel and the map is three-quarters finished. The Society will want it. I am going deeper to finish the last chamber. A geographer does not leave a map incomplete.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_hrothgar.hook: The mountain monastery of the Greybeards, perched halfway up the Throat of the World above seven thousand steps. Those who climb it come looking for silence, or for the Voice.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_hrothgar.pilgr:
~Kyne, I have climbed your seven thousand steps,
~My knees are broken and my breath is gone.
~I came to ask the Greybeards for a word,
~And found I had no question left to ask.

I meant to ask why my son died in the war. I meant to ask which side was right. At the top there was only the wind, and the door, and the quiet, and somewhere above that, the mountain thinking. I left this prayer on the steps and walked back down. I think that was the answer.
place_lore.nirncraft.high_hrothgar.rumou: The Greybeards haven't said a word aloud in years, so they say, because their voices would shake the mountain down. Klimmek from Ivarstead hauls their supplies up. Nobody else bothers.

place_lore.nirncraft.high_hrothgar.suppl:
^FOR THE GREYBEARDS
Salted fish: 2 crates
Barley: 1 sack
Candles: 40
Lamp oil: 1 jug
Wool blankets: 3 (Master Arngeir asked, through Brother Borri's gestures. I think it was blankets. It might have been goats.)

Paid in full, as always, with a nod. Note to self: the steps are icier this year past the fourth shrine. Bring the spiked boots. Do not stop to look down. Do not stop to look at the frost trolls either. Especially do not stop to look at the frost trolls.

place_lore.nirncraft.highpoint_tower.arv:
#Night of the 3rd, Rain's Hand
Red Mountain glows tonight, faintly. My instruments say the fire under it is not dead, only sleeping, the way a wounded man sleeps. I have recorded the glow on fourteen nights this season. Neloth says I am wasting my talents. Neloth says that about every talent he does not have.

#Night of the 9th
Bound a guardian of fire and ash to the tower. It will keep my instruments and my grimoire safe while I sail to Sadrith Mora to present my findings. It understands only one instruction: let no one up the stair who is not me.
Final entry, scrawled in haste: Recalled to Vvardenfell by my house. I will return in a month. The grimoire stays in the top chamber. The guardian stays with it.
place_lore.nirncraft.highpoint_tower.gua: Sergeant, as asked, I looked at Highpoint Tower. The door is open. The stairs go up. Something burning walks round and round the top chamber and does not stop. The Telvanni who built it left eleven years ago, according to the Company records, and did not come back. The thing upstairs is still waiting for him. I did not go up. I would like that noted as wisdom, not cowardice.
Postscript: There is a lamp lit in the top window every night at the hour the wizard used to look at the mountain. Nobody climbs up to light it. I would also like that noted.
place_lore.nirncraft.highpoint_tower.hoo: A slender Telvanni tower on a crag north of Fort Frostmoth, grown and then abandoned by a wizard who wanted to watch Red Mountain. Something he summoned to guard it is still on watch.
place_lore.nirncraft.highpoint_tower.rum: Highpoint Tower was some Telvanni's observatory. He left, and his guardian didn't. The Redoran Guard won't go up there. They say the stairs move.

place_lore.nirncraft.hill_of_shattered_s:
^HERE ARE THE SWORDS OF THREE ARMIES.
^NONE OF THEM WON.
^LET THE WIND SING FOR THE ONES WHO COULD NOT.

A drover's scrawl beneath: 'I took a blade once, a small one, for luck. It hummed all the way home and would not stop. I carried it back at night and planted it in the same row. It sang once, short, like a cat settling.'
A hill planted, row on row, with thousands of broken sword-blades, left where armies fell. When the dry wind crosses it, the blades hum a single long note.
You cannot take a blade from the hill. Not because anyone will stop you, but because the blades have a way of finding your hands again at dawn, wherever you left them.
place_lore.nirncraft.hillgrunds_tomb.des:
Cousin Torvar,
You went into the tomb to lay Grandfather's urn with the rest of the line, and you never came back. Our family has done this for twenty generations. Not once has the old chief stirred. Now the guards at Valtheim say they hear iron dragging inside the hill at night.

Grandmother says the old chief's horn was taken from his bier by a grave-robber last summer, and that he will not rest until it is returned. I do not believe in such things. I also do not go near the hill anymore.
If you are alive, come home. If you are not, I hope someone sets the horn back where it belongs.
place_lore.nirncraft.hillgrunds_tomb.hoo: The barrow of Hillgrund, a chieftain of the Merethic Era, at the southern edge of the Pale above the Valtheim road. His descendants still come here, and lately they have stopped coming back.
place_lore.nirncraft.hillgrunds_tomb.rob: Took a drinking horn off the old chief's slab. Silver rim, carved with ravens. Worth a hundred to the right buyer at Darkshade. Got as far as the door and the whole tomb woke up behind me.

Hid the horn in the side passage and holed up here. They keep walking past. The big one keeps stopping at the passage and smelling the air. If I put it back, maybe they'll let me go. If I put it back, I'm poor again.
place_lore.nirncraft.hillgrunds_tomb.rum: Hillgrund's Tomb. The old chief's family still buries their dead there. Old Hillgrund doesn't seem to like the company.

place_lore.nirncraft.hist_stride_camp.ch:
#Rules
No scaring the guar. No riding the guar. No telling the grown-ups where the guar is. If the guar likes you, it will eat your dates. If the guar does not like you, it will still eat your dates.
place_lore.nirncraft.hist_stride_camp.ho: A ragged tent-camp of Gideon's edge, where children feed dates to whatever wanders in, whether or not it has a rider.
place_lore.nirncraft.hist_stride_camp.ru: A guar wandered into the Hist-Stride camp last week and was fed dates by three delighted children. It has been looking vindicated ever since.
place_lore.nirncraft.hjaalmarch_imperial: A Legion field camp in the Hjaalmarch marsh, guarding the road to Morthal and glaring at the Stormcloaks across the fog. Its soldiers are bored, damp and very far from Cyrodiil.

Hakon,
I'll be there. I'll bring the wine. You'll admit it's better. The centurion has started counting the night patrols, so I'll have to come by the long way round the ruins, past the old stones where the lantern ghost walks. If I'm late, it's the ghost's fault.

There's talk of the camps being moved before Sun's Dusk. If they move us, look for me in Solitude, at the Winking Skeever, every Sundas until one of us is dead or the war is over. I'm not aiming at all, Hakon. Not at you. Not at anybody I've shared bread with.
The Legion camp south of Ustengrav buys everything Morthal will sell them. Mostly dry socks. You can't get a pair in town for under three septims since they arrived.

Requested from Solitude: Socks, wool, 60 pairs. Oiled cloaks, 30. Boots, any, the marsh has eaten ours. Lamp oil, 10 jars; the fog swallows torches. Mudcrab nets, 4, to supplement rations, the men having developed a taste.

Also requested: a priest of Stendarr or of Arkay, for the barrow next door is restless and the men say they hear knocking under the tents at night. Also requested: relief. We have been here since Rain's Hand. Also requested: someone to tell Legionary Calvus to stop volunteering for the night watch, because I am beginning to suspect why.
place_lore.nirncraft.hjaalmarch_stormclo: A Stormcloak camp on the eastern edge of the Hjaalmarch marsh, facing the Legion across the fog and the barrow of Ustengrav. The soldiers are cold, wet and spoiling for a fight they are not allowed to start.

Livia,
Kjenstag again, the night after the next new moon. Same broken pillar. I'll bring the bread, you bring the Imperial wine you swear is better than mead and isn't.

My sergeant asked me why I volunteer for every night watch on the west side. I told him I like the fog. He told me to stop lying. I told him I like the fog because it hides things. He said that wasn't better.
If it comes to a fight between the camps, I will aim high. Promise me you'll aim high too. When this is over, we'll argue about Talos over supper, like civilised people.
The rebels and the Legion have camped across the marsh from each other since Rain's Hand. Not a sword drawn yet. My cousin says they trade insults by moonlight, and mead by daylight.
Two men on the barrow road at all times. Two men watching the Imperial camp. One man watching the two men watching the Imperial camp, because Hakon is one of them and Hakon wanders.

No one goes into Ustengrav. If the Legion goes in, we go in after them. If the grave robbers come out with anything that looks like it belongs to Jurgen Windcaller, it is taken from them and sent to Windhelm with an escort of six. The Jarl of Eastmarch reveres the Windcaller. So should you.
place_lore.nirncraft.hla_oad.hook: A tidal fishing village of smoke-racks where the tide leaves mudflats scattered with brass glints.
place_lore.nirncraft.hla_oad.rumour: The Hla Oad mudflats give up brass at every ebb. A trader pays triple if it has a little thumb-print.
place_lore.nirncraft.hla_oad.web.author: Collector's agent
place_lore.nirncraft.hla_oad.web.p0: Paid: 3 coin per thumbed cog, 1 coin per plain. Total this month: 214 thumbs. Deliver to the master at Balmora via Gnaar Mok. Do not clean them. The print is the point. No questions of the sea-folk; they have found more than we can carry.
place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_council_mano: The terraced manor of the Hlaalu council, all balconies and beeswax, where every ledger is a favour in a better coat.
A steward at the Manor leaves a ledger unwatched in his study each Fredas, they say, and it is never the same ledger twice. Somebody wants it taken. Somebody else wants it found taken.

#To whom it may concern
The study is to be left unlocked after the sixth bell on Fredas. The ledger on the desk is the dull one. The ledger under it is the one that matters, and is not to be touched, discussed, or noticed by anyone who wishes to remain on the staff.

If the dull ledger goes missing, report it at once to the Factor. If the second goes missing, report it to nobody.
place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_farm.argonia: Ten years on the Windhelm docks. Ten years of Shatter-Shield coin counted twice and paid once. Here the Dunmer counts once and pays once. The Nords in the bunkhouse do not like me, but they eat at the same table and nobody spits in the stew. This is what warm feels like, in Skyrim.
If the men from the Candlehearth come with torches, I will be at the gate. The hist did not bring me this far to watch a good roof burn.
place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_farm.hook: A Dunmer-owned farm beside Hollyfrost, worked by Nord and Argonian hands for equal pay, which in Windhelm's shadow makes it either a scandal or a miracle depending on who is talking.
place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_farm.rumour: The Dunmer at Hlaalu Farm pays his lizards the same as his Nords. Some say he'll be burned out by spring. Some say they'd like to see who tries.
place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_farm.sk4_not: Folio #7 (2011, -655): Field inspection recorded for Hlaalu Farm within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.hlaalu_farm.wages_l:
#Sun's Dusk, week the first
Works-the-Furrow: 6 days, 18 septims.
Olaf Stone-Knee: 6 days, 18 septims.
Teeba-Dar: 5 days (fever), 18 septims all the same, because a fever is not a choice.
Gunnhild: 6 days, 18 septims, and a jar of saltrice for her mother.

A man from the Candlehearth Hall came to tell me that I was making the Nords of this farm look cheap by paying them as much as Argonians. I told him I was making the Argonians look expensive. He did not laugh.
Memo: buy a dog. A big one. And more oil for the lamp by the gate.

place_lore.nirncraft.hobs_fall_cave.expu:
To Vinicia Sallus, formerly Apprentice.
You are hereby expelled from the College of Winterhold for the following: the unauthorised removal of a cadaver from the Winterhold cemetery; the unauthorised animation of the same in the Hall of Countenance; and the theft of the restricted volume 'Concordance of the Unquiet' from the Arcanaeum.

The Arcanaeum's keeper wishes it known that the volume is irreplaceable and that he will see it returned, even if he has to fetch it from Oblivion himself. You have until the end of Frostfall to return it before the matter is passed to the Jarl.
The College regrets nothing but the waste.
place_lore.nirncraft.hobs_fall_cave.hook: A sea cave on the Winterhold coast where a disgraced College mage has set up house among the drowned. Bodies wash in on the tide, and not all of them stay dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.hobs_fall_cave.rumo: Hob's Fall. The tide brings bodies in there from the wrecks. Something in the cave gets them up and walking again.
place_lore.nirncraft.hobs_fall_cave.sk4_: Folio #11 (773, -1640): Field inspection recorded for Hobs Fall Cave within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.hobs_fall_cave.vini: Specimens this week: two drowned sailors from Pilgrim's Trench, one Legionary from the camp to the west who wandered too close to the cliff, and one very old Nord who was already half-preserved by the ice.

The Concordance is everything I hoped. The old masters understood that the cold does half the work. Salt, frost and patience: a body kept in the sea caves rises clean.
Sold three jars of grave salts to the lunatic at Yngvild. He wants more. Everybody always wants more, and the College calls ME a disgrace.

place_lore.nirncraft.hollyfrost_farm.hoo: A hardscrabble farm on the frozen fields east of Windhelm, where a widow keeps the hearth lit for a son who marched off with the Stormcloaks and has stopped writing.
place_lore.nirncraft.hollyfrost_farm.ing:
Bjorlam,
The snow has come early and the goat has stopped giving milk, which you will say is my fault for naming her after your aunt. I have sold the second plough. Do not be angry. I could not pull it alone and it was only sitting there reminding me.
The quartermaster's men came asking after you on the 3rd. They would not say why. They were polite in the way men are polite when they mean to be something else later.

Whatever you have done, you are mine. There is a bed here, and nobody in the world will look for you under your mother's roof but your mother.
^Ingrid
place_lore.nirncraft.hollyfrost_farm.rum: Ingrid at Hollyfrost asks every soldier who passes whether they've seen her Bjorlam. Most of them look away. I think they've heard something.

place_lore.nirncraft.honeystrand_cave.be:
Put the money from the Goldenglow wax by the old stump. Not the one by the cave mouth, the bears dig there. The one about thirty paces past the cave on the east side, with the bee-strand hanging over it, under the flat stone.

Remember: thirty paces east. Not thirty paces north, Rolf. Last time you dug for a whole morning in the wrong place and a bear watched you do it.
place_lore.nirncraft.honeystrand_cave.ho: A den of bears south of Ivarstead, named for the wild bee-strands that hang in the trees above it. The bears have learned that beekeepers taste better than honey.
place_lore.nirncraft.honeystrand_cave.ru: There's wild honey all round Honeystrand. There's also more bears than honey. My cousin went up for the comb and came back with half an ear.

place_lore.nirncraft.honningbrew_meadery:
#Last Seed, 4E 201
2nd: 12 casks to the Bannered Mare. Delivered.
6th: 8 casks to Riverwood. Delivered.
9th: 10 casks to Rorikstead. Cart found empty near the river ford. Driver beaten, says the men wore wolf pelts and came from the east.

14th: 6 casks to Whiterun. Taken at the same ford.
18th: 6 casks, with two guards. Guards drunk on our own mead when found. Casks gone.

The trail goes east along the river every time, toward that cave they call White River Watch. Sabjorn says hire swords. With what coin? They are drinking our coin.
A busy meadery south-east of Whiterun, its honey barrels rolling out by the cartload. Lately the carts have been coming back lighter than they left.
Honningbrew's the best mead this side of Riften, and don't let a Black-Briar tell you otherwise. Trouble is, half of it gets stolen before it reaches the city. Eirik at the meadery is fit to be tied.

Folio #10 (176, 163): Field inspection recorded for Honningbrew Meadery within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #10 for honningbrew_meadery: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Honningbrew Meadery are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

~Honey from the hive and water from the hill,
~Drink it slow, my friend, or drink it till you're ill.
~Bees work all the summer so a Nord can sing,
~One horn for the Jarl and two for everything.

~Black-Briar's for Riften, where the rain comes down,
~Honningbrew's for Whiterun, best mead in the town.

Underneath, in a different hand: 'Whoever wrote this owes me a cask. You know who you are, Mallus.'

A third hand, smaller, beneath that: 'Mallus says he never wrote any verse in his life, and that he certainly owes nobody a cask. Sabjorn says to stop writing on the barrels. Sabjorn wrote that on a barrel.'
place_lore.nirncraft.honrich_stone_circl: A ring of lichen-crusted standing stones on a low bluff overlooking the autumn reflections of Lake Honrich.
Old fishers on Lake Honrich say the stones in the circle cast seven shadows at sunset even though only five pillars are still standing.

Folio #61 (880, 1640): Field inspection recorded for Honrich Stone Circle within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #61 for honrich_stone_circle: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Honrich Stone Circle are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
The five upright monoliths align with the winter solstice sunrise over the Velothi peaks, while the two fallen lintels bear faint star-charts in the style of the early Atmoran sky-watchers.

place_lore.nirncraft.horker_island.hook: A rocky islet east of Gyldenhul Barrow where horkers haul out by the hundred. The Skaal hunt here with thanks; a salvager buried a purse here with none.
place_lore.nirncraft.horker_island.rumou: Horker Island stinks worse than a Windhelm tannery. There's a bull horker there the size of a longboat that the Skaal won't hunt. They say he's lucky.
place_lore.nirncraft.horker_island.skaal: Cut in Skaal runes on a stone above the tide line: Take one in ten. Take none with calves. Do not take the old bull, who has fathered half the island and is the All-Maker's own joke. Return the bones to the water before you sail. Leave no fire burning. Leave no blood unwashed. The horkers remember, and so do we.

Scratched underneath, in Cyrodilic, by a less respectful visitor: The old bull bit my boat. I have never in my life been so insulted by an animal. He is still there, by the flat stone in the middle of the island. Do not take him. He is not worth it. He is entirely made of spite.
place_lore.nirncraft.hot_spring_bathers_: A timber bath-shelter steamed by the mineral pools of the volcanic tundra, where hunters and miners soak frostbitten joints between shifts.
Trappers down at the hot springs say a pair of poachers moved into the bath-shelter and started charging silver just to dip your boots in the warm water.

Steam rises off the sulfur ledges day and night, keeping the frost back twenty paces from the timber planks. Three miners from Kynesgrove paid two silver apiece to soak their shoulders after a week on the malachite face. I told them to leave their pickaxes by the rack and keep out of the deep boiling vent to the east.

place_lore.nirncraft.hrodulfs_house.drea:
#First night
Woke at the door with my hand on the latch. Cold floor, no memory. Wrote it down so I would not think I dreamed it.
#Fourth night
Woke on the path toward Raven Rock with mud to the knee. There was a voice in my sleep, patient and kind. It said I was building something important.

#Ninth night
I tied my ankle to the bedpost with a rope. Woke with the rope cut cleanly and a sharp stone in my hand. I do not own a knife that sharp.
#Last entry
The voice says I am nearly finished. It says the work is beautiful. I believe it. I do not want to believe it. Whoever reads this: do not sleep in this house.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrodulfs_house.hook: A Nord's lonely cottage on the southern coast, between Fort Frostmoth and the sea. Its owner left in the middle of the night, barefoot, and walked north toward the stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrodulfs_house.rumo: Hrodulf's House has stood empty since Hrodulf walked off in his sleep. The door was found wide open, the fire still lit, and his boots by the bed. Nobody's touched it since.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrothmunds_barrow.c:
~The first was taken, the first was wronged,
~The first will wake and take what is his.
~We dig in his name and sleep in his dream,
~We open the doors the traitors sealed.

Beneath, in plain prose: Hrothmund betrayed the Master in the old days and was buried with the key to a door the Master once used. Brother Ulfgar will find the key. The sleepers from Raven Rock will carry the stones. When the key is found, the Master will remember who opened the door, and the ones who did not will build his halls forever.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrothmunds_barrow.h: An ancient tomb in the snowy uplands, where masked strangers have been seen carrying lanterns down the steps. The Skaal say Hrothmund was a traitor once. Someone is praying to traitors again.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrothmunds_barrow.r: Masked folk going in and out of Hrothmund's Barrow. Not draugr. People. They wear the same masks as those cultists who attacked travellers at the docks. Nobody's been brave enough to ask what they want.
place_lore.nirncraft.hrothmunds_barrow.s: Hrothmund served the dragon-masked priests in the old days, when the island was theirs. When the people rose against the priests he took a torch and burned the doors of his own master's house. Some called him a hero. The priests called him a thief. He was buried here under a stone with no name, and with him a key no one could explain. The Skaal do not go here. Not because he was a traitor, but because a man who betrays once is buried uneasily.
place_lore.nirncraft.hubalajad_palace.ho: A walled lord's estate in the Hews Bane hills, with a long colonnade and a conservatory of potted palms.
place_lore.nirncraft.hubalajad_palace.ru: At Hubalajad the lord has been dead twenty years and still orders palms by the barrow-load.
place_lore.nirncraft.hubalajad_palace.we: Planted this season: 31. Rooted: 28. Blooming: 4. The lord's line is long; the garden is long; the list is long. I do not ask what blooms. I record the water. The bloom is said to cure the sand-fever, but only in blood of the line. I am no physician.
place_lore.nirncraft.hundings_dojo.dojo_:
^THE FIRST RULE: YOU MAY WALK AWAY.
^THE SECOND RULE: YOU NEVER WILL.
^THE THIRD RULE IS FOR THE STUDENT TO INVENT.

A student has added in the sand with a stick, which has been raked over and rewritten countless times: 'The third rule is not a rule. It is a question. I have been asking it for nine years. I think the answer is a sword. I think the answer is not.'
place_lore.nirncraft.hundings_dojo.hook: A sunken courtyard dojo on a Yokudan island, a bowl of white sand ringed with columns, tiers of benches and a single bright pavilion where the Way of the Sword is still, quietly, taught.
place_lore.nirncraft.hundings_dojo.rumou: No one in Hunding's Dojo has ever been seen to eat. They are said to live on discipline and hot tea. The tea, at least, has been confirmed.

Archers use the Hunter's Cliff Blind to spot elk moving through the mist, though lately poachers have been using it to watch the coaching road instead.

Two hundred paces to the split birch by the game-lick; three hundred to the ford below the ridge. Allow two fingers left when the morning draft pulls up from Lake Ilinalta. Left a tin of bow-wax and six bodkin shafts under the dry slate.
place_lore.nirncraft.hunters_rest.asvald:
#Sundas
Hroa wounded a great stag by the stream and it ran north into Moss Mother Cavern. She went after it. I told her to wait for me to finish skinning the doe. She never waits.
#Morndas
Not back. Fire kept.
#Tirdas
Not back. Went to the mouth. Heard her name said back to me by something in the dark. Not my voice.

#Turdas
If anyone finds this, I have gone in after her. She carries Mother's ash bow, pale wood with a raven cut on the grip. If you find the bow and not me, bring it back here and lay it on the hearth. That way we are both home, in a manner of speaking.
place_lore.nirncraft.hunters_rest.guest_:
Burn what you need. Cut twice what you burn.
Leave one cut of meat in the cold box for the next one.
No Legion business, no Stormcloak business, no talk of either.
If the spriggans come close, go inside and bar the door, and do not answer them, even if they use a voice you know.
Asvald and Hroa keep this place. Be decent or be gone.

Added beneath in a younger hand: 'And if you take the last mead, replace it, Asvald. Yes, you. I know it was you.' And below that, in an older one: 'Hroa drank it. I have witnesses. The witnesses are the empty bottles, and they are under her bed.'
place_lore.nirncraft.hunters_rest.hook: A hunters' cabin in the western pines, shared by whoever needs a roof for the night. Its hearth has gone cold for the first time in years.
place_lore.nirncraft.hunters_rest.rumour: Asvald and his sister kept the fire at Hunter's Rest burning for any hunter who passed. Asvald's gone looking for her. Now nobody keeps it.

A woodland clearing and skinning-shed under the tall pines where foresters cure venison and trade fletching feathers.
Stop by Hunter's Rest Stead if you need dry bowstrings, but don't ask them to guide you near the coven caves after moonrise.

Sixteen winter red-deer hides scraped and salted on the frames, plus four bundles of goose-quill fletching traded to the road-wardens. A hunter came limping in from the western glen with briar-scratches across his forearms, swearing the witches up by Glenmoril have hung bone fetishes across the old game trail.
place_lore.nirncraft.hutan_tzel.hook: A fishing hamlet on the southern delta, with drying racks and a graveyard whose markers are wooden reeds.
place_lore.nirncraft.hutan_tzel.rumour: At Hutan Tzel the dead are buried inland, now. The singers don't sing them to the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.hutan_tzel.web.p0: To the Grave-Singers: my father was not sung to the water. He lies in a field that is not ours, in a place that will be dry within a year. Please. The dirge is the only road he has and it has been closed. Someone has money in the Gideon fields and my father has been sold for rain.
place_lore.nirncraft.hvitkald_peak.hook: A white peak north of Raven Rock, standing over the Abandoned Lodge. Ash and snow streak its flanks in grey bands, and from its top the whole southern coast lies open.
place_lore.nirncraft.hvitkald_peak.looko: To Sergeant Indaram. Lookout on Hvitkald, third day. Smoke from the Abandoned Lodge chimney last night, though the lodge has stood empty since Frostfall. No smoke this morning. Wolf howls from the direction of Frostmoon Crag, many, at moonrise. Torchlight moving on the barrow road toward Bloodskal Barrow, four or five lights. Grave robbers, I think, not draugr; draugr do not need torches. Requesting relief. Requesting a warmer cloak. Requesting that the relief bring the cloak.
Postscript: The sergeant should know that Helga from the docks walked past my post again this Loredas, carrying boots up to the lodge. I told her it was empty. She said she knew. She went anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.hvitkald_peak.rumou: Hvitkald Peak. The Nords named it white-cold. Since the Red Year it's been more grey-cold. The view's still good, if you like looking at ash.

Fishers toss a copper coin onto the Drowned Altar before casting nets in the deep channel, just in case the old lake-spirits are listening.

May the Keeper of the Wheel remember those whose bones rest beneath cold water rather than consecrated pine-earth. Though the lake has risen over the lower steps of this altar since the First Era, the carved reliefs still face the Lady Stone across the waves.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_falls.hook: A foaming cataract where cold mountain meltwater plunges over stepped limestone ledges into the southern arm of Lake Ilinalta.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_falls.rumo: Salmon leap by the hundreds at Ilinalta Falls in the spring thaw, drawing both bears and poachers to the spray-soaked rocks.

place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_falls.ward: The deep eddy behind the second cascade holds the largest lake-trout in the hold, provided you can keep your footing on the wet slate. Watch the timber boom downstream toward Half-Moon Mill; a slipped log will carry a boat straight over the lip.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_fishery.ho: A weathered plank fishery on the southern shore of Lake Ilinalta, hung with eel-traps, hemp nets, and smoke-racks.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_fishery.ru: The net-makers at Ilinalta Fishery won't row out past the reed-beds after dusk; they swear lanterns burn under the water near the drowned fort.

place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_fishery.wa: Three tubs of silver-perch and two dozen smoked lake-eels packed in pine sawdust for the inn at Falkreath. We lost another two gill-nets near the sunken masonry of Ilinalta's Deep; something down on the flooded flagstones sliced the hemp lines clean through as if with an iron knife.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_rebel_bivo: A concealed camp of pine-bough shelters along the wooded ridges above Lake Ilinalta, used by rebel scouts watching the Falkreath roads.
Hunters near the lake shore say you can smell woodsmoke from the rebel bivouac only when the rain drives it down into the ferns.

Two owl-calls from the birch knoll mean the Legion patrol has passed the mill bridge; three mean they are searching the timber carts. Keep the campfires banked with wet moss during daylight and send word to the old Jarl's friends in town.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinalta_ridge_moun: An ancient ringed barrow-mound set among the pines on the ridge dividing Lake Ilinalta from the western valleys.
Lumberjacks cutting above the mill say their axes ring hollow whenever they drop a trunk near the Ilinalta Ridge Mound.

We marked the pines around the stone circle with white chalk so the saw-crews would leave them standing. The roots of the old hemlocks wrap right around the carved curb-stones, and nobody in Falkreath wants to wake what was sealed under that hill.
A moss-draped monument of dark granite standing on a wooded promontory above the cold waters of Lake Ilinalta.
Old fishers steer by the Ilinalta Word Wall on foggy mornings when the pines on the shore all look alike.

Carved into the lakeward face are verses honoring a shield-thane who drowned in winter armor while crossing the ice to relieve the shore-watch. Lichen fills the deep grooves, giving the letters a pale silver sheen at dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinaltas_deep.garr:
#Rain's Hand
The lake is up another hand's breadth. The cellar stores are lost. I have asked Falkreath for pitch and timber twice and received neither.
#Second Seed
The lower gate is under water. The mages in the east wing say the rise is natural. The mages in the east wing are the only ones who seem pleased about it.

#Midyear
Orders from the Jarl: abandon the Deep. The garrison marches to Falkreath tomorrow. The mages have refused to leave. They say the water keeps away the curious and the dead keep away the rest. I did not ask what they meant by the second part. I am glad to be going.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinaltas_deep.hook: A fortress half-swallowed by Lake Ilinalta, its lower halls flooded since the water rose a generation ago. Lights still move in its drowned windows at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinaltas_deep.mage: Subject four retained its shape for nine weeks submerged, against three weeks in open air. Lake water from the Deep is colder than the shallows by a margin that cannot be explained by depth alone. Something under the fort is drinking the warmth out of it.

Our fishing friend from the mill rowed close again last night. I extinguished the lamp before he saw too much. Recommend we stop working at the windows. Recommend we stop bringing subjects in by boat. Recommend, for the third time, that we stop recommending things and simply leave this lake.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinaltas_deep.rumo: Ilinalta's Deep was a mage's fort once, before the lake came up and took it. Fishers say there's someone still working down there. Lamps don't light themselves underwater.
place_lore.nirncraft.ilinaltas_deep.sk4_: Folio #11 (-795, 661): Field inspection recorded for Ilinaltas Deep within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_bridge_inn: An inn half on a stone bridge and half on the bank, with lanterns strung along the span and the river passing beneath its floorboards.
The river under the Bridge Inn drops every year though it rains. The keeper pays a tax nobody can name.

Paid to the Ring: 22 gold, spring. 24, summer. 29, autumn. For the Bridge Inn's water rights, granted in a charter nobody has seen. I asked a clerk in Chorrol. She went white and said 'sluice 14'. I do not know what that means. The cellar wheel turns by itself some nights.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_chapels.ch:
#A confession noted, not recorded
Three guards left their posts at dusk, three days running, to tend a lamp for a fourth. The sin is very small. The punishment would be very large. I shall relight the lamp myself, quietly, at the proper hour. The walls will not notice. Neither will the Legate, if I am discreet.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_chapels.ho: The garrison chapels of Ebonheart, where confessions are short because nobody does anything wrong, and a quiet war is waged with candles.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_chapels.ru: Three guards confessed the same sin this week in three different words: a night off the walls, a gate left open, a lamp left lit. The Chaplain says nothing, which is how you know.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_city.dockh:
Dear Aulus,
Wages on the Waterfront are down again. The Company says the war is over and so the war rate is over. I say the war is not over if you count the Justiciars, but nobody pays me to count.

I put two drakes on the Arena last Fredas. A Nord girl called Svala the Unbending, fighting for the Yellow. She lost in a breath. The fellow beside me laughed and won thirty. He was wearing Blue. So was the referee's cousin.

Mother asks if you will come up from Leyawiin for her name-day. Bring Blackwood honey and do not bring that Argonian you play dice with, the watch here still remembers the last time.
Your brother, Petrus
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_city.hook: The White-Gold Tower still stands over the city that the Elves besieged in the Great War. Justiciars walk the Talos Plaza, the Arena roars, and every district hides a quarrel older than the Concordat.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_city.justi:
#Register of Observances, Talos Plaza District
Morndas, 9th of Last Seed, 4E 201
Addressed to the Office of the First Emissary, Embassy of the Aldmeri Dominion.

Item. The household of the cloth-merchant Varus Albecius continues to keep a lamp lit on Tirdas evenings. The lamp is unremarkable. The schedule is not. Recommend a visit after the next lamp.
Item. A wall in the alley behind the Gilded Carafe bears a carved hand with nine lines. Scraped. Recarved by morning. Assign a watcher.

Item. The Imperial Watch captain of this district responds to our requests with exemplary courtesy and no results. His courtesy is to be commended. His results are to be noted.
The Concordat is not a treaty, Emissary. It is a lesson. We are merely teaching it slowly.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_city.rumou: The city's quiet these days. Quiet the way a room goes quiet when a Justiciar walks in. Keep your amulets under your shirt, friend, and your prayers under your breath.
place_lore.nirncraft.imperial_city_priso: The Imperial City Prison squats below the Waterfront, a place of locks and ledgers where a man may be forgotten in perfectly good order.
They say the Prison has a cell for every sort of crime, and one with no number at all. The warders pass it quickly and do not look at the door.

^WARDER'S TALLY, WATERFRONT BLOCK
^Month of the Sun's Dusk
Cell eleven: one forger, unrepentant. Cell twelve: one forger, penitent. Cell fourteen: empty, though the straw is warm. Cell fifteen: occupied. I did not note by whom. The lock was turned from the inside.

To the next warder: do not take the lamp past cell sixteen. Whoever lives there likes the dark, and has asked, politely, for a little more of it. I have been polite in return. It is not the worst arrangement I have made in twenty years of service.
place_lore.nirncraft.irkngthand.hook: A great Dwemer city in the southern hills of the Pale, its towers half-hidden by snow. Falmer haunt its lower halls, and someone recently walked in through the front door very quietly.
place_lore.nirncraft.irkngthand.hunter_j:
#Frostfall
We made it into the upper halls of Irkngthand. Gold leaf on the walls, brass in every corner. Then the Falmer. We pulled back to the camp outside the gate.

#Two days later
Somebody else is inside. We heard them on the high walkways, three or four, quiet as cats. Not Falmer, they're too quick and they talk. Thieves, if I'm any judge.
We will wait until they come out and see what they carry. Or we will wait until they come out and pretend we never saw them. Depends on how big they are.
place_lore.nirncraft.irkngthand.rumour: Irkngthand. Big Dwemer ruin south of the lift. There's a camp of treasure-hunters near the entrance, and they're nervous about something.
place_lore.nirncraft.irkngthand.vesk_irk: Irkngthand is by some distance the largest Dwemer site in the north, and the worst studied. Its upper halls contain a lens-and-mirror gallery for which I would give my second-best robe and my toe (the other one).

Unhappily the halls also contain Falmer in great numbers, and the College refuses to fund an escort. I am told the Thieves Guild of Riften has an interest in the site. I suggest the College ask the Guild for a map. I am told this suggestion is 'unseemly'.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironback_hideout.fa:
~Ninth of the Nine, and first of men,
~we meet in the hills because the city is afraid.
~We are not afraid. We are only careful.
~Careful is a kind of courage in a winter like this one.

~Bless the hearth that hides your likeness,
~bless the hands that carved it from Ironback ore,
~bless the old man who leads us
~and the young ones who will lead when he cannot.
^Said in the hideout, in a low voice, on the first Sundas.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironback_hideout.ho: A lonely cabin in the hills west of the Thalmor Embassy. The Talos faithful of Haafingar met here in secret until the Justiciars came. Something they treasured is still hidden inside.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironback_hideout.ru: Folks used to go up to the Ironback cabin to 'hunt' on the first Sundas of the month. Never brought back any meat. Then the elves went up there, and now nobody goes at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironback_hideout.wa:
To any of the faithful who come back:
They took Hjorvar. The Justiciars came at dawn, four of them with an embassy agent who knew all our names. Somebody among us talked. I do not know who and I have stopped trying to guess, because guessing is how they win.

The icon is still under the hearthstone. They searched twice and did not find it. Do not try to take it yourselves; the elves watch this cabin and leave men here some nights. If a stranger finds this, a stranger who still remembers the Ninth: lift the stone, take the icon somewhere safe, and pray for an old man in Northwatch.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironbind_barrow.bro: We, Thorkel, Bjorn and Ivar, called the Lucky, swear by our mother's luck-stone that whatever we find in Ironbind Barrow we split three ways. If one falls, his share goes to the other two. If two fall, the last one buys the drinks at Nightgate Inn until the treasure runs out.

Each of us carries a piece of the luck-stone. Put together, the three pieces make a whole, and the whole brings us home. Mother said so. Mother was usually right.
Signed, Thorkel. Signed, Bjorn. Signed (mark), Ivar, who never learned to write.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironbind_barrow.hoo: A Nordic barrow near Nightgate Inn where a warlord was buried bound in iron chains so that he could never rise. Three treasure-hunting brothers went to test the chains.
place_lore.nirncraft.ironbind_barrow.iva: Ivar fell at the chain-door. The big one in the iron mask came off its slab and the chains just fell away from it like they'd been waiting. I got Ivar's piece of the stone. Thorkel ran. I don't blame him.
Arm's broken. Can't climb back. If Thorkel ever comes back for us, the two pieces are on me. Tell him to put them with his own and go home and stop being lucky.

Third piece is with Thorkel. If you're not Thorkel and you're reading this, take the two pieces to him at Nightgate Inn. He'll be at the bar. He's always at the bar.
Bjorn
place_lore.nirncraft.ironbind_barrow.rum: Ironbind Barrow. The Lucky brothers went in with a pick and a song. One came back, and he's stopped singing.
place_lore.nirncraft.isle_of_balfiera.ho: A hill-island with a ring of ruined towers in the bay, half-sunk at high tide.
place_lore.nirncraft.isle_of_balfiera.ru: The Isle of Balfiera is a few inches lower each year, though the tides are the same.
place_lore.nirncraft.isle_of_balfiera.we: The ring of towers is a lock, not a fortification. Each tower guards a drain-sluice to the isle's underside. The island is sinking because the pump drinks from beneath it. If the pump is closed at the cliff-bastion, the isle will rise. I will submit this to the court. They will not read it.
place_lore.nirncraft.isle_of_contemplati: A tiny isle off the Auridon coast with a single meditation platform, reachable only at low tide, where Altmer mystics sit in silence for weeks and are not disturbed.

^SIT AND BE A STONE.
^LET THE TIDE COME AND GO.
^WHEN YOU CANNOT TELL YOURSELF FROM THE SEA, RISE, AND BE A PERSON AGAIN.

A pilgrim has added in charcoal: 'I tried for nine days. On the tenth I realised the stone had been trying for eleven hundred years and had not got anywhere either. We shared a very comfortable silence.'
No one has ever seen the same mystic twice on the isle. The old fishermen say there is only one, and he has been sitting there for eleven hundred years, and he is very patient.
place_lore.nirncraft.isle_of_the_drowned:
^WE STAYED. THE SEA CAME. WE DID NOT MOVE.
^LET THE SWORDS STAND WHERE WE STOOD.
^LET THE TIDE KNOW WHAT IT HAS TAKEN.
Beneath, a fisherman's scratch: 'I once tried to pull one out. It was very heavy. It was very cold. It said, quite distinctly, in a voice I do not wish to describe: not yet.'
A low green island in the Yokudan sunken isles, where a company of Ansei is said to have gone down together, sword by sword, rather than abandon their trust.
On the isle, at low tide, you can see swords standing in the sand, upright, in a ring. They are not planted. They are not anyone's. They are, the fishermen say, keeping watch.
place_lore.nirncraft.ivarstead.barrow_co:
To the steward in Riften,
Three weeks I have written and three weeks nobody has answered. My son Asvar is gone into Shroud Hearth Barrow, up the slope from our houses. He said a fence in the Ratway would pay forty septims for a burial urn with the old silver bands. Forty septims, for a boy who earns two a day hauling stone.

I went to the entrance myself with a lantern. There is a cold breath that comes out of it, and in that breath I heard something knocking. Slow. Like a man tapping a hammer on a coffin lid to see if anyone's inside.

I am a coward and I came home. Send someone who isn't. I will pay what I can.
Hjorvald
place_lore.nirncraft.ivarstead.hook: A small timber village on the Darkwater River at the foot of the Throat of the World. Every pilgrim bound for the Seven Thousand Steps sleeps a night at the Vilemyr Inn first.
place_lore.nirncraft.ivarstead.pilgrim_t:
#Pilgrims this year, 4E 201
Morning Star: 2. Sun's Dawn: 0 (snow). First Seed: 4. Rain's Hand: 9, a whole family from Bruma, and they paid in Cyrodiilic coin which nobody here will take.
Second Seed: 11. Midyear: 14. Sun's Height: 6, and one of them a Khajiit who climbed in bare feet.

Last Seed: 3. Hearthfire: 5.
Frostfall: 1, an old man with a brass bell who would not tell me his name and would not stop smiling. He wants to ring it at the top. Told him about the bandits at Nilheim. He said the Divines would see to them.

The Divines, in my experience, are slow on the pass road.
place_lore.nirncraft.ivarstead.rumour: Ivarstead's quiet, mostly. Pilgrims, lumber, the river. Only the barrow up the hill keeps folk awake, and the bandits in that old tower on the pass.
place_lore.nirncraft.ivarstead.sk4_note_: Folio #4 (896, 901): Field inspection recorded for Ivarstead within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.iveran_ancestral_to: A Sathil family tomb off the Necrom road, its door sealed from the inside and its lamps still lit after forty years.
The Sathil tomb is sealed from the inside. Something in there waits. The gravedigger will not dig the grave that should have been dug for it.

#Here are the Sathil
We came when called. We stayed until the last was home. If one of us is missing, the door is not to be opened until the grave is dug and the name is said. Only then shall we let you in, and only then shall we let ourselves out.

#THE LAW
A chief rules by right of strength. A chief rules by right of the clan's will. A chief who cannot do both is not a chief, but a very large visitor.
The duel shall be witnessed by one who owes the clan nothing. Their word is the law, and their silence is law too.
place_lore.nirncraft.jathsogur.hook: An Orc stronghold in the Valenwood forest, where a chieftain wants a trial of strength witnessed by a stranger who owes the clan nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.jathsogur.rumour: Jathsogur has two sons and one seat. The older is slow and sure; the younger is quick and clever. Every Orc in the forest has an opinion, and none of them will say it before the tavern closes.

place_lore.nirncraft.jeevu_rice_paddy.ho: A rice paddy in the Shadowfen, with rows of seedlings in black water and a harvest-counter's high chair.
place_lore.nirncraft.jeevu_rice_paddy.ru: The rice-counter at Jeevu counts forty-two at dusk where there were forty-one at dawn. She doesn't like it.
place_lore.nirncraft.jeevu_rice_paddy.we: Dawn count: 41. Dusk count: 42. Bowls set: 42. Bowls emptied: 42. I do not feed one extra worker. I feed forty-one and the forty-second bowl is emptied by morning. The harvest has been good, and I will not question what labours in the dark. But I count, and the count does not lie.

A wind-scoured dragon burial mound crowning a high spur of the Jerall Mountains along the southern border.
Shepherds on the high scree stay clear of the Jerall Crest Mound; lightning strikes its capstone in every summer storm.

Folio #60 (-1360, 1560): Field inspection recorded for Jerall Crest Mound within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #60 for jerall_crest_mound: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Jerall Crest Mound are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

At four thousand paces above the valley floor, this circular cairn dominates the southern skyline. The radial capstones have shifted outward as if heaved from below by frost—or by something stirring within the burial vault.
place_lore.nirncraft.jerall_stone_bridge: A single-arch bridge of heavy mountain granite spanning a roaring meltwater ravine on the old climb toward the southern passes.
Drovers check the keystone of the Jerall Stone Bridge every spring; if that span ever goes, the southern steads are cut off for good.

Folio #64 (-1200, 1400): Field inspection recorded for Jerall Stone Bridge within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #64 for jerall_stone_bridge: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Jerall Stone Bridge are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

The First Era arch-stones still hold firm despite the frost-heave in the ravine walls, though bandits have pried three parapet blocks loose to drop on passing wagons. Keep your mules to the center of the roadway where the granite is thickest.

place_lore.nirncraft.journeymans_nook.ca: Waymark 14: Journeyman's Nook. Old traveller's shrine, sound roof, good shelter for one night. Whistling Mine lies an easy hour southwest; the road to the Shrine of Azura goes west past it.

Personal note, not for the College copy: I buried my emergency purse behind the Nook, north side, below the stone with the carved boot. Twenty paces out, under a flat rock. If I'm dead, take it. If I'm alive and you took it, I will find you.

^Added later, in a hurrier hand
If you see a Khajiit with one ear asking after me, you never read this note. He thinks I owe him for a compass. I do. But not that much.
place_lore.nirncraft.journeymans_nook.ho: A small Nordic ruin southeast of Winterhold, once a shrine where travellers left offerings for safe passage over the snowfields. Cartographers still use it as a waymark.
place_lore.nirncraft.journeymans_nook.ru: Journeyman's Nook? Old travellers' shrine. You leave a coin and a crust for the road. If you take the coins someone else left, the road takes you.

place_lore.nirncraft.jylkurfyk.garrison_:
#GARRISON, THIS WINTER
One hundred and four shields, thirty-one spears, and nine lamps that burn without oil. We hold the Door. We do not know what is behind it. The first captain's order was to hold it. He did not say against what.
We have held it for nine hundred winters. It has never been opened from either side. In the spring the knock comes, very soft, and in the summer it is gone. We do not answer. That is the order.
place_lore.nirncraft.jylkurfyk.hook: A fort of black basalt and whale-bone on the Atmoran coast, built by the first ships' captains and still held, in the long dark, by a garrison no one has relieved.
place_lore.nirncraft.jylkurfyk.rumour: The fort of Jylkurfyk has never been given a name by its builders. They called it only The Door, and left, and did not say which side of it they stood on.
place_lore.nirncraft.ka_po_tun_steppe_fo: A steppe fort of grey tile and black timber on the edge of the Ka Po' Tun, held by a garrison that has marched out every spring for a thousand years and found nothing to fight.

#THE DAWN PATROL
Out at the first bell. Steppe: grass. Sky: sky. Enemy: none. Returned at the last bell. I have walked the same ten miles for forty years. I have begun to name the grasses. There is one, near the stream, that I call Patience.

Today, at the stream, a horse stood. It was not ours. It was grey, and thin, and had no rider. It looked at me and did not run. I gave it water. In the morning it was gone, and the stream had a new bank.
The fort sends out a patrol every dawn. The patrol returns every dusk. In a thousand years, they have never met an enemy, and never once admitted to being disappointed.

place_lore.nirncraft.kagrenzel.dwemer_pl: Above the shaft, a brass plaque in Dwemer script, with a scholar's chalk translation scrawled beneath it on the stone:
'Kagrenzel. Descent to the lower works. The guardians are tuned to the voices of the clan. Those who are not of the clan, descend at the pleasure of the guardians.'

And under that, smaller: 'The clan is gone. The guardians are not. Draw your own conclusions, and then draw your sword.'

A last line, in a cramped Imperial hand, the chalk worn almost away: 'Septimus, if you climb back up this far, we lowered a second rope at dawn. Pull twice.'
place_lore.nirncraft.kagrenzel.hook: A lonely Dwemer shaft in the far south-east hills, a single brass door over a drop so deep that dropped torches go out before they land, and something below that climbs.
#22nd of Hearthfire
On the Legate's orders, legionary Gaius Septimus lowered into the Kagrenzel shaft on two hundred feet of rope to assess the ruin for use as a store. Signal agreed: two tugs for well, three for haul.
At a hundred and forty feet: two tugs. At a hundred and eighty: two tugs. At two hundred: three tugs, then many, then none. Rope hauled up. End cut cleanly as if by a blade. No blood.
Septimus carried the cohort's token on a chain at his neck. The Legate wants it recovered. I want Septimus recovered, but I am a sergeant, and I know which want carries weight.
place_lore.nirncraft.kagrenzel.rumour: Kagrenzel's just a hole with a door on it. The Imperials lowered a man down on a rope last month. The rope came back. Cut clean.

place_lore.nirncraft.kagrumez.hook: A Dwemer ruin whose resonance chambers still sing, west of the dragon burial mound. The Dwemer built it to test something with sound; the gems still answer anyone who strikes them.
place_lore.nirncraft.kagrumez.rumour: Kagrumez sings. I mean it. You stand at the door and you can hear the stones humming. Some Telvanni scholar is desperate to know what tune.
place_lore.nirncraft.kagrumez.scavenger_: Chalked on a pipe, in a sloppy hand: Wrong gem, the spiders come. Wrong gem twice, the big ball comes. Wrong gem three times and you are me, sitting behind a pipe writing this with chalk while something rolls up and down the hall looking for you. Do not take the shiny ones in the first room. They are the wrong ones. They are always the wrong ones.

Under it, in different chalk: Burzol at the Ramshackle Trading Post buys the gears for twenty drakes. Tel Mithryn buys them from Burzol for eighty. Cut out the Orc. Also, do not cut out the Orc where he can hear you.
place_lore.nirncraft.kagrumez.tuning_not: Each chamber holds plinths. Each plinth holds a gem, or held one; most are scattered. Placed correctly, the gems sound together and a door opens. Placed incorrectly, the guardians wake. I placed them incorrectly. Twice.

The theory: the Dwemer made the chambers to train the ear, or perhaps to train the soul, in the tones that hold the world together. The practice: there is a tuning key, a brass fork as long as my forearm, in the deepest chamber. With it one can read the correct tones without guessing. My wager is that the key still lies on the master plinth. My other wager is that I will not survive to collect on the first.

Soldiers at the Karth Gorge Legion Camp spend half their watch clearing boulders that raiders roll down from the upper crags.

place_lore.nirncraft.karth_gorge_sky_bur: A high limestone ledge and bone-scaffold above the Karth Gorge where Reachfolk expose their honored dead to the mountain hawks.
Barge-hands on the Karth never look up when passing the Sky Burial cliffs; the old clans put a curse on anyone who climbs the scaffold stair.

Leave the flesh to the red-tailed hawk and the wind of the crags; leave the iron blade broken beside the stone so no Nord bailiff may claim it. From this shelf our ancestors watch the river bend from dawn until the stars return.
place_lore.nirncraft.karth_river_stead.h: A stone-terraced homestead perched above the churning rapids of the Karth, where hardy barley and mountain goats are raised behind dry-stone walls.
place_lore.nirncraft.karth_river_stead.r: The family at Karth River Stead keeps a signal-horn by the door to warn the river barges whenever raiders gather on the cliffs.

A narrow fissure in the canyon limestone choked with pale webbing and empty miner helmets.
Don't follow a stray goat into the Karth Spider Cleft; the webs in that crack are thick enough to dull a woodman's axe.

Three of our lads chased a rich silver-lead vein into this side-cleft last Frostfall and stirred up a nest of giant frostbite spiders. We boarded up the lower adit, but they still crawl out over the upper rocks after dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.karth_spire_mound.h: A circular dragon burial mound perched atop a sheer limestone spire overlooking the confluence of the Karth.
place_lore.nirncraft.karth_spire_mound.r: Miners at Karthwasten say the capstone on the Karth Spire Mound cracked straight down the middle the week Helgen burned.

place_lore.nirncraft.karth_spire_mound.w: Only a narrow goat-ledge reaches the summit of this limestone needle, yet the ancient masons hauled thirty-ton wedge slabs to its crown. The inscription around the rim names a winged tyrant who ruled the silver valleys before the first mines were sunk.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire.blades_f: ...and so in the reign of Reman the Dragonguard raised a sanctuary in the Reach, behind the spire that the Reachmen call Karth's Tooth. Its door bore the face of a dragon and would open only to blood of a certain kind, the old Dragonguard being much concerned with such things.

Within, on a great wall, the Akaviri carved what they had learned of the end of days, so that those who came after would know the shape of it. The chronicler does not record whether any of them understood the carving. Only that they spoke of it in low voices, and that the Grandmaster took his meals facing the other way.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire.hook: A towering crag above the Karth valley, held by Forsworn and wrapped in mist. Old soldiers' tales speak of a hidden temple of the Blades in the cliffs behind it.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire.rumour: Karthspire's crawling with Forsworn. My grandfather used to say the Blades built something up there in the old days, before the Thalmor ran them all down.

place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire_camp.hoo: A Forsworn camp on the trail up the Karthspire, where sentries watch the bridge and the valley below with arrows nocked and ears open.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire_camp.rum: There's a Forsworn camp guarding the way up Karthspire. Why they'd guard a rock nobody wants is anyone's guess.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthspire_camp.sen: Watch the bridge. Watch the valley. If Nords come in twos, shoot them. If Nords come in tens, run to the spire and warn the others. If someone comes alone and knows the old path behind the falls, do not shoot them. Follow them. Find out what they know.

The crones say there is a door in the spire that the Nords' ancestors made. A door with a dragon's face. It does not open for Reachmen. It does not open for hagravens. It waits for someone. We watch for that someone too.

place_lore.nirncraft.karthwasten.assay_s:
Ore, Karthwasten main shaft. Grade: good. Fair price per ingot at Markarth smelter: 25 septims.
Price offered by Silver-Blood factor: 9 septims.
Price offered by Silver-Blood factor after miners refused: 9 septims and an explanation of how many accidents can happen to a shaft that loses its timbers.
We sold. Of course we sold.

On the back, pressed hard enough to tear the paper:
The factor's man weighed our ore on his own scales, the ones with the dented pan. Ainar says the dent is worth two ingots in every ten. If anyone ever comes from Understone Keep to ask why Karthwasten is poor, show them this slip and show them the pan.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthwasten.hook: A cluster of miners' houses above the Karth, where the silver belongs to whoever is strongest this season. Lately that has been the Silver-Bloods' sellswords, and the miners are counting the days.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthwasten.miners_:
To the Jarl of the Reach, in Understone Keep.
We the undersigned miners of Karthwasten ask for three things. One: a patrol on the road to Markarth, because the Forsworn of Broken Tower Redoubt have taken four of us since the thaw. Two: that the Silver-Bloods' hirelings stop 'inspecting' our ore and keeping a share for the trouble.

Three: that someone, anyone, ask after Bergljot's brother Hrofi, who was dragged off toward Broken Tower on the 9th of Sun's Height. He is alive. The Forsworn shout his name from the ridge to mock us.
Signed with marks, eleven of them. Fjola says we shouldn't send it. Fjola says the last petition got a man killed.
place_lore.nirncraft.karthwasten.rumour: Karthwasten? Good silver, bad neighbours. The Forsworn on one side, Silver-Blood thugs on the other, and the miners stuck in the middle with their picks.

place_lore.nirncraft.katlas_farm.hook: The stables and fields at the foot of Solitude's great rock, where travellers hire carriages and gossip changes hands with the horses.
place_lore.nirncraft.katlas_farm.rumour: Katla's stableboy Ottar has been asking every traveller about his sister. Went off toward the northern hills a month ago and never came back. He keeps her hair ribbon in his pocket.
place_lore.nirncraft.katlas_farm.stable_:
Carriage to Morthal, Turdas, one Breton and a goat: 20 septims. Goat extra.
Carriage to Dragon Bridge, Fredas, two Legion couriers: paid by voucher from Castle Dour. Vouchers never paid on time.
Shoeing the grey mare: 4 septims. Feed for the month: 30 septims.

Freydis, Ottar's sister, has not come back. Left on the 2nd of Hearthfire with a basket and a knife and said she was going to gather nightshade. Ottar says she was talking to a crow-woman in the hills toward Ravenscar Hollow before that. I told him crows don't talk. He looked at me like I was the fool.
Ottar's wages: docked nothing. Let the boy grieve.

place_lore.nirncraft.khuul.hook: A single street of ash-grey houses on a sea cliff with a long wooden stair running down to the water and a lantern at every landing.
place_lore.nirncraft.khuul.rumour: In Khuul, someone walks the cliff stair asleep every night. The elders leave the lanterns lit and do not wake them.
place_lore.nirncraft.khuul.web.author: Selvil Sathram
place_lore.nirncraft.khuul.web.p0: Eleven this winter. Nine walked up the stair in the night with their eyes shut and their lips moving. I asked the youngest what she was saying. She said, 'Counting steps.' A Temple pilgrim told me the ash is dreaming, not them. I told her to take her theology elsewhere. We keep lanterns lit. It is all we can do.

place_lore.nirncraft.kings_haven.apple_l:
#ELEVEN LABELS, ELEVEN APPLES
'From her', each one. A tidy script. Eleven apples, kept in a cool cellar in a row, each one exactly as red as the day it was given. They do not rot. I do not know what that means.

I have a twelfth. I picked it myself, from the very tree. I have not eaten it. I have not given it. It sits on the kitchen sill, between the salt and the bread, and watches me with an expression I can only describe as fond.
place_lore.nirncraft.kings_haven.hook: A keep and an orchard of golden apples at the foot of the Summerset downs, where two ancient dames dispute whose tree the great one is, and have done so for a hundred years.
place_lore.nirncraft.kings_haven.rumour: The apples of King's Haven are said to cure grief, which is why nobody dares eat them while the dispute lasts. One must be perfectly sad to enjoy one, and the dames are only furious.

place_lore.nirncraft.kjenstag_ruins.guar:
To the Steward:
Investigated the lights at Kjenstag as ordered. Found the ruins empty, then not empty. A figure with a lamp, very old, in grave wrappings, walking the circle. It did not attack. It searched the ground as if it had dropped something.

Also found a grave robbers' camp nearby, recently used, and a bronze horn among their rubbish, too green to sell. I left it where it lay; I am not paid to fetch ghosts their belongings. The robbers themselves are dead in the marsh. The lantern-man did not do it. Something under the stones did.
place_lore.nirncraft.kjenstag_ruins.hook: A circle of broken Nord stones in the marsh east of Morthal. At midnight a green lantern walks among them, carried by no living hand.
place_lore.nirncraft.kjenstag_ruins.lant:
HERE KJENSTAG THE LAMPBEARER.
HE LIT THE ROAD THROUGH THE MARSH FOR THE LIVING AND THE DEAD.
HE WAS GIVEN A HORN OF BRONZE TO CALL THE LOST.

THIEVES TOOK HIS HORN FROM HIS HAND IN HIS GRAVE.
NOW HE WALKS WITH HIS LAMP AND CANNOT CALL.
PUT THE HORN BACK IN HIS HAND AND HE WILL SLEEP.
LET THE MARSH KEEP THE THIEVES.
AND LET HIS WARDEN BENEATH THE STONES WATCH OVER HIM, SO THAT NO HAND BUT A KIND ONE COMES NEAR.
HE CALLED THE LOST HOME FOR FORTY WINTERS. CALL HIM HOME IN TURN.
place_lore.nirncraft.kjenstag_ruins.rumo: Follow the lantern at Kjenstag and you'll find treasure, that's what they say. Funny how the folk who say that never followed it themselves.
#Ninth winter
We burn the driftwood, then the hull-planks, then the benches. I have kept the fire for nine hundred nights. There is a rule: the hearth must never be out when the sun is not up. I have broken it twice, and been forgiven both times, by the hearth.
We had seal on the solstice. The skald sang. The jarl wept, and said it was the smoke. There is no smoke in the Last Hearth. We have a very good chimney. We have always had it.
place_lore.nirncraft.kjolvik.hook: The last Atmoran hold on an ice shelf: ten long halls half-buried in drifts, whale-bone arches, a stone-lined harbour where the ice cracks, and the aurora overhead. Older and harsher than any Nord town.
place_lore.nirncraft.kjolvik.rumour: Kjolvik has never been conquered. It has, in nine winters, been very nearly forgotten, which a Nord will tell you is far worse.

place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_ridge.bu:
...whatever you heard, Hjolfrid, I did not leave you for her. I left because the Jarl's men were coming for me over the debt, and I did not want them to find you with me. I am in Bruma now. There is work. If you can get away from Falkreath, come. If you cannot, I will understand. Only do not do anything foolish. You always did foolish things with fire when you were...
The rest has been held in a flame until it curled.
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_ridge.hj:
Rule one: we take carts, not lives, unless the cart fights. Bolli fought. That was his choice.
Rule two: lookouts at Bannermist Tower keep their lamps lit and their mouths shut. I'll know if they don't.
Rule three: we don't touch Legion supply. The Legion pays the Jarl and the Jarl pays nobody. As long as we leave the soldiers alone, nobody comes up this ridge.

Rule four, since somebody asked: no, we are not going to raid the graveyard in Falkreath. I don't know who's been digging there and I don't want to. Whoever it is has a lantern that burns green and walks the old road to the Roadside Ruins at night. Leave them be.
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_ridge.ho: A bandit camp on the rocky ridge west of Falkreath, where the gang of Hjolfrid Ashpine counts its stolen silver. The Jarl has finally put a price on her head.
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_ridge.ru: Hjolfrid Ashpine runs Knifepoint Ridge. Burned her own face in a forge to stop crying over a man, they say. Now she makes other people do the crying.
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_ridge.sh:
Last Seed take: 4 carts. 610 septims, 30 planks (sold at the Stormcloak camp, no questions), 1 ox (eaten).
Hjolfrid: 200.
Finnvid and the Bannermist lookouts: 60 each (complained).
Sigge: 40 and his boots back.
Set aside: 150, buried. Only Hjolfrid knows where. She says it's for when this ends. Nobody asked what she meant by ends.

In the margin, in Hjolfrid's hand: 'The buried share is for Bruma. If I go, Sigge gets it and takes it to the man named in the letter in my chest. If Sigge reads this and keeps it, I will come back from Sovngarde personally and take it back out of his hide.'
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_stead.ho: A small hillside steading west of Falkreath that supplies charcoal and salted mutton to the nearby iron and corundum workings.
place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_stead.ru: Folk at Knifepoint Stead say you can hear the outlaws hammering stolen iron up in the ridge quarry whenever the wind blows from the west.

place_lore.nirncraft.knifepoint_stead.wa: Delivered six panniers of birch charcoal to the smelter below the ridge, though the driver refused to linger once dusk settled over the pines. Until the hold guard clears the gang out of Knifepoint Ridge, no carter in his right mind will haul ore past the western mile-stone without armed outriders.
place_lore.nirncraft.knights_of_the_thor: A modest lodge on the Cheydinhal road with a thorny rose carved above the door, empty and swept, and cleaner than its reputation.

^VISITORS TO THE LODGE
^Dawn of Frostfall: a Breton, hungry. Fed.
^Noon: two Legion deserters. Fed, and sent down the south road with directions and a warning.
^Dusk: a knight who gave no name and drank only water. He left his sword on the table and walked out. I do not know whether it was a gift or a debt.
^Midnight: the sword is gone. So is the water. The cup is full. I will not describe the sound the cup made.
The Knights of the Thorn are said to have a hall near Cheydinhal. The lodge-keeper says the knights are gone. The candles say otherwise.

place_lore.nirncraft.koeglin_village.hoo: A cliff-side village under a lighthouse on the Stormhaven coast, with steep stairs and nets hung from the cliff edge.
place_lore.nirncraft.koeglin_village.rum: The Koeglin nets are hauling up salt water from where there's no water to haul.
place_lore.nirncraft.koeglin_village.web: Drip count, cup one: forty to the hour. Cup two, from the inn: sixty. The giant's cheek is wet at noon. I asked the old men. They said his tears are the sea and he has never stopped. I asked who is making him cry. Nobody knew. The water tastes of iron and hot copper.
place_lore.nirncraft.kogoruhn.hook: A blasted ash-fortress at the foot of the mountain, with broken keeps half-buried in drifts and a collapsed amphitheatre.
place_lore.nirncraft.kogoruhn.rumour: At Kogoruhn the ash seats are full of sleepers. They don't turn their heads when you walk through.
place_lore.nirncraft.kogoruhn.web.author: a Kogoruhn sleeper
place_lore.nirncraft.kogoruhn.web.p0: ~We came in slippers and we came in silk,~we came by milk-road and by milk,~we sat in rows on a seat of ash,~the lights went down with a gentle crash.~Someone hums on the stage tonight:~it is not a song, it is only light.

place_lore.nirncraft.kolbjorn_barrow.dig:
^Diggers Wanted at Kolbjorn Barrow
Strong backs and short memories required. Wages paid on reaching the inner door, with a bonus for each artefact handed over intact. The Redoran Guard has been informed and has expressed no objection, or at least no objection I could hear over the wind. Apply at the dig. Bring your own shovel. Bring your own lantern. Bring, if you have one, your own courage; the barrow supplies none.

Scrawled across the bottom by some disgruntled digger: Wages paid on reaching the inner door. We have not reached the inner door. We will never reach the inner door. The inner door, Ralis, is a lie you tell yourself.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolbjorn_barrow.hoo: An old Nordic barrow half buried by ash a short walk from Raven Rock. Diggers paid by the hopeful excavator Ralis Sedarys are clearing it a bucket at a time, and not all of them come up again at dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolbjorn_barrow.ner:
#Middas
Cleared six buckets of ash from the second gallery. Found a Nord bracelet, bronze, gave it to the foreman like an honest fool. Father would be proud. Father would also want the wages.

#Fredas
Broke through to a side chamber behind the second gallery. Old bones in the niches. Some of them turned their heads when my lantern passed. I am not mad. Varis saw it too.

#Sundas
The gallery fell in behind us. Varis got out. I am in the side chamber with a lantern, half a loaf, and my pass from Sergeant Indaram. The bones are standing up. If someone finds this before they find me, I am behind the third pillar, and I would very much like to go home.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolbjorn_barrow.rum: Kolbjorn Barrow's being dug out by that Dunmer, Ralis Sedarys. Paying good coin, when he pays. Tilvur Sadas's boy Neral went down a week ago and hasn't come up. Ralis says he's fine. Ralis says everything's fine.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_mine.gold:
The richest seam runs east, toward Sky Haven way, but the old Dwemer workings cut across it. Our picks broke into a Dwemer tunnel last winter. Warm air came out, and the smell of oil.
I marked the spot with a red cross on the wall and the foreman bricked it over. Every miner in Kolskeggr knows where the red cross is. Not one of us will tell the Silver-Bloods, because they'd send us back in.

Second page, folded small:
If the Silver-Bloods ever get hold of this mine for good, they'll break that wall in a day and send us down the Dwemer tunnel with a lamp and no wages. I'd rather it stayed in Forsworn hands than theirs. Don't tell anyone I said that. Especially not in Markarth.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_mine.hook: A gold mine in the hills east of Markarth that once fed half the Reach. The miners have been driven out by Forsworn, and the gold sits in the dark with no one to dig it.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_mine.rumo: Kolskeggr Mine used to keep Markarth in gold. Now the Forsworn have it, and the only one who still goes near is an Imperial named Pavo who won't give up his claim.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_mine.shif:
#Kolskeggr Mine, 4E 201
Morning shift: Olfrid, Hrogar, Ennis, Rolf. Afternoon shift: Ulfr, Thane's boy, Margret.
Night shift: none since the Forsworn came down from the Lover Stone path.
Pay for the month: withheld by the Silver-Blood factor until the mine produces again. The mine cannot produce while the Forsworn hold it. The factor says that is our problem.

Scratched beside the roster with a nail: Pavo Attius, the Imperial who holds the claim now, came to tell us the Forsworn would be gone by spring. That was two springs ago. Ennis says he'd sooner swing a pick for the Forsworn than wait for the Silver-Bloods to pay us. Ennis says a lot of things after dark.
