place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_stead.hoo: A small stone steading beside the gold-smelting road east of Markarth, supplying timber props and tallow candles to the mine crews.
place_lore.nirncraft.kolskeggr_stead.rum: Miners stopping at Kolskeggr Stead say the air around the valley smells of briar-smoke whenever the redoubts beat their drums.

place_lore.nirncraft.korvanjund.hook: An ancient Nordic crypt in the central Pale, said to hold the crown of the old High Kings. Soldiers of both sides of the war have been seen scouting its approach.
place_lore.nirncraft.korvanjund.kings_la:
~They laid the king beneath the hill,
~And bound his brow with jagged gold,
~And told his sons to wait until
~The crown should rise when Skyrim's old.
~Now Skyrim's old, and sons are many,
~And every son would be a king.
~The hill keeps one, and gives not any,
~And the dead keep counting everything.

^Note on the back of the page
Sung in the alehouses of Dawnstar and Windhelm both, though the last verse changes depending on who is buying. The Windhelm version names Ulfric. The Solitude version names nobody, and the singer looks over his shoulder.
place_lore.nirncraft.korvanjund.rumour: Korvanjund's got an old king's crown in it, or so they say. The Legion wants it to keep it from Ulfric. Ulfric wants it to wear. The draugr want everyone to leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.korvanjund.scout_di:
To the Commander, Fort Dunstad.
Korvanjund: entrance clear of snow, recently. Fresh tracks, heavy boots, at least a dozen. Somebody is preparing an expedition. I saw a blue sash in the scrub. Stormcloaks, almost certainly.

Shepherds say the crypt was opened in the time of the old kings and resealed with something buried in it that the kings did not want found. They also say the sheep near it come back with frost in their wool in summer. I believe the second part.

place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch.family_lette:
To whoever reads this, at the rebuilding:
My family were Atrius of Kvatch, glassblowers, with a shop in the lane beneath the cathedral. My great-great-grandmother fled the night the Gate opened. She buried the family seal-stone in the cellar first, because she meant to come back.

She never did. None of us did. But the story came down to me: a grey stone, palm-sized, carved with a swallow, under the third flag from the hearth. If the masons have reached our lane, I beg you, look. Bring it to the steward's table at the wall and I will pay what I can.
We are glassblowers. We are owed one thing that did not melt.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch.hook: The city that burned first in the Oblivion Crisis is rising again, stone by stone. Its masons dig through two centuries of rubble, and not everything under the ash wants to be found.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch.masons_roste:
#Week of the 3rd, Sun's Dawn
Orc crew of Durga gra-Bol: 14 hands. Laid 60 courses. Asked for meat twice a week. Granted.
Imperial crew: 9 hands. Laid 22 courses. Asked for a priest to bless the foundations. Granted, grudgingly; the priest charges by the stone.

Found in the rubble by the old chapel: a strongbox, empty; a child's wooden horse; a sword with the blade fused to its scabbard by the Gate-fire. I have kept the horse on my desk. I do not know why.
Reminder: no one digs at the scar where the Gate stood. The ground there is still warm. Two centuries, and it is still warm.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch.rumour: Kvatch is half scaffold and half ghost story. The masons turn up old things every day. Coins, bones, once a Count's own door-knocker. Sometimes the families come looking for what's theirs.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_arena.canvas:
^THE CANVAS CUP
^Soup, gritty. Bread, warm. Ale, in helmets. Wine, in smaller helmets.
^RULES: No fighting in the cup. No fighting near the cup. No fighting about whose cup it is. The cup is the cup. Hetta is Hetta.
On the back, in a different hand: "Sixteen helmets. Sixteen men. If you drink from one, say his name. If you do not know his name, ask. Hetta will tell you. She has them all."
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_arena.hook: The ring of seats under which Kvatch's survivors huddle in canvas and rope, a place of spectacle turned shelter.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_arena.rumour: Under the arena stands, the tavern-keeper pours her ale into dented Legion helmets. She will tell you it is a joke. If you ask whose helmets, she will tell you something else.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_gate.hook: The burning crater edge where the Gate first opened, with a wrecked siege-tower, a plume of ash and a ring of lava glass.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_gate.rumour: At dusk the ash at the crater rises instead of falling. The masons say it is looking for someone.
place_lore.nirncraft.kvatch_gate.web.p0: Light the wick, close the door, and leave the latch alone. Let the drowned go home and let the burning stay out. We did not know the door had two sides. Forgive us the one we left on the latch.
place_lore.nirncraft.kynesgrove.hook: A small mining village on the warm slopes south of Windhelm, its Braidwood Inn full of miners who swear the ground has been growing warmer, and a dragon mound watching from the ridge above.
place_lore.nirncraft.kynesgrove.miner_ta:
#Week of the 3rd, Frostfall
Iron, 22 loads. Corundum, 4 loads. Men fainted from the heat in the lower drift: 2. Men who claim they heard singing in the rock: 3 (all the same three, all the same tavern).

#Week of the 10th, Frostfall
Iron, 19 loads. Lower drift closed after the floor went soft and hot as bread. Water runs from the walls steaming. The old hands say Kyne's Tear is restless. I say the drift is too deep and we should stop digging toward whatever is warming it.

#Week of the 17th, Frostfall
Iron, 21 loads. Someone left a cup of water on the mine step every morning this week. Nobody will own to it. I have started leaving one myself.
place_lore.nirncraft.kynesgrove.priest_c: Sidgar, keeper of the Kynesgrove shrine

Brothers in Windhelm,
The graves behind our shrine have been opened twice since Hearthfire. Not looted: emptied. Old Thrunvar, buried in Last Seed, is gone, and the Widow Asta with him, and both their grave goods left lying in the snow as if they were worthless.
A herder saw lanterns moving along Cragwallow Slope on the night of the second digging, south-east past the mound, toward the old cairns. No honest man walks those slopes at night.
I am an old man and a priest, not a warrior. If you cannot spare a templar, send coin and I will hire someone with a strong arm and a short memory. Our dead deserve to lie where we put them.
place_lore.nirncraft.kynesgrove.rumour: Kynesgrove? Good ore, bad sleep. The miners say the hill hums at night. And the graves behind the shrine have been dug up twice since Hearthfire.
place_lore.nirncraft.kynesgrove.sk4_note: Folio #2 (1825, -298): Field inspection recorded for Kynesgrove within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #2 for kynesgrove: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Kynesgrove are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinth.hook: A hedge-and-root maze that rearranges each time you leave a junction, with carved arrows that lie and wisp-lights as false guides.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinth.rumour: The Labyrinth hedge changes each time you look away. From the ridge you can see it is a map.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinth.web.p0: From the ridge, the hedge is a street grid. The central cross is the market, the north lobes the lamp-wards. I have walked it three times and left a ribbon at each turning. The ribbons were gone by morning. The exit is at the old gate, and the gate is a thing you must be invited through.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinthian.bromju:
IN BROMJUNAAR THE PRIESTS GATHERED, AND THE MASKS WERE MANY.
THEY SPOKE WITH THE VOICE OF THE DRAGONS AND THE PEOPLE KNELT.

WHEN THE DRAGONS FELL, THE MASKS WERE BROUGHT HERE AND THE DOORS WERE SHUT.
OF ALL THE PRIESTS, ONE DID NOT GO QUIETLY.
HIS VOICE IS IN THE STONES. DO NOT ANSWER IT.
THE MASONS WHO SEALED THE LOWER HALLS WERE SEALED IN WITH THEM, SO THAT NONE WOULD KNOW THE WAY BACK. THEIR NAMES ARE CUT ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE DOOR. THEY ASKED THAT IT BE SO.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinthian.hook: The great ruin of Bromjunaar in the snowy hills of southern Hjaalmarch, once the seat of the dragon priests and later the maze of Archmage Shalidor. Scholars still come to study it. Fewer leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinthian.rumour: Labyrinthian. A whole dead city in the snow, and a maze underneath it. The College at Winterhold sends students to study it. Every few years one of them doesn't come back, and they send another.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinthian.studen:
#1st day
Arrived at Labyrinthian with notebook, chalk and three days' bread. My thesis: that Shalidor's maze was built not to keep things out, but to keep a particular thing in. My tutor called this 'romantic.' I called my tutor something I will not record.

#2nd day
The skeletons in the outer halls are animated by something old and indifferent. They do not pursue past certain lines in the floor. I have mapped the lines. They form a pattern. The pattern is a word.
#3rd day
I have gone too far in to come out the way I came. I have hidden my notebook of the lines under a loose slab in the hall of the broken masks. If I do not return, someone must take it to the College. My tutor must be told he was wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.labyrinthian.valkyg: A rough map, inked on deer hide. Labyrinthian is drawn as a spiral. A short way north-east, between the spiral and a stone marked with wings, there is a small square and the words: the forgotten door, sealed from within.

In the margin: 'The priests of Bromjunaar buried their betrayer close, so they could watch him. Svana says it's a blade worth a jarl's ransom. Svana says a lot of things.'
On the back, in pencil: 'Take wool, take fire, take two friends. Do not take Svana. She'll talk the whole way and run at the end.'

place_lore.nirncraft.lakeview.deed_of_sa: Office of the Steward of Falkreath

^DEED OF SALE

The hill plot overlooking Lake Ilinalta, north of Pinewatch and bounded by the old pine line, is held in the gift of the Jarl of Falkreath and is offered for honest settlement. The holder may build, fence and farm, and shall render the Jarl a tithe of timber when called.

The previous holders, Gunnar and Sigrun Lake-Holm, have surrendered their claim. Their debts to Gray Pine Goods are settled by forfeit of the land. The hold makes no promise as to bears, wolves, or the neighbours at Pinewatch.
place_lore.nirncraft.lakeview.hook: A hillside plot above Lake Ilinalta, sold by the Jarl of Falkreath to anyone with the gold to build on it. The last family who tried left in a hurry and left something behind.
place_lore.nirncraft.lakeview.lakeholm_l:
Brother,
We are leaving the lake. Sigrun will not stay another winter, not after the men from Pinewatch came asking how much we had saved and whether we kept it in the house. We do not. I buried it where Father taught us, under the two pines that lean together, downhill of the house and toward the water.

We left in the night with only the cart. When the road is safer I will come back for the pot. If I do not, it is yours. Grandmother's gold ring is in there too. Do not let Sigrun know I told you, she thinks it is bad luck to write down where money sleeps.
Gunnar
place_lore.nirncraft.lakeview.rumour: The Jarl sells that lake plot to whoever pays. The family before, the Lake-Holms, packed up overnight. Bears, they said. I say there was more to it.
place_lore.nirncraft.lakeview.sk4_note_3: Folio #4 (-468, 982): Field inspection recorded for Lakeview within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Durz went west. To the Nord barrow, Angarvunde. He said: a blood-kin of Largashbur brings home a Nord dead-king's blade, the curse breaks, the chief smiles.

Curse does not break for blades. Chief does not smile. Durz is a fool. Durz is my brother.

Nine days. I mark them here. Ten marks and I go myself. Or a stranger goes. Strangers are cheaper than sisters.
place_lore.nirncraft.largashbur.hook: An Orc stronghold in the southern hills of the Rift, its palisade hung with bones and its people sick with a curse their chief will not name. Outsiders are not welcome. Outsiders who can fight are tolerated.
place_lore.nirncraft.largashbur.rumour: Largashbur Orcs don't trade with us much since the sickness came on them. Their hunters still come down to the mill for salt. Proud folk. Grim folk.

place_lore.nirncraft.last_vigil.hook: A cliffside bandit camp in the eastern mountains, perched over the old Dunmer border road. The bandits there take what they like and answer to nobody, not even Maven Black-Briar.
place_lore.nirncraft.last_vigil.rumour: Last Vigil's lot are mad. They hit a Black-Briar mead wagon last week. Can you imagine? Maven will have their skins for boot leather.

place_lore.nirncraft.last_vigil.vigil_bo:
#20th of Frostfall
Took a Black-Briar wagon on the lake road. Two guards, both ran. One cask, sealed with the black thorn, so heavy it took three of us to roll it. Reserve stock, the label says. Must be the good stuff.

#21st of Frostfall
Tried to tap it. It's not mead. There's a false bottom with something red underneath, bottles of it, sweet as summer berries. I know what that is. Everyone in the Ratway knows what that is.

Maven's selling the Redwater skooma. Or someone is, in her barrels. Either way, this cask is worth more to the right person in Riften than all the gold in the Rift.
place_lore.nirncraft.last_vigil.vigil_wa:
LAST VIGIL
TURN BACK
WE DON'T PAY THE BRIAR
WE DON'T PAY THE KNIVES
WE DON'T PAY THE JARL
YOU PAY US

Below, painted over and then scratched out again: 'or come in and drink with us, we're not so bad'

The plank is nailed to a dead pine where the path from the lake road turns up toward the cliffs. Around it, on the lower branches, hang a dozen tin cups and a Black-Briar bottle with the neck snapped off, rattling in the wind like a warning bell. Whoever made the sign has a sense of humour. Whoever made the cliff path did not: it is steep, narrow and overlooked by bowmen the whole way up.

place_lore.nirncraft.left_hand_mine.hook: A silver mine just outside Markarth's walls, worked by free miners who sell to the Silver-Bloods. Its deepest drift broke into an old Dwemer cut, and something cold came up through the gap.
place_lore.nirncraft.left_hand_mine.luca:
Scratched with a knife on a pit prop deep in the closed drift:
LUCAN WAS HERE. FOUND THE PICK. SPIDERS BETWEEN ME AND THE LIGHT. GOING THROUGH THE DWARF DOOR TO FIND ANOTHER WAY OUT.
IF I AM NOT HOME BY THE MARKET DAY TELL AURELIA THE PICK IS FATHER'S AND SHE MUST HAVE IT. I AM NOT LEAVING IT TO A SPIDER.

Scratched further along the same timber, fainter, as if by a tired hand:
DWARF DOOR LEADS DOWN NOT UP. COLD. WEBS. SOMETHING BIG HAS ITS NEST BY THE STEAM PIPE. I HAVE THE PICK. I AM GOING TO SIT VERY STILL UNTIL IT SLEEPS. AURELIA, THE SPICED BREAD WAS GOOD. SAVE ME SOME.
place_lore.nirncraft.left_hand_mine.rumo: Left Hand Mine shut its deep drift last month. Spiders, says Skaggi. Big ones, from the old Dwarven tunnels. The Salvius boy was down there when they closed it.

place_lore.nirncraft.left_hand_mine.skag:
DEEP DRIFT IS CLOSED.
Frostbite spiders came through the Dwarven cut. Two men bitten, one dead. No mining past the second timber frame until the Jarl sends guards or the spiders get bored.
The Jarl will not send guards. Spiders do not get bored.

To whoever took Lucan Salvius's pick from the rack: it was not on the rack. He went back down for it after we closed the drift. I told him not to. He's an Imperial. They never listen, they just quote laws at you.

place_lore.nirncraft.leyawiin.black_lace:
Darling Ottavio,
You asked why I wear black at weddings. It saves time, dearest. Nobody ever asks the bride of three seasons why she buys her mourning ahead.

I went to the spider stones west of the city on the new moon. I left a silk scarf and a secret, as one does. I came home with a name. Yours, Ottavio, was not the name. Yours was the one before it. Do be a darling and stay away from my sweets until the Lady of Whispers changes her mind.
place_lore.nirncraft.leyawiin.count_decr:
^Let it be known
That no Argonian of the Blackwood shall pass the river gate after the bells of dusk without a letter of surety from a citizen of Leyawiin, the said citizen to stand liable for the conduct of the said Argonian in every particular.

Under this, in chalk: 'And who stands surety for the Count?'
Under that, in another hand: 'The Count's wife, poor woman.'
Under that, scratched with a claw: 'We remember when the river was ours. We are patient. Sleep well, Count.'
place_lore.nirncraft.leyawiin.hook: The southern gate of the Empire, a stone city on the Blackwood marshes where Imperials and Argonians eye each other across a river and a war neither side has properly finished.
place_lore.nirncraft.leyawiin.rumour: Leyawiin keeps its gates shut at dusk now. Not for bandits. For the marsh folk. And for the noblewoman on the hill who's buried three husbands in black lace.
place_lore.nirncraft.liars_retreat.crew_: Lads. The moonstone from Soljund's Sinkhole stays in the strongbox till the fence from Markarth comes. Nobody touches it. Nobody tells the Stormcloaks next door about it either. They'd call it 'requisitioning' and give us a speech about Talos.

If the Soljund's folk send someone, tell them the cart went into the river. Weep a little if you can. Gjuki, you're good at weeping, do the weeping.
The escorts we took are in the back cave, eating our food. Ransom them or let them go, I don't care, but stop feeding them the good cheese.
place_lore.nirncraft.liars_retreat.hook: A river cave on the Karth where a smooth-talking bandit keeps his crew and his stolen moonstone. Half the stories he tells are lies. The other half are worse.
place_lore.nirncraft.liars_retreat.ottar:
Copy number nine. Sold for 40 septims each to eight fools so far.
The map shows Four Skull Lookout, south of Karthwasten, with an X by the skull that faces west and the words 'Dig beneath the sunset skull, a Legion paymaster's chest, lost 4E 176'.

In smaller writing on the back, in Ottar's own hand, not meant for buyers:
The joke is, I made it up from a story my old captain told me, and the captain swore it was true. Never dug there myself. Never wanted to know. A man who digs up his own lie has nothing left to sell.
place_lore.nirncraft.liars_retreat.rumou: Sweet-Tongue Ottar runs Liar's Retreat. He'll sell you a treasure map, a horse, his own mother. Not one of them's real.

place_lore.nirncraft.lillandril.hook: A city of open-air libraries and bronze observatories climbing a seaside rock in terraces, where ring galleries of book-stacks stand open to the sky and no voice is raised above a whisper.
place_lore.nirncraft.lillandril.reading_:
#THE STACKS ASK ONLY THIS
Find the shelf. Read the book. Return the book to the shelf it left, and not the nearest one. Do not whisper to the volumes; they are shy. Do not lend a book you have not read, and do not read a book you have not been lent.

In pencil: 'The catalogue is a mirror. The books are the room behind it. When the catalogue disagrees with the room, trust the room. I have asked the room very politely to stop disagreeing. It has not answered.'
place_lore.nirncraft.lillandril.rumour: The library of Lillandril has no roof, they say, because its books are not afraid of weather. They are afraid of people who cannot read the weather. It is a distinction that scholars love to explain.
place_lore.nirncraft.lillandril.student_:
#THINGS TO CHECK
1. On the Seventh Colour of Light: not in the Restricted Ring. Not on the shelf. Ask the Acropolis. 2. Maelia leaves her office every Tuesday at the third bell, for exactly forty minutes. Where does she go? 3. Why is the Ninth Ring's dust always freshly disturbed?
place_lore.nirncraft.lilmoth.customs_let: Quintus Mallo, Imperial Customs-Master of Lilmoth

My dear Vibia,
The Empire is leaving Lilmoth and I am leaving with it, though my strongbox is not. The Argonians stand on every pier and watch us pack. I cannot carry it past them without awkward questions, and every answer would get me hanged in two provinces.

So I have sunk it. Off the end of the old customs pier, in the shadow of the harbour tower, where the water is deep and the fish are large. Thirty years of 'gifts', my love. If I do not come back for it, tell our son. Tell him to bring a long hook and a short temper, because the slaughterfish there are the size of dogs and twice as loyal.
place_lore.nirncraft.lilmoth.gazetteer.p:
#Names on the water
Keeper Sees-Many-Moons tends the Hist pool. Boatwife Mudtoe knows every canal's name and mood. Trader Ocheeva imports Cyrodiilic cloth and wine and regrets it. Tribune Lucius Varro counts what comes in and refuses to accept that it does not match. Sap-Fence Ruu sells the not-sacred kind of sap, by the thimble.

#Beds, bowls and small debts
The Dripping Reed asks guests to say where they are going; the canals are patient, not forgiving. A rice merchant on the fourth canal keeps seven debt-boats and a second ledger in the rafters. The fourth canal's old tenant is bad-tempered but not yet hungry. Keep to the left of every bend.
place_lore.nirncraft.lilmoth.hook: The capital of Argonia, a port city of reed-roofed towers and drowned Imperial stone, where the King holds court without a crown and the harbour mud hides the Empire's last customs strongbox.
place_lore.nirncraft.lilmoth.royal_court:
To the Mission in Alinor:
I have attended the so-called court of the so-called King of Argonia. There is no throne. There is a tree. The King sits beneath it and listens to petitioners who speak to the tree, not to him. When I asked to be presented, I was told that the tree had already been informed of my presence and was considering it.
I recommend we not attempt anything in Lilmoth. Every Argonian in the room looked at me at once when I entered, and I am quite certain none of them turned their heads.
place_lore.nirncraft.lilmoth.rumour: Every diver in Lilmoth's tried for the old customs strongbox in the harbour mud. Thirty years of Imperial bribes, they say. The slaughterfish like that patch of water. A lot.

place_lore.nirncraft.loreius_farm.hook: An Imperial family's farm on the road south of Dawnstar, the last green fields before the snowfields begin. The farmer has opinions about everything, starting with the Empire.
place_lore.nirncraft.loreius_farm.loreiu:
Dear Cassia,
You ask how the farm fares. The cabbages are well. The goats are well. My knees are not, and the Empire is worse.
The Legion marched past on their way to Fort Dunstad and took four sacks of potatoes 'on account'. I asked whose account. They pointed at the dragon on their shields. I have never seen a dragon pay for potatoes.

Giants have moved closer, up at Blizzard Rest. One of them walked past the fence last week carrying a whole pine like a toothpick. I waved. He did not wave back.
If you hear I have been eaten by a giant, know that I went down complaining.
Your cousin, Vantus
place_lore.nirncraft.loreius_farm.rumour: Old Vantus Loreius would argue with a snowdrift if it blocked his cart. Mind, the snowdrift would probably lose.

place_lore.nirncraft.lost_city_of_the_na: A buried city under the dunes, sand-choked streets below ground, a sunken temple and glass-roofed houses lit by a thin shaft of light.
At noon the lost city lets a single beam through its glass roof, and the dunes above seem to breathe.

O Cup, O Well, O Water that waits. We give you back what we have drunk. Take the debt from the caravan and the debt from the child. Let the sand be sand again, and the king be a king in memory only. Let the cup be full.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_echo_cave.bard: Edda Fairvoice, student of the Bards College

#4th of Frostfall
Master Viarmo said no student has ever composed in Lost Echo Cave. I intend to be the first. The cave is a day north of Steepfall Burrow and I have brought my good lute, three candles and an unreasonable amount of cheese.

#5th of Frostfall
I sang one note and the cave sang it back nine times, each a little lower, as though the stone were tuning itself. Then a tenth answer came, from somewhere deep, and that one was not my voice.

#6th of Frostfall
They move when I play and stop when I stop. I think they are blind and hunting by sound. I will be very quiet now. I will leave the lute here, wedged in the rocks. If someone finds it, please take it home to Solitude.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_echo_cave.hook: A cave in the cold northern hills near Volskygge, named for the way a single shout comes back a dozen times. The Falmer below have learned to listen for it.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_echo_cave.rumo: A bard from the College went looking for Lost Echo Cave to hear its famous echo. They say her song's still bouncing around down there. She isn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_echo_cave.warn:
DONT SHOUT
DONT SING
DONT DROP YOUR PICK

They hear everything. Went down for the ore the Dwemer left and lost Fjolnir to a sound no louder than a cough. If you have a voice, leave it outside. If you are reading this down here, you already came too far. Walk back the way you came, slowly, on the soft parts of your feet.

Below, in a second hand, smaller: 'Fjolnir's brother here. Came back for him. Found his pick and his left boot. Taking them home to Solitude. Whoever wrote this was right about the soft parts of the feet. I made it out by walking like a cat on ice. You will want to do the same.'
A smugglers' cave in the hills south-west of Fort Amol, where the Lost Knife gang trades in everything the war has made scarce and lately fancies itself an army.

Below, in a dozen different hands, the names of members and the places they lost a blade: 'Hakon, at Refugees' Rest.' 'Ysolde, in a Riften magistrate's ribs.' 'Old Borkul, at Mistwatch, in a man who said no.'
And at the bottom, the gang's oath, cut deep: 'A knife lost is a debt owed. Somebody always pays.'

A newer name has been added under the oath, the cuts still pale: 'Ulfgar, at Fort Amol, in a Stormcloak bedroll.' Someone has scored a line through the word 'bedroll' and written 'banner' above it, and someone else has drawn a very rude picture beside it.
Lost Knife Hideout? You can buy anything there: arrows, grain, a man's name off a Jarl's list. Lately they're buying, too. They want swords.

Folio #30 (1197, 341): Field inspection recorded for Lost Knife Hideout within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #30 for lost_knife_hideout: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Lost Knife Hideout are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
Ulfgar has taken Fort Amol with eleven men and a bad smell. I am told he sleeps under the Stormcloak standard. If he lives to spring, I will be astonished, and I will be his partner.
Until then: half the grain goes up to the Abandoned Prison, half to Fort Amol. The arrows go to the fort. The cider goes to me.
Anyone caught selling our routes to Darkwater Crossing or the Imperial camp loses their knife hand. We are the Lost Knives. We can afford to lose a few more.
#Out, by night, Frostfall
6 crates marked ORE. Contents: Cyrodiilic brandy, untaxed.
2 crates marked ORE. Contents: Imperial customs seals, blank.
4 casks marked MEAD. Contents: not my business, I'm told, and from Redwater.

#In
1 Imperial customs clerk, nosy. To the lodge. Not to be harmed. Not to leave.
I keep this list because nobody else does and someday someone will ask me what went through this mine, and I mean to have the answer when they ask. Lady forgive me. Or rather, Lady never find this.
A small mine in the eastern hills near Black-Briar Lodge, worked out years ago. The Black-Briars bought it anyway, and crates still go in and out by night.

On the timber over the main shaft someone carved, many years ago:

^LOST PROSPECT
^NO SILVER, NO IRON, NO LUCK
^4E 160

Beneath, in fresh black paint: PROPERTY OF THE BLACK-BRIAR FAMILY. TRESPASSERS WILL BE DISCOURAGED.

The timber is old and grey and the carving has softened with damp, but the paint below it is new, still tacky in places. The track beneath the sign is rutted deep with cart wheels, far deeper than an empty mine needs, and the ruts lead not toward Riften but east, to the lodge in the woods. A miner's lamp hangs just inside the entrance, trimmed and full of oil. Someone comes here often, and comes here at night.
Lost Prospect hasn't produced ore since my grandmother's time, but there's always a cart outside it with the Black-Briar thorn on the tailboard. Odd, for an empty mine.

place_lore.nirncraft.lost_shipwreck.hook: A wreck on the Vivec shoals, ribs showing, full of crates and rumours and the occasional unwilling sailor.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_shipwreck.mani:
#Manifest
40 crates oilskin umbrellas, waxed, furled.
6 crates moon-sugar, ground fine, in oilskin.
12 casks sujamma.

Note in a second hand: the umbrella handles are hollow. Be careful on the gangway. Mind the weight at the handle end.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_shipwreck.rumo: Bethal Aryon of Vivec has lost forty umbrellas to the Lost Shipwreck, she says, and wants them back. Odd, the customs men say, how heavy forty umbrellas can be.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_tongue_overloo:
The stone at the foot of the stair carries a long text in the old Nord script, worn but legible. My rendering, with the help of an old priest's lexicon:

'Here the people of the lake bowed their heads, and here the masters came down from the sky to drink their bows like wine. Speak softly here. The wall listens. The wall remembers every word given to it.'
My note: there is fresh ash on the stair and the bones of an elk picked very clean. Whatever comes here still comes.
A high stone shrine in the far south of the Rift, built by the Dragon Cult to honour their masters. A word wall stands there still, and dragons come to it as if called.

#Hearthfire, last week
I came all the way from Ivarstead because the Greybeards wouldn't teach me. I thought: the words are written on walls, all over Skyrim. I'll learn them myself.

#Same day, evening
I touched the wall. A word burned behind my eyes like the sun through closed lids, but I couldn't hold it. It slipped away. Something is circling overhead now, very high.

I think I understand why the Greybeards wait so long to teach. It isn't that the words are hard to learn. It's that they get heard.
Lost Tongue Overlook? Up past the old mound. Dragons sit on it like it's their front porch. My uncle says there's writing on a wall up there only the dragons can read.

place_lore.nirncraft.lost_valkygg.advent:
#Day 1
Found the door by the stones my map promised, between Labyrinthian and the dragon altar. It was sealed with ice from the inside, which is not how ice usually works.

#Day 2
The draugr here are colder than any I've fought. Frost on their blades. My fingers are numb even through gloves. There's a voice in the deepest hall that speaks in Nordic so old I only understand every third word, and the words I understand are 'betrayed' and 'pale.'
#Day 3
I'm turning back. Some treasure isn't treasure. It's a grudge with a hilt.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_valkygg.hook: A forgotten Nord ruin beside Labyrinthian, sealed and half-buried in snow. Its dead are restless, and a pale, cold blade is said to lie in the deepest hall.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_valkygg.rumour: Lost Valkygg was lost for a reason, my grandfather used to say. Somebody went to a lot of trouble to forget it. Let's not go to a lot of trouble to remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_valkygg.sealin:
HERE LIES ONE WHO WAS LOVED AND WHO DID NOT LOVE IN RETURN.
HE WAS SEALED IN WITH HIS BLADE, AND HIS BLADE WAS SEALED IN WITH HIS COLD.

LET THE SNOW COVER THE DOOR.
LET THE NAME OF THIS PLACE BE FORGOTTEN.
LET THE ONE WHO WAS WRONGED FIND REST, IF ANY ONE CAN.
WE WHO SEALED IT WILL NOT SPEAK OF IT AGAIN.
AND IF THE DOOR IS EVER OPENED, LET THE OPENER KNOW THIS: THE COLD WILL FOLLOW THE BLADE, AND THE GRUDGE WILL FOLLOW THE COLD, UNTIL THE GRUDGE IS ANSWERED.
place_lore.nirncraft.lost_valley_redoubt: A Forsworn stronghold built around the falls of Bard's Leap, where hagravens keep prisoners in cages over the water and a word wall broods on the heights.

The word on the wall above says something about winds. The Nords who carved it would not tell. Dragons speak only to dragons, and to the Dragonborn, whatever that is.
The singer is useful. Songs are a kind of magic. If I learn the shape of his songs I will put it in a briar and make a Briarheart who sings men's courage out of them. Dead Crone Rock will envy me.

A second tablet, broken across:
The Nord's songs have no magic in them, only cleverness. Cleverness is not nothing. He tricked a sentry into opening his cage with a song about a key. I fed the sentry to the falls. The singer I keep. A creature that sings its way out of a cage is worth more than a dozen who only scream.

#Day 4 of captivity
The hagraven Kerath Burnt-Feather wants a new song every night. I have sung her every ballad I know and three I made up on the spot. She liked 'The Crone on the Crag'. Of course she did.

#Day 9
She is running out of patience and I am running out of songs. Tonight I sang 'Ragnar the Red' and she fed my lute to the fire. Tomorrow, she says, it's my turn.
If a hero reads this: the cages hang above the falls. The crone holds the keys in her claws. You'll have to take them off her.
A minstrel from the College in Solitude was taken near Lost Valley Redoubt. They say the crones keep him singing for his supper. One wrong note and he's the supper.

place_lore.nirncraft.lower_steepfall_bur: A frozen troll cave in the northern hills of Haafingar, its floor littered with bones and broken traps. A white-backed troll has made it home, and the trappers who hunted it have all gone quiet.

By order of the commander of Fort Hraggstad:
For every troll pelt delivered to this fort from the burrows at Steepfall, twenty septims. For a sabre cat pelt from the upper den, twelve septims. For wolf pelts, four septims, and please stop bringing us dogs.

The Legion cannot spare men to clear the burrows while the Stormcloaks are camped south of us. Hunters who take this work do so at their own risk. The Legion will not retrieve bodies. The Legion will, however, pay for pelts found on bodies, if the finder is honest about it.
There's a troll up past Steepfall with a back white as snow. Asgeir Coldhand swore he'd have its hide by Frostfall. It's Frostfall. Nobody's seen Asgeir.

#22nd of Hearthfire
Found tracks above Steepfall, big as a shield. The white-back. The Legion pays twenty for an ordinary troll pelt. A white one would fetch two hundred from the furriers in Solitude, and my name in every tavern.

#29th of Hearthfire
Set six traps at the mouth of the lower burrow. Five sprung, one gone entirely, chain and stake and all. It is not stupid, this troll. It is patient.
#3rd of Frostfall
I have its den. I have my father's hunting horn to call the others if I need them. I will not need them. Tonight Greyback, tomorrow the Winking Skeever.

place_lore.nirncraft.lucky_old_lady_stat: A weathered stone woman at the top of Bravil's oldest stair, her open hand dark with the polish of a thousand wishes.
The Lucky Old Lady is meant to answer one wish a year. Mother Nettle says she answers none, and takes the coin for being listened to.

^Scraps of paper, folded small, left tucked into the stone fingers:
"Let my boy come back from the Gold Coast with all his fingers."
"Let the Count die slowly and the clerk quickly."
"Let Mother Nettle's eels love me."

"Let someone read this and know that I am not well, and I am not saying anything, and the rope is still where I left it." (The last note is torn. Someone has written beneath it, in a different hand: "Come to the Lodge on Morndas. There is soup.")

place_lore.nirncraft.lunar_fang_docks.ho: Rickety lake docks lit by a string of pale moonlamps, with a dozen boats that never leave and a single candle on the harbour-master's step.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunar_fang_docks.ru: The Lunar Fang boats don't fish the south reach any more. They light a candle and sit in the dark instead.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunar_fang_docks.th: Night boats from the Lunar Fang dock to carry sealed ledgers to the Bitter Coast. No questions. No passengers. If a passenger is found aboard, the passenger is to be delivered to the master at the swamp-market, who will see that no harm comes to them. We pay in years.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunar_fang_docks.we: To the brothers of the Candle. The man from Kvatch asked us to leave the sea-door unbarred for one night so the dead might walk home. We did. Do not light the candle again until we know what came through. If anyone asks, the docks were never ours.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunds_hut.hook: A trapper's hut in the hills north-west of Rorikstead, its door hanging open and its smokehouse cold. The wolves have been circling closer since its owner stopped coming home.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunds_hut.lund_jour:
#2nd of Hearthfire
Traps on the west ridge empty again. Three snapped, not sprung. Something is taking the bait and the trap both. Wolf tracks, too many to count.

#5th of Hearthfire
Found the pack's den in the rocks above Bleakwind Bluff. Big grey leader with a white blaze, bolder than any wolf I've seen. He watched me reset the traps and didn't run.
#6th of Hearthfire
Going up to the den tomorrow with the long bow. If I'm not back by the 8th, Hjalla, don't come looking. Send someone with a sword. Take the good pelts to Whiterun and get a fair price from Belethor, not what he offers first.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunds_hut.rumour: Lund the trapper hasn't been down from his hut in two weeks. His wife Hjalla's in Rorikstead asking everyone to go and look. Nobody's gone. The wolves up there are bold this year.
place_lore.nirncraft.lunds_hut.sk4_note_: Folio #21 (-1760, -396): Field inspection recorded for Lunds Hut within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #21 for lunds_hut: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Lunds Hut are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

place_lore.nirncraft.maras_eye_pond.hook: A still, round pond in the hills north of Mixwater Mill where lovers come to swear oaths before Mara, and where, lately, some of them have not gone home.
place_lore.nirncraft.maras_eye_pond.love:
~Mara, whose eye is this water, look on us.
~We are two, and we would be one.
~I, Sigrun of Mixwater, take Ottar of Kynesgrove.
~I, Ottar, take her, and the cold of every winter with her.

~If either of us breaks this oath, let the water close over the oath-breaker.
~If the world breaks it for us, let the water remember.
^Sworn on the 20th of Frostfall, 4E 201, under a pale moon.
Cut beneath, in a rougher hand: SHE IS IN THE CAVE TO THE SOUTH. CRONVANGR. I COULD NOT FOLLOW.
place_lore.nirncraft.maras_eye_pond.rumo: Couples go to Mara's Eye Pond to make their promises. Two went up there in Frostfall and only their lantern came down. Blood on it, they say.

place_lore.nirncraft.maras_kiss_public_h: A bright public house famed for its matchmaking, where a matchmaker with four hundred pairs to her name keeps a ledger and a very good sherry.

#THE MATCHES
Four hundred and one, and the last the oddest. Drathelin and Merelin. A good family, a better name, and, I now believe, a very bad fit. He wishes to be a fisher. She wishes to be a Justiciar. I did not ask. Matchmakers do not ask. That is the whole of the art, and the whole of the sin.

Beneath it, in a different, harder ink: 'To make a match is to wager that two people will not change. They always change. That is the only thing I have ever been sure of. I should like to be sure of something else before I die.'
They say a match made at Mara's Kiss is the strongest in Summerset. A couple that quarrels there is asked to leave. A couple that does not is asked to stay.
place_lore.nirncraft.marbruk.hook: A glade fort-town of grey-brown stone ringed by a living wall of thorn, with a central fire-pit, watch-posts at every gap and a Watch Hall that never seems to be empty.
place_lore.nirncraft.marbruk.rumour: You cannot cut the Thorn Wall of Marbruk. You can only ask it, and it answers by growing back. Marbruk has been besieged four times, and the wall has won every one without raising a thorn.
#STANDING ORDERS
1. Walk the Wall at dusk. 2. Walk it again at dawn. 3. Do not cut. 4. Do not burn. 5. If the wall bleeds sap, say nothing. It is the wall's business.
A later hand has added in pencil: '6. If the wall hums at night, stand very still. 7. If it hums a word, do not say it back.'

place_lore.nirncraft.markarth.dibella_le: Lady of Beauty, I know the priestesses read these before you do, so I will be brief for their sake. My husband Ragnar went to work the carts to Karthwasten in Last Seed. The Silver-Blood factor says Forsworn took the cart at Bruca's Leap.

But Ragnar's knife came back to me. A guard sold it in the market, and he would not say where he got it. If the Forsworn took my husband, why does a city guard have his knife? Give me the courage to ask that question louder, Lady, or give me the sense to stop asking it.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth.hook: The city of stone and silver, carved by the Dwemer into the cliffs above the Karth. Every coin here is stamped by the Silver-Bloods, and every secret is buried in Cidhna Mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth.rumour: Mind what you say in Markarth, friend. The walls are Dwarven and the ears are Silver-Blood, and both of them remember everything.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth.sk4_note_2: Folio #3 (-3102, -191): Field inspection recorded for Markarth within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.markarth.smelter_le:
#Week of the 3rd, Hearthfire, 4E 201
Ingots from Cidhna: 46.
Ingots from Left Hand Mine: 19.
Ingots from Karthwasten (by cart): 31, should be 44. Cart three never arrived. Driver's widow asks for his wages. Thonar says no wages for undelivered ore.

#Week of the 10th
Cidhna: 51. Left Hand: 17, Skaggi complains of spiders in the lower drift.
Kolskeggr: none. Kolskeggr is never anything anymore.
Note to self: when Master asks why the scales read light, do NOT say 'because the Silver-Bloods take a pinch'. Last apprentice said it. Last apprentice is in Cidhna now.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth_stables.ca:
CARRIAGE TO WHITERUN: leaves at dawn, Morndas and Fredas. 20 septims. Driver not responsible for Forsworn.
WANTED: escort for silver wagon to Karthwasten. Pay good. Ask at the Silver-Blood Inn. Do NOT ask what happened to the last escort.
LOST: grey mare, white socks, answers to Hilde. Went north toward Ragnvald on her own. Horses have more sense than men, usually.
Scrawled at the bottom: Has anyone seen Eirik Hollow-Voice? Went to Ragnvald on the 2nd of Hearthfire with two hired diggers. The diggers came back. Ask Dagny at the stable.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth_stables.ho: The last stop before the gates of Markarth, where carters water their horses and swap stories about the road. Most of the stories this year are about Ragnvald.
place_lore.nirncraft.markarth_stables.ru: Ask the stablehand at Markarth Stables about her brother. Then buy her a drink. He went up to Ragnvald for treasure and the treasure kept him.

place_lore.nirncraft.meekos_shack.hermit:
Brother,
You will have heard I left the city. You will have heard why, I expect, and I won't argue it in a letter. I live in the woods now with a dog who has no opinions about me, which is restful.

I have been coughing since the first snow. The dog sleeps against my chest at night, and it helps, or I tell myself it does. If anything happens, I would like you to come and take him. He eats anything, he hates rabbits personally, and he will sit by the door until someone tells him otherwise. Someone should tell him. I don't think I'll be able to.
place_lore.nirncraft.meekos_shack.hook: A tumbledown hut in the wooded hills between Haafingar and Hjaalmarch. Its owner is long dead, but his dog still waits by the door for someone to come home.
place_lore.nirncraft.meekos_shack.rumour: There's a dog that lives at a shack out past the sawmill, all on its own. The hunters throw it scraps. It won't leave. Loyal beast. Better than most men I know.
place_lore.nirncraft.mehrunes_spite.hook: A red-spired fortress of Dagon's cult with lava channels around a central court, spike gardens and a ritual hall under a brazier-crown.
place_lore.nirncraft.mehrunes_spite.rumo: A red fortress on the Auridon cliffs has a hall where a crystal hums. The cult say it is the future. The grove says otherwise.
Break the glass in the heart of the world and let the new light in. Break the heart in the glass of the world and let the old night out. We are the splinters, we are the sharp, we are the ones who do not sleep. Let the grove sing us, let the sea receive us, let the seed be sown.

place_lore.nirncraft.merryfair_farm.hook: A tidy Black-Briar farm just west of Riften's stables, kept by a hired Dunmer mage who keeps the crops growing and the questions to a minimum.
place_lore.nirncraft.merryfair_farm.rumo: Merryfair always gets its harvest in on time and never pays the road toll. Funny, that. Owner's name starts with B and ends with an empty purse for everyone else.

place_lore.nirncraft.merryfair_farm.ston:
#14th of Frostfall
The frost came down off the Velothi hills two weeks early. The north rows held. The south rows did not. I have tried a warming ward drawn in the soil, the kind my mother used on the ash farms near Kragenmoor. It works, but it drinks magicka like a Nord drinks mead.

#16th of Frostfall
Maven's man came by asking why the yield is down. I explained frost. He explained that frost is not the Lady's concern. I will try the ward again tonight and pray to Mephala that nobody asks me to explain the weather twice.

place_lore.nirncraft.mire_song_burrow.ci:
#Drawn
Night one: one hand. Night two: one hand. Night three: one hand and a half. The trader pays by the barrel and does not ask. The valve is cracked and weeps at the seam; we have packed it with clay and prayed.

If the keeper finds the pipe, run. If the keeper finds the cistern, run faster.
place_lore.nirncraft.mire_song_burrow.ho: A burrow beneath the dry plateau where a hidden cistern sings softly, and the singing has lately drawn thieves.
place_lore.nirncraft.mire_song_burrow.ru: Water has been drawn from the Basin Well at night, a hand a night, for three nights. The well-keeper says there is a second pipe, and a cistern, and a song in the dark that does not come from a throat.
place_lore.nirncraft.miscarcand.hook: A buried Ayleid city-vault of lit welkynd stone, tiered cisterns and bridges over drowned galleries.
place_lore.nirncraft.miscarcand.rumour: Miscarcand's gate lamps burn blue when a name is read, and some say the dead there are waiting to be asked.
place_lore.nirncraft.miscarcand.thread.p: To Aelwyn at the Tower. Two stones lit and the vault at Miscarcand is awake: do not let the Warden count the names while the lamps are new. I have left a seal on the lintel. We proceed to Ne Salas. The dead are listening; keep your voice level.
place_lore.nirncraft.miscarcand.web.p0: HERE LIES THE ACCOUNT OF THE UNNUMBERED. Whoever takes a plate takes a person. Whoever restores a plate restores a debt. The Warden counts, and the count will not be closed by force, only by name.
place_lore.nirncraft.missamsi.hook: A corrupted ashland sanctum of blighted stone and red crystal growths, descending through ash-choked halls to a pulsing chamber.
place_lore.nirncraft.missamsi.rumour: Something under Missamsi is still keeping a bed warm. Stay out of the ash after dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.missamsi.web.author: Neloth Ulven
place_lore.nirncraft.missamsi.web.p0: Eighth night. They come to us now unbidden and lie down in the ash as quietly as children. The Voice does not speak but the crystals hum in our teeth. It does not want worship, it wants us to stay. I think it is lonely. When I told the others, they laughed. I have started to dream of rooms with no doors.
A hidden waterfall pool in the Nibenay valley that mirrors a different night sky from the one overhead, ringed in cut stones under the water.
The pool at Mist Mirror shows the wrong stars. I do not go at night, and I do not go alone.

~Water lies still and the stars come down,~not ours, not ours, but some old town.~Each star a name, each name a flame,~each flame put out by a man who came.~Say it not aloud, say it not twice,~the pool will give you your price.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistveil_village.ho: A fishing village of stilt-houses and pearl-rakes on a misted Pyandonean inlet, where the Maormer poor live with the tide, the gulls and the endless threat of a fleet that does not care.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistveil_village.pe:
#THIS SEASON
Forty pearls, of which nine were round, three were black and one was a very small, very bright thing that I did not give the fleet. I sewed it into the hem of my daughter's dress. It is the only wealth of this house.
The fleet-tax is thirty. I told them forty-one. I told them I had given the fleet its due. They believed me. It is the first lie I have told in ten years, and the best.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistveil_village.ru: The people of Mistveil say they are quiet because the mist takes the sound. The mist, for its part, says nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistwatch.hook: A tall stone tower south of the Atronach Stone, seized by bandits who watch the Darkwater ore road from its top and know, somehow, exactly which cart carries gold.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistwatch.mage_cach: I was meditating at the Atronach Stone when these brutes came down from the tower. They took my purse, my robe and my dignity, in that order. They did not take what matters.

My soul gems and my coin are buried in a sealed pot, a dozen paces south of the Stone, where the snow never settles because the ground is warm. If I am still their 'guest' by the time anyone reads this, take what you find and spend some of it on getting me out.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistwatch.rumour: Mistwatch bandits only ever take the gold carts from Darkwater Crossing. Never the iron, never the empties. That's not luck. That's somebody talking.
place_lore.nirncraft.mistwatch.toll_tall:
#Payments to our friend at the Crossing
9th of Hearthfire: 30 septims for word of the gold cart. Gold taken: 2 loads.
1st of Frostfall: 40 septims, he asked for more. Gold taken: 3 loads.
16th of Frostfall: no word sent. Cart came through with a spear on it. Our friend is getting nervous.
Our friend signs himself 'E.' Whoever he is, he lives close enough to the Goldenrock Mine to know which day the ore is weighed, and he wants his coin left under the third stone of the ford post.
Note: if E. grows a conscience, we sell his name to the mine. That way we get paid twice.
place_lore.nirncraft.mixwater_mill.giant: For the death of the one-tusked giant of Broken Limb Camp, who on the 14th of Frostfall came down to the river road, smashed two log carts flat, and threw a yoke of oxen into the water like they were apples.
Proof required: the giant's club or its toes, whichever you can carry. Payment on delivery, in coin, from me, Gralfr, at the mill. No questions asked about how. None answered about why.
Scrawled beneath in another hand, by someone who did not sign: 'Ask Gralfr where he sold the little tusks. Ask Sten why he drinks alone now.'
place_lore.nirncraft.mixwater_mill.hook: A lumber mill where the White River's two streams meet, its saws running all day and its carters muttering about the giants of Broken Limb Camp just over the rise.
place_lore.nirncraft.mixwater_mill.rumou: Mixwater Mill pays well for anyone who'll sort out the giant at Broken Limb Camp. Funny how the foreman never says what started it.
place_lore.nirncraft.mixwater_mill.sk4_n: Folio #4 (1414, -15): Field inspection recorded for Mixwater Mill within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #4 for mixwater_mill: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Mixwater Mill are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.mixwater_mill.torva:
Steward,
My brother Ulmir was taken from this mill on the 2nd of Frostfall by men in silver-buckled leathers who called him a beast and a murderer. They had no warrant and no Jarl's seal. They had chains, and they knew how to use them.

They have taken him to Gallows Rock, the old fort west of here where your grandfather's grandfather hanged traitors. I have heard screaming from that ridge at night. I am told it is not always a man's voice. I do not care whose voice it is. He is my brother.
I have asked the guards. I have asked the priests. Now I am asking you, and after you I will ask anyone with a blade.
place_lore.nirncraft.moesring_pass.hook: The high road over the Moesring mountains, the only way between the island's ash-grey south and its frozen north for anyone without wings. It is narrow, windy, and watched.
place_lore.nirncraft.moesring_pass.porte: Painted on a slab at the narrowest point, in Cyrodilic and in Skaal runes both: North lies the snow, south lies the ash. The wind changes at noon. Walk with your shoulder to the mountain. Do not stop here to look at the view of Mount Moesring; the view does not care for you. Three porters, one Telvanni apprentice, and a goat have taught us this. The goat survived.

Beneath it someone has added, with a knife: Also do not stop to look at the bones in the ravine. They are mostly goat. Mostly. If you hear rocks falling above you, that is not the wind either. That is rieklings, and they think it is very funny.
place_lore.nirncraft.moesring_pass.rumou: Take Moesring Pass in the morning, never at dusk. The wind up there pushes. A Company porter went over the edge last Last Seed, pack and all. They found the pack.

place_lore.nirncraft.moiras_hope.hook: A tiny shrine hamlet on a moor-edge, with a single prayer-stone ringed in candle-ends and a bell that does not ring.
place_lore.nirncraft.moiras_hope.rumour: At Moira's Hope the villagers light a candle for each who says yes to the fog.
place_lore.nirncraft.moiras_hope.web.p0: Lady of hope, hold my lantern. I said I would not go, and then I did, and then I could not tell you which way is back. If the fog sings tonight, do not let me answer. If the fog asks, let me remember I have a name.
place_lore.nirncraft.molag_mar.gazetteer:
#Who keeps the heat
Warden Ilu Dren keeps the canton lift: three bells down, three bells up, no exceptions. Dren the Lavacutter has cut glass for twenty years and never looked at it straight. Sister Mavia collects the ashes the living leave behind and plants lilies with them. Kesha-Teb sells glass and obsidian, and not-recently-cursed jewellery.

#The Cinder Cup
Orvyn Hlaalo's inn charges for the cooling; it is a joke his father made, and he inherited. A Redoran inspector wants it banned. A Hlaalu competitor wants it franchised. Both will be invited to soup.
place_lore.nirncraft.molag_mar.hook: A cliff-cut town with a lava-lit grotto at its heart, red light and black stone from far off, where the cooling is charged by the cup.
place_lore.nirncraft.molag_mar.rumour: A heat-vent failed in the Underworks last night and the channel ran twenty degrees over. Warden Ilu says nobody died. The Lavacutter says nobody has, yet.
place_lore.nirncraft.molag_mar.vent_noti:
^BY ORDER OF THE CANTON
The lower station closes at the third bell after any vent alarm. No exceptions for weather, kings or prayer. Do not touch the glass. Do not look at it straight. If you hear the pool hiss, climb.

place_lore.nirncraft.moldering_ruins.dra:
^ODVAR BRONZE-CROWN
^WHO WATCHED THE WEST

He watched for the Reachmen from this hill for sixty years, and when he died his people sat him on the stone so that he might keep watching. They closed the door upon him with his eyes open. Do not close his eyes. He has not finished watching.

Scratched beside it in charcoal, recently, by an unsteady hand: 'Agnar, if you ever come back here, his eyes follow you. They do. I saw them move. Don't look at the chair. Get your knife and don't look at the chair.' The rest of the charcoal has been smeared, as if by a sleeve dragged across it in a hurry.
place_lore.nirncraft.moldering_ruins.hoo: A collapsed Nordic ruin on the western edge of the Tundra, half buried in turf and mould. The farmers of Rorikstead give it a wide berth, and their sheep refuse to graze near it.
place_lore.nirncraft.moldering_ruins.rum: The Moldering Ruins? Lemkil's sheep won't go within a bowshot of them. Smart sheep. There's a cold comes out of that place even in Sun's Height.
place_lore.nirncraft.moldering_ruins.she:
To anyone who finds this by the ruins:
My little brother Agnar came here looking for a lost lamb on the 4th of Sun's Height. He came home white as milk and has not spoken a whole sentence since. He keeps drawing the same thing: a man with a crown of bronze, sitting on a stone chair, with his eyes open.

Agnar dropped his knife in there, the one Father gave him. He cries for it in his sleep. I think if it came back, some of him would come back with it.

I cannot go in. I am all Mother has left who can work the field. If you are braver than me, bring the knife to Rorikstead and ask for Svala.

place_lore.nirncraft.moon_sugar_meadow.h:
^PICK ONLY WHAT THE MOONS HAVE KISSED.
^LEAVE THE REST FOR THE NEXT NIGHT.
^NEVER PICK TWICE FROM THE SAME STEM, FOR THE STEM WILL SULK, AND A SULKING STEM BEARS NO SUGAR FOR A YEAR.
A meadow of pale flowers that glow faintly at night and ripen into the finest moon-sugar only on the one night when both moons are full.
place_lore.nirncraft.moon_sugar_meadow.r: You can smell the meadow from a mile off on the right night. They say it smells like a sweet thing you once forgot, and are glad to remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.moot_of_the_five_hu: A ring of tall standing stones on the Atmoran ice where the five hundred skalds of the first ships met, once, to decide whether to cross the sea.

^FIVE HUNDRED SPOKE. TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY-NINE SAID STAY.
^TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY-ONE SAID GO.
^TWO SKALDS ABSTAINED, AND ARE NOT NAMED.
Beneath, much later, in a very fine hand: 'The two who abstained went last, and wept the most, and never said which way they would have voted. It is the only secret the First Ships kept.'
The Moot stones are said to hold their last argument still. On a still night you can hear the vote. It was close.
place_lore.nirncraft.mor_khazgur.hook: A hard Orc stronghold in the Druadach foothills, where the chief keeps his own laws and his own debts. Its hunters range as far as the black mouth of Darkfall Cave.
place_lore.nirncraft.mor_khazgur.hunters:
Seven notches: elk, the north meadow.
Three notches: sabre cat, by the falls. One of them nearly had Durz.
One long cut: Durz went into Darkfall Cave after the wounded bear. I told him a wounded bear in a dark hole is the bear's luck, not ours. He went anyway. That was eleven days ago.
No more notches after that. Bashnag doesn't hunt until his brother comes back, or until he knows what in that cave took him. The chief calls it pride. The chief is right.
place_lore.nirncraft.mor_khazgur.rumour: The Mor Khazgur hunters lost one of their own in Darkfall Cave. Orcs don't usually ask outsiders for anything. They're asking now.

place_lore.nirncraft.morkul_stronghold_h: A small Orc palisade in the Wrothgarian foothills with forges roaring and a hide-covered stone at its gate.
At Morkul they carve no name on the stone, and yet one appears each dusk. The smith won't speak of it.

Do not read the stone. If you read a name you know, say nothing. The date is nine days. If a name is yours, go to the Paragon's column before the date and ask who carved it. Do not tell your clan. They will try to stop it with spears.

place_lore.nirncraft.morthal.brynja_lett:
Kolbjorn,
Geirlund went out to check his traps on the 12th and did not come home. His bow was found by the path to the old cave north-east of town, the one the hunters call Movarth's Lair. The guards say a bear. A bear does not leave a bow so neatly, strung and set down, as if a man had been asked to.

The Jarl's men won't go in. They say the cave is old trouble and they have new trouble enough. Falion told me, kindly, that I should stop hoping. I have not stopped. I've started sharpening Geirlund's old silver knife. If you love me, send coin for a mercenary. If you can't, send prayers to Arkay. I'll take either.
place_lore.nirncraft.morthal.fogwife_ver: Old Grelka, as written down by her granddaughter

~Salt on the sill and iron at the door,
~Garlic by the cradle and ash upon the floor.
~If it knocks three times, it's a friend come late.
~If it knocks four times, let it wait.

~If it calls your name in your mother's voice,
~Bite your thumb and make no choice.
~If it shows a light upon the marsh,
~Close your eyes, though the dark is harsh.
^Grandmother swore by these. She lived to ninety-one, and never once went out after dark. Or so she said.
place_lore.nirncraft.morthal.highmoon_no: Thorvar Mist-Eye, Steward to the Jarl

By order of Jarl Idgrod Ravencrone:
Until further notice, no one is to leave the town walls between dusk and dawn without leave of the guard. This includes fishing, wood-gathering, courting and the fetching of wandering goats.

The patrol sent to Fort Snowhawk on the 8th of Frostfall has not returned. Anyone with knowledge of Guardsman Sten, Guardsman Ofrid or Guardsman Hallgerd is asked to come to Highmoon Hall at once. The Jarl does not want rumours. The Jarl wants her guards back.
place_lore.nirncraft.morthal.hook: The capital of Hjaalmarch, a town of wet timber and closed shutters in the heart of the fog-bound marsh. Its Jarl sees visions, its wizard is feared, and its people do not go out after dark.
place_lore.nirncraft.morthal.rumour: Morthal's a fine place if you like mist, mudcrabs and neighbours who stare. Mind you, after dark even the neighbours stay in. There's a reason for that, and nobody'll tell you what it is.
place_lore.nirncraft.mortrag_peak.glacie: Skjald the Elder, as told to a Raven Rock scribe

In my grandmother's grandmother's time the moon bled and a great hunt was called across Solstheim. The prey was a mortal, and the hunters were not. They raced across this glacier and down into the halls beneath it, and where they fought the ice cracked, and where it cracked it swallowed.

We still find them sometimes, when the summer is long. A hand in the ice. A spear. Once a wolf with a man's eyes, frozen in mid-leap. We leave them where they are. The All-Maker gave the ice to keep them, and who are we to open a gift that was not given to us?
place_lore.nirncraft.mortrag_peak.hook: A crown of rock and glacier in the north, above Castle Karstaag. In the last age the Huntsman's prey was hunted across this ice, and the hunters say the ice has not forgotten.
place_lore.nirncraft.mortrag_peak.rumour: Mortrag Peak is where it all ended the year the moon went red. The old Skaal won't say what happened. They'll only say the glacier ate a lot of hunters.

place_lore.nirncraft.morvunskar.college_:
To Ralis Varvel, wherever you have gone,
The Arch-Mage has instructed me to remind you that your expulsion was not a misunderstanding, that your notes on 'tethered summoning' remain confiscated, and that taking apprentices outside the College does not make you a teacher.

If the young woman named Elsbet is with you, she is to be returned to Winterhold before the snows close the road. Master Tolfdir has asked me to add that he remembers her fondly, and that he remembers you somewhat less so.
place_lore.nirncraft.morvunskar.conjurer:
#Observation the ninth
The spring under the north tower is not volcanic, as the vulgar suppose. Its heat rises and falls with the moons. I propose that the boundary between Nirn and the Deadlands is thinner here than at any point in Eastmarch.

#Observation the twelfth
A flame atronach summoned within six paces of the spring persists for nearly twice the expected duration. The girl, Elsbet, objects to the 'tethering' I propose. She objects to a great deal for an apprentice.

#Observation the fifteenth
The tethering requires a living anchor of some talent. Elsbet has some talent. She will thank me when she understands.
place_lore.nirncraft.morvunskar.elsbet_j:
#Sun's Height
Master Varvel says the College is too timid to teach what I need. He says it with such certainty that I believed him for nearly two months.

#Hearthfire
He has started locking the lower door at night. He keeps asking how far I can reach with my mind toward the spring, and writing down the answers.

#Frostfall
I have hidden my copy of his notes in the chest by the stair. If I am chained in the cellar by the time anyone finds this, then I was right, and I would have very much liked to be wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.morvunskar.hook: A fort of three squat towers north-west of Kynesgrove, held now by mages who came to study the hot springs beneath it and stayed to study things a good deal hotter.
place_lore.nirncraft.morvunskar.rumour: Mages at Morvunskar. Not the friendly College kind. A girl from Winterhold went there to learn conjuration and her letters stopped coming.

To any hunter who follows game into this cavern: the deer are bait. The moss is bait. The light is bait. Everything in here that looks soft and easy has been put here for you by something that has been patient for longer than Falkreath has had a wall.
If you must go in, bring fire, and do not touch the roots.

The arrow that pins the note is fletched with raven feathers, Hunter's Rest work. Scratched along the shaft in tiny letters: 'Hroa, if you come back out and find this, I went in too. Wait for me at the cabin. Don't come in after me. One of us has to keep the fire. A.'
A deep, damp cavern in the western woods carpeted in moss and lit by fungus, home to an old spriggan that hunters call the Moss Mother. Her children are never far.

A notched stick, each notch carefully labelled in tiny runes:
Stag, wounded high, followed in. Blood on the moss.
Two spriggans, small. Went round them.
Bones by the pool, man and elk together, roots grown through both.

Last notch, cut deeper than the rest:
The old one sits at the back. Big as a tree. Moss falls off her like a cloak. She is not angry. She is looking at me the way I look at a deer before the arrow. Asvald, I am sorry. Keep the fire going.
Hroa from Hunter's Rest went into Moss Mother Cavern after a stag she'd wounded. Her brother waited a week at the cabin. The stag came out. Hroa didn't.

place_lore.nirncraft.motalion_necropolis: A tiered necropolis cut into a cliff, crowded with sarcophagus niches and a lightless stair.
The necropolis at Motalion has a cold wind that blows out of the empty niche.

Eleven heralds are laid in niches. The twelfth niche stands open. The twelfth has not died but does not live. The twelfth carries the king's bell and rings it at each oasis at dawn. It is not to be spoken to. It will not answer, but it will remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_anthor.hook: A high peak south of the Sightless Pit, crowned by an ancient word wall. A dragon has taken the summit, and the shepherds of the valleys below are losing more than sheep.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_anthor.rumour: Mount Anthor has a dragon on it now. Big grey one. Sits on the old wall like it's reading the words. Maybe it is.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_anthor.shephe:
Flock at Midyear: 64. At Last Seed: 51. At Hearthfire: 39. At Frostfall: 22.
The dragon takes them two at a time, one in each foot. It flies back to the mountain and lands on the wall with the old writing. Then it sings. It is not a song. I do not know what it is.

My son wants to go up and fight it with his grandfather's axe. He is fifteen. I have hidden the axe under the floor. If someone who has killed a dragon before comes by, Kyne send them to us before my boy finds the axe.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_anthor.sk4_no: Folio #25 (1194, -1184): Field inspection recorded for Mount Anthor within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.mount_anthor.wall_r: Waymark 31: Mount Anthor. A word wall of the old dragon cult, near the summit, cut in the claw-script. I could make out perhaps one word in five. One of them repeats: a word the Greybeards say means 'frost'.
I took a rubbing and climbed down fast, because the wall was warm under my hand on a morning cold enough to crack teeth. Something had been lying against it recently. Something large.
Dragon sightings over Mount Anthor: three in Hearthfire, five in Frostfall. Shepherds' losses mounting. I recommend avoiding the peak entirely, a recommendation I am aware I have just ignored.

place_lore.nirncraft.mount_moesring.hook: The great grey mountain at the island's heart, split by the Moesring Pass. Ash drifts on its southern slopes and snow on its northern, and on the summit they meet.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_moesring.rumo: From the top of Mount Moesring you can see Red Mountain smoking across the sea. My mother says the mountain is looking back at us, the way it did in the Red Year.
place_lore.nirncraft.mount_moesring.summ:
#8th of Last Seed
Climbed on my day of leave. South, the island is black and grey to the shore, and beyond the water Red Mountain is still smoking, as if it had only just done the thing it did. North, everything is white. Up here the ash falls into the snow and makes it look like a ledger with too many entries.

I thought about my grandfather, who left Vvardenfell the year the sky fell, and about how far a person can run and still see the thing behind them. I left a stone for him at the top. Then I walked down to Raven Rock and took the night watch, because that is what we do.
place_lore.nirncraft.mournhold.council_n: Clerk of the Grand Council of Morrowind

^By the Grand Council, in session at Mournhold
It is resolved that the southern border with the so-called Kingdom of Argonia shall be patrolled by levies of the Great Houses in rotation. House Redoran in Morning Star and Sun's Dawn. House Indoril in First Seed and Rain's Hand. House Hlaalu...

...House Hlaalu, having declined to name a month, is assigned all the remaining months by default, until such time as it learns to attend council.
It is further resolved that the Twilight Stone of Deshaan, taken from the shrine of the Lady Azura in the border raids of 4E 158, remains a matter of honour for every House, and that a reward stands for its return. The reward has stood for forty-three years.
place_lore.nirncraft.mournhold.garden_le:
Uvren,
The new stone in the lower city is pale. It looks like a scar on the old black. The masters say it will darken with ash in thirty years. I don't want to wait thirty years. I want it to look like home now.

Priestess Ilvari came through the gardens this evening and stood by the south wall till the sun was gone. I asked her what she was looking at. She said 'something of the Lady's, in the hands of something that isn't'. Then she gave me a twilight rose to plant. It took. It's the only thing this season that has.
place_lore.nirncraft.mournhold.gazetteer:
#Names worth knowing
Archcanon Teris Ulvani receives visitors in the temple courtyard and asks for nothing. Mistress Hlaren runs the Great Bazaar's guild stall and stamps contracts. Old Sedyn leads a lantern into Old Mournhold every Sundas and has never been lost. Gaela Nelvan serves cold tea at the Silver Samovar whenever someone is listening.

#What the guide does not say
The Silver Samovar's back table is where deals are made. Orlen Veloth's smithy opens when he has stopped shouting at the anvil. Ravos Dren is a student of public architecture; keep your purse in your hand. The palace archive has a second basement. We have all agreed that it does not.
place_lore.nirncraft.mournhold.hook: The capital of Morrowind, a city of domes and gardens in the Deshaan where the Grand Council meets, the Temple keeps its old splendour, and the scars of the Argonian border wars are hidden under fresh paint.
place_lore.nirncraft.mournhold.rumour: Mournhold's grand again, if you don't look too close. The Argonians burned the lower city in the last border war. We rebuilt it in stone. Priestess Ilvari still looks south every evening, toward what they took.

place_lore.nirncraft.movarths_lair.geirl: I can't tell how many days. They let me write because the woman says my handwriting is pretty. She calls herself Vessa. She is pale as the inside of a shell and she keeps my wedding ring on a string round her neck and touches it while she feeds.

She says she was a farm girl from near Dragon Bridge, once. She says the master of this cave turned her and left her, and now she's turning others so she won't be alone. She asked if I wanted to stay. I said I have a wife. She laughed and said, so did the master, once.
Brynja. Don't come. Send someone with fire.
place_lore.nirncraft.movarths_lair.hook: A cave in the marsh north-east of Morthal, named for an old vampire whose name the townsfolk still won't say indoors. Hunters who go near it leave their bows behind, neatly strung.
place_lore.nirncraft.movarths_lair.rumou: Nobody goes near Movarth's Lair. Nobody. Brynja's husband went past it to check his traps and now she's walking around town with a silver knife, asking for help. Don't help her. Pray for her.
place_lore.nirncraft.movarths_lair.vessa:
Master,
You left me this cave and three thralls who are no company. I have added a hunter. He is strong and he talks about his wife, which I find soothing in the way rain is soothing.

You told me the Morthal folk would never come. You told me Idgrod sees but does not act. You told me a great many things before you went away. I am beginning to believe you did not go away for my sake.
When you return, I will be stronger. When you do not return, I will be stronger still.

place_lore.nirncraft.mthartzel.thread.p0: DIAL SIX. PRESSURE: NIL. TIME: UNTIL. The pump is no longer the first concern of this hall. The hall exists for the dial. If the dial reaches its mark, every pump will cease at once and every door will open. Let it reach its mark. Let us be recalled.
place_lore.nirncraft.mthartzel.web.p0: Pump One draws from the Lower Cavern at forty gallons a bell. The Direnni asked for a thing that could weep; we built it, and ran it dry. It must be fed. It must be fed. Do not close the valve while the giant still thirsts.

^Spring clutch, the village of the Bent Hist
Eggs laid: forty-one. Eggs hatched: thirty-three. Eggs that sleep and will not hatch: three. Eggs taken by thieves in the night: five.
Tah-Weesh says: the thieves took the five best. They knew which ones. Someone told them.

The Bright-Throat clan says it was the Archeins. The Archeins say it was the Bright-Throats. Tah-Weesh says it was a foreigner who paid someone in this village with Imperial silver. Tah-Weesh says: when I find who, the Hist will remember them, but I will not.
#The people
Elder Nulaa keeps the fire in the middle of the spiral. Hunter Teek hunts in silence and has found that most things can wait. Rice-Mother Mussa grows three crops a year and says you are too thin. Pip is a child, and talks more than the rest together.

#The path
Every child walks the spiral once and brings a coal back to their own door. You do not speak. You do not drop the coal. Nobody tells what the fire said. The north paddy had a frog in a noble's collar; the scarecrow wears it now.
place_lore.nirncraft.murkmire.hook: A cluster of Saxhleel villages deep in the southern marsh, where the paths shift with the water, egg-thieves raid the hatcheries, and every village keeps its memory in a single chosen child.
place_lore.nirncraft.murkmire.rumour: Murkmire's the true marsh. Tah-Weesh the Egg-Keeper's been robbed again, and the Archeins and the Bright-Throats are feuding over a canoe. Go with a guide or don't go at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.murkmire.travellers:
Dear Society,
I have mapped the path from Lilmoth to Murkmire four times. It has been a different path each time. My guide says the path did not change; I did. I have asked him to clarify. He says I will understand when I hatch.

I enclose all four maps. Please file them together under 'Murkmire, approaches, provisional'. Please do not send another cartographer. Please do send boots. Mine have been adopted by a family of frogs, and the village elders say it would be rude to reclaim them.

place_lore.nirncraft.mzinchaleft.college: The plaque above the second door appears to be a work schedule(1). Its final line, which I render with some hesitation, reads: 'Lift to the deep works shall run until the Lowest Door is sealed, or until the Tonal Architects declare otherwise.'(2)

(1) The Dwemer, like the Imperial bureaucracy, were never happier than when timing something.
(2) The Lowest Door is presumably the Great Lift, south of here, which descends into the dark beneath Skyrim. I note that nobody ever declared otherwise. The lift is therefore, by its own reckoning, still on shift.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzinchaleft.hook: A Dwemer city half-buried in the snowy hills of eastern Hjaalmarch, its brass pipes still steaming. Miners from Stonehills went in after metal. The Falmer below were waiting.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzinchaleft.knud_jo:
#5th of Frostfall
We're through the first great door. Brass everywhere. Sigrun will be rich and unbearable. The spiders made of metal came at us in the second hall; we broke two with picks. Hrodulf took a bite. He's walking.

#7th of Frostfall
The Falmer came up from below. They don't need light. Olaf and Grim went down screaming. We hid in the lift-house. Hrodulf ran for it. I gave him my token for Sigrun, in case.
#8th of Frostfall
I can hear them in the pipes. I'm going to try for the door. If I don't make it, tell my sister the east tunnel at Rockwallow comes out here, and she should brick it up tonight.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzinchaleft.rumour: Mzinchaleft is full of Dwemer metal, and Dwemer metal is full of money. That's what Sigrun's crew thought. The ones who went in are still in there, and the money's still there too.
