place_lore.nirncraft.mzulft.falmer_shrin: Crude marks gouged into the brass by claws or bone knives, beside a translation chalked by a careful scholar's hand:
'The singers below took our eyes. Now we take theirs. The brass is ours. The warm halls are ours. The sound in the deep is our god's voice and it is hungry.'
And under the translation, the scholar's own note: 'They have built their shrine against the resonance pipes. They believe the hum is a god. I am no longer certain they are wrong.'
place_lore.nirncraft.mzulft.hook: A Dwemer ruin in the steaming hills south-east of Kynesgrove, its brass domes still warm from the machines below, where scholars come to study the Oculory and the Falmer come to feed on the scholars.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzulft.rumour: Mzulft? Scholars go in, Falmer come out. There's a Breton fellow from the Geographical Society asking about his partner who went down in Hearthfire. I didn't have the heart to tell him.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzulft.society_lett:
Livia,
I write this not knowing whether it will reach you. I was taken on the road by bandits who live in the Uttering Hills; I bought my freedom with my map and my boots. The map I can redraw. You I cannot.

If you find this, come out by the south door and walk north to Kynesgrove. I will be at the Braidwood Inn every evening until the snows close the road, and then, Mara help me, I will come in after you.
place_lore.nirncraft.mzulft.survey_journ:
#3rd of Hearthfire
Entered Mzulft by the south door. Bertrand stayed behind to finish his map of the approaches. He says I am too eager. I say a ruin that has waited four thousand years can wait while he sketches, but I cannot.

#5th of Hearthfire
The lower halls are warm and dry. The machines are dormant, mostly. I have taken a rubbing of the great resonance plate in the boiler hall: the Dwemer script on it speaks of 'tuning the earth', which I take to be poetic.

#8th of Hearthfire
Not poetic. Something tuned. Something is answering. I have heard footsteps and seen no one. I am going down once more for the plate itself and then I will go home to Bertrand and let him say he told me so.

place_lore.nirncraft.narzulbur.chief_tal:
#Frostfall
Ebony out of Gloombound: 11 bars this moon. Last moon: 18. The moon before: 20.
Why the drop: miners won't work the deep east drift. Dushgar says the dark there eats lantern-light. Dushgar has never been afraid of anything, so the chief broke his nose for saying it.

#Later
Dushgar went back down to prove he was brave. Dushgar did not come back up. The chief has stopped breaking noses. That is how we know it is bad.
Trade for the moon: 4 bars to the Windhelm smith, 2 to the Kynesgrove tinker, 1 kept for Malacath's altar. The rest is spoken for, by blood.
place_lore.nirncraft.narzulbur.hook: An Orc stronghold sunk into the hills east of Kynesgrove, rich in ebony from Gloombound Mine and closed to outsiders who have not earned the chief's leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.narzulbur.rumour: The Orcs of Narzulbur will sell you ebony if you're polite, and break your arm if you're not. Lately they're short-tempered. Something's wrong in their mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.narzulbur.sk4_note_: Folio #5 (2224, -304): Field inspection recorded for Narzulbur within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #5 for narzulbur: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Narzulbur are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.narzulbur.wife_pray:
~Malacath, who keeps the oaths of the scorned,
~Keep the oath my husband swore to come home.
~He went down into Gloombound with a pick and a grudge.
~Send him up with both, or send me the one who kept him.

~I do not ask you for mercy. You have none and that is why we love you.
~I ask you for a debt to be paid.
~Let the dark in the east drift learn the weight of an Orc's anger,
~And if my arm is not enough, send me a stranger's.

place_lore.nirncraft.nchardak.hook: A great Dwemer ruin on the eastern coast, half drowned and still humming with steam. Treasure hunters, Telvanni scholars, and worse all have business in its flooded halls.
place_lore.nirncraft.nchardak.rumour: Nchardak's full of water and machines and books nobody should read. Master Neloth goes there sometimes. Comes back muttering. Everyone else who goes comes back wet, if they come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.nchardak.steam_warn: Burned into a brass plate fixed to the inner door, in elegant Telvanni script: This ruin is under the study of Master Neloth of Tel Mithryn. Removal of anything without the master's consent will be noticed. Being noticed by the master is not recommended. Being noticed twice is not survivable. This notice is the only one you will receive.
Scratched beneath the plate with a knife point, in Cyrodilic: Noted. Twice. Signed, a visitor who now has one ear fewer. And beneath that, burned neatly into the brass: Three times.
place_lore.nirncraft.nchardak.treasure_h:
#20th of Hearthfire
The water rises and falls in the great hall when you turn the cubes in the pedestals. Nobody told me that. Nobody told me the water has slaughterfish in it, either, four thousand years old and still hungry.

#22nd of Hearthfire
Found a sealed room at the heart of the ruin with a book on a lectern, and a Telvanni seal on the door that is much newer than the Dwemer stone around it. I did not open the book. I did not open the door. I have heard what happens to people who read the wrong books on this island. They go to sleep and walk somewhere, and they don't come back.

place_lore.nirncraft.ne_quin_al.hook: The ruined plateau city of the early Khajiit kings, its terraced streets half buried in drifted sand, its palace gate still standing alone against the sky.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_quin_al.rumour: Scholars come to Ne Quin-al to find the first writing of the Khajiit. The Khajiit who live nearby say the first writing is on their grandmothers' hands, and has no need of stone.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_quin_al.scholar_:
#Day nine
The sand is a fine beast, patient and clean. We have uncovered a flight of steps and a doorway that leads to a wall. The wall has a door painted on it. The door has a tiny door painted on it. I am beginning to suspect the first Kings had a sense of humour.
Day twelve. We broke the wall. Behind it, a hall of cats' paw-prints, thousands of them, pressed into clay, each different. The oldest census in Tamriel. We have not told the Mane.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_salas.hook: A tower-city underground, a spiral of ring galleries around a central crystal pillar, bright and cold.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_salas.rumour: Under the great tree is a second light, say the root-diggers, one that doesn't flicker.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_salas.thread.p0: Ne Salas: the pillar relit at the fourth bell. A tone rose from it that no instrument could name. The cabal agrees that the stones are one voice and that we have only the third note of nine. We go to the Reliquary, then to the ashes. Say nothing to the Order.
place_lore.nirncraft.ne_salas.web.p0: WHAT WE NAME, WE KEEP. WHAT WE KEEP, WE LIGHT. Each lamp burns a name and each name must be renewed. Let no keeper forget this, nor the one who tends the crown: a lamp unfed becomes a door.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.gazetteer.au: Mirele Sathil of the Pilgrims' Rest
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.gazetteer.p0:
#The living of the Row
Keeper Salvu hears the dead and passes on the polite ones. Elder Nerevi guards the Row and lets no outlander in without a guest list. Aldrin the Restless has dug four hundred graves and will not dig one more. Tadrik Ulvo sells shrouds, urns and sympathy cards, with no refunds.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.gazetteer.p1:
#Candles, counts and one small secret
The Pilgrims' Rest sets out forty-one candles each night and finds forty-two each morning. The extra belongs to a girl who never reached the shrine. Say her name aloud. It helps. Mind the third step of the Row; the elder's husband did.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.hook: The holy city of the dead on Morrowind's eastern coast, where every Dunmer family hopes to rest, pilgrims walk the bone-lined streets, and grave-robbers have begun to steal ancestors for Daedric rites.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.mortician_ap:
To any pilgrim, sellsword or Ordinator who reads this:
In the last month, eleven urns have been broken in the lower catacombs and the ashes carried off. Among them, the urn of Ancestor Llaren Indavel, who founded this mortuary and who has not been moved in seven hundred years.

We know where they go. The robbers sell to Daedra-worshippers, and they camp in the hollow by the Sheogorath shrine north-west of the city, because pilgrims will not walk that road. Recover Llaren's urn. Bring it to me at the mortuary. The rest of the dead will forgive us. Llaren will not, and he is not quiet when he is displeased.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.pilgrim_comp:
#Arrived Necrom
The city is bone-white and silent. The priests walk softly. A child asked me whose grandmother I had come to visit. I said mine. She said 'which one?' and pointed down. I did not sleep well.

#Second day
Laid Mother's ashes in the Ules alcove. The alcove was already full. The priest said 'they'll make room', and something below the floor shifted. I gave a larger donation than I had planned. I suspect that is how the mortuary is funded.
place_lore.nirncraft.necrom.rumour: Somebody's breaking urns in the City of the Dead and carrying the ashes off. The priests are frantic. Mortician Mirvala says the robbers camp near the Mad God's shrine, where pilgrims don't walk.

A fortified temple on the hill above Dawnstar, sealed for decades by an old order of priests. Some in town think whatever is giving them nightmares lives behind its doors.
That temple on the hill east of town has been locked since my grandmother's time. Lately, though, I swear I've seen candlelight in the high windows.

#Year unknown, the long siege
The Orcs are at the gate and the Brother-Prior has ordered the doors sealed from within. We will not let what sleeps in the lower vault fall into their hands. If we must sleep with it, so be it.

The Prior has lit the smoke. It is sweet, like burnt honey. He says it will keep us all asleep, defenders and attackers alike, until someone worthy comes to wake us.
I am afraid. I can feel the dream coming up the stairs. I can feel her smiling.

Folio #8 (328, -1722): Field inspection recorded for Nightcaller Temple within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #8 for nightcaller_temple: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Nightcaller Temple are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

To Jarl Skald, Lord of the Pale, from the undersigned who cannot sleep.
We ask that the temple on the hill be searched, or burned, or blessed, whichever the Jarl thinks wisest. Since Sun's Height not a soul in Dawnstar has had a night's rest. The mines are short of hands; the boats are short of crews.

Signed (or marked):
Thyra Gull-Wife, fisher.
Leif, sled-master at Iron-Breaker.
The smith.
A mark like a fish.
A mark like a hammer.
A mark like an open eye, which nobody will admit to making.
place_lore.nirncraft.nightgate_inn.hook: A lonely inn on the road between Windhelm and Dawnstar, warm and smoky, ringed by barrows, Dwemer ruins and the snow of the high Pale.
place_lore.nirncraft.nightgate_inn.inn_n:
TRAVELLERS, READ THIS BEFORE YOU ASK ME ANYTHING.
The road north to Dawnstar is open but the wolves are not shy.
The cave by Bronze Water is a bear's house. The bear is home.
Ironbind Barrow is not a shelter. The last party who used it for one is still there.

The big Dwemer lift east of here goes down. All the way down. Nobody who has ridden it has come back to tell me what's at the bottom, which tells me enough.
Forsaken Cave is called that for a reason.
Rooms are ten septims. Stew is free if you bring news.
place_lore.nirncraft.nightgate_inn.rumou: Nightgate Inn's the only fire for a day's walk in any direction. The innkeeper hears every tale on the road, and believes about half.
place_lore.nirncraft.nightgate_inn.sk4_n: Folio #4 (856, -848): Field inspection recorded for Nightgate Inn within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.nightingale_hall.ho: A cave in the wooded hills just south of Riften that the locals avoid without being able to say why. Thieves speak of it only in lowered voices, if at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.nightingale_hall.ru: That cave south of town? Don't. I'm not saying why. I'm just saying don't. And if a man in a dark hood asks you what you saw there, you saw nothing.

place_lore.nirncraft.nightingale_hall.th:
#Sun's Dusk, many years back
Old Mercer sent me to drop a parcel at the mouth of the cave south of the Shadow Stone. 'Drop it and don't look,' he said. I dropped it. I looked.

There was nobody there. The parcel was gone by the time I'd turned round. I never heard a footstep.

Bad luck has followed me ever since. Every lock jams, every mark wakes up. Brynjolf says it's because I looked. He was joking. I think.

If you're in the trade, a word of advice: pray to the Shadow Stone before a job, never at the cave. The cave doesn't listen to prayers. It listens to oaths.

place_lore.nirncraft.nilheim.hook: A crumbling Nord watchtower on the pass road east of Ivarstead, held by bandits who prey on pilgrims bound for the Seven Thousand Steps.
place_lore.nirncraft.nilheim.nilheim_ord: Lookouts, listen. We don't rob soldiers, Stormcloak or Legion. We don't rob anything with a Black-Briar seal. We rob pilgrims. Pilgrims don't fight, pilgrims carry their offerings, and pilgrims are too holy to go to the guard.

Last week's best catch: one brass bell, very old, rings sweet. The old fool who carried it wept like a child. I'll sell it in Riften once I find a fence who won't ask whose temple it's from.

Anyone caught ringing it for fun gets the other half of my hand on their face.
place_lore.nirncraft.nilheim.pilgrim_ple:
Divines forgive them, for I can't. My father carried that bell up the Steps when I was a boy and rang it at the top for my mother's soul. I meant to ring it for his. I'm eighty-one years old and I walked all the way from Riften and they took it from me in the time it takes to sneeze.

I'll wait at the Vilemyr Inn. If anyone brings it back, I'll ask the Greybeards to remember their name.
place_lore.nirncraft.nilheim.rumour: Nilheim's bandits rob the pilgrims going up to High Hrothgar. Takes a special sort of villain to rob a man on his way to pray.

place_lore.nirncraft.north_brittleshin_p: The northern mouth of a winding cave that cuts under the hills between Lake Ilinalta and the Whiterun plains, infested with skeevers and the bones of travellers who took the shortcut.

North mouth: forty-one skeevers by tail count. Paid two coppers apiece by the miller's wife, for the ones that come up into her grain.
They nest deep, in the bend where the pass dips under the stream. Bones there. Not all skeever. Somebody's buckle, a boot with the foot gone out of it.

Pass comes out at South Brittleshin, near the old drowned fort. Do NOT go through in spring. The water rises and the skeevers come up with it, all at once, like a carpet that bites. Lost my second-best trap that way and very nearly my second-best leg.
Brittleshin Pass saves you half a day if you're a skeever. If you're anything bigger, take the road.

place_lore.nirncraft.north_cold_rock_pas:
^TRAVELLER, ADD A STONE
This cairn was raised for Arngrim the drover, who was carried off in this pass in the winter of the year his son was born. We found his boots in the webs at the mouth of Brood Cavern, to the north-west, and nothing more.

Below, in fresher cuts: 'The webs are thicker this year. Keep to the middle of the road. Do not stop to look up.'

And lower still, in a child's hand: 'I added two stones. One for Arngrim. One for me.'
A narrow, wind-cut pass in the western hills where the road squeezes between two cliffs. Travellers leave stones on the cairn for luck, and webs gather in the cracks overhead.
Cold Rock Pass? Take it fast and take it in daylight. The spiders from Brood Cavern come down to hunt there when the frost bites hard.

place_lore.nirncraft.north_shriekwind_ba: The old chiefs of this valley were the brothers Hjalti and Eyvind, born the same night. Their father left one torc of gold and no word as to who should wear it. Hjalti took it by force. Eyvind took it back by guile. They fought until the clan was halved.

The elders buried them apart, Hjalti in the north barrow and Eyvind in the south, and buried the torc with neither. I set this down because the north barrow has begun to call for its brother, and I fear that a man who has shouted for three thousand years may soon decide to go and fetch him.

To the Captain of the Guard, Falkreath.
On my patrol of the north road on the night of the 11th of Frostfall, the wind from North Shriekwind Bastion was heard plainly at the town gate. I report that it was not wind. It said 'Eyvind' three times, clear as a man calling across a field, and then 'mine'.

I went up as far as the outer stones. The door stood open. Fresh tracks in the mud, made by bare feet that had been a long time without flesh. I did not go further, Captain, and I will not unless ordered, and I respectfully ask not to be ordered.
The northern of two ancient barrows above Falkreath, where the wind through the stones makes a sound like a man screaming. Lately it has been screaming words.
North Shriekwind's always howled. But Runil's been sleeping badly since the howl started saying a name. Nobody'll tell me whose.

place_lore.nirncraft.north_skybound_watc:
#22nd of Frostfall
I light the beacon every night now. My brother went out to Orphan Rock in Sun's Height to see the witches who live there, for a cure for his cough, and he has not come down. If he is wandering the hills, he will see the fire and come home.

#30th of Frostfall
A Stormcloak patrol from the camp below came up to tell me to put the fire out, because the Legion might think it a signal. I told them it is a signal. It says come home. They left me a little bread. I do not think they were bad men.
A crumbling Nordic watch post on the mountainside east of Riverwood, its stair cut into the cliff and its old beacon long cold. Someone has been lighting it again.

Worn letters on the topmost step, the kind of Nordic runes found on the oldest barrows:
'From here the sky is near and the enemy is far. Keep the fire, keep the watch, keep the pass. If the fire goes out, the valley will know why.'
Someone has carved beneath, much more recently: 'I am keeping it.'

Next to the old runes, scorched into the rock with a hot iron, is a small rough drawing: a figure on a tall spire of stone, another on a tower, and a line of dots running between them. The dots stop halfway. The drawing is recent, and whoever made it pressed so hard that the iron cracked the stone.
North Skybound Watch had a fire on top three nights running last week. Nobody's lived up there in a hundred years. Signals, maybe. Or someone wants to be found.

place_lore.nirncraft.northpoint.reeve_no:
^NOTICE
^Citizens are reminded that the moor is not a road. It does not take a person from one place to another; it takes a person to another place entirely.
^Peat-cutters are to carry a lantern and a rope. Children are to carry nothing and go nowhere. The Fog Horn Arms will sound the horn on the hour. If you cannot hear it, you are too far from home.

^Anyone who sees a second lamp on the moor is to remember that it is a grave-light and not a beacon. It is to be left lit. It is not to be followed. If it is followed, report to the Reeve what you saw. The Reeve will not say what happened. The Reeve will only write it down.
place_lore.nirncraft.northpoint.rumour: There are two lights at Northpoint, the tower and the moor. The tower is for ships. The moor is for the ones who did not come home.

place_lore.nirncraft.northwatch_keep.cel:
~Talos, who was a man and walked as men walk,
~who bled as we bleed and rose as we cannot,
~I do not ask you to open this door.
~I ask you to keep my mouth shut when they open it.

~Keep the faithful at Ironback safe.
~Keep the icon under the stone until a braver hand lifts it.
~And if the elves are right, and you are nothing,
~then let me be wrong in good company.
^Hjorvar, Frostfall 4E 201
place_lore.nirncraft.northwatch_keep.hoo: A grim fortress on the windswept north-west coast, taken by the Thalmor and turned into a prison. Nords who pray to the wrong god are brought here, and few are seen again.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwatch_keep.int: Session four. Subject recited the deeds of Tiber Septim for two hours, in order, with dates. Remarkable memory. Recommend it be used against him; the recitation ceases only when he loses his place.

Session six. Subject asked after the health of my mother. I have not told him I have a mother. Session terminated early.
Session seven. Subject states the faithful hid 'the iron icon' somewhere beneath their hearth before the arrest, and that we will never find it. We searched the Ironback Hideout twice. He laughed when I told him so. I will not report that he laughed.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwatch_keep.pri:
Prisoner 11. Nord, male, aged about seventy. Called Hjorvar the Grey. Self-styled priest of the heretic Talos. Taken at the Ironback Hideout. Condition: stubborn.
Prisoner 12. Nord, male, young. Kin to a Whiterun clan. Condition: defiant. Retain for leverage.
Prisoner 13. Imperial, female. Smuggler. Condition: cooperative. Release to Solitude by arrangement.

Prisoner 14. Nord, female. Talos amulet found sewn into hem. Condition: deceased, 2nd of Frostfall.
Prisoner 11 continues to refuse names. Recommend escalation. Recommend also that the guards on his corridor be rotated weekly; he has a voice that carries.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwatch_keep.rum: They say Northwatch is just an elven outpost. Then why does every fisherman on that coast row past it with his eyes shut? I'll tell you why: they hear the screaming over the waves.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_mine.fore:
^MINE CLOSED
By my word as foreman, 4E 179.
We broke through into a cave below the third gallery. It was warm and smelled of vinegar and there were eggs in it as big as a man's head.

One of the eggs hatched while we watched. We left the carts. We left the ore. I left my father's pick in the third gallery, and if any Northwind man goes back for it I'll break his legs myself.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_mine.gran:
Grandfather is dying. He won't say so but the healer at Shor's Stone does. Every night he asks about the pick. Silver bands, three runes on the haft: hearth, ore, home. His father made it. It was meant to be buried with him.

I'm not brave. I went as far as the second gallery and heard clicking in the walls. If anyone with a sword goes deeper, the pick is in the third gallery, by the broken cart. Bring it to Shor's Stone. He'll die happy, or at least less angry.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_mine.hook: An abandoned iron mine in the northern Rift, closed when its miners broke into a nest of chaurus. The tools are still where they dropped them.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_mine.rumo: Northwind Mine shut down years back. Chaurus, they said. Old Brandulf still talks about his grandfather's pick in there. Silver-bound, with runes on the haft.

place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_summit.ca: Taken down by Filnjar of Shor's Stone

Ulfr says: he was taking ore to Riften by the high road when the light went out, like a cloud over the sun, only the cloud had wings. It took the lead ox in its claws, and the cart with it, because the traces held.

It carried them up to Northwind Summit and dropped the cart on the rocks. It ate the ox up there. Ulfr says he watched it eat from the ditch until dark and then walked home without his boots, because he'd run out of them.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_summit.ho: A wind-scoured peak above Northwind Mine crowned with an old dragon shrine. Bones and broken carts lie scattered below it, dropped from a great height.
place_lore.nirncraft.northwind_summit.ru: There's a dragon perch on Northwind Summit. My cousin the carter says a whole ore wagon went up into the sky last month. Came down in pieces near Shor's Stone.

place_lore.nirncraft.old_attius_farm.far:
#Hearthfire, 4E 201
Ash-yams, eleven baskets to the Retching Netch: 33 drakes.
Scathecraw, one bundle to the apothecary: 8 drakes.
New hoe blade from the smith: owed, 12 drakes.
Neral's first wages from the diggers at Kolbjorn Barrow: 20 drakes. Good boy.

#Frostfall
Ash-yams, six baskets. The ash blight took the north rows.
Neral's wages: none. The foreman says they will be paid when the dig reaches the inner door.
Neral's wages: none.
Neral has not come home. I have written to the Guard. I will go up to the barrow myself if the sergeant does nothing. A farmer with a hoe is better than no one.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_attius_farm.hoo: An old homestead south of Raven Rock, where hardy ash-yams grow in volcanic dirt. The farmer here has been short of help since his son took work digging at Kolbjorn Barrow.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_attius_farm.rum: Tilvur Sadas grows the only decent yams on the island. His boy went digging for that excavator Ralis Sedarys at Kolbjorn Barrow. Hasn't come home for supper in a week.

place_lore.nirncraft.old_hroldan.battle_: ~The Reach held Hroldan, stone on stone,
~The sky took breath, the sky took sides,
~And thunder spoke where the Reachman hides.
^Below, in a later hand: and the Reachmen remember, so keep your purse close when you leave by the west road.

Under the carving, a guest has added in charcoal: The innkeeper says the third line is the truest. The day Hjalti took the village, the clouds came down over the walls and a voice rolled out of them that knocked the Reachmen from the battlements. My grandfather said it was the Greybeards. My grandmother said it was the ale. Both of them were there.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_hroldan.guest_b:
Gaius Ventrus, of Bruma. Slept in the Emperor's room on a dare. Left at midnight. Paid in full, didn't take his boots.
Solvi of Rorikstead. Heard marching. Says it was the Legion on the road. There was no Legion on the road.

Unnamed Breton lady. Asked for the room, stayed three nights, wept the whole time. Said he was kind to her. Would not say who.
Ulfgar the Lamp-Keeper adds: the lamp in that room is to be filled every evening, whether or not a guest takes it. House rule since my grandmother's day. Don't ask me what happens if you forget. Someone forgot once.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_hroldan.hook: A roadside inn on the old route to Markarth, raised on the field where Hjalti Early-Beard won a battle that made him an emperor. The room he slept in is still kept, and some say still occupied.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_hroldan.rumour: Stay at Old Hroldan if you like, just don't ask for the upstairs room. It's taken, has been for about four hundred years.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_hroldan.sk4_not: Folio #6 (-2131, -10): Field inspection recorded for Old Hroldan within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #6 for old_hroldan: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Old Hroldan are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

place_lore.nirncraft.old_mournhold.hook: The ruined twin of the city above: the same plan, dark and sunk and wrong-handed, where lamps burn for no one.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_mournhold.rumou: A lantern goes down into Old Mournhold every Sundas in the hand of a half-blind sexton, and has never failed to come up again. The ghosts, he says, take it personally if you whistle.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_mournhold.sexto:
#Sundas, Hearthfire
Third lamp. The twin plaza fountain is running backwards again. I said nothing. Lit the fourth lamp. Heard the Warden's step on the stair. Did not look.

#Sundas, a week later
Someone has taken the key from the fountain. They will wish they had not. The Warden will not be pleased. I shall take a spare lantern.

place_lore.nirncraft.old_orsinium.hook: The first Orc city, buried, with huge sloping halls in blackened stone, tilted streets, a trophy-ringed throne and a collapsed forge.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_orsinium.rumour: In Old Orsinium a hammer rings against an anvil with no smith, and it is carving something.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_orsinium.thread: THE THIRD SMITH BROKE THE CROWN. The fourth smith broke the sword. The fifth smith did not break the ring, for she could not; she buried it in the forge, and the forge forgot. Let no hand lift it, for a ring lifted is a ring that remembers its finger.
place_lore.nirncraft.old_orsinium.web.p0: HE WHO HOLDS THE HAMMER KEEPS THE ACCOUNT. I do not choose, I only cut. If you would stop me, take the hammer, and be the one who cuts. Or break it, and let the names be what they are: unwritten, free.

place_lore.nirncraft.onsis_breath.hook: A ring of wind-carved arches on the Bangkorai coast, whose stones sing in the wind with a hollow note.
place_lore.nirncraft.onsis_breath.rumour: Onsi's arches hum on a westerly. The sailors say the wind is reading tides aloud.
place_lore.nirncraft.onsis_breath.thread: Onsi's arches are dragon vertebrae. One is replaced by a pale stone, cut to fit, with a tag: 'Number 23.' Beneath the stone is a dry niche where the true bone was. Whoever took it left a good copy and a note of thanks. I would have preferred an apology. The wind sings through the gap in the wrong key.
place_lore.nirncraft.onsis_breath.web.p0: FIFTH YEAR: BRING THE PAGE. FIFTH YEAR: LEAVE THE PAGE. The ledger is torn in nine for the safety of the sea. One piece sleeps beneath this arch, until a captain who can read it comes.
place_lore.nirncraft.orcrest.cistern_ros:
#THE FIVE CISTERNS
First, by the Gate: for guards and caravans. Second, under the Watchtower: for the high houses. Third, beneath the Claw-and-Cistern: the best water, the deepest well, the one nobody speaks of. Fourth, in the lower court. Fifth, which is dry. The Fifth is always dry. Do not ask.

Marked in pencil at the bottom: 'The Third is down a barrel again. Four nights since the last. Raz says it is evaporation. Mala has watched evaporation for thirty years, and it does not take barrels.'
place_lore.nirncraft.orcrest.gate_oath.p:
^WHILE WATER IS IN THE TOWN, THE GATE SHALL STAND.
^WHILE THE GATE STANDS, THE TOWN SHALL SHARE.
^IF EITHER FAILS, THE OTHER SHALL REMEMBER.
Below the oath, scratched by a later hand: 'The Gate remembers. It has been remembering the debt of the Fifth Cistern since before my grandmother, and it has not yet forgotten.'
place_lore.nirncraft.orcrest.hook: A mesa-top fort-town in orange rock, its gate carved like a pair of raised claws, where every rooftop is a cistern and every citizen counts water in their sleep.
place_lore.nirncraft.orcrest.rumour: Orcrest is the only city in Elsweyr that closes its gate before dusk. Ask why and a guard will say 'water.' Ask again and she will say 'thieves.' Ask a third time and she will ask for your name.
place_lore.nirncraft.orcs_finger_ruins.h: At place.nirncraft.orcs_finger_ruins, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the dark crags and cliff-ports of Rivenspire, where Shornhelm's three noble houses light the Second Lamp against night-drinkers and coastal wreckers.

place_lore.nirncraft.orgnums_citadel.hoo: A sea-serpent citadel on a crag with boat-lifts, brine tanks, serpent pens and a throne hall with a window onto the deep.
place_lore.nirncraft.orgnums_citadel.rum: The sea-king stares into the deep and will not eat. The court says he is waiting for it to blink.
place_lore.nirncraft.orgnums_citadel.thr: THE SIXTH PAGE LOOKS ON THE DEEP. The sea-king keeps it where his gaze may rest upon it. He says it is a map to a place he does not wish to visit. If you take it, he will know. If you do not, he will wonder, and wondering is how kingdoms fall.
place_lore.nirncraft.orgnums_citadel.web: My lord does not sleep. He has stood at the great window since the reef came within sight. I fear he will go out to it. Some say he should: that it is a gift from the sea. Others say it is a plague. I say it does not matter what it is: we cannot hold it, and we cannot feed it, and we have not the sense to leave.

place_lore.nirncraft.orotheim.captive_le:
Mother,
I couldn't pay the toll. I'm working it off in the cave hauling water and cleaning their boots. They feed me. The Weighman says another month will see me square.

I don't believe him. Nobody here has ever been squared. There's a ledger with all our names, and the numbers next to them only grow. If anyone comes through Rorikstead looking for work, tell them the Orotheim chief keeps the key to the work-pen on his belt, and sleeps heavy after supper.
place_lore.nirncraft.orotheim.hook: A bandit cave in the hills north of Rorikstead, where a gang of cutthroats charges a toll on every cart that passes. Those who cannot pay are invited to stay.
place_lore.nirncraft.orotheim.rumour: The Orotheim gang will take a septim from every wheel that rolls past their hill. Can't pay? Then you'll work in their cave till you can. My neighbour's been working there since Hearthfire.
place_lore.nirncraft.orotheim.toll_order: One septim a wheel. Two for a wagon with a canopy, because anyone with a canopy can afford it. Five for anyone wearing a Legion or Stormcloak coat, because we are neutral and neutrality is expensive.

Those who can't pay, work. Those who won't work, we sell to the Brood Cavern lot. That was a joke. The Brood Cavern lot are dead. Spiders. Don't go near Brood Cavern.
Nobody touches the Rorikstead farmers. Rorikstead grows our bread, and a man who robs his baker eats stone.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphan_rock.cradle_: The shepherds of the Helgen valley tell how, in the hard winter after the Red Year, a cradle was found at the foot of the great rock with a girl in it and no footprints in the snow leading away. She was raised by the shepherds and became the best tracker in the valley.

When she was grown she climbed the rock to learn who had left her, and when she came down she would not speak of it. She hung a charm of carved birchwood at the top, a little cradle on a cord, and visited it every year until she died. The charm is said to protect any lost child who reaches the rock.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphan_rock.hook: A jagged spire of stone in the hills between Helgen and the Stormcloak camp. The tale is that a child was abandoned there once; what lives there now does not care for children.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphan_rock.rumour: Orphan Rock. The hagraven up there will trade you a cure for your cough or your curse, and take something you didn't know you'd miss. Ragna's brother went. Ragna still lights fires for him.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphan_rock.sk4_not: Folio #23 (259, 981): Field inspection recorded for Orphan Rock within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #23 for orphan_rock: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Orphan Rock are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphan_rock.torn_ba:
Written in a hand like a bird's foot:
Cough cured: one year of breath.
Curse lifted: one memory, chosen by us.
Lost thing found: one found thing lost.
The cradle charm stays with us. The lost come to the rock and the lost are ours. Mother Thornclaw has spoken. The brother of the fire-woman is paid for. Do not let her come up.

Below the list, a crude drawing of a beacon fire, crossed through with a talon. Then: 'The fire-woman on the watchtower burns her lamp each night. Let her burn. The ones who climb to us from the valley see it and think they are not alone. They are wrong. Up here the lost are always alone, until they are ours.'
place_lore.nirncraft.orphans_tear.hook: A Company merchantman torn open on the northern rocks, named for the lonely sea-stack that killed her. Her strongbox was never brought ashore, and the salvagers say her crew never left.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphans_tear.last_l:
#11th of Hearthfire
Cleared the Karth at noon with wool, salt, and the Company's quarterly pay for the northern posts, eight hundred septims in the iron strongbox under my bunk. Wind fair. The men are singing.

#13th of Hearthfire
Gale from the north-west. We cannot hold off the coast. The lighthouse is a pinprick behind us and there is no other light ahead. I have chained the strongbox to the bulkhead so it does not go over the side with the rest of us.
If we strike, it stays aboard. If you find it, it belongs to the Company, and to the widows of my crew, in that order or the other one. I would prefer the other one.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphans_tear.rumour: The Orphan's Tear went down in the first gale of Hearthfire with the Company's pay chest aboard. Half the coast has rowed out to look for it. The other half rowed out and didn't come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.orphans_tear.ship_b:
Dear Grelod's Girls,
I am writing this from a real ship. I am the cabin boy and I get a hammock and a whole sausage on Sundas. The captain says I am the first orphan from Honorhall ever to sail on a ship called the Orphan's Tear, and that it is a sign. He did not say a sign of what.

The sea is enormous. There is nothing on it but us and gulls. I am saving my pay to buy a boat of my own, and when I have it I will sail to Riften and take all of you away and we will never have to say Grelod is kind again.
We are going north tomorrow. The cook says there is a storm coming. The cook says that every day.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium.code_table:
~Here stood the city. Here it fell.
~Here stood the city again.
~Count the fallings, stranger, and then count the risings,
~and know which number is larger.

Beneath, scratched by many hands in many years: notches. Rows of them. Someone has carved a last notch, deeper than the rest, beside the newest gatestone, and beneath it in plain letters: NOT THIS TIME. A Breton visitor once asked a gate-guard what the notches meant. The guard said they were a tally of lessons. The visitor asked who had been taught. The guard only smiled, and showed him the gate, and told him the toll had just gone up.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium.envoy_lett: Sir Lucien Dorrel, envoy of the Court of Wayrest

#Orsinium, 2nd of Hearthfire, 4E 201
To His Majesty's Chancellery,
I have presented my credentials to King Gurak. He received them, read them, and used them to light his pipe. I am told this is a mark of informality rather than contempt. I am told a great many things here, chiefly by large people standing too close.

The city is larger than our maps admit, its walls thicker, its smiths more numerous. The Hall of the Clans shouts more and decides faster than our own council ever has. I recommend, with respect, that the Crown abandon any notion of a punitive expedition and instead purchase as many Orcish blades as the forgemasters will sell. I have already bought three. For the Crown, naturally.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium.forge_orde: Axe heads, 40, for the Bloodfist clan. Paid. Breastplates, 12, for a Redguard captain from Bangkorai. Paid in good gold, half of it bitten by me. Horseshoes, 200, for the Breton envoy. He asked for them 'with fewer spikes'. Made them with fewer spikes. Charged extra for the disappointment.

Took the first blade of the new ore to the shrine south-west of the city, as my mother did and hers before. Laid it on the stone and left it. Did not look back. The Furious One does not like smiths who look back at what they have given. The ogres were thick in the valley again. Walked around them. A smith's arms are for the hammer.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium.hook: The City of Orcs, rebuilt yet again in the mountains of Wrothgar by a people who have never once accepted that it should stay fallen. Its forges never cool and its gates never bow.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium.rumour: Bretons have burned Orsinium more times than they can count. The Orcs have counted. Every single time. They keep the number over the gate.
place_lore.nirncraft.orsinium_outlaws_re: A smugglers' stair under the wall of Orsinium, where Breton merchants buy what orc smiths are not supposed to sell.

^PASSED THE WALL THIS WEEK
^Four bolts of Breton wool, for the forge-aprons (the aprons are wool; the forge does not care).
^One crate of real wine, labelled as vinegar.
^Three iron ingots, entering. Three, leaving, with a different mark.
^One grandfather, in a barrel. Do not ask.

Note for the Chieftain, should he read this: the grandfather has since been returned to his family. He was not dead. He had merely fallen asleep in the barrel, and been shipped. Orsinium is, at heart, a very forgiving city.
The refuge beneath Orsinium is run by a woman who is half orc and wholly unconcerned. She pays the wardens in iron and the Chieftain in jokes.
A bone-walled ossuary built in terraced galleries, skulls arranged by family line, each tier's door answering to a name read aloud.
The Ossuary doors will open if you read the right name aloud. Nobody remembers the right name.

First tier: the Keepers. Second: the Lamp-Wardens. Third: the Name-Singers. Fourth: those who were not named. Fifth, flooded: the Warden whose name was struck. Speak it, and the lamp will know its keeper. Fail to speak it, and the lamp will not be fooled.
A Legion camp on the cold western coast of the Pale, keeping watch over the road and the sea. Its quartermaster is waiting for a pay shipment that is long overdue.

To Legate Fasendil, General Tullius's staff, Solitude.
Sir, the pay for this camp, three barrels in coin, was dispatched aboard the merchant ship Brinehammer under seal. The Brinehammer has not arrived at Dawnstar. A fisherman tells me there is a wreck on the rocks north of here, broken in two.

I have sent two men to look. They came back with tales of Nord salvagers diving at low tide and a great bull horker that chased them up the beach.
The men grumble. A soldier will march on an empty stomach but not on an empty purse. Request permission to recover the coin by force, or failing that, to borrow against the Legate's wine allowance.
The Legion boys at the coast camp haven't been paid since Last Seed. You can tell by how hard they haggle for bread.

Folio #9 (-349, -1722): Field inspection recorded for Pale Imperial Camp within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #9 for pale_imperial_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Pale Imperial Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

My dear Livia,
The north is cold beyond telling. I sleep in my cloak, my boots and two blankets and still dream of your mother's kitchen in Chorrol. There is a dragon mound just south of camp. The centurion says it is only an old grave. Last night it steamed in the frost like a pot on the boil.

When I am paid, I will send you every coin, and you can buy that blue cloth you liked. When I am paid. I say it every night like a prayer.
Yours until the wind stops,
Aulus

^Postscript
They say the Brinehammer has sunk with our pay aboard. If that is true, Livia, the blue cloth must wait. I am sorry. I am always sorry, these days.
place_lore.nirncraft.pale_pass_dragon_mo: A snow-mantled dragon burial mound guarding the high mountain throat where the old road climbs toward Cyrodiil.
Couriers riding the high pass swear the snow on the Pale Pass Dragon Mound steams like a hearth whenever a shadow crosses the sun.

When the blizzard blinds the road-markers above Helgen, feel for the carved spiral curb of the great mound beside the gorge. Shelter under its lee wall if you must, but do not build a fire atop the center slabs.
place_lore.nirncraft.pale_pass_legion_ca: A snow-swept Imperial field camp guarding the northern approach to Pale Pass, where supply mules wait for the rockslides to be cleared.
Legionnaires at the Pale Pass camp say the avalanches buried three supply trains in the high throat of the mountains.

Nineteen pack-mules picketed along the pine line, carrying hardtack, winter cloaks, and spare pilum heads from the border depot. Until the engineers clear the rockfall in the upper defile, all dispatches for Cyrodiil must go by courier over the ridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.pale_stormcloak_cam:
Bear-and-Axe Company, the Pale camp.
Present: 22. Wounded: 4. Sick (nightmares, Dawnstar men, useless): 3. Deserted: 1, Kolbeinn Rime-Hand, with the banner. Dead: 0 this month, Talos be thanked.

Supplies: arrows short, mead shorter. The Winter War was meant to bring the arrows to the Winterhold camp and some on to us. No word of her.
Orders from Windhelm: hold the road, watch Fort Dunstad, do not provoke the giants. Sergeant's additional orders: do not provoke the sergeant.

^Added in Gunnvor's hand
Rumour from the Nightgate road says Kolbeinn went into Forsaken Cave. If any of you go after him on your own, you're on latrines until Ulfric is High King.
A Stormcloak war camp in the eastern Pale, close to the Dwemer ruins and the Windhelm road. Its sergeant is short-tempered, short of men, and short one company banner.
The Stormcloak camp near Raldbthar is a cheerful place. Well, it was until their banner walked off with one of their own.
place_lore.nirncraft.paragons_remembranc: A tall memorial column of names, with a flat processional ground before it and a bowl for offerings.
The Paragon's column shows names of Orcs who are still alive, and they have started to die in that order.

Cut this season by no hand I know: Dura gro-Mazog, Grat Quick-Eye, Ushnar. Dura died on the date. Grat has seven days. Ushnar I do not know. I have tried covering the lower tier; the names grow up through the cloth. Someone is writing on the stone from the inside.

place_lore.nirncraft.peaks_shade_tower.h: A Nordic tower on the hill east of Falkreath, in the shade of the Jerall peaks. Old lovers' initials cover its walls, and lately so do the marks of an armed watch.
place_lore.nirncraft.peaks_shade_tower.l:
Haki,
I waited at the tower on Fredas until the moons came up. You said you'd come after your watch. I carved our letters again beside the old ones, since the rain has nearly washed them out. My father says a guardsman's wage will never buy a house in Falkreath. I told him I don't want a house, I want a man who keeps his promises.
So keep them. The tower, next Fredas, at dusk. If you don't come, I will assume you have finally been eaten by a bear, and I will mourn you properly and marry the miller's son. Solveig.
place_lore.nirncraft.peaks_shade_tower.r: Peak's Shade Tower's where Falkreath sweethearts go to carve their names. Lately somebody's been keeping watch up there, and they're not there for romance.
place_lore.nirncraft.peaks_shade_tower.s: Folio #32 (-600, 1273): Field inspection recorded for Peaks Shade Tower within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #32 for peaks_shade_tower: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Peaks Shade Tower are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

East gate of Falkreath: two guards by day, one by night, often asleep.
Walls: timber, rotten in the southeast corner by the graveyard.
Legion patrols: through the west gate on Middas and Loredas, back by dusk.
The old jarl's word is good. Carry this report back to camp and tell the commander the tower will do for a signal post. Also tell him there are two sweethearts who come up here on Fredas and I am tired of hiding behind the stair.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagia_farm.hook: An Imperial family's farm in the shadow of Whiterun's walls, its fences mended more often than they should be. Giant tracks cross the lower field.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagia_farm.rumour: Severio Pelagia's a decent sort for an Imperial. His hand Gunnvor lost one of the cows to the giants at Bleakwind Basin. She wants it back, if you can believe that.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagia_farm.severi:
Dear Cassius,
You ask if I regret coming north. Some mornings I do. The wind off the Tundra goes straight through a Colovian coat. The Nords at the market still call me 'the Imperial' after twenty years, as if it were my given name.

But the ground is good, and the city buys everything I grow. Our only real trouble is the giants of Bleakwind Basin. They mean no harm, I think. They just do not understand fences. Last month one stepped over ours, took a cow under each arm and walked home as if they were his.

Gunnvor, my farmhand, swears she will get Brindle back. I have told her she is mad. She says that is why I hired her.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagia_farm.sk4_no: Folio #11 (-9, 151): Field inspection recorded for Pelagia Farm within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.pelagiad.hook: A fortified hill village with a half-built fort and a granary where the roads from the pier all meet.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagiad.rumour: Every night the pilgrims leave the Pelagiad granary in a quiet line. The captain locks his door.
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagiad.web.author: Captain Ulric Dorn
place_lore.nirncraft.pelagiad.web.p0: Pilgrims: 44 departed on the old road, 0 returned. Escort refused; the order was countersigned by the Temple's own seal. I would like it noted that I do not like this. The chalk crescents change colour after rain, and the line of travellers follows the new colour.

place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_rest_stead: A sheltered stone way-stead at the foot of the eastern mountain shrine trail where Dunmer and Nord pilgrims warm themselves before the climb.
Anyone climbing toward the great statue stops at Pilgrim's Rest Stead for hot ash-tea and a pair of ice-crampons.

Three pilgrims from Windhelm's Grey Quarter and a scholar from the College shared the hearth-bench tonight while the blizzard howled outside. Leave a bundle of dry kindling in the porch-box for the next traveler coming down from the Shrine.
place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_trench.hoo: A trench in the sea ice off the Winterhold coast where three ships went down within sight of each other. On clear days you can see their masts beneath the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_trench.pil:
Sister,
We sail at dawn on the Fair Hjordis, two other ships beside us, all of us bound for the tomb of the Harbinger. I carry the reliquary from our shrine in Windhelm: the arm-ring the old priests say was worn by one of the Five Hundred. We mean to lay it at his door.

The captain is nervous. The ice came early. He says the trench off the coast is where the sea is deepest and the ice weakest, and we must cross it in the dark to make the tide.
If anything should happen, Sister, know that the ring is in the iron box under my bunk. It should reach Ysgramor even if I do not.
place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_trench.rum: Pilgrim's Trench. Three ships carrying pilgrims to Ysgramor's Tomb, all sunk on the same night. The ice there's thin, and the slaughterfish aren't.
place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_trench.sk4: Folio #8 (1007, -1984): Field inspection recorded for Pilgrims Trench within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #8 for pilgrims_trench: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Pilgrims Trench are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.pilgrims_trench_bea: A salt-encrusted iron signal-brazier and shattered hull-rib wedged onto a sea-stack above the treacherous ships' graveyard of Pilgrim's Trench.
Wreckers on the ice-packs light the Pilgrim's Trench Beacon on stormy nights—not to save ships, some say, but to draw them onto the reef.
Hauled two casks of seal-oil up the icy iron rungs before the tide rose over the reef. Below the sea-stack, the masts of three sunken merchantmen still poke through the black swells at low water.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinefrost_tower.age:
To the Third Emissary:
The exile Elenthir continues to occupy the burrow at Rimerock. He has bound a Daedra of some strength to his door. I recommend we let the Daedra do our work for us. Bindings of that kind seldom hold through a winter.

Separately: the Stormcloak camp near Meridia's statue sends a rider north-east every fourth day. I have taken his route down in the margin. I have not shared it with the Legion. The Legion has not asked, and it is unwise to teach them to rely on us.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinefrost_tower.hoo: An old Imperial watchtower on the western ridge of Haafingar, abandoned since the Great War. The wind talks through its arrow slits, and someone has been watching from the top again.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinefrost_tower.rum: Pinefrost Tower's been empty since my father's day. But someone's been up there with a spyglass lately, watching the hills. Elf, by the look of the cloak.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinefrost_tower.wat:
#Sun's Height, 4E 174
No sign of the Dominion on this coast. There is a rumour that they will come by sea. I watch the sea. The sea watches me back.

#Last Seed, 4E 175
Word has come of the treaty. Talos is outlawed. We are to take down the shrine in the tower's lower room. Varro refused and was flogged. I did it myself, so it would be done gently, and I hid the little statue in the wall behind the third stone. Nobody asked me where it went. Somebody should find it when this foolishness is over. I begin to suspect it will not be in my lifetime.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinemoon_cave.chief: Listen, you lot. The Legion box stays sealed and stays with me. You get your share when I say, and I say when the Legion's done looking. Anyone opens it early gets his fingers bitten. You know I mean it.

Next run: the payroll for Hraggstad comes by the Dragon Bridge road again on the first Fredas of Sun's Dusk. Same as before. Pine in your caps so the survivors remember it was us; frightened soldiers walk slower.
And whoever's been sneaking out to Clearpine at night, I know about it. Bring back what you buried and I'll only bite one hand.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinemoon_cave.hidde:
Note to me, for when I'm drunk and forget:
My share of the first payroll, before Rolf gets greedy, is at Clearpine Pond. North shore, by the rotten stump, a forearm deep. Gold ring from the dead escort too, the one with the little eagle.

If I die, the fisherman saw me bury it, so it's his now. Gods know he's earned it, putting up with us shouting by his pond. If he doesn't want it, whoever reads this can have it. Just don't give it to Rolf.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinemoon_cave.hook: A bandit cave in the pinewoods north-west of Dragon Bridge. Its occupants wear pine sprigs in their caps and have grown fat on stolen Legion silver.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinemoon_cave.rumou: The Pinemoon gang took the Legion payroll right off the road. Didn't even bother wearing masks. Their chief, Rolf Coin-Biter, bites every coin he steals, to be sure it's real.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinepeak_cavern.hoo: A bear den in the pines above Ivarstead. The hunters call its master Old Scarback, a grey sow with an arrow-scar across her snout who has killed two men and a horse.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinepeak_cavern.hun:
#3rd of Frostfall
Found her prints again by the Pinepeak track, wide as a shield. She drags her left hind foot since I put an arrow in her hip two winters ago. She remembers me, I think. Bears do.

#5th of Frostfall
Went into the cave mouth at first light. Bones everywhere. Goat, deer, the Ivarstead horse, and a boot with a foot still in it. That's Hakon's boot. I knew that boot.

#5th, later
She's awake. I can hear her breathing in the dark like a bellows. If you find this, I didn't get out. Kill her for Hakon, and for me. Aim for the scarred side. She can't see from it.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinepeak_cavern.rum: Old Scarback came down to Ivarstead last spring and carried off a goat in her mouth like a kitten. Nobody's been brave enough to follow her home.

place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch.cellar_ru:
Upstairs we are a family. Mother, Father, Cousin. Smile at visitors. Offer them stew. Never ever open the trapdoor while anyone is in the house who isn't one of us.
Downstairs we are what we are. Take what comes off the Half-Moon road, sort it, and keep it until Lakeview's buyer comes on Sundas.

The Gray Pine lockbox stays in the vault until we've read every page of that ledger. There's coin in other people's debts if you know who to ask. Nobody spends the shop silver in Falkreath. We are not stupid. Mostly.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch.hook: A modest cabin in the pines south of Lake Ilinalta. The family who seem to live there are pleasant enough; the trapdoor under their table leads somewhere much less pleasant.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch.merchant_:
Bailiff Eirik,
This is my third letter. The lockbox taken from my shop on the 2nd of Frostfall held not only the week's takings but my ledger of debts owed, and half of Falkreath is in that book. Whoever has it can blackmail every family in the hold, or simply forgive themselves what they owe me.

I saw the thief run south, toward Pinewatch. I know the family there call themselves honest. I also know they paid me last month in silver that I sold to a carter the month before, a carter who was robbed on the Half-Moon road. Send somebody. Or I will hire somebody, and you will not like whom.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch.rumour: Pinewatch? Nice folk. Always have new boots, new cloaks, new everything. Never seen 'em sell so much as an egg. Makes you think.

place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch_stead.hoo: A timbered out-stead beside the eastern coaching road where rye sheaves and split pine cordwood are stored for the hold's winter tithe.
place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch_stead.rum: The carters at Pinewatch Stead lock their barn doors before sundown; too many strangers have been walking the ridge above the road.

place_lore.nirncraft.pinewatch_stead.war: Fourteen cords of seasoned pine stacked by the roadside shed, and eight sacks of winter rye bound for the granary in Falkreath. Our neighbor up on the hill at Pinewatch claims to be a simple homesteader, yet I have counted ten pairs of iron-shod boots on his porch and not a single plow-ox in his paddock.
place_lore.nirncraft.plateau_of_the_trav: A lone rock plateau with a view across the delta and a flat stone, polished by feet, at its edge.
From the lone plateau you can see two paths. One is silver, one is dark. Choose carefully which you follow.

At dusk the old route shines like a fish's back down to the sea. The new route runs due east through the drier fields of Gideon. The two paths part at a mound near the third marsh-bend. I walked the new route. It ended in a plantation courtyard with a bell. The bell was silent, and the courtyard was full of coffins waiting.
place_lore.nirncraft.port_hunding.hook: The old customs quay of Stros M'Kai, where a Redguard captain once broke an Imperial blockade and was hanged for it, and now has a statue.
place_lore.nirncraft.port_hunding.hundin: The Customs Clerk of Port Hunding

^STAMPED THIS DAY: seventy-one ships, none of them real. Forty-three sailors, of whom I can account for four. I have stamped the sky, and I have stamped the sea. I have stamped my own hand and found it did not wash.

^If you are reading this, you have been stamped. It will not hurt. It may itch. You will find that doors open for you in Stros M'Kai that were not open before, and that some doors you had used for years are now, quite simply, gone.
place_lore.nirncraft.port_hunding.rumour: Port Hunding is said to have a ghost. The ghost is a customs clerk. He asks for papers. If you do not have them, he stamps you anyway, and the stamp does not wash off.

place_lore.nirncraft.prowls_edge_dragons: A ridge of colossal bones leading to a lair on a mesa, an open-air scour you can walk inside with ribs forming arches.
At Prowl's Edge a steam rises from the bones on a cold night, as if something were quenched.
WHAT IS SWORN IS SWORN. WHAT IS BROKEN IS BROKEN. WHAT IS FORGED HERE IS BOTH. Let no hand take the blade who has not broken a vow. Let no hand put it down who has not kept one.
place_lore.nirncraft.psijic_relic_vaults: A vault of sliding walls and phase-doors where rooms rearrange as you move and time-eddies freeze torches.
The Psijic vaults move their rooms. Folk say there is one that has been moved so often it is no longer anywhere.

THE NINTH LAMP BURNS NOT FOR LIGHT BUT FOR REMEMBRANCE. Those who tend it tend the dead. Those who extinguish it forget the dead. Those who keep it must be willing to hear, in the dark, all that was done in the light.

THE HOUR IS KEPT, NOT KILLED. Let it burn until the one who spilled the cup is known. Let it not be hidden from the one who lost it. The Order has been wrong before; the Order will be wrong again. Let the hour be remembered.
place_lore.nirncraft.purewater_run.herba: Purewater Run, by the falls: river betty, abundant. Mountain flower, blue and purple. Water drawn from the source spring keeps a potion fresh twice as long as Karth water, I do not know why.

Do not go into the cave. Something lives there with a large appetite and a Reachman's patience. Forsworn have been seen collecting water at dawn, carrying it south in hide bags toward Hag Rock. Someone among them is ill, I think, or someone is brewing something that needs pure water. Briars are thirsty things.
place_lore.nirncraft.purewater_run.hook: A clear stream tumbles from a cave in the hills south of Markarth. The water is the sweetest in the Reach, and the den above it is full of things that think so too.
place_lore.nirncraft.purewater_run.rumou: Purewater Run's water'll cure a hangover and a heartache both, the old women say. You just have to get past what's living in the cave above it.

place_lore.nirncraft.pyandonean_fleet_an:
#ORDERS
The watch shall change at the third bell. Lanterns shall be trimmed. The prisoner in the hold shall be fed and not spoken to. If the sea is calm, it is a trick. If the sea is rough, it is a courtesy.

Pencilled on the back, small and very steady: 'The prisoner has asked three times to speak to the Admiral. I have told him she is busy. She is not busy. She is afraid of what he knows. I have decided, for the sake of my own sleep, not to ask what it is.'
A fleet at anchor: a raft-city of shell-hulled ships lashed together under green glass lanterns, a coral flagship at the centre, serpent-prowed boats alongside, everything gleaming wet.
The Maormer say the fleet has never been in port. It is the port. The ships are the streets, and the streets are the ships, and the only place a Maormer sets foot on land is to bury his dead.

A camp on the Yokudan desert's edge, sand-coloured tents, a drill-yard and a training-post carved with four forms.
At the Ra Gada camp they will tell you the fourth form is taught on the water, and then they stop speaking.

A seventh page, nailed under the lesson-post by a hand I did not see. I have no wish to read it. It is the property of the kings, not the camp. The final two pages lie beyond the water, in a place where the kings sleep. If you mean to read the ledger, you must first complete the Last Lesson.

Four forms: the Wave, the Wind, the Stone, the Return. The first three I taught in this yard. The fourth is a thing the old masters said could only be taught on the water, to one who has learnt the others. None has learnt. The last student drowned. The sandal is his. I keep it, as one keeps a lesson not yet finished.

place_lore.nirncraft.ragnvald.eirik_jour:
#2nd of Hearthfire
Arrived with Brand and Olaf, hired at the Silver-Blood Inn. The courtyard is real, just as Grandfather drew it. Draugr asleep in the walls. We tiptoe like thieves in a nursery.

#3rd of Hearthfire
The tithe-chamber. Silver plate, a whole wall of it, offerings to the barrow's master. Brand and Olaf filled their packs and left me in the dark. Cowards. I still have the lantern.

#4th of Hearthfire
The master woke. Hrodulf, it says on his coffin. Tithe-Keeper. He wants the silver back, every piece, and I am the only one left to pay. I am hiding behind his throne. Dagny, if this reaches you, I'm sorry about the mare.
place_lore.nirncraft.ragnvald.hook: An ancient Nordic ruin in the hills north of Markarth, built around a sunken courtyard where the dead keep watch. Treasure hunters go there in pairs, and come back in ones.
place_lore.nirncraft.ragnvald.rumour: Ragnvald's an old Nord tomb up north of Markarth. Eirik Hollow-Voice went there for gold. His sister's still waiting at the stables.
place_lore.nirncraft.ragnvald.sk4_note_2: Folio #27 (-3069, -540): Field inspection recorded for Ragnvald within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #27 for ragnvald: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Ragnvald are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.ragnvald.tithe_insc:
Rendered by a scholar's rough hand from the old Nordic runes:
Here Hrodulf keeps the tithe of the valley. What the living gave, the dead hold. Whoever takes from the wall pays from the blood.
And beneath, the scholar adds: The runes for 'valley' here are those used for the lands of the Karth before the Reachmen drove the first Nords out. This barrow is older than Markarth's Nord kings. Treat it with respect, or with a very large axe.

place_lore.nirncraft.raldbthar.bandit_co: We took this ruin because it was warm. Nobody said the warm came from the machines. Nobody said the machines would wake up when Gorm kicked the brass spider. Gorm's dead. The brass spider is fine.
Rule from now on: nobody goes below the third stair. Nobody kicks anything. Nobody listens to that mage who keeps sending letters about rods.

Second rule: the warm part of the ruin is ours, the clicking part belongs to the machines, and the scholar can come and have his rod if he wants it so badly. Third rule: if the scholar sends a sellsword instead, we hide. Gorm didn't hide. Look how that turned out.
place_lore.nirncraft.raldbthar.hook: A Dwemer ruin in the southern Pale, its halls still guarded by brass constructs. Quaestor Vesk of the College has staked his reputation on what lies inside.
place_lore.nirncraft.raldbthar.rumour: Raldbthar. Bandits camp in the upper halls, Dwemer machines guard the lower ones. Either way, you'll be fighting somebody's property.
place_lore.nirncraft.raldbthar.vesk_comm:
Commission for any competent person (1).
In the lower halls of Raldbthar there is a chamber containing a tonal regulator: a brass rod fixed in a cradle of struts, which hums when touched. I require it, intact, at the College of Winterhold. My fee is generous and my gratitude is, I am told, tiresome.

(1) Competence is defined as: able to tell a Dwemer sphere from a Dwemer chamber-pot, and able to run away from the former.
Beware the bandits in the upper halls; they are not interested in scholarship. Beware the centurion in the lower; it is not interested in anything at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.ramshackle_trading_: A wind-battered trading post on the road between Kagrumez and the coast, run by an Orc who buys anything and asks nothing. Half the stolen goods on the island pass across his counter.

The Ramshackle Trading Post buys anything. Dwemer scrap, Skaal furs, a riekling's spear, your mother's teeth. The Orc who runs it doesn't ask where any of it came from, and you shouldn't ask where it goes.

Bought: Dwemer gears, four, from a Dunmer with singed eyebrows who came from Kagrumez. 20 drakes. Sold same to Tel Mithryn for 80.
Bought: furs, Skaal-made, eleven, from a reaver who said they were his. They were not his. 30 drakes. Sold to the Company for 90.
Bought: one silver-banded ash urn, Dunmer, from a fellow called Fevyn. Refused. Some things have a curse on them even when they haven't.

Note to self: the reavers at Bujold's Retreat owe me for two casks of mead and a new boat. Do not sell them anything else until they pay. Do not tell them where I keep the strongbox. Do not let Gnaw-Tooth's rieklings near the mead, whatever they offer to trade. Last time they offered me a horker. A live horker.
place_lore.nirncraft.rannveigs_fast.gray:
#12th of Frostfall
Grandmother always said Rannveig was a Gray-Mane, a hundred generations back, before we had the name. I never believed her. Then I found the ring drawn in the margin of the clan's old saga at the house in Whiterun: a band of iron with a wolf's mouth closing on a stone.

#14th of Frostfall
I am inside. The dead are stirring and the ring is further in than I can reach alone. They move when I touch the walls.

If a stranger finds this: the ring belongs with the Gray-Manes in Whiterun. Bring it out of the dark and tell them Sigrid tried.
place_lore.nirncraft.rannveigs_fast.hook: An old Nord barrow sunk into the hills west of Whiterun, named for a shieldmaiden who swore to starve beside its door until the dead inside lay still. A Word of Power waits in the deep halls.
place_lore.nirncraft.rannveigs_fast.rann:
^HERE RANNVEIG IRON-MOUTH
^KEPT HER FAST

She swore before Kyne that she would take neither bread nor water while the dead of this hall walked. On the thirtieth day the halls fell silent, and so did she.

Her shield-sisters set her oath-ring on the stone of the inner hall, where the dead would see it and remember that the living do not forget. Let none take the ring from this place while the dead still stir, lest the fast be broken.
place_lore.nirncraft.rannveigs_fast.rumo: Rannveig's Fast, it's called. The old story says she sat at the door and didn't eat for a month. Her oath-ring's still in there somewhere, and the Gray-Manes would pay to see it home.

place_lore.nirncraft.raven_rock.bulwark_: Mileth Indaram, Sergeant of the Redoran Guard

^By leave of the Councilor
1. The south gate is barred from dusk to first light. No exceptions for Company men, Telvanni errand-boys, or anyone who claims to have forgotten their pipe at the Retching Netch.
2. Any citizen seen walking toward the Earth Stone at night is to be stopped, gently. Do not wake them by shouting. Turn them by the shoulders and walk them home.

3. Ash spawn are to be fought at the wall, never past it. Last Seed taught us that lesson at the cost of two good guards.
4. Grave-diggers bound for Kolbjorn Barrow carry a pass with my seal. If they come back without the pass, they come back without their wages.
5. Report anything strange. I am aware that this is Solstheim and everything is strange. Report it anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.raven_rock.gazettee:
#The garrison and the diggers
Captain Veleth Adren counts rations by the bowl and the dead by the grave. Foreman Gorm Stonehand reports nine; the graves say fourteen. Sister Ilvani keeps the one-hall chapel and a congregation of forty on a good Sundas. Ashlander Tuvi trades at the gate and sleeps outside it.

#The wharf and the heap
Tindra Hael's Salvage and Salt prices everything the mine spits out. Rolan the dockhand will teach you the middle plank. The windward wall has two sentries too many at the second bell. Whatever you do, do not whistle on the third landing of the shaft.
place_lore.nirncraft.raven_rock.hook: The Dunmer town of Raven Rock squats behind the Bulwark, its roofs grey with ash from Red Mountain. The Redoran Guard keeps the wall, the mine keeps the coin, and lately the townsfolk keep waking up far from their beds.
place_lore.nirncraft.raven_rock.letter_t:
Brother,
You asked whether Raven Rock is better than Windhelm. The Nords here do not spit at us. The ash, on the other hand, gets into everything: the bedding, the scuttle, my teeth. I sweep the step four times a day and Mother says it is the ancestors visiting.

Something else, and do not laugh. Three nights ago I woke on the road outside the gate with my hands bleeding and a stone in each fist. Old Aulus, the Imperial, found me and walked me back. He says he saw a dozen others out there, all carrying stones toward the west. Nobody remembers. Nobody wants to talk about it. Send word from Windhelm if you hear of a cure for walking in one's sleep. Your sister, Ilvi.
place_lore.nirncraft.raven_rock.rumour: The Guard doubled the watch on the Bulwark. Not for ash spawn this time. For our own people, walking out of the gate in their sleep with their eyes wide open.

place_lore.nirncraft.ravenscar_hollow.fr:
Ottar,
I did not get lost. Tell Katla I'm sorry about the basket.
You remember when Mother was sick and the priest in Solitude said there was nothing to do but pray to Arkay? The crow-mother would have saved her. She told me so, and she showed me how. She has shown me so much.

There is a price. There is always a price, she says, and I have begun to pay it. My hands do not look like my hands any more. I am not afraid. Mostly I am not afraid.
If you come for me, don't. If you come anyway, bring Mother's clasp so I remember who I was before I decide who I will be.
place_lore.nirncraft.ravenscar_hollow.ho: A crow-haunted cave in the northern hills of Haafingar where hagravens nest among bones and feathers. Lately a young woman from Katla's Farm was seen walking toward it, alone.
place_lore.nirncraft.ravenscar_hollow.le:
FIRST LESSON. THE BODY IS A COAT. TAKE IT OFF AND THE WIND COMES IN.
SECOND LESSON. THE CROW REMEMBERS. ASK THE CROW.
THIRD LESSON. PAY IN BLOOD, NOT IN SILVER. SILVER LIES.

FOURTH LESSON. THE GIRL FROM THE HORSE-FARM LEARNS FAST. SHE ASKS WHY. GOOD. THOSE WHO ASK WHY BECOME MOTHERS. THOSE WHO ASK HOW BECOME BONES.
FIFTH LESSON. WHEN HER BROTHER COMES, AND HE WILL, SHE MUST CHOOSE.
SIXTH LESSON. IF SHE CHOOSES THE FARM, LET HER GO. A MOTHER MADE BY FORCE IS ONLY A CAGE WITH FEATHERS. IF SHE CHOOSES US, THE BROTHER GOES HOME ALONE, OR DOES NOT GO HOME.
place_lore.nirncraft.ravenscar_hollow.ru: Ravenscar Hollow's full of crows and worse than crows. Hagravens, old ones. They say a hagraven can't take you. You have to go to her. That's what makes it so terrible.

place_lore.nirncraft.rawlkha.hook: A Khajiiti trade-town of canvas and bamboo strung between the trees of Reaper's March, where bazaar tents hang over rope bridges and a forest of lanterns glows at dusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.rawlkha.market_pact:
#BE IT KNOWN
That no tree shall be felled for a stall. That no stall shall be lit by living flame within a spear's length of a bough. That no merchant shall sell the wood of the forest, nor the sap, nor the leaf, nor the ghost of a leaf.

Whereas the Khajiit traders of Rawlkha shall bring what is not of the forest, and the Bosmer of the forest shall buy it, and neither shall remark on the other's prices. Signed, in three leaf-prints and one paw.
place_lore.nirncraft.rawlkha.rumour: A Bosmer will not sell you a rope. A Khajiit will sell you a rope, a knot, a lesson in the knot and, on the third day, a bridge. That is the whole difference between the two peoples, and Rawlkha lives in the gap.

place_lore.nirncraft.reach_imperial_camp: A Legion war camp at the foot of the hills below Bthardamz, holding the Reach for the Empire and for Jarl Igmund. Its couriers ride out every week, and lately not all of them ride back.

To the General's office, Castle Dour, Solitude.
Sir, I regret to report that dispatch rider Quintus Asellio did not arrive at Dragon Bridge on schedule. His horse returned without him on the 11th of Frostfall, with a Forsworn arrow in the saddle.

I do not accept the obvious answer. The Stormcloak camp near Liar's Retreat has openly boasted of stopping riders on that road, and a Forsworn arrow is easy enough to buy in Karthwasten. Asellio carried the troop rolls for the whole Reach garrison. If they fell into Ulfric's hands, every patrol from Markarth to Bthardamz is compromised.
I request permission to send a party to Deep Folk Crossing to recover the satchel. Failing permission, I intend to hire someone and not ask.

Arrows: low. Request sent to Markarth. Request ignored by Markarth.
Bandages: low, owing to the Forsworn.
Wine: none, owing to the soldiers.
Morale: see Wine.
Note for the tribune: the men will not stand watch facing the Dragon Burial Mound to the south. They say it moves at night. I have explained that mounds do not move. They have explained that I do not stand watch.

Further requests, unanswered:
One (1) priest of Arkay, for the men's nerves and the dead's sake.
One (1) map of the Bthardamz approaches that does not end in the words 'here be machines'.
Rope: plenty. We have so much rope. Nobody knows why. Do not let the men near the rope after the wine runs out.
The Legion lost a dispatch rider on the Deep Folk Crossing road. The legate's fuming. Wants to know if it was the Forsworn or the bearded ones from Windhelm.

Folio #25 (-2882, -680): Field inspection recorded for Reach Imperial Camp within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #25 for reach_imperial_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Reach Imperial Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.reach_stormcloak_ca:
1. No soldier leaves the camp alone. The Forsworn in Broken Tower Redoubt have taken two sentries this month.
2. The Imperial camp is at the foot of the hills by Bthardamz. You are not to engage it without orders. We are here to watch, not to start a war we can't finish from a tent.

3. Any dispatch rider seen on the Deep Folk Crossing road is to be stopped and searched. The Legion moves its letters that way.
4. The bandits in Liar's Retreat are not our allies, whatever they say. Sweet-Tongue offered me moonstone for safe passage. I said yes. Now none of you will touch it until I say so.
5. Talos guide us. Shine your boots.
A Stormcloak war camp pitched on a ridge in the middle Reach, close enough to Markarth to make the Jarl nervous and close enough to the Forsworn to make the soldiers jumpy.
There's a Stormcloak camp up past Karthwasten. The men in it remember the Markarth Incident and they're itching to see the Reach under Ulfric again.
