Addendum #20 for reach_stormcloak_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Reach Stormcloak Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Mother,
We are camped in the Reach. It is not like Windhelm. The rocks here are red and the people look at you as if you owe them something. Maybe we do. Old Varmund says when Ulfric took Markarth back from the Forsworn, the streets ran so red you could not tell blood from the stone.
I do not tell Varmund that I don't think that's a thing to be proud of. Bake Inga a honey cake for me. I'll be home by Evening Star, or I won't.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachcliff_cave.hoo: A barrow cut into the cliffs of the southern Reach, home to the hungry dead and, some whisper, to living worshippers with a terrible appetite.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachcliff_cave.mis:
Scrawled on the back of a Markarth guard notice:
Orla, beggar, went south toward the cliffs, Sun's Height.
The Bosmer trapper from Dushnikh Yal's road, Last Seed.
Two pilgrims bound for Old Hroldan, Hearthfire.
All seen last on the road past Reachcliff Cave. All with no family worth asking. Whoever's doing this chooses well.
And beneath, in red that is not ink: Not 'whoever'. We are many, and we are always hungry, and our Lady is pleased.

Folded into the list, a second scrap in a shaking hand:
I followed the beggar Orla's tracks to the cave mouth and smelled cooking. Good cooking. Herbs and fat and smoke. I nearly went in. Then I saw the bones stacked by the door, neat as firewood, and every one of them had been scraped clean with a knife. I am going back to Markarth and I am never eating meat again.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachcliff_cave.rum: Something's living in Reachcliff Cave that leaves bones picked clean. Not wolves. Wolves don't use knives.

place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_rock.hoo: An ancient tomb hidden in the cliffs where the Reach's waters spill from the rock. Grave robbers use its outer halls as a hideout and have not yet learned to fear the inner ones.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_rock.rob:
Share-out, 20th of Last Seed:
Silver urn from the outer hall: sold in Markarth, 60 septims, split five ways.
Draugr rings: 4, sold, 30 septims. Kalf wants his own share for doing the prising. Kalf gets a fist.
Orichalcum axe, from the Orc stronghold at Dushnikh Yal (the night raid): NOT sold. Nobody in Markarth will touch it. Orc carvings on the haft, a grudge-mark, they say.
Note to self: the inner door has a puzzle of claws and pillars. Kalf thinks he's worked it out. If he's wrong we lose Kalf. If he's right we get rich. Either way the shares go further.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_rock.rum: The diggers in Reachwater Rock robbed an Orc stronghold and sold the loot in Markarth. Bold. Stupid, but bold. The Orcs want their axe back.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_rock.sk4: Folio #37 (-2550, -60): Field inspection recorded for Reachwater Rock within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_rock.tom:
Rendered from the old runes:
Here sleep the oath-keepers of the Reachwater. Water runs from the rock and memory runs from the dead. Drink the one and you will live. Take the other and you will join us.
Below, freshly scratched: Kalf drank from the pool. Kalf's fine. Kalf took a ring off a body. Kalf's not fine.

A third line, scratched hard into the stone beside the door, in the same rough hand:
Kalf woke them. They're all awake now. Fjotra says the Orc axe brought the bad luck and wants to throw it in the pool. I say we sell it back to the Orcs. Fjotra says the Orcs will kill us. I say the draugr will kill us first.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwater_sealed_a: A weathered Nordic stone arch wedged into a narrow canyon wall, its iron grates welded shut over a flooded subterranean stair.
Prospectors near Reachwater say you can hear water hammering against bronze doors deep behind the Sealed Arch.

The outer lintel bears First Era quarantine marks cut over older Reach-clan spirals. Whoever barred this side-entrance to the river caverns poured molten lead into the hinge-sockets so the iron grate could never be lifted from outside.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwind_eyrie.hoo: A wind-scoured Nordic watchtower on a crag above Dushnikh Yal's valley, where hawks nest in the broken battlements and old signal fires still smudge the stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwind_eyrie.rum: The Orcs of Dushnikh Yal climb up to Reachwind Eyrie to take hawk chicks for training. Brave lot. The wind up there's taken more men than the Forsworn ever did.
place_lore.nirncraft.reachwind_eyrie.sig:
A tally of fire-codes carved by the Nord wardens who held this tower in the Second Era:
ONE FIRE: Reachmen on the river.
TWO FIRES: Reachmen in the hills.
THREE FIRES: dragon. (This line has been scratched out, then carved again, then scratched out once more.)

Added later, by an Orc hand, in thick strokes:
No Nord wardens here now. Only Gashna's hawks and the wind. If you come for chicks, leave a strip of meat for the mother. She remembers the ones who don't.

place_lore.nirncraft.reapers_henge.hook: A stone circle with a bone-white altar on a rise in Reaper's March, where the Pact's tithe-walks end and the forest lays its yearly gift.
place_lore.nirncraft.reapers_henge.rumou: Do not count the stones at Reaper's Henge. The first Warden who did came up with eleven, and the second with thirteen, and neither would say which they preferred.
place_lore.nirncraft.reapers_henge.tithe:
#THE TITHE-WALK
Begin at the east stone. Walk sunwise. Carry the gift in your left hand, the lamp in your right. At the altar, say nothing. Leave the gift. Do not look behind you. Do not answer the voice, if it asks for more.
It will ask for more. The Wardens have been very clear: it is not yours to give.
place_lore.nirncraft.rebels_cairn.hook: A barrow raised over Faolan the Red Eagle, the Reach king who would not kneel. The Forsworn guard it as a holy place, and now someone else is digging.
place_lore.nirncraft.rebels_cairn.necro_: The Red Eagle's bones are not ordinary bones. A man who gave his heart to the hagravens and still walked keeps the habit of walking. With the right working he will walk for me.

The Forsworn who come to pray are a nuisance. Killed two. Raised one. He is a poor servant, keeps trying to kneel at the tomb.
The Eagle's sword is not here, which annoys me. The Forsworn at Red Eagle Redoubt have it, I suspect. No matter. I want the king, not his cutlery. One more night of chanting and the seal on the inner chamber breaks.
place_lore.nirncraft.rebels_cairn.reach_:
Chipped into a standing stone at the entrance, in the Reach tongue, with a Nord's translation chalked beneath:
~Here lies the Eagle, who would not bow.

~He gave his heart for one more spring.
~The spring came. The Eagle fell.
~Wake him, and he will fight again. Let him sleep, and he will dream us free.

Beneath the lament, painted fresh in ochre: The pale man with candles came last night. He spat on the Eagle's stone and called it a rock. Three of us went to drive him off. One came back, and that one now walks the cairn with empty eyes and kneels to nobody. Briarhearts of Red Eagle Redoubt, if you hear this, come.
place_lore.nirncraft.rebels_cairn.rumour: They say Red Eagle sleeps in Rebel's Cairn with his sword on his chest. Lately someone with a shovel and a lot of candles has been poking around up there.
place_lore.nirncraft.rebels_cairn.sk4_no: Folio #29 (-2054, -486): Field inspection recorded for Rebels Cairn within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.red_eagle_redoubt.h: A Forsworn stronghold in the hills by Karthspire, named for the Red Eagle and fiercely held by those who keep his memory. His sword is said to lie somewhere in its depths.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_eagle_redoubt.k:
Carved in the Reach tongue and painted with ochre, renewed every spring:
WE ARE THE EAGLE'S FEATHERS. WE GUARD HIS TALON. WHOEVER TAKES IT WITHOUT HIS BLESSING TAKES IT FROM OUR HANDS AND OUR HANDS DO NOT OPEN.
Below, newer: Rebel's Cairn is disturbed. A pale man with candles. Send three Briarhearts. Send all.

And under that, a third carving, crude and furious:
The pale man has been driven off for now. Two Briarhearts dead. The cairn's seal holds. Whoever comes to this door with Nord steel and no blessing, know that the Eagle's feathers do not forgive. Know also that we are tired, and that tired men fight harder.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_eagle_redoubt.n:
Counted fifteen Forsworn at Red Eagle Redoubt, including two Briarhearts and one crone. They go out by the south path to Karthspire Camp and to the river at Soljund's Sinkhole.
Their chief speaks of an old sword as if it were a living king. The men treat the inner chamber as a shrine. Recommend we leave it alone until we have the men. Recommend we never have the men.

Added at the bottom in the steward's hand: The Jarl agrees. Red Eagle Redoubt is to be marked on the maps and avoided. Any adventurer who wishes to try it may do so at their own expense and with their own life. The Jarl regrets in advance. The Jarl does not offer a refund.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_eagle_redoubt.r: Red Eagle Redoubt is where the Forsworn keep their pride. And their old king's sword, if the songs are right. Nobody's been in to check and come out.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_eagle_redoubt.s: Folio #31 (-2307, -364): Field inspection recorded for Red Eagle Redoubt within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.red_mountain.ash_pi:
#First day of the climb
My Ashlander guide left me at the foot of the slope. She said, 'from here the mountain is your guide'. She did not say whether it was a good one.

#Second day
Ash to my knees. A shape followed me all afternoon at the edge of the haze, too tall to be a man, too still to be a beast. When the wind cleared, there was nothing. There were footprints, though. Bare. Pointing up the mountain, not down.

#Third day
I reached the bowl of water the pilgrims leave below the crater. It was full. Someone had filled it today. Someone up here drinks. I am going on. If I do not come down, tell the Temple that the mountain is not empty. Tell them it is listening.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_mountain.hook: The volcano at the heart of Vvardenfell, still smoking two centuries after the Heart was broken and decades after the Red Year. Ash storms, ash creatures, and the Ghostfence are all that stand between it and the island.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_mountain.ordina: All patrols on the mountain slope will move in fours. No patrol will follow a voice in the ash. If a voice calls you by your name, you will answer only with the Litany of the Three, aloud, until it stops.

Sleepers found on the slopes are to be restrained and carried to the Ghostfence, not slain, unless they are no longer what they were. The distinction is yours to make. The Temple trusts you to make it. The Temple will also judge you if you make it wrongly. Walk with Vivec.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_mountain.rumour: Don't climb the mountain without an Ashlander guide and a Temple blessing, and even then, don't. Sleepers walk down from it in the storms. Whatever's up there isn't finished with us.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_road_pass.hook: A narrow pass through red-stained rock south of Windward Ruins, held by a family of giants. A Dawnstar ore sled went through it last month and came out in pieces.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_road_pass.rumou: They call it the Red Road because of the rocks. Or because of the sledders who tried to rush the giants. Depends who's telling it.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_road_pass.sk4_n: Folio #11 (32, -1381): Field inspection recorded for Red Road Pass within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.red_road_pass.sled_:
To the foreman at Iron-Breaker Mine.
As ordered, I took the short road south through the pass with four loads of iron and the strongbox with the month's ore money. The giants were not where they usually are. Then they were. One of them took the lead ox by the horns and threw it.

We ran. All of us, thank Kyne. But the sled and the strongbox are still up there among the mammoth bones. The giants have set the box by their fire like a footstool. I am not going back for it, foreman. You can dock my pay. You will be docking it anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_rook_camp.hook: At place.nirncraft.red_rook_camp, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the rain-soaked moors and ancient cairns of Glenumbra, where Camlorn's cathedral clergy and the Beldama Wyrd keep uneasy watch over the barrow-dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_rook_camp.rumou: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.red_rook_camp report signs of moorland werewolf packs, barrow-wights, and Llugwych blood-courtiers operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.red_rook_camp.v8_lo:

Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

place_lore.nirncraft.redorans_retreat.ch:
Thorgar,
We've got the courier's satchel. Most of it is rubbish: a Rorikstead widow's will, a love letter, three bills from Belethor. But one is sealed by the Steward of Whiterun, and that one might be worth more than the rest of this cave.

I've put it in the iron box with the rest of the satchel. Nobody opens that box but me. If the Steward wants it back, he can pay. If he sends guards instead, we burn it.

And tell the lads to stop wearing the courier's boots. They are too small for all of you, and you look ridiculous. Astrid.
place_lore.nirncraft.redorans_retreat.ho: A bandit cave in the hills west of Whiterun, named for a Dunmer exile who held it long ago. Its new masters prey on couriers on the western road.
place_lore.nirncraft.redorans_retreat.re:
On the cave wall, half covered by bandit soot, an old carving in the Dunmeri script. A rough translation has been chalked beside it by some later visitor:

'I, Faryn of House Redoran, was cast out for honour. Here I kept my honour alone. Let no thief shelter in this place.'
Under it, in fresh charcoal: 'Too late, Faryn.'

Further along the wall, a second old carving, smaller and more careful: a list of names, each with a mark beside it. Faryn's guests, perhaps, or Faryn's dead. The last name in the list is his own, carved by someone else, and under it the word for 'honoured' in the Dunmeri script.
place_lore.nirncraft.redorans_retreat.ru: Redoran's Retreat is a bandit hole now. They robbed Kjeld the courier last month, stripped him to his smallclothes and sent him walking. He's still angry about the boots.
place_lore.nirncraft.redorans_retreat.sk: Folio #27 (-557, -232): Field inspection recorded for Redorans Retreat within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.redwater_den.den_ru:
1. Guests pay upstairs. Guests drink downstairs. Guests never go back up the stairs.
2. Feed them the red twice a day. They grow docile. They grow warm. They grow very, very sweet.
3. Nobody touches the young Nord from Riften. He's reserved. He has his mother's eyes and I mean to have them.
4. Our Black-Briar casks come back empty and go out full. Whoever is rolling them through Greenwall does not know what is in them and does not need to. A good partnership is a quiet partnership.
place_lore.nirncraft.redwater_den.hjalma:
My name is Hjalmar. I came for Edda. Edda's dead. They drank her. They're not people. Their mouths are red and it isn't the skooma.

I've stopped drinking the red so I can stay awake. If my mother sends anyone, my copper bracelet is in the box by the stairs. They took it the first night. I want her to have it, whatever happens to me.
place_lore.nirncraft.redwater_den.hook: A modest cabin by a spring in the hills north-west of the lake. The skooma sold in the Ratway comes from here, red as blood and sweet as berries, and the people who come for more go down below and stay.
place_lore.nirncraft.redwater_den.rumour: There's a cabin up by a red spring where they sell a sweeter kind of skooma. Folk go up for a taste and never come down. Hjalla's son went up there after his mother's friend.

place_lore.nirncraft.refugees_rest.bandi: What we got: 3 sacks of grain off the Hollyfrost road, 1 Imperial saddle, 2 bows (one good), 1 urn with grey dust in it and a pretty silver band round the neck.

Tried to sell the urn at the Grey Quarter. Old Dunmer woman at the market went white as snow and offered me 100 septims for it, so I knew it was worth 500. Told her to come up here and haggle. She hasn't. Yet.
Note to self: tip the dust out before we sell it. Nobody wants a pot full of dead elf.
place_lore.nirncraft.refugees_rest.hook: A crumbling watchtower on the eastern hills where Dunmer fleeing the Red Mountain sheltered their first Skyrim winter, and where their ashes still rest beneath the bandits' bedrolls.
place_lore.nirncraft.refugees_rest.refug:
#4E 5, Evening Star
We walked from Ebonheart with the mountain behind us and the sky raining fire. We came over the snow with nothing but our dead. Here, at last, the Nords let us stop.

~Here lie Saryoni Ralen, potter, who carried her kiln-tools across three provinces.
~Here lies Dravil Ralen, her son, who carried her.
~Here lie the eleven whose names the cold took before we could carve them.
~Do not forget us. We will not forget you.
place_lore.nirncraft.refugees_rest.rumou: Refugees' Rest? The Dunmer call it a shrine. The bandits who sleep there call it a roof. I don't think either of them would like the other's word for it.
place_lore.nirncraft.refugees_rest.sk4_n: Folio #11 (2387, -713): Field inspection recorded for Refugees Rest within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #11 for refugees_rest: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Refugees Rest are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
Gideon was where an Imperial empress was born, they say, a girl of Black Marsh who went to the White-Gold Tower. The Imperials built her a statue in the square. The Saxhleel tell a different story: that she went north because the Hist told her to, and that she never stopped hearing its voice in the Tower.
The plantation houses round Gideon are being stripped for stone. The Saxhleel take the walls and leave the ballrooms open to the rain. Lovely in a storm, I hear.
An Imperial magistrate near Gideon still keeps Saxhleel in 'debt-service'. The King has noticed. People who are noticed by the King don't stay noticed for long.
The Mages Guild in Gideon lost a scholar to the marsh. Lirrian, a Breton. Went out to read with the Hist and the Daedra and came back... well, she didn't.

When the Saxhleel marched north into Morrowind in the Red Year's wake, the warriors of Helstrom were first across the border. They came back carrying nothing but the chains their grandparents had worn, and they sank them in the black pool at the edge of town. The pool has never been clear since.
Helstrom's closest to the Dunmer border and the most nervous for it. When the wind blows from the north the Saxhleel smell ash and the old ones start sharpening their spears.
There are Morag Tong in the marsh near Helstrom. They walk like they own the paths. The Shadowscales are not pleased.
The shrines of the Dunmer's House of Troubles stand just north of Helstrom, right on the border. Raiders from both sides camp near them, because nobody honest goes there.

The Hist were here before the land. They dreamed the marsh and then they dreamed the Saxhleel to walk in it. When an Argonian dies, the Hist remembers them, and if you lay your cheek against the bark of your egg-tree on a still night, you can hear your grandmother's voice, faint, in the sap.

Before the Saxhleel, the Kothringi lived in the marsh, silver-skinned folk who traded with everyone. Then came the Knahaten Flu, and in a single season they were gone, every one. The Saxhleel did not catch it. Nobody has ever proven why. Some Imperials still say the Hist did it on purpose. The Hist does not answer.

The Shadowscales are hatched under the moonless sign of the Shadow and given to the Sithis of the marsh to raise. A mother who gives up a Shadowscale egg weeps for one night only, and then never speaks of it again, and the whole village honours her silence.

Lilmoth was drowned once, in the age of the Kothringi, and raised again by the Hist in a single night. The fishers say that on the lowest tide of the year you can still see the old Kothringi rooftops below the harbour, silver as their makers, and lights moving in the windows.
Lilmoth's harbour is full of ships from everywhere. Khajiit from Senchal, Redguards, even a Thalmor cutter, which nobody here invited and nobody here will sell water to.
The old Imperial customs house in Lilmoth sank into the harbour mud when the Empire left. The customs-master's strongbox went with it, so they say, full of every bribe paid in thirty years.
The King of Argonia holds court in Lilmoth with no crown, no throne and no guards that you can see. You can't see the Shadowscales either. That's rather the point.

In Murkmire they say the Hist of each village chooses one hatchling in a generation to carry the village's whole memory. That child never learns to read and never needs to. Ask them anything about the village's past and they will answer in the voice of whoever was there.
Somebody's been stealing hatchling eggs from Murkmire and selling them to Imperial collectors. The Egg-Keeper's posted guards. The guards are her grandsons. They're very serious about it.
Murkmire's the deep marsh. Paths move. Trees walk. If a Saxhleel offers to guide you, pay what they ask and don't argue.
Archeins and Bright-Throats are feuding again in the Murkmire villages. Over a stolen canoe, this time. Last time it was a song.
The King's envoy in Stormhold signs contracts with a claw-mark now, not a seal. The Imperials left their seals behind when they left. The Saxhleel left them in the mud.
There's sickness in the roots of the great Hist, they say. The sap-thieves are bleeding the trees while they're weak. Everybody's angry and nobody can say at whom.
Dunmer slavers haven't dared the border in forty years, but something's been taking Saxhleel off the Shadowfen paths. Somebody's chains have come back.
Imperial plantations round Gideon stand empty, half of them. Vines through the windows. The Lukiul who stayed say the houses sigh at night for their old masters. Good, say the others.
A skooma barge from Senchal ran aground off Lilmoth. The whole harbour was singing for three days. The King has asked very politely that it not happen again.
The old Daedric stones in the Shadowfen were built by Dunmer, Imperials, Kothringi, nobody remembers. The Saxhleel let them stand. The Hist didn't object, so neither do we.

The Shadowfen is where the Knahaten Flu first rose, the elders say, from a pool that no Saxhleel will drink from. The Kothringi drank from it. The pool is still there, still clear and sweet, and the herons won't land on it.
The Shadowfen's stitched with Daedric shrines along the Morrowind border. Dunmer raised some, Imperials raised others. The Saxhleel just call them 'the noisy stones'.
Rot-eaters at the Namira stones south of Mournhold have a pale stone that glows at dusk. They light their feasts by it. It was stolen from the Dunmer, they say. They say it like a joke.
Somebody's taking Saxhleel off the Shadowfen paths and chaining them at the Molag Bal stones near the Necrom border. Somebody who speaks Dunmeri and wears a Hlervu ring.
Root in the water, water in the root,
Egg in the mud and the mud in the fruit,
We were here before the Empire, we'll be here when it's gone,
The Hist remembers everyone, and the marsh goes on.
Root and Water

Stormhold was a Saxhleel town before the Imperials built their walls around it, and it will be a Saxhleel town when the walls are moss. The elders say that when the Imperial governor raised his flag over the gate, the river rose and drowned the flagpole up to the eagle's neck, and left it there.
Stormhold's still half Imperial stone and half Saxhleel reed. The Lukiul who keep the old customs-house still write their ledgers in Cyrodilic, out of habit, and the young ones mock them for it.

Five Daedric shrines in a row in the marsh west of Stormhold, close as beads on a string. The elders say an Imperial governor built them, one a year, trying to find a Prince who'd keep him alive in the swamp. None did.
A Gideon scholar went to read at the Hermaeus Mora stones west of town. Her assistant came back alone and wouldn't stop counting his fingers.
The Shadowscales are hiring again. Not hiring. Choosing. Same thing, if they choose you.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.bla: The Blackwood is so named because the trees drink so much black water their heartwood turns dark as ebony. Carpenters who use it say the boards creak at night in a language nobody in Leyawiin speaks, but every Argonian in Leyawiin pretends not to understand.
Leyawiin's Count has doubled the guard on the river gate since the Argonians took back Blackwood's south bank in the last age. They never forgave and we never forgot.
A noblewoman of Leyawiin buried her third husband this spring. Lovely funeral. She wore Mephala's black, which some folk thought a peculiar choice.
The marsh between Leyawiin and the Vaermina stones is full of sleepers. Folk who lay down to rest in the reeds and won't wake. Their eyes move under the lids.
Fighters Guild lads are pulling mudcrabs as big as cartwheels out of the Blackwood flats. Good eating if you can get the shell off before it gets your hand.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.col: The Colovian horse-lords swore oaths on their swords, never on gods, because gods change their minds and steel doesn't. That's why a Colovian's handshake is worth more than a Nibenese contract, and why Colovians are so bad at contracts.
The Great Oak in Chorrol dropped a branch the size of a cart on the chapel steps. The priests call it an omen. The carpenters call it firewood.
There's a fellow in Chorrol, Ostorius Varro, who was drowning in debt last spring. Now he's dry and every one of his creditors is dead. Ask him how and he goes white.
The Fighters Guild posted a bounty on goblins in the hills west of town. Twenty drakes an ear. My cousin's been sharpening his knife and practising his growl.
The beggars of Chorrol walk south to the old Namira stones every new moon and come back fat. Nobody asks what they eat out there. Nobody wants to know.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.gol: Anvil's lighthouse was lit once by a woman whose husband never came back from the Abecean. She kept it burning forty years, and when she died the lamp went out on its own. The keepers say it gutters, still, whenever a widow climbs the stairs.
The East Empire Company has three new ships in Anvil harbour and not one sailor willing to crew them for Company wages. They're hiring Khajiit and Redguards off the docks and paying in promises.
Kvatch's masons are mostly Orcs now, hired out of the Valus. They do good work and they hold a grudge for a hundred years if you shortchange them.
Pirates off the Abecean have a new captain. They say she spares any ship that flies a Kvatch flag. Nobody knows why, which makes it worse.
A boy digging in the Kvatch rubble found a Count's seal-ring. The steward took it off him and gave him a single drake. That's Gold Coast justice for you.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.hea: The White-Gold Tower was raised by the Ayleids around a stone that sings. Every hundred years, on a still night, the Tower hums a single note, and every glass in the city rings in answer. The last time, folk say, was the night before the Elves came over the walls.
The Arena's got a new Grand Champion every other season since the war. Fixed fights, they say. The Blue Team's bettors drink at the Waterfront and they're never short of coin.
There's lights at the old shrine of Meridia north-east of the city again, and not the good kind. A shepherd saw bones walking in a line, like pilgrims.
The Thalmor Embassy took another house on the Talos Plaza. Nobody sold it to them. The family just isn't there anymore.
The Rumare's full of eels this year. My father says that means a hard winter; my mother says it means my father should mend the nets instead of talking.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.jer: When the Gate opened outside Bruma in the Crisis, the Nords of the town sang the old war songs so loud that the dremora at the gate faltered. The town still sings them every Frostfall, on the night of the battle, and no one in Bruma is ever allowed to stop mid-verse.
A woodcutter out of Bruma went up the north trail for pine and came back without his axe, his boots or his voice. He writes on slates now. He writes the same word over and over: 'chains'.
There's a ring of fighters at the old Boethiah stones south-west of town. Sell-swords from both sides of the border, cutting each other for coin and for a Prince who keeps no score.
The Pale Pass is open early this year. Nords coming down, Nords going up, and every second wagon has a false bottom.
Snow-trolls took two goats off the Hrodmund place. The Count's huntsmen are 'considering the matter'. Meanwhile we eat porridge.
Stone at our backs and the snow at our feet,
The sky burning red and no road for retreat,
We sang till the mountains sang with us again,
And the gate fell silent, and so did the men.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.leg: When the Gates opened, two hundred years gone, the sky over Kvatch burned for a night and a day. Gold Coast farmers still won't plough the hill where the first Gate stood. Whatever grows there, they say, comes up the colour of rust and tastes of ash.

Before men, the Heartland belonged to the Ayleids, who built in white stone and kept captive stars in glass. Their welkynd stones still glow in the ruins. A farmer who carries one home will find his milk soured and his dog barking at the cellar door, until he carries it back.

In the Temple District stands a dragon of stone, caught mid-roar over the ruin of the old Temple of the One. The priests say the last of the Septims became that dragon. Children are told that if they lay a hand on its claw and tell the truth, it is warm; if they lie, it is cold as a grave.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.nib: The Nibenese say every river in the Basin is a strand of a single net cast by the Divines to hold the Heartland together. Where a strand is cut, by a dam or a bridge built without a priest, the land on either side quarrels for a hundred years.
Cheydinhal's Dunmer have opened a third shrine to the Tribunal in the old Imperial chapel cellar. The Count pretends it's a wine store.
A Mages Guild scholar went up to the Hermaeus Mora stones north of the city with forty books and a mule. The mule came back.
Don't buy a house in Cheydinhal that's going cheap. My brother-in-law did, and he's never got the smell out of the cellar.
Thieves in the Nibenay pray to Nocturnal at the stones west of Cheydinhal before a big job. If the night is moonless they take it as a yes.

Bravil was built where the Niben drowns its secrets. Every flood leaves something on the bank: a ring, a door, once a whole boat with the table laid for supper. The Bravilese throw back anything they can't explain, and they can't explain most things.
The Lucky Old Lady in Bravil turned her face a finger's breadth east in the night. Every skooma-boatman on the river's laying bets on what it means.
Hooded folk camp by the old Dagon shrine west of town. The watch counted nine of them. The Imperial Cult wants a sword sent; the watch wants a raise first.
The Mad God's shrine north-west of Bravil has a new offering bowl. It's a soup tureen. It's full of buttons. Nobody admits to the buttons.
A dream-seller in the Bravil slums sells sleep by the hour. You lie in her loft and wake with somebody else's memories. Half the beggars in town are hooked on it.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.rum: Justiciars walked a man out of the Elven Gardens in irons last Loredas. A Talos amulet sewn into his coat lining, they say. His wife still lays a place for him at supper.
Kvatch has walls again. Not a whole city, mind, but walls, with the Count's banner on them for the first time since the Gates. Savlian Matius says the rest will take a generation.
The Gold Road toll went up two drakes at Skingrad. The Count says it pays for bridges. I've walked that road twice this month and I've yet to see a new bridge.
Half of Cheydinhal speaks Dunmeri now. Ever since the mountain burst, the refugees kept coming over the Valus passes, and they never stopped coming.
Bravil's watch found another skooma boat under the bridge, loaded to the gunwales with Senchal sugar. The Khajiit on the docks swear they've never seen it before in their lives.
The old Daedric shrines out in the wilds have been busy since the war. More smoke, more offerings. When the Nine go quiet, folk start knocking on other doors.
Bruma sells iron north over the mountains and calls it trade with kin. The Legion pretends not to notice, so long as the Stormcloaks keep their quarrel on their own side of the Jeralls.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.son: Round the White-Gold the Elves made a ring,
Steel on the water and fire on the wing,
Twelve thousand fell where the Rumare runs red,
And the Emperor rode with the living and dead.
Drink to the Ring, lads, and drink to the cost,
And never ask after the treaty we lost.
Up from Kvatch with a load of stone,
Down from Skingrad with wine for home,
Mind the bandit and mind the toll,
And the Gold Road will take its share of your soul.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.cyrodiil.wes: The first vine of the West Weald was planted by a Colovian soldier who swore he'd never shed blood again. He made wine instead of war, and the Weald grapes are red because they drink what he gave up. Skingrad vintners still pour the first cup of every barrel onto the soil.
The Count of Skingrad's never seen at noon. Never. My grandfather says he wasn't seen at noon in his grandfather's day either.
There's a revel in the hills between Skingrad and Kvatch where the wine never runs out and the guests never leave. A vintner's daughter went last month. She's still dancing, they say.
Hunters out of Skingrad won't shoot a white stag in the Weald. Last fellow who did woke with the antlers on his pillow and the stag nowhere in sight.
Tomato blight's in the lower vineyards and a cough's going through the farms by the Peryite shrine. Same week, same farms. You don't need a priest to add that up.
One for the Count and one for the cellar,
One for the stranger and one for the teller,
Drink up the Shiraz and drink up the Tamika,
And thank the Nine there's no Skingrad seeker.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.aneq: Anequina was once a kingdom of horse-lords and desert warriors, and Pellitine a kingdom of silk and temples. The Mane married the two together, and like any old married couple they still keep separate rooms and quarrel about the cooking.
The Mane sits in Riverhold and the Thalmor sit nearby with their hands folded. Nobody in Anequina has seen a Thalmor smile. This one thinks perhaps they cannot.
There are slavers at the Molag Bal stones south of Riverhold, taking Khajiit for the mines of the High Elves, they say. The Mane's guard says they are only rumours. The rumours have chains.
The Sanguine stones west of Riverhold had a moon-sugar revel so loud last month that the Mane's own cooks went to join it. Dinner was very late.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.lege: Azurah made the Khajiit from the Bosmer who lived in Elsweyr, shaping each kind by the phase of the moons on the night it was born: the great Senche, the swift Cathay, the small and clever Ohmes. That is why a Khajiit's form is a matter of the sky, and why every Khajiit mother watches the moons on the night her cubs come.

The Lunar Lattice is the road the moons walk, and the Khajiit are its keepers. When the moons went dark in the Void Nights, the Moon-Priests did not run. They sat in the temples and sang to the empty sky every night for two years, and when the moons came back, the first thing they saw was a Khajiit still singing.

Namiira is the Great Darkness, the first thing, older than the Lattice. Khajiit whose souls fall into her when they die become Dro-m'Athra, the dark-souled, who hunger for the moons' light because they can no longer find it. That is why Khajiit leave a candle burning for the newly dead, so that they can see the way home.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.pell: Boethra, whom the Khajiit call the Clever Warrior, taught the first Pellitine swordmasters that the strongest blow is the one your enemy does not see coming. That is why the Pellitine schools teach courtesy first: a warrior who bows deeply has already measured your stance.
A warrior called Hazadir holds the Boethiah stones in the Pellitine hills and fights any who challenge him. Nine have challenged. Nine have died. All nine had their tea with him first.
The Pellitine sword-schools train their students to fight blindfolded, by smell and sound. A blindfolded Khajiit is still a better duellist than a sighted Nord, they say. Never say this to a Nord.
The jungle road south of the sword-schools floods every spring, and the caravans that wait it out always pay the same toll: one story each, told by the fire, and it had better be new.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.rimm: Rimmen was built by a Khajiit queen who loved an Imperial merchant and wanted a city that faced both ways, north to his country and south to hers. She built two great gates and never decided which was the front. The citizens still argue about it.
Rimmen sits closest to Cyrodiil and the Thalmor watch it closest. The Renrijra Krin watch the Thalmor. Everybody in Rimmen watches everybody. It is a very attentive city.
Hunters out of Rimmen went to the Hircine stones west of the city to ask for a good senche-hunt. They came back with a senche cub that follows them everywhere. The cub is now larger than the hunters.
An Imperial pilgrim from Bravil lives at the Meridia stones north of Rimmen. She burns things. Mostly the dead. This one is glad they are mostly the dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.rumo: The Mane receives the Thalmor envoys in Riverhold with every courtesy and sends them home with nothing. This one thinks the Mane has been doing it for forty years and is very good at it.
Moon sugar is dear this season. The Moon-Bishop says the fields are being raided. The skooma-cooks say the Moon-Bishop is raising prices. Both are probably telling the truth, which is very annoying.
The Renrijra Krin laugh in the dunes outside Rimmen and steal from Thalmor wagons. The Thalmor call them bandits. Many Khajiit call them cousins. A few call them dinner guests.
A caravan stopped for water at the Peryite stones south of Rimmen and came to Torval with half its people coughing and walking in straight lines. Ri'jasha the caravaneer is looking for a brave fool.
The Elves say they saved the moons. In the Void Nights, the moons went dark, and the Thalmor brought them back, and they never, ever let the Khajiit forget it.
Senchal's harbour has more skooma in it than water, the sailors say. That's a lie, of course. It's about even.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.senc: Rajhin the Footpad stole a tattoo from the neck of the Empress while she slept, and sold it back to her the next morning without her ever knowing it had been missing. Senchal's thieves say this is the finest theft ever done, because nothing was harmed and everyone profited, and Rajhin got breakfast.
Senchal is the city of thieves and the thieves are proud of it. Rajhin was born here, they say, the greatest thief of all. Every pickpocket in the city claims to be his great-great-grandcub.
Somebody robbed the Nocturnal stones west of Senchal. Robbed the shrine of a thief-god. Every honest thief in Senchal is furious.
Smugglers in Senchal sell anything: sugar, silk, swords, secrets. The Thalmor customs post takes a share. The Renrijra Krin take the customs post. Business goes on.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.song: Masser is the elder and Secunda is the small,
Masser takes the long way and Secunda takes it all,
Dance them on the Lattice, dance them through the sand,
And one day they will dance you home, with sugar in your hand.
Up from Senchal, down from Rimmen,
Twelve good wagons and one bad cousin,
Sugar for the Bishop and silk for the Mane,
And this one walks the sands again.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.elsweyr.torv: Torval was built on the place where the moons touched the sand. The Moon-Priests say if you stand in the great court at midnight on the Two-Moons Dance, your shadow falls in two directions at once, and one of them is the shadow of who you will become.
The Moon-Bishop Hadoba says the Lattice is strong this year. She says it every year. This one has never once seen her look worried, which worries this one.
A caravan came into Torval sick and coughing, from the Peryite stones north of the city. Ri'jasha the caravaneer escaped it. Her people did not. She waits in the market for a hero.
The Clavicus stones north of Torval grant wishes to merchants. Khajiit merchants are very careful how they wish. Khajiit merchants are careful how they do everything.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.a: Sentinel's Necropolis is older than the city, and the priests of Tu'whacca say the first Redguard king of the Alik'r is buried there with his sword across his chest. When the city is in danger, the king turns in his tomb and the sword rings, and every Ansei in Sentinel hears it in his dreams.
Lord Hamaad's dying in Sentinel. Lady Yasreen's ready to take the chair. Her cousin Ahzid is dining with Forebears. Everyone in the Alik'r is placing bets.
The Ashtown elves lost their moonstone lamp to sand-raiders. Their priestess walks the dunes at night looking for it. Brave, for a Dunmer. Or foolish.
The grey silk in Skaven market comes from spiders at the Mephala stones. Pretty stuff. Wear it and you start hearing other people's secrets.
Nomads say the dreams from the Vaermina stones south of Sentinel have gone bad. They dream their deaths now, and the deaths come true before the dream.
Where the dunes turn red at evening and the jackals start to cry,
there's a well of sweet water that never will run dry;
but the man who dug it sold something he could not see,
and his son drinks the water, and his son is not free.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.b: Bangkorai's great fortress at the pass was built to keep the Bretons out of Hammerfell, then rebuilt to keep the Redguards out of High Rock, then rebuilt again to keep the Orcs out of both. The sentries say its stones remember every army that ever broke against them, and grumble on cold nights.
The Red Pass Company is holding the Bangkorai road again. They'll let you through for a toll. They'll also let your enemy through, for a bigger one.
Wayrest's caravans take the Bangkorai pass now, since the bay crossings got dear. The pass is cheaper. It's also full of sellswords and old shrines.
Somebody scratched 'Captain Oriel Sand-Tongue owes me money' on the Boethiah stone. Somebody else scratched 'Not any more' underneath.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.c: Over Craglorn the constellations of the Celestials once came down to walk the earth: the Warrior, the Mage and the Thief, and the Serpent, which eats the others. The Elinhir astronomers still chart the Serpent's slow crawl across the sky, and on the night it reaches the Warrior's heart, they say, Craglorn will burn again.
The springs north of Elinhir run red and hot as blood. The Ansei rode up to look and came back without a word. That's never good.
Somebody stole the Serpent Tower's great lens in Elinhir. The mages are offering a reward. The thieves are offering a better one, to keep quiet.
Craglorn's stars move, they say. Elinhir's mages watch them every night and argue about it every day. Nobody's sure which is worse.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.d: The Dragontail Mountains are said to be the spine of a dragon that Frandar Hunding's sword-singers slew in the first years after the Crossing. Its tail lies in the desert and its head in the sea, and the hot springs along the ridge are where its blood still runs.
The Ash'abah say a bone-singer's raised Old Jafar's whole caravan in the hills north of Rihad. Camels and all. You can hear the bells at night.
Old Qamar's well in Skaven was bought at the Clavicus stone. His son wants out of the bargain. Good luck to him. Princes don't refund.
Rihad's wine heirs went up to the Sanguine stones with twelve casks. They came back with a vineyard, a goat, and no memory of any of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.h: Hew's Bane is named for Hew the Wrathful, a Ra Gada warlord who tried to conquer the peninsula and was defeated not by its warriors but by its beasts: the lions came down from the hills by night and carried off his sentries one by one until his army fled. The hunters of the Hew's Bane hills still leave the first lion skull of each season at the Huntsman's stones, to thank the beasts for their help.
Yusuf the beast-trader's tiger escaped on the Taneth quay and went north over the wall. Now it's hunting by the Hircine stones. Yusuf's offering gold. The hunters are offering prayers.
Fisherfolk vanish from the villages north of Taneth. Lord Ezhar's put a price on the slaver Iron-Collar's head. Big price. Nobody's collected.
A Taneth captain gave his ship to Sheogorath and walked inland. He's been sailing the dunes for three years. Says the wind's better there.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.l: When Yokuda sank into the sea, the Ra Gada sailed east in the ships of Frandar Hunding, carrying nothing but their swords and their ancestors' names. The first thing they did when they reached the shore of Hammerfell was cut down everything in their way. The second thing was to bury their dead properly. A Redguard will forgive you for the first. Never for neglecting the second.

The Hiradirge was the warrior's path of the old Yokudan sword-masters, and the greatest among them could cut the very air between two moments. The Ansei say Frandar Hunding wrote the whole of the sword's teaching in a single book, and that a true student reads it once, then closes it forever, because the rest must be learned from the blade.

The Alik'r nomads say that the desert is the bed of a sea that once loved a man so much it dried itself out to follow him inland. Wherever you find a well in the sand, they say, the sea is still weeping for him.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.r: The Crowns and the Forebears are at each other's throats again. Same as every year. Only now there's no Empire to stop them and no Dominion to unite them, so it's real swords instead of polite ones.
Hammerfell threw the Thalmor out on its own, after the Emperor signed it away. Ask any Redguard about the White-Gold Concordat and watch his hand go to his sword.
The sword-singers are teaching again, in the old schools near Sentinel. They say an Ansei can make a blade out of nothing but his own spirit. I've seen it. It's not nothing.

Alik'r nomads came in from the deep desert talking about a city of sand that rose out of the dunes for one night, with lights in its windows. Nomads say a lot of things. They don't usually all say the same thing.
The Forebear merchants of Taneth are buying Dwemer brass by the cartload. Nobody knows why. The Crowns say they're building a fleet. The Forebears say they're decorating.
Orcs of Orsinium came down the Bangkorai pass to sell steel in Elinhir. Nobody fought anybody. My grandfather wouldn't believe it.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.hammerfell.s: Because no pious Redguard warrior may strike the risen corpse of an ancestor without staining his lineage, the Kings of Sentinel chartered the Order of the Candle and hired unsworn blades to keep the royal necropolis clean.
Beneath the white limestone domes of Sentinel Palace lies a cool vaulted cistern fed by subterranean qanats older than the Ra Gada landing.
The brass funerary lamps at Tu'whacca's Throne flickered green in the sea-fog last night, and the Knights of the Candle doubled the watch at the palace cisterns.
In Sentinel's Dyers' Quarter, Forebear ship-factors and Crown palace-bailiffs won't drink from the same well until the Betony customs tariff is settled.
Fishermen off Zauun Docks hauled up an embalming jar sealed with sea-kelp—the mark of the Coven of the Tide.
Trim the wick in the salt-wind, pour the oil in the brass,
Where the kings of the sand-sea in silence must pass;
Let the Crown keep the terrace, the Forebear the quay,
While the Candle stands watch o'er the dead and the sea.
Lamps of Tu'whacca's Throne
We left the drowned land singing,
our fathers' bones aboard;
we came ashore with nothing
but the memory of the sword.
And when they ask what Hammerfell is,
we answer with the sword.
The Crossing

Stros M'Kai was once the seat of Prince A'tor, who fought the armies of Tiber Septim from these rocks until the last of his ships went down. The islanders say his flagship lies just off the southern cliffs, and that on still nights its lanterns burn under the water, still waiting for the order to sail.
The Brinewash pirates took another of Captain Noraya's ships off the south cove. The Forebears are hiring every blade on the island.
Hakim the guide will take you to the Dwemer doors in the cliffs. He won't take you through them. Ask him about his brother. Actually, don't.
They still celebrate the treaty every year on the beach. Lots of fish, lots of wine, lots of speeches about the Dominion. The speeches get longer every year.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.an: When the first settlers cleared the woods around Alcaire Bay, they struck a boundary-oath with the Skeffington Coven: the axe would never cross the third brook, and the witches would never cross the plough-furrow.
In the courtyard of Alcaire Castle stands the well where young Emeric first swore to unite the bay's merchant roads against the highland raiders.
The burghers of Alcaire nail rowan-crosses above their lintels by day and leave birch-bundles at the forest edge by night so the Skeffington witches spare their cattle.
Preceptor Malo's Knights of the Flame have been stopping grain wagons between Alcaire and Weeping Giant, searching for witch-tallow in the flour sacks.
Miners at Koeglin swear the deepest adit broke into a brick vault where candles of red wax burn without smoke.
Leave a twist of white birch where the plough-iron turns,
Where the mara-lamp shines and the hearth-faggot burns;
For the wood has long ears and the knight has a brand,
And the tenant pays twice for the peace of the land.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.bj: The Bjoulsae, they say, was once the boundary between the lands of the Bretons and the Redguards, and a Redguard prince and a Breton princess drowned together trying to swim across it to meet. The river runs a little warmer on the night they died, and the bargemen leave two cups of wine on the bank to keep it from flooding.
The bargemen won't put in at the Namira landing any more. The beggars there smile too much and ask about the cargo too closely.
Huntmaster Lorne's called off the King's autumn hunt. He says it's a bear. Bears don't stand up and open doors.
Timber's down from Evermor, cheap and plenty. The river's high and the barges are fast this year. Something's got to go wrong. It always does.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.da: Before the Warp in the West folded thirty petty crowns into Castle Daggerfall's ledger, every bluff-lord kept his own seal-press and gallows-hill—and half those presses still turn in the cellars beneath the city.
Old sailors in Daggerfall harbour swear that King Lysandus's ghost only rests while the Betony beacon and the harbour chain are kept by honest hands.
Three baronial toll-collectors were found drained white beside the Daggerfall harbour chain, and the Dragon lancers are blaming the Owl's clerks.
The shepherds above Deleyn's Mill still leave unshorn wool on the bluff-stones so the Sisters of Ilessan keep the sea-fog off the lambs.
Every frost-moon a riderless warhorse is heard galloping from Cryngaine Field toward the outer barbican of Castle Daggerfall.
Raise the links at the turning tide, count the silver on the quay,
One coin for the Dragon's lance, one coin for the open sea;
But bolt your shutter when the blue fog climbs the sandstone stair,
For the old barons ride the bluff when the night-wind stirs the air.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.dw: The Order of the Raven was founded to hold the limestone passes of Dwynnen against upland monsters, but after three generations of border debt its preceptories became strongrooms for promissory tallies.
At Shinji's Scarp, Breton and Redguard veterans alike still drop an iron arrowhead into the cairn-trench before crossing the ridge.
Discharged pikemen from the Bjoulsae wars are camping on Shinji's Scarp, waiting to see whether Kambria's bailiffs or the deserter-captains pay better.
Three ravens perched on the Kambria assize-roof before the mortgage-rolls were read, and not a single farmer in the square dared bid on a foreclosed plot.
Smugglers using the karst sinkholes around Telaata say the underground streams carry carved elven gaming-pieces from a flooded vault.
My breastplate is pawned to the clerk in the hall,
My halberd hangs rusting on Kambria's wall;
Two crowns take the fleece and the raven takes toll,
While the karst-wind blows cold through the veteran's soul.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.gl: Long ago, Camlorn's dead would not stay in their graves, and walked the walls every winter night, calling the names of the living. The city's priests could do nothing. In the end a knight walked out to the bright stone south-east of the city and asked a Prince of Light for help, and the next dawn burned so fiercely that every ghost on the walls was gone. The knight was never seen again. Her shield hangs in the Dawn Chapel, and it is always warm.
Young lords keep riding out to the Boethiah stones north of Daggerfall. Then they come home and their elder brothers die in duels. Strange how that keeps happening.

The Masked Revel at the Sanguine stones west of Daggerfall's still going, they say. Started at the dark of the moon. Lord Aubin Gaudrel's mother wants him home. Lord Aubin Gaudrel seems to want otherwise.
Camlorn's merchants all got rich the same summer, and none of their daughters sing any more. I'm not saying there's a connection. I'm saying I've stopped singing near Camlorn.
There's a mad poet by the Sheogorath stone south of Camlorn who rhymes better than the Count's own bard. The Count's own bard has taken it very personally.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.le: The Bretons say their grandmothers' grandmothers were Nedes who married the elves of the Direnni, and that this is why a Breton can always talk his way into a tower and out of a dungeon. The Direnni tower still stands on its island in the bay, and old families leave a candle burning toward it on the longest night of the year, so the elves will remember they are owed nothing.

When the knights of Daggerfall and the warriors of Sentinel laid siege to Orsinium for thirty years in the First Era, the Orcs inside held out by eating their leather, then their boots, then their pride. When the walls finally fell, the Breton knights found the last Orc defenders sitting on the gate with their axes across their knees, too weak to stand and too proud to lie down. The Orcs have told that story to their children ever since, and they tell it as a victory.

Somewhere under the Wrothgar snows lies the old Orsinium, the first one, and the Orc smiths say its forges have never gone cold. Stand on the right mountainside on a still winter night and you can hear hammers under the ice.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.ri: Rivenspire's fogs are said to be the breath of a dragon that sleeps under the northern hills, and the great houses of Shornhelm each claim descent from a knight who once tried to wake it. None of them succeeded. All of them, in the family histories, came very close.
Shornhelm's children are walking in their sleep, all down the same road toward the Vaermina stones. The Sheriff's asking for help. The Council's asking about the cost.
The Dowager Tamrith wants her husband's sword back from the Molag Bal shrine west of the city. She's offering a fortune. She's also offering a lecture, so be ready.
Old Archivist Haldane went to the Mora shrine and came back knowing every noble secret in Rivenspire. Half the great houses want him dead. The other half want him to dinner.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.ru: Wayrest and Daggerfall are bowing to each other again this season. When two Breton kings bow that low, somebody's about to get stabbed under the table.
The Orcs have rebuilt Orsinium, bigger than before. The Breton lords keep talking about doing something about it. The Breton smiths keep quietly buying Orcish steel.
A hedge-witch in Stormhaven will read your fortune in a bowl of milk for two septims. For five she'll tell you whose fortune you're about to ruin.
Every Breton house has a mage in the family tree and a Daedra somewhere in the cellar. The trick is not to mention either at dinner.
Knights of the Dragon and Knights of the Rose both rode out to the Bangkorai pass this summer. Neither will say what for. Both came back with fewer horses.
Shornhelm's nobles are feuding again. One of them sent another a cake. Nobody's eaten it. It's been sitting on the council table for a week, and everybody's watching it.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.so: O bow to the Duke and bow to the Duchess,
and kiss the cold hand of the Count;
smile as you pour, keep your back to the door,
and never let on what you've found.
For the knife in the court is a courteous knife,
and it says 'by your leave' as it goes.
They burned our city, so we built it higher,
they burned it again, so we built it of fire;
count up the burnings, count up the stones,
Orsinium stands on a mountain of bones.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.st: Stormhaven is named, the old folk say, for a great storm that drove a fleet of Nedic ships onto its shore in the Merethic Era. The survivors married into the elves of the coast and became the first Bretons, and every great storm since has been the sea trying to take them back.
Lord Belcourt of the Old Lodge doesn't hunt by day any more. Only by night, and alone. His hounds won't come near him. His steward has started praying.
A hedge-witch near the Namira stones sells cures for the lung-rot. Works, they say. Don't ask what's in it.
Stormhaven's coast is full of old wrecks and older wreckers. If you see a lantern on the cliffs on a stormy night, don't steer toward it.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.wa: Wayrest was built by a merchant who bought a fishing village from its lord with a single pearl, then sold the lord the fish. The Wayresters say every coin in the city has passed through that first merchant's hands, and that if you listen at the bridges on a quiet night, you can hear the pearl rolling.
The Knights of the Rose have the docks quiet at last. Quiet docks in Wayrest, imagine. The fishwives don't know what to do with themselves.
Somebody's been burning circles in the grass by the Dagon shrine north of the city. The Watch is putting up notices. The Watch is always putting up notices.
Old Penhallow the apothecary had his whole case of cures stolen on the fen road. He keeps saying there's one recipe in it nobody should ever brew. Then he goes very pale and changes the subject.
Down by the Fish Bridge the fiddlers play,
the knights ride by at the close of day,
the widows walk where the Lady waits,
and the merchants count at the Bay Gate.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.high_rock.wr: Malacath, the Orcs say, was once the elven god Trinimac, until a trickster swallowed him and he came out changed, and his followers changed with him. The Orcs do not mourn what they were. They say they were made in the belly of a betrayal, and that is why they never forget one.
King Gurak's opened Orsinium's gates to traders from Wayrest and Sentinel both. The old Orc chiefs grumble. The young ones are buying silk shirts.
Ogres in the valley below the Malacath shrine again. Orsinium's smiths walk around them like they're furniture. Furniture that eats goats.
Smugglers carry Orcish steel down the passes west of Orsinium by night and sell it to Breton lords who swear they've never bought a single Orc blade.
Strike once for the mountain, strike twice for the clan,
strike thrice for the Furious One who made us what we are;
the snow on the anvil, the fire in the hand,
and the blade cools hard as a grudge.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.as: Vivec raised his city on the water so that no army could march on it, only sail, and no fleet could take it, because the cantons themselves would close their doors and float. Nobody has ever seen a canton float. Everyone in Vivec has an uncle who has.
The plantations along the Ascadian coast pay their field hands in coin now, by Imperial law. They pay in coin and charge for the roof. The sums come out much the same.
Somebody left a fresh heart at the Molag Bal stones between Balmora and Vivec. Not an animal heart, the Ordinators say. They're asking questions in every canton.
The Hlaalu councillors pray at the Boethiah stones before every council vote. Never together. Never on the same night.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.de: Mournhold was built where Almalexia first set her foot in the Deshaan, and for an age the city glowed at night from within. When she was gone, the glow went out house by house over a single winter. The last house to go dark is said to be the one where the city's first mason was born.
The Twilight Stone was stolen from Azura's shrine east of Mournhold by Argonian raiders, forty-three winters gone. Priestess Ilvari has been looking for it her whole life.
A Meridian zealot smashed the ancestor shrine of House Llethan's cousins near the Meridia stones. Called the bones an abomination. The family has posted a reward for his ears.
Mournhold's Great Bazaar has Argonian goods again, sold by Hlaalu factors who swear they came by way of Cyrodiil. They didn't.
The Orcs who work the Ebonheart docks go up to the Malacath stones on feast days. The Ordinators follow them. Nobody's come to blows yet.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.le: When the moon that Vivec held in the sky came down in the Red Year, it did not fall like a stone. It fell slowly, like a held breath let go, and those who saw it say it wept fire the whole way down. Some Dunmer still will not look at the sky on the anniversary.

Azura told the Chimer they would be changed, and they were: grey-skinned and red-eyed, the colour of ash and blood. The Ashlanders say this was not a curse but a reminder. A people who betray their hero should wear the colour of what that betrayal costs.

The Daedra whom the Dunmer call the House of Troubles stand at the four corners of the land like posts of a tent: Molag Bal, Malacath, Sheogorath, Mehrunes Dagon. Pull one post, and the tent sags. Pull all four and the sky falls in. So the Temple does not destroy their shrines. It watches them.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.mo: Necrom is the oldest city of the dead in Morrowind. Every Dunmer family wishes to rest there, and the dead are packed so close beneath the streets that the priests say a funeral is really a negotiation: the new arrival must be introduced, and the old ones must agree to move up.
Necrom's priests are asking for help in the City of the Dead. Grave-robbers broke a dozen urns last month and carried off the ashes for some Daedric rite.
Red-robed worshippers at the Dagon stones west of Necrom. The Ordinators went in five strong and came back four. The Temple's quiet about the fifth.
The pilgrims to Necrom say the Mad God's shrine on the road talks to you if you walk past it alone. It asks after your mother. It knows her name.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.re: Red Mountain is the Heart's grave, the Ashlanders say. Lorkhan's heart was hidden beneath it, and every Dunmer feels it beat at least once in their life, usually on the night before something terrible.
The Ghostfence still holds, the Temple says. The Temple also said the moon would never fall.
The Morag Tong walk up to the Mephala stones under the mountain's shoulder. They say there are spiders nesting there now, big as netch.
Ash pilgrims climb the mountain every Mid Year and leave bowls of water at the crater's lip. Most of them come back down. Most.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.ru: Ash came down on Mournhold three days running, all the way across the Inner Sea. Old folk put out bowls of water for the ancestors, so they'd have something clean to drink.
The Archcanon calls on the Great Houses to stand together. The Houses agree, and then they go home and count each other's guards.
Argonian raiders crossed the Deshaan border again last month. Burned a kwama egg farm and wrote something in the ash with their claws. Nobody will say what it said.
A Telvanni wizard grew a tower overnight on the coast past Sadrith Mora. The tower next door woke up, so they say, and it was not pleased.
Sleepers are walking out of the ash in Balmora and Ald'ruhn again. Not many. Enough. The Temple calls it a sickness. My grandmother calls it a memory.
Necrom's had so many pilgrims since the Red Year that the dead are complaining about the noise. The priests swear it's true. The priests would know.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.so: The Skaal say the frost giant Karstaag once ruled the north of the island from a hall of living ice. When he fell, his blood froze into the walls, and that is why the ice of Castle Karstaag never melts, even in Sun's Height.

In the last age the moon over Solstheim turned red, and the Huntsman of the Princes came down to play his game with mortal prey. The beasts of the island still remember. When the moon swells, the wolves that are not wolves gather at Frostmoon Crag.

Stalhrim is ice the All-Maker made to remember. A smith who works it without a prayer will find the blade cold to the bone and the edge turning on its master. Only the Skaal know the words, and they do not teach them to strangers.

Haknir Death-Brand sailed the Sea of Ghosts with a crew sworn to follow him past dying. His ship broke on the shoal that bears his name. On still nights you can hear oars dip where no boat floats, and a voice counting the stroke.
Ash came down on Raven Rock again last night. The Redoran Guard swept the Bulwark at dawn, and still my bread tastes of Red Mountain.
The Skaal won't sell stalhrim to anyone. A Telvanni offered them a chest of drakes for one sliver, and they laughed him all the way back to his mushroom.
Folk wake up with raw hands and stone dust in their hair and no memory of the night. My cousin found her boots full of ash. People whisper about the Earth Stone.
Rieklings came down to the road past Thirsk Mead Hall with spears and a stolen war-horn. Little blue things, but there were twenty of them, and they were laughing.
Somebody at Tel Mithryn pays good coin for Dwemer scrap out of Kagrumez. Telvanni coin, mind. Count it twice and bite every piece.
Fort Frostmoth's been empty since the Red Year. Empty of the living, anyway. Fishermen won't beach on that shore after dark.
Reavers have dug in at Bujold's Retreat. Wreckers and cutthroats from every port between Windhelm and Necrom, and the Skaal say they've started taking their sledges.
Ash from the south and ice from the north,
The island between them holds its breath.
Raven on the wall and Skaal by the fire,
Each keeps a watch, and each keeps death.
Sing to the stones when the night walks loud,
And do not answer the one in the cloud.
Ash from the South
Small blue thief with a horn too big,
Rides on a boar and dances a jig,
Stole the mead of Thirsk and the bench beside,
Now the Nords drink snow and the rieklings ride.
The Riekling's Horn
Dig the yam and shake the ash,
Mind the guar and mind the lash,
Mountain sleeps and mountain wakes,
Mountain gives and mountain takes.
Sing it low and sing it slow,
The ancestors are listening below.
Ash-Yam Song
The moon came down on Vivec's town,
And the sea came up to meet it,
We lost our god and kept our gods,
And the Houses still compete it.
The Moon Came Down
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.st: Ebonheart was built from the black stone of the Stonefalls, which fell from the sky when Lorkhan's heart was torn out. Masons say the stone is still warm in the middle, and that if you lay your ear to the castle wall at night you can hear something counting.
The East Empire Company is losing money at Ebonheart and everyone in the Company knows except the Factor. He still thinks it's the weather.
The Legion garrison at Ebonheart is half the size it was before the Great War. The other half went to Cyrodiil and never came back. The Argonians have noticed.
Kwama miners near Ebonheart broke into an old Daedric cellar. They sealed it again the same day. Nobody will say what was down there, but they're drinking more.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.te: The first Telvanni tower was grown from a spore a wizard carried in his mouth across the sea, because he trusted no pocket. When he spat it onto the shore, it rooted before it touched the sand, and it has been growing upward and arguing ever since.
Sadrith Mora's guard asks your business at the dock. Say 'trade'. Never say 'study'. A Telvanni hears 'study' and wonders whose secrets you're after.
Mistress Dratha's tower has been coughing up spores for a week. The fishers say she's sneezing. Nobody in Sadrith Mora finds that funny.
A Telvanni hireling contract was read out in the Gateway Inn, all forty clauses. The man who signed it is now a mushroom. Read before you sign.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.vv: Ald'ruhn is built inside the shell of an emperor crab so large that it took a hundred Redoran warriors a hundred days to kill it. The shell still hums in an ash storm. Children are told it is the crab, dreaming of the sea.
Ash storm on the way to Ald'ruhn. Seal your doors, cover your guar, and if somebody knocks in the storm, don't open. Nobody knocks in a storm.

A Telvanni mouth was seen at the Hermaeus Mora stones west of Ald'ruhn, bargaining with something in the rock. The Redoran guard sent word to the Temple and then to the mouth's master. Only one answered.
Bal Molagmer are back, they say. Thieves who only rob those who've wronged the poor. Ald'ruhn's councillors have started locking their doors twice.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.morrowind.we: The Odai river was cut by a single tear Vivec shed for the Chimer who died at Red Mountain. The water is sweet because grief, the Hlaalu say, is the one thing that never goes sour.
The Camonna Tong own every second door in Balmora. If an Imperial asks you for directions, give him the wrong ones. Safer for everyone.
A Caldera ebony miner wished at the Clavicus stones for a vein that would never run out. It hasn't. He's still down there digging, and he won't come up to eat.
Fevyn Andalor's brother walks out of Balmora in his sleep every night, always north-east, always toward the mountain. She ties him to the bed now. He chews through the rope.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.eastm: They say Ysgramor's people raised Windhelm's first stones before they had roofs over their own heads, because a king needs a hall before his people need beds. The great bridge over the White River was built in a single winter, and every mason who worked on it was buried in its piers so that it would never forget whom it served.

When Kyne wept for the warriors fallen at the end of the Dragon War, one tear struck the tundra east of the White River and the ground has never cooled since. That is why the springs steam, why the moss stays green under the snow, and why the old folk of Kynesgrove still leave a cup of water on the doorstep each First Seed.

The Eldergleam was old when the Dwemer still sang beneath Mzulft. Druids of the first Nords swore that whoever harmed the great tree would never again find their way home, and in Eastmarch to this day a lost traveller is said to have 'cut the gleam'.

The giants of Eastmarch count their years by the hot pools, not by the sun. Each clan has its own spring, and when a giant dies its kin carry the body to the water, wash it, and leave it to the steam. Nords who have seen it say no one was ever mourned so quietly.
Ulfric's men drill in the snow below the Palace of the Kings every dawn now. Nobody drills like that unless they expect the Legion before the thaw.
The Grey Quarter's cistern froze solid again, and the guards told the Dunmer to melt snow like honest folk. As if the snow in that quarter were any cleaner.
Teamsters won't take the road past Mzulft after dark. The Imperials camped down there shoot at anything wearing blue, and they aren't fussy about the shade.
Darkwater Crossing sends good ore south every week, and half of it never gets past Mistwatch. Somebody up in that tower is eating very well this winter.
Giants came down off Steamcrag to sit in the hot pools again. Leave them be and they'll leave you be. Mostly. Ask the Mixwater carters about mostly.
That Dunmer at Hlaalu Farm pays his Argonian hands the same coin as his Nords. Half the Candlehearth thinks it's a scandal and the other half wants work there.
Kynesgrove's miners say the stone is warm under the snow this year, warmer than any of them remember. The priest says it's only the springs. He says it too quickly.
Coal-carters from Kynesgrove say the hot springs have been bubbling black silt since the tremors started under the Dwemer ruins. [Hearth-Tally]
Quartermasters at the Palace of the Kings have been buying every horseshoe and salt-barrel between Windhelm and Darkwater Crossing. [Hearth-Tally]
Refugee peddlers on the Velothi road say the border pickets are turning back anyone without a stamped hold pass. [Hearth-Tally]
The ice on the White River is thick as a shield,
And the Stormcloaks march out over furrow and field;
My love wore the blue and he sang as he went,
Now his song's in the snow and his summer is spent.
So pour me the mead, and pour it for two,
For the ice will break up, but my heart never knew.
The Ice on the White River
We came over the mountains with ash in our hair,
And they gave us a corner and called it our share.
The stones are all borrowed, the bread is all dear,
But the dead of Red Mountain still find us here.
Ash in the Grey Quarter
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.falkr: They say Falkreath's graveyard was dug before the town was built. The first settlers came to bury their dead from some forgotten war, found the soil soft and the pines quiet, and simply never left.

Lake Ilinalta is named for a maiden who waited on its shore for a lover who drowned crossing it in winter. Fishers claim that on still nights her lantern can be seen moving over the water toward the Lady Stone, still looking.

The Shriekwind barrows are said to hold two brothers who quarrelled over a single crown and were buried a hundred paces apart so they could never reach each other. When the wind blows between the mounds, it is the two of them, still shouting.

Hunters in the Jerall foothills leave the first antler of every season at the foot of a pine. The old ones say the forest keeps a tally, and a hunter whose debt grows too large is taken by the spriggans to pay it.
Gravedigger says three plots in the Falkreath yard were turned over last month, and none of it was her doing. Folk are leaving coins on the graves now, as if that would help.
Smoke still rises off Helgen some mornings. The Legion says it's looters burning what's left. My cousin swears she saw something big circling the ruins at dusk.
Herders up by Southfringe say the mountain passes toward Cyrodiil are choked with early snow and restless border-guards. [Hearth-Tally]
Fishers on Lake Ilinalta swear the water around the Lady Stone stays unfrozen even in the hardest midwinter gale. [Hearth-Tally]
Carters passing Pinewatch Stead say the homestead on the hill receives wagonloads of provisions at midnight and never sends a sack of grain to market. [Hearth-Tally]
Don't take the road past Knifepoint Ridge after dark. Jarl Siddgeir's posted a bounty, which tells you how bad it's got, seeing how little that man stirs himself.
The fishers on Lake Ilinalta won't cast near the sunken fort anymore. Say the water goes cold as a grave there, even in Sun's Height.
A Legion camp in the west woods and a Stormcloak camp in the east, and Falkreath in the middle selling bread to both. Mark me, one of them will want more than bread soon.
Someone's been taking travellers on the Pale Pass road, up past Bloodlet Throne. Found a cart with the horses still in harness and no driver anywhere.
An Imperial scholar's been drinking at Dead Man's Drink every night, asking about the dragon mounds. Says three of them in this hold alone have been dug open from the inside.
Lumber-crews at Half-Moon Mill say the lake fog smells of old cellar-stone whenever the wind blows from the sunken fort. [Hearth-Tally]
Charcoal-burners below Knifepoint Ridge found three abandoned ore-carts with the strongboxes pried open on the western road. [Hearth-Tally]
Runil's novices have been lighting extra lanterns along the cemetery wall every night since the frost set in. [Hearth-Tally]
Lay him down where the needles fall,
Lay him down by the old stone wall,
Arkay's hand and the hemlock shade,
Count the graves that the winter made.
Sing it low, for the pines can hear,
Every name we have buried here.
The Pines Keep Count
Out on the water a lantern glows,
Where it is going, nobody knows,
Cast your nets on the eastern side,
Leave the west to the drowned man's bride.
Ilinalta's Lantern
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.haafi: They say Potema, the Wolf Queen, still walks under Solitude on the night she died, counting the dead she raised in her war. Mothers in the Temple quarter tell their children the wind moaning through the great arch is her laughter, and that a candle in the window keeps her from choosing your house.

The bridge at Dragon Bridge is older than any Nord king's line. Some say Akaviri hands cut its carvings. Others swear the stones were laid over the neck of a dragon that fell into the Karth, and that on a still night you can feel the whole span breathing under your boots.

Before the Thalmor took Northwatch Keep, its garrison kept a bronze bell that would ring by itself whenever a ship went down in the Sea of Ghosts. The elves had it taken down the first winter. Fishermen say they still hear it on foggy nights, rung somewhere under the water.
