The East Empire Company lost two cargoes this season between the Katariah's anchorage and the lighthouse. The clerks on the Solitude docks blame the weather. The sailors blame wreckers.
There's a Thalmor carriage on the embassy road every Tirdas with its curtains drawn. Nobody I know has seen who rides in it, and nobody I know wants to.
The Legion doubled the patrols out of Fort Hraggstad after High King Torygg died. Doubled them, and still the Stormcloaks keep a cookfire burning in the hills below the Statue to Meridia.
The woodcutters at the Solitude Sawmill won't go near the Steepfall burrows after dark. Trolls, they say, big ones, with the frost still on their backs.
My cousin rows out of the Icewater Jetty. He says there's an island in the western fog where the sky goes red at dusk, and no boat that steers for it comes back the same.
Pilgrims climb to the Statue to Meridia with lanterns, even in a blizzard. One told me the light up there burned her nightmares away. She didn't say what it left behind.
If you're riding to Dragon Bridge, keep to the road. Pinemoon Cave has new tenants, and they've learned the Legion paymaster's schedule better than the paymaster has.
Harbor-clerks at the Solitude docks say two coasters came in with shredded sails after passing the northern sea-cliffs. [Hearth-Tally]
Guards at Dragon Bridge have doubled the watch on the stone span since the supply convoys began moving south. [Hearth-Tally]
Warehouse watchmen down by the East Empire Company pier swear someone has been signaling with shuttered lanterns from the marsh shore. [Hearth-Tally]
The Karth runs grey beneath the Arch,
The gulls cry over Solitude,
My love went out on a Company bark
With salt for bread and sea for food.
I light the lamp, I trim the wick,
I count the sails that round the Tear,
And every sail is his, for a breath,
And none of them have brought him here.
The Karth Runs Grey
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.hjaal: Long before Highmoon Hall was raised, a jarl of Hjaalmarch tried to drain the marsh and plant barley. The marsh let him dig for seven summers, then rose in a single night and took his hall, his fields and his heirs. Morthal's grandmothers say the marsh keeps everything it takes, and gives things back only to those who ask politely.

When Jurgen Windcaller was beaten at Red Mountain, he swore never again to use the Voice for war. He went silent for the rest of his days, and some say he was laid in Ustengrav so the marsh would muffle his last breath. Hunters still lower their voices when they pass the barrow.

Bromjunaar, which men now call Labyrinthian, was the high seat of the dragon priests. When the dragons fell, the priests were sealed in with their masks, and later Shalidor built his maze among the broken stones. The wind has wandered those halls for an age and still has not found the way out.
The fog came off the marsh so thick last Middas that Jonna at the Moorside lost a customer between her door and the woodpile. They found him at dawn, sitting in the reeds and humming.
The Imperials camp on one side of Ustengrav and the Stormcloaks on the other, and the barrow sits between them like a dog that both men are afraid to kick.
Jarl Idgrod sees things. Everyone in Morthal knows it. What nobody says out loud is that lately she's stopped telling anyone what she sees.
The Stonehills men are digging deeper in the Rockwallow Mine than their fathers ever dared. Some say they've broken into one of the old Dwemer roads out of Mzinchaleft.
There's a light that walks the marsh near Kjenstag at midnight. Follow it and you'll find treasure, or the bottom of a bog. Same thing, if you ask my uncle.
Don't sleep with the shutters open in Morthal. Mother says it's for the damp. Father says it's for the things that live in the damp.
That Dwemer tower up past Stonehills hums when the stars come out. Even the giants at Stonehill Bluff won't sleep on that side of their fire.
Peat-cutters east of Morthal say the bog-channels have risen a foot since the autumn rains, uncovering carved First Era lintels. [Hearth-Tally]
Miners up at Stonehills keep a barrel of pitch burning by the pit-head whenever the cold fog rolls down from the Labyrinth. [Hearth-Tally]
Eel-trappers at Drajkmyr Fishery won't cast their lines near the northern salt-marsh after sundown. [Hearth-Tally]
Lantern, lantern, low and green,
Walking where no road has been,
Show me silver, show me gold,
Show me where the drowned are cold.
Mother bar the door tonight,
Something's carrying a light.
Lantern on the Marsh
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.the_p: They say that long before the Oblivion Crisis a whole winter passed in Dawnstar without a single dream. Men slept like stones and woke unrested, and by Sun's Dawn they were quarrelling over nets and knifing each other on the docks. When the thaw came every soul in town dreamed the same dream on the same night: a black door on the hill east of the harbour, and a woman behind it, laughing.

The Lantern-Wife walks the snowfields between Dawnstar and the southern mines. Her husband went to work the night shift in a storm two hundred winters ago and never came up, so she carries a lamp from shaft to shaft, looking. Follow her light in a blizzard and it will lead you to shelter. Speak to her and it will lead you to him.

Fishermen on the Pale coast tell of the Horker-King, a bull horker the size of a longboat with tusks of yellow ivory and one eye milky from an old harpoon. He is said to sleep on the ice off the Brinehammer wreck, and any boat that takes a calf from his herd will find its nets slashed before the week is out.
Half of Dawnstar woke screaming again on Tirdas. The priests blame bad fish. The fishermen blame bad priests.
The ore sleds from the Dawnstar mines are coming down lighter every week. Either the veins are thinning, or somebody between the pit and the harbour has quick hands.
Watchmen on the Dawnstar palisade say strange lights flicker around the bronze domes of the high Dwemer lifts on clear nights. [Hearth-Tally]
The giants at Blizzard Rest have pushed their mammoths right up to the fences of Heljarchen Hall. Nobody's brave enough to tell them where the property line is.
A cog out of Solitude went down past the Brinehammer's bones before the ice closed. The Sea of Ghosts never gives anything back, not even the gulls.
Legion riders out of Fort Dunstad stop every sled on the road south. Hunting deserters, they say. Hunting mead, more like.
Ever since the Stormcloaks went poking about Korvanjund, the shepherds won't graze the hills near it. The sheep come back with frost in their wool in the middle of Midyear.
Up near Windward Ruins the snow keeps tracks for a week. If you see one set going in and none coming out, keep walking.
Ore-sledges between Iron-Breaker and Quicksilver Mine are running double shifts to fill the hold's military contracts. [Hearth-Tally]
Skippers in Dawnstar harbor keep an axe by the mooring-lines in case the sea-ice closes the channel overnight. [Hearth-Tally]
Carters down at Loreius Farm say the giants on the southern tundra border have been driving their mammoths closer to the road. [Hearth-Tally]
Hush now, the boats are in, the lamps are low,
The sea has kept its ghosts beneath the snow.
Close your eyes and do not wander far,
Dream of the shore, and not of what's beyond the star.
And if a lady calls you from the hill,
Lie still, my heart, my little one, lie still.
Dawnstar Lullaby
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.the_r: Before the Nords, before the Dwemer, the Reachfolk say the Druadach peaks were the bones of a giant who tried to climb into the sky and was struck down. The hagravens still pick at his ribs, and that is why the stone here bleeds silver.

Faolan, called the Red Eagle, once held every valley from the Karth to the Sea of Ghosts against the Nordic kings. When his last fortress fell he gave his heart to the crones and rose again to fight one more summer. The Reachfolk say he did not die in that last battle. He only lay down to wait for a better one.

The Dwemer cut Markarth from the cliff with tools that sang. When the miners of Cidhna strike a seam at night, some swear they hear the old song answer from below, a low humming that stops the moment anyone speaks.

When Hjalti Early-Beard took Old Hroldan, the storm that broke over the walls spoke his name. Every year since, on the anniversary, the shutters of the inn rattle without wind, and a careful listener can hear a soldier's laugh in the empty room upstairs.
Three silver carts came down from Karthwasten last month and only two reached Markarth. The Silver-Bloods say Forsworn. The carters say nothing at all, which is worse.
Somebody left a hagraven feather on the shrine at Old Hroldan. Eydis burned it in the hearth and the smoke went green. Nobody's slept in Tiber Septim's room since.
Drovers at Old Hroldan won't move wool-wagons after dusk while the briar-fires are burning on the southern crags. [Hearth-Tally]
Miners at Karthwasten posted their own sentries on the silver-stacks after two assay-ledgers vanished from the counting-house. [Hearth-Tally]
Gold-washers near Kolskeggr say the hill-clans have staked bone totems across every goat-path leading into the eastern valleys. [Hearth-Tally]
Apothecaries in the stone city pay double for juniper berries gathered near the high waterfalls, though few pickers dare the climb. [Hearth-Tally]
The Legion pitched a camp near Bthardamz and the Stormcloaks have one above Liar's Retreat. Half a day's walk apart. Any morning now one of them will wake up dead.
Fishermen on the Karth say the river runs red some mornings below Bruca's Leap. Ore runoff, the miners claim. Funny how it only happens after a raid.
The Orcs at Dushnikh Yal are buying every snow fox pelt they can get. Won't say why. My guess is they know something about this winter we don't.
A Dwemer door opened by itself under Markarth last Loredas. Calcelmo had the guards seal the corridor before anyone could see where it went.
Don't take the old road past Dead Crone Rock after dark. The crones up there can sing a man right off a cliff, and they do.
They found a Briarheart dead near Sundered Towers with his chest stitched shut and no heart inside. Even the Forsworn are afraid of whoever did that.
Barge-pilots on the Karth River carry iron-rimmed shields to turn the arrows fired from the limestone ledges above the gorge. [Hearth-Tally]
Smelter-hands at Markarth say the lower steam-conduits under the city have been clanking out of rhythm all week. [Hearth-Tally]
Silver in the stone and blood upon the silver,
Cidhna takes the strong and gives the city coin.
Down goes the lamp and down goes the digger,
Up comes the ore, and none of it is his.
Sing for the Karth, it carries what we bury,
Sing for the Reach, it never once forgives.
Silver in the Stone
Feathers on her shoulders, ashes in her hair,
She sings upon the crag and the wind goes still to hear.
Shepherd, shut your shutter, hunter, bar your door,
She wants a heart of briar, and she'll take yours if it's near.
The Crone on the Crag

Before Riften had walls, the fishers of Lake Honrich say a Nord chieftain named Honrich drowned himself in it rather than yield to the Dragon Cult. On still autumn mornings the mist forms a man's shape over the water, and the old women set out a cup of mead on the docks for him.

The birches of the Rift turn gold every year because a priestess of Kynareth wept over them during the long winter after the Dragon War. Her tears were so warm the trees forgot how to go grey. Cut a Rift birch out of season, the woodsmen say, and its sap will run the colour of honey and blood.

Forelhost did not fall to the siege. The monks of the Dragon Cult poisoned their own well rather than open the gates, and the soldiers outside waited a month for a surrender that never came. When they finally broke in, the halls were full of the dead and every one of them was smiling.
There is a stone south of Riften that drinks the shadows of anyone who sleeps beside it. Thieves pray to it before a job. Honest folk walk the long way round.
Maven Black-Briar bought another farm outside Riften this season. Nobody remembers it being for sale.
The road guards at Fort Greenwall wave the Black-Briar wagons through and search everyone else down to their boot-soles. Make of that what you will.
Orchard-hands at Heartwood Mill say the autumn leaves haven't fallen from the birch groves around the southern watchtowers. [Hearth-Tally]
Fishers on Lake Honrich steer clear of the sunken pilings when the evening mist rises off the water. [Hearth-Tally]
Pilgrims keep coming through Ivarstead to climb the Seven Thousand Steps. Most come back down quiet. A few don't come back down at all.
Something's been taking sheep along the shore of Lake Honrich. Wolves, says the steward. Wolves don't open gates.
Somebody's selling Redwater skooma in the Ratway again. Bright red, sweet as berries. Two dockhands dead of it since Hearthfire.
Miners from Shor's Stone won't work the deep seams past dusk any more. They say they hear chanting coming up from the Ruunvald side.
The Ashwood Knives have been taking a toll on the Riften road. Pay them or walk home barefoot, that's how it goes now.
Mead-carters on the Ivarstead road travel in convoys of four since the bridge-tolls started up in the birch hills. [Hearth-Tally]
Canal-watchmen in Riften's lower boardwalks say the iron grates to the cisterns have been oiled from the inside. [Hearth-Tally]
Miners at Shor's Stone keep a smith's hammer by every timber prop in case the frostbite spiders break through the lower gallery. [Hearth-Tally]
The birch leaves fall like coin on the water,
The mist rolls in from the eastern hills,
I gave my heart to a fisher's daughter,
And Lake Honrich keeps it still.
The Jarl sits high and the Briar sits higher,
The canal runs black and the bells ring thin,
But a fire on the shore and a song for the singer
Will warm the coldest Riften in.
Gold on the Honrich
One for the mother and one for the son,
One for the oath you swore to someone,
Seven thousand steps and the wind on your face,
And never a fire, and never a place.
Climb if you must, but climb with your mouth shut,
The Greybeards hear a whisper as loud as a shout.
Seven Thousand Steps
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.white: Before Whiterun had walls, the hill was called the Shield of the Plain, and Ysgramor's people raised Jorrvaskr there because a wounded eagle landed on the summit and would not leave. They took it as a sign that the hill would never fall, and so far it never has.

The plains were once a single forest, the old folk say, and a giant king named Gruv-Ulf cleared it in a night to make room for his herds. The trees he pulled up he threw into the White River, and the river has run pale with their bark ever since.

Kynareth is said to have walked the Tundra in the shape of a grey hawk the summer after the Dragon War, blessing every spring she drank from. Shepherds still leave a cup of water at a dry spring in hope that she will come back for it.

The Greybeards' first word, spoken when High Hrothgar was finished, rolled down the mountain and across the plains for three days. Where it passed, the grass lay flat in a line pointing at the Throat of the World, and the herdsmen of Rorikstead still call that line the Kneeling Road.
Somebody's been dragging the old shields off the walls of Whitewatch Tower and hanging them back up painted red. Bandits marking their road, my uncle says.
The guards swear they saw something big circling over the Western Watchtower last week. Something with wings. I told them to lay off Hulda's mead.
Honningbrew lost six casks on the river road this month. Sabjorn's sure it's the cave-folk at White River Watch, and he's not wrong often about his own mead.
The giants at Bleakwind Basin have been bolder since the snow came off the plains. One walked right past Pelagia Farm with a mammoth on a lead, calm as a priest.
Don't go near the stone with the skulls round it, east of the river. Lights there on moonless nights, and the farmers say the ground's been turned over like a field.
A Legion courier rode out from the camp near Rorikstead and never reached Whiterun. They've doubled the patrols, for all the good it does.
Fellglow Keep has smoke in its chimneys again. Nobody honest lives in that place, not since the Legion walked out of it.
The Battle-Borns and the Gray-Manes nearly came to blows at the Bannered Mare over a bowl of stew. Over the war, really. It's always over the war.
Caravan-factors outside Whiterun's main gate say the road-tolls near Valtheim have doubled since the watch-patrols were pulled back. [Hearth-Tally]
Mill-hands at Riverwood have been chaining their pine rafts to the bank at dusk so the river-raiders can't cut them loose. [Hearth-Tally]
Wind on the Tundra, wind on the hill,
Blowing the barley, never stands still,
Carry my love home from Rorikstead's plain,
And I'll pour you a horn when you blow back again.
The Tundra Wind
Stone on stone and shield on shield,
Whiterun's sons will never yield,
Let the dragon come, let the giants roar,
We held this hill, and we'll hold it more.
Bring me ale from the Bannered Mare,
And a song for the dead who are drinking there.
Hold the Hill
place_lore.nirncraft.region.skyrim.winte: In 4E 122 the sea rose up in a single night and swallowed most of Winterhold: its temple, its markets, its great houses and its harbour. The townsfolk blame the College, whose tower alone stood untouched. The College blames the sea. On the lowest tides of Evening Star, the fishermen say, you can still hear the drowned temple bell ringing under the waves, calling the faithful to a service nobody comes to.

Saarthal was the first city of men in Skyrim, built by Ysgramor's people. On the Night of Tears the snow elves fell upon it and slaughtered all but a handful. Ysgramor sailed home to Atmora and came back with Five Hundred Companions, and the snow was red for a generation after. Old Winterhold women still will not light a fire on the anniversary.

The glacier behind the College moves, the old folk say, the width of a finger every year, always toward the town. Grandmothers tell children that when it finally reaches the cliff where the old palace stood, Winterhold will have paid its debt to the sea, and the drowned city will rise again under the ice.
The College keeps its lamps burning all night. Jarl Korir says they're up to mischief. I say if they were boiling the sea, we'd at least be warm.
Another house went over the cliff on the north side last Rain's Hand. Old Brannoc was still asleep in it. They fished out the bed. Not Brannoc.
Trappers along the northern ice-packs say three merchant hulls were driven onto the reef at Pilgrim's Trench in the last gale. [Hearth-Tally]
Excavation guards on the road to Saarthal carry warm tallow-brick to keep their lantern oil from freezing solid. [Hearth-Tally]
There's a Dunmer ship broken on the rocks east of the College. The grey-skins in town still walk out there on Morndas to scatter ash on the deck.
Fishermen saw lights moving inside the Skytemple Ruins. Apprentices, probably. Or something the apprentices woke up.
Nobody has seen the priestess from the Shrine of Azura come down for flour since the first snows. Somebody ought to check on her. Somebody else.
They're digging at Saarthal again. Every time someone digs at Saarthal, Winterhold loses something.
The Legion and the Stormcloaks have both pitched tents in the hold. Korir hasn't decided which of them to hate more, so he's hating both.
Coal-drivers from Whistling Mine travel with roped sledges whenever the sea-gales sweep across the road past Amol hamlet. [Hearth-Tally]
Pilgrims climbing the eastern mountain steps leave iron crampons and dry firewood at the way-stead for the next party. [Hearth-Tally]
Townsfolk in Winterhold bar their doors early when the blue lights flare across the broken bridge of the College. [Hearth-Tally]
Winterhold was wider when my grandsire was a boy,
With a market by the water and a temple full of joy.
Then the sea came up one evening and it took the better half,
And the mages in their tower, they were dry enough to laugh.
So drink to the drowned and the doors that we lost,
And curse every wizard who sleeps without frost.
Winterhold Was Wider
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.ar: When the Altmer first chose to build towers and worship gods, a few among them refused, and said the Old Ways were better: to watch, to wait, to understand rather than command. Those few took ship to Artaeum and have lived there since, and the island has learned their trick of being present and absent at once. It is said that Artaeum once vanished for a whole era, and that when it came back, its monks had not noticed they were gone.
Artaeum came out of the fog off the western shoals again. My uncle saw a white tower and an old woman nodding at him. His nets were full. He's been unbearable since.
The Psijics take an apprentice now and then, they say, without warning. One day you're a fisherman's daughter. Next day you're gone and your mother gets a very polite letter.
The Thalmor don't like the Psijics. The Psijics don't seem to notice. That makes the Thalmor dislike them more.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.au: Auridon was the first island of the Summerset archipelago to be settled, and Firsthold was the first city. The Altmer say the first High King built its harbour wall with his own hands, stone by stone, and that he set into it one stone that was black, so that the city would always remember that even the first and best of works has a flaw.
Firsthold customs towed another sick ship to the quarantine anchorage. The sailors row to the Peryite shrine at night. Customs pretends not to notice. For now.
The Moth's robbed Magistrate Caladwe again. The Justiciars dug up half the hill by the Nocturnal shrine looking for her stash. All they found were moths.
The Orc dockers of Firsthold are paid half what the Altmer get. They pray to Malacath about it. Overseer Varanil has developed a rash. Coincidence, surely.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.le: The Altmer say that when the world was made, the gods who helped make it lost their divinity in the act, and that the Altmer are their mortal descendants. That is why the Altmer strive so hard to be perfect, and why they grieve so quietly: every one of them is mourning something they never had.

The Crystal Tower of Summerset, the Altmer say, was raised over the place where the first elves came ashore, and its light holds the memory of everything the elves have learned since. The Sapiarchs guard its upper chambers, and the deepest of them, it is said, holds a single shelf on which the Psijics once left a book. No Sapiarch has ever read it. No Sapiarch has ever dared to take it down.

During the Oblivion Crisis, when the gates opened across Summerset, the Altmer held the Daedra off without an Emperor, without the Legion, and without asking for help. The Thalmor tell this story as proof that the elves need no one. The old ones who were there tell it differently: they say they asked, and no one came.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.ru: The Thalmor took Summerset over in the name of the old Aldmeri glory. Now the old Aldmeri glory needs a stamped permit to visit its cousins on Auridon.
Maormer sails off the southern capes again. The Sea Elves never stop trying, and the Altmer never stop pretending they're not worried.
The Crystal Tower's lights burned blue three nights running. The Sapiarchs say it means nothing. The Sapiarchs never say anything means nothing, so that means something.
The genealogists of the Directorate came to my neighbour's house with measuring rods. His family's been on the island for four thousand years. Apparently that's not quite long enough.
Fishermen out past the western shoals swear they saw Artaeum through the fog. Every year somebody does. Every year the Psijics don't send a letter.
Summerset's the most beautiful place in Tamriel, and the quietest. Nobody talks too loud here. The walls are white and very thin.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.so: White walls, white towers, white gulls on the quay,
my love had a crooked smile and they took her away.
The genealogist came with his silver and his book,
and the sea was so blue that I could not look.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.summerset.su: The Altmer say the first elves came ashore on Summerset from somewhere over the western sea, and that the island received them by raising the Crystal Tower overnight out of its own bedrock. The Sapiarchs do not like this tale, because it suggests the island chose the elves rather than the other way about.
Someone's leaving fresh blood at the Dagon shrine north of Alinor, beside the memorial to the Oblivion dead. Old Tirenwe at the Tower is furious. The Justiciars are calm. Too calm.
The crooked ones of the Namira shrine west of the city get bread from somewhere every night. The Directorate would very much like to know where.
The Lords' Hunt's been cancelled again. There's a fox in the south-west preserve. A large fox. With a family name.
There's a painter by the Sheogorath shrine who paints the Justiciars as chickens. They keep confiscating the chickens. He keeps painting.
There's a lamp on the western hill that's burned two hundred years,
the dead won't come to Alinor while the Lady's light is near;
the Justiciars climbed up the hill to tell the lamp to go,
and came back down a deal more red than when they went, you know.
The Lamp on the Western Hill
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.gr: The great graht-oak of Elden Root was planted, the Spinners say, by Y'ffre himself on the first morning of the world, and the city grew in its branches because the Bosmer were too respectful to build on the ground and too clever to live without walls. When the tree dies, so will the Bosmer nation. The tree, the Spinners add with a smile, is in excellent health.
The Thalmor have a man with a book hiding in the bushes by the Peryite shrine north of Elden Root. Everyone knows he's there. He coughs.
The elders are angry about the felled graht-oak east of the city. There's talk of the old rite. My brother's a hunter. I've told him to go visit cousins in Woodhearth.
The Wood Orcs in the deep forest have stopped trading with Elden Root. They say they're tired of being called guests. They're not wrong.
The moons are rising over Grahtwood, sugar-sweet and slow,
the caravans are singing where the green-roofed rivers go;
the cats will pray to Azurah and the elves will pray to none,
and the road from Rimmen's long, my love, but the road is nearly done.

Greenshade was the first forest Y'ffre sang, the Spinners say, and its trees still remember the tune. On certain windless nights the whole forest sways together, as if dancing, and any Bosmer who hears the song in the leaves will dream of the shape she wore before she was a Bosmer, and wake up homesick for it.
Someone's burning the forest north-east of Woodhearth, one perfect circle at a time. Warden Ilthaer is hunting them. I wouldn't want to be found by Ilthaer.
The Mandate-Breakers at the Namira shrine have two net-boys from the docks. The wardens are arguing about whether the Pact allows it. The mothers aren't arguing.
Halbor the cheese-eater's still out by the Sheogorath shrine. The Spinners still can't decide if he's broken the Pact. The Silvenar's said he'll rule on it next year. Or the year after.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.le: Before the Green Pact the Bosmer were formless, and changed shape as the forest did. Y'ffre the Storyteller sang them into the shapes they wear now, and asked in return only that they never harm the green. Each Spinner keeps a strand of that first song, and when the last strand is forgotten, the Spinners say, the Bosmer will lose their shapes again.

The Wild Hunt is the oldest and worst rite of the Bosmer. When the elders call it, the hunters drink a draught and become beasts, a tide of teeth and claws with no master, that runs until it has devoured its target or itself. It has been called only a few times in history. The Bosmer do not say how many. Every time they are asked, they look away.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.ma: Falinesti, the Walking Tree, once strolled across Valenwood with the seasons, wintering in the south and summering in the north, and the Bosmer of the city lived their whole lives without once setting foot on the ground. When it finally rooted, in the Third Era, the old ones wept, and said that the tree was not tired, only sad, and that it would walk again when it had something to walk toward.
Falinesti's humming again at night. The rootkeepers say the Walking Tree's getting restless. If it walks, half the Thalmor tax-rolls walk with it.
There's a thorn-grove east of Falinesti where the trees grow bent like slaves. Molag Bal's shrine is in the middle. Warden Aldoril went in last spring. Hasn't come out.
The Kin-Breakers of Malabal Tor are holding the toll-road now. Outlaws who cut living wood. Even the Thalmor are scandalised, and the Thalmor log everything.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.re: Reaper's March is named for the harvest the Khajiit and Bosmer fought over a thousand years ago, when the wheat of the border grew so tall that the two armies could not see each other and cut down their own men instead. Neither side won. The wheat was never harvested. And every year since, the people of Arenthia leave the last row of their fields uncut, for the ghosts of both armies to share.
Arenthia's sleepers keep walking north to the Vaermina stones. Shazah at the Two Moons is beside herself. Her own cub walked last night.
The Silken Sisters at the Mephala shrine sell secrets to everyone: Khajiit, Bosmer, Thalmor. Doesn't matter who's buying. Everyone's betrayed by the end.
Ri'zahd the caravan-master leaves bigger offerings at the Nocturnal shrine than the thieves do. Says it's prudence. Jo'darr the thief says it's cheating.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.ru: The Thalmor say Valenwood is a loyal province of the Dominion. The Bosmer say the trees haven't been asked. Nobody's brave enough to ask the trees.
Colovian loggers keep crossing the border to fell graht-oaks east of Elden Root. The wardens keep sending back their axes. The loggers don't always come with them.
The Silvenar's a good man, they say, and the Green Lady's a fierce one. Between them they speak for every Bosmer. That's a lot of talking to do, and the Thalmor are always listening.
Bosmer won't cut a living branch, but they'll eat a man they killed in battle within three days. Visitors tend to find the first rule charming and the second one less so.
There's talk of the Wild Hunt in Grahtwood again. My mother says it's only talk. My mother also nailed a deer skull over our door.
place_lore.nirncraft.region.valenwood.so: Leave the tree and take the deer,
leave the root and take the boar,
the forest feeds the hound that's true,
and the Huntsman keeps the score.
A domed observatory-vault whose ceiling is a map of the night sky in inlaid crystal, with floor rings that rotate by lever.
Under the reliquary's dome the stars go out one by one. The cartographers swear it was full of them a decade ago.

The ceiling is a chart, not a sky. Four stars lit, thirty to go, and the vault answers with niches opening. We read one scroll: it was a list of the lamps themselves, nine in all, ending at a place called the Tower of Ten Thousand Years. I think we have been told where to go.

The star-lamp is lit by names, the sky by lamps. Each star is a name; each name a debt. When the debt is paid the star may rest. When the debt is unpaid the star must be fed. The Keepers have forgotten how to feed them. The Reliquary remembers. It will not forgive.
place_lore.nirncraft.renaud_farm.hook: At place.nirncraft.renaud_farm, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the abbey turnpikes and hospice-valleys of central Stormhaven, where pilgrim companies travel between Shalgora, Urvaius, and Wind Keep.
place_lore.nirncraft.renaud_farm.rumour: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.renaud_farm report signs of turnpike highwaymen, Sanguine revel-cultists, and woodland thorn-covens operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.renaud_farm.v8_lore:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.renaud_farm

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.renaud_farm. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.renaud_farm

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the abbey turnpikes and hospice-valleys of central Stormhaven, where pilgrim companies travel between Shalgora, Urvaius, and Wind Keep. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.renaud_farm have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by turnpike highwaymen, Sanguine revel-cultists, and woodland thorn-covens. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

place_lore.nirncraft.rift_frost_spider_h: A damp sinkhole in the birch forest where silk canopies hang between the fallen trunks and rotting logs.
Honey-gatherers stay well north of the Frost Spider Hollow; once your boots stick in the ground-webbing, you don't walk out.

Folio #57 (800, 1560): Field inspection recorded for Rift Frost Spider Hollow within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #57 for rift_frost_spider_hollow: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Rift Frost Spider Hollow are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Blazed three X-marks into the white birch bark along the rim of this hollow so the honey-crews won't blunder into it after dusk. Bring lamp-oil and fire-salts if the hold guard ever gets around to burning the egg-sacs.
A Legion war camp in the forest south of Ivarstead, keeping watch over the pass road and the Stormcloak lines to the north.

General Tullius,
The Rift remains Ulfric's in name and Black-Briar's in fact. I recommend we stop thinking of the Jarl as the obstacle. Maven Black-Briar would sell Riften to us tomorrow if we offered her the right price and the right title.

Item: a customs clerk, Corvus Tullian, has not reported since the 6th of Frostfall. His last letter mentioned irregularities at a Black-Briar mine. I would like to send men. I do not have men.

Item: the dragons. One was seen over Autumnwatch Tower on the 14th. My men are soldiers, sir, not dragon hunters.
The Legion's camped in the woods south of Ivarstead. They don't buy bread, they requisition it. Still, nobody's been robbed on that road since they came.

place_lore.nirncraft.rift_stormcloak_cam:
Commander,
Ulfric wants the Rift held without a fight if a fight can be avoided. Jarl Laila is with us, but her court is not, and the Black-Briar woman sits on both sides of every fence.

Watch the Legion's camp south of Ivarstead. Watch the Watchtower east of you, which the bandits seem to think they own. Do not provoke Maven Black-Briar. Talos guard you, and remember: a man who pays for his bread is a man the farmers won't betray.
Galmar
A Stormcloak war camp in the hills north-west of Lake Honrich, close enough to Riften to keep the Jarl honest and the Legion nervous.
The Stormcloaks camp in the hills above Sarethi Farm. They buy bread and pay for it, which is more than I'll say for some.

Folio #19 (1517, 913): Field inspection recorded for Rift Stormcloak Camp within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Mother,
The Rift is beautiful this time of year. Gold leaves everywhere. You'd like it. The food is bad and the sergeant is worse and I have not killed anyone yet, which I am glad of, though I am not supposed to say so.

There is a Dunmer woman at the farm below us who grows singing plants. I bought one for you. It hums in my pack all night. The sergeant says it's an Imperial trick. I think it's just lonely.
place_lore.nirncraft.rift_watchtower.hoo: A stone watchtower on the road between Ivarstead and Riften, abandoned by the guard and taken by whoever is boldest that season. This season, it's bandits.
place_lore.nirncraft.rift_watchtower.rum: Rift Watchtower? Bandits, last I heard. They take the tower, the guard takes it back, the bandits take it again. Like a game of tafl nobody wins.

place_lore.nirncraft.rift_watchtower.tow:
#2nd of Frostfall
Two men short. Relief from Riften promised for the 5th.
#5th of Frostfall
No relief. Captain sends word the Knives at Faldar's Tooth are the priority.
#8th of Frostfall
Smoke on the ridge. Six of them, maybe seven.

#8th, night
They're at the door. They asked if we'd rather walk to Riften or be carried. Jarl's tower or no, I'm not dying for a heap of stones the Jarl forgot she owned. Leaving this log for whoever cares. Nobody, I expect.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften.briar_debt_l:
#Accounts due, Frostfall 4E 201
Merryfair Farm: paid in full, as always.
Snow-Shod Farm: forty septims short. Send someone polite. Then someone less polite.
Heartwood Mill: lumber for the meadery vats, owed since Hearthfire.

#Road income
Fort Greenwall toll, the Brannoc arrangement: 310 septims this month, less his cut. He is skimming. Tell him so, once.
Last Vigil: no payment. Those are not our people. Let the guard find them.
Note to self: the Greenwall toll book must never reach the Jarl's steward. Brannoc keeps it in his strongbox like a fool. If he hangs, the book must burn with him.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften.guard_notice:
^BY ORDER OF JARL LAILA LAW-GIVER
The band calling itself the Ashwood Knives has robbed travellers on the western road between Heartwood Mill and Riften no fewer than eleven times since Last Seed.

The guard believes they shelter in the ruin of Faldar's Tooth. A bounty of two hundred septims is offered for proof that their captain, one Ottar Ashwood, will trouble the road no longer.

The guard will not be sending men. The guard has its hands full.
Scratched underneath in a different hand: 'hands full of Briar coin more like'
place_lore.nirncraft.riften.hook: Riften sits on the shore of Lake Honrich behind wooden walls and older debts. The Black-Briars own the meadery, the guards and most of the Jarl's good opinions, and the Thieves Guild owns the rest.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften.ratway_plank:
DONT BUY THE RED
it tastes like summer and then it takes you. Edda went to the den up north of the lake for more and never came back. Her boy went after her. Neither of them.

Redwater. They say it's just a cabin by the spring. It goes down further than a cabin goes.
Somebody else has added: Ask for Hjalla Grey-Shawl by the canal if you are going up there. Her boy is the one who went. She pays what she has.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften.rumour: Keep your purse in your shirt and your opinions in your mouth. In Riften, the walls have ears and the ears have friends.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften_stables.carr:
#Frostfall bookings
3rd: Two to Windhelm. Paid.
7th: One to Whiterun, a nervous Imperial clerk. Paid double to leave at night. Never turned up.
11th: One to Ivarstead, an old man with a bell. Paid in copper bits. Walked the last mile because the horse wouldn't go past Nilheim.
15th: Black-Briar crates to the lake road. Not paid. Never paid.
Reminder to myself: if a man in a grey hood asks who went where, the answer is always 'I don't remember'. It's cheaper than remembering.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften_stables.hook: The stables outside Riften's north gate, where caravans unload, carriages leave for the rest of Skyrim and every passing stranger is studied by somebody who works for somebody.
place_lore.nirncraft.riften_stables.rumo: Want to leave Riften quick? Carriage at the stables. Want to leave without anyone knowing? That costs more, and you don't ask the driver.

place_lore.nirncraft.rihad.ashabah_lette:
Brother,
The city still will not let us inside the walls after dark. They buy our protection by day and bar the gate against us by night, as if the smell of the grave were on us. Let them. We camp at the bright stone north of the city, where the Lady of Light keeps her shrine, and we watch.

There is a bone-singer in the hills. He has raised the caravan of Old Jafar, every camel and drover of it, and walks them in circles under the moon. Worse: he has dug up an Ansei. One of the old sword-singers, buried with his blade. The blade sings for the necromancer now. Come quickly. Bring salt.
place_lore.nirncraft.rihad.hook: A Forebear trading city on the Gold Coast border, rich in wine and wagons, where the Ash'abah watch the sands for the walking dead and the merchants watch the road to Cyrodiil for buyers.
place_lore.nirncraft.rihad.rumour: Rihad wine's the best in Hammerfell, and the Rihad dead are the worst. The Ash'abah say the bone-singers have come back to the hills north of town. Drink while you can.
place_lore.nirncraft.rihad.wine_ledger.p: Pressed this season: 400 casks of the red, 120 of the gold. Sold to Kvatch: 90. Sold to Anvil: 160. Sold to Lord Ezhar's agents in Taneth: everything else, at a price that made me weep.

Missing: 12 casks of the gold, the very best, taken from the cellar by my own son and carried north-east to the Sanguine shrine for some revel. He came back on the third day with no shoes, a goat, and a deed to a vineyard in Cyrodiil he does not remember winning. The deed is genuine. The goat will not leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimerock_burrow.cac:
In case the dremora wins the argument:
I have hidden my reserves at the foot of Pinefrost Tower, south of here. Walk round the tower until you face the sea. Count twelve paces downhill. Under the flat grey stone with a lichen like a hand, there is a box.
In it, two soul gems I charged myself and coin enough to cross to High Rock. I will not need either if I am dead. Whoever reads this: spend it on something the Thalmor would hate.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimerock_burrow.exi:
#Morning Star, 4E 199
I left Summerset with three books, one robe and an opinion. The Justiciars would have tolerated the robe. The books were questionable. The opinion was fatal: that Talos, whatever else he was, was a man who became more than a man, and that the Dominion fears this because it suggests anyone might.

#Frostfall, 4E 201
The embassy has found me. I saw their agent on the ridge by Pinefrost Tower. I have bound a dremora to the door, a Valkynaz of some standing. He despises me, which makes him reliable.
#Later
The binding is slipping. He has started speaking to me through the wall in a very calm voice. I have written everything I know of the Dominion's work in Skyrim in this journal. If I die, someone in Solitude should have it.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimerock_burrow.hoo: A frost-sealed cave in the far west of Haafingar, warmed by a sorcerer's fires. An elven exile hid here from the Thalmor, and bound something to guard his door.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimerock_burrow.rum: There's a high elf living in a hole up in the western hills, and he's no friend of the embassy. The embassy's been asking about him. So has something with red skin that walks the snow at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen.caravaneer_l:
Cousin Ja'darri,
This one writes from Rimmen, where the spice road is bad and the Thalmor are worse. A caravan cannot move three hours without a new paper to stamp. This one has learned to forge the stamps. The forgeries are better than the real ones. The Thalmor have praised them.

If you are still in Leyawiin, tell the Count's wife the silk she ordered is coming. Tell her it is coming slowly because the road passes the Mephala stones and this one will not go near them at night. She will understand. That woman understands everything she should not.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen.hook: A walled Khajiit city on the northern edge of Elsweyr, facing Cyrodiil, where Thalmor overseers, Imperial traders and the laughing rebels of the Renrijra Krin all watch each other over the same market stalls.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen.rumour: Rimmen is a fine city for watching. The Thalmor watch the gates, the Renrijra Krin watch the Thalmor, and the merchants watch everybody's purses. Watch your own, friend.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen.thalmor_tari: Overseer Ilmendil, Aldmeri Trade Office, Rimmen

^By arrangement with the Mane
All caravans entering or leaving Rimmen shall present their goods at the Trade Office for inspection. Moon sugar shall be declared by weight. Weapons shall be declared by number. Grievances shall be declared in writing, and will be filed.

Beneath, in claw-scratched Ta'agra, translated by a helpful passer-by: 'Grievances are filed. Then they are burned. This one has filed eleven. Here is the twelfth: the Overseer's purse is heavier on Fredas than on Morndas. The Renrijra Krin will be happy to file it for him.'
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen_artisans_dis:
#OPEN COMMISSIONS
For the Prince: a seven-strand cloth. (Do not ask Kahlil.) For the Temple: nine lamps, each with a different flame. For the Hall: a pillar, blank, to be left blank.
For anyone: a spoon for a cat who outlived everyone, ten years in the making.
The craft quarter of Rimmen, stepped down the cliff in terraces of kiln-smoke and chisel-song, where a hundred artisans work under the shadow of the palace.
In the Artisans' District no one is ever done. Ask a potter if a bowl is finished and she will turn it, and tell you it needs one more glaze.
#THE HALL, BY THE HOUR
Dawn: Smiths. Mid-morning: Weavers. Noon: Glaziers, who are not to be spoken to. Afternoon: Potters. Dusk: Carvers. Night: Jewellers and Lamp-makers, sharing the great table by long-standing and bitter agreement.
A long-roofed hall of workshops below the Rimmen cliff where the seven guilds of artisans hammer, weave, glaze and argue under the same rafters.
No two guilds agree on the colour of the Masterworks roof, and so it has been painted seven times in seven layers, each guild's colour on its own stripe.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen_necropolis.h: A vast city of the dead in layers, with crypt avenues, moon-lit atria and a lunar clock chamber that descends with the moons' cycle.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen_necropolis.r: The Rimmen necropolis has a clock that stopped between two moons. Some say it is waiting for faces.
place_lore.nirncraft.rimmen_necropolis.w: EACH NICHE A FACE, EACH FACE A NAME. The clock does not run while a niche stands empty. It is not cruelty; it is order. Return what was taken. The dead are not impatient. They have time.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverhold.envoy_com: Envoy Telarnil, to the Thalmor in Alinor

Third audience with the Mane. I was received with great warmth. I was offered tea, then a second tea, then a recital of Khajiit poetry that lasted two hours and concerned a sand-flea. At the end the Mane thanked me for my patience and dismissed the court.

I have still not been permitted to raise the matter of the Rimmen tariffs. I suspect I never will be. I also suspect the poem was about me. Recommend we send someone the Mane dislikes; it may be the only way to be taken seriously.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverhold.guard_led: Captain Shazar-ri of the Mane's Guard

#Duties, the week of Hearthfire
Gate: Ja'zhar, Ma'dara, the twins. Thalmor escorts: J'riss, who smiles best. Dungeon: nobody, because there is nobody in it, because the Mane does not keep prisoners, because the Mane is merciful.

Special: Ra'vinni to ride south to the Molag Bal stones and see if the slaver-rumours are true. He is to look and not fight. He is a Cathay-raht and will fight anyway. Send Do'sara with him to drag him home.
Special: someone ask the cooks why they keep going to the Sanguine stones. It is becoming a problem with the soup.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverhold.hook: The seat of the Mane, spiritual leader of all Khajiit, in the dry hills of Anequina, where the Thalmor are received with honey and silk and sent home with nothing at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverhold.rumour: The Mane sits in Riverhold and smiles at the Elves. A Khajiit smile has many meanings. You should hear the Mane's guard laugh after the envoys leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverside_shack.hoo: A trapper's shack on the White River south of Morvunskar, abandoned in a hurry with the stew still in the pot, and a dead hunter's warnings scrawled in its daybook.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverside_shack.kje: For my sister Rannveig, if I don't make it to Kynesgrove:

Thirty years of pelts are in an iron box under the flat stone on the west bank of Mara's Eye Pond, the one with the moss shaped like a hand. Dig on the side away from the water. It is not much. It is more than the Jarl ever thought a trapper was worth.

Buy yourself a house in town. Somewhere with a wall. And Mother's gold ring is in there too, wrapped in the fox fur. Wear it. She always said it was wasted on a trapper's sister, and she was wrong about that, as she was about most things.

#11th of Frostfall
Traps by the pond empty three days running. Not robbed: emptied of blood. The fox in the last one was white as frost and light as a glove.

#13th of Frostfall
Saw pale folk walking the bank at dusk, no torch between them, toward the hills where Cronvangr Cave opens. They did not leave tracks in the snow, or I could not see them. I do not know which is worse.

#14th of Frostfall
I am going to Kynesgrove tomorrow and I am not coming back to this shack. Let them have the stew.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverside_shack.rum: Old Kjeld at the Riverside Shack used to sell pelts at the Kynesgrove market every Fredas. He hasn't come since Frostfall. Nobody wants to be the one to check.

place_lore.nirncraft.riverwood.fisher_ta:
#Week of the 10th, Second Seed
Salmon: 14. Two to the Sleeping Giant, Orgnar paid in coin for once. Six to the Riverwood Trader, Lucan haggled like a Khajiit. Rest smoked.
Slaughterfish: 3. Bit the net through. Bit my thumb too.

#Week of the 17th
Salmon: 4. The pool below the bridge has gone mean. Something big has moved in under the rocks, and on Tirdas it tore Father's net-charm right off the line, the iron fish he carved before I was born.

I will get it back. Not alone, though. Not with those teeth in the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverwood.hook: A mill town where the White River leaves the mountains, smelling of sawdust and pine. Bleak Falls Barrow watches from the ridge above, and Riverwood watches it right back.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverwood.mill_lett:
Dear Ingrid,
The mill keeps me busy and my back aches, so all is as it should be. Gerdur pays fair and feeds better. The river is high from the thaw and we lost two logs past the falls, which Hod blamed on me and I blamed on Kyne.

There is a thing I did not want to write, but you always know when I hide something. Three nights now there has been a light on the ridge, up at Bleak Falls Barrow. Not a campfire. Blue, and steady, and it goes out all at once when you stare at it.

Nobody here will talk of it after dark. Come for Mother's name-day if you can. Bring the honey cakes. Your brother, Torsten.
place_lore.nirncraft.riverwood.rumour: Riverwood's quiet enough, if you don't count the barrow on the cliff. Thyra the fisher lost her father's charm in the river last week. Ask her about it, she's been in a black mood since.

place_lore.nirncraft.rkhardahrk.rumour: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.rkhardahrk report signs of Devilrock cinder-witches, corrupt ore-overseers, and Khulari mine-stalkers operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.rkhardahrk.v8_lore_:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.rkhardahrk

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.rkhardahrk. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.rkhardahrk

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the red iron-passes and volcanic tubes of the Dragontail Mountains between Rihad, Tigonus, and Shedungent, worked by indentured debt-miners. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.rkhardahrk have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by Devilrock cinder-witches, corrupt ore-overseers, and Khulari mine-stalkers. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

place_lore.nirncraft.rkuldumz_spire.hook: A tall brass-pipe tower on a rock island off the Telvannis coast, whose top vents steam at fixed hours.
place_lore.nirncraft.rkuldumz_spire.rumo: Rkuldumz steams once at the turn of every tide and the brass glints on the mud shift on the hour.
place_lore.nirncraft.rkuldumz_spire.thre: ALL DIALS ANSWER HERE. When the eighth hand meets its mark the spire speaks, and all the halls of the world awaken at once. This may be a recall or a release. The dial does not distinguish. Hold the hand or let it fall. Choose carefully, hearer.
The spire sounds a note I cannot hear but my mushroom-tower's tiles do. Each steam-peak, the cogs on the coast shift an inch toward Balmora, as if called. It is not a beacon; it is a summons. Something wants to be whole and has been asking politely for two thousand years.

place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_bright_sci: A white-washed roadhouse beneath a painted scimitar, where caravan men and pirates drink on opposite sides of the same long table and pretend not to see each other.
The Bright Scimitar has one rule posted over the bar: no quarrels at the table. Outside, the road is long, and the sand is deep, and they have been known to settle things there.

^HOUSE RULES
^One: no quarrels at the table.
^Two: no quarrels at the bar.
^Three: no quarrels in the yard before sundown.
^Four: if you must quarrel, the road is wide, and the dunes are patient.

^A note in a different hand: "I have been the innkeeper for nineteen years and have buried eleven of the road's quarrels. The twelfth is waiting. If you are the twelfth, do not drink the red. If you are the thirteenth, I am sorry."

place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_green_boug:
#THE FLOORS
First: the taproom. Second to fifth: rooms. Sixth: storeroom. Seventh: Tamlin's own, with the good bed. Eighth to tenth: guest rooms, not yet furnished. Eleventh: the growing floor, newly grown, smelling of sap and surprise.
Below, a note in a different hand: 'It has begun to grow a floor on the outside, too. Do not go out on it.'
A roadside inn built into a great bough that has been growing a new floor each year, and which no one has been able to stop or explain.
The Green Bough has eleven floors now and the roof is a very long way up. At the top the room has no door, and the bough, they say, is still thinking about it.

place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_ruins.corv:
#11th of Hearthfire
The Falkreath yard is a wonder. Twenty generations of the dead, and the soil keeps them fresh as winter apples. The tanner was a fine first subject. His ring I kept as a fee; he will not miss it.
#14th
The cooper's child. I hesitated. I am not proud of the hesitation. The Mistress wants small ones for the work at the sanctum, to fit in the narrow places.

#19th
The widow Asgerd walks well. I have taught her to fetch. The gravedigger has seen my boot prints, I think. She sits up at night now with a shovel across her knees. Brave woman. Waste of good bones to let her live, but the Mistress forbids attention.
place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_ruins.hook: A tumbled Nordic ruin beside the old road northwest of Falkreath. Its lower vault has a new tenant who carries a green lantern and brings home bodies from the town graveyard.
place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_ruins.rumo: There's a cold green light in the Roadside Ruins at night. The gravedigger reckons that's where her missing dead have gone. She's not wrong often.
place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_ruins.sk4_: Folio #28 (-1003, 1131): Field inspection recorded for Roadside Ruins within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #28 for roadside_ruins: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Roadside Ruins are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_ruins.velm:
Corvus,
Your last delivery arrived at Southfringe Sanctum in good order, save the child, who keeps trying to walk home. I have bound her more firmly. Do not be sentimental. Sentiment is a poor binding agent.

Send three more before the snows close the Helgen road. Take from the old rows, where no one visits. If the gravedigger troubles you, do not kill her: a murder brings the Jarl, a theft brings only gossip. I keep the ledger of names, Corvus. Every one of them will serve. Velmira.

place_lore.nirncraft.roadside_twin_moons: A roadhouse where travellers bet on the phase of the two moons and the keeper keeps losing, and never learns to stop.
Ma'tir has lost eleven cellars, three horses and one husband to the moons, and says the husband was the least interesting loss.

#WAGERS OF THIS MONTH
Masser full, Secunda waning: lost three casks. Both new: lost a mule. Secunda full, Masser a sliver: lost the roof, but only temporarily. The sky is not honest, and I pay for it.
place_lore.nirncraft.robbers_gorge.hook: A narrow cut above a river crossing in the marshy north, where a gang of bandits has strung a rope and calls it a toll gate. Nobody voted on the price.
place_lore.nirncraft.robbers_gorge.rumou: The fishers at Crabber's Shanty pay a toll now just to bring their catch downriver. Bandits in Robber's Gorge. Took a whole barrel of mudcrab off old Hroald last week.
place_lore.nirncraft.robbers_gorge.toll_:
Listen, you lot. The rope stays up from dawn to dusk. Anyone crossing pays one in five of whatever they carry. Fish, furs, coin, I don't care.
If they can't pay, take their boots. If they argue, take their boots and their boat.

Nobody touches the Crabber's Shanty folk past what's owed. A dead fisher catches no fish, and a fisher with no fish pays no toll. Think long, not short.
Anybody caught skimming from the toll chest hangs from the rope instead. I'm not saying it twice.
Brenna

Hroald of Crabber's Shanty: 1 barrel mudcrab. Argued. Took his hat as well.
Two pilgrims bound for Dead Men's Respite: 14 septims, 1 prayer book (useless), 1 candle.
Nord trapper: 3 wolf pelts. Gave them up quick. Smart man.
Legion courier: ran. Arrows. Satchel in the river. Brenna says don't do that again, Legion counts its couriers.

Brenna's note at the bottom: 'Pilgrims pay half. We're not monsters. And somebody give Hroald his hat back next time he comes through, he was crying about it to the whole marsh and now the Shanty folk won't sell us bait. A gang that can't get bait is a gang that eats bark.'

place_lore.nirncraft.root_whisper_villag: An abandoned Hist-village, huts overgrown with root-vine and a central fire-pit still warm at the edges.
Root Whisper's folk left in a night. The roots have grown into their huts and their table has a chair that stays warm.

~From the red hill to the green,~from the mountain to the mire,~ash goes drifting, ash is seen,~ash goes carrying its fire.~What it burned it will not lose.~What it knew it will not choose.~In the root, the ash is heard,~each name a quiet, rooted word.

The root spoke, three nights running. A name, nothing more. We could not hear it exactly, but we knew it was a name. We began to set a place. The elders thought it was an ancestor. The children said no. It was someone who had never been counted. The thirteenth night, the root said it again, and we left. I am sorry.
place_lore.nirncraft.rorikstead.frostfru:
^FROSTFRUIT INN
^Prices this season
Bed, one night: 10 septims
Bowl of cabbage stew: 3
Tankard of Honningbrew: 6
Tankard of anything else: 4, and you'll wish you'd paid the 6

WANTED: strong hands for the barley harvest. Board and wages. Ask Lemkil, if he is in a good mood. He is never in a good mood.

LOST: one trapper, Lund by name, tall, grey beard, smells of pelts. Last seen heading for his hut in the northwest hills. His wife Hjalla asks anyone passing that way to knock on his door.
place_lore.nirncraft.rorikstead.hook: A farming village on the western edge of the Tundra, famous for crops that never fail even when the rest of Skyrim starves. Nobody can quite say why.
place_lore.nirncraft.rorikstead.rumour: Rorikstead's never had a bad harvest, not once in living memory. Some thank Kynareth, some thank Rorik's luck. Hjalla, the trapper's wife, just wants her husband back from the hills.
place_lore.nirncraft.rorikstead.sk4_note: Folio #9 (-1652, -228): Field inspection recorded for Rorikstead within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.rorikstead.soil_let: Aurelia Venn, of the Imperial agricultural survey

To the Office of the Imperial Steward at Solitude,
I have spent nine days testing the soil of Rorikstead, as instructed. I regret to report that it is ordinary soil. Clay, a little sand, the usual stones. I have seen better earth in the Nibenay valley that produced half as much.

The villagers are unhelpful. One told me the founder Rorik made a bargain with the ground itself. Another told me to stop digging holes in his turnips. A third, the most honest, said that if I found the secret I should keep it to myself, because the Thalmor would want it next.

I request leave to return to Cyrodiil. I do not like how well everything grows here.

place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_bthalft.as:
The Dwemer built here because the veil was thin. They were not fools, whatever else they were. The Prince of Change has touched these stones before and will again.

Third offering made the 12th of Frostfall: a ram, a ledger stolen from a Riften tax clerk, and a lock of hair from a Legion deserter. The Prince prefers broken oaths to blood. Blood is merely convenient.
Fourth offering on the night of the dark moon. I need a living one this time. Someone the Legion camp will not miss. They never count their deserters properly.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_bthalft.dw:
The plate is in the old Dwemer script, which nobody in the Rift reads. Someone has tried anyway and written their guesses beneath each line in charcoal:

'...door... or gate?...'
'...hot... beneath? under the hill?...'
'...do not... (do not what? the rest is cracked)'

At the bottom, newer and in a firmer hand: 'Do not open it. That's what it says. I'd stake my life on it.'
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_bthalft.ho: A tumble of Dwemer stonework in the woods south-east of Ivarstead, older than the Nords who now ignore it. Lately someone has been leaving burnt offerings on the steps.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_bthalft.ru: Hunters say there's red light at the old Dwemer stones at night now, and a smell like brimstone. Whoever's up there isn't praying to the Nine.

place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_mazzatun.h: A xanmeer of stepped chambers where the floor is a flooded city, with sap-vein walls and a central shaft.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_mazzatun.r: Mazzatun's flood rises a hand per year. Folk say a quiet figure sits at the bottom and counts.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_mazzatun.w: HE WHO WAS FIRST HAS NO NAME BECAUSE NONE WAS GIVEN. He built the first hut, and the first fire. He wished to be counted and was not. Let whoever finds this give him a name of the marsh, and let it be a good one.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_rkund.hook: A broken circle of Nord stones in the southern hills, where the old clans of the Rift once made their oaths. The stones are cracked, and the oaths with them.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_rkund.oath:
^WHAT IS SWORN HERE IS SWORN FOREVER
^WHAT IS BROKEN HERE IS BROKEN FOREVER

The stone is cracked through from top to bottom. Around the crack, scratched by many hands over many years, are names: Hrothi swore to Asta. Gunnar swore to the Jarl. Ulf swore to his brother. Some names have been struck through. Most of them.
The most recent, cut deep: 'Ottar Ashwood swore to Brannoc Tollhand, the Knives and the Wall stand together.' It has not been struck through. Yet.
place_lore.nirncraft.ruins_of_rkund.rumo: Rkund's just old rocks now. Bandits camp there sometimes. My grandfather said a Nord swore an oath on those stones and broke it, and the stones broke too, out of shame.

place_lore.nirncraft.ruunvald_excavation: A Nord ruin being dug out in the north-eastern hills, promising triple wages to miners from Shor's Stone. The miners go in. The wages never come out.

THRUD
THEY ARE NOT DIGGING FOR ORE
they are digging for a dead man and they want us for his hands
i hid my father's token under the third cart in the cut so they can't use it on me. they use your own things to bind you. thrud dont let anyone come here for me. let someone come here for THEM

#Workers acquired
From Shor's Stone: Kolbjorn (strong, stubborn), Hrafn's brother (weak), the one with the stammer. From the Riften Ratway: two, nameless, unmissed.

The miners dig the outer halls by day and are bound at night. When the cut reaches the vault of the old priest, they will be the vessel. Strong backs make strong thralls.
Our patron in Boulderfall sends word that the Riften supplier wants more coin. Tell him that dead men cost less than live ones, and we are very nearly finished with the live ones.
Ruunvald pays triple. That's what they told Kolbjorn. That's what they told all of them. Haven't seen a coin of it come home yet, nor a man.

place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal.dig_notice:
BY ORDER OF THE COLLEGE OF WINTERHOLD
The excavation at Saarthal is the property of the College. Unauthorised digging, removal of artefacts, or entering the lower halls is forbidden. The lower halls are forbidden to College personnel also.

The College accepts no responsibility for persons lost in the lower halls, nor for anything that may follow them out. The sealed passage marked with red chalk is to remain sealed.
If you hear voices from the red-chalked door, inform a master and do not answer.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal.digger_jou:
#12th of Second Seed, 4E 189
Hired on as a digger for the College men at Saarthal. Two septims a day and soup. Ysolde says I'm a fool to work for the people who drowned the city. I said the College pays better than the sea.

#20th of Second Seed
Broke through into a lower hall today. Old Atmoran carvings, ships and wolves and a great fire. The mage in charge went white as milk and said we were to seal it again at once. The others did. I went back after supper. I had to see.

#No date
The dead here are not resting. I am cut off from the upper halls and my lamp is low. I have Mother's amulet of Kyne in my fist. Ysolde, if anyone brings you this, I am sorry. I should have listened.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal.hook: The ruins of the first city of men in Skyrim, dug into the hills south of Winterhold. The College is excavating it, and Winterhold folk remember the last dig that went wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal.rumour: The College has its diggers back in Saarthal. My brother went in with the last lot, years ago. He never came out.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal.sk4_note_1: Folio #13 (1144, -1573): Field inspection recorded for Saarthal within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #13 for saarthal: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Saarthal are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarthal_ridge_moun: A frost-rimmed dragon burial mound crowning the glacial ridge above the ancient excavations of Saarthal.
Scholars walking out to Saarthal say compass needles spin wild whenever you pass within twenty paces of the Saarthal Ridge Mound.

While surveying the upper glacial moraine above the dig site, we cleared snow from a circular ring of interlocking basalt blocks. The runes along the inner curb predate even the late First Era timber halls down in Winterhold.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarvik_landing.hoo: A landing of broken ships on an Atmoran shore, ribs and masts half-buried in drifts, a single cairn at the tide line.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarvik_landing.rum: At Saarvik the ships sit in drifts, and the cairn's rune glows when the ice speaks.
place_lore.nirncraft.saarvik_landing.web: ICE CRACKS UNDER THE LONG HALLS. WHO HAS EARS, HEAR IT. The ships here were broken by those who chose not to leave. Do not make their choice. The captain's ship waits in the howe. Wake her before the thaw.
place_lore.nirncraft.sacellum_of_boethia: ^THE SACELLUM ASKS NOTHING THAT YOU WOULD NOT TAKE

~Trust is a door. Walk through it.
~Love is a blade. Hold it by the grip.
~The weak are betrayed. The strong betray first.
~Boethiah watches the hand, not the heart.
^Kneel. And when you rise, rise alone.

Below the chiselled words, someone has scratched a tally of names with a knife-point, each one crossed out by a different hand: Eyvind. Brunhild. Olfrid the Younger. Marcus, a legionary. Two dozen more. Beside the last uncrossed name, Harrald, a fresh line has been started, and left unfinished, as if whoever was cutting it was interrupted, or changed their mind.
A ring of black stone on a hill east of Windhelm where the cult of Boethiah gathers, offering the Prince of Plots the one sacrifice she prizes most: a friend's trust.

#14th of Frostfall
The priestess said the Lady wants a betrayal, not a corpse. Any fool can kill. To be chosen, I must give her someone who would never have believed I would do it.

#16th of Frostfall
I brought Eyvind. Twenty years we have hunted together. I told him there was a sabre cat at the shrine. I told him I would watch his back.

#17th of Frostfall
The Lady was pleased. I have her blessing. My hands do not stop shaking and the blessing does nothing for that. I cannot remember why I wanted this. I can only remember that Eyvind smiled at me, right at the end, as if it were a joke he did not yet understand.
There's a temple to Boethiah out east, past the farms. They say the price of joining is a friend, and they don't mean a recommendation.

place_lore.nirncraft.sadrith_mora.gazett: Dalyne Hlaren of the Gateway Inn

#Who lives where
Magister Gaenor Dreth levitates above the Council Spire and is perpetually bored. Magister Ulveni Rathra keeps fourteen floors, eleven guardians and a singing teapot at Tel Naga. Skeema the Sporekeeper tends the greenhouses and will tell you not to look at the grey ones. Apprentice Veya carries slippers up fourteen floors and would like to learn something else.

#Rooms and rumours
Every window of the Gateway Inn shows somewhere; room nine has recently shown a woman in a green shawl. Fennik Sul's Spore & Sundry sells fumigation salts and asks that glowing jars be closed again. Sergeant Maro Gallus keeps the Wolverine Hall garrison and the Legion's distance from the towers.
place_lore.nirncraft.sadrith_mora.hireli:
^Articles of Hire
Article 1. The Hireling shall perform such errands as the Master sees fit.
Article 7. Errands may include the gathering of reagents, the carrying of correspondence, the testing of potions and the being of a subject.
Article 12. 'Subject' shall be understood in the broadest sense.

Article 19. The Hireling waives all claim to the shape the Hireling began service in.
Article 31. The Master is not liable for spores.
Article 40. The Hireling acknowledges having read all forty Articles. The Hireling, by signing, also acknowledges Articles 41 through 60, which are written in an ink visible only by the light of Secunda.
place_lore.nirncraft.sadrith_mora.hook: The Telvanni town on an island off the east coast, where giant mushroom towers house the most powerful and least neighbourly wizards in Morrowind, and every contract has a clause you didn't read.
place_lore.nirncraft.sadrith_mora.rumour: Sadrith Mora's safe enough if you keep your eyes down and your hands where a wizard can see them. Never, ever sign anything they hand you in the Gateway Inn.
place_lore.nirncraft.sadrith_mora.spore_:
Honoured Steward,
The Mistress's tower has been coughing spores onto the harbour for nine days. My nets are white with them. My catch has grown little caps. My wife's hair has grown a little cap. I ask, with every respect, that the Mistress be asked to cover her tower's mouth.

I understand that the Mistress does not answer petitions from fishermen. I understand that the Mistress has a long memory. I would point out, respectfully, that I also have a long memory, and a boat, and I know which rocks the Mistress's supply ships like to avoid.
place_lore.nirncraft.saerings_watch.drag:
#3rd of Sun's Dusk
Set up the ballista bolts on the ridge. The beast comes back to the watch every dusk and lands beside the word wall. It speaks to the wall. I swear it. It speaks, and the letters glow.

#5th of Sun's Dusk
We hit it once. Once. Halla is burned. Ofeig ran. I am writing this behind the word wall, which the fire does not seem to touch. If you find this, do not come with three men and a bolt-thrower. Come with a Voice, or do not come at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.saerings_watch.hook: A high stone perch in the snowy north where a dragon once kept watch for the Dragon Priests. Wingbeats echo off the peaks again, and the old word wall is scorched black.
place_lore.nirncraft.saerings_watch.rumo: A dragon roosts on Saering's Watch. I've seen it circle Frykte Peak at dawn. The Skaal say it's waiting for someone. I don't intend to find out who.
place_lore.nirncraft.saerings_watch.saer:
~Saering sat on the high grey rock,
~Watching the sea for the tall ships' mast,
~Watching the snow for the hunters' track,
~Watching the priests till the priests had passed.

~The priests are bones, the ships are wood,
~The hunters' grandsons hunt no more,
~But Saering's children keep the watch,
~And still they count us, shore to shore.

~Old Saering sleeps, his children wake,
~They wheel above the Frykte stone.
~Who climbs the watch must bring a voice,
~Or climb the watch and stay alone.
The Skaal sing this to children who wander too far north. Then they sing it again, slower, to the ones who wander back.

place_lore.nirncraft.saintsport.hook: A shrine harbour on the Stros M'Kai coast, with a shrine to a drowned saint and a bell that rings under water.
place_lore.nirncraft.saintsport.rumour: Saintsport's bell rings under water every fifth year, and a family goes quiet.
place_lore.nirncraft.saintsport.web.p0: Saint of the swallowed bell, whom the sea took on the fifth year: hold the ship's tilt in your two hands. Bring us back or let us be the ones who did not come. We do not ask what we carry. We carry it. Amen. Amen. Amen.

place_lore.nirncraft.salvius_farm.farm_a:
#Last Seed, 4E 201
Sold to Markarth market: cabbage, 2 crates. Leeks, 1 crate. 34 septims.
Sold to Left Hand Mine kitchen: bread, cheese, 18 septims. Skaggi still owes for Hearthfire last.
Paid: rent to the Silver-Bloods for the lower field, 40 septims. Rent was 25 last year.

Lucan's wages from the mine have stopped. Skaggi says the deep drift was closed after the spiders came up through the old Dwemer cut, and that my brother 'went the wrong way'. He went to fetch his tools, Skaggi. He went to fetch the pick Father gave him.
place_lore.nirncraft.salvius_farm.hook: A stubborn Imperial family farm in the shadow of Markarth's walls, growing what it can in rocky soil and feeding the miners of Left Hand Mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.salvius_farm.rumour: The Salvius girl walks a basket of bread up to Left Hand Mine every morning. Lately she comes back with it still full. Her brother hasn't been eating, or hasn't been there.

place_lore.nirncraft.sancre_tor.hook: A mountaintop Akaviri fortress above a barrow of dragon-hunters, with pagoda-curved halls over long tomb galleries.
place_lore.nirncraft.sancre_tor.rumour: Sancre Tor's walls once rang. The hunters swore the barrow's gate rings three notes on the night before a storm.
place_lore.nirncraft.sancre_tor.thread.p: Bone nineteen of forty-one: taken from the Sancre Tor barrow in the winter of last year. A Tsaesci in a monk's robe made the cut, courteous, and left a donation. I did not stop him; I did not know the count. Forty-one graves, forty-one bones. I do not know where the others are. I suspect the east.
place_lore.nirncraft.sancre_tor.web.p0: We came in boats from the east with orders to guard a door. The door was already guarded by the ones who built it. We stayed. We hung our bells to keep our dead company. When the empire forgot us, the bells became a lock. If you ring all seven, you will know what we are guarding. Do not.
place_lore.nirncraft.sanctum_ophidia.hoo: A serpent-cult sanctum of coiled-column rooms with spiral ramps, scale-patterned floors and a mirror-pool.
place_lore.nirncraft.sanctum_ophidia.rum: The serpent cult of Sanctum Ophidia coils its pool-mirror toward the stair and awaits an end to the world with perfect good manners.
place_lore.nirncraft.sanctum_ophidia.web: Coil, coil, and coil once more. The stair is long and the mirror deep. We have seen what the panels foretell: a figure on a stair, a stepping off. We ask only to be swallowed gently when the Great Coil comes. We have swept the floors, polished the scales, and kept the pool quite clear. Come when you are ready.
place_lore.nirncraft.sand_drowned_villag:
#WE HAVE GONE TO THE WELL
Back by dusk. Do not wait. Dinner is in the pot. The goat has been fed. If the sand rises, leave it. It is not unkind. It is only slow.
The sand has risen. The goat has been fed. The pot is still on the fire, and the fire is still faintly warm. I did not stay. I do not think you would have either.
A village of white-walled houses sunk to the eaves in the Yokudan dunes, its streets still readable beneath a skin of sand, and its well-head still faintly damp.
The village of Sand-Drowned was buried in a single night, they say, and its people simply walked out of their front doors into the sand and did not come back. The doors are still open.

place_lore.nirncraft.sanguines_demesne.h: A realm-pocket of red velvet with banqueting halls, endless mirror corridors and a throne of bones where the party has gone on too long.
place_lore.nirncraft.sanguines_demesne.r: The invitations say the supper is held in a demesne of red velvet, where no one is unhappy and no one remembers the way home.
place_lore.nirncraft.sanguines_demesne.w: ~The wine is red and the music high,~the candles never think to die.~We dance and eat and laugh and bow,~and none of us remember how~we came, or why, or when to leave.~The fog is thick. We do not grieve.
