place_lore.nirncraft.sarethi_farm.avrusa:
Elgrim,
I cannot send the nirnroot this month. The bandits who squat in Treva's Watch came down on the 8th and took twelve plants with the soil still on the roots. My hand, Brelas, tried to stop them. They broke his arm in two places and laughed while they did it.

Their leader wears a grey bear-cloak and calls herself Saltcheek. She told me the Watch is owed a share of everything that grows between the river and the lake. If someone could make her stop believing that, I would pay in coin and in root, both.

Avrusa
place_lore.nirncraft.sarethi_farm.hook: A lonely Dunmer farm west of the lake where the Sarethi family grows nirnroot under careful cover, and trades it to every alchemist in the Rift. Bandits have learned it is worth stealing.
place_lore.nirncraft.sarethi_farm.rumour: Old Sarethi grows nirnroot, of all things. You can hear it singing in the rows at night. Somebody tried to rob her last month. Somebody from Treva's Watch.

place_lore.nirncraft.secundas_kiss.hook: A giant camp on the hill above the river, named for the way the smaller moon seems to touch its peak in autumn. The giants guard their mammoths and their quiet with equal patience.
place_lore.nirncraft.secundas_kiss.rumou: Give Secunda's Kiss a wide berth. The giants up there don't care about you unless you care about their mammoths, and then they care a great deal.
place_lore.nirncraft.secundas_kiss.sheph:
To the Jarl's man in Whiterun, or Falkreath, or whoever owns this hill, for nobody will tell me.
The giant at Secunda's Kiss has taken four of my goats this season. Not killed. Taken. They follow him now. I have seen them grazing among his mammoths as content as you please.

I went to ask for them back and he looked at me the way I look at a goat. I have decided to let them go. But I would like it on record that I am owed four goats by a giant, and if the hold ever means to collect, I will happily stand behind whoever goes to do it. Far behind.

place_lore.nirncraft.senchal.hook: A great port city on Elsweyr's southern coast, home to smugglers, skooma dens and the thieves who claim descent from Rajhin himself, ringed by shrines to the Princes of shadow, secrets and nightmares.
place_lore.nirncraft.senchal.rumour: Senchal is the finest city in Elsweyr for buying anything at all, especially things you should not. Somebody robbed the Nocturnal stones west of town. The thieves of Senchal are scandalised.
place_lore.nirncraft.senchal.skooma_ledg:
#Ships out, Last Seed
The Swift Gull for Anvil: 4 crates herbs (medicinal). Very medicinal. Very many herbs.
The Laughing Kettle for Lilmoth: 60 barrels sugar. Note: last time the Lilmoth harbour sang for three days. The Argonian King sent a polite letter. Do not send so many barrels this time.

#Payments
Thalmor customs post: the usual. Customs post (after the Renrijra Krin visited): nothing, as there is no customs post this week.
To the dream-woman at the Vaermina stones: nothing. This one does not pay that one. This one does not sleep near that one. This one recommends everybody else does the same.
place_lore.nirncraft.senchal.thieves_let: Old Ja'khirr, called the Last Footpad

To the thieves of Senchal, all of you, even the bad ones:
Someone has robbed the Lady's stones west of the city. A gang that calls itself the Shadow-Claws. They took the offerings: coins, rings, and the bow that Rajhin himself hung at the Lady's feet, which no thief has touched in four hundred years.

A thief who robs a thief is a thief. A thief who robs the Lady is a fool, and a fool who robs Rajhin is a corpse who hasn't heard yet. This one is too old to hunt them. This one has left a message at the shrine for whoever comes next. Honour among thieves is a lie told by guardsmen. Honour toward the Lady is not.
place_lore.nirncraft.senchal_merchant_sq: A broad square of striped awnings behind the Senchal quay where sugar, silks and rumours change hands at the same speed, and almost nobody counts which is which.
The square has a rule: whatever you sell in the morning, you may buy back in the afternoon at three times the price. People do this on purpose. It is called loyalty.

#PRICES TODAY
Moon sugar, white: 8. Moon sugar, grey: not for sale, ask elsewhere. Candied peel: 3. Honeyed figs: 4, or 2 if you do not ask where they came from. Advice: free. Silence: dear.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel.harbourmas:
#Week of the 8th of Hearthfire, 4E 201
In: four dhows from Taneth (Forebear cargo, inspected twice, as His Lordship's nephew asked me not to). Two Breton cogs from Wayrest, cloth and wine. One Altmer sloop, turned away at the mole. The Dominion has not been welcome in this harbour since the treaty and I do not intend to be the one who forgets it.

Ashtown, the Dunmer quarter behind the fish market, asks again for leave to keep night lamps burning on the south road. Their priestess walks out to the old Azura stone in the dunes each dusk and the lamps guide her home. Leave granted. They have paid their harbour dues without complaint for thirty years. That is more than I can say for the Forebears.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel.hook: The great harbour-city of the Alik'r coast, seat of the Crowns, where an old lord lies dying in his palace and every faction in Hammerfell has come to watch which way the chair will fall.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel.priest_war: Arkhan at-Sentinel, keeper of the Necropolis gate

Children of the Crowns, remember: Tu'whacca keeps the road for the dead, and the road must be clean. We wash our dead. We wrap them. We sing them across the desert to the Far Shores. We do not leave them for the jackal or the vulture, and we do not leave them for the ones who live by the Namira stone in the dunes south-west of the city.

Some of you have given those people bread. That is kindness and I do not forbid it. But when a beggar of the stone asks you whether any old ones in your household are sickly, do not answer. Close your door. Come and tell me. The dead are owed their journey, and some in this land would cut it short for a meal.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel.rumour: Lord Hamaad's failing. The Crowns say Lady Yasreen will hold Sentinel. The Forebears smile and say nothing. When a Forebear smiles in Sentinel, check the harbour for new ships.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel.veterans_l:
Daughter,
You ask why I will not sit at the Forebear table at your wedding. I will sit. I will eat. I will even dance, if my knee permits. But I marched from Sentinel to the Alik'r wells in the war against the Dominion, and I watched the Forebears in Taneth and Rihad count their profits while the Crowns counted their dead. When the Emperor signed us away to the elves, it was not the merchants who drove the elves out.

That is old dust now. Hammerfell is free and stands alone, and I am glad of it. Marry your Forebear boy. He has good teeth and a kind mother. Only teach your children the names of the dead before you teach them the price of silk.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel_docks.dock:
^NIGHT GANG TALLY, CHALKED BEHIND THE FOURTH BOLLARD
^Barrels in: sixteen. Barrels out: nineteen. I counted three times and the third time there were twenty-two.
^If you read this, the numbers are wrong because the gang is wrong. I will say no more. I have a daughter.
^Under the tally, in blue chalk, a single word: COBALT. And beneath it, smaller: "Do not ask Zareen. She knows, and it will not do her any good."
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel_docks.hook: The long quays of Sentinel, where the Yokudan tide-flags of every Hammerfell clan fly above the cargo of a continent.
place_lore.nirncraft.sentinel_docks.rumo: Every ship at Sentinel is stamped three times. The first stamp is lawful. The second is for the guards. The third nobody admits to, and it is the only one that matters.

place_lore.nirncraft.septimus_signuss_ou:
#Sun's Dusk, 4E 201
Twelfth run to the old man's ice hole. Salt pork, candles, three blank journals, a pot of ink that froze solid on the way. He paid me with a Dwemer coin and a lecture about the Elder Scrolls I did not understand one word of.

He asked me to take a letter to the College. Then he took it back. Then he asked again. In the end I left with it, and on the glacier the wind tore my satchel open. The letter went down a crevasse with my spare mittens.
I went down after the mittens. I found ice wraiths instead.
I am not going back down there. But if someone braver than me fished out that letter, the old man might finally stop asking me about it.
A hollow in the glacier at the very top of the world, where a mad old scholar lives beside a Dwemer lockbox that hums at night.
There's an old Imperial living in the ice north of the College. He talks to a box. Sometimes I think the box talks back.

The lock is not a lock. The lock is a question. The Dwemer did not secure their heart; they ASKED it to stay, and it agreed, and the agreement is the lock.
Therefore: what answers a question? Not a key. A voice. Many voices. Blood remembers voices.
Note to self: eat something. Note to self: the courier is not a spy. Probably. Note to self: do not shout at the box, it does not help, it has never helped.
Note to self, underlined twice: the Dwemer were not gods. They were only very, very good at asking. And asking is a thing I can learn.

place_lore.nirncraft.serpent_pens.hook: A serpent pen of coral-walled pools on a Maormer isle, with feeding platforms and pole-and-net gates.
place_lore.nirncraft.serpent_pens.rumour: The serpents at the pens eat a pink weed and grow, and one pen has already burst. The keepers don't speak of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.serpent_pens.thread: To the admiral: a page of the Yokudan ledger has come into my keeping. It was in the totem's hollow. I am told it is the fifth of nine. I do not know what it is for. It seems to be tides. If it is valuable, I would like an honest price. If it is dangerous, I would like it taken away.
place_lore.nirncraft.serpent_pens.web.p0: Pen 4: burst. Pen 7: bloated, one dead. Pen 9: normal, but the coral grows through the gate. The coral is from the Thras sea; it drifts. I fed them on it because the fish run is poor. They are bigger. They are hungrier. I do not think the coral is food. I think it is an invitation.
place_lore.nirncraft.serpents_bluff_redo: Father, I'm alive. They caught me at the goat pen. They don't hurt me, they just stare and talk in that tongue. One of them, the old woman with the thorns in her hair, keeps a heart in a box and sings to it.

She says when the heart is ready, they'll go west and burn the farms. I heard her say 'Rorikstead' plain as day. Please tell the Legion camp. Please tell someone. I hid this in the wall of my cage. If you are not Father, please bring this to him in Rorikstead. Sissel.

The Nords took the Reach. The Nords took Markarth. The Nords took our dead and buried them in the wrong earth.

Now we take from them. The goats of the Rorik-town. The fat fields. The fat men.

When the briar heart is planted, we burn the Rorik-town's barley and salt its ground, so nothing grows there ever again. Then let them call it lucky.

The serpent on the bluff watches east. The thorn-mother watches with it.

Blood of the Reach. Thorn of the Reach. We do not forget.
A Forsworn stronghold carved into a bluff south-west of Rorikstead, hung with bones and feathers. The Reachmen have pushed further east than ever, and Rorikstead's herds are paying for it.

Forsworn at Serpent's Bluff, this far east! They took four of Lemkil's goats and left a ring of crow feathers round the pen. Their hag-mother calls herself Kaie Thorn-Mother, and she's sworn to burn Rorikstead's fields.

place_lore.nirncraft.seyda_neen.hook: A tiny customs-house port at a lagoon edge, with a silt-strider stop, a pier and a lighthouse with a ledger-room.
place_lore.nirncraft.seyda_neen.rumour: The Seyda Neen clerk says there are more pilgrims coming in than going out. She has stopped opening the post.
place_lore.nirncraft.seyda_neen.web.p0: Landed this month: 212. Departed: 41. Marked 'in transit': 171. In transit to where? The Temple says the canton, the canton says Mournhold, Mournhold says Seyda Neen. I stamp them and they walk inland. Not one has come back through my gate.

~Kyne, mother of the wind,
~we take only the fallen branch.
~We cut no living root.
~We leave honey for the green ones
~and go out the way we came.
^Hunters of Haafingar, before the elves came, and after.

^Cut beneath, with a finer blade:
The elf with the basket did not read this, or read it and did not care. He cut the heart-root and took the shining sap away in glass. Since then the green ones walk the cave all night, and the honey we leave goes untouched. Kyne forgive us. We did not stop him. We did not even try.

#Observation the seventh
The heart-tree of Shadowgreen thrives without sunlight, fed by some current in the stone. Its sap glows faintly when cut. The local spriggans tolerate my presence if I sing while I work. They prefer older songs.

#Observation the ninth
The First Emissary's office has requested a full vial of heartsap, sealed, for 'examination in Alinor.' I am not told why. I am a botanist, not an agent, and I have begun to suspect that the distinction no longer matters to anyone but me.

#Observation the tenth
The spriggans no longer tolerate me. I took too much. I have left the vial hidden in the roots and will not return. If someone else wants it, let them sing louder than I did. The scholar in Solitude who wrote to me about root-magic may give a fairer price than Alinor.
A green-lit cavern north of the Thalmor Embassy where an old tree grows in the dark, tended by spriggans. Someone from the embassy has been taking cuttings.
There's a cave up north where the trees grow underground, green as midsummer. Spriggans keep it. An elf from the embassy goes up there with a basket and comes back with all his fingers, somehow.

place_lore.nirncraft.shardiuss_excavatio: A cut-away of a Blackwood hillside held in scaffolds above a stepped Ayleid terrace, with ladders going down into pale-white stone.
They say the diggers at Shardiuss all quit on one day, paid in barrels instead of coin, and none will go near the pit.

Stone one: relit, Shardiuss. Stone two: Miscarcand's cold vault, relit by the third night. Stone three: Ne Salas pillar, pending. The cabal's instruction: light in order, do not skip. The order matters. Do not ask why; we have asked, and the answer was a silence like a held breath.

Day 31. Sixty names read off the lintel, as the contract asks. At the sixtieth the lamps came on without oil and a voice answered from the cut. I have paid the men in wine as I was told and sent the rubbing to the gate at Alma Ruma. Do not read aloud. Do not say them.

place_lore.nirncraft.shattered_grove.gar:
#DAY ONE
The sapling is a forearm tall. The ribbon says three feet by dusk. I measure again at midnight. It is taller. I measure again at dawn. I am no longer sure what I am measuring.

On the third day I put my ear to the bark. It is not a tree's heartbeat. It is slower, and larger, and there is a second one, faint, behind it. I will not say what I think. I am a gardener. I am only measuring.
place_lore.nirncraft.shattered_grove.hoo: A fallen grove of white trees on the Summerset coast, once a Direnni garden, in which a single young tree has begun to grow at a rate that alarms the gardeners.
place_lore.nirncraft.shattered_grove.rum: The Grove is called Shattered because every tree in it was struck by lightning on the same night, three hundred years ago. All except one. It stood in a ring of burnt wood, untouched. People say it is thinking of something.

place_lore.nirncraft.shearpoint.climber_:
#Frostfall
I have climbed every peak between Whiterun and the sea and Shearpoint is the last. A dragon circles it on fine days; on foul days it doesn't, so I'll climb on a foul day.

#Later
Reached the wall at the summit. A figure in robes and a carved mask, hovering a hand's breadth above the snow, turned to look at me. I said good morning. It raised its staff and the air went cold enough to crack my teeth.
I ran. I'm writing this in a crevice below the summit. My hands are blue. I left my best ice-axe up there. Somebody please fetch it for me.
place_lore.nirncraft.shearpoint.hook: A jagged peak in the hills of the southern Pale, crowned by a dragon wall and haunted by a masked priest of the old cult who never truly died.
place_lore.nirncraft.shearpoint.rumour: Shearpoint's a dragon roost. And not just a dragon. There's a masked thing up there, floating, that the dragon seems to bow to.

place_lore.nirncraft.shimmerene.hook: A busy bay port of white-wood wharves, dockside lanterns on high poles, crane-masts and sail-lofts, where every ship in the west of Summerset is repaired, provisioned and gossiped about.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmerene.rumour: You can tell a Shimmerene sailor by his rope-burns and his opinions. He has strong views on the Maormer, the tides and which tavern waters its wine. All three views are correct, and no two sailors agree.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmerene.wharf_bo:
#THIS WEEK
In: the Silver Plover, the Brine Wasp, three unnamed lighters, and a ship that did not give its name and has been moved on. Out: the Teal Heron, the Loyalty, and every fisher who would like to be paid.
Fen's own addendum, underlined: 'Pole twelve is not mine. It is not on the rota. If it is lit, do not tie up beneath it. If it is dark, do not trust it.'
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmerene_dockwork:
#Third watch
Loaded: forty crates, a barrel, one unlabelled box marked FRAGILE and kept apart. I did not open it. It was warm. It hummed. I put it where the Dock-Master said, between the sail-loft and the quay, and did not ask.

Fifth watch. A man in a blue cloak asked me the weight of the unlabelled box. I told him. He gave me a very small, very heavy coin. I have it. I shall not spend it. It has a wave on one side and a serpent on the other.
The great timber dockworks of Shimmerene, an unbroken sweep of wharves, cranes, rope-walks and sail-lofts that has been rebuilt after every storm for three thousand years.
The dockworks have never fallen down, they say, because the cranes are too proud to be seen on their knees. A crane that is tired simply pretends to be asleep until the tide is high.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmermist_cave.br:
Eyvind,
If you crawl out of that hole and find this, you owe me a mead and a beating, in that order. I waited by the mist for three days. I heard you blow Father's horn once, deep down, on the second night. Then nothing.

I can't go in. I've seen the things that come out at dusk, pale and blind and sniffing the air like dogs, and I'm not ashamed to say I ran.

If it's not Eyvind reading this but some stranger with a stout heart: our father's hunting horn was carved from a mammoth's tusk with a running elk on the side. Bring it back and I'll know. Either way, I'll know. Bodvar.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmermist_cave.fa: A lost apprentice of the College of Winterhold

The Falmer here mark their tunnels with scratched lines, three short and one long, repeated at every bend. I believe they are not words but distances, counted in steps, so the blind can find their way home.

I also believe I am lost. I have been following the marks the wrong way. They count toward the heart of the cave, not out of it. If I am right, I should be close to their nest. I can hear something breathing that is not me. I shall stop writing now.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmermist_cave.ho: A deep cave north-east of Whiterun, named for the glittering mist that pours from its mouth at dawn. The Falmer who dwell below have started taking hunters who stray too near.
place_lore.nirncraft.shimmermist_cave.ru: Shimmermist Cave goes down a long way, past where any Nord should go. A hunter's brother went in after a wounded elk and never came out. They say the snow elves took him.

place_lore.nirncraft.shornhelm.hook: The black-roofed capital of Rivenspire, a city of fog, feuding noble houses and long winter nights, where the old families measure their honour in centuries and their grudges in blood.
place_lore.nirncraft.shornhelm.rumour: Rivenspire nobles don't forgive and don't forget. They write it all down, bind it in leather, and read it to their grandchildren.
place_lore.nirncraft.shornhelm.sheriff_r:
#To the Council of Houses, 14th of Frostfall
My lords, the sleepwalkers. I have now eleven cases, all children of the lower town, all found at dawn on the south-east road, barefoot and asleep, walking toward the old Daedric stones beyond the river. Each wakes screaming and each tells the same dream: a tower of purple glass, and a woman inside who wants to hear their stories.

The Temple says it is a fever of the season. Fevers do not walk in step. I request leave to post men at the shrine itself, and I request it before the twelfth child. If the Council will not pay for it, I will ask any capable stranger with a sword. I have already started asking.
place_lore.nirncraft.shornhelm.widow_let:
My dear Bertrand,
Your father's blade has not come home. The men who went to the shrine of the Lord of Chains to find him brought back his horse, his gauntlets and nothing else. They say the stones there are cold even at noon, and that there were chains on the ground, and that some of them were warm.

I will not have the family sword hanging in some Daedra's hall. It was forged when Shornhelm first raised its walls and it has never been sold, lost or surrendered. You are to do nothing foolish. You are to hire someone who does foolish things professionally. Spare no cost, but do bargain. We are Tamriths, not Montclairs.
Your mother.
place_lore.nirncraft.shornhelm_outlaws_r: A cellar beneath the old armoury of Shornhelm where men who have left the garrison without leave wait for forgiveness or boat.

^STANDING ORDER, NOT TO BE POSTED
^The lower armoury cellar is to be kept dry, lit and stocked with bread and a barrel. No soldier of this garrison is to enter it in the first hour of any watch. No soldier who finds a man there is to ask his name.

^A man who has run has already paid. A man who has been asked to pay twice has nothing left to give. I will not have my garrison made poorer by the loss of a single one. Anyone who objects may take it up with me.
In the wall under Shornhelm there is a place for men who have run. The Marshal knows. She leaves it unlocked. She is, in her way, a kind woman.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone.hook: A huddle of miners' houses at the mouth of Redbelly Mine, named for a standing rock the first settlers swore was set there by Shor himself. Lately its miners have been going missing.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone.redbell:
#Shifts, week of Frostfall 12th
Morning: Grogmar, Sylgja, Hrafn.
Afternoon: Ulfr, Eyja, the Dunmer lad.
Night shift: CANCELLED. No one goes below after dusk until the Jarl sends men.

Reminder: spiders in the east gallery again. Torches, not candles. Candles go out. Torches you can swing.

Ore for Riften leaves Loredas by cart. The Greenwall toll is twelve septims a cart now. Twelve. Mention this to the steward if you ever see one.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone.rumour: Shor's Stone? Ore and spiders, friend. And now folk vanishing on the way to the Ruunvald dig. Three men since Hearthfire. Their wives are going grey waiting.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone.sk4_not: Folio #5 (2269, 842): Field inspection recorded for Shors Stone within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #5 for shors_stone: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shors Stone are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone.thrud_l:
Kolbjorn,
I'm writing this because the priest says it helps, and I don't know where else to put it. You went to Ruunvald on the ninth of Hearthfire because the foreman there paid triple wages. Triple. I told you no honest dig pays triple.

Grogmar went up after you and came back white as milk. He says the dig has no foreman now, only people in black robes, and that they were singing over something in the deep cut. He won't say what.

You still have your father's iron token on the cord round your neck. If anyone finds it, I want it back. I want something back.
Thrud
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_stone_watch_c: A timber watch-post and tent ring on the ridge above Shor's Stone, keeping watch over the northern iron road.
The watchmen at Shor's Stone Camp have their hands full between the spiders in the mine and the patrols coming down from Eastmarch.

Folio #58 (800, 1720): Field inspection recorded for Shors Stone Watch Camp within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #58 for shors_stone_watch_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shors Stone Watch Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Four ore-wagons cleared down the hill road since sunrise, and two couriers riding hard from Windhelm with sealed pouches. Keep the watch-fire stoked with dry birch so the miners at the pit-head can see the signal.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_watchtower.ho: A stone watchtower overlooking the northern road above Shor's Stone, its lookout fire long cold. Travellers report smoke from it again, and arrows.
place_lore.nirncraft.shors_watchtower.ru: Somebody's moved into Shor's Watchtower. Not the guard. The guard doesn't shoot at carts.

place_lore.nirncraft.shors_watchtower.wa:
#Who can hit what from the top
Geirlaug: ox at sixty paces, two out of three. Wins 5.
The Redguard: cart driver's hat, clean through. Wins 10.
Kjeld: missed the Shor's Stone smith twice. Pays 6.

Rule: we shoot to scare, not to kill. Dead men don't pay tolls. Rule two: when the Knives come up from Faldar's Tooth to talk, everybody keeps their bows unstrung. They think this road is theirs. Let them think it until spring.
place_lore.nirncraft.shriekwind_word_wal: A high cliffside word wall where mountain gales whistle through fluted stone channels above the pine canopy.
When the north wind hits the Shriekwind Word Wall, you can hear it Moaning all the way down in Falkreath's graveyard.

Folio #57 (-1440, 1320): Field inspection recorded for Shriekwind Word Wall within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #57 for shriekwind_word_wall: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shriekwind Word Wall are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Folio #87 (-1440, 1320): Field inspection recorded for Shriekwind Word Wall within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #87 for shriekwind_word_wall: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shriekwind Word Wall are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

The ancient builders cut narrow vents between the rune-blocks so the valley updrafts would sound a low chord before every storm. Those who keep watch in Shriekwind Bastion use the pitch of the stone to tell when a blizzard is crossing the lake.

place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_black_: Seven-Scars, once of a Dres plantation

Lady of Dusk, the Dunmer who kept me prayed to you every evening and beat me every morning. I listened to the prayers. I thought: if she is their god, she is a cruel one. Then one evening my master prayed for a good harvest, and that night the river took his fields.

I do not think you were ever theirs. I think you were waiting for them to deserve you, and they did not. So here I am, a free Saxhleel, at your stones in the marsh, and I bring you the only thing I own that I chose for myself: this evening. Take it. It is a good one. The light is very gold.
A moss-draped statue of Azura in the marsh west of Stormhold, kept by Saxhleel who were once slaves in Morrowind and learned the Lady's name from the very masters they escaped.
The old freed-slaves go to the Azura stones west of Stormhold at dusk. They learned her from the Dunmer. Funny thing, to keep your master's god. They say she was never the master's.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_cyrodi: A tall statue of Azura in the Great Forest south-west of the Imperial City, her hands raised to the twin hours of dusk and dawn. Dunmer refugees walk out here from the capital to pray for a home they can't return to.
The Dunmer from the city's poor districts walk out to the Azura statue in the forest every evening. They don't beg there. They just stand, and when the sun goes they go home quieter than they came.
Neria Dalvilo, of the Imperial City's Elven Gardens

Mother of the Rose, it is Neria again. I came out of Ald'ruhn on my father's back when the mountain spoke. I am thirty now. I sweep floors in the Elven Gardens for an Altmer who calls me 'the grey girl'. He does not know my name. You do.

I do not ask you for home. Home is ash. I ask you for one dusk where I am not tired, and one dawn where I do not wake already ashamed of being glad to be alive. You took us out of the old Temple's hands once and made us your people again. Take us out of this one. Or only stay with me until the light goes.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_elswey: Azurah, who shaped us from the old forest folk and gave us the moons to walk by, here is another. Her name is Ri'shara. She came on the night Masser was full and Secunda was thin, so she will be quick and stubborn, like her mother, like her grandmother, like you.

This one asks you to watch her when the Elves come to count us. This one asks you to keep her paws on the sand and her nose out of the skooma dens. This one asks you to let her be a Khajiit, whatever that means by the time she is grown. Look at her. Is she not perfect? Of course she is. You made her.
A gentle statue of Azurah, mother of the Khajiit, in the dunes south-west of Rimmen, where grandmothers bring newborn cubs to be shown to the moons.
Our grandmothers carry every new cub out to Azurah's statue south-west of Rimmen and hold it up to the moons. She made us, after all. It is only polite to show her what she made.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_hammer:
~Mother of the Rose, Queen of the in-between hour,
~your mountain burned and your children ran.
~We crossed the whole of Tamriel with ash in our hair,
~and in this land of sand and strangers we set your stone again.

My grandmother carried the moonstone lamp from Ebonheart on her back. It burned on this stone every night since. Last month it was taken by sand-raiders from the Alik'r who camp in the dunes south of here. They want gold for it. I have no gold. I have only you, Lady, and you have always preferred that we help ourselves.
If a stranger reads this: I am in Sentinel, in Ashtown, behind the fish market. Bring her light home.
A shrine of Azura among the dunes south of Sentinel, kept by Dunmer whose grandparents fled the Red Year. Their lamp of moonstone has burned here for seventy years, until raiders took it last month.
The Ashtown elves walk to the Azura stone every dusk and every dawn. Sand-raiders stole their moonstone lamp. Priestess Nerevi's been out there praying in the dark ever since.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_high_r: A slender stone of Azura on the hills north-west of Wayrest, where Breton widows come at the turning of the light to ask the Queen of Dusk and Dawn for one more glimpse of what they have lost.

^Written in many hands, in a calf-bound book chained to the stone
~Lady of the in-between, of the hour the lamps are lit,
~I do not ask you for him back. I know the bargain of the world.
~I ask only to see his face once at dusk, as he looked
~coming up the Fish Bridge with the catch, before the fever.

-- Margaux, 3rd of Sun's Dawn. She showed me. He was laughing.

Lady, my son sailed for Stros M'Kai and the sea took him. Let me know only whether he was afraid. -- Hélène, 19th of Rain's Hand.

She showed me a ship's lantern, burning steady. I choose to believe it means no. -- H.
Do not write here unless you mean it. The Lady reads every word and she remembers the liars. -- A widow of thirty years.
The rose-widows of Wayrest walk out to the Azura stone every evening. They say the Lady shows you a dream of your dead if you sit still long enough. I'd rather not sit that still.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_morrow:
~Mother of Dusk, we have kept your light without its heart,
~Lamp without flame, cup without wine.
~Forty winters we have turned to the south at sunset,
~And forty springs the south has not answered.

Below, more recent, in a firm hand: 'The Stone is in Black Marsh, in the hands of rot-eaters who worship the Lady of Decay, at her stones in the Shadowfen south of here. They use it to light their feasts. I am too old to go. I will find someone who is not. Ilvari, priestess, Mournhold.'

A great statue of Azura in the Deshaan east of Mournhold, beloved by Dunmer since before the Tribunal. An empty socket in its base marks where the Twilight Stone sat until the Argonians carried it off.

The Lady's statue east of Mournhold lost its stone to Argonian raiders. The socket's still there, black and empty. Priestess Ilvari in Mournhold has heard where it went. She needs someone brave enough to cross the border.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_summer: A shrine of Azura in the hills north of Alinor, where Altmer of old families still come at dusk to honour the Queen of Twilight, and Thalmor Justiciars come to write down their names.
Justiciar Aranelya, Directorate of Public Virtue

#Observation of the 7th to the 14th of Hearthfire
Visitors at dusk: eleven. Of these, six of established lineage (names attached), three of uncertain lineage, one Bosmer servant, one elderly scholar who claimed to be 'sketching the light'. The scholar's sketches have been confiscated. They are, regrettably, very good.

Assessment: the cult of the Twilight Queen among the Altmer is aesthetic rather than devotional. The visitors are moved by the hour and the colour of the sky rather than by the Prince. Recommendation: continued observation, no action. Personal note, to be removed before filing: I have been watching this shrine for two years. The light at dusk here is the loveliest I have ever seen. I do not know what to do with that.
The Azura shrine north of Alinor's the only Daedric stone the old families still visit openly. Twilight's beautiful, they say, and beauty's not illegal. Not yet.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_azura_valenw: Ma'jhira, caravan-mother of the Long Road

~Azurah, Mother of the Twilight, who taught the cats to be cats,
~this one has walked from Rimmen to Elden Root eleven times.
~She asks no more roads. She asks only that the road be kind
~to the young ones who walk it after her.

Ma'jhira's cubs do not know the old prayers. They know the price of moon-sugar in six cities and the names of every Thalmor tax-officer between here and Senchal. They are clever. They are not wise. Teach them, Mother, as you taught Ma'jhira, at the hour when the moons are rising and the sun has not yet gone. That is the only hour when a Khajiit will listen.
A shrine of Azura in the Grahtwood canopy north-west of Elden Root, built by Khajiit caravans on the long road to Elsweyr, where the Moon-Mother's light falls through the leaves at dusk.
The cat caravans stop at the Azura shrine on the Grahtwood road and sing to the Moon-Mother. The Bosmer don't mind. They say it's the only time Khajiit are quiet enough to hear a bowstring.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_bla: A spear-scarred statue of Boethiah in the marsh west of Stormhold, where Saxhleel veterans of the northern war tally what they took back from Morrowind and what it cost them.
The veterans of the northern war go to the Boethiah stones and cut marks into the statue. One mark for each chain broken. One for each friend lost. The statue's very scarred.

Boethiah, Prince of the Turned Knife, the Dunmer say you taught them to overthrow their old gods. We listened. We learned. We turned the knife they taught us, and we turned it back on them, in the Red Year, when their mountain had them on their knees.

Marks for chains broken: thirty-one. Marks for friends lost: eleven. Marks for things done in the Dunmer towns that I will not tell my hatchlings about: I will not cut those. You know them, Prince. You were there. You were smiling. I was too, and that is why I come here instead of the Hist.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_cyr: A Daedric statue of Boethiah on a windswept shelf of the Jeralls south-west of Bruma, where sell-swords from both sides of the Skyrim border settle blood-debts in a ring of trampled snow.
Gunnhild the Unfriended, Keeper of the Ring

^The Ring of Snow
One. Any blood-debt may be brought here. Kin-killing, oath-breaking, stolen pay. The Prince does not care whose side you fought on. The Prince cares who walks away.
Two. No healers in the ring. No healers after, either, unless you can walk to Bruma on your own feet.

Three. Betrayal is permitted. Betrayal is admired. If your second turns on you, that is a lesson, and Boethiah loves a lesson.
Four. The winner takes the loser's boots. In the Jeralls that is not a joke.
Five. Keep the Legion out of it. Last summer's sergeant still owes the Prince a rematch.
There's a fighting ring at the Boethiah stones above Bruma. Nords, Imperials, Redguards, all bleeding for the Prince. The Countess calls it murder. The fighters call it 'clearing accounts'.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_els: A warrior-statue of Boethra, the Clever Warrior, in the hills of Pellitine south of Riverhold, held by a duellist named Hazadir who has killed nine challengers in the Prince's name.
Hazadir the Unbowed holds Boethra's stones in Pellitine. Nine have challenged him and nine have died, all after tea. You'd think one of them would have refused the tea.
Master Ahzirr of the Silk-Blade School

To whoever stands at Boethra's stones, from Master Ahzirr:
Hazadir was my student. He was the finest and the worst. He has killed nine challengers here, my students among them, and each one drank his tea first. I have tasted the dregs. Cobweb root. A little numbness in the paw, nothing a fighter would notice until the third pass.

The Clever Warrior admires a trick. So do I. But a trick is a feint, not a poison in a cup. Challenge him. Refuse the tea. Kill him, if you can, and bring me his notched ring at Riverhold, where I teach now by the Mane's gate, so that I can take the nine notches off it one by one and say each name. Boethra will not mind. Boethra respects the one who sees the trick coming.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_ham: A shrine of Boethiah high in the Bangkorai pass between Wayrest and Elinhir, where sellsword companies swear blood-oaths before a war and settle their mutinies after one.

^We who sign here, Redguard, Breton, Orc and one very angry Nord, swear before the Prince of the Knife:
To hold the pass for whoever pays, until they stop paying. To take what is owed from employers who forget. To follow the captain while the captain wins, and to replace the captain the moment the captain loses.

Signed by forty marks, crosses and one drawing of a goat.
Added later, in red: Captain Hessa lost at Fallen Grotto. Replaced. Captain Brannoc lost his nerve. Replaced. Captain Oriel Sand-Tongue holds the roll. She sleeps with her back to the wall and her eyes half open, which is the only way the Prince approves of.
The Red Pass Company took its oaths at the Boethiah stone in Bangkorai. Forty swords went in. Thirty-one came out. The other nine are buried under the shrine, and they were the officers.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_hig: A dark shrine of Boethiah on the Glenumbra heath north of Daggerfall. Ambitious young lords ride out to it before dawn, and the duels fought there end with a funeral and a promotion.
They say if you want your elder brother's title in Daggerfall, you go pray at the Boethiah stone. Then you wait for him to insult the wrong swordsman. It never takes long.

^Compact of the Unbound, sworn before the Prince of Plots
I, who am second-born, swear that I will no longer be second. I will take what the accident of birth denied me, and I will take it by the old Breton right, steel in the morning mist, so that no court can name it murder. The Unbound will supply the champion. I will supply the insult.

In payment I give to the Prince the blood of my brother and the faith of all who trusted him. The champion of the Unbound, Sir Brayan Ferrec, keeps his vigil at this stone each night until the matter is concluded.
The next name on our list is that of Lady Gaudrel's brother-in-law. Then the Lady herself, if she keeps asking questions.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_mor: unsigned, sealed with a Hlaalu ring
Prince of Plots, who taught Veloth's people to leave the old gods and follow the new, I ask nothing so grand. I ask for Councillor Dravos's majority on the canal tariff.

I have bought three votes. He has bought four. I know which of his four are for sale twice. You taught us that loyalty is a garment, not a skin. Give me the patience to wait for him to take it off.
I leave you a dagger that has never been used, because you like potential. I will come back with it when it has been.
A statue of Boethiah on the Ascadian Isles between Balmora and Vivec, the Prince who freed the Chimer, where Hlaalu councillors come by night to pray before they ruin one another.
The Hlaalu say they pray at the Boethiah stones for wisdom. What they mean is for a good knife. Watch whose palanquin goes out on the night before a council vote.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_sum: A shrine of Boethiah on Auridon south-west of Firsthold, where young Thalmor officers are rumoured to make secret offerings for advancement, and senior officers are rumoured to have made them first.

#Rain's Hand, 4E 201
The Station Chief has held his post for forty years. He will hold it forty more unless something changes. I have served loyally. I have filed every report. Loyalty is apparently a ladder with no rungs. Tonight I went to the old shrine on the hill and asked the Prince of Plots for a rung.

#Second Seed
The Station Chief's deputy has been recalled to Alinor, under a cloud. I did not cause it. I merely noticed something and mentioned it to someone. The deputy's post is vacant. I have been asked to fill it, temporarily.
#Midyear
The Station Chief has begun to look at me oddly. I have begun to look at him the same way. It is very instructive, this shrine.
The ambitious ones in the Thalmor pray at the Boethiah stone on Auridon. Not officially, of course. Officially there's no ambition in the Thalmor. Only loyalty, and sudden vacancies.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_boethiah_val: A shrine of Boethiah deep in Malabal Tor, where Bosmer outlaws who have broken the Green Pact swear themselves to the Prince of Plots, since no tree in Valenwood will shelter them now.

I, Vanthir, cut the living wood. I did it in the open, at noon, before the Silvenar's own messenger, and I did it because the Pact is a leash. The Spinners say Y'ffre made us. Y'ffre made us small and hungry and forbade us to build. Boethiah made nobody, and forbids nothing.

The Prince of Plots asks only that we be strong enough to take what we want and clever enough to keep it. So we have taken this log, and this clearing, and this shrine. Next we will take Falinesti's toll-road. The wardens will come. The wardens always come. And one of them will join us, because one of them always does.
The Kin-Breakers of Malabal Tor took an axe to a living tree and the Green Pact cast them out. Now they pray to Boethiah. Funny thing about outcasts: they always find a god who wants them.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_clavicus_vil: Governor Aulus Teretius, Imperial Province of Black Marsh

#Second year of my governorship
Azura would not answer. Boethiah laughed. Hermaeus Mora asked a price I will not write down. The little Prince of Bargains, at least, is a gentleman. He asked only what I wanted.

I said: 'I do not want to die in this swamp.' He smiled with his dog's teeth and his own, and the deal was struck.
#Fourth year
I am leaving Black Marsh tomorrow. I am going home to Cheydinhal at last. I have ordered a hot bath for the evening of my arrival. Ten years of mud, and at last, clean water. I can hardly wait.
A crumbling statue of Clavicus Vile in the marsh north-west of Stormhold, raised by an Imperial governor who bargained with every Prince in turn to survive the swamp and lost to all of them.
That Clavicus statue west of Stormhold was built by an Imperial governor who wished he'd never die in Black Marsh. He didn't. They found him in Cyrodiil, ten days after he left, drowned in a bathtub.
unknown hand

^Terms of Exchange, Shrine of the Prince of Bargains
The Petitioner asks. The Prince grants. The Prince is not responsible for the Petitioner's grammar, the Petitioner's intent, the Petitioner's family, or the Petitioner's continued breath.

Under the terms, scratched deeper: 'I asked for a horse that would never leave me. It won't. It stands at the foot of my bed every night, and it is not alive, and I cannot sell the farm. Do not ask for anything with the word never in it.' Under that, in charcoal: 'Or always.' Under that: 'Or settled.'
A smiling statue of Clavicus Vile in the Colovian hills south of Chorrol, where desperate folk come to make wishes and leave with exactly what they asked for.
Never say 'settled' out at the Clavicus stones. That's what Ostorius Varro said, and now all Chorrol knows what the Prince does with a careless word.
A statue of Clavicus Vile in the dunes just north of Torval, where Khajiit merchants come to make the most carefully worded wishes in all of Tamriel.
Bazrag-dar, caravan-master

Draft the seventh: This one, Bazrag-dar, of the clan of the Long Road, wishes that his caravans will reach their destinations safely (meaning with all wagons, all goods, all kin and all animals alive, whole and in their right minds), in a reasonable time (meaning not more than ten days late), without loss (meaning neither by theft, nor by fire, nor by tax, nor by Thalmor).

Note from the Prince, written in the sand after: 'Granted. And for wasting my evening with a contract, I have made you honest. Enjoy your wagons.'
Note from Bazrag-dar, a month later: 'This one cannot lie about the price of anything. This one is ruined. Never wish carefully. He hates it.'
Khajiit merchants wish at the Clavicus stones north of Torval. They bring a lawyer. Several, sometimes. The Prince, they say, enjoys it very much. Nobody else does.
A grinning shrine of Clavicus Vile in the scrubland east of Skaven, where a desperate man once traded for a well that never runs dry. His son still sells the water, and still owes the debt.
The Qamar well in Skaven was bought at the Clavicus stone. Old Qamar paid with 'something of no value'. Young Qamar thinks that something was his own soul. He'd like it back.

^Agreed upon this 1st of Midyear, 4E 161, between Qamar son of Hafiz, well-digger of Skaven, and a Prince of Bargains, by proxy of his faithful hound.
The Prince grants: a well in the East Quarter of Skaven that shall never run dry so long as the house of Qamar holds it.

Qamar grants: the thing that is of no value to him, to be collected at the Prince's convenience, from him or his heirs.
The original lies sealed in the shrine, under the dog's paw. The house of Qamar keeps no copy, for the house of Qamar was not given one. Note, in the margin, in a newer hand: 'Father, what did you think you were worth?'
A smiling shrine of Clavicus Vile in the fields east of Camlorn. Camlorn merchants deny ever visiting it, and yet the path to it is worn as smooth as a guildhall stair.
Gilbert Verrine

To whatever reads letters left at this stone,
I asked for prosperity and you gave it. Every venture has turned to gold. The salt sells before it lands. The wine sells before it is pressed. My rivals go bankrupt in their sleep. I have bought the house on the hill with the blue shutters that my father could only look at.

My daughter Lisette does not sing any more. She does not laugh. She does her lessons and eats her supper and looks at me as if I were a stranger who has paid for her board. Your dog said I would lose one thing I did not value. I did not know I did not value it until it was gone.
Take the house back. Take the gold. I am told that is not how this works. I am leaving this letter anyway.
Half the rich men of Camlorn got rich in a single season. Ask how, and they say 'shrewd investment'. Ask where they invested, and they look east and go quiet.
A statue of Clavicus Vile in the West Gash hills between Balmora and Ald'ruhn, where miners of the Caldera ebony diggings come to wish for one more good vein.
Bjorn Hollow-Eye, ebony miner

To the foreman, and to whoever goes to the stones next:
The vein doesn't stop. That's the trouble. Every time I think I'll stop, there's another seam just there, black and fat, and my hands go to it before I can think. The Prince said 'never run dry'. He didn't say the vein. He meant me.

Send bread, and send a priest who isn't afraid of Daedra, and if neither will come, send the next fool who wants to wish for something. I'll tell him what I learned. Never wish for a thing to go on. Wish for it to end well. The Prince can't do much with 'well'. He hates the word.
A Nord miner from Caldera wished at the Clavicus stones for a vein that would never run dry. It hasn't. He hasn't come up in four months. They send down bread on a rope.
A shrine of Clavicus Vile in the hills south of Alinor, where an Altmer lord of falling fortunes once traded for an heir of perfect blood. He got one. He has never been able to look at her.
Lord Ondeneth of the House of the Seven Spires

To the Prince of Bargains,
My house was failing. Our lineage was questioned; a Bosmer great-grandmother, they said, of whom no record should have survived. My wife was barren. I came to this shrine and asked for an heir whose blood the Directorate could not fault. You gave me Laerwen.

She is perfect. Her lineage is perfect. Her ears, her eyes, her manners, her magic, all perfect. She does not cry. She has never cried, not even as an infant. My wife died the night she was born and Laerwen did not look up. Your dog told me that what I paid with was 'the family resemblance.' I understand now. She is not like us. She is like what we pretend to be.
Lord Ondeneth asked the Clavicus stone for a child with perfect lineage. The Directorate's genealogists couldn't fault her. That's what bothers him. Nobody's that perfect. Not even the Thalmor.
Faelin of Greenshade

To the Prince of Wishes and his excellent hound,
I wished never to go hungry. I meant: never to want for meat. I meant: never to have to hunt it in the rain. You know what I meant. Your dog laughed when I said it, and I should have known then.

Now I do not go hungry. I do not feel hunger at all. Nor taste, nor satisfaction, nor the warmth of a full belly by a fire. My wife's roast is ashes in my mouth. The Meat Mandate is a mockery to me; I keep it out of duty, like a priest who has lost his faith. I wish to unwish it. Your dog says unwishing costs more. What could cost more than this?
A shrine of Clavicus Vile in Greenshade east of Woodhearth, where a famously idle Bosmer once wished never to be hungry again, and has been regretting the precise wording ever since.
Old Faelin out by the Clavicus shrine asked the Prince never to go hungry. Now he's never hungry. Never full, either. Never anything. Eats out of habit. Says meat tastes of rain.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hermaeus_mor: A tentacled monument to Hermaeus Mora in the marsh south-west of Stormhold, through which an ancient Hist root has grown, so that the sap that weeps from the stone is full of whispering.
Adrienne Lirrian, Associate of the Mages Guild

#Day nineteen at the root
The Hist and the Prince of Knowledge are not at war here. They are bargaining. The root offers memories, the memories of every Saxhleel who ever drank its sap. The stone offers to keep them forever. I have been reading the bargain as it is written, in the sap, one drop at a time.

#Day twenty
Kassus has stopped eating. He sits at the root with his mouth open and catches the drops and recites. I wrote down what he said. It was my mother's name, and the day she died, and the words she said, which I never told anyone.
#Day twenty-one
I am going to taste the sap. If I do not come back, my journal is under the root. Take it to Gideon. Do not read it on the way.

There's a Hist root growing through the Mora stones west of Stormhold. The sap that drips off it whispers. A Breton scholar went to listen. Now her assistant's out there, reading pages that aren't there.
A writhing Daedric monument to Hermaeus Mora in the hills north of Cheydinhal, littered with mildewed books that scholars of the Arcane University swear they never brought here.
There's a scholar from the University living at the Hermaeus Mora stones north of Cheydinhal. He sends the town letters asking for ink. Lots of ink. More ink than one man could ever use.
Magister Quintus Avidius, Arcane University (on leave)

To the stationer of Cheydinhal:
Kindly forward a further twelve pots of oak-gall ink and the same of lampblack. My previous order has been consumed. I do not mean used. I mean consumed. The books here are hungry, and I have a theory, which I set out in a footnote that is, I regret to say, now four hundred pages long.

Footnote, the only one I will trouble you with: the Arch-Mage forbids the study of the Prince of Knowledge on pain of expulsion. The Arch-Mage has never stood here at midnight and heard every book open at once. If he had, he would understand why one does not leave. Do not send a guard. Send ink.
A writhing statue of Herma-Mora, the Woodland Man, in the hills north of Senchal, which the Moon-Priests warn the young to avoid, for he once tried to make the Khajiit his own.
Moon-Priest Talizar of Senchal
Cub, if you have walked this far to the Woodland Man's stones, you are curious. Curiosity is a fine thing in a Khajiit. It is how we find the best fish. But listen to this one now.

Herma-Mora once whispered to the Khajiit that they need not be Azurah's children; that they could be his, and know everything, and stop being cats. Some listened. Alkosh and the Riddle'Thar brought them home, but they came back with something missing behind the eyes.
Turn round. Go home. Ask your grandmother the question you came here to ask. She will not know the answer. She will give you a fish. That is better.

The Moon-Priests tell cubs about the Woodland Man in the hills north of Senchal. He tried to steal the Khajiit away from Azurah once, long ago. They say he is still waiting for someone curious enough.
A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the hills north-west of Rihad, where Redguard scholars come in search of the lost maps of drowned Yokuda and come back fluent in tongues no one has spoken in an age.
A Rihad scholar went to the Mora shrine asking where old Yokuda sank. Came back reciting the names of every ship of the Crossing. He can't stop. His wife's moved to her sister's.
Tariq al-Hazir of Rihad

#Sun's Height, the 2nd
Every Redguard child is told the land of our ancestors sank into the sea. No Redguard scholar has ever been told where. Our maps begin with the Crossing and end with the shore. I am tired of beginning at the shore.

#Sun's Height, the 5th
The Lord of Knowledge answered. He showed me Yokuda under the waves, its towers drowned in green light. He showed me the Hiradirge, the old sword-singers' halls. He showed me where the Ra Gada first set out. He showed me the way back.

#Sun's Height, the 6th
He asked for my name in exchange. Not the word. The thing. I did not understand. I said yes. My wife called me this morning by my name and I did not turn my head.
Archivist Dorien Haldane

#Second Seed, the 9th
The Montclair archives are silent on the death of Lord Bastien. I have read every ledger, every letter, every laundry list. Someone has cut the pages I need with a very sharp knife. There is one library in Rivenspire that no one can cut. I am going to the stones south of the city tomorrow.

#Second Seed, the 10th
I asked. The eyes in the stone opened. I was shown the name of the poisoner, and the name of the man who paid him, and the name of the man who paid him, and so on back, house by house, three hundred years. Every noble line in Rivenspire is in it. Every one.

#Second Seed, the 30th
I have not slept. I cannot stop knowing. It is very quiet in my head now, except for the pages turning. I think the pages are turning me.
A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the misty hills south of Shornhelm, ringed by stones carved with eyes. Rivenspire scholars who come to it seeking one answer tend to leave with too many.
The old archivist of Shornhelm went to the Mora stone to learn who poisoned his patron. He learned. Then he learned everything else, and now he doesn't sleep.

A tentacled monument to Hermaeus Mora in the Ashlands west of Ald'ruhn, where Telvanni wizards come to trade secrets they'll regret and Ashlanders leave their dreams so the Prince won't come for them.
Arvil Sethan, Mouth of Tel Naga

#Bargain the first
Offered: the name of my master's apprentice who poisons him slowly. Received: the third word of the binding my master uses on his doors. A fair trade. The apprentice would have been caught regardless.

#Bargain the second
Offered: my mother's face. I did not think I would miss it. Received: the location of a Dwemer vault under the Ashlands. I cannot picture her now. I picture the vault.
#Bargain the third
Offered: the way home. Received: everything. I am going to sit here a little longer and read. The ink is moving. It is beautiful. Tell Tel Naga I have resigned.
A Telvanni mouth walked out to the Mora stones west of Ald'ruhn and hasn't walked back. The Ashlanders say the Prince of Secrets keeps what he's given. The Redoran say good.
A shrine of Hermaeus Mora on Auridon north-west of Firsthold, where a circle of Sapiarch students reads from a folio that the Crystal Tower struck from its catalogue three hundred years ago.
The young Sapiarchs sneak off to the Mora shrine on Auridon to read some forbidden folio. Two of them came back speaking backwards. The Tower says it is the strain of their examinations.
Eradil, candidate of the Crystal Tower

The Unnumbered Folio was removed from the Tower's catalogue in the Third Era by order of the Sapiarchs, who called it 'an inquiry the Altmer are not yet ready to complete'. We found it here, in the shrine, in a box of black wood that opens only when you are not looking at it. Every night we read one page. Every night the page is different.

Last night's page explained, quite clearly, how the Aldmeri lineage might be traced back beyond the Dawn Era, to whatever the Aldmer were before they were Aldmer. Caelinor laughed and laughed and then could not stop. The keeper of the folio, a robed thing with too many eyes in its hood, says the answer is on the next page. We are all going back tonight.
A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the Reaper's March south of Arenthia, where a Spinner once traded her own memories for every story that was ever told in the forest, and lost her name in the bargain.
There's a Spinner sits by the Mora shrine south of Arenthia, telling stories nobody else knows. Ask her name and she'll tell you a tale about it. It's never the same name twice.

~I went to the many-eyed one and said: I am a Spinner.
~I carry the tales of my people as the river carries rain.
~But tales are lost when Spinners die, and I am growing old.
~Give me every story, so that none is ever lost.

~He said: there is no room in you for every story
~unless you give me yours.
~So I gave him my mother's face, my wedding, my first kill.
~Now I know the tale of every Bosmer who ever lived,
~and when I come to my own, the page is blank.
^(Carved beneath:) Do not ask her who she is. She will tell you, and she will be wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_blac: A beast-headed statue of Hircine in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where a deserter from the Legion, cursed with the Huntsman's blood, has begun hunting Saxhleel hunters for sport.

Written by the Lukiul scribe, as spoken: The Huntsman's stones are an old place. Saxhleel hunters have left a feather there after a good hunt for longer than the Empire has been an Empire. It is a fair thing, a feather. The Huntsman likes fair things.

Now there is something at the stones that is not fair. A man who becomes a wolf, a man who was a soldier of the Empire, who ran from his legion and ran into the Huntsman's blood. He does not eat what he kills. He sets their spears in the mud by the statue, points up, and waits for the next. Five spears now. One of them was my brother's. Hunt the hunter. The Huntsman, I think, would like that.
There's a wolf in the Shadowfen that walks on two legs and wears the scraps of a Legion tunic. He hunts our hunters. He leaves their spears stuck in the ground at the Hircine stones, like trophies.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_cyro: A great antlered statue of Hircine in the woods of the West Weald, where Skingrad's hunters leave the first heart of every season, and where something leaves heads in return.

#Offerings to the Huntsman, by season
First Seed: heart of a red stag. Accepted, the heart gone by dawn.
Mid Year: heart of a boar. Accepted.
Hearthfire: heart of a bear, the big sow from the ridge above Skingrad. Accepted, and the ridge silent for a month.

Evening Star: heart of nothing. The lodge voted to stop. Too old for superstition, they said.
Sun's Dawn: Marius Aelian, my brother, dead in his bed with the door barred. Paw-prints on the sill, too big for any wolf of the Weald.
I have made the offering since, alone. The lodge does not know. The Huntsman does.
The Skingrad hunting lodge leaves a stag's heart at the Hircine stones every spring. Last spring they forgot. That's the spring old Marius got his throat opened in his own bed.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_elsw: A beast-headed statue of Hircine in the scrubland west of Rimmen, where the hunters of the city ask the Huntsman for a fair chase against the great senche-tigers of the plains.
Rimmen's hunters ask the Huntsman for a fair chase against the senche-tigers. A fair chase against a senche is when you run and it doesn't catch you. This one doesn't hunt.

#First day
Asked the Huntsman for a great senche. Left him a jerky. This one thinks the Huntsman does not like jerky. This one thinks perhaps a better offering would have been wise.

#Second day
Found the great senche. It found this one first. We looked at each other for a long time. Then it lay down and yawned and let a cub out from behind it, a little one, very fierce, who tried to eat this one's boot.
#Third day
The cub has followed this one home. This one will raise it. The Huntsman has a sense of humour. Next time this one will bring a better offering. Next time this one will also bring more boots.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_hamm: A shrine of Hircine in the dry hills north of Taneth, piled with the skulls of lions and jackals left by the hunters of Hew's Bane. Lately the skulls have been joined by bones that nobody left.

~Father of the Hunt, Lord of the Dry Grass,
~here is the lion of the Hew's Bane hills.
~I took him with a spear, as the old way asks.
~I did not take him from behind.

Cut beneath, by another hand, deeper and fresher: 'Father of the Hunt, the great cat from Elsweyr has come to your stones and the city men want her dead with poison and nets. That is no hunt. Give her to a hunter worthy of her, or let her go free. -- Malik of the Hills, who has seen her drink at the dry well at dawn.'
Hew's Bane hunters say the Huntsman's sent them a beast: the escaped tiger from Yusuf's cages. They're laying bets on who'll take her skin. Yusuf's betting on the tiger.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_high: A shrine of Hircine in the Stormhaven woods south-west of Evermor, hung with antlers and old hunting horns. The king's huntsmen avoid it; something that wears a man's face does not.
Hugo Morel, steward of the Old Lodge

^Kills of the Old Lodge, offered at the Stone of the Huntsman
Sun's Dawn: one stag, twelve tines, taken by Lord Remy on foot. Rain's Hand: a boar, a brace of hares, a Reachman poacher (accidental; regretted; reported). Midyear: one bear, taken by Lord Remy with a knife, after which his lordship was abed nine days.

Sun's Height: his lordship hunted alone, by night, and brought back nothing that he would name. Hearthfire: his lordship asks that we no longer bolt the kennel. The hounds have begun to howl when he comes near. I have written to Huntmaster Lorne at Evermor. I do not know what else a steward is to do.
Huntmaster Lorne's lost three hounds and a beater by the Hircine stone. He says it's a bear. He's an honest man, Gaspard. That's why he can't lie well.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_morr: A beast-headed statue of Hircine on Azura's Coast west of Sadrith Mora, where Telvanni hunters and Ashlander trackers meet at the Huntsman's altar and argue over who has the right to the season's great prey.

To all who hunt on Azura's Coast: the Huntsman has marked his prey for this season. A bull kagouti, called Ashtusk by the Zainab trackers, with one tusk snapped into a crown. He grazes in the scrub north of this altar and he has killed four hunters and a guar-herd since Rain's Hand.

The rules of the Huntsman's season are old and simple. Hunt him with your own hand. Take the crowned tusk, not the head. Lay nothing at this altar but the hunt itself. The Ashlanders say whoever brings down Ashtusk will run with the Huntsman's favour until the next Bloodmoon. I say whoever does it will also be paid, by me, if I am still alive to pay.

There's a kagouti on the coast as big as a silt strider calf, with a tusk broken like a crown. The hunters call it Ashtusk. Hircine's chosen, they say. Nobody who's hunted it has come back with the tusk.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_summ: Warden Sorondil, of the Alinor Preserves

To the Directorate,
As instructed, the annual Lords' Hunt has been suspended. I record the reason plainly, since no one else will. During the hunt of 4E 199, the young lord Faralan of the House of the Seven Spires separated from the party near the old shrine of the Huntsman. He was found at dawn, bitten, and laughing.

He was confined to the family's estate. He is no longer confined anywhere. The deer in the south-west preserve have become very few, and the shepherds of the hill farms very nervous. I request permission to hunt the creature. I am told that it is a member of a noble house and may not be hunted. I am told to call it a fox.
A shrine of Hircine in the wild south-west of the Summerset Isle, where Altmer lords once hunted for sport, and where something from the last hunt has never stopped hunting them back.
The Altmer lords stopped holding hunts at the Hircine shrine after the Faralan boy came back on four legs. They say he's still out there in the scrub. The lords say it's a fox. A very large fox.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_hircine_vale:
~Father of Hunts, we are your hounds.
~We take the deer, and leave the tree.
~We take the boar, and leave the root.
~We take the foe who shoots at us, and leave nothing.

Scratched below in a shaking hand: 'Father, the elders are angry about the felled oak east of the city, and there is talk among them of the old rite, the one that makes the hounds into beasts with no master. Do not answer them. Please. My brother is one of the hunters they would use. I have left you a stag. I will leave you anything else you ask, if you will only stay your hand.'
An antlered shrine of Hircine in Grahtwood north-west of Elden Root, where Bosmer hunters lay the year's first kill and swear the old oath that keeps the hounds of the Pact from becoming the hunted.
Every Bosmer hunter in Grahtwood lays the first kill of the year at the Hircine shrine. The ones who skip it have unlucky seasons. The ones who mock it have short ones.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_bla: A statue of Malacath in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where the Naga, the marsh's outcast raider-clans whom other Saxhleel will not shelter, swear war-oaths to the Prince of the Spurned.
the Naga of the Long Teeth

^To the Prince Who Was Thrown Out
The Hist would not keep us. The villages would not keep us. The King would not keep us. We keep ourselves.

We swear on our teeth, which are long, and our hunger, which is longer: we will take from the Dunmer what they took from us, and we will take from the villages what they refused us, and we will take from the King nothing at all, because he has nothing we want.
We are the Naga. We are what is left when everyone else has been kind. Prince of the Spurned, we are your favourite. Say it.
The Naga swear their oaths at the Malacath stones south of Mournhold. Even other Saxhleel don't go there. The Naga don't care who's spurned them. They're spurned by everybody, and proud of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_cyr:
^Remembered before the Furious One
Foreman Tullus of the Cathedral works: kept back four days' pay at Frostfall. Paid, after the scaffold fell beside him. Name struck through.
The merchant Albus of Anvil: sold us rotten timber for the Count's gate. Not yet paid.

The priest who blessed the Imperial crew's stones and not ours: not yet paid.
The Gate itself, that burned the city we are building: paid. Two hundred years ago. By a man who walked into fire. Malacath remembers him too.
We build Kvatch with our hands. We will be remembered in it, or the walls will learn our names some other way.
A brooding statue of Malacath in the hills east of Kvatch, where the Orc masons rebuilding the city carve their grievances into the stone, one name at a time.

The Orcs building Kvatch's walls walk out to the Malacath stones on rest-days. My brother says they carve the names of foremen who cheat them. My brother says a lot of things, but he hasn't cheated an Orc since.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_els: A statue of Malooc, the Orcs' god and old enemy of the Khajiit, in the hills south of Riverhold, kept by Orc caravan guards whom the Khajiit hire, distrust, and quietly need.
Gashna gra-Shug and the Iron Road guards

Malacath, Malooc, whatever the cats call you, it is your name. Your sons and daughters guard Khajiit wagons on the sand roads. The cats pay us. They don't thank us. They tell their cubs stories about you with us standing right there.

We swear: we will guard the wagons. We will take the arrows. We will not take the moon sugar, even though it is right there, and it smells good. When the Renrijra Krin come laughing, we will stand. When the cats tell their stories, we will laugh louder. One day a cat will thank us. On that day we will carve the name here, so you can see it too.
The Orc caravan guards keep the Malooc stones south of Riverhold. Malooc is the Khajiit's old enemy. The Orcs know. They pray there anyway, loudly, just so we hear.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_ham: A shrine of Malacath in the rocky waste east of Sentinel, kept by Orc swords-for-hire whom Hammerfell paid to fight its wars and then forgot to thank.
Ghorza gra-Bagol, captain of the Iron Wells band

~Malacath, we held the wells of the Alik'r for the Crowns.
~We bled for them at the Dominion line.
~They promised land when the elves were gone.
~The elves are gone. The land is not ours.

We do not ask you to curse the Crowns. Curses are for the weak. We ask you to remember, as we remember. Every Orc of the Iron Wells band who dies in Hammerfell's service is named here, cut in the stone, so that when the Crowns forget, the stone will not.
There are eighty-one names. There is room for more. We have checked.
The Orcs east of Sentinel fought for the Crowns against the Dominion. Then the war ended and the Crowns stopped answering their letters. They've stopped writing letters. Now they pray.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_hig: A brutal shrine of Malacath in the crags south-west of Orsinium, where Orc smiths lay the first blade of every new ore and Orc warriors come to be reminded of the Code, whether they like it or not.
Orsinium's smiths walk out to the Malacath shrine with a new blade and walk home without it. Ogres in that valley, mind. The smiths say the ogres are part of the test.

~Furious One, Lord of the Spurned,
~this is the first edge of the new seam.
~I did not make it beautiful. I made it true.
~Take it, and keep the next one sharp in my hand.

Scratched along the fuller in a smaller hand: 'Mother said you hear us best when we are angry. I am angry that the Bretons still call us beasts. I am angry that the ore runs thin. I am angry that my son wants to be a poet. Hear me, then. And if you could make the boy rhyme a little better, I would not complain.'
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_mor: A statue of Malacath in the Deshaan hills east of Ebonheart, one of the four corners of the Dunmer House of Troubles, where Orcish dockhands and exiled Dunmer outcasts swear oaths of vengeance side by side.
Erur Dralor, once of House Dres

I was Dres. My House cast me out for refusing to sell an Argonian child I had raised as my own. My House says Malacath is a curse, a Corner of the House of Troubles. My House should know. It made me his.

Prince of the Spurned, I swear: I will not beg my House to take me back. I will build a new one, of the cast-out and the cursed, and it will outlast theirs. I swear it on the iron of my father's ring, which I melted, and on the name of the child, whom they sold anyway.
Below, in Orcish: 'We heard you, grey brother. Come drink with us at the docks.'

The Temple calls Malacath a Corner of the House of Troubles and sends Ordinators to watch his stones. The Orcs from the Ebonheart docks go anyway. So do a lot of Dunmer who've been thrown out of their Houses.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_sum: Grashak gro-Durz, foreman of the Third Quay

~Malacath, you who were Trinimac,
~the high elves made you a god and then made you a monster,
~and they think that settles it.
~They do not know that we remember.

Lord of the Spurned, the Altmer of Firsthold pay us half what they pay their own and call it generosity. They let us carry their crates but not walk their streets after dark. Give us patience, so that we do not drop their crates on their feet. Give us strength, so that we do not need to. And give the overseer Varanil a long and itching rash. You know where.
A shrine of Malacath on Auridon south of Firsthold, kept by Orc dockhands who work the Firsthold quays and who remind every Altmer who sneers at it that the Orcs were once Altmer too.
The Orc dockers of Firsthold pray at the Malacath stone south of town. Altmer priests call it Trinimac's grave. The Orcs say if it's a grave, it's a grave with a very long memory.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_malacath_val: A shrine of Malacath in the Grahtwood forest, kept by a clan of Wood Orcs who have lived in Valenwood for centuries, keep a version of the Green Pact all their own, and are tired of being called guests.
The Wood Orcs of Grahtwood keep a Malacath shrine in the deep forest. They don't cut trees, they don't build stone, they just glare. Bosmer leave them be. Orc arrows fly as far as anyone's.
Murzga gro-Dulk, chief of the Root-Tusk clan

Malacath, we came into this forest when the Bretons burned Orsinium the first time. The Bosmer said: you may stay, if you keep our Pact. So we kept it. We cut no tree. We ate only meat. We raised no forge, because a forge needs wood, and we made our blades of bone and stone like our grandfathers' grandfathers.

Five hundred years we have kept their Pact. And still they call us guests. Still the Thalmor tax-men count us twice, once as Orcs and once as trouble. Hear us, Furious One. We do not want their trees. We want our name on the land we have bled for. We want to be from here.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mehrunes_dag: A jagged statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the Shadowfen just south of the Morrowind border, where Dunmer prisoners of the northern war were once held, and where their scratched messages still cover the stone.
Dunmer prisoners of 4E 6
Day 9. Penned here at the Destroyer's stones like guar. The lizards think it fitting. Perhaps it is. My House prayed to the Three. The Three are gone. Who is left but the one who burns?

Day 31. Varel prayed to the statue tonight. Begged for fire to take the lizards. Fire came: a fever. It took Varel.
Day 40. They are letting us go. A trade, for their own taken north. I will walk home to Necrom past the stones. I will not look at the statue. I will not thank it. But I will remember it was the only god who answered, and that it answered the way it always does.
The Dagon stones near the Necrom border were a pen for Dunmer prisoners in the war. The scratches are still on the stone. Saxhleel don't read Dunmeri, mostly. That's probably for the best.
Ruinous Cassia

#The Third Teaching of the Unmaking
You were told the Gates failed. They did not fail. They were interrupted. A Septim broke himself to close them, and there are no more Septims. Think on that, brothers. Think on what holds the door now. A Mede. A treaty. A tower with no fire in it.

The world is a house built on a lie, and every lie is kindling. We do not need to open a Gate. We need only wait at the door with a lamp. The Prince of Change is patient as a coal. Be patient with him.
Bring oil to the next gathering. Bring a name you would like to see burn. The Prince keeps a list.
a Bravil eel-fisher

Fishers of the west bank! Do not set nets past this post. The red hoods took my brother's boat and his net and they gave him a pamphlet. He read it. He does not fish now. He sits by the fire at the Dagon stones and smiles at it.
If you go to fetch him, take a priest and two friends. Do not take a pamphlet.
A jagged statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the swampy hills west of Bravil, where red-hooded remnants of the old Mythic Dawn have gathered to preach the world's ending once again.
Red hoods at the Dagon stones west of Bravil. The Imperial Cult's sending someone, they say. I hope it's someone big. I hope it's someone who doesn't mind fire.
Moon-Priest Ahnissi

On the third moonless night of Frostfall, the eyes of Merrunz took fire again. Three priests went with the songs of binding and the water of the Torval wells. The flames sang back. They sang the Riddle'Thar backwards, which this one has never heard before and wishes not to hear again.

We bound them by dawn. Priest Jo'zarra's whiskers burned off and will not grow back. She says she does not mind; she says she is lighter now. This one asks the Bishop to send five priests next time, not three. Merrunz is learning the songs. A demon who learns is a demon who waits.

A jagged statue of Merrunz, the cat-demon who is Mehrunes Dagon to the Khajiit, in the dunes north-east of Torval, where Moon-Priests come to bind the fires that leap from its eyes on moonless nights.
