The Merrunz stones north-east of Torval spit fire from their eyes when there's no moon. The Moon-Priests go out with water and songs. So far the songs have worked. So far.
A spiked shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the Craglorn hills north of Elinhir, where the springs have begun to boil and caravans to vanish. The Ansei of the Crowns came back from it silent.
The springs below the Dagon shrine north of Elinhir run red and hot now. My cousin swears he saw a gate of fire open in the rocks for a heartbeat. He's a liar, my cousin. He's also gone very pale.
Jamila, sword-singer of the Crowns

#To the Lord Warden of Elinhir, Frostfall
The shrine of the Destroyer is in use. Fresh ash on the altar, fresh blood on the spikes. Seven cultists in red, Breton and Redguard both, singing in a tongue that made my teeth ache. When they sang, the spring below the shrine boiled.

I did not engage. The Shehai would not come to my hand there. That has never happened to me. The spirit-sword simply would not form, as if something in the stones drank it. I recommend fire-wards, priests of Stendarr, and twenty swords of plain steel. Mine will not do this time.
Watchman Alard

Left here by Watchman Alard, 21st of Sun's Height. Followed four torches up from the north road like a fool. Counted eleven of them at the stone in red hoods. Heard them talk of the Merchants' Feast. Heard one say the name 'Corvane', which is a guild name.

They saw me. I am behind the rocks east of the shrine and my leg is no good. If anyone finds this before they find me, tell the Sergeant-at-Arms: it isn't beggars and it isn't madmen. It's guildsmen. Tell him to check the Feast list.
A spiked shrine of Mehrunes Dagon on the hills north of Wayrest, ringed by scorched circles in the grass. Someone in the city has been praying for ruin, and doing it in company.
The Watch found a boot in one of those burnt circles north of town. Just a boot. Good leather, too. Wayrest cut, by the stitching.

^THE CITY OF COINS SHALL BURN
Brothers and sisters of the Ember, Wayrest has grown fat on other men's labour. Its bridges are built on debts and its guilds on lies. The Prince of Ruin does not hate the city. He only wishes to show it what it already is: kindling.

We meet at the stone on the dark of each moon. Bring a coal from your own hearth. Bring the name of one who has wronged you. You will not need to bring anything else. The Ember provides.
(Below, half burnt away:) ...the Bay Gate warehouses, on the night of the Merchants' Feast, when the Knights are all at table...
A spiked statue of Mehrunes Dagon in the lava fields of Molag Amur west of Necrom, where a cult that blames the Red Year on the Tribunal's weakness preaches ruin and recruits from the refugee camps.
Sul Indaram

The Three told you they held up the sky. Then the moon came down. The Three told you they held back the mountain. Then the ash came down. The Three told you they would always be with you. Where are they?
Mehrunes Dagon never lied to you. He promised fire, and he gave it. He promised ruin, and here it is. There is a terrible comfort in a god who keeps his word. Come and warm your hands at it.
Ordinator Sereth Arvel

To the Archcanon, by way of the Necrom chapter:
We approached the shrine at dusk, five strong. Twelve cultists, two summoned dremora, and their speaker, Sul Indaram, a refugee from Kragenmoor who lost his family in the ash. He preaches that the Tribunal failed us and that only the Prince of Destruction is honest about the world.

Ordinator Dral fell to the dremora. His mask was taken, and the cult wears it at their rites to mock the Temple. We withdrew. We are not enough to try again.
I request that the Temple seek outside help. Kill Indaram. Recover Dral's mask. A mask of the Ordinators must not be worn by heretics in sight of Necrom's dead.

Five Ordinators went to clear the Dagon stones west of Necrom. Four came back. The cult there calls itself the Unbroken Ash and says the Red Year was Dagon's mercy. Its leader's a Dunmer named Sul Indaram.

^In memory of the citizens of Alinor who fell in the hills above the city
^when the gates of the Deadlands opened, 3E 433
Here the Daedra came. Here the city's guard and its mages, its scholars and its fishermen held them until the gates closed. Here we buried them. Their names are written on the Tower's roll, and on the hearts of those who are left.
Below, scratched in recent days, in a neat hand: 'The gates did not close. They were only waiting. The Lord of Destruction remembers Alinor fondly, and will return to it by the same road. -- V.'
Vorondil, Keeper of the Returning Dawn

The Thalmor promised the Altmer a return to glory. They give us genealogy tables and curfews. The Prince of Destruction promised the world an ending, and he keeps his promises. The Mythic Dawn failed because it was clumsy. We will not be clumsy.

Offerings made: twelve. Dremora summoned and bound: two, both of the Valkynaz. The third will come at the dark of the moon, and with three, the old gate in the hillside can be reopened for the space of a breath. A breath is enough. Alinor never thanked its dead. Let it join them.

A shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the hills north of Alinor, where the Daedra came through during the Oblivion Crisis. A memorial to the dead stands beside it, and someone has begun leaving fresh offerings again.
Someone's leaving blood at the Dagon shrine north of Alinor, right next to the memorial to the Oblivion dead. The Justiciars say it's vandals. Old Tirenwe at the Tower says vandals don't chant.
Caedwen the Ashen

The Green Pact is a cage of leaves. We are forbidden to build, forbidden to cut, forbidden to change. The Altmer laugh at us, the Imperials log our forests from the east, and still we kneel to trees. The Prince of Ruin teaches that all things must burn to be renewed. The forest will be renewed.

Each circle we burn is a door. When there are nine, the doors will open together and the forest will learn what fire can teach. Six are done. Three remain. I will light the seventh myself, at the shrine, at the dark of the moon. Let the wardens come. Let them see what a Bosmer looks like when she is no longer afraid.

A shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the deep Greenshade forest north-east of Woodhearth, ringed by perfect circles of burned trees. In Valenwood there is no worse crime, and someone is committing it on purpose.
Someone's burning the forest around the Dagon shrine in Greenshade, a circle at a time. The wardens say it's a cult. The old folk say it's worse: they say it's a Bosmer.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_blac:
To the Grey Thread, in Necrom:
The Shadowscales lost two of their own this month to ambushes on the Helstrom paths. They suspect a traitor in their enclave. They are right. You know which. I know which. Let them hunt for it a while longer; a frightened enclave is a careless one.

In exchange: the name of the Morag Tong agent who walks the Helstrom paths with a writ for the Elder. I enclose it, woven into the second fold. Burn the silk after reading. If you do not burn it, Mephala will know, and so will I, and of the two of us, I am less forgiving.
A spider-limbed statue of Mephala in the Shadowfen south of Necrom, where Dunmer spies and Saxhleel informers leave coded messages in the webs for each other's masters to find.
Dunmer agents leave messages at the Mephala stones south of Necrom, folded in silk. Saxhleel agents leave other messages in the same spot. Sometimes they're the same agents.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_cyro: A many-armed statue of Mephala in the Blackwood west of Leyawiin, where the city's nobility send veiled servants on moonless nights to bargain for secrets and poisons.

The Leyawiin quality don't go to the Mephala stones themselves. They send a servant in a veil. My cousin went once, for her lady. She came back knowing who her lady meant to poison and has never sweetened her tea since.

Girl,
You will walk to the spider stones by the west path, not the road. You will wear the grey veil. At the altar you will leave the silk scarf and whisper the secret I have written on the inside of your wrist. Then you will wash your wrist in the marsh.

If a voice answers you, you will memorise every word and repeat them to me and to no one else. If no voice answers, you will wait until it does.
If anyone in Leyawiin asks where you were, you were at the Chapel of Zenithar praying for a better position. You will be getting one, if you are discreet. You will be getting another kind if you are not.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_elsw:
Sister Nazhira,
This one went to Mafala's stones on the dark of Secunda. The Weaver showed this one the threads of the Senchal clans. Your nephew is stealing from the harbour. My grandson is stealing from your nephew. The harbour master is stealing from both. Nobody is stealing from the Thalmor, which is a disgrace.

This one proposes the usual: we say nothing to the men, we arrange two marriages, we let the harbour master keep his post and his life in exchange for a tenth. Mafala taught our grandmothers that every secret is a thread. Pull gently. Never cut. Tie, and keep the knots where only we can see.
A spider-limbed statue of Mafala in the hills west of Senchal, where the Clan Mothers of the southern coast keep the secret rites that Mafala taught their ancestors.
The Clan Mothers go to Mafala's stones west of Senchal and come back knowing everything about everyone. That is not a rumour. That is how being a Clan Mother works.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_hamm: A shrine of Mephala in the hot rocks south-east of Skaven, its stones veiled in grey spider-silk finer than any loom in the Alik'r could weave, and worth more than its weight in secrets.
That grey silk in Skaven market comes from the Webspinner's stones. Wear it and you hear whispers. Sell it and you hear more. The Weavers' Court is tearing itself apart.

Mother of Webs, the Weavers' Court of Skaven called me a beggar's girl and spat in my bowl. Now they buy my silk with both hands and every bolt carries one of your whispers into their houses. Mistress Zainab cheats the dye-tax. Master Rahim's wife is not his wife. The Court's treasurer has a second family in Rihad.

I do not sell their secrets, Mother. Not yet. I only let them know I know. It is so much sweeter to watch them wonder. When they are all quite frightened, I will ask for a seat on the Court. And they will give it, and they will smile, and they will never sleep again. Thank you for the spiders.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_high: A shrine of Mephala on the heath north-east of Daggerfall, its stones strung with silk threads tied in knots. Every knot is a secret someone left in trade for another.

^Kept by the Keeper of Threads, for the Mother of Whispers
Red knot: the Duchess of the Northern Wing has paid her gambling debts with her husband's signet. Traded for: the name of the Duke's mistress.
Blue knot: the Captain of the Harbour sells the Dragon Knights' sailing dates. Traded for: the name of the man who buys them.
Black knot: Lady Gaudrel keeps a list. Traded for: who is on it.

Green knot: the Lord Commander knows nothing of any of this. He is the only honest man at court and therefore the most dangerous. Traded for: nothing yet. No one has a secret worth so much.
Every knot is a strand. Every strand is a web. Pull gently.
At the Webspinner's stone outside Daggerfall you tie a knot and whisper a secret into it. Next morning you know one of somebody else's. That's how the court got the way it is.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_morr: A many-armed statue of Mephala on the southern shoulder of Red Mountain, sacred to the Morag Tong, whose agents climb here to renew their vows in the Webspinner's shadow.
The Morag Tong climb to the Mephala stones under Red Mountain every season to renew their vows. Lately there are spiders nesting there, and the Grandmaster is not pleased.
an initiate of the Morag Tong

Webspinner, Mother of the Threads, I come to your shadow under the mountain with a sanctioned writ in my hand and no hatred in my heart. I kill by the law of the Houses and the writ of the Tong. I kill so that the Houses need not go to war.

Let my hand be quiet and my thread be short. Let my target know my face, as the law demands, and let them not see it twice.
Added in another hand: 'The threads of the shrine are gone. Spiders where the threads were. Brothers and sisters, be wary at the altar. Eno Hlaalu is seeking them.'
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_summ: Signed only with a spider drawn in ink

To the one who reads this next,
The Justiciars of Auridon pay twelve gold for every name of a disloyal citizen. They pay twenty for the name of a disloyal Justiciar. They pay nothing at all for the name of the person who has been selling them both lists for nine years. That is because they do not know that person exists.

I serve the Mother of Whispers, and I serve the Thalmor, and I find the two services almost identical. Both demand that you trust no one, that you remember everything, and that you smile. The only difference is that the Mother of Whispers admits it. If you would like to know your own name on the lists, leave fifty gold in the web. I will not tell you which list.
A shrine of Mephala on Auridon south of Firsthold, where those who inform for the Thalmor, and those who inform on the informers, leave messages for one another in the webs.
Want to know who's informing for the Justiciars in Firsthold? Ask at the Mephala stone. Want to know who's informing on the informers? Same stone. Same spiders, too.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_mephala_vale: A shrine of Mephala in the Reaper's March south-west of Arenthia, draped in the webs of great spiders, where a sect of Bosmer weavers gathers secrets for anyone who will pay, including the Thalmor.
The web-weavers at the Mephala shrine sell secrets. They sell them to the Khajiit, the Bosmer, the Thalmor. Doesn't matter who's buying. The spiders always get their share.

Sold to the Thalmor envoy at Arenthia: the names of the Khajiit smugglers on the Rimmen road. Price: one hundred gold and the envoy's promise to look away from our grove. Sold to the Khajiit smugglers: the name of the Bosmer who sold them to the Thalmor. Price: two hundred gold.

Sold to the Bosmer elders: the name of the Thalmor envoy's informant in their own council. Price: three hundred gold and the right to weave undisturbed for another year. The Mother of Webs is pleased. Everyone has paid, everyone is betrayed, and no one has thought to ask who sold them out. Feed the spiders. They have earned it.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_blac: A gleaming statue of Meridia in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where an Imperial missionary has spent twenty years trying to burn the bog-dead out of the marsh one wraith at a time.

Brothers,
You sent me to Black Marsh twenty years ago to bring the Saxhleel to Stendarr. They declined, politely, and gave me a canoe. I have since found a better use for my faith. The marsh is full of the restless dead, drowned Kothringi, slavers who sank in their chains, travellers who took the wrong path.

The Lady Meridia, whose stones I live beside, hates the walking dead even more than Stendarr does. I hope you will forgive me for borrowing her light. It is very bright and it works. Ninety-three wraiths laid to rest. I keep a tally on the statue. The Saxhleel have started to bring me tea.
There's a mad old Imperial at the Meridia stones in the Shadowfen. Hunts bog-wraiths with a lamp and a mace. He's not wrong, you know. There are a lot of bog-wraiths. There are fewer now.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_cyro: A shining statue of Meridia on a hilltop north-east of the Imperial City, built over the bones of an Ayleid sanctuary. Its light has gone dim, and the dead are walking up the hill in a line.

#17th of Sun's Height
I have kept the light here nine years. The Lady asks only three things: that the dead stay dead, that the light be kept, that the keeper not lie to herself. Tonight I lie to myself. I tell myself the shapes on the road are deer.

#19th of Sun's Height
They are not deer. A necromancer calling himself Corvus the Pale has camped in the Ayleid cellars beneath the shrine. He raises the old Elven dead and walks them up the hill to stand around the statue, facing it, so their unlight smothers hers. The lens in her hands has gone grey.

#20th of Sun's Height
I cannot fight him. I can only write this, and leave it where the Lady can see it. Whoever reads: break his line of dead, end him, and lift the lens from the statue's hands so its light can be kindled again. She rewards those who keep her light. She always has.
The Meridia statue past the Heartland farms used to glow at night like a lantern. It's dark now. A shepherd saw skeletons walking up to it in a row, and a man in black walking behind them.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_elsw: A shining statue of Meridia on the border hills north of Rimmen, where a stubborn Imperial pilgrim from Bravil has lived for years, burning the walking dead of the old war out of the dunes.

Dear Marcella,
Yes, I am still alive. No, I am not coming home. The dunes north of Rimmen are thick with the dead of the old wars, Imperial and Khajiit both, and some necromancer in the Void Nights stirred them up and never laid them down again. The Lady's light is the only thing they fear.

The Khajiit think I am mad. They bring me dates and leave quickly. One of them, a little Cathay boy, asked me why I don't go home. I told him: because I finally found something I'm good at. He thought about it and said 'this one is good at stealing dates'. We have an arrangement now.
There's an old Imperial woman at the Meridia stones north of Rimmen. She came from Bravil to burn the dead. Elsweyr has a great deal of dead. She is very busy.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_hamm:
~We are the ones the cities will not house.
~We wash the dead whom no one else will touch.
~Lady of the shining edge, the bone-singer walks again,
~and he has taken an Ansei from his grave.

The bone-singer Khalil calls himself the Dune-King. He hides in the hollows north-east of this stone, among the dead of Jafar's caravan. He carries the old Ansei's blade, and it sings for him, and that is an insult to every sword-singer who ever lived. We are too few to break him. If a stranger stands here and reads this, Lady, send them to us. The blade must go back into the earth, or into worthy hands.
A shining shrine of Meridia in the hills north of Rihad, where the Ash'abah, Hammerfell's outcast hunters of the dead, keep their camp. A bone-singer is loose in the hills, and he has woken an Ansei.
The Ash'abah camp by the Meridia stone north of Rihad. They're not allowed inside the walls after dark, poor souls. Funny, isn't it, how the city still sends for them when the dead get up.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_high: A bright shrine of Meridia south-east of Camlorn, where knights of the old city still kneel at sunrise and swear to give the restless dead the rest that Camlorn once could not.

~Lady of the bright edge, of the light that will not bend,
~we were the city that could not bury its dead.
~We remember the winter the mourners walked the walls,
~and the morning you broke it.

~Lend me the light for one more night.
~What rises without leave, I will put down.
~What is bound against its will, I will cut loose.
~And when I fall, let me fall facing the sunrise.
^Sworn by Dame Clemence Varre, Sir Odo of the Wall, and eleven whose names the wind has taken.
Camlorn knights pray at the Meridia stone before they go after a haunting. The priests pretend not to know. Saves everyone a great deal of ink.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_morr: A radiant statue of Meridia in the Deshaan east of Mournhold, where a zealot who calls the Dunmer's ancestor guardians abominations has begun smashing family shrines in the Lady's name.
There's a Meridian zealot in the hills east of Mournhold who's broken six ancestor shrines this year. Says the guardian spirits are undead and the Lady wants them freed. The families want him dead.
Brother Vanel Orethi, Servant of the Radiance

Grey folk, hear me. You bind your dead to your doorsteps and call it love. You trap your grandmothers in bone and ash to guard your silver and call it reverence. The Lady of Infinite Energies calls it what it is: a prison of the dead, kept by the living.

I do not break your shrines in hate. I break them so that your ancestors may go into the Light at last, as they were always meant to. You will curse me. They will thank me.
Scrawled across the bottom: 'My grandmother asked to stay, you fool. She chose. Come near the Llethan tomb again and you will meet the Light sooner than you planned.'
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_summ: A shining shrine of Meridia in the hills west of Alinor, where an old Altmer lamp-keeper has tended the light every night for two centuries, and has never once let a walking dead thing past it.
Ellaraine, keeper of the bright stone

#The 30,112th night
Lamp lit at sunset. Oil: good. Wick: trimmed. Necromancers in the hills: one, a student of the Tower who had read too much and been loved too little. Raised a cat. Cat put down by the light. Student sent home with a stern word and a biscuit.

#The 30,113th night
Lamp lit. Justiciars came, two, to ask under whose authority I keep a Daedric shrine. I told them: under the authority of everyone who has not been eaten by their grandmother. They wrote it down. I hope they file it. The Lady of Light enjoys a jest. She enjoys it more when the jest is true.
The lamp-keeper at the Meridia shrine west of Alinor is older than the Dominion. The Justiciars tried to move her on once. They came back down the hill rather quickly and very sunburned.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_meridia_vale:
~We are the hunters of the hunters' bones,
~we stalk the stalkers in the burial groves.
~The Pact forbids the axe, the saw, the flame,
~but the Pact has nothing to say of light.

~Lady of the shining edge, we eat no corpse that walks;
~we leave it to your light.
~When the bone-callers come to Grahtwood's dead,
~we will sing as we go in.
~We will sing as we come out.
~And if we do not come out, Lady, sing for us.

A radiant shrine of Meridia in Grahtwood west of Elden Root, where Bosmer hunters of the dead come before they go into the old barrows, since even the Green Pact has no rule against killing what is already dead.
Bosmer don't bury their dead deep, so the necromancers love Grahtwood. The hunters who deal with them pray at the Meridia shrine. Then they go into the barrows singing. Gives you chills.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_bl:
To my hirelings:
We hold nine. We will hold twenty by the next Bloodmoon. Keep them chained at the statue; the Lord of Domination likes to see his gift kept close. Feed them enough to walk. Not enough to run.

My House was ruined in the Red Year and the lizards' war. We were Dres cousins, wealthy, respected, served. Now I am a beggar in Necrom, and the Saxhleel have a king. I do not accept it. Molag Bal does not accept it. He has promised that what was taken from House Hlervu will be returned in chains.
If the Helstrom warriors come, kill them. If a stranger comes, kill them faster.
A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the Shadowfen near the Necrom border, where a Dunmer slaver of an old fallen House has returned to chain Saxhleel captives in the Prince of Domination's name.
There are Saxhleel in chains at the Molag Bal stones by the Necrom border. Real chains, new iron. A Dunmer with a Hlervu ring calls himself the Chain-Lord. Helstrom wants every spear it can find.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_cy: A hunched statue of Molag Bal high in the Jeralls north-west of Bruma, where chains are set into the rock and the snow around them is never quite white.

#Accounts of the Shackled Gift
One carter, Imperial, strong back. Offered to the Lord of Domination at the Frostfall new moon. Kept forty days. Excellent.
One carter, Nord, loud. Kept nine days. The Lord prefers the quiet ones, I find, but the loud ones are more satisfying to quiet.

One girl, Bruma, called Hilde, the daughter of a tavern cook. Taken on the north road with a basket of bread. Not yet offered. She sings to herself in the cold. I have decided to let her finish the song first.
Note: the Countess's guard came within a mile last week and turned back. Send her another case of Skingrad red. Keep her drinking.
Three carters gone on the north road this season, all near the Molag Bal stones. And now Jorunn's girl Hilde. Bruma's watch says wolves. Wolves don't use chains.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_el: A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the hills just south of Riverhold, where slavers have begun to gather Khajiit captives, almost in sight of the Mane's own walls.

Captain, this one is writing in the rocks above the stones. Do'sara is watching. The rumours are true. Twelve captives, Khajiit, chained to the Lord of Brutality's statue, with a Bosmer and two Imperials standing guard and a fourth person who wears no colours at all.

The fourth person carries a paper with a Thalmor seal. This one cannot see the words. Do'sara says do not fight. This one is a Cathay-raht and wishes to fight very much. This one will wait for the guard. If the guard does not come, this one will not wait
Slavers at the Molag Bal stones south of Riverhold, they say. The Mane's guard says they're rumours. The Mane's guard also sent two riders to look. The riders haven't come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_ha: A shrine of Molag Bal in the hills north of Taneth, ringed with iron stakes. Slavers who are banned from the Forebear harbour meet their buyers here by night, and pay their tithe to the Lord of Chains.
Fisherfolk keep going missing north of Taneth. Everyone knows where they go: the Molag Bal shrine, and a slaver they call Iron-Collar. Lord Ezhar's put a price on him. Nobody's collected.

Taken from the fishing hamlets, Frostfall: 6. Two strong, three middling, one old woman who will not stop singing. Sold to the Khajiit buyer: 2. Sold to the Bosmer buyer: 1. Tithed to the Lord of Chains: the old woman, at the dark moon, as is proper.

Lord Ezhar has put a price on my head. Very flattering. Taneth sells silk made by children and tigers broken with whips, and calls me the monster. I keep the stock in the pens behind the shrine. Five left. If the Forebears come, kill the stock first. Dead goods tell no tales.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_hi: My name is Etienne Coste. I am a groom of House Tamrith. I rode with my lord to burn this place. My lord is dead. They kept me because they wanted someone to watch.

There are four of us left. The Lady of Chains feeds every third night. She wears my lord's ring on a thread around her neck and she keeps his sword in the stone like a trophy. She says no one will come. Tell the Dowager we tried. Tell her the sword is here. Tell her to send someone who is not afraid of the cold.

A shrine of Molag Bal in the cold hills west of Shornhelm, strewn with rusted chains. A lord of House Tamrith rode out to burn it and never came home; his ancestral sword is still somewhere inside the circle.
Lord Tamrith went to cleanse the Molag Bal shrine and the shrine cleansed him. They say his sword's still there, stuck in the stone, and that something sits beside it and waits for the next fool.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_mo: A hulking statue of Molag Bal in the Ascadian Isles between Balmora and Vivec, a Corner of the House of Troubles, where vampires of the old Vvardenfell clans are said to come to pay homage to their father.

Signs at the shrine: fresh blood on the left hand of the statue, none on the right. That is the Aundae custom, offering with the hand that does not hold the knife. The Quarra would leave nothing; the Berne would leave a body.

So: an Aundae coven, refined, patient, thinks itself above the brute clans. They will have a manor, or a plantation house, with a host who never eats at his own table. Check every Ascadian estate where the field hands have grown pale and the master has grown young. I am too old to do it. Someone is not.
Somebody left a heart at the Molag Bal stones south of Balmora. A Dunmer heart. The Ordinators say a vampire clan's moved in from the Ashlands. The plantation folk lock their shutters by dusk now.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_su: A shrine of Molag Bal on Auridon west of Firsthold, where a renegade Justiciar is said to have carried out interrogations that even the Thalmor would not sanction. The shrine has not been the same since.

Subject: Bosmer, male, accused of sedition. Question: who wrote the pamphlet? Answer, after the first hour: he did. Answer, after the second hour: his brother did. Answer, after the third: the Silvenar himself. All three answers are false. Truth is not the purpose. The purpose is the moment he stops caring which answer I want.

The Directorate dismissed me for excess. The Directorate does not understand its own work. The Lord of Domination does. Every interrogation is a small prayer to him: the slow bending of a will until it no longer remembers being straight. He is pleased. He has shown me the Coldharbour in every cell. I will build one here.
There's a Justiciar who got thrown out of the Thalmor for being too cruel. Think about that. He's at the Molag Bal shrine west of Firsthold now, asking questions. Nobody sends him the questions.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_molag_bal_va: A shrine of Molag Bal at the heart of a thorn-grove east of Falinesti, where the trees grow bent and chains are wound into the roots. The Bosmer will not enter. Something inside invites them every night.
There's a grove east of Falinesti where the trees grow crooked, like slaves under a load. Molag Bal's shrine is in there. The Bosmer won't go near it. They say the trees inside are screaming.

#First night
The thing that keeps this grove is a vampire, old, Altmer, who calls the trees her prisoners. She has bound the grove with chains of Coldharbour iron, and each tree she bends is a Bosmer she has drained and planted in the earth. She says the Green Pact forbids me to harm a tree. She says it smiling.

#Fifth night
She has asked me which I would rather be: a tree that cannot move, or a servant that cannot refuse. She says the Lord of Domination gives everyone a choice, and then makes them regret it. I have found a sharp stone. I am going to choose a third thing. If anyone reads this, I chose it.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_black: A crouching statue of Namira in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where a cult of rot-eaters gathers to feast by the light of a pale stone that was stolen from the Dunmer long ago.

~What falls in the water, the water will keep,
~What dies in the marsh will go down deep,
~And the Lady of Leavings sets her table there,
~With a stone from the north for a candle-flare.

We took the pale stone from the grey folk's goddess when the raiders went north. It burns at dusk, only at dusk, a little sad light. The grey folk loved it. We love it more, because it is stolen, and stolen things are the Lady's favourite: the leftovers of someone else's love. Whoever comes for it will join the feast. One way or another.
The rot-eaters at the Namira stones feast by the light of a pale stone that glows at dusk. Stolen off the Dunmer, they say. Somebody in Mournhold would pay well to have it back.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_cyrod: Old Fennia, Queen of the Chorrol Gutter

~The fine folk step around us, the fine folk hold their nose,
~The fine folk give a copper and they wipe it on their clothes,
~But the Lady of the Leavings sets a table in the stone,
~And she never once has asked us what we're doing on our own.

To the two who stayed, Septimus Crow and Big Arelia: you were good company and better eating company, and I hope the Lady keeps you warm down in the dark. Nobody in Chorrol will miss you. That's why she loves you. That's why she loves us all.
Next feast: the new moon of Rain's Hand. Bring your own spoon.
A crouching statue of Namira in the hills south-east of Chorrol, where the town's beggars hold a feast every new moon and nobody in Chorrol asks what is served.
Every new moon the beggars of Chorrol walk out to the Namira stones and come home well fed. Two didn't come home last month. The other beggars say they were 'invited to stay'.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_elswe: A statue of Namiira, the Great Darkness, in the dunes north-west of Torval, where the dark-souled Dro-m'Athra gather on moonless nights, and where a mother has gone looking for the son she lost to them.

J'kar, my cub,
You came to these stones to steal a dark-moon pendant from the Dro-m'Athra, because a fool in a skooma den said it would bring you luck. You stole it. You put it on. And when you came home, your shadow did not come with you.

Now you walk with them on the moonless nights. You looked at me last time through the window and there was nothing behind your eyes. The Moon-Priests say the pendant holds you to Namiira. Whoever reads this: break my son's hold. Take the pendant. If you have to end him to do it, then end him gently, and bring the pendant out into the light. He was a good boy. He was a very bad thief.
The Dro-m'Athra gather at Namiira's stones north-west of Torval when there are no moons. Old Za'mira's son J'kar went out there to steal from them. He came back, in a way. He came back wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_hamme: A shrine of Namira among the dunes south-west of Sentinel, kept by a sect of beggars who live in old tombs and whom the priests of Tu'whacca accuse of robbing the dead of their journey.
The Namira folk in the south-west dunes live in the old Yokudan tombs. Priests say they eat what they find in there. I say a priest will say anything to get you to tithe.

The priests of Tu'whacca say we rob the dead. The dead do not need robbing. They have nothing and they are going nowhere. It is the living who robbed us: the landlords of Sentinel, the Crowns who took our fathers' fields, the Forebears who took our boats.

So we live where no one will follow. We sleep in the cool stone with the old kings and we are not afraid of them. The Lady of Decay has taught us that everything rots, the rich man's silk and the beggar's rags alike, and that the rot is honest. We do not eat the dead. Mostly. Not unless the winter is very long. Tell the priest that, and watch his face.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_high_:
~Lady of the spider and the slug, of the cellar and the sore,
~the bright folk of Evermor do not look at us.
~So be it. We look at them.
~We see them throw away their bread, their cloth, their old men.

~We take what they throw away, and we give thanks.
~We are the mouth at the end of the world.
~Nothing is wasted while we live,
~and when we die, Lady, nothing will be wasted then either.
^Kept at the river landing by Mother Crell, who has not been warm since Sun's Dusk of 4E 170.

A shrine of Namira by a Bjoulsae landing in Stormhaven, tended by beggars, lepers and the unloved of three cities. They are kind to strangers. They are unusually curious about what strangers are carrying.
The Namira beggars by the river landing won't take your coin. They want your leftovers. All your leftovers. Some say they're not fussy what kind.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_morro: A statue of Namira in the West Gash scrub between Balmora and Ald'ruhn, where the blighted, the scarred and the unwanted of Vvardenfell gather in a ragged congregation that the Temple cannot bring itself to disperse.
The ash-scarred beggars of Balmora walk north to the Namira stones on feast days. The Temple won't move them on. Too many of them are Temple pilgrims who came back from the mountain changed.

~They turn their eyes when we go by, the ash has kissed our skin,
~They give us alms with gloves on and they will not let us in.
~But the Lady of the Unloved does not flinch to see our face,
~She keeps a seat for every scar, and every scar its place.

We were pilgrims once. We climbed the mountain for the Three and the mountain sent us back with blisters where our faces were. The Temple feeds us. The Temple will not touch us. Namira touches us. That is all the theology a beggar needs.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_summe: A shrine of Namira in the hills west of Alinor, the refuge of Altmer cast out for being born imperfect. The Directorate pretends it does not exist. Its people pretend they do not mind.

~They measured my daughter with rods of silver,
~her spine, her ears, the gap between her eyes.
~They found her wanting, and they wrote it in a book,
~and the book was closed, and she was gone.

~Lady of all ugly things, of the beetle and the scar,
~you do not measure. You do not count.
~You take what the beautiful ones throw away,
~and you call it yours, and it is.
~Here on the hill my daughter laughs. Her spine is crooked.
~Her laugh is perfect. Write that in your book.
The crooked ones live out by the Namira shrine west of Alinor. Born wrong, the genealogists said. They're the kindest folk on the island, my mother says. She's not supposed to know that.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_namira_valen: A shrine of Namira in Greenshade north-east of Woodhearth, held by Mandate-Breakers who claim the Green Pact's oldest law for their own, and who no longer wait for a battle before they feast.

Brothers and sisters, the Spinners tell us the Meat Mandate is Y'ffre's gift: eat the foe you slay, so that nothing is wasted. But why wait for a war? Why only the foe? The Lady of Decay teaches that every body is meat in waiting, the elder and the infant, the Altmer and the Bosmer. Waste is the only sin.

We have two of the net-boys from Woodhearth in the pit. They will be our feast at the dark moon. Some among us are squeamish. Some among us say the boys are kin. Kin is a word. Meat is a fact. If the wardens come, we will remind them that the Pact is on our side, and see how long they argue with themselves.
The Mandate-Breakers out by the Namira shrine say all flesh is one flesh. Two net-boys from the Woodhearth docks are missing. The wardens are still deciding whether it's a Pact matter. I'm not.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_bl: A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where Cyrodiilic smugglers and Saxhleel born under the Shadow both leave offerings, each insisting the Lady is really theirs.
The smugglers who run the Cheydinhal-Shadowfen paths leave a coin at the Nocturnal stones. The Shadowscales leave something else there. Nobody's sure what, and nobody's asking.

Partner,
The route through the Shadowfen to Cheydinhal is clean this month. Coin left at the Lady's statue as usual. I noticed someone else had been there before me: a black feather, a single scale, and the shape of a hand pressed in the moss where nobody's hand could reach.

I think the Shadowscales use the Lady's stones too. I think they're telling us something: that the shadow is theirs and we're guests in it. I'm going to be a very polite guest from now on. Leave two coins next time, not one. Leave three if you've been rude to an Argonian lately. I have.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_cy: A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the woods west of Cheydinhal, where Nibenese thieves leave a coin before every big job and Dunmer refugees come to pray for a little shadow to hide in.

No thief in the Nibenay works a big job without leaving a coin at the Nocturnal stones west of Cheydinhal first. The Gray Fox did, they say. My uncle did, and he's never been caught. He's never been paid either.

^Shadow hide you.
Beneath it, a ladder of chalk marks, each with a coin-mark beside it: 'Dorian, the Bravil counting-house, done.' 'Little Mouse, the Chorrol wool-factor, done.' 'Teeth, the Skingrad castle cellar, NOT done, Teeth is not with us now.'

Newest of all, in a careful hand: 'Taren's mother. She came to pray for sleep. Leave her be, all of you, or answer to me. She is not ours, but the Lady listened to her anyway. A shadow is a shadow, whoever stands in it.' The coin beside it is Morrowind silver.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_el: Old Ja'khirr, called the Last Footpad

If you are reading this, you are standing where Rajhin stood. He hung his bow at the Lady's feet four hundred years ago and swore never to steal again. Then he stole the oath back. That is the story. Nobody knows if it is true.

The Shadow-Claws took it. Their chief is Jo'vahn, called the Unlucky, and he is about to be very much more unlucky. They have a hideout in the rocks close by, and they come back to the stones to mock the Lady with her own offerings. Find them. Take back the offering box. Rajhin's bow is the Lady's to give, not theirs to keep. The Lady may decide you have earned it. Rajhin would have.
A hooded statue of Nocturnal in the hills north-west of Senchal, sacred to the city's thieves, robbed this season of its offerings, including a bow hung there by Rajhin the Footpad himself.
The Shadow-Claws robbed the Lady's stones near Senchal. Took Rajhin's own bow, they say. Every thief in Senchal wants them dead. Not one of them dares to do it. Funny how that works.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_ha:
^For the Mistress, a share of every haul
The purse of a Breton envoy, emptied on the Wayrest road: two pearls to the shrine. A caravan of Skaven silk: one bolt, the grey one, which nobody would buy anyway. The great lens of the Serpent Tower: kept whole, for now.

The mages think the lens is about stars. It is about the Mistress. When the moons are dark and the lens is turned to the sky, it shows the paths of shadow between the stars, and a thief who knows those paths can walk anywhere. We will keep it until the next dark moon. Then the Serpent can find its own way.
A shrine of Nocturnal in the broken hills south of Elinhir, where the thieves' crews of Craglorn pledge their takings to the Night Mistress. The Observatory's stolen lens is said to lie here now.
Craglorn thieves leave a share for Nocturnal at the stone south of Elinhir. Somebody's left a great glass lens there lately. Big as a cartwheel. The mages are beside themselves.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_hi: A shadowed shrine of Nocturnal in the Wrothgar foothills west of Orsinium, a waypoint for smugglers who carry Orcish steel to Breton buyers who would rather not be seen buying it.
Smugglers leave a coin for the Night Mistress at that shrine west of Orsinium before they cross the passes. The ones who forget don't usually make it to Evermor.

For the crew, in case I don't come back from Orsinium. You know the route: shrine to the Malacath crags, crags to the river, river to Evermor, no lanterns, no songs. Leave the Mistress her coin. Always the coin.

The Breton factor stiffed us on the last run, so I kept the twelve finest blades back as surety. They're under the flat black stone south-east of the shrine, about twenty paces out, wrapped in oilcloth with a crow feather tied to the bundle. If I'm dead, sell them. If I'm alive, and you've touched them, I'll know.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_mo:
^Under the Lady's cloak, in the storm of the 9th
Councillor Dravel of the Ald'ruhn Hall: took the Andas family's land for a debt that was already paid. Mark. Take the deed and burn it on his own hearth.
The Hlaalu factor at the Ald'ruhn bazaar: weights his scales with lead. Mark. Take the lead. Leave the scales.

The Redoran Guard captain who beats beggars at the gate: mark, but gently. Take his boots. He can walk in the ash as they do.
To the Lady of Shadows we give a tenth of all taken. To the Andas family we give the rest. To the councillors we give nothing at all, which is what they gave.
A cloaked statue of Nocturnal in the Ashlands north of Ald'ruhn, where the Bal Molagmer, Dunmer thieves who rob only those who wrong the poor, meet in the ash storms to choose their marks.
The Bal Molagmer meet at the Nocturnal stones north of Ald'ruhn when a storm comes in. They choose a councillor, and by spring that councillor is a lot poorer and a lot quieter.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_su: A shrine of Nocturnal on Auridon just west of Firsthold, where the thief called the Moth makes her offerings, and where, the Justiciars believe, she hides what she takes from the island's most loyal houses.

To whoever is clever enough to find this, and not a Justiciar,
I am leaving the island before the Directorate's hounds catch my scent. My takings stay behind. I have no use for Caladwe's circlet; I only took it because he wore it while he signed the order that sent my brother to the quarantine anchorage.

Everything I took from him is buried thirty paces north of the shrine, beneath the twisted cypress with the moth carved on its root. Take it. Sell it. Give some to the sick in the anchorage, if you have a heart. The Night Mistress keeps nothing, and neither should you.

The Moth's robbed Magistrate Caladwe four times. Took his ceremonial circlet last month. The Justiciars say she stashes her takings by the Nocturnal stone. They've dug up half the hill and found nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_nocturnal_va: A shadowed shrine of Nocturnal in the Reaper's March north-west of Arenthia, where Khajiit thieves pay their dues to the Night Mistress before working the rich caravans of the Elsweyr road.

Mistress of the Night, this one is Jo'darr. He has taken carpets from Ri'zahd, silk from the Thalmor, and once, a whole roast boar from the Silvenar's own table, with the Silvenar still sitting at it. He leaves you the tusks. They are very fine tusks.

Ri'zahd has also prayed here, Jo'darr knows. Ri'zahd left more gold than Jo'darr. This is cheating, Mistress. A merchant should not bribe the patron of thieves. Jo'darr will steal Ri'zahd's offering and give it back to you twice, so that you are paid by both of us and owe neither. This is fair. This is the way of shadows.
The cat-thieves of the Elsweyr road all pray at the shadow-shrine near Arenthia. Ri'zahd the caravan-master prays there too, and pays more. Says it's cheaper than guards.

place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_azura.hoo: A colossal statue of Azura, Daedric Prince of Dusk and Dawn, raised on a mountain south of Winterhold by Dunmer who foresaw the fall of Vvardenfell.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_azura.pil:
Mother of the Rose, Queen of the Night Sky,
You warned your faithful and they built you this place, so that some of us would have somewhere to stand when the ash came. I was six years old on the Pride of Tel Vos. My sister Nivera was nine. She held my hand on the rocks below the College.

She died in Winterhold the first winter, of the cough. I live. I do not know why you chose me, but I am grateful, and I am angry, and I think you understand both.
Light her way, Azura. I will light a candle here every Morndas until my own dusk comes.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_azura.rum: The great statue on the mountain? Built by Dunmer before Red Mountain blew. They say Azura told them it was coming. Pity she didn't tell everyone.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_azura.sk4: Folio #19 (1451, -1351): Field inspection recorded for Shrine Of Azura within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #19 for shrine_of_azura: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shrine Of Azura are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_azura.sta: Waymark 9: Shrine of Azura. Steps from the road to the statue: three hundred and four, though the snow makes it feel like four thousand. Statue faces south and east, toward Morrowind. Height impossible to measure without a ladder no sane person would climb.
The priestess who keeps it would not give her name. She said the goddess sees the dawn and the dusk and nothing between matters much. I offered her bread; she took it. Even prophets get hungry.

place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_mehrunes_: Lord of Razors, Breaker of the Ruby Throne, I have nothing of worth to give you but my anger. Take it. I have carried it since the Legion burned my village in the Markarth Incident and called it peace.
The door of your house is shut. I will wait at it. You were patient for a thousand years before the Oblivion Crisis, and so I will be patient for you. When it opens, let me be the first one through.
A spiked shrine to Mehrunes Dagon, Prince of Destruction, on a peak in the southern Pale. It has stood silent for years, and the Vigilants of Stendarr keep a careful eye on it.
That shrine to Dagon up in the mountains has been shut for years. Good. Some doors should stay shut, and that's one of them.

To the Keeper of the Hall.
The shrine is quiet. The doors are sealed and the brazier cold. Someone has been here, though: fresh tracks in the snow, a leather strip of burned prayers, the bones of a goat laid on the altar.
No more than one worshipper, I judge, and a lonely one. I will watch for him. Lonely worshippers of the Prince of Destruction do not stay lonely, or harmless, for long.

Request: one more Vigilant for this post through the winter, and a lamp that does not blow out when you look at the altar. Mine has gone out four times. The wind does not blow inside that hollow. I checked.
