place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_the_black: A sacred shrine built into a gaping rock mouth with processional halls and a great black pool.
The Black Maw's pool has a metal thing in it now. The shrine-keepers say it is a thorn in the world's tongue.

WHAT IS DRAWN RETURNS, WHAT IS TAKEN IS OWED. The Root remembers every hand that touched it. Draw not what is not yours; and if you have drawn it, return it threefold. The black water is patient, but it is not blind.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_of_the_cats_: A stepped shrine whose terraces are lined with giant stone cats, each a different pose, each watching the hill of broken swords with the patience of the very old.
Pilgrims leave milk at the feet of the cats and in the morning the bowls are dry. The priests say they evaporate. The cats say nothing, which is what cats say best.

~O watcher with the patient eyes,
~who sees the swords and does not rise,
~who knows the moons by their small names:
~keep the hill, and keep the flame.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_blac: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, raised long ago by the last of the Kothringi as the Knahaten Flu killed them, in the hope that the Taskmaster would spare an orderly people.
the last scribes of the Kothringi

Taskmaster, Lord of the Ordered Plague, we have kept our ledgers. We have counted our dead in rows. We have buried them in straight lines. We have done everything a tidy people can do. We ask you to see that we are tidy, and to pass us by.

Added below, in a shakier hand: 'The Saxhleel do not sicken. The Imperials do not sicken. Only we sicken. If this is your order, we do not understand it.'
Below that, in a single silver line: 'There are four of us left. We will finish the inscription tomorrow.' The inscription ends there.
The Peryite stones in the Shadowfen are Kothringi work, the last thing they built before the Flu took them all. Saxhleel won't touch the stones. They say the Flu sleeps in them still.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_cyro: A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the farmland south-east of Skingrad, where a strange cough has begun to spread through the vineyards, and its victims have begun to keep their houses unnaturally tidy.

#1st of Hearthfire
Cough began. Swept the yard. Swept it again. The stones by the road are untidy. I have rearranged them. They are better now.

#4th of Hearthfire
Wife says I talk in my sleep about 'the Taskmaster's ledger'. She does not understand that every sickness is a list and every list must be completed. I have walked to the shrine and set the offering bowls in a straight line. The dragon approves. The cough approves.
#5th of Hearthfire
Nineteen sick. Twenty is a rounder number. I will visit my sister.
The sick from the farms near the Peryite stones sweep their floors three times a day and line their spoons up by size. My aunt caught the cough and alphabetised her chickens.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_elsw: One. Two. Three wagons. Four wheels. Sixteen wheels. Thirty-two spokes. Spokes are in order. Wagons are in order. Cousins are in order. Cousin Ri'jasha is not in order. Cousin Ri'jasha ran.

The Taskmaster says that is a mistake. The Taskmaster says mistakes are corrected. The bell on the lead wagon rings out of order when the wind blows. The bell must be stopped. The bell is the last thing that is out of order.
One. Two. Three. This one cannot remember what this one was before this one could count. This one does not mind. Four.
A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite in the dunes north of Torval, beside a clear spring, where Ri'jasha's caravan stopped for water and her clan caught the Taskmaster's orderly plague.
Don't drink at the Peryite spring north of Torval. Ri'jasha's clan did. They're still out there, walking in rows around the statue, counting. Counting what, nobody wants to know.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_hamm: A shrine of Peryite in the waste south of Skaven, raised by the survivors of a caravan that was quarantined in the desert during an old fever and left to die by the city it was trying to reach.

#Day 6 outside the walls
Skaven will not open its gates. The fever is in three of the wagons. They throw down bread from the walls and shoot arrows at anyone who comes closer. We have moved to the old stones south of the city, where at least there is shade.

#Day 19
We prayed to the Eight. The Eight did not come. We prayed to the Lord of Pestilence because he, at least, was already here. He came. The fever has stopped spreading. It has not stopped. It only waits, he says, for the order he will give it. He says we are his now, and that one day he will send us back to Skaven. My people are not afraid of that day. They long for it.
The Peryite shrine south of Skaven is where they left the sick caravan in the old plague. Skaven's grandmothers still won't buy goods that came by that road. Some grudges outlive fevers.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_high: A sickly shrine of Peryite in the fens north-east of Wayrest, where plague-penitents come to beg the Taskmaster for a cure, or for a curse to send downriver to someone else.

The old fool's case is a treasure. Forty years of fevers, catalogued, cured and, in the last pages, reversed. He found how the Knahaten sickness might be woken from dust. Then he lost his nerve and wrote 'NEVER' across it in red. Cowards always write in red.

The Taskmaster is pleased with us. He likes order, and nothing is so orderly as a plague: it takes the weak first, the proud second, and leaves the rest to sweep up. We will brew the first measure here at the shrine on the next dark moon and send it downriver to Wayrest in the fish barrels. The Lower Bridges will learn humility.
Old Penhallow the apothecary had his case of cures stolen on the fen road by the Peryite stone. He says there's a recipe in it nobody should brew. He says it like he's brewed it.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_morr: Observation. Ash-blight does not spread at random. It moves in rows, like a farmer sowing. It favours the third house in a street, then the sixth, then the ninth. A Daedra of pestilence and order would understand this. Peryite understands this.

Hypothesis. If the blight is a sentence, then it can be finished. If it can be finished, it can be ended. If it can be ended, it can also be begun, by someone who knows the grammar.
Note to myself: burn page two before the Archmagister's mouth visits. He will not understand the difference between a cure and a weapon. Neither, some nights, do I.

A dragon-shaped statue of Peryite on Azura's Coast west of Sadrith Mora, where a Telvanni healer studies the blight that crawls down from Red Mountain and has started to wonder whether it can be ordered rather than cured.
A Telvanni healer lives at the Peryite stones west of Sadrith Mora. Says the blight is a language and she's learning to speak it. The fishermen won't sell her fish anymore.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_summ: A shrine of Peryite on Auridon north-west of Firsthold, where the sick of the quarantine anchorage row ashore by night to pray, because the Directorate's healers will not treat anyone not on the census.
The sailors from the quarantine anchorage row to the Peryite shrine at night. Customs knows. Customs looks the other way. Customs, I think, has a heart. It won't last.
Jory Penwick, bosun of the 'Fair Winifred'

Lord of Sickness, I am a Breton and a sailor and I never prayed to any god but Kynareth and the price of pepper. My captain is dead of the grey blisters. Half my crew is dead. The Altmer will not let us land and will not let us leave. We are anchored off Firsthold like a fish nobody will gut.

You keep order in plague, they say. Then keep it now. Let it take me if it must, but let it pass over the boy Tam, who is twelve and stowed away and should never have come. In return I will do whatever a bosun can do for a Prince. I can tie very good knots. I can curse in nine languages. I am leaving my mother's ring on the stone. It is all I have.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_peryite_vale: A shrine of Peryite in Grahtwood north of Elden Root, where sick Bosmer come for cures the Thalmor healers will not give them, and where the Thalmor now quietly write down every name.
The Peryite shrine north of Elden Root cures the spore-cough, they say, when the Altmer healers won't. Thalmor have a man with a book in the bushes now. Writing down everyone who goes.

For the spore-cough of the deep groves, which the Altmer healers in Elden Root will only treat for those who can pay in Dominion gold: one measure of spriggan sap, one of bear fat, three crushed nirnroot leaves, all burned at the Taskmaster's stone with an honest prayer. Breathe the smoke. Cough the spores. Live.

The Lord of Pestilence keeps order in sickness as in all things. He does not cure for love. He cures because the spore-cough is a disorder and he dislikes disorder. That is enough for me. Note: the Thalmor watcher in the hazel thicket is called Nerion. He has the cough himself. I have left him a pouch of smoke. We will see whose list he writes me on.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_bla: A leering statue of Sanguine in the Shadowfen south of Mournhold, where border smugglers of both races meet for revels so wild that, for one night a month, Dunmer and Saxhleel forget they hate each other.

To all smugglers, deserters, poets and other undesirables of the Shadowfen and the Deshaan: the full moon revel will be held at the Prince's stones as usual. Bring drink. Bring music. Leave your grudges at the treeline; there is a pile there, you will find it.

Rules: no blades past the treeline. No talk of the Red Year. No talk of the chains. Anyone who starts a fight will be made to dance with the Naga, and they do not let go. Dunmer bring the wine, Saxhleel bring the sap. The Prince brings the rest. You'll know it when it arrives.
There's a revel at the Sanguine stones on the border every full moon. Dunmer and Saxhleel, dancing together. By morning they've remembered they're enemies. But the night's the night.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_cyr: A leering statue of Sanguine in the vineyard hills between Skingrad and Kvatch, where an endless revel is said to wait for any guest who takes the first cup.

To Lucilla Vinicius, who is far too clever for her father's cellar:
You are invited to a gathering in your honour in the hills west of Skingrad. Wear the green. Bring nothing. Leave nothing behind but your name-day and your good sense.

There will be wine you have never tasted, music you will never stop hearing, and company who will never tire of you. Arrive at moonrise. The door is the statue; knock with a full cup.
P.S. Your father's Shiraz is adequate. Ours is better. You may tell him so yourself, if you ever see him again.
There's always music near the Sanguine stones in the Weald, even when nobody's there. Galen Vinicius's daughter followed it on her name-day. That was a month ago.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_els:
Captain Shazar-ri,
You asked why the cooks keep going to the Sanguine stones. Here is the truth. The Prince's revellers have a spice. It is not moon sugar. It is not skooma. It is a red powder that makes a stew taste like your grandmother's on the best day she ever had.

We go to get the spice. We stay for the dancing. We come back without our aprons, sometimes without our names, but always with the spice. The Mane has never eaten so well. If the Mane asks, it is a family recipe. It is, in a way. The Prince says he is everyone's family, at a revel.
A grinning statue of Sanguine in the hills west of Riverhold, where moon-sugar revels last for days and the Mane's own cooks have been known to leave the soup to join them.

The Sanguine stones west of Riverhold have a revel every full moon. Sugar, wine, music. The Mane's cooks keep slipping out to join it. This one has tasted the Mane's soup lately and does not blame them.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_ham: A shrine of Sanguine in the vine-covered hills north-east of Rihad, where the young heirs of the Forebear wine houses hold revels so lavish that the losses are settled in vineyards.

^Wagered this night of revel, before the Lord of Debauchery and all his cheerful company:
By Tahir son of Barid, vintner's heir of Rihad: twelve casks of his father's gold vintage, against the deed to a vineyard below Kvatch, held by a gentleman in a red mask who says he has never lost a bet in nine hundred years.

Contest: who shall drink the most and still recite the full list of Ra Gada kings.
Result: Tahir, by three cups and one king. The gentleman in red paid his debt with the deed, and a goat, and a curious smile. He said Tahir would understand the goat later. Witnessed by: nobody sober.
Rihad's young merchant sons go up to the Sanguine stones with a cartload of their fathers' best. They come back with no shoes and a goat. It's always a goat. Nobody knows why.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_hig: A shrine of Sanguine in the woods west of Daggerfall, where masked Breton nobles hold revels that last three days and are discussed for three years. Not every guest comes home.

^Sign with your mask, not your name
The Grinning Fox: came for the wine, stayed for the wager.
The Gilded Owl: lost my wife's pearls to a dremora at dice. Worth it.
The Weeping Moon: has anyone seen my coachman?
The Silver Stag (in a young, careful hand): just a cup or two, then home before Mother wakes.

The Silver Stag (the same hand, much later, much less careful): The host says I can win back the signet if I play one more round. The host has such kind red eyes. I do not think I will be home before Mother wakes. I do not think I will be home at all. It is the best night of my life.
Young Lord Aubin Gaudrel went to a masked revel by the Sanguine stones and hasn't been seen since. His mother is pretending she isn't frantic. She's very good at it, and it isn't working.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_mor:
#Fredas
Went to the revel at the stones with Tribune Salvo's adjutant. He said it would be a lark. It was a lark. I drank something purple that an Indoril lady poured into my mouth from a shell. Then I danced. I do not dance.

#Loredas, dawn
I have woken by the statue with a hangover the size of Vvardenfell and the Company seal-ring on someone else's finger. A Khajiit's. He was snoring. I took it back. He woke and called me 'partner'.
I do not know what I have signed. I am very afraid it was a cargo of Ebonheart's entire winter salt.

A statue of Sanguine in the Deshaan near Ebonheart, where sailors, Legion deserters and bored young nobles of House Indoril hold revels that start at dusk and end only when someone has sold something they shouldn't.
The Sanguine stones south-east of Ebonheart have a party every Fredas. My cousin went once. Came back with a new tattoo, no boots, and a deed to a ship he's never seen.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_sum: A shrine of Sanguine just south-west of Alinor's walls, where the city's most decorous lords shed their decorum once a season in revels the Directorate officially knows nothing about.

^The Lord of Revels requests the honour of your indiscretion
^at his stone beyond the south-west gate
^upon the night of the Directorate's Founding Feast
Dress: none required. Masks: obligatory. Lineage: irrelevant, for one night only. Conversation on the subjects of genealogy, the Thalmor and the correct shape of ears is forbidden on pain of a forfeit.

Note, in a cramped hand on the back: 'Darling, last year you wore the Justiciar's sash and nobody knew it was you. Wear it again. It caused the most delicious panic. And do bring the Bosmer wine, the illegal one. The Prince adores contraband. So do I. -- L.'
The Sanguine revels south of Alinor are the worst-kept secret in the Dominion. Half the Directorate goes. The other half takes notes. They swap places every season.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sanguine_val: A shrine of Sanguine in Greenshade south of Falinesti, where Bosmer revellers brew rotmeth strong enough to make a Nord weep and hold feasts that sometimes forget which guests are on the menu.

^Sacred to the Lord of Revels
Take the haunch of a boar that died frightened. Seal it in a gourd with its own blood and let it rot for a moon. Add honey, a spoonful of crushed beetle, and three drops of whatever the Khajiit at the next fire is drinking. Bury it under the shrine for nine nights. Dig it up while singing. Do not stop singing.

Warning: drink it only at the stone. Last Midyear, Cousin Faenor carried a gourd home to Falinesti and drank it alone, without singing, and the Lord of Revels was offended. Faenor danced for four days. The rootkeepers had to tie him to a branch. He still taps his foot in his sleep.
They brew rotmeth at the Sanguine shrine south of Falinesti. One cup and you sing. Two and you dance. Three and you wake up in Woodhearth married to a Khajiit. I'm told the marriage holds.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_b: A grinning statue of Sheogorath in the Shadowfen south of Necrom, kept by a Saxhleel who drank sap from a Hist that was struck by lightning and has been talking to the Mad God ever since.
There's an old Saxhleel at the Mad God's stones who drank sap from a lightning-struck Hist. He tells fortunes. They're all wrong. And then, a year later, they're all right.

The lightning hit the Hist, and I drank the burnt sap, and the Hist said 'oops'. Then a voice that was not the Hist said 'oh, I like this one'. That was the Mad God. He likes me. I like him. We talk about fish.

Prophecies, this month: a Dunmer will bring me a pie. A King will sneeze. A Khajiit will sell the moon. A stranger will read this and think 'he is mad'. All will come true; one already has. The God says to tell you that you are standing on his foot. You are not. But you will move, now, won't you? There, he says. Good.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_c: Fulvius Pell, formerly of Bravil, presently of his own head

To the Management:
On the night of the 6th I left a button at your shrine, per local custom. In exchange you took my shadow and gave me a cat's. It is a fine shadow, it chases moths, but it is not mine and it will not sit for supper.

Further, your scamp has my hat. My good hat, the green with the heron feather. He wears it at an angle that I consider provocative. I demand the hat's return. My shadow you may keep, as I have grown fond of the cat's.
Anyone reading this who is braver than me, which is everyone: please get my hat. I will pay in buttons. Also money.
A grinning statue of Sheogorath in the reeds north-west of Bravil, with a soup tureen of buttons for an offering bowl and a gentleman scamp in a borrowed hat for a doorman.
The Mad God's stones by Bravil have a doorman now. A scamp in a feathered hat. My neighbour Fulvius swears it's his hat. Fulvius has also sworn he's a teapot, so who can say.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_e: A grinning statue of Sheggorath, the Skooma Cat, in the dunes just east of Torval, where addicts come to bargain for one more dream and Moon-Priests come to bargain them back.
The Skooma Cat's stones east of Torval are full of dreamers and the Moon-Priests who chase them. Sheggorath laughs at both. This one has heard him. He sounds like a kettle.

~What is the cat who is sweet and who bites?
~What is the moon that is three moons at night?
~What is the dream that you buy and you lose?
~And what is the Lattice when no one can choose?

Beneath, in a Moon-Priest's tidy hand: 'The answers are skooma, skooma, skooma and skooma. Go home.'
Beneath that, scratched: 'Wrong. The answer is cheese. The Skooma Cat says so. He also says the Moon-Priest has a crumb in her whiskers, and she does, this one checked, and now this one believes everything.'
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_h: Captain Bakr al-Tanethi, master of the dry dhow 'Pomegranate'

#Day 1,092 at anchor
Wind: sideways. Sea: sand. Crew: four lizards, a goat and a very patient scorpion. The Lord of the Isles came by at dawn and commended the lizards' knots. I gave him a ration of cheese and a promotion.

#Day 1,093
The Forebear harbour-master sent a letter asking me to return my ship's papers. I have eaten them. They were not seaworthy. The scorpion has mutinied and taken the goat. I will sail after them as soon as the dunes turn to water. The Lord says it will be soon. The Lord says that every morning. Every morning I believe him. That is the only sane thing I have left.
A gaudy shrine of Sheogorath in the hills east of Taneth, kept by a sea captain who sailed off the edge of his own sanity and swears he found a second sea on the other side.
Captain Bakr from Taneth gave his ship to the Mad God and walked inland to the shrine. He's been there three years, teaching the lizards to sail. He says they're quick learners.
A crooked shrine of Sheogorath in the Glenumbra meadows south-west of Camlorn, decorated by its devotees with spoons, cheese rinds and some genuinely excellent poetry.

~I asked the Lord of Madness for a rhyme,
~he gave me nine, and took away the time.
~Now Turdas comes on Sundas twice a week,
~and all my spoons are learning how to speak.

~The Count of Camlorn wears a cheese for crown;
~I told him so. He would not take it down.
~O Breton lords, so certain, proud and wise,
~it's you he laughs at, wearing my disguise.
^(Below:) Leave cheese. Leave spoons. Leave anything you are too sure of. -- G.
There's a poet camps at the Sheogorath stone south of Camlorn. Says the Mad God writes his verses for him. They're better than the court poet's. That's what worries people.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_m: A grinning statue of Sheogorath on the pilgrim road north-west of Necrom, a Corner of the House of Troubles, where travellers walking alone swear the stone asks after their families by name.

It asked me how my mother was. I told it she was dead. It said, 'Oh, I know, I meant how is she being dead? Is she enjoying it?' I said I didn't know. It said I should ask her, it's only polite, and then it told me where she's buried, which was not where I buried her.

I dug at the place it said. I found a jar of pickled scuttle and a note in my mother's hand that said 'I knew you'd look'. I have not been sane since, but I have been much happier. The grave-robbers in the hollow wanted to know what the stone told me. I told them it was asking after their mothers too. They didn't like that.
Don't walk past the Mad God's stones on the Necrom road alone. It talks to you. It asks after your mother. And now there are grave-robbers camped in the hollow behind it.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_s: A shrine of Sheogorath in the hills south-west of Alinor, decorated by an Altmer painter who was expelled from the Academy for painting the sky the wrong colour, and who has been painting it every colour since.

The Academy of Alinor teaches that there are seven acceptable blues for the sky over Summerset, and that a painter who uses an eighth is not merely wrong but disloyal. I used an eighth. I was expelled. The Lord of Madness visited me that very night and said the sky had complained to him that it was tired of being blue.

So I paint it green on Morndas and red on Tirdas and on Sundas I let it choose. I paint the Justiciars as chickens because they asked me to paint them as they truly are. I paint the Directorate as an empty frame. Nobody has confiscated that one. Nobody has understood it.
The mad painter by the Sheogorath stone paints the sky green, the sea purple, and the Justiciars as chickens. They keep confiscating the chickens. He keeps painting more.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_sheogorath_v:
#Day the first of my enlightenment
The Lord of Madness appeared to me as a talking badger and asked why I eat only meat. I said: the Green Pact. He said: and is cheese a plant? I said: no. He said: and is cheese an animal? I said: no. He laughed for an hour and gave me a wheel of Colovian goat cheese.

#Day the three-hundredth
The Spinners cannot decide whether I have broken the Pact. The Silvenar has sent a messenger to ask. The tree beside the shrine has also been asked, and says nothing, which the elders take as disapproval and I take as shyness. I have never been happier. The badger visits on Fredas.

A shrine of Sheogorath in the Greenshade forest south-east of Woodhearth, where a Bosmer hunter who once took the Mad God's advice now eats nothing but cheese and claims to be on speaking terms with a tree.
There's a Bosmer at the Sheogorath shrine south of Woodhearth who gave up meat for cheese. Breaks the Pact, eating cheese. Nobody's sure. The Spinners have been arguing about it for a year.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_to_peryite.a:
Those who went to Bthardamz to serve the Taskmaster:
Orchendor? No - he LEADS. He does not go, he sends.
Kjar of Dragon Bridge. Hilda the Pale. Two Bretons from Markarth who would not give names. Askar, who was a guard in Understone Keep until his skin went grey.
Those who stay at the shrine: me. I am still deciding. When the pustules reach my eyes I will go too. They say in Bthardamz the pain becomes a kind of song.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_to_peryite.h: A Daedric shrine in a misty glade west of Karthwasten, where the sick and the desperate pray to Peryite, Taskmaster of the lowest Oblivion, for a cure or a curse.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_to_peryite.p: Taskmaster, you who keep the order of the rot. My boy has the brain rot and the healers at the Temple of Dibella want silver I do not have. The priests of Arkay say pray. I prayed. He got worse.

So I pray to you now, Lord of Pestilence, because you are the only god in the Reach who admits what sickness is. Take it from him. Put it in me if you must. I am old, the boy is not.
The sick ones who camp by the shrine tell me you never give without a price. Fine. Name it.
- Fjola of Karthwasten
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_to_peryite.r: Folk with the rattles go to the Shrine to Peryite to pray. Some come back cured. Some come back worse. Most don't come back at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_to_peryite.s: Folio #24 (-2619, -748): Field inspection recorded for Shrine To Peryite within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #24 for shrine_to_peryite: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shrine To Peryite are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_bla: A dark statue of Vaermina in the Shadowfen east of Cheydinhal, where Saxhleel who drink Hist sap for its visions wake to find that someone else has been dreaming in their place.
Hist-sap dreams are sacred to the Saxhleel. Near the Vaermina stones east of Cheydinhal, they've gone wrong. Hunters wake with nightmares that aren't theirs, in voices they don't recognise.

I drank the sap at my egg-tree and slept. In the sap-dream I should have seen my ancestors. Instead I saw a Breton woman burning in a tower I have never seen, and a voice laughed and said 'thank you, little lizard, she was delicious'.

I woke at the Vaermina stones. I did not walk here. Three others woke beside me. All of us had the same dream. The Lady of Nightmares is drinking the sap-dreams through us, like a mosquito through a reed. I will not taste the sap again until the elders find a way to close the reed.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_cyr:
#Harvest, the 3rd of Frostfall
Sleeper by the long reed: a fisherman. Dreamt of drowning. Common stock. Two drakes the hour.
Sleeper by the stone: a Legion veteran. Dreamt of the Red Ring. Rare stock. Twenty drakes the hour, and the Bravil gentlemen fight over it.

Sleeper under the willow: a child. Dreamt of her mother. I did not take it. I am not a monster. I took the one after, when she dreamt of the Prince instead.
Note: the Lady of Nightmares grows impatient with the small stock. She asks for a dreamer of rank. A priest, perhaps. Or one of those fine Leyawiin ladies who never sleep at all.
A dark statue of Vaermina in the Nibenay marshes between Bravil and Leyawiin, where a dream-seller harvests sleepers lying in the reeds and sells their nightmares in Bravil's skooma dens.
Sleepers in the reeds by the Vaermina stones. Dozens. Eyes moving under the lids. The dream-woman from Bravil walks among them with a sack, and she never looks tired.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_els: A dark statue of Vaermina in the hills south-west of Senchal, where a dream-woman sells nightmares to skooma-sleepers, and no honest smuggler in the city will sleep within a mile of her.
There's a dream-woman at the Vaermina stones south-west of Senchal. Even Dar'jazad won't deal with her, and Dar'jazad deals with Thalmor. That should tell you enough.

Do not sleep here. Do not sleep here. Do not sleep here.
This one slept here, one night, after too much sugar, by the statue, because the ground was warm. This one dreamed of the Void Nights, when the moons were gone, every night of two years, in one night.

When this one woke, the dream-woman was sitting by this one's head with a little glass jar, and she said 'thank you, that one will sell very well in Bravil'. This one has not dreamed since. Not one dream. Not a good one, not a bad one. That is worse than you would think. Do not sleep here.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_ham: A shrine of Vaermina in the Alik'r dunes south of Sentinel, where nomads once came to buy prophetic dreams and now come in fear, because the dreams have started to come true in the wrong order.

Traveller. My people came to this stone for four generations to buy dreams of where the water lies. The Mistress of Dreams was a fair trader. One dream of water for one of our memories, an old one, of no great use.

This year she is hungry. She takes the new memories now: our children's names, the faces of our wives. And the dreams she gives back are of death, and they come true. My brother dreamed of a scorpion and died of a sting a month before he had the dream. Do not sleep within sight of this stone. If you must sleep, sleep with a pebble under your tongue. It keeps her fingers out.
The Alik'r nomads used to trade at the Vaermina stones for dreams of water. Now they dream of their own deaths, and three of them have already happened. Backwards. Don't ask me how.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_hig: Sister Oriane, formerly of the Temple of Shornhelm

#Frostfall the 2nd
The nobles of Shornhelm will not pay me for their dreams any longer. Very well. Children dream more freely, and more honestly, and in such vivid colours. The Mistress of the Orb is delighted with them.

#Frostfall the 9th
The eleventh child walked all the way to the stone before her mother caught her. Such a lovely dream: she was a queen of a drowned city, and everyone she loved was a fish. I took the dream and left her the fear. That is the tithe. The Sheriff has started asking questions. The Mistress says I should give him a dream of his own.
A shrine of Vaermina across the river south-east of Shornhelm. Since autumn, children of the lower town have been sleepwalking toward it in the night, all dreaming the same purple dream.
The sleepwalking children of Shornhelm all walk the same road, toward the Vaermina stones. The Sheriff's asking for swords. The Temple's asking for calm. I'm asking for a lock on my door.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_mor:
~Sleep, little ash-child, the mountain is near,
~Dream me your dying and dream me your fear,
~Give me the fire and give me the fall,
~And Mother will keep them, and Mother keeps all.

The mountain sends them to me, the sleepers. Something under the Ghostfence calls them, and I only stand between and catch what spills. Their dreams are red and full of the old Sixth House songs. The Lady of Nightmares drinks them like wine. I keep the best in a glass vial for myself. One taste, and you see the Heart.

A statue of Vaermina on the western shoulder of Red Mountain, where a priestess calling herself the Dream-Mother draws the ash-sleepers of Balmora and Ald'ruhn to stand in a ring and feed her their nightmares.
The ash-sleepers walk to the Vaermina stones under the mountain and stand in a ring, smiling. There's a woman in the middle singing. Fevyn Andalor in Balmora says her brother is one of them.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_sum: Sapiarch Ilaeril of the Faculty of Dreams

Subject the Fourth (Bosmer servant, paid one gold): dreamed of the forest. On waking, could not remember the word for 'tree'. Subject the Ninth (Altmer clerk, paid one gold): dreamed of his own funeral, in great detail, attended by no one. On waking, resigned from the Directorate and went to sea.

Hypothesis: the Mistress of the Orb does not create nightmares. She reveals the nightmare that already lies beneath each sleeper. Altmer nightmares are uniformly about being found imperfect. I find this academically significant. I find it personally disquieting. Subject the Twelfth will be myself.
A shrine of Vaermina in the hills north-west of Alinor, where a Sapiarch of dreams conducts studies of the sleeping mind that the Crystal Tower funds, and is careful never to ask about.
There's a Sapiarch who studies dreams at the Vaermina shrine. Pays volunteers a gold piece a night to sleep there. Nobody volunteers twice. Some of them haven't woken up from the first time.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrine_vaermina_val: A shrine of Vaermina north of Arenthia, where a Bosmer dream-thief called the Lantern-Bearer draws the sleepers of the town out of their beds each night and harvests their dreams in a basket.

#Sun's Dusk, the 4th
Bosmer dream of the hunt. Khajiit dream of the moons. Mixed together in my basket they make the most extraordinary colours. The Mistress of the Orb has never tasted their like. She has promised me the purple lantern for good if I fill the basket by the dark of the moon.

#Sun's Dusk, the 11th
The innkeeper's cub had a dream of a great golden cat walking across the sky. It was the loveliest yet. I kept it, and left her only the dark. She will wake screaming every night for a year. The Mistress says that is the tithe. I say it is a small price for something so lovely. The basket is nearly full.
The sleepwalkers of Arenthia all go north to the Vaermina stones. There's a woman there with a purple lantern. Shazah at the inn's ready to claw her face off. She'd pay you to do it first.
place_lore.nirncraft.shroud_hearth_barro:
#First night
The fence in the Ratway said the urns are in the deep hall, the ones with silver bands round the neck. He drew me a map. The map is wrong already. There's a door here he didn't draw, with a hearth carved over it and a bowl of cold ash in front.

#Second night, I think
I took one urn. Just one. When I lifted it, every coffin in the hall knocked once, all together, like a heartbeat. I put it back. They kept knocking.

There's a big one at the end of the hall in a cloak of rotten fur. Its eyes are open. Hearthkeeper, the carving says. It keeps the fire. I took its fire. I'm sorry. Tell Father I'm sorry.

^Here the clan of Ivar banked the last fire
^of the long winter, and swore
^that it should never go out.

The ash in the bowl is grey and old. Somebody has written beneath it, in charcoal, much more recently: 'it went out. it went out. i'm sorry.'

Around the door the stone is blackened with old soot, as if the fire once burned right up against it for years on end. The villagers of Ivarstead still bank their hearths on the longest night and say the name of Ivar over the coals. Most of them have forgotten why. The barrow, it seems, has not forgotten. Whatever keeps this door expects the fire to be kept too.
An old Nord barrow on the slope just above Ivarstead, close enough that the villagers can hear it at night. A stonemason's son went in for silver three weeks ago.
Don't go poking at Shroud Hearth. Hjorvald's boy did, for a Ratway fence and forty septims. Now there's knocking at night, and Hjorvald doesn't sleep.

Folio #14 (945, 871): Field inspection recorded for Shroud Hearth Barrow within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #14 for shroud_hearth_barrow: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Shroud Hearth Barrow are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_grove.herb:
#5th of Hearthfire
For thirty years I have gathered snowberries and frost mirriam in the Shrouded Grove, and for thirty years the spriggans have let me. I leave them honey; they leave me be. That is the bargain.

#22nd of Hearthfire
The eldest spriggan, the one with the antlers of white birch, attacked me today. Her bark has gone black at the heart, like rot, and her lights are red. Someone has cut into the old tree at the centre of the grove and taken heartwood. A woodcutter's axe-marks. A greedy fool.

#23rd of Hearthfire
The heartwood must be put back, or the elder must be put down. I can do neither. If a kind soul passes, there is honey in the jar by my door.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_grove.hook: A misty grove in the snowfields of the central Pale where warm springs keep the trees green through winter. Its spriggans have turned savage, and an old herbalist wants to know why.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_grove.rumo: The Shrouded Grove stays green in the dead of winter. Pretty, if you don't mind the tree-women watching you from behind the trunks.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_pass.hook: At place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the dark crags and cliff-ports of Rivenspire, where Shornhelm's three noble houses light the Second Lamp against night-drinkers and coastal wreckers.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_pass.rumou: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass report signs of feral Montclair vampires, false-beacon wreckers, and Ayleid tomb-thralls operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.shrouded_pass.v8_lo:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the dark crags and cliff-ports of Rivenspire, where Shornhelm's three noble houses light the Second Lamp against night-drinkers and coastal wreckers. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.shrouded_pass have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by feral Montclair vampires, false-beacon wreckers, and Ayleid tomb-thralls. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by clanless mountain raiders, Daughters of Wroth frost-hags, and Lyrezi peak-vampires. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.
place_lore.nirncraft.sightless_pit.falme:
Observation the first: the Falmer of this pit are entirely blind, yet they track a dropped coin across a stone floor with perfect accuracy.
Observation the second: they keep the chaurus as we keep cattle, and with considerably more affection.

Observation the third: they are aware of me. They have been aware of me for some time. They are simply waiting for me to go deeper.
I do not intend to oblige them. Tomorrow I return to the College with my findings.
place_lore.nirncraft.sightless_pit.hook: A deep pit in the hills south of Winterhold, home to the blind Falmer and their chaurus. A miner from Whistling Mine was dragged into it a week ago.
place_lore.nirncraft.sightless_pit.miner:
To the Jarl's steward, Winterhold.
Three nights ago the Falmer came up out of the ground near the mine and took Torbjorn Coal-Eye. We heard him shouting all the way down the hill. We followed the tracks to the Sightless Pit and could go no further. The smell alone turned us back.

Torbjorn had a little silver hammer on a chain, his father's mining charm, that he never took off. If he's dead, his wife wants it back. If he's alive, gods help him.
The Jarl's guards will not go down there. Surely someone will, for the right price.
place_lore.nirncraft.sightless_pit.rumou: The Sightless Pit. Blind elves down there, and they hear everything. Don't even breathe loudly near the entrance.
place_lore.nirncraft.sightless_pit.sk4_n: Folio #18 (1270, -1365): Field inspection recorded for Sightless Pit within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #18 for sightless_pit: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Sightless Pit are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.silent_moons_camp.h: A bandit camp ringed around an ancient forge north-west of Whiterun. When the moons are up, the anvil glows with a cold light, and the blades made there burn with it.

Night of both moons full. Laid the pale ore from Halted Stream in the coals at moonrise. The forge drank the light and the iron went white, then blue, then silver. Quenched it in snowmelt. Struck the anvil once and it rang like a bell in the next valley.

Finest blade I have ever made. Brattvar thinks it is for him. It is not. I will call it Moonsliver and I will keep it in the iron chest by the forge until the day I leave this rabble and sell it in Solitude for enough to buy a house with a door that locks.

The lunar forge does not care who works it. That is the one thing I like about it.
place_lore.nirncraft.silent_moons_camp.l:
The stone around the forge is carved with old marks, Nordic but older than any Nord now living can read. Someone has scratched a rough translation beside them:

'Two eyes of the night. One red, one pale. What is struck beneath them remembers them.'

Below, a second hand: 'The forge only takes when both moons look on. Under a new moon it is cold iron and nothing more. Don't waste good ore on a dark night.'

A third note, in charcoal: 'Hrodna, the ore's here.'
place_lore.nirncraft.silent_moons_camp.r: There's a forge at Silent Moons that only works under the moons. The bandits there make blades that glow like Masser on a clear night. I'd like to see one. I'd like even more not to be stabbed with one.

place_lore.nirncraft.silvenar.audience_r:
#THIS SEASON'S AUDIENCES
To a Pact-Warden of the east, with a grievance about foxes. To a spinner from Falinesti, with a story. To a Khajiit trader from Rawlkha, with a very small gift and a very large favour. Denied: two Imperial envoys, one Thalmor Justiciar, and a man who said he was the Silvenar's brother.
A margin in the Scribe's hand: 'The man was the Silvenar's brother. The Silvenar has been informed. He declined to be audience-ed by himself.'
place_lore.nirncraft.silvenar.gate_riddl:
^WHAT WALKS IN, BUT NEVER OUT?
^WHAT SPEAKS WITHOUT A MOUTH?
^WHAT DOES THE GATE-WARDEN WANT TO HEAR?
^(Answer all three. Answer wrongly. See what happens. The gate-warden is in a mood.)
place_lore.nirncraft.silvenar.hook: A hidden court beneath hollowed root arches in the Malabal mist, where the Silvenar holds audience in a single hall and fireflies drift through the lantern-light.
place_lore.nirncraft.silvenar.rumour: Silvenar is not on the road. You find it, or it finds you. The old guides say you need only be lost on purpose and very polite about it.
place_lore.nirncraft.silvenars_audience_:
^1. SPEAK ONLY WHEN ADDRESSED.
^2. DO NOT ADDRESS THE FLOOR.
^3. IF THE HALL ASKS A QUESTION, ANSWER IT BEFORE THE KING DOES.
^4. LEAVE BY THE DOOR YOU ENTERED.
Beneath, in the Scribe's small hand: 'Rule 5 is not written down. You will know it when you break it.'
A single great hall in the roots of Silvenar, its ceiling a tangle of living arches and its floor of polished bark, where a king who rarely speaks holds audience in lamplight.
The hall has seats for forty and a Silvenar who needs none. Most days it is empty. On a few days it is so full that the walls bulge, and nobody can say afterward who was in the room.
place_lore.nirncraft.silver_gorge_bandit: A palisaded outlaw camp wedged into a narrow bend of the silver road, rigged with rock-chutes and rope bridges.
Highwaymen at the Silver Gorge Bandit Camp have been taxing every peddler who can't afford a mercenary guard.

Let the big silver convoys with twenty guards pass through untouched; our meat is the lone tinker, the spice-wagon, and the bailiff's tax-rider. Drop the log-gate the moment the horn blows from the upper bridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.silverdrift_lair.ba:
Master Ulvar,
You always said the Saga of the White Strand ends mid-verse because the last skald who knew it died before he could teach it. I have found where he learned it. The old priests carved the closing stanza on a tablet in Silverdrift Lair, near the great wall at the heart of the barrow.

I am going in to make a copy. The College would pay for the rubbing, but I would rather the saga were finished at your fire than sat in their library.
If I am not back in Dawnstar by Sun's Dusk, send someone who can swing a sword and has a good memory. The tablet is small enough to carry.
place_lore.nirncraft.silverdrift_lair.ho: A Nordic barrow in the hills of the southern Pale whose old name means 'silver snow'. Bards say the last verse of a lost Dawnstar saga is carved somewhere in its depths.
place_lore.nirncraft.silverdrift_lair.ru: Silverdrift Lair has a verse carved in it that no living bard knows. Every few years one of them goes in to copy it. Mostly they don't come back to sing it.
place_lore.nirncraft.silverdrift_lair.sa:
~The longships beached on the white strand,
~The wolves of Atmora came to land,
~They lit their fires on the frozen shore
~And swore the oath that was sworn before...
^The fragment ends here, as every known copy does.

^Note in the margin, signed H. S.-V.
Every skald in the Pale knows these four lines and no more. My master learned them from his master, who learned them from his. All of them swore the rest was carved below Silverdrift by the priests who first heard it sung. I mean to find out whether they were liars or merely lazy. Gods willing, by Sun's Dusk Dawnstar will hear the end of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.silverdrift_lair.sk: Folio #17 (625, -967): Field inspection recorded for Silverdrift Lair within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #17 for silverdrift_lair: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Silverdrift Lair are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.silyanorn_ruins.hoo: An Ayleid watchpost in the gorge below Stormhold, half-swallowed by moss, where river-thieves hide what they should not have borrowed.
place_lore.nirncraft.silyanorn_ruins.rum: A river man called Gorge-Eel uses the old ruins below the south hill as a storehouse. He took the north hill's sleeping idol and carried it down in a sling, and he rocks it like a child.
place_lore.nirncraft.silyanorn_ruins.thi:
#Tally
Idol, one, stone, grey-green, heavy. Sling, one, rope, mine. Pursuers, none, so far. I did not take it for coin. I took it because it looked lonely on its hill and I could not sleep for the thought. If it wakes, I shall tell it I am sorry.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaal_village.allma:
~All-Maker, you made the snow and the seal beneath it.
~You made the spear-arm and the hunger.
~What I take today I do not own;
~I hold it for a while, as I hold my breath.
~When I fall, take me back the way you take the beast:
~without anger, and without waste.

Spoken by every Skaal hunter at the edge of the village before the hunt, with the right hand on the doorpost and the left on the spear. Children learn it before they learn to throw. Outlanders who hear it sometimes laugh. The Skaal let them laugh, and notice which ones come home from the ice with full sledges and which do not.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaal_village.gazet:
#Who sits at the fire
Elder Hjalmgerd keeps the fire that has never gone out and the Telling, ninety-nine verses of a hundred. Aslfur Wide-Eye hunts and brings home trophies that are slightly wrong. Wren Wind-Listener says the wind has gone quiet. Bodil Hide-Scraper trades pelts and silence. Torvald Boat-Mender talks politely to the sea.

#The hundredth verse
It is said chief Frodi named Haknir's Shoal with his last breath. A bone slip lies in a cairn there. Ketil says the wind has a name, and it is Frodi. Wren did not say no.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaal_village.hook: A ring of timber longhouses in the northern snows, home of the Skaal, who honour the All-Maker and trust no one who comes asking for stalhrim. Their hunters know every trail of the island.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaal_village.hunte:
#Notches since the first frost
Six horker at Horker Island. Thanks given for each, fat kept, bones returned to the water.
Two bristlebacks near Bristleback Cave. One too young, let go.
One bear. It gave itself on the third day, as bears do.

Two sledges lost on the shore road south of Gyldenhul Barrow. Not lost. Taken. Iron-shod boot tracks, smell of tar and cheap mead. Reavers from Bujold's Retreat. They took Old Skjald's carved hunting-mask, which was his father's, and his father's. The Adversary is in men who take what they did not make.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaal_village.rumou: The Skaal let me trade furs once. They looked at my iron knife like it was a sickness. Their hunter Yrsa says reavers have been raiding their sledges near Bujold's Retreat.
place_lore.nirncraft.skar.duel_notice.p0:
#By leave of the Council
A duel will be fought at the gate of the Skar at the second bell, between two of the Redoran blood, over a grievance named in the register. The witness shall be unaffiliated. The blades shall be of the House. No other weapon shall be introduced, and no substance shall be applied to any blade.

The Council notes with regret the necessity of the last clause.
place_lore.nirncraft.skar.hook: The great shell-chamber of Ald'ruhn, rib-arched and banner-hung, where Redoran councillors count honour like grain.
place_lore.nirncraft.skar.rumour: A Redoran duel at the gate of the Skar ends at the second bell, they say, and the witness must be someone who owes neither house a favour. Councilor Brara has been seen looking for one.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaven.hook: A walled oasis city of the Alik'r interior, rich in silk and water, where the wells are worth more than gold and an old family once bought theirs from someone who was not quite a man.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaven.rumour: Every family in Skaven owns a well, a grudge, or both. The Qamar family's well never runs dry. People ask why. The Qamars stop smiling.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaven.silk_guild_l: Mistress Zainab, of the Weavers' Court

Sister,
The new silk from the south-east is finer than anything from the coast. Too fine. It is grey as smoke and it does not tear, and the girl who brings it will not say where she gets it. I followed her. She walks out past the walls to the old Webspinner's stones and comes back with a bolt each week and a new secret each day.

She knows things about the Weavers' Court that only the Court should know. She knows which of us cheats on the dye-tax. She smiles when she passes my stall. I have stopped buying her silk. The others have not. Come home, sister, and bring a sharper sword than mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.skaven.well_warden_: Wells of the East Quarter, Hearthfire count: eleven dry, four brackish, one sweet. The sweet one is the Qamar well, as ever. It has never dropped a hand's breadth in forty years, not even in the drought of 4E 189 when we buried the camels.

Old Qamar the elder bought that well, they say, from a smiling man with a dog at the shrine east of the city. The price was 'nothing of value to him.' His wife left him the same summer. His son, Qamar the younger, sells the water now and does not sleep. I note this only because the Warden's office is asked to report anything unusual about the wells. This is unusual.
place_lore.nirncraft.skingrad.healer_mem: Cases this month: nineteen. All from the farms south-east of the city, all within a morning's walk of the Peryite shrine. Symptoms: dry cough, black spots on the tongue, an unnatural tidiness. Two patients folded their blankets eleven times each before I could stop them.

I have prescribed garlic and rest. I suspect the stones would prescribe something else. I am requesting a priest of Stendarr, a barrel of vinegar and, if the Count can spare one, a guard who is not afraid of farmers who cough in rows.
place_lore.nirncraft.skingrad.hook: A walled Colovian city of vineyards and tomato farms on the Gold Road, ruled by a Count nobody has ever seen by daylight, and ringed by shrines to the Princes of revelry, plague and the hunt.
place_lore.nirncraft.skingrad.rumour: Best wine in the Empire and the Count's never seen at noon. Ask me no more about the Count. Ask Galen Vinicius about his daughter instead; he's been asking everyone else.
place_lore.nirncraft.skingrad.vintner_or:
To the cellars of Galen Vinicius:
His Excellency requires forty bottles of the Weald Shiraz of the year 4E 188, to be delivered after sunset to the castle's lower gate. Not the gate on the hill. The lower gate. After sunset.

His Excellency notes with sympathy the absence of your daughter Lucilla, and observes that young persons who go dancing in the hills sometimes return, and sometimes are better not sought. He offers no further counsel.
Payment enclosed. Please do not ask the courier to stay for supper. He will refuse.
place_lore.nirncraft.skjaldborg.hook: A shield-fort on the Atmoran ice, its wall a ring of battered shields and a single hall of frosted wood.
place_lore.nirncraft.skjaldborg.rumour: The shields at Skjaldborg all face the ice now. The captain won't say who turned them.
place_lore.nirncraft.skjaldborg.web.p0: The ice is groaning at night; the seam runs under the halls of Kjolvik and out to sea. The old chiefs swore to keep the howe's ship, but nobody has been to the howe in three generations. Send word to the hold. Tell them the dragon-mound is the pin. If the pin goes, the shelf goes.
place_lore.nirncraft.sky_haven_temple.ak:
Carved in a flowing foreign script beside the stair, with a Tamrielic gloss in a much later and more careful hand:
WE WERE THE WATCHERS OF THE DRAGON'S BLOOD. WE KEPT OUR VIGIL HERE WHEN THE EMPIRE FORGOT THE SKY.

The gloss continues: The Blades who left this here believed the dragons would return and that only one of dragon blood could stand against them. Most of Skyrim thought them fools. In the last year, Skyrim has been revising its opinion.
place_lore.nirncraft.sky_haven_temple.ho: Behind the Karthspire, carved deep into the mountain, lies an ancient sanctuary of the Blades from the days of Reman. Its dragon-faced door has not opened in centuries.
place_lore.nirncraft.sky_haven_temple.ru: There's a story about a door in the cliffs behind Karthspire with a dragon's face on it. Won't open for picks, won't open for spells. Waiting for someone, I suppose.

place_lore.nirncraft.skyborn_altar.altar:
HERE THE SKY-BORN CAME DOWN TO TAKE WHAT WAS GIVEN.
HERE THE PRIESTS OF BROMJUNAAR LAID THE OFFERING: GOLD, GRAIN, AND THE FIRSTBORN OF THOSE WHO REFUSED.

BOW TO THE WING. BOW TO THE CLAW. BOW TO THE VOICE THAT ENDS ALL VOICES.
THE PRIEST WHO KEEPS THIS ALTAR SHALL CARRY THE FANG-BLADE, AND WITH IT TAKE THE HEARTS OF THE SKY-BORN WHO DISOBEY.
^Beneath, cut more roughly and much later:
WE BOWED LONG ENOUGH. THE PRIESTS ARE DUST AND THE DRAGONS ARE BONES, AND THIS STONE IS ONLY A STONE. BUT DON'T SLEEP ON IT.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyborn_altar.hook: A dragon perch of ancient stone on a high ridge above Labyrinthian, where the old priests offered to their masters. Dragons still land here, as if they remember the way.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyborn_altar.hunte:
Sigrun,
You asked me to write it down so you could stop me telling it at the mine, so here it is. I was on the ridge above the old dragon altar after elk. A shadow went over me bigger than the mine-house. It landed on the altar like it owned it, folded its wings, and looked out over Labyrinthian for the whole of an hour, still as a statue.

Then it spoke. Not to me. To the ruins. One word, and the snow came off every roof in that dead city at once. Then it flew west, toward Eldersblood Peak. I lay in the snow until dark. I have not been elk hunting since. There. Now you can't say I'm lying.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyborn_altar.rumou: Skyborn Altar's a bad place to have a picnic. Dragons sit up there like crows on a fence. My brother saw one there in Hearthfire. He's moved to Whiterun. Says the walls are higher.

place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_pinnacle.h: A spire of rock standing alone in dunes, ringed by stairs that wind to a small platform at the top.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_pinnacle.r: The lone spire of Skyreach has a stair wound around it and a step-off notch at the top. The cult wants a figure to fall, and so does the arena.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_pinnacle.w: HERE THE LAST PANEL STANDS. A figure steps; a figure falls; a figure walks on. The stone does not say which. The valley's carving is a forecast, not a command. Stand where the panel stands and choose, and let the stone be surprised.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_temple.hoo: A wind-scoured temple at the edge of the Elinhir cliffs, its columns pitted by sand and its altar kept swept by a hermit nobody has seen.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_temple.rum: Every dawn the Skyreach Temple altar is found clean, though no one comes. The Elinhir priests say a sword-singer keeps it. The sword-singer, if he exists, has never once been thanked.
place_lore.nirncraft.skyreach_temple.sky:
^I sweep the temple that nobody visits
For a god who does not ask to be swept.
The sand returns each night, a patient pilgrim,
And each dawn I send it on its way.

^If you find this, do not wait for me.
The broom is by the door. The water is in the jar.
If you stay long enough, you will begin to sweep.
It is not a punishment. It is the only prayer that I know.
place_lore.nirncraft.skytemple_ruins.dar:
#Fredas night
The wager is simple: one night in the Skytemple Ruins, and Onmund owes me a week's worth of soul gems. I have a candle, a blanket and a flask of Colovian brandy for courage. The brandy is mostly gone.

#Later
There is a voice in the old stones. It does not speak Dunmeris or Tamrielic. It speaks the language the Nords cut on their walls. It is saying the same three words over and over, and the words are getting louder.

#Later
I have dropped my focus crystal down the inner stair, the one with my master's sigil on it. Without it I am a Dunmer with a candle. I am going down to fetch it. If I don't come back, tell Onmund the wager is void.
place_lore.nirncraft.skytemple_ruins.hoo: A Nordic temple to the sky on a crag north of the College, older than the Collapse and older than the College. Apprentices dare each other to spend a night in it.
place_lore.nirncraft.skytemple_ruins.rum: The Skytemple Ruins? Students go up there on a dare. Most come back. The ones who do won't say what they heard.
place_lore.nirncraft.skytemple_ruins.sk4: Folio #6 (1586, -2046): Field inspection recorded for Skytemple Ruins within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #6 for skytemple_ruins: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Skytemple Ruins are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.skytemple_ruins.sky:
^Copied by a careful hand from the lintel stones
Here the sons of Ysgramor lifted their eyes. Here the wind was a priest and the storm a choir. Whoever stands here in the gale stands nearer to Kyne than to the earth.
Let no one bring fire into this house but the lightning.

^Added below in College ink
The last line was clearly meant literally. Scorch marks on the inner altar are consistent with repeated lightning strikes, though the altar is sheltered from the sky. Recommend no further overnight stays by novices until this is understood. (Recommendation ignored, as usual.)
place_lore.nirncraft.skywatch.hook: A hill-city of blue-white stone crowned by a vast ring-orrery, with concentric ring-walks, a star-chart terrace and observatories on every ring.
place_lore.nirncraft.skywatch.ring_log.p:
#Fifty-ninth year
I am told the heavens move. I have swept the same ring for sixty years and I have noticed only that the dust is the same colour. If the heavens move, they do it when I am looking at the broom.
I once saw a very small light on the south edge of the sky, from the outer ring, past midnight. I told no one. It is not my department. But I think it is moving, and I think it knows my name.
place_lore.nirncraft.skywatch.rumour: Skywatch has more clocks than people, and the clocks disagree on purpose. The city keeps a hundred times, and picks the one that is least wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.sleeping_tree_altar: A sunken stone basin at the edge of the purple-leaved bog where sap-collectors leave offerings before tapping the ancient trunk.
Alchemists in Whiterun pay good gold for a phial from the Sleeping Tree Altar, provided the giants don't flatten you first.

Folio #47 (-1420, -320): Field inspection recorded for Sleeping Tree Altar within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #47 for sleeping_tree_altar: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Sleeping Tree Altar are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Drive the brass spigot only into the lower root-buttress beside the stone basin, never into the main trunk where the giant paints his swirl-marks. One flask of violet sap is enough to make a winter's profit if you walk away quietly.
A giant camp in the western Tundra, gathered around an ancient tree that weeps a drowsy golden sap. Alchemists pay well for the sap, if the giants let anyone near enough to tap it.
The giants at Sleeping Tree drink the sap and snore for days. Arcadia in Whiterun pays good money for a flask. Just don't wake them. Gods, don't wake them.

The sap of the great tree west of Whiterun is unlike any resin I know. A drop on the tongue brings visions and a deep, dreamless sleep. The giants drink it in the evening, and in the morning they are calm as lambs.

I have a buyer in Solitude who will pay three hundred septims for a full flask. I am too old to crawl past a sleeping giant, and too honest to send a child. If an adventurer with quiet feet brings me a flask, I will split the price fairly.

Approach from the south, downwind. The giants sleep hardest just after the sun goes down. Take only what you need. The tree does not like greed.

Addendum #40 for sleeping_tree_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Sleeping Tree Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.sload_spawning_pool:
#Dive forty-one
Down to the fourth pool. The coral is the colour of a bruise. It sings. I have never heard coral sing before. I have a wax in my ears. It does not help. I am humming, and I do not know the tune.

Dive forty-two. I have been humming the tune for a month. It is the tune of a drowned bell. I think the heart is calling for me. I think it is lonely. I think I am the only one who can hear it, and I am not sure I want to be.
A sprawl of warm, sluggish pools in the Thrassian reefs where the Sload breed their strange young, and where a plague-diver goes in at dawn and comes out, sometimes, at dusk.
The pools are never still. At night they glow a very faint green. The Sload say it is the young, dreaming. The plague-divers say it is the dreaming that is the problem.
place_lore.nirncraft.snapleg_cave.hagrav:
To make a calling-horn:
Take the horn of a man who hunted. Take his breath, the last one, in a bladder. Blow the breath through the horn under no moon. Those who knew the man will hear him calling and come.

Already come: the hunter's brother, the hunter's friend, a stupid boy who thought it was his father.
Still to come: the hunter's woman at the Crossing. She is strong. Her heart will be strong. It will make a fine charm.
When she is here, burn the horn. Waste is a sin, but greed is a worse one.
place_lore.nirncraft.snapleg_cave.hook: A hagraven's den in the gorge below Darkwater Pass, where a missing hunter's horn sounds at night, calling his friends in one by one.
place_lore.nirncraft.snapleg_cave.orgnar:
Haldis,
I am writing this on the back of the mine bill you gave me to pay, which I never paid, so you will not be surprised at this, at least.
The witch has my horn. She blows it with something that is not my breath and calls out with something that is not my voice. If you hear me in the hills, it is not me. Stay at the Crossing.
I know you will not stay at the Crossing. So bring someone better with a blade than I was.
place_lore.nirncraft.snapleg_cave.rumour: There's a horn blowing at night down by Snapleg Cave, and it's Orgnar's horn. Orgnar's been dead a month. Don't you dare go and answer it.
place_lore.nirncraft.snapleg_cave.sk4_no: Folio #2 (1531, 762): Field inspection recorded for Snapleg Cave within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #2 for snapleg_cave: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Snapleg Cave are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_shod_farm.chil:
I saw a bird lady at the bottom field. She had feathers in her hair and a face like a dry apple. She said if I brought her a lock of Mama's hair she would make the bad men go away.

She lives in the tall tower behind the hills, the dark one. I did not give her anything. I am writing it down so I remember not to.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_shod_farm.farm:
Snow-Shod,
Forty septims by the end of Frostfall. You know whose forty. We've been patient because the Lady is patient, and the Lady is patient because she likes to see a thing grow before she takes it.

Your barn is very dry this time of year. Your children play very near the barn. Nobody wants to be clumsy with a lantern.

Below, in a woman's careful hand: Asgeir, I counted again. Twenty-six. If we sell the mare, thirty-four. We could ask at Goldenglow; they buy honey-wax. Don't go to the Knives. I know you're thinking it. Don't.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_shod_farm.hook: A Nord farm south of Riften that grows more cabbages than sense and owes the Black-Briars more than it can pay. The family has started sleeping with axes by the bed.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_shod_farm.rumo: The Snow-Shods are behind on their Black-Briar debt. Heard Maven's men came round twice already. The third time, they bring a torch.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_shod_farm.sk4_: Folio #8 (2316, 1606): Field inspection recorded for Snow Shod Farm within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.
