place_lore.nirncraft.snow_veil_sanctum.h: A sealed Nordic sanctum in the hills south of the Winterhold coast. Its doors were opened recently, and the draugr inside are no longer the only ones who know its halls.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_veil_sanctum.p:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
Here lie the priests who kept the snow-veil drawn across the face of the dead, that no light might trouble them and no thief might find them.

The veil is a wall of words. Speak the wrong word, and the veil becomes a shroud for the speaker. Speak the right word, and the priests will rise to greet you, which is worse.
^Scratched below: the translator recommends speaking no words at all.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_veil_sanctum.r: Snow Veil Sanctum. Someone's been in there lately, a city type, soft boots. Whatever he wanted, he got it, and he left the dead awake behind him.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_veil_sanctum.s: Folio #22 (1992, -1255): Field inspection recorded for Snow Veil Sanctum within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #22 for snow_veil_sanctum: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Snow Veil Sanctum are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.snow_veil_sanctum.t: Got as far as the second hall. The puzzle doors are Nordic and the Nords never met a riddle they couldn't make lethal. Saw tracks of somebody who got here before me: fine boots, light step, knew exactly where to put his feet.

Whoever he was, he went straight through, took what he wanted from the inner chamber, and left the rest. I'm not that good. I'm going back to Riften before something in a funeral mask decides I'm the next thing it wants to keep.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowclad_ruins.hook: Broken Nordic stones half-buried in snow above the Moesring Pass, crowned by a word wall that hums when the wind blows from the north. Scholars come here. Some stay longer than they meant to.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowclad_ruins.rumo: There's writing on the old wall at Snowclad Ruins that only dragons can read. A scholar from the mainland sat in front of it for a week trying. Got frostbite and a headache for his trouble.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowclad_ruins.scho:
Esteemed colleague,
I write from the Snowclad Ruins with three working fingers. The wall here bears a Word in the dragon tongue, which I have copied, and which I believe concerns ice, or the becoming of ice. I have not been able to speak it aloud. I suspect I am meant to be unable.

One further observation, which I set down at the risk of your ridicule: the snow here does not drift against the wall. It drifts around it, in a perfect ring, as if the wall were warm. It is not warm. I touched it. I am still waking at night with the shape of the letters in my palm. Yours, in some distress, Aurelian.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowclad_ruins.skaa: Tied to a chime of horker bones on the ruin's arch: Skaal walk around this place, not through it. The wall speaks to dragons, and dragons answer. If the chimes are ringing and there is no wind, walk faster.

On the other side of the bark, a fainter line: The scholar from the mainland did not walk faster. He sat down by the wall and stayed there all night with his eyes open, saying a word over and over. We carried him to Raven Rock. He still says it in his sleep, and the candle flames bend when he does.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowpoint_beacon.be:
To the Commander, Fort Dunstad.
The beacon is in order. The pitch is dry. The signal horn is cleaned and hung by the brazier. If a raider so much as sneezes off the coast, you will know of it by the evening bell.

Note: the wind has been odd. On still nights there is a cold that moves about the tower by itself, like a person pacing. Old Ulf says it is a wraith out of the ice. Old Ulf says a great many things. We will keep the fire going and see.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowpoint_beacon.ho: A crumbling signal tower in the snow between Winterhold and the Pale. Its beacon once passed warnings from the coast to Fort Dunstad; now the wind has a voice there.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowpoint_beacon.ru: Snowpoint Beacon used to burn when raiders came in from the sea. Nobody's lit it in twenty years. Something up there doesn't want it lit.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowpoint_beacon.sk: Folio #24 (538, -1239): Field inspection recorded for Snowpoint Beacon within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #24 for snowpoint_beacon: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Snowpoint Beacon are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.snowpoint_beacon.ul:
Fire went out by itself. Hrongar went to relight it and the cold came down the stair and wrapped him like a cloak. He is still standing at the top. He is still standing there. I cannot look at him.
Whoever lights this beacon again, light it fast and do not look at the faces in the frost.

I am going down to Fort Dunstad to tell them. They will laugh at me. Let them laugh. Twenty years the beacon has burned without fail and tonight it went out by itself, and a good man is standing on the stair with frost in his open eyes.
Ulf, watchman, the 9th of Evening Star
place_lore.nirncraft.soft_scale_clearing: A clearing of pale sand and leaning stones beyond Helstrom, in whose middle sits a single hand of baked clay, palm up.

#Mine
This wall was mine. I was halfway up the second course when the ground went. If you are laying stones here, mind the line, mind the mortar, and set one more for me. I never finished. It is a small request.
Mason Noo's mortar sets in the shape of a hand, whatever mould he uses. It came from the old quarry sand beyond Helstrom, where a mason once fell and was never found.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude.bard_lette:
Dearest Mama,
Solitude is everything they promised and colder. Our masters say the Jarl will not hear any song with Ulfric's name in it, even if he is the villain, so half the old ballads have been rewritten in a week. Viarmo says it is a lesson in tact. I say it is a lesson in cowardice, but quietly.

The Thalmor came to the Blue Palace on Fredas. Tall, golden, and they do not blink enough. One of them asked me to sing something from the Summerset Isles and corrected my vowels.
I have not been sleeping well. There is a draught in the dormitory that sounds like a woman laughing. The older girls say it is the Wolf Queen and that I should keep a candle lit. I have spent four septims on candles. Please send money. And socks.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude.company_no: Aulus Carvain, Senior Clerk, Solitude Office

^TO ALL MASTERS, MATES AND HONEST MEN OF THE HARBOUR
On the nights of the 3rd, 4th and 9th of Frostfall, the lamp of the Solitude Lighthouse was seen to be dark. On the 9th the cutter Silver Gull struck the shoals north of the Dainty Sload and lost her whole cargo of Cyrodilic wine.

The keeper has not answered the Company's letters. The Company offers fifty septims for any true account of who darkens that lamp, and a further two hundred for the return of the Gull's cargo or the heads of those who took it. Apply at the warehouse office. Do not apply drunk. Do not apply as a joke, Hrolfdir.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude.headsman_l:
#Castle Dour, accounts of the year 4E 201
Rope, hemp, three lengths: 9 septims.
Block, oak, replacing old block split in Sun's Dawn: 22 septims.
Whetstone: 2 septims.
Fee, the traitor from Dragon Bridge: 20 septims.
Fee, the deserter from Fort Hraggstad, pardoned at the steps: 0 septims. Note to the steward: I was promised payment for attendance regardless.

Fee, the smuggler from the Broken Oar crew: 20 septims. He spat at the priest and laughed at me. Said his captain would buy the rope back and hang me with it.
New hood, black wool: 6 septims. The old one was recognised at the Winking Skeever. A man should be able to drink in peace.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude.hook: The Imperial capital of Skyrim, perched on its great stone arch above the Karth. Its docks feed the East Empire Company, its palace mourns a murdered king, and the Thalmor dine at its table.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude.rumour: Solitude's never been busier, or quieter. Ships in the harbour, Legion on the walls, Thalmor in the Blue Palace, and every one of them listening to what you say over your mead.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude_lighthouse: The lighthouse on the rocks north of Solitude has guided ships through the Karth's mouth for generations. This season its lamp keeps going dark, and ships keep dying.

#2nd of Frostfall
Wind from the north. Lamp trimmed, oil at half. Saw lights at Brinewater Grotto again, three short, one long. Not fishermen. Fishermen don't signal.

#4th of Frostfall
Woke on the floor with my head split open and the lamp dark. Somebody was up here. The great brass lens is gone from its cradle. Without it the flame is a candle in a gale.
#5th of Frostfall
I've hung a lantern on the gallery, but it won't reach the shoals. I'm writing to the Company. If they don't answer, I'll row to that grotto myself and ask the wreckers for my lens back. Politely, with a hammer.

#9th of Frostfall
A cutter went onto the rocks tonight. I heard them calling. I could do nothing. I am going to Brinewater in the morning. If this log is found and I am not, the lens is there. Tell the Company.
Old Ulfgar keeps the lighthouse. Kept it. Nobody's seen him in town since the lamp started going out, and his boat's still tied up at the rocks.

Old man,
Fifty septims a night, and all you need do is sleep. On the nights we choose, you trim no wick and see no ships. Leave the lamp dark and the coin will be under this same stone in the morning, regular as tide.

Refuse and we'll take the choice out of your hands. We know you live alone. We know your boat. We know the stair is steep and an old man can fall.
Answer by leaving a white rag on the gallery rail. Do not answer by going to the Company. Their clerks are cheaper than you are, and some of them are already ours.
Brinewater
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude_sawmill.fo:
Planks for the East Empire Company, 300 lengths, delivered to Solitude docks. Paid.
Palisade stakes for Fort Hraggstad, 120. Paid half. Legion says the other half 'in due course'. I have heard that before.
Coffin boards for the Hall of the Dead, 40. Paid in full and in advance. Nobody ever argues about coffins.

Men are refusing the northern stands past Steepfall. Two trolls seen by the burrows, one with a white back. Lost an axe and nearly lost Gunnar. I am told the Legion will deal with it in due course.
Do not let the boys cut the old pine at Clearpine Pond. The fisherman who camps there says it is bad luck, and I have enough bad luck already.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude_sawmill.ho: A busy mill on the Karth below Solitude, cutting pine for Imperial ships, Legion palisades and the coffins of a long war.
place_lore.nirncraft.solitude_sawmill.ru: The sawmill's taken on so many Legion orders the foreman sleeps by the blade. Says if the Stormcloaks want Solitude, they'll have to come through his lumber first.
place_lore.nirncraft.soljunds_sinkhole.f:
LOWER GALLERY IS SHUT.
It was shut by Soljund himself and it stays shut. If you hear knocking from the other side, that is not a trapped miner. Our miners all come home at sundown, we count them.
If the count is short, we go to the lower gallery with torches and six men. Never one. Never two. Six.

^Added in a different hand:
Count was short on Tirdas. We went with six. We came back with five, and the bar was on the other side of the door.
place_lore.nirncraft.soljunds_sinkhole.h: A moonstone mine cut into a sinkhole in the Reach hills. The miners dug too deep once, and they still bar the lowest gallery with oak and iron every night.
place_lore.nirncraft.soljunds_sinkhole.m:
#Shipment of the 14th, Last Seed
Moonstone ore, 30 pieces, bound for the smelter at Markarth by the river road.
Escort: two hired swords from Dragon Bridge.
#Remarks
Cart found overturned near Liar's Retreat. Both escorts gone. No blood. Moonstone gone. Escorts paid in advance, which Pa told me never to do. Next time I listen to Pa.

#Postscript
Asked the Stormcloak patrol on the river road if they saw anything. They said they were 'busy with the war'. One of them had a moonstone pin on his cloak. Raw moonstone, uncut, the kind we dig. I did not ask where he got it. I am a clerk, not a fool.
place_lore.nirncraft.soljunds_sinkhole.r: The Soljund's Sinkhole moonstone shipment got lifted on the road again. Bandits holed up in Liar's Retreat, if you believe the miners. And I do.
place_lore.nirncraft.soljunds_sinkhole.s: Folio #5 (-2180, -217): Field inspection recorded for Soljunds Sinkhole within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.sorel_crypt.hook: At place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the chalk horse-downs and lock-channels of the Bjoulsae River valley from Evermor to Bhoriane, guarded by the Order of the Wheel.
place_lore.nirncraft.sorel_crypt.rumour: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt report signs of Winterborn Reach briar-hearts, river-lock saboteurs, and island-crypt undead operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.sorel_crypt.v8_lore:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

Survey Entry — place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt

Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the chalk horse-downs and lock-channels of the Bjoulsae River valley from Evermor to Bhoriane, guarded by the Order of the Wheel. For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.sorel_crypt have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by Winterborn Reach briar-hearts, river-lock saboteurs, and island-crypt undead. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

place_lore.nirncraft.soul_cairn_portal.h: A sunken stone rotunda and arcane stair hidden in the sea-cliffs where cold violet light seeps through a fracture between worlds.
place_lore.nirncraft.soul_cairn_portal.r: Sailors rowing past the northern sea-caves say a purple mist leaks out of the cliffside ruin and turns the surf dead calm.
place_lore.nirncraft.soul_cairn_portal.w: The geometry of the basin requires exact proportions of ground bone, void salts, and purified soul-shards before the lower steps will align. Even with the seal dormant, a freezing draft pulls inward toward the focal ring, carrying the sound of distant thunder.
#The living
Barge-Mother Seeth carries the dead to the isle and is paid in lilies. Lily-Tender Pi keeps the beds: white for the quiet, red for the angry, and if one blooms black she stops. Priest Eesh tells the dead where they are; it is astonishing how few know. Gaar the Lantern-Seller sells waterproof, windproof and argument-proof lamps.

#One bed that will not bloom
The Teeb bed has been bare three years. The family keeps a lantern lit in the window for a daughter who went into the marsh. They will not bury what they have not lost.
place_lore.nirncraft.soulrest.hook: A necropolis-town on a black lagoon, stilt-houses divided by narrow canals and white lily-beds, where the dead go by barge and the living speak softly.
place_lore.nirncraft.soulrest.rumour: The Barge-Mother of Soulrest carries one dead a night to the Isle of Tombs, and tonight her oar-arm will not hold. She wants a steady stranger, a good song, and a blade.
place_lore.nirncraft.south_brittleshin_p: The southern mouth of Brittleshin Pass, opening onto the slopes above Lake Ilinalta. Skeevers swarm the tunnels, and someone has been trapping them for coin.
The skeever trapper who works Brittleshin Pass sells tails to the mill for coppers. Brave man or mad. Both, likely.

Snorri,
You said forty skeevers by Sun's Dawn and I have counted twenty-two tails, three of which I am fairly sure are the same tail cut in pieces. I am not paying for the same skeever three times.
The grain loft at the mill is still full of them. Come back to Half-Moon Mill when you have the rest, and bring the real tails, and I will pay what I promised plus a loaf for your trouble. Do not bring me any more alive in a sack. I am still finding the one that got out.
place_lore.nirncraft.south_cold_rock_pas: The southern mouth of Cold Rock Pass, where the road drops toward the barrow of Rannveig's Fast. Old waymarkers here are carved with warnings no one bothers to read.
There's a barrow past the south end of Cold Rock Pass. The Greybeards send pilgrims there, they say. Brave pilgrims, or stupid ones.

Folio #16 (-1068, -627): Field inspection recorded for South Cold Rock Pass within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #16 for south_cold_rock_pass: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing South Cold Rock Pass are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

^SOUTH: RANNVEIG'S FAST
^NORTH: THE COLD ROCK
^EAST: THE SLOW ROAD TO WHITERUN

Under the old lettering, someone has added with a knife: 'The south road goes to the barrow and nowhere else. If a man tells you there is an inn down there, he wants your boots.'

Lower, worn almost smooth: 'Rannveig kept her fast here. She would not eat until the dead were quiet. They are not quiet yet.'

The rest has been scraped away by ice and time.
place_lore.nirncraft.south_shriekwind_ba:
Sister Hilde,
I know you said the barrow is not safe and that Runil would give Rorik a fine plot in the town yard. But Rorik's line has lain in South Shriekwind since the brothers were buried, and he made me swear on our wedding day that he would lie with them. A promise is a promise, even to ashes.

I am taking the urn up myself. The alcove is the seventh on the left in the long hall, his grandfather showed it to him as a boy. If I am not back by Fredas, please do not send anyone after me. Only light a candle. Asta.

Carved on the great sarcophagus at the barrow's heart, the runes sharp despite their age:
'Eyvind, who was cleverer than his brother and less fortunate. He sleeps facing north so that he may see Hjalti coming. Let no one turn him.'
Someone, long ago, has scratched a crude torc beside the words, and then scratched it out.

Lower down, half hidden by dust, a second carving in the same style: 'If Hjalti comes, let Eyvind be woken. He will not be pleased to see his brother, but he will be ready.' The sarcophagus lid has shifted, very slightly, toward the north.

A list copied from the alcoves of the long hall by some patient visitor:
First left: Ulfa. Second left: Ulfa's son, name worn. Third: Brand the Steady. Fourth: empty. Fifth: Gisli Rorikson. Sixth: Rorik the Elder. Seventh: empty, swept clean, awaiting.
Underneath: 'The seventh is waiting for someone. The family says it is always waiting for someone.'

Beneath the list, in fresh charcoal, a woman's careful hand: 'Seventh left. Rorik, son of Rorik, laid here by his wife Asta in the year 4E 201. He wanted to come home. Now he is home.' The charcoal is smudged at the end, as if the writer was crying, or bleeding.
The southern Shriekwind barrow, nearest to Falkreath, where a grieving widow went to lay her husband's ashes among his ancestors. The draugr were not expecting a visitor.
Asta took her Rorik's ashes up to South Shriekwind, where his family's buried since before Falkreath had a name. That was five days ago. Sister Hilde's beside herself.
place_lore.nirncraft.south_skybound_watc: A Nordic watchtower on the ridge north of Helgen, overlooking the burned town. Looters have made it their storehouse.

From Helgen:
2 swords, Legion, melted at the tip. Sell to Falkreath smith.
1 barrel mead (Inn). Mostly drunk.
6 candlesticks (temple?). Silver. KEEP.
Cloak, blue, Stormcloak cut. Burned. Wear anyway.
Still to fetch: smith's strongbox by the north gate. Too heavy for one. Wait for Arne.
Patrol came by the ruins on Loredas. Legion, six of them. One looked right at the tower. Arne says they won't climb up for a few candlesticks. Arne is an idiot but he may be right.

Scratched low on the tower wall, as if by someone sitting:
'Hid here night of the dragon. Saw it go over the tower, black as a burned field. It roared and the sky split. Helgen gone. If anyone from the inn lived, I am going to Riverwood. Signed, Lofa the cook.'

Beneath, in charcoal, a different hand: 'Lofa made it to Riverwood. She cooks at the Sleeping Giant now. Torolf the smith's girl Ylva made it too. If you are from Helgen and reading this, there are people waiting for you. Go to them.'
Folk picking over Helgen's bones carry the loot up to South Skybound Watch. If you've lost something in the fire, that's where it went.

place_lore.nirncraft.south_wall_cornercl: A cornerclub with rules for singing and rules for cheating, and a bard who keeps both books.

#No singing before sundown
No cheating after. Everything between is a negotiation, and a negotiation may be settled by song, so long as it is sundown. If it is not sundown, the song is a bribe, and the bribe is a crime, and the crime is payable in beer.

Strangers may be rude only once. After that they are regulars.
The South Wall Cornerclub keeps two sets of rules: the ones on the wall, and the ones in Dathan Selvil's head. Only one set is ever enforced, and it is never the written one.
place_lore.nirncraft.southfringe_sanctum:
The old altar at the heart of the sanctum still bears its blessing, carved by Arkay's priests long ago:
'Here the dead rest in the circle of birth and death, and none shall break it.'
Across the words someone has daubed, in dark paint: 'Circles are made to be broken.' The paint is flaking. The carving underneath is not.

At the foot of the altar, scratched into the stone floor in a child's uneven letters: SIGRID. And beside it, smaller, in an adult's neat hand: 'I am sorry. - H.' Somebody has left a dried flower on the name, the only clean thing in the room.

#Sun's Dusk
Mistress Velmira has me mending the bindings on the little one. She keeps walking north toward Falkreath. I asked the Mistress why we do not let her go, since she is so small and so much trouble. The Mistress looked at me for a long while and I have not asked anything since.

#Later
I found the little one's name scratched on the wall of her alcove, in her own hand, I think, from before. Sigrid. I have started calling her that. She stopped walking north for a whole day. If the Mistress finds out I will be in the kitchen with the widow.
A necromancers' refuge dug into the hills at the southern edge of Falkreath, where the stolen dead of the town graveyard are put to work in the dark.

Received from the Falkreath yard, by the Lantern-Bearer:
Hrofar, tanner. Strong hands. To the digging.
Asgerd, widow. Obedient. To the kitchen.
The cooper's child. Small. To the narrow galleries. Restless. Rebind weekly.

Remarks: the yard is the finest source in Skyrim. The dead of Falkreath are many and their families visit seldom. With forty more I can finish opening the lower vault, and what lies under it was old when Arkay was new. I do not intend to share it with the cell in the Reach. Corvus is not to know of this page.
Southfringe Sanctum. Old shrine to Arkay, they say, gone wrong. If the gravedigger's dead have walked anywhere, it's down there, digging for someone new.
place_lore.nirncraft.southfringe_stead.h: An isolated mountain steading tucked beneath the southern peaks where goat-herders watch the high snow-passes toward Cyrodiil.
place_lore.nirncraft.southfringe_stead.r: Herders at Southfringe Stead say smoke and strange chanting drift down from the sanctum cave whenever the mountain fog rolls in.

place_lore.nirncraft.southfringe_stead.w: Brought the goats down from the upper scree before the early frost could crust the lichen. Twice this week we saw blue torchlight flickering near the mouth of Southfringe Sanctum, and three of our bell-wethers vanished near the ice-bridge leading toward Bloodlet Throne.

place_lore.nirncraft.sren_ja.feud_petiti:
#To the Reeve of Sren Ja
I have swept the plank every dawn for six years and my neighbour has swept it every dawn for the same, and neither of us has ever walked on it. I do not know why we sweep it. I would like to stop. But if I stop, he wins. Please advise.
In the margin, in a stern hand: 'The Reeve advises that you may both stop. The Reeve has also been sweeping this plank for six years, from below.'
place_lore.nirncraft.sren_ja.hook: A treehouse hamlet where two families have feuded for six years over a single shared bridge-plank, each sweeping it every dawn from opposite ends.
place_lore.nirncraft.sren_ja.rumour: The plank of Sren Ja is the cleanest piece of timber in Valenwood and the most hotly disputed. It has never been replaced, because neither side will agree to let the other buy the new one.

place_lore.nirncraft.stalhrim_source.hoo: A seam of stalhrim, the deathless blue ice of Solstheim, breaking the surface of the snowfield. The Skaal guard its secret; smugglers guard their caches nearby.
place_lore.nirncraft.stalhrim_source.rum: There's a place where the black ice comes right up out of the snow, below Mortrag Peak. Smugglers bury what they cut and come back for it in spring. Most of them come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.stalhrim_source.ska: In the Skaal runes, with a hand pressed flat beneath them: This ice is the All-Maker's memory. Cut it with thanks, and it will cut for you. Cut it with greed, and it will remember you. We have cut here for a hundred winters and taken only what we needed. The ice keeps count. The ice keeps count of you too, stranger.

Lower, in the trade-tongue of Raven Rock, scratched in by somebody else entirely: We tried. Three of us, one winter. Two came home. The one who did not come home was the one who laughed at this stone. I am writing this here so that the next one who laughs reads it first.
place_lore.nirncraft.star_haven_adeptori: A tiny academy under a stone dome in the dunes, where three cubs and one tutor map the stars, and one star-chart has gone missing from the lectern.

#TONIGHT
Masser, big and fat. Secunda, thin and cross. Somewhere low on the south there is a very dim thing that Zhazir says is nothing, in a voice that says it is not nothing. I have drawn it, in pencil, and rubbed it out, and drawn it again.
The adeptorium is so small that the stars outnumber the students. Zhazir says this is the correct ratio.
A colossal statue of the Psijic archmage Syrabane standing on the strait before Artaeum, one hand raised in a gesture that is either a blessing or a warning.

^SYRABANE STANDS BETWEEN THE ISLE AND THE WORLD.
^HE DOES NOT KEEP YOU OUT. HE ASKS WHETHER YOU WISH TO COME IN.
^ANSWER HONESTLY. THE SEA IS LISTENING.
Carved beneath, very small: 'If the answer is yes, bring a lantern. If the answer is no, bring two.'
The statue's hand was lowered once, a thousand years ago, and the whole island vanished from the charts until it was raised again. Nobody now touches the hand. Nobody even points.
place_lore.nirncraft.statue_to_meridia.h: A great statue of Meridia on the peak of Mount Kilkreath, holding a star that burns even at night. Pilgrims climb to it to pray against the dead; lately the dead have been climbing too.
place_lore.nirncraft.statue_to_meridia.p:
#16th of Frostfall
Climbed with my lantern before dawn. At the top the light from the Lady's star fell on me and for the first time since my husband's barrow was robbed I did not see his face rotting. I wept like a girl.

#18th of Frostfall
There were men in robes at the foot of the mountain, coming up the path from the direction of Wolfskull Cave. They had skeletons carrying their packs. They set something down by the steps, a bundle of bones bound with black cord, and laughed, and went away.
The Lady's light dims where the bundle lies. I am too afraid to touch it. I am leaving my lantern by the plinth so someone braver will know where to look.

~Lady of the Infinite Energies,
~you who hate the stolen breath
~and the corpse that walks against its will,
~burn us clean and send us home.

~What is dead, let it lie.
~What is living, let it shine.
~What lies between, let your light decide.
^Cut by grateful pilgrims of Haafingar. Do not leave the dead at this stone.

^Added in charcoal on the plinth's side:
Someone has left the dead at this stone. A bundle of bones and black cord lies by the lowest step, and the star burns dimmer over it every night. I have prayed beside it for three days. The Lady does not answer prayers. She answers deeds. Whoever reads this, do the deed.
place_lore.nirncraft.statue_to_meridia.r: My aunt climbed to Meridia's statue to pray away the bad dreams. She says there were bones on the steps that hadn't been there the week before. Fresh bones, with the green fire still on them.
A merchant's stilt mansion in the Stormhold marsh with a boat-shed, a bright awning and a lantern-lit veranda.
The merchant at Stay-Moist has more sap than a thousand trees could give, and he sells it by the cask to the Imperials.

Casks tapped: 214 this season. Sold to the Imperial pharmacists: 198. Retained for private use: 12. Spoiled: 4. The Root yields well to a determined hand. If the Hist-folk complain, remind them that a tree is not a person. I have never believed in it, but I wouldn't say it aloud in the hearing of the Root.
place_lore.nirncraft.steamcrag_camp.herd:
Father,
I am sorry I ran. I am sorry I ran from the pond and left Sigrun, and I am sorry I have not come home since. I am living rough near the Steamcrag springs. The giants tolerate me so long as I do not touch the water or the mammoths.
One of them, an old female with a broken tusk necklace, leaves bones by my fire sometimes, picked clean. I think she is feeding me. I think she thinks I am a stray.
Tell Sigrun's mother at Mixwater that I am going back for her daughter when I am brave enough. Tell her I am almost brave enough.
place_lore.nirncraft.steamcrag_camp.hook: A giants' camp among the steaming pools south of Kynesgrove, where the herds of mammoths wallow in warm water and the giants guard the springs as fiercely as any jarl guards a hall.
place_lore.nirncraft.steamcrag_camp.rumo: The Steamcrag giants let mammoths bathe in the hot pools all winter. Kynesgrove herders say a mammoth that's had its bath is the happiest creature in Skyrim. Don't test that.
place_lore.nirncraft.steamcrag_camp.sk4_: Folio #22 (1961, 40): Field inspection recorded for Steamcrag Camp within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #22 for steamcrag_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Steamcrag Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.steamcrag_camp.spri: Observed at the Steamcrag springs over nine days: the giants bathe in strict order, eldest first, mammoths last. A juvenile who broke the order was struck once, gently, and sat apart for the rest of the day. No sound was made by any party.

When a mammoth calf was taken by a sabre cat, the clan carried the calf's body to the hottest pool and left it there. They watched it until the steam hid it. I have seen Nord funerals with less ceremony and more noise.
I conclude that the giants are not savage, merely private. I further conclude that I am never coming back here.
place_lore.nirncraft.steepfall_burrow.ho: A cold den carved into the cliffs above the Sea of Ghosts, where sabre cats drag their kills. The bones of Legion scouts lie among the elk.
place_lore.nirncraft.steepfall_burrow.ru: The upper burrow at Steepfall belongs to the cats. The lower one belongs to the trolls. And the whole hill belongs to nobody who wants to live.
place_lore.nirncraft.steepfall_burrow.sc:
Commander,
Surveyed the Steepfall burrows as ordered. The upper den holds two sabre cats, one with cubs. The lower burrow holds trolls, at least one very large. Both openings command the old coastal path that runs north to Northwatch Keep.

My recommendation: do not use the coastal path. My second recommendation: do not let the Thalmor use it either. Their couriers ride it twice a week to Northwatch, and the cats have already taken one. I saw the gold trim of his cloak in the den. I did not go in for it.
I am writing this from a tree. I will come down when the cat finishes eating.
place_lore.nirncraft.steepfall_burrow.th:
To the Commander of Northwatch Keep, from the Embassy.
The prisoner Hjorvar is to be kept apart from the Gray-Mane boy and the other Nords. He preaches. He preached to the guards on the road. Two of them are now under review.

Continue interrogation regarding the remaining members of the Ironback assembly. Exhaust what he knows; then exhaust him. The Dominion requires no confession. It requires names.
The courier carrying this pouch is to take the coastal path past Steepfall. It is quicker, and the Legion does not patrol it. Report any delay to the Third Emissary in person.
place_lore.nirncraft.stendarrs_beacon.ho: A stone watchtower in the south-eastern hills where the Vigilants of Stendarr once kept a fire burning against the darkness. The fire has gone out, and the Vigilants with it.
place_lore.nirncraft.stendarrs_beacon.ru: The Vigilants' beacon has gone dark. First time in my life. My mother used to say as long as the beacon burns, nothing evil comes down from the hills.
place_lore.nirncraft.stendarrs_beacon.sk: Folio #50 (2811, 1736): Field inspection recorded for Stendarrs Beacon within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #50 for stendarrs_beacon: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Stendarrs Beacon are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.stendarrs_beacon.vi:
~Stendarr, steadfast and merciful,
~where the night grows long, let us be the fire,
~where the dead walk, let us be the wall,
~where the weak cry out, let us be the answer.

Below the carving the hearth is cold, and the ash is old. Someone has drawn a single burning candle in soot on the stone.

The Vigilants of Stendarr kept the beacon lit for longer than anyone in Riften can remember, feeding it with pine and tallow and prayer. Travellers on the southern roads steered by it, and mothers in the farms below told their children that while it burned, nothing from the hills would come for them. Before the hearth the flagstones are scorched, and a long dark smear leads out toward the stair.

#10th of Frostfall
Brother Tolfr has not returned from Darklight Tower. Sister Imra has gone to look for him. The beacon burns. Stendarr keeps us.

#13th of Frostfall
Something came up the hill at moonrise. Skeletons, and behind them a pale man in a fine coat who smiled at the fire like a man smiles at an old enemy. He asked us to put it out. We refused.

#14th of Frostfall
They came at dawn. Only I am left. I have hidden the beacon log in the lower chest. If anyone finds it, relight the fire. Then go to Riften and tell them it was the Redwater man. He told me so himself. He was proud of it.
place_lore.nirncraft.steppe_barrow_pit.h: A collapsed turf barrow on the wind-swept steppe whose sunken roof exposes a circle of ancient burial lintels.
place_lore.nirncraft.steppe_barrow_pit.r: Shepherds on the central plains pen their ewes away from the Steppe Barrow Pit; cold blue lights dance in the shaft after midnight.
place_lore.nirncraft.steppe_barrow_pit.w: We broke through the turf roof expecting bronze armbands and burial urns, only to find a black-robed conjurer already using the lower slab as an altar. Left our shovels by the rope-ladder and ran before the dead stood up.
place_lore.nirncraft.stillborn_cave.asta:
~The wind came white across the ridge,
~And Asta found the cave too late,
~She sang until her voice was ice,
~And ice was all that sang with her.
~Now when the storms come down from the north,
~She walks the cave with empty arms,
~And gathers every cradle-charm
~To rock a child who is not there.

^Set down by a midwife of Winterhold
The song is sung to newborns in this hold, to keep them safe in storms. The old women say Asta will never harm a child, only take what is left for one. The charms we tie at her cave are not for her. They are to remind her that someone else is watching.
place_lore.nirncraft.stillborn_cave.hook: An ice cave in the hills of southern Winterhold with a grim old name. Midwives in the hold still tie charms to the cairn at its mouth, and something inside keeps taking them.
place_lore.nirncraft.stillborn_cave.midw:
Kyne, mother of storms, and Mara, mother of all,
Two hundred years ago a woman named Asta sheltered here in the great storm and lost her child in the dark. Every midwife since has tied a charm to this cairn so that no other mother in Winterhold is left in the dark the same way.

My grandmother's cradle-charm, the one of carved antler with a thread of red wool, has hung here forty years. This Frostfall it was gone, and the tracks led into the cave, frosted over, light and cold as nothing living.
I am too old to go in. Bring it back to the cairn, whoever you are, and every child I deliver this winter will bear your name in my prayers.
place_lore.nirncraft.stillborn_cave.rumo: Stillborn Cave. A woman lost her baby there in a blizzard, long ago. The midwives still leave charms at the cave mouth. Lately the charms have been disappearing.
place_lore.nirncraft.stillborn_cave.sk4_: Folio #27 (1726, -1134): Field inspection recorded for Stillborn Cave within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.stonehill_bluff.far:
Steward,
The giants at Stonehill Bluff have taken three of my cows this month. Not killed. Taken. They are grazing with the mammoths now and look very happy. I have tried asking for them back. A giant looked at me for a long while and then put a rock in my hand, very gently, as if paying.

I have the rock. It is a good rock. It is not three cows. Please advise. I note also that the giants have moved their fire round to the far side of the bluff from the Dwemer tower, and that the mammoths will not graze to the east. When giants are afraid of something, I want to know what.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehill_bluff.hoo: A giant camp on a windy bluff in the east of Hjaalmarch, near the Tower of Mzark. The giants herd mammoths here and keep a fire burning, but always on the side away from the tower.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehill_bluff.rum: Leave the giants at Stonehill Bluff alone and they'll leave you alone. Stray too close to their mammoths and they'll send you home in three directions at once.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehills.hook: A hard little mining village in the stony hills of eastern Hjaalmarch, built around the Rockwallow Mine. Its miners dig deeper every year, and lately they have dug into something old.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehills.mine_led:
Iron ore, Last Seed: 212 measures. Sent to Morthal by cart.
Iron ore, Hearthfire: 140 measures. Tunnel flooded on the east face, two days lost.
Picks replaced: 6. Lamps replaced: 3. Arguments with Bulfrek about pay: 14.

The east tunnel broke into a worked passage on the 2nd of Frostfall. Square stone, brass pipe, still warm. Bulfrek says Dwemer. I say Dwemer metal sells for ten times iron in Solitude. Took five men to Mzinchaleft to see where the passage leads from the other end. Back by the 10th.
The 10th has come and gone.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehills.returned:
THEY CAN'T SEE. THEY DON'T NEED TO.
THEY HEAR YOUR HEART.
THE METAL SPIDERS CLICK BEFORE THEY BITE. THE BLIND MEN DON'T.

Sigrun, I couldn't say it to your face so I'm writing it here. Your brother Knud is still down there. He gave me his token to bring to you. I dropped it running. It's past the first great door, by the brass pillar with the broken arm. I'm sorry. I'm sorry I ran.
I hear the clicking every time I shut my eyes. Don't send anyone down without fire and a lot of it, and don't send Bulfrek, he can't run.
place_lore.nirncraft.stonehills.rumour: Stonehills folk are tough as the rock they dig. But Sigrun's whole crew went down into the old Dwemer ruin at Mzinchaleft after metal, and only one came up. He hasn't spoken since.

place_lore.nirncraft.stony_creek_cave.ho: A bandit cave by a cold creek south of the Eastmarch Imperial Camp, where a Redguard chief has grown fat on the Legion's supply wagons without either army ever catching her.
place_lore.nirncraft.stony_creek_cave.na:
#Frostfall
Taken at the ford: 400 arrows, 12 barrels salt pork, 1 legate's cloak (fur-lined, very fine, my new favourite).
Sold to the Stormcloak picket at Kynesgrove: 300 arrows at 2 septims the dozen. Kept 100. Never sell all your arrows to a man who might be your enemy next week.
Salt pork to the Cragslane boys in exchange for a cask of moon sugar. I do not touch it myself. I sell it to men who cannot stop touching it.
Rule of the cave: we do not kill legionaries unless we must. Dead men's officers come looking. Robbed men's officers only write letters.
place_lore.nirncraft.stony_creek_cave.re: Ma, I said I'd tell you when I found steady work. It's steady. I stand at the ford, wave at the wagons, and when the Imperials stop, the others come out of the rocks. Nobody's been hurt. Mostly.

Nazira says I've a good honest face, and that's worth more than a sword in this trade. I don't know if that's a compliment. I've decided to take it as one.
I'm sending you ten septims with this. Don't ask where it came from. Buy flour, and fix the roof before Sun's Dusk, and don't tell Uncle Bersi I'm south of Mzulft. Burn this.
place_lore.nirncraft.stony_creek_cave.ru: Stony Creek Cave's chief robs the Legion and sells the loot to the Stormcloaks. Both sides want her dead and both sides keep buying. That's a businesswoman.

place_lore.nirncraft.stormhold.envoy_not: Teeba-Enoo, Royal Envoy of the King of Argonia

^By the King's word
All Saxhleel held in debt-service on the lands of any foreigner are free from this day, and the debts are void. Any foreigner who disputes this is invited to dispute it with the Envoy in Stormhold, in person, at dusk.

The Envoy notes that few have accepted this invitation. The Envoy notes that those who did were persuaded. The Envoy wishes all foreigners a pleasant and lawful stay in the King's marsh, and reminds them that the marsh has a very long memory and very many eyes.
place_lore.nirncraft.stormhold.gazetteer:
#People of the stones
Warden Scales-Her-Chains keeps the bridge and the peace between the hills. Stone-Carver Nook carves what is not the stone and refuses to touch the idol. Scout Fast-Eyes sees much and says a tenth. Pebble-Pocket sells rope, hook, oil and boots, and will not sell the gorge.

#Beds and a quiet secret
The Two Hills Rest has a door for each ziggurat and soup on the bridge. Do not drop the bowl. The sleeping idol of the north hill has one eye very slightly open, and the south hill carved it so. The old White Rose prison holds one elder who wishes only to be asked a question.
place_lore.nirncraft.stormhold.hook: An old Imperial walled town sinking slowly into the Black Marsh, where the Shadowscales keep their enclave, the King's envoy signs royal contracts, and Lukiul clerks still keep the Empire's ledgers out of habit.
place_lore.nirncraft.stormhold.lukiul_le:
#Customs, Stormhold Gate, Second Seed
One Khajiit caravan: spices, silk, moon sugar (declared as 'cooking sugar'). Duty assessed: none, as there is no longer any duty. Recorded anyway.
One Imperial missionary of Stendarr: three books, one bell. Asked to see the governor. Told there is no governor. Recorded his disappointment.

Note to myself: my grand-hatchling asks why I keep this book when the Empire is gone. I tell her the Empire is not gone; it is only somewhere else. She tells me that is what the Saxhleel say about the dead. Perhaps the Empire and the dead have more in common than I would like. I will keep the book a little longer.
place_lore.nirncraft.stormhold.rumour: Stormhold's where the King's business is done, when it isn't done in the dark. Mind your manners at the gate and don't ask the Elder anything you don't want answered.
place_lore.nirncraft.stros_mkai.fisherwi:
Mother,
The catch is good and the prices are poor, which is how the gods like it. The Brinewash pirates took another of Captain Noraya's ships last week off the south cove. Now nobody from Taneth will sail here without an escort, and the escorts eat more fish than they guard.

I am sending the girls to you in Sentinel on the next grain boat. It is only until the Forebears deal with the pirates, or the pirates deal with the Forebears. I do not much care which. Tell Grandfather not to teach them any more Yokudan curses. The little one used one on the priest.
place_lore.nirncraft.stros_mkai.guide_ad:
^SEE THE WONDERS OF THE DEEP FOLK!
Hakim, born on this very rock, will lead visitors to the brass doors of the old Dwemer halls in the cliffs. The walk includes lantern, rope, bread, and a short and very moving speech about the treaty. Price negotiable. Bravery not included.

Note: Hakim does not go INSIDE. Hakim has been inside. Hakim's brother went further inside. Hakim does not have a brother any more. Gentlemen of learning who wish to go inside may do so at their own expense, and are asked to settle their bill first.
place_lore.nirncraft.stros_mkai.hook: A rocky island town off the Hammerfell coast, where the old treaty that freed Hammerfell from the Dominion was signed, and where Dwemer ruins and pirate coves are both just a short and dangerous walk away.
place_lore.nirncraft.stros_mkai.rumour: Stros M'Kai's where Hammerfell told the Dominion to go home. Proudest rock in the sea. Mind the pirates on the far side, though. They don't read treaties.

place_lore.nirncraft.sun_egg_ruins.gate_:
^THE NINTH GATE
We built eight stairs for the living and one for the keeper. The keeper holds the gate. The gate holds the knowing. If you carry the key, step lightly and speak plainly. If you carry nothing, turn back.
place_lore.nirncraft.sun_egg_ruins.hook: A broken temple of the Helstrom ring at the top of a stair that ends at the sky, where a sealed gate waits for its keeper's key.
place_lore.nirncraft.sun_egg_ruins.rumou: The ninth stair of the Broken Ring climbs two hundred steps and stops at nothing. The elder says there was a gate once, and a keeper, and something beyond it that was not meant for the sun.
place_lore.nirncraft.sun_fang_sanctum.ho: The Isle of Tombs: a hill of white stone in black water with one open door and one patient candle, where the barge-dead are laid down.
place_lore.nirncraft.sun_fang_sanctum.is:
#To the one who has arrived
You are at the Isle of Tombs. You are not alone. You are not lost. You were carried here by someone who did not want you to go the last mile on your own. Rest. The candle is lit. The lilies on the far bed are for you.
place_lore.nirncraft.sun_fang_sanctum.ru: A funeral barge goes to the Isle of Tombs every night. The priest on the isle says the dead hear everything said to them, even when they say nothing back.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_hills_moun: A great circular burial mound standing on the broken limestone hills between the Reach and the western tundra.
Drovers on the border road use the Sundered Hills Mound as a noon landmark, though their horses always shy at the stone curb.

Folio #101 (-3220, -840): Field inspection recorded for Sundered Hills Mound within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #101 for sundered_hills_mound: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Sundered Hills Mound are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

The curved basalt blocks of this mound must have been quarried leagues away, for all the rock around it is grey Reach limestone. The turf in the center has sunk into a shallow bowl where neither grass nor scrub-pine will grow.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_towers.dou:
#Kept separately from the Silver-Blood books
Sun's Dawn: 40 steel arrowheads to the Towers. Received in kind: one silver cart from the Karthwasten road, contents to be 'recovered' by me and returned to the Silver-Bloods at a finder's fee.
First Seed: 12 steel knives. Received: the Karthwasten payroll, likewise recovered.

So the Forsworn get steel, the miners get robbed, and I get a reward for finding what I paid to have stolen. Thonar must never see this book. He would not object to the scheme. He would object that I did not cut him in.
Note: Nairne the Stone-Singer is getting greedy. Bring her a hagraven feather cloak from Markarth next time, she likes those.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_towers.for: ~The Nord sells steel to kill the Nord,
~And we take it, and we laugh.
~He thinks the Reach is bought with knives,
~The Reach is bought with blood, and half.
^Translated from the Reach tongue by a guard of Markarth, who added: 'Half of what? Never found out. Ask them.'

The same guard's report continues: The Forsworn at the Towers sang this as they drove the Karthwasten silver wagon off the road. I lay in the ditch and heard every word. When they were gone I found the wagon's strongbox already opened with a key, not broken. Forsworn don't carry keys. Somebody gave them one.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_towers.hoo: Twin broken towers on a ridge above the Karth, held by a Forsworn band that is far too well armed for raiders who live on roots and stolen goats.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_towers.rum: Funny thing about the Sundered Towers Forsworn. Steel arrowheads, new bowstrings, Markarth-forged knives. Somebody in the city is selling. Somebody in the city is getting rich.
place_lore.nirncraft.sundered_towers.sk4: Folio #26 (-2186, -560): Field inspection recorded for Sundered Towers within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #26 for sundered_towers: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Sundered Towers are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.sunderstone_gorge.a:
#2nd of Hearthfire
Runil sent me to see why the pilgrims have stopped coming to the falls. The water is grey and smells of lamp oil and old bone. The seal of Arkay above the inner door of the barrow is cracked clean through.

#3rd of Hearthfire
The seal stone has been pried out and carried inside. Someone wanted the door open. I can hear something walking beyond it, slow and heavy, with a sound like a chain dragging. The old texts name the lord buried here as Sunder Grey-Hand, who sacked three villages and was buried with them.

#4th of Hearthfire
I will go in and bring the seal back out, and set it in its place, and say the words. If Arkay wills it, the Grey-Hand sleeps again. If not, tell Runil I tried.
place_lore.nirncraft.sunderstone_gorge.b:
Copied from the stone by a careful hand:
'Here lies Sunder, called the Grey-Hand, who took the hearths of Brennvik, Hollow Ash and Myrkstead. Their people lie at his feet that he may command them in the life beyond. Close this door, and close it well, and do not open it for gold, for there is none here but what he took, and he is not finished taking.'

Below the copy, the copyist has added in a shakier hand: 'The seal of Arkay was set over these words by the priests of Falkreath in the First Era, after the Grey-Hand's ghost walked the gorge for nine winters. Whoever moved the seal knew exactly what they were doing. I pray it was only greed.'
place_lore.nirncraft.sunderstone_gorge.h: An ancient barrow cut into a waterfall gorge in the western woods. A priest of Arkay went in to reseal its inner door and the gorge has been louder ever since.
place_lore.nirncraft.sunderstone_gorge.r: That waterfall in Sunderstone Gorge used to be a pilgrim's spot. Now the water runs grey, and Runil's young acolyte who went to bless it never came back to Falkreath.

place_lore.nirncraft.sunderstone_word_wa: A scorched semi-circle of carved basalt deep in the western gorge, inscribed with ancient runes of fire and mourning.
Even the stone around the Sunderstone Word Wall feels warm to the touch, as if the old dragon-breath never quite cooled.

Folio #56 (-1520, 1640): Field inspection recorded for Sunderstone Word Wall within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

The runes along the upper frieze are blackened by oil-smoke, yet the chisel-cuts remain sharp beneath the soot. They commemorate a warrior who fell beneath scorching wings and whose kinsmen raised this wall where the canyon rock itself split open.

place_lore.nirncraft.sunken_temple_of_th: A sunken sea-temple of flooded halls, coral shelves and air pockets, with a king's funeral barge filling the central hall and walls carved with a voyage.
The sunken temple's barge has never left. The Ra Gada say it is waiting for someone who has finished their lessons.

NINE PAGES, NINE PORTS, NINE HANDS. The road home is not a place but a tide, and it comes but once in each age. Read it aloud and the barge will sail. Burn it, and the kings will sleep. The tide does not care which you choose.

~The Wave, the Wind, the Stone, the Return.~The first you learn and the last you earn.~Row, row, the barge is old,~the kings are heavy, the water cold.~But a hand on the oar and a heart that is true~will carry the lesson, and the kings, home too.
#THE DOORFRAME (EXCERPT)
Year nine: 'Water will take the low house.' Year twelve: 'The king in green will go to ground.' Year twenty-six: 'The brother who left will return in the same boots.' Year forty: [the line has not yet been carved].
I have tried not to look at the blank. It looks at me anyway.
A hermit's hut in the forest where a prophecy is carved on the doorframe, one line a year, and every line has come true.
Do not read the doorframe aloud. Do not read it silently, either. Read it as if it were a letter from a stranger who knows your name.

place_lore.nirncraft.swindlers_den.fence:
Bought from Halted Stream (Brattvar's lot): 9 sacks iron ore at 4 each. Told him 3. He believed me.
Bought from White River Watch: 6 casks Honningbrew. Watered two and sold them to Redoran's Retreat at full price.

Bought from two Legion deserters: one leather dispatch case, Legion seal, unopened. Paid 40. Worth 400 to the right Stormcloak. Holding it in the strongbox till the right Stormcloak comes asking. There's a camp of them east of the river. Word will get round.

Note: nobody touches the strongbox. Nobody.
place_lore.nirncraft.swindlers_den.hook: A cave in the western hills that serves as a thieves' market for every robber in the hold. Stolen ore, stolen mead and stolen secrets all pass through its fence's hands.
place_lore.nirncraft.swindlers_den.rumou: Swindler's Den. You can buy anything there, if you don't ask where it came from and don't mind someone selling your purse back to you on the way out.
place_lore.nirncraft.swindlers_den.sk4_n: Folio #30 (-1045, -151): Field inspection recorded for Swindlers Den within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #30 for swindlers_den: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Swindlers Den are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.swindlers_den.swind:
1. No stealing from each other. Steal from the customers.
2. No fighting inside. Take it outside where the wolves can clean up.
3. Everything has a price. Everyone has a price. Find it.
4. If the guards come, you've never heard of Grelka.
5. If Grelka asks, you've never heard of the guards.

6. The Legion seal is not to be broken. Sealed is worth more.
7. Whoever keeps eating the cheese, stop.

8. The cave belongs to whoever pays Grelka the most. Right now that is Grelka.

A giant camp on the open tundra north of Rorikstead, gathered round a great standing stone that hums in the wind. The giants seem to listen to it.
The giants at Talking Stone sit round their big rock at night like old men round a fire, and the rock hums back at them. My father swears he heard it say his name. My father drinks.

I lay on the ridge above the giant camp for two nights and listened. The stone does hum when the wind is from the west. The giants sit with their backs to it, eyes closed, and sometimes one of them hums back, very low, a note so deep I felt it in my teeth rather than heard it.

I do not know if they are praying, or singing, or simply keeping the stone company. On the second night the eldest giant turned and looked directly at my hiding place, and then turned back, and hummed again. I think I was being told I was welcome to listen, so long as I stayed where I was. I stayed.
place_lore.nirncraft.tall_papas_spire.ho: A tall, thin spire of white stone on the Yokudan desert, said to have been raised by a single mason who could not stop climbing, and who is still, in some tellings, at the top.
place_lore.nirncraft.tall_papas_spire.ru: Tall Papa's Spire has no door. A visitor must climb the outside, which is smooth as glass, and which has been the downfall of a great many confident people.
place_lore.nirncraft.tall_papas_spire.sp:
#I WAS HERE
At the fortieth course. My hands are bleeding. I regret nothing. The wind up here tastes of cold stone. I can see a grey line of sea on the west. I am told there is more, higher. I do not believe it. I am going to find out.
Another hand, much higher, in a different ink: 'I was here, too. It was not worth it. It was exactly worth it. Come up.'
place_lore.nirncraft.talos_massacre_shri: A hidden woodland shrine in a rocky hollow where offerings of iron swords and wildflowers lie disturbed beside recent struggle marks.
Woodcutters east of Lake Ilinalta whisper that a whole company of secret worshippers was cornered at a forest shrine last month.

place_lore.nirncraft.taneth.beast_trader:
#Frostfall the 3rd
The great senche from Elsweyr broke her cage on the quay last night. Old Saffron, the dock boys call her: twice the size of a horse and the colour of ripe dates. She killed my best handler and went over the north wall like a cat over a fence.

#Frostfall the 9th
She has been seen near the Hircine stones north of the city, where the Hew's Bane hunters leave skulls. She is eating goats. Soon she will stop eating goats. Lord Ezhar's steward says the fine for an escaped beast is my whole stock. I would rather pay a hunter. I would rather pay a hunter a great deal.
place_lore.nirncraft.taneth.harbour_noti:
^BY ORDER OF LORD EZHAR AT-TANETH
The trade in persons is forbidden in this harbour and in all of Hew's Bane. Any captain found carrying shackled passengers will forfeit his ship, his cargo and his right hand.

It has come to the Court's notice that persons are nonetheless being taken from the fishing villages north of the city and marched inland to the shrine of the Lord of Chains, where they are sold to buyers who come over the hills by night. The Court offers two hundred gold for the name of the slaver called Iron-Collar. The Court offers more for his head.
place_lore.nirncraft.taneth.hook: The proud harbour of the Forebears on the Hew's Bane coast, crowded with dhows, warehouses and beast-markets, where Lord Ezhar's merchants deal with all the world and ask no questions of its coin.
place_lore.nirncraft.taneth.rumour: Taneth sells anything: silk, steel, tigers. Somebody sold a tiger last month that didn't stay sold. It's out there north of the walls now, and it remembers the man with the whip.
place_lore.nirncraft.tang_mo_harbor_vill: A harbour of lacquered junks and floating lantern-masts, houses raised on bamboo piles with curved roofs, a dragon-prowed ship at the quay and a tea-house for every tide.
Tang Mo has more lanterns than people. They are hung for the dead, for the lost and for those who have not yet been born. The harbour at night is the brightest sea in the world.

#THIS TIDE
Green: for the nervous. Black: for the grieving. White: for those who wish to be forgiven. Grey: for those who do not know. Red, which is not tea, and is not for sale, and is for the ones who have already decided.
In the margin, in Li's impatient brush: 'The lantern on the mast is not a tea. I do not know what it is for. I have brewed all five colours at it and it has accepted none.'
place_lore.nirncraft.tang_mo_watch.hook: A border watchtower on the Tang Mo coast with a lantern at its crown and a stone at its foot carved with a fourfold seal.
place_lore.nirncraft.tang_mo_watch.rumou: The watchmen say the border stone has been rubbed smooth by pilgrims, all but one corner that stays cold.
place_lore.nirncraft.tang_mo_watch.web.p: Do not let pilgrims chip the stone. The fourth quarter is cold. Do not touch it with bare hands. Send word to the harbour that the seal's strength fails by a quarter per generation. The court that holds the last has not answered in two hundred years. Keep the lantern lit.

#THE LAST HARVEST
Thirty years of cane, each year in a hand a little shakier. The final line, written in charcoal: 'Four hands. I counted the footprints. One of them wore the boots my husband gave away at the funeral.'
A burned sugar-farm, its cane reduced to black stubble, and an owner who will not say who set the fire.
Tathara will not say, but she does not lock her gate any more. She says she wants whoever did it to come back and see.

place_lore.nirncraft.teeth_of_sithis.hoo: A ring of black teeth rising from the mire around a sunken hollow, with root paths between each tooth, each tooth a different trial.
place_lore.nirncraft.teeth_of_sithis.rum: The ring of teeth is quiet. The old folk say it used to sing.
place_lore.nirncraft.teeth_of_sithis.web: WHEN THE DIRGE IS SUNG THE TEETH ARE QUIET. WHEN THE DIRGE IS LOST THE TEETH ARE HUNGRY. Sing the dead down the water. Do not sell the road. Do not bend the song. The teeth are patient but they are not kind.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_branora.hook: A single huge mushroom tower on a lagoon, with a master and his servants and a tidal causeway that floods twice a day.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_branora.rumour: The master of Tel Branora has been dead for six years. His letters still arrive every season.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_branora.web.p0: My lord has not left the lower hall since the third flood. The papers still need signing, and each season the signature appears on its own, a little more crooked. I have stopped asking. The servants set his place and clear it. The vote requires his seat, they say; the seat is filled.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_mithryn.gazette:
#Who lives in the cap
Magister Ildar Neloth-Kin is brilliant and petulant and wishes to be his uncle. Apprentice Duvren has touched the mushroom with the ribbon on it. Yarda Net-Girl sells rumours for cake and coin. Pelli Sporeheart tends the garden and says: wipe your boots.

#Rules of the tower
The tower grows by a rule: one spore asked, one spore given. The cellar holds a second mushroom that eats compliments. Do not say anyone looks well. The test chamber breathes; count to four before you act.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_mithryn.hook: A Telvanni tower grown from a giant mushroom on the island's southeastern coast. The wizard Neloth rules here, and his household of nervous apprentices pays well for anything Dwemer, dangerous, or both.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_mithryn.rumour: Tel Mithryn? The scholar Ulvo Nerano will pay you for Dwemer rubbish, so long as you don't touch anything on the way in. Last fellow who touched something grew a second shadow.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_mithryn.ulvo_su: Ulvo Nerano, scholar of Tel Mithryn

A provisional list, compiled at my own expense since the master considers the subject beneath him.
I. Nchardak, to the east. Flooded, partly. The master has opinions about it which he shares at length and in no useful detail.
II. Kagrumez, west of the dragon mound. The resonance chambers still hum. The gems sing; I wish to know in what key.

III. Fahlbtharz, far to the north and west, where the steam pipes have not stopped hissing in four thousand years. A prospector from the Company went in last spring. He came out with burns on both arms and a theory, neither of which he would explain.
Note to self: hire someone sturdier than myself. Possibly several someones.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_mithryn.visitor:
Visitors to the tower are reminded:
Do not touch the netches. They are not pets.
Do not touch the apprentices. They are not pets either, though some of them may be experiments.
Do not ask the master about his age, his health, his rivals, or Vvardenfell.
Do not climb the stalks. The levitation stops working at the top for anyone the master has not keyed into it. He has keyed in no one.
The steward accepts no responsibility for growths, curses, or transfigurations acquired while ignoring this notice.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_naga.hook: The fourteen-floor tower of Magister Ulveni Rathra, reached by rope-bridges and bad temper, guarded by eleven guardians and one sulking teapot.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_naga.rumour: A singing teapot on the fourteenth floor of Tel Naga hums three notes when lifted and sulks when set down. Magister Gaenor has wagered a stranger could lift it. Ulveni has wagered the stranger would not leave the third bridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.tel_naga.sign.p0:
^TO ALL WHO CROSS
The bridge holds six. It has held eleven once. We do not speak of that. The gap beyond the fourth rope is a levitation gap. Do not attempt it without the proper preparation, or the proper embarrassment.

If a spell-guard asks you a question, answer it. If the teapot asks, do not.

A ridge-top temple with terraces in four stages, prayer-wheels and a hollow dome, whose sanctum is aligned to a single moonrise.
The temple of Agamanus no longer lights its lamp. The keepers say it will be lit again once the moon is on time.

The lamp is not to be lit until the moon touches the dome. If it is late, it is late; do not alter the dome or the brass. Do not post this order. Do not tell the pilgrims. The moon is the moon, and it is the priests' duty to be right even when the moon is wrong.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_miraak.cu:
Sleepers assigned to the outer stair: eleven. Stone-carriers: six. Two collapsed on the third night; return them to the Earth Stone road where the Guard will find them. The Master has no use for broken tools.
The Faithful are reminded that the masks are not to be removed in the presence of sleepers. They remember faces in their dreams, though not on waking. Brother Ulfgar is at Hrothmund's Barrow seeking the key and is not to be disturbed.
In the margin, a smaller hand: Durel Rendas comes every night to the outer door. He has seen his wife on the stair twice. Kill him, or let him join the sleepers. The Master does not care which.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_miraak.ho: A great ruined temple rising from the stone west of Thirsk, built in the Dragon Priests' age. Sleepwalkers have come here from Raven Rock, and not every family has found its missing.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_miraak.ru: Folk from Raven Rock walk out to the Temple of Miraak in their sleep. Most come home. Durel Rendas's wife Mirisa walked there last month and they haven't found her yet. The Guard says she's not inside. They didn't look very hard.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_miraak.se:
Mirisa,
If you are inside and you wake up, if you find this: I came. I came every night for a week. The masked ones would not let me down the stairs. I left bread and your shawl by the door. The shawl is gone. I choose to believe you took it.
The Guard says to wait. Sergeant Indaram says the sleepers come home on their own. Some of them do. Come home, Mirisa. The kettle is on. The kettle is always on now. Durel.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_satakal.h: A temple to the world-eater snake on an island, its roof a great coil and its floor a mosaic of scales.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_satakal.r: The temple's priests teach a dance on a floor of scales. They say it ends where it should.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_satakal.w: WHO DANCES HERE DANCES TOWARD THE MOUTH. The world-eater is patient, the world-eater is kind in its way. Dance, and be swallowed, and be returned. The fourth form is taught on the water. The snake is the water's friend.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_sul.hook: A sun-temple with bright shafts and a gold altar, its roof carved to focus a single beam at noon.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_sul.rumou: The Temple of Sul's gold is real, but the priest who kept it hasn't prayed in a year.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_sul.web.p: In the name of the sun, the bearer is granted the right to gather sap from the Root at such sites as the bearer chooses, for the sum of three hundred pieces of gold per season. The temple will not be held to account. The sun is a witness, and the sun does not testify.
place_lore.nirncraft.temple_of_the_serpe: A tall serpent-roofed temple on a Tsaesci ridge, with coils of painted stair and a bell-gate at the summit.
The serpent-priests wait. They wait without hurry, and they are not the ones who fear.
FORTY-ONE FOR THE LADDER, FORTY-ONE FOR THE CLIMB. When the last is set the court will rise. We have waited a thousand years. We can wait for two more bones, and a quiet that does not end.

Three have bowed, one waits. Let the emperor's coil close upon the last. We are patient: we were patient in the ice and patient in the fire. We will be patient until the fourth is brought to us in a cold hand. Great coil, great hunger, great quiet.

place_lore.nirncraft.thalaras_winery.hoo: A single-family cellar estate with a stone press, where the vines have grown over a flagstone floor that is, in fact, a lamp-hall roof.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalaras_winery.rum: The Thalaras cellar sells a wine that tastes like a memory. No one who drinks it will say whose.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalaras_winery.web: To whoever holds the estate after me. Do not sell the oldest rows to the Count's steward. The vines drink from the vault, and the vault is full of names that the Warden keeps. Press them, bottle them, give each its day, but never let one be spoken whole at once. Miscarcand is only a door. We are the lock.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalmor_embassy.dis: Third Emissary, Office of the First Emissary

#14 Frostfall, 4E 201
Agent Merilar reports that a gathering of Talos worshippers meets in the cabin known locally as the Ironback Hideout, west of this embassy, on the first Sundas of each month. Their numbers are small. Their convictions are not.

You are to observe the next assembly and identify all participants. Do not intervene. Arrests made within sight of Solitude embarrass the Jarl, and an embarrassed Jarl is a less useful Jarl.
The elderly priest among them is to be detained separately and transferred to Northwatch Keep. Interrogators there have been notified. Burn this dispatch once read. The Dominion is patient; it is also thorough.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalmor_embassy.hoo: A walled elven compound on the cold hills west of Solitude. The Aldmeri Dominion hosts fine receptions here, and keeps a dungeon beneath them for Nords who still pray to Talos.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalmor_embassy.rum: The embassy throws a reception and half of Solitude's nobles go, smiling. The other half don't go, and some of them aren't seen again. Draw your own sums.
place_lore.nirncraft.thalmor_embassy.ser:
Sister,
I cannot come to Dragon Bridge for Mother's naming day. They will not give leave before the reception, and after the reception they will not give leave because of the mess the reception made. The elves wanted snow berries from Katla's Farm frozen in their wine. Have you ever tried to keep a berry frozen in a kitchen with six ovens?

The pay is good. That is the only good thing. There is a door in the cellar that the guards walk past without looking at, and on some nights I hear someone behind it, praying in Nordic. I put an extra heel of bread by the door once. In the morning it was gone and the guard was eating it. I do not do that any more.
Burn this letter. I mean it, Hildi.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_apprentice_ston: An ancient standing stone in the marsh between Solitude and Morthal, carved with the Apprentice. Mages swear by it, though it makes them reckless.
Touched the stone at dusk. Magicka returns like a tide coming in, faster than I've ever felt it. Also feel like a crab without its shell. Every spell that flies past me makes my teeth itch.

Master says the Apprentice favours those who learn quickly and forgives nothing. Master says it as a warning. I am taking it as a compliment.
Firebolts cast before supper: 31. Mudcrabs hit: 2. Hats lost in the bog: 1.
Note for tomorrow: practise wards before firebolts. A frost spell from some passing hedge-witch in the fog nearly froze my eyebrows off, and I felt it twice as hard as I should have.
The Apprentice Stone, out in the bog. Young mages walk all the way from Solitude to touch it. They come back full of fire and empty of sense, my husband says. But he says that about all mages.
One of the ancient standing stones, raised on a warm hillside north of Mistwatch, which deepens a mage's well of magicka at the price of slower recovery.
Mages walk all the way from Winterhold to stand at the Atronach Stone. Most come back with more power. Some come back short a purse; the Mistwatch lot rob them on the road.

The Atronach is the Golem among the constellations, a vessel that absorbs what is thrown at it. Those born beneath it are deep wells that fill slowly. The Stone grants a similar gift to those who were not so fortunate in their birth.

I have stood here three nights. On the first I felt nothing. On the second I felt the ground's warmth climbing into my fingers. On the third I felt as though I were a cup someone was patiently making larger.
Note: the hill is pleasant, the view fine, and the tower to the south full of thieves. Do not meditate with your purse on the ground.
A Daedric prison under a spire with cell-blocks of obsidian, chains and windows on nothing.
A prison under a spire holds those who said no to the fever. They are asking to be let out and they are right.

To whom it may concern, I am not mad, I am glass. The seed sings to me but I do not sing back. They keep us because we are proof the fever can be borne. The fortress's heart is a crystal as tall as a man. Break it and the grove will fall silent. I cannot reach it; my legs are no longer mine.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_blue_netch.hook: A Skingrad-road inn whose sign shows a blue netch the size of a barn, which, by the innkeeper's account, is a modest likeness.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_blue_netch.netc:
^TAB BOARD, THE BLUE NETCH
^Rolf the cooper owes 6 silver. Rolf the cooper says he is not Rolf the cooper. Rolf the cooper owes 6 silver.
^The Count's own coachman owes 14 and has been told to pay in wine.
^One Dunmer scholar owes nothing and has asked, three times, whether the netch on the sign is anatomically correct.

Note to self: do not let the scholar into the cellar. Last time he took measurements and left a note on the door saying the netch was "forty hands shy of life size, in the mouth." We have been drinking quieter since.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_blue_netch.rumo: They say the Blue Netch's ale is made with water from a well that was dug by Ayleids. It makes your hands very cold, and your jokes very good.
