place_lore.nirncraft.the_frozen_dragon_m: A mound of ice with a dragon's head frozen at its crown, jaws open in a final roar.
The frozen dragon has begun to weep at the throat, and the ice-seam under the halls is following it.

A foreign man came to the mound last year in a cloak of red silk. He cut a bone from the dragon's throat while it slept, and the dragon, which had not stirred in a thousand years, shuddered. The ice began to crack that night. Do not let any who wear red silk near the mound.

The head is the pin and the pin must hold. If it thaws, the shelf will break, and the hold will drift out to sea in ten halves. We swore to keep the howe's ship ready for such a day. Ready, I say, as if we had ever opened her gate. The oath is an old man's boast. Wake the ship, whoever comes.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_golden_netch.ho: An inn under a bobbing netch-balloon where the yearly balloon race begins, and where, for nine years running, the winner has gone up and never come down.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_golden_netch.ra:
#THE GREAT NETCH RACE
Open to any balloon of any make and any pilot of any nerve. Course: from the Golden Netch, over the coast, to a marker set at the Committee's discretion. Prize: a golden netch, and the freedom of the skies.

A small note at the bottom: 'The Committee regrets that it cannot be responsible for the pilot's whereabouts after the finish. Pilots are advised to leave a forwarding address. Nobody has ever collected one.'
place_lore.nirncraft.the_golden_netch.ru: The Golden Netch has a wall of winners' portraits, nine of them. They are hung high, out of reach, so no one can see that all nine are smiling in exactly the same way.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_guardian_stones:
Buyer,
Next load from Embershard will be at the stones on Middas, at dusk, ground clean of the mark. Bring the usual and not a copper less, Skarn says the price of iron's gone up since the war. Stand by the Thief stone, it's the one in the shadow. Don't bring Riverwood folk. Don't bring anybody.

Last load short by two sacks. Skarn says that's on you, not us, since you counted it in the dark. Bring a lantern this time. But keep it hooded till you're past the stones, the Riverwood guards walk the road on Middas now. If they stop you, you're a pilgrim. You've come to pray to the Thief. It's not even a lie.
Three ancient standing stones on the road between Riverwood and Helgen, each marked with a constellation: the Warrior, the Mage and the Thief. Every traveller is said to be drawn to one.
Everyone who walks past the Guardian Stones feels one of them pulling. Mine was the Thief. My wife says that explains a great deal.

Scratched into the flat rock between the three stones by some long-gone traveller:
'The Warrior asked me what I would fight for. The Mage asked me what I would learn. The Thief asked me what I would take. I could not answer all three, so I chose the one that asked the question I was afraid of.'
Below it, in a different hand: 'Which one was that?' And below that, in the first hand again: 'Go and find out.'

Travellers have added to the carving over the years. One has scratched a sword, one a book, one a key. Someone has scratched all three and written beside them: 'Greedy.' Another has answered: 'Prepared.'

Folio #39 (-274, 824): Field inspection recorded for The Guardian Stones within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_katariah.hook: The Emperor's great ship lies in the Karth estuary below Solitude. Its decks are half-crewed while it waits for its master, and its lower holds carry more than anyone wrote down.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_katariah.rumour: That big Imperial ship by the estuary? The sailors aboard are paid triple to keep their mouths shut. My brother-in-law hauled crates out to it. He says one of them was warm.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_katariah.stowaw:
#Day 6
The after hold is dry and the wine is good. I have learned the watches. The cat knows I am here and has not told anyone.

#Day 9
The bosun has noticed the wine. I am drinking slower and topping up with river water, which is worse for both of us.
#Day 12
I meant to stow aboard and sail to Cyrodiil and be someone. But they say the ship does not sail until the Emperor comes, and the Emperor has not come. I have been someone on this ship for twelve days. Pellin the wine-thief. Pellin who talks to cats. It is more than I was in the Solitude gutters.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_katariah.watch_:
First watch: Casca, Duronius, Big Hrothmar.
Middle watch: Tullia, Sevari, the Dunmer boy.
Morning watch: whoever is sober.
Standing orders: no fires below the waterline. No rowing ashore after dark. No guests. If a man tells you he is a guest of the Emperor, he is lying, and you will put him in the bilge until an officer says otherwise.

Someone has been at the wine in the after hold again. The seals are cut clean and the barrels topped up with Karth water. I will find the man. When I find him, he will learn to swim in the Sea of Ghosts in Frostfall.
Also: stop feeding the cat. It is not a ship's cat. It came aboard on its own and it looks at me like it knows something.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lady_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone on a small island in Lake Ilinalta, blessed by the Lady sign. Pilgrims row out to it for healing, and the millfolk of Half-Moon leave wreaths.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lady_stone.pilg:
~Lady of the lake stone, mend what I broke,
~The bone and the promise, the word that I spoke,
~Make whole what is torn, make warm what is cold,
~And keep me, when weary, from growing too old.

A slip of paper tucked into a crack in the stone, weighted with a pebble.
The paper is signed only with a small drawing of a crutch. Beneath the pebble that weights it lies another, and beneath that another: a little cairn of pebbles, one for every pilgrim who came here limping and rowed home without needing to.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lady_stone.rumo: Brynja rows out to the Lady Stone every spring with a wreath for her mother. Says her mother lost something in the shallows there on her wedding day and never got it back.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lady_stone.sk4_: Folio #38 (-829, 761): Field inspection recorded for The Lady Stone within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_lady_stone.ston:
Carved around the foot of the stone, in old runes worn soft by the lake wind:
'The Lady keeps the mended and the mending. Rest here, and rise whole.'
Newer letters have been cut beside them by a less practised hand: 'Ingrun and Ottar, wed here on the 9th of Second Seed. She dropped her comb in the water. He said he'd find it. He never did. He said he'd find it every year after. Love, Brynja.'

On the far side of the stone, someone has cut a tally of short lines in groups of five, thirty in all. The most recent are deeper and more careful than the rest, as if made by an old man who had to rest between each one.
A one-lamp inn on a moor in the fog, with a single lantern in the window and a table laid for a guest.
The Lonely Lantern keeps its one lamp lit all night. Guests who sleep there leave a card and no footprints.
You are cordially invited to the supper that never ends. Wear what you wore when you were happiest. Leave your lantern at the door. The host is quite certain you will come. R.S.V.P. with the fog.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_lord_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone in the hills between Stonehills and the Dwemer ruins, carved with the Lord. Those who touch it find their skin a little harder to break.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lord_stone.rumo: Soldiers from both camps go up to the Lord Stone before they move out. Never at the same time, mind. Wouldn't do to be seen praying next to the enemy.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lord_stone.sold:
~Lord of the sky, armoured and patient,
~make my skin like your stone and my heart like your stillness.
~I am not asking to win.
~I am asking to be standing when it's done.

^Folded with it, a second note in a different hand:
So am I. Whoever you are. Blue coat or red, I hope you're standing too.
^And a third, pressed in deeper, the ink smudged by rain:
I found both your notes. I'm a farmer from Stonehills and I fight for nobody. I pray you both come home, and that you never meet each other on a field. Leave the stone in peace when you're done.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lover_stone.aiw:
Leif,
You did not come on the night of the new moon. I waited until the frost was on my hair. Then my mother's people came and I had to go with them.
I am leaving you my braided token. It is the only thing I own that is mine and not my clan's. My mother says I am promised to the crones at Blind Cliff Cave. Do not come for me. I mean it.

I do not mean it. Come for me.
No. Do not. You are a miner's son from Karthwasten with a pick and a kind face and they would eat you alive.
Keep the token. Remember me by it. The Lover's blessing go with you, wherever it goes. - A.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lover_stone.hoo: An ancient standing stone in the Reach hills, blessed by the Lover constellation. Couples come to it to pledge themselves, and some leave letters for those who never came.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lover_stone.lov:
Ancient Nordic letters, barely readable, worn by hands and weather:
UNDER THE LOVER, ALL ARE ONE BLOOD.
Carved beneath in a dozen hands, some old and some fresh: initials joined with lines. H and S. B and T. Two Reach marks joined to a Nord rune. A and L, the newest, the lines still pale in the stone.

Someone has left a small offering at the foot of the stone: a sprig of mountain flower, a copper ring and a wooden spoon carved with a hawk. A scrap of bark tied to the spoon reads, in a careful Nord hand: For A. I came on the second night. You were already gone. I will keep coming. - L.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_lover_stone.rum: Young folk from Karthwasten meet at the Lover Stone, even Nords and Reachfolk, if you can believe it. There's a letter tucked under the stone right now, if the gossip's right.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_middens.hook: A shadowed warren of lean-tos and sunless alleys beneath the lowest roots of Elden Root, where those the Pact forgets sell what the city throws away.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_middens.peddler:
^HONEST LANTERNS
^Cheap. Quiet. No questions about the bracket.
^Ask for Sorwe, or for the other fellow, who is not Sorwe.

Scrawled below by a Gate guard: 'Seven lamps gone from the Root Gate this month. Every one of them turns up here, a quarter of the price. Nobody on the Gate can find the cutter. Whoever it is, they never touch the wood.'
place_lore.nirncraft.the_middens.rumour: Everything that falls from the city ends in the Middens. Nobody lives in the Middens, you understand. They only happen to sleep there, a great many of them, with their eyes open.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_orrery.hook: A hanging orrery of bronze rings and polished wood, slung in the boughs of the Elden Tree, which tracks the moons, the seasons and the slow turning of the great tree itself.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_orrery.orrery_l:
#Third night, still
The outer ring slipped again. It slips every month, always by the same amount, always at the same hour. I have stopped adjusting it. I think the tree moves, a little, each month, and the ring is the only honest witness.
Fifth night: I measured the slip. It is not random. It is a rhythm. The tree is breathing, and the ring is its lung. I have told the Silvenar's Voice. He asked me to lower my voice.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_orrery.rumour: The Orrery has one ring too many. The Spinners say it measures the tree's heartbeat. The Tree says it measures whatever is listening.

An inn built under a grown netch-balloon that bobs on a rope above the courtyard, where a balloonist trades rides for stories and has never once been told the same tale twice.

#RIDES TODAY
One story, one ride. Two stories, one ride and a drink. Three stories, Q'ri will take you somewhere nobody has been. Rides do not come back the same. Stories do not either.
The netch is older than the inn, and the inn was built to keep it company. At night, the balloon dreams. The patrons say they can hear it, if they have had enough.

An Ald'ruhn tavern famed for its sign: a rat, a pot, and an inspector who has never recovered.

#Stews
Stew of the day: the one nobody orders.
Stew of the night: the one you will wish you had ordered earlier.
House special: any stew you request, in a pot that has been recently scrubbed.

#A note on the sign
The rat is a mascot. The pot is a fact. If the inspector from the Council returns, the stew is on the house, and so is the apology.
There is no rat in the Rat in the Pot. There was a rat once. There is a pot. The connection, say the regulars, is purely nominal, and the sign is rather fond of a very small crown.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_ritual_stone.ho: A standing stone east of Whiterun ringed with old graves, said to grant the power to raise the dead. Someone has been testing that claim by moonlight.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_ritual_stone.mo: The stone is honest. Stand in its shadow at midnight with the right words and the dead stand up beside you. Six of the old graves answered tonight. They are slow and forget their tasks, but the magister at Fellglow will be pleased with the grave dust.

Problem: the farmers have seen lights. A Whiterun priestess came to the road and sprinkled water about and sang. The dead did not like it. I did not like it.

Tomorrow I will raise all the rest, set them round the stone and see if the priestess wants to sing to them all at once.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_ritual_stone.ru: The Ritual Stone's been busy. Somebody's been digging up the old graves around it, and the guards found a skeleton walking the road by itself last Tirdas. Sister Hildrun at the temple wants it stopped.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_ritual_stone.sk: Folio #43 (491, -34): Field inspection recorded for The Ritual Stone within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #43 for the_ritual_stone: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing The Ritual Stone are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_ritual_stone.st:
^THE RITUAL
Carved in the old Nord way around the base of the stone, half hidden by lichen: 'Those who lie here lay down their swords. Let no one take them up again.'
Someone has chipped at the carving with a knife, trying to scratch out the word 'no'. They have not quite managed it.

Around the far side of the stone, older marks again, nearly worn away: a ring of small figures lying down, and one figure standing over them with its arms raised. The standing figure has been carved with no face. Shepherds who graze nearby say the old priests did that on purpose, so the dead would never know who woke them.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sentinel.hook: A lone statue guardian on a ridge above the Valus road, hand raised against something no traveller can see.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sentinel.rumour: Wind drops dead at the foot of the Sentinel, and the ravens won't land on it.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sentinel.web.p0: KEEP THE VIGIL. Whoever raises a bell on this ridge lets something hear. Whoever takes one down keeps the dark in its place. Sentinel, watch the seven. Sentinel, watch the door.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_serpent_stone.c: Field note for Master Tolfdir's class on standing stones. The Serpent Stone is the most isolated of the thirteen. It stands on a floe that has not drifted in living memory, though every floe around it does.
I touched it. My fingertips went numb and then very hot, and for an hour afterward anything I touched felt like a beehive. Recommend gloves. Recommend not falling in on the way back, which I did.

Master Tolfdir says the sting of the Serpent is the Stone's blessing: a venom in the fingertips that the bearer may cast on a foe. I believe him. I accidentally cast it on a mudcrab and the mudcrab has not forgiven me.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_serpent_stone.h: A standing stone on a lonely ice floe off the eastern Winterhold coast, marked with the sign of the Serpent. Reaching it means crossing the ice, which is a test in itself.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_serpent_stone.r: The Serpent Stone's out on the ice. You get there by jumping floe to floe with the slaughterfish watching. It gives you a sting in your fingers, they say. Worth it? Ask the fish.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_serpent_stone.s:
~The Serpent wanders through the sky,
~It has no house, it has no throne,
~It bites the stars and passes by,
~And leaves its venom in the stone.
^Carved below by another hand: I crossed six floes to read this. It does not rhyme as well as I hoped. Still, my hands are tingling.

^Below that, scratched in the ice and already half-melted
Three floes south, the slaughterfish wait. They always wait. Cross quickly and do not stop to admire the view, however fine it is in the dawn light.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_shadow_stone.ho: An ancient standing stone in the woods south of Riften, carved with the sign of the Shadow. Those born under it slip through the world unseen, and thieves leave it small offerings for luck.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_shadow_stone.of:
To the Shadow,
You kept me hidden from Maven's men on the night of the Goldenglow fire, and I swore if I lived I'd give you a share. I lived.

I've buried the share where only someone who knows how to look will find it: twelve paces from the stone toward Snow-Shod Farm, under a flat rock with a crescent scratched on it. Picks and a purse. Whoever finds it, you have my blessing. Shadows don't need gold, after all. People do.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_shadow_stone.ru: Every cutpurse in Riften kisses the Shadow Stone before a job. I don't hold with it myself. Mind you, I've never been caught.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_shadow_stone.sk: Folio #54 (2399, 1630): Field inspection recorded for The Shadow Stone within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #54 for the_shadow_stone: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing The Shadow Stone are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
A roadhouse on the Dragontail road, a long low building with a well-yard and a tally-board hung from the eaves.
The Silver Pilgrim's tally-board gets a new line every dawn, in a hand nobody knows.

Wells owed: thirty-one. Wells paid: nine. Caravans in arrears: forty-two. Collector: the Herald, who is not a man I have ever met. I copy the board each dawn and burn the copy. The board is always new again. It is a sort of mercy to be owed by someone who cannot be seen.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_stable_steed.ho: A Gideon inn where the guar eat first, the riders second and the accountants last, in the shade of a plateau that has not seen rain in eleven years.

#Order of service
1. The guar eats first. It is not discrimination. It is economics.
2. The rider eats second, and is charged for both.
3. The accountant eats last and is charged for the shade.

Guests who attempt to bargain with the guar will be asked to leave. The guar will be asked to stay.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_stable_steed.ru: A merchant's guar vanished from the Stable Steed last week and the merchant will not leave until it returns. It has eaten first at every meal for six days. Folk say it found dates.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_steed_stone.cou:
~Steed of the north, I've a long road to go,
~A satchel of letters and boots full of snow,
~Lend me your back and lend me your stride,
~And I'll ride you to Solitude, though I can't ride.

^chalked beneath, in another hand:
The Thalmor rider who passed here at dawn did not touch the stone. His horse did, with its nose. Even the horse knows better than the elf.
^And beneath that, in a child's careful letters:
I touched it too and carried Papa's whole bundle of firewood home from the Ironback road without stopping once. Papa says it was the stone. I say it was me.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_steed_stone.hoo: An ancient standing stone in the hills west of Solitude, carved with the Steed. Those who touch it carry their burdens more easily, as couriers and soldiers have known for an age.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_steed_stone.rum: Every Legion courier between Solitude and Fort Hraggstad slaps the Steed Stone on the way past. Says it lightens the pack. Maybe it does. Maybe it just lightens the walk.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sugar_bowl.hook: A bowl-shaped courtyard tavern in Rimmen, hollowed down into the rock so every table sits in a shade, and run, cooked, swept and sung by one cat.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sugar_bowl.hous:
#THE HOUSE WINE
Grapes, when Tamhir can get them. Plums, when he cannot. Moon-sugar, on feast nights. Honey, because the bees of Corinthe sent a gift last winter and he did not know how to refuse. Cinnamon. A single, very discreet pepper.

Do not ask what else is in it. There is a crossed-out line at the bottom of the list, and a note: 'The cellar tenant has asked that her share be left out of the account. She says she is not a shareholder.'
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sugar_bowl.rumo: Tamhir keeps seventeen casks in the Sugar Bowl cellar and will tell you only sixteen. The seventeenth is for a guest who has not come yet.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_sweet_breezes_i:
#GLASS, THIS WINTER
Ninth-floor bay window: eleven times. Third-floor bay window: nine. Kitchen window: thrice, and the cook admits to two. Cellar skylight: twice, by a seagull that I will personally murder.
Marginal note: 'The wind pays for what it breaks, in its own way. Three nights a week it leaves a coin on the third-floor sill. I have decided it is penance, and I take it.'
A three-storey inn on the Senchal waterfront where every room faces the sea and every window has been broken at least once by a wind that insists on coming in.
The Sweet Breezes has a tab of glass that no one has ever settled. Zhaleh blames the wind. The wind, to be fair, has never denied it.

place_lore.nirncraft.the_tower_stone.hoo: An ancient standing stone on the frozen Winterhold coast, carved with the sign of the Tower. Those who touch it are said to find locks yielding and doors opening for them.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_tower_stone.rum: The Tower Stone gives you a knack for getting into places. Thieves swear by it. So do jailers' wives, and that's a whole other story.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_tower_stone.thi:
Stone of the Tower,
Last year I touched you and the next three locks in Windhelm opened like flowers. Then the fourth one opened onto the guard captain's bedroom, with the guard captain in it. I am writing this from the road to Dawnstar, which is where I live now.
I am grateful, but next time could you be more particular about which doors you open? I leave you a lockpick, bent, in thanks. It is the last one I have.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_vile_pavilion.h: A rotting banquet pavilion on the mire with floating platforms joined by plank walks and a long table with plates that still steam.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_vile_pavilion.r: A pavilion in the mire has food that steams on a night with frost. Nobody who sits there has returned for dessert.
place_lore.nirncraft.the_vile_pavilion.w: The Lord of the Long Supper

My dear guest: you are late, and the soup has gone cold, but I have made it warm again. Sit. Eat. We have been so long without company. The plates were set at the turn of the season, and the season turned eighteen times. I am so sorry about the weather. Do not leave before the sweets.

place_lore.nirncraft.thirsk_mead_hall.br:
To Geldis Sadri at the Retching Netch,
You owe me for four casks of honey-mead, and I owe you an apology for the state of your back room after my cousins drank there. Call it even. I need a favour instead of coin.

Send me anyone who can fight and does not drink more than they kill. The riekling chief who calls himself Kruk Gnaw-Tooth sits at Frossel on the north shore with the Spear of Thirsk across his knees. My people will not follow me into that den again until someone shows them it can be done. I will pay what I have, and the spear goes to the one who takes it, if they swear to bring it to the hall on feast days. Brenna.
place_lore.nirncraft.thirsk_mead_hall.ga:
#Under the ribs
Skald Hrolf Iron-Brow wants a beast. Ingrid Bone-Singer sings battles that did not happen to crowds that weep. Odd the Brewer's mead is honest; his dice are not. Brynja Trail-Reader reads tracks like letters. Sigrun Rib-Wright hangs the beams and mends the spears.

#The yard and the dice
The oldest rib-beam was once carried off by a boar who thought it was its grandfather's. The dice have lead on the one. The ridge above the Beast Stone has a snow-boar the size of a hut.
place_lore.nirncraft.thirsk_mead_hall.ha:
^Here the chieftains of Thirsk are named
The first carved the beam. The second set the hearth. The third went hunting the great bristleback alone and came back with half a hand and the whole beast.

Below the names, in fresher cuts: The hall fell to the small blue folk in the winter of the black ice. Their chief carried off the Spear of Thirsk, and they danced in our benches and drank our honey. We took it back with axes. The spear is still in Frossel. The beam has room for the name of whoever brings it home.
place_lore.nirncraft.thirsk_mead_hall.ho: A great Nord mead hall on the island's eastern slopes, raised in the last age and fought over ever since. The hall has been won back from the rieklings, but its heirloom spear has not.
place_lore.nirncraft.thirsk_mead_hall.ru: They say the Nords at Thirsk took the hall back from the rieklings last winter. Took the hall, not the spear. The riekling chief at Frossel still carries it, and Brenna Ice-Mead won't sleep until it's home.
place_lore.nirncraft.thizzrini_arena.cha:
#TONIGHT AT THE THIZZRINI
COMING TO THE SAND: Lysa Sixfeathers of Haven, against the Ash-Maw of Rawlkha, a bear who will not be named. The crowd shall be fed, the loser shall be forgotten, and the arena shall be left as it was found.
In the margin: 'The Ash-Maw won. The crowd was not fed. The arena was not left as found. The stands are still there.'
place_lore.nirncraft.thizzrini_arena.hoo: A ruined arena grown over with vines and jungle roots, where Bosmer and Khajiit champions once fought for sport and the stands still hold their echoes of cheers.
place_lore.nirncraft.thizzrini_arena.rum: The arena has no gate. The vines closed it. Locals say they can hear the crowd on a still night, and the fight, and the final roar.
place_lore.nirncraft.thorn.gazetteer.p0:
#Names under the tree
Hist-Keeper Eeka hums to the pool and will not say what it answers. Walker Yill knows every root-walk and has fallen off most. Sap-Cutter Horu asks the tree before he cuts, and the tree decides. Hush-Moss at the Root Cellar serves what the tree gives that day. It gave soup.
place_lore.nirncraft.thorn.gazetteer.p1:
#Rules of the rite
Never hold the blade by the edge. Never speak while the tree listens. If the tree sighs, stop and wait. If it bleeds gold, you have been polite. Carry the cup to the pool in the dark. Do not look at the eyes in the bark; they look at you only once.
place_lore.nirncraft.thorn.hook: A hub-town hung from the roots of one enormous Hist tree, its huts swaying on rope-walks above a sap-lit pool, where every hatchling drinks once and sees what it will.
^THE THIRD ROOT
Where the bark is soft as a cheek, you may cut. Where it is hard, you may not. The tree knows the difference. So will you, if you have been quiet.
place_lore.nirncraft.thorn.rumour: The Hist-Keeper of Thorn has asked for a stranger to drink at the pool, they say, and a stranger the Hist asks for does not usually say no.

place_lore.nirncraft.thrall_cove.hook: A slavers' former cove with rotting pens on a half-tide beach and a cliff stair of rusted rings.
place_lore.nirncraft.thrall_cove.rumour: Thrall Cove's freedmen all have a palm-leaf pinned to their coat. They don't say what they plant.
place_lore.nirncraft.thrall_cove.web.p0: The bearer, being free, agrees to plant and tend such palms as the lord shall provide, in such place as shall be named, for a period of twenty years. The bearer will be told the place when needed. The bearer will not be told why. Wages paid in water.
place_lore.nirncraft.throat_of_the_world: The highest peak in Tamriel, where the sky seems close enough to touch and the wind howls in the voice of dragons. Few who climb past High Hrothgar ever come down to speak of it.
Nobody climbs past High Hrothgar. There's a wind up there that tears a man off his feet. Some say a dragon sits on the summit, but who'd believe that?

Folio #42 (579, 652): Field inspection recorded for Throat Of The World within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #42 for throat_of_the_world: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Throat Of The World are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

~Here the world ends and the sky begins,
~Here Kyne breathed first upon the land,
~Here the dragons came to talk with time,
~Here the cold wind takes the climber's hand.
Under it, carved deep: 'I climbed for the view. I stayed for the silence. If you are reading this, look east. There is nothing in Tamriel you cannot see from here except yourself.'

Further down the stone, so faint it might be weather and not writing: 'There was a great grey shape on the peak when I came. It watched me carve this. It did not move, and it did not harm me. I think it was very old, and very tired, and glad of the company.'

place_lore.nirncraft.tiger_plains_villag: A mountain village of curved-roof pagodas on rice terraces, a vermilion shrine gate, bamboo and paper lanterns, the most alien place in the pack, with a roofline that is long, low and level.
The village of Tiger Plains does not lock its doors. It has no need. The tiger sees to that. It has been asleep for sixty years, and the thieves still check, very carefully, before they try.

~The water falls from step to step,
~each field a mirror, each a sky;
~the farmer bows, and does not know
~she plants a thousand moons in rows.
Mei has copied it, she says, from the lid of a very old rice-bowl. The poet was a farmer. He never wrote anything else. He did not need to.

place_lore.nirncraft.tolvalds_cave.falme:
Crude scratches cut into a shell of chaurus chitin, arranged around a carving of a lantern with rays coming out of it. Someone who has seen Falmer shrines before has added a note in the margin of the scratchings:

'They've made a god of it. A lantern that burned for weeks in the dark. They'll fight to keep it, I'd wager. You don't give up a god easily, even a stolen one.'
place_lore.nirncraft.tolvalds_cave.hook: A deep cave in the north-eastern mountains named for the young Nord who went in looking for glory and found the Falmer instead. His mother still leaves a lantern burning for him.
place_lore.nirncraft.tolvalds_cave.rumou: Tolvald went into that cave years ago. Never came out. His mother still lights a lantern in her window every night. Breaks your heart, it does.
place_lore.nirncraft.tolvalds_cave.sk4_n: Folio #35 (2535, 630): Field inspection recorded for Tolvalds Cave within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.tolvalds_cave.tolva:
#Day one
Mother gave me her brass lantern, the one Father carried in the Great War. 'So you can find your way home,' she said. I laughed. I'm twenty. I don't need to find my way home.

#Day six
The cave goes down into a city of the snow elves. They're blind, but they hear everything. I hear them too, now. Clicking. Always clicking.

#Day ?
Lantern oil nearly gone. I keep it lit anyway. I've hidden in a side passage near a pool of glowing mushrooms. If someone finds this, take the lantern home to her. She lives in Riften, by the canal. Tell her I tried to come home. Tell her it was dark.

A dynasty's necropolis with named sarcophagi and a family tree carved on the great wall, each room one king.
The Tomb of Lost Kings has an eighth door that some days is there and some days is not.

place_lore.nirncraft.tomb_of_the_apostat: A hollow great tree whose heartwood is carved with tombs, stairs spiralling inside the trunk.
At dusk the hollow tree sings. The Pact-wardens put their hands over their ears and call it wind.

One panel gone from the heartwood: a carving of a crowned figure with its face hollowed out. The tree is not a tomb for the Pact's dead; it was a tomb for something older, planted over it to keep it quiet. The apostates' chant, I now suspect, was never to the great walker. It was to the thing in the heartwood.

Walk to us, great walker, tree of ten thousand roots. Walk to us who have been forgotten by the Pact. We offer the hollow, we offer the dark, we offer the quiet that is not a death. Walk and be ours. Walk and be still.
place_lore.nirncraft.tomb_of_the_moon_si: A choir-tomb of echoing chambers, each room tuned to a note of the moon's phase, cut into an Anequina hill.
The Moon Singers' tomb hums a note lower than it did when my mother was a kitten.

~Low is the moon and the note is low,~low is the song where the singers go.~Three keys for the gates, and a choir for each,~and the vault to the blades is a thing out of reach.~Sing it true, sing it true, sing it true,~till the moon rises up and is late no more.

place_lore.nirncraft.torval.caravan_plea:
To the brave, the foolish, and the well-paid:
This one's caravan of the clan Ra'zhan stopped for water at the Peryite stones north of the city. The water was clean. The air was not. By morning her cousins were coughing, and by evening they were walking in rows around the dragon-statue, counting.

This one ran. This one is ashamed. The clan's caravan bell is still on the lead wagon, and without it the clan cannot be called home, for the bell is how the Ra'zhan call their dead to the Lattice. Find Ri'jasha in the market of Torval. She will pay with everything she has left, which is not much, and with her gratitude, which is a great deal.
place_lore.nirncraft.torval.dance_notice:
^The Two-Moons Dance comes.
All are welcome in the great court of Torval at the rising of both moons. Bring a lamp for the dead. Bring a song for the living. Do not bring skooma; the Temple guard will take it, and they will not give it back, and they will look very happy.

To the pilgrims from Cyrodiil: the dance is not a performance. You will be asked to join. To refuse is not an insult, but it is noticed, and the moons have long memories. Better to dance badly than not at all. This one has seen Imperials dance. It is very bad. The moons forgave them anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.torval.hook: The capital of Elsweyr and holy city of the Moon-Priests, where the Temple of the Lattice crowns the hill, moon sugar is blessed in great vats, and the Two-Moons Dance fills the streets each year.
place_lore.nirncraft.torval.rumour: Torval is the holiest city of the Khajiit, and the busiest. The Moon-Bishop is blessing sugar, the caravans are selling it, and poor Ri'jasha in the market is begging someone to go to the Peryite stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.torval.sugar_blessi: Moon sugar is the moonlight that falls on the sand of Elsweyr and is caught by the cane. It is holy. To eat it is to taste the Lattice. To boil it into skooma is to taste the Lattice too much, and fall through.

The sugar of the Temple fields is blessed each night under the moons by three priests, who sing the Riddle'Thar until the vats glow. Unblessed sugar is still sweet. But only blessed sugar remembers where it came from, and so the one who eats it remembers too.
This is why the skooma-cooks raid our fields. They do not want sugar. They want to forget, and blessed sugar is the hardest to make forget.

#BY THE HAND THAT HOLDS THE HEAVENS
Let every room be swept. Let every lamp be lit. Let every table be laid. The guests will come in their time, and I will not have it said that Ka Po' Tun was caught unready.
A servant has scrawled beneath: 'We have swept for eleven hundred years. The table is laid. Nobody has come. I am beginning to suspect that we were the guests.'
place_lore.nirncraft.tosh_rakas_palace.h: A palace of vermilion and black lacquer on a spur of the Ka Po' Tun, its roofs curved like drawn bows, built by an emperor who was never seen to leave it.
place_lore.nirncraft.tosh_rakas_palace.r: The palace has nine hundred rooms, and the emperor used one. The rest were built for the people who he believed would come and did not.

place_lore.nirncraft.tower_of_mzark.hook: A Dwemer tower rising from the snowy hills east of Stonehills, its brass dome open to the stars. Something inside it was built to look at the sky through more than glass.
place_lore.nirncraft.tower_of_mzark.mage: The tower is a surface terminus, connected by shaft to the deep works below. Its dome houses a lens array of extraordinary complexity, still aligned, still lubricated, still waiting. There is a cradle at the focus for some object the size of a scroll case. Without that object, the array focuses nothing.

I attempted to turn the main dial and was gently, but firmly, prevented by the dial. I record that a Dwemer mechanism has better manners than most of my colleagues. I record also that I heard a voice from the shaft. I did not record what it said, because I left.
place_lore.nirncraft.tower_of_mzark.rumo: The Tower of Mzark hums at night. Go up close and you can hear gears turning, like it's waiting for somebody. Whoever it's waiting for, I hope they're not from round here.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_post.bjorl:
Mother,
Hollyfrost is two hours' walk from here. I can see the smoke of the Hlaalu chimney from the ridge on clear days. I could be at your door by supper and I have not gone, because Kolgeir watches the path and he means what he signed.

I did not run because I was afraid. I ran because of what I was told to do to the men at the picket, and because I did it, once, before I ran. Tell no one that. Tell them I died somewhere cold and brave. It is nearly true.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_post.deser: Bjorlam Frost-Hand, Kolgeir, and Ulfa Grey-Eye
We three, having seen what was done at the picket on the Winterhold road to men who surrendered, swear that we are done with Ulfric's war and Ulfric's Palace and Ulfric's quartermaster.
The strongbox is ours by right, for four months' pay we were never given. We split it three ways, and none of us leaves this cabin alone before the thaw, for a man alone talks.

Any of us who sells the others to the Palace will be found. Any of us who sells the others to the Legion will be found faster.
^Signed in blood, which Kolgeir says is foolish, and which he signed anyway.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_post.hook: A lonely cabin in the hills east of Windhelm, named for a betrayal nobody remembers and now living up to it: Stormcloak deserters have holed up there with a stolen payroll.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_post.rumou: Smoke's been rising from Traitor's Post all month. The quartermaster's lost a strongbox and three soldiers, and I'd wager they're all keeping warm by the same fire.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_post.sk4_n: Folio #10 (2265, -713): Field inspection recorded for Traitors Post within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #10 for traitors_post: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Traitors Post are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_vault.hook: A vault of false doors on Artaeum where each room offers three exits, two of which loop back through mirrors.
place_lore.nirncraft.traitors_vault.rumo: The Traitor's Vault has more doors than rooms. The ones that open lead to the same place.
A hundred false doors, one real. The real one is the wall. Do not break it with a sword; use a hammer that remembers. The reward behind it is not gold but a thing the Order wished to forget, and they have paid me well for forgetting. I have forgotten. I am frightened at how easily.

^THE VOW IS A GIFT, NOT A CHAIN.
^A MAN WHO BREAKS IT FOR LOVE HAS NOT BROKEN IT.
^A MAN WHO BREAKS IT FOR VANITY HAS NOT KEPT IT.

The Abbot has added in a different, smaller hand: 'I am away three weeks, on pilgrimage to the Isle of Contemplation. If any brother has done a great wrong, I ask that he wait to be forgiven until my return, and not, in the meanwhile, forgive himself.'
A monastery of a silent vow on the Summerset shore, where a novice has broken it and will say why only to a stranger.
The monks of Trebbite are not forbidden to speak. They have simply never found anything worth the effort. Speak to one, and you will be given a very long, very kind look, and a bowl of soup.
place_lore.nirncraft.treva_cascade_falls: A stepped series of mossy waterfalls where the Treva River drops out of the birch highlands toward Lake Honrich.
Anglers at Ivarstead swear the pools under Treva Cascade Falls hold pearls inside the river-mussels.

Folio #60 (880, 1480): Field inspection recorded for Treva Cascade Falls within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #60 for treva_cascade_falls: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Treva Cascade Falls are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

When the white water covers the third granite step of the cascade, the lower footbridges toward Lake Honrich will be awash by noon. Left a pair of gaff-hooks and a creel in the dry cleft behind the spray.
place_lore.nirncraft.treva_crossing_camp: A riverside camp beside the stone ford of the Treva, where scouts monitor the western approaches to the hold.
Travelers fording near Treva's Watch say the soldiers at the crossing camp check every saddlebag for contraband skooma and stolen silver.

Folio #59 (800, 1880): Field inspection recorded for Treva Crossing Camp within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

The water at the Treva ford is knee-deep after the autumn rains, slowing the supply carts from Ivarstead. Keep two bowmen watching the broken battlements of Treva's Watch upstream; mercenary deserters are still holding the inner courtyard.
place_lore.nirncraft.trevas_watch.hook: A walled fort on a rocky spur west of Lake Honrich, built by the old Treva line and now squatted by bandits who call themselves the rightful lords of the river country.
place_lore.nirncraft.trevas_watch.rumour: There's a bandit chief at Treva's Watch called Saltcheek. Broke the Sarethi hand's arm for trying to save a nirnroot. A nirnroot!
place_lore.nirncraft.trevas_watch.saltch:
#What the river country owes the Watch
Sarethi Farm: twelve nirnroot, taken. Alchemist in Riften pays nine septims a root. That's more than a year of tithe from a cabbage farm.
Heartwood Mill: nothing yet. The Knives at Faldar's Tooth claim the mill. We'll see.
Stormcloak camp: they pay in nothing but threats. Leave them be.

My mother was a Treva on the wrong side of the blanket. That makes this my fort and this my land. A court in Riften would laugh at that. A court in Riften laughs at a lot of things, and it isn't laughing at me.
place_lore.nirncraft.trevas_watch.sk4_no: Folio #25 (1463, 1196): Field inspection recorded for Trevas Watch within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.trevas_watch.treva_:
^TREVA HOLDS THE RIVER
^THE RIVER HOLDS THE LAND
^THE LAND HOLDS THE DEAD

The old letters have been gouged with a knife, and new ones scratched in: SALTCHEEK HOLDS THE LOT. Someone else has added, smaller, beneath: for now.

The Treva family held this spur for three generations, taxing the river barges that came down from the Darkwater toward Lake Honrich. The last of the true line died without heirs in the year of the Red Mountain ash-fall, and the fort passed to the hold. The hold let it rot. Now anyone with a sharp enough knife and a loud enough voice can call themselves its lord, and the farmers between the river and the lake pay for it.

place_lore.nirncraft.tumble_arch_pass.ca:
This one writes for the next caravan.
Giants under the arch. They do not like bells. They do not like music. They do not like Ri'saad's cousin, who rang a bell and played music. Ri'saad's cousin is now a little flatter than before.

Go round by Korvanjund, or wait for night when the giants sleep and walk softly. Do not ring bells. Do not be Ri'saad's cousin.
May your road lead you to warm sands.

^Postscript from a second Khajiit
This one adds: the giants also do not like moon sugar. They do not like it when you throw it at them. That one tried. It does not distract them. It only makes them sticky and more angry.
place_lore.nirncraft.tumble_arch_pass.ho: A natural rock arch over the road in the hills of the eastern Pale, with giants camped beneath it. Travellers must choose between a long detour and a short, loud conversation.
place_lore.nirncraft.tumble_arch_pass.ru: Tumble Arch? Giants under it, like trolls under a bridge. You can go round. It takes a day. Most folk take the day.

place_lore.nirncraft.tuwhaccas_throne.ho: A ceremonial throne-hall of an ancient king with a procession of statues, colossal doors and a long colonnade.
place_lore.nirncraft.tuwhaccas_throne.ru: At Tuwhacca's Throne the statues' heads all face a door. Some mornings one has moved.
place_lore.nirncraft.tuwhaccas_throne.th: The east arm of the throne was cut away in the dry season by a thief who left the sword and the ring and took only this. The arm bore a name in a script I have not seen anywhere else. I copied it before the arm was taken. It reads: HOLLOW. I do not know what else. I am afraid to say it twice.
place_lore.nirncraft.tuwhaccas_throne.we: LET NO WELL RUN DRY WHILE I SLEEP. LET EVERY CARAVAN PAY. LET THE CITY OPEN ONLY WHEN THE LAST CUP IS RETURNED. This is the word of the sand, which is more patient than any king.
A hidden temple of Nocturnal, sunk into the hills of western Falkreath behind an unmarked door. Few know what it guards. Fewer come back to tell.

I came to the Sepulcher to beg the Lady of Shadows for a little of her luck, as thieves have done for an age. The door was cold. The air beyond it was colder. The halls are full of the old guardians, and they do not sleep as Nord draugr sleep. They walk in shadow and stop when you look straight at them.

I did not reach the inner shrine. I left a coin on the step and a lockpick broken in two, which is the custom, and backed out without turning round, which is also the custom. Outside, a raven sat on the lintel and watched me all the way to the trees.
There's a temple out in the west woods that no priest of the Nine will name. A woman in a grey hood asked me the way once. I told her I didn't know. She smiled like she knew I did.

Folio #29 (-1440, 1160): Field inspection recorded for Twilight Sepulcher within Falkreath Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

~Lady of the unlit hour, keep what we have hidden.
~Lady of the empty purse, fill it before dawn.
~We watch the door you gave us.
~We sleep only when the shadow says we may.

Written in silver ink that seems to fade under direct light and return in the dark.
Folded into the vellum is a small strip of grey cloth, the kind used to wrap a lockpick, and a note in a different, hurried hand: 'Left for the Lady, with thanks for the house on the hill in Riften that was empty that one night. Will repay in kind.'

place_lore.nirncraft.twyllbek_ruins.hook: A tumbled Imperial survey-post on the plateau road, its archive niche sealed under a lead cap nobody has lifted in two hundred years.
place_lore.nirncraft.twyllbek_ruins.rumo: The old survey ruins on the Gideon road hold a lead tube with the original grant of the Eastern Cut. Folk say it was never lost, only filed under the wrong river.
place_lore.nirncraft.twyllbek_ruins.surv:
#Surveyed and recorded
The Cut to the road. The road to the people. The people to the stones. We have set this post so that it may be found by those who need it, and missed by those who do not. A lead tube is in the niche, capped, dated, signed. Read it before you build a fence.

place_lore.nirncraft.urshilaku_camp.hook: An Ashlander camp of yurts under hide, a wise woman's fire in the centre, and sleeping-mats ringed in ash-cord.
place_lore.nirncraft.urshilaku_camp.rumo: The Urshilaku wise woman has been saying the ash is awake and has been for a year. The Temple laughs. The sleepers do not.
Hold the knot, keep the flame, say each name, do not sleep. The ash has eyes this season. The fence is wearing thin and something stands at the doorway of it, patient as a stone. Ancestors, lend me your eyes, for I have kept them closed too long.

place_lore.nirncraft.ustengrav.hook: A vast barrow beneath the Hjaalmarch marsh where Jurgen Windcaller, founder of the Way of the Voice, was laid to rest. Grave robbers and worse have dug their way in ahead of you.
place_lore.nirncraft.ustengrav.imperial_:
Sir,
As ordered, I observed the barrow at Ustengrav for two days. Grave robbers entering daily, with a robed man who walks with the dead. The Stormcloak camp to the east has also observed them. Neither camp has moved, because whoever moves first is assumed to be making a play for the barrow.

In plain words: we are leaving the tomb of the greatest Voice in Nord history to thieves because we are afraid the other side will accuse us of wanting it. I respectfully suggest that this is a very Nord problem, and that I am glad I am an Imperial.
place_lore.nirncraft.ustengrav.robber_pl: Upper level: cleared. Old pots, a few rings, a lot of dead men who didn't stay dead. Paid the necromancer to keep them down. He does it, mostly. He says he wants nothing from the tomb but 'conversation with the residents.' Mad, but useful.

Lower level: three gates that open and shut on their own, like breathing. Hagni ran at them and got caught between. We don't talk about Hagni.
Beyond the gates there's a horn on a stone hand, or so the necromancer says. Leave it. Every Nord with a sword between here and Whiterun would hunt us for it. Take the rings.
place_lore.nirncraft.ustengrav.rumour: Ustengrav's the Windcaller's tomb, they say. Grave robbers have been at it for a month, and a necromancer came with them. The Legion camp's right next door and does nothing. Too busy watching the Stormcloaks do nothing.
place_lore.nirncraft.uttering_hills_cave: Bertrand Vanne, of the Imperial Geographical Society, held here eleven days. They took my survey of the Mzulft approaches. I have redrawn it on this wall from memory because I am too stubborn to let it be lost: south-east past Cragwallow Slope, the domes visible from the third ridge.
If I do not leave this place, I ask whoever reads this to tell the Society that the domes are warmer than they ought to be, and that something inside Mzulft is still awake.
A bandit hole in the hills west of Windhelm, where a chief who prices everything in pairs holds the road from Anga's Mill and charges a toll in coin or fingers.
Uttering Hills Cave belongs to Hadring Two-Coins. Pay him twice what he asks and he lets you pass. Pay him once and he keeps one of your hands as change.

Folio #13 (1329, -439): Field inspection recorded for Uttering Hills Cave within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #13 for uttering_hills_cave: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Uttering Hills Cave are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
One. Everything costs two. Two coins to pass, two days' food for a cart, two fingers if they argue. A man remembers a price that comes in pairs.
Two. Nobody touches the timber carts from Anga's Mill. Their foreman pays us every month to leave him be. If he stops, then we touch the carts, and then we touch the foreman.
Three. The Breton's book stays in my chest. I don't care if it's 'scholarly'. Somebody in Windhelm will pay for it, and they'll pay two.

place_lore.nirncraft.vahloks_tomb.assist:
Master Nerano,
As instructed I entered the Jailor's tomb with charcoal, paper, and a very good lantern. I took eleven rubbings of the inscriptions in the long hall. They describe an oath sworn by Vahlok to keep a certain prisoner from ever returning to the world. The prisoner is not named. Everyone in the inscriptions is extremely careful not to name him.

At the twelfth rubbing the dead woke up. I ran, and dropped the satchel with all eleven rubbings in the long hall, beside the brazier with the dragon carved on it. I will not be going back. I would like to discuss my wages. Fendryn.
place_lore.nirncraft.vahloks_tomb.hook: The sealed tomb of Vahlok the Jailor, a dragon priest who stood guard against his own kind in the old days. Scholars want rubbings from its walls; its guardians want them to leave.
place_lore.nirncraft.vahloks_tomb.jailor:
Cut into the stone above the sarcophagus, in old Nordic, with a translation pencilled beneath by a living hand: I who served the dragons will watch the one who betrayed them. I will not sleep while he sleeps. I will not wake until he wakes. Let the island be my cell and his, and let my bones be the bars.
In the margin: He has started waking, then. I don't like that at all.

Under the pencil, scrawled in charcoal by a different scholar: Ulvo, do not send another assistant here. The Jailor is awake, and he is not angry with us. He is afraid. A dragon priest afraid. Think about that before you publish anything.
place_lore.nirncraft.vahloks_tomb.rumour: Vahlok's Tomb belongs to a dragon priest who turned warden. A scholar from Tel Mithryn sent his assistant to take rubbings of the walls. The assistant came back without the rubbings and without his eyebrows.
place_lore.nirncraft.valley_of_scars.hoo: A canyon whose walls are carved with battle-reliefs from rim to floor, in a rust-red stone.
place_lore.nirncraft.valley_of_scars.rum: A fresh scene appears on the Valley of Scars each season. Guides now sell tours before it fills in.
place_lore.nirncraft.valley_of_scars.web: The panels used to be old. Now they are new. A dozen figures on a stair, and one of them has a face I have seen in my tour-books. Each season another is carved. Nobody sees the chisel. I tell visitors it is only a trick of the light. It is not a trick of the light.

place_lore.nirncraft.valtheim_towers.hoo: Twin ruined towers bridging the river road east of Whiterun, held by raiders who charge a toll to cross. Lately their chief has a voice that shakes the stones.
place_lore.nirncraft.valtheim_towers.mer:
To any honest guard of Whiterun,
This one's caravan paid the Valtheim toll twice in a month, and was robbed anyway at Guldun Rock, where the giants took our salt and the raiders took what the giants left.

Khajiit are patient. Khajiit are not THIS patient. The towers stand on the Jarl's road, and the Jarl's road should not belong to a man who shouts down bridges. If Whiterun will not clear them, perhaps Windhelm will. This one does not care which flag flies over the towers, so long as the toll is less than our whole wagon.
place_lore.nirncraft.valtheim_towers.rum: Valtheim Towers is a toll-gate now, and the toll goes up every week. The new chief there shouts so loud he knocks men off the bridge. Even the Greybeards have heard of him, they say.
place_lore.nirncraft.valtheim_towers.sk4: Folio #32 (866, -101): Field inspection recorded for Valtheim Towers within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #32 for valtheim_towers: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Valtheim Towers are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.valtheim_towers.tol:
^VALTHEIM CROSSING
^Tolls by order of the master of the towers
On foot: 20 septims
On horse: 50
Cart: 100, or the cart
Anyone wearing Stormcloak blue or Legion red: double
Anyone who argues: the river

Below, scrawled: 'The master says the toll goes up again on Morndas. He says he can feel the stone sing when he shouts at it. He says a lot of things. Nobody's arguing. Hjorvald argued. Hjorvald's in the river.'

Nobody's crossing much either, these days, except the giants from Guldun Rock, and they don't pay.
place_lore.nirncraft.valthume.hook: A sealed Nordic barrow in the hills south of Old Hroldan, where the dead of an ancient war were buried with their weapons and, some say, their oaths still unbroken.
place_lore.nirncraft.valthume.ketil_lett:
To whoever opens this tomb in a kinder age.
The soldier Ketil fought for Hjalti when Old Hroldan was taken. He died in my inn, in the upstairs room, with his shield still on his arm. The Reachmen's dead are buried here in Valthume and the Nords' dead were laid beside them, because there was no time to separate friend from foe.

Ketil's shield was taken into Valthume by mistake with the others. Since then he walks the upstairs room at night looking for it. He is a kind ghost. He fixes the shutters. But he is not at rest.
If you can bring his shield back to the inn, hang it on the wall above the bed. My family will keep the lamp lit for him until then. I have made my children swear it.
place_lore.nirncraft.valthume.rumour: Ulfgar the Lamp-Keeper at Old Hroldan tells a story about Valthume and the ghost in his inn. The story's long. The ale's cheap. Go on.
place_lore.nirncraft.valthume.sk4_note_4: Folio #44 (-2138, 377): Field inspection recorded for Valthume within The Reach Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.valthume.valthume_w:
Rendered from the ancient runes:
Here lie together Reach and Nord, for the war ended at the grave's edge and not before. Let none who sleep here wake to fight again.
Someone has carved beneath it, much later: The dead did not listen. The warden of this hall still fights, and every shield in the barrow is his now. He will not give them back. You will have to take them.

Lower still, faint and recent: Ketil's shield is the round one with the hawk painted on it, faded nearly away. I saw it on the warden's arm as he passed me in the dark. He was holding it the way a man holds a stolen thing he means to keep. I did not ask him to give it back. You may have more courage than I did.

place_lore.nirncraft.vault_of_the_heaven: A sealed vault of lunar weapons, a long hall of racked blades that wake when moonlight enters the skylights and an antechamber of three keyed moon-gates.
The vault's blades hum at moonrise. Folk say they have started to hum before the moon comes.
THREE KEYS, THREE NOTES, THREE MOONRISES. Do not enter before the moon. Do not enter after. The blades wake to the moon that is, not the moon that was. If the moon is late, the blades are hungry.
place_lore.nirncraft.velothi_border_pick: A high wind-swept picket station watching the eastern mountain saddle between Skyrim and Morrowind.
Soldiers up at the Velothi Border Picket burn pine pitch just to keep their fingers warm enough to draw a bowstring.

Snow has drifted six feet against the eastern palisade, burying the mile-markers toward the border arch. Two ash-salt peddlers passed through at noon reporting rockslides along the lower switchbacks. We have rationed the firewood to three logs a watch until the pack-mules get through from the valley.
A wind-swept crag and ruined watch-beacon high on the eastern border wall overlooking the passes toward Morrowind.
Goatherds on the eastern crags say you can see the ash-plumes of the distant east from the Velothi Crag Eyrie on a clear morning.

Folio #63 (960, 1560): Field inspection recorded for Velothi Crag Eyrie within The Rift Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #63 for velothi_crag_eyrie: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Velothi Crag Eyrie are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Three tar-barrels and a stack of dry juniper branches stored under the stone overhang beside the beacon brazier. The wind up here tears the shingles off any timber roof, so only dry-laid granite holds against the winter gales.
place_lore.nirncraft.velothi_refugee_cai: A weathered stone cairn and sunken vault along the eastern pass where families fleeing the Red Year buried what heirlooms they could no longer carry.
Refugees coming down the Velothi road still stop at the old cairn to leave ash-yam cakes, though grave-robbers have been prying at the lower stones.

Here beneath the boundary stones of the western pass we laid the bone-ash urns of three cousins who did not survive the blizzard above Blacklight. Let no Nord bailiff or mountain outlaw disturb these niches; there is no gold within, only clay seals, family signets, and prayers to the Reclamations.

place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.canton_ledger:
#Rents collected, Hearthfire
The Dren cousins, ground floor: paid in full, with a note complaining of the smell of the Waterworks. Complaint filed under 'water'.
The Argonian fishmonger Sweet-Tail: paid in full in fish. Fish accepted at market rate minus the smell.

Unit 14, upper tier: unpaid three months. The tenant is a 'scholar of the Boethiah stones' and says he will pay when the Prince of Plots grants him a fortune. Councillor Curio says to leave him be, as he finds the man amusing. I find him behind in his rent. We are both right.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.gazetteer.p0:
#Who is where
Warden Telyne Aryon keeps the canton stairs, mornings, and knows which are loose. Tosa the Cantonkeeper minds the water-gates; find her at low tide, never at flood. Brother Fendil sells blessings on the Temple stairs at any hour that has pilgrims. Hlenil Dro ferries to every canton and will not discuss what lies under the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.gazetteer.p1:
#Inns, shops and small secrets
The Sunken Lantern (Ruvene Olvyn) charges by the flight of stairs to your room; she has counted them all. Bethal's Dry Goods and Wet Alibis sells umbrellas in a city where it never rains. The handles are hollow. Do not ask. The Last Stair at the Palace gate is a wall; the hospice behind the shrine, sixteen cots, is not.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.hook: The great canton city on the water south of Vvardenfell, seat of the Archcanon and the Morag Tong, where pilgrims climb the stairs of the Temple and every canton is a town with its own feud.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.pilgrim_guide: Brother Llevel of the Foreign Quarter

Welcome, pilgrim. You will want to go everywhere at once. Do not. The cantons are larger than they look and the bridges are longer than they feel, and the guar-hide sandals sold in the Foreign Quarter will not last the climb to the High Fane.

Do pray at the shrines of the Tribunal. Do not pray aloud at the shrines of the old Daedra, the Reclamations, even though the Temple honours them now. The older priests still flinch.
Do not ask an Ordinator for directions. Do not ask a Morag Tong agent anything at all. If someone in the Arena canton offers you a good price on anything, it is not a good price.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivec.rumour: Vivec's cantons still stand, those the sea didn't take. Walk the bridges at night and you'll hear three languages, four prayers and at least one Morag Tong writ being read out loud.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivecs_antlers.hook: Two giant antlered peaks over the Stonefalls coast, one broken, with a pilgrims' ladder rungs worn smooth.
place_lore.nirncraft.vivecs_antlers.rumo: The pilgrims' ladder on the broken antler goes up and the pilgrims go up and I have never seen one come down.
THE LADDER ENDS WHERE THE FAITHFUL DO. Take off your shoes at the bottom: you shall not need them. The quiet house welcomes all who climb with a quiet heart. Do not look down.
place_lore.nirncraft.volenfell.hook: A Dwemer ruin under a dune, half-flooded with sand, with mechanical halls and drifts.
place_lore.nirncraft.volenfell.rumour: Volenfell hums when the wind is right. The old shepherds say it drinks.
place_lore.nirncraft.volenfell.thread.p0: Found under a dune, a bronze plate with a hand that moves. I did not touch it. It ticked all night. At dawn a second hand appeared on the same dial, thin as a hair, and began to move faster. I do not like it. I have covered it with a goat-skin. I have asked a priest. He said it is not a prayer.
place_lore.nirncraft.volenfell.web.p0: PUMP SEVEN: DRAWS FOR THE KING OF THE SAND. Do not stop while the king still lives. When the king is dead, continue until the king is remembered. Pump Seven shall not be stopped by the living.
place_lore.nirncraft.volskygge.eirik_jou:
#3rd of Frostfall
Made the summit. The door was open, which a sensible man would take as a warning. I took it as an invitation. Father's axe is heavy but it's the only thing of his I have, and it would be a poor thing to come all this way and not use it.

#4th of Frostfall
The dead walk here, just like the stories. I've killed two. The third had a face of iron and a voice like a rockslide, and I ran. I've barricaded myself in a side chamber. My torch is half gone.
#5th of Frostfall
If Ragnvald were here, we'd have done this together. But he's gone to the Stormcloaks, and Mother is alone at the bridge, and I wanted to come home with something that would make her stop crying. Stupid. Stupid.
place_lore.nirncraft.volskygge.hook: An ancient barrow high in the western mountains of Haafingar, where a dragon priest once listened to the sky. A young treasure hunter from Dragon Bridge climbed up to it a week ago.
place_lore.nirncraft.volskygge.hulda_let:
Eirik,
I am putting this in your pack because you won't listen when I say it. You don't need gold. You don't need a barrow. You don't need to prove anything to your brother, who is off in a camp somewhere in a blue coat proving things to Ulfric.

I lost your father to the sea and I have lost Ragnvald to the war. Come back with nothing and I will cook you the best supper of your life. Come back with treasure and I'll cook the same supper and scold you through it. But come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.volskygge.priest_ta:
HERE THE PRIEST WHO LISTENED.
HE STOOD ON THE MOUNTAIN AND HEARD THE SKY SPEAK, AND THE SKY SPOKE ONLY TO HIM.
HIS WARDEN HROKK STANDS AT THE DOOR, IRON-JAWED, UNSLEEPING.

LET NO MAN COME UP WHO HAS NOT BEEN CALLED.
LET NO MAN GO DOWN WHO HAS HEARD WHAT HE HEARD.
THE WIND KEEPS HIS SECRETS. THE WIND KEEPS EVERYTHING.
THE PEOPLE OF THE VALLEY BROUGHT HIM BREAD AND SALT EACH SPRING, AND HE TOLD THEM WHEN THE STORMS WOULD COME. WHEN HE DIED THEY BROUGHT NO MORE BREAD, AND THE STORMS CAME WITHOUT WARNING.
place_lore.nirncraft.volskygge.rumour: Volskygge? It's a barrow on a mountaintop, and the wind up there could strip a goat bald. Hulda's boy Eirik went up looking for treasure. Hulda's been at the bridge every evening since, watching the road.
place_lore.nirncraft.volunruud.hook: A Nordic tomb hidden in the hills of the western Pale, where a rich and nervous stranger has been seen meeting cloaked figures at night.
place_lore.nirncraft.volunruud.mercenary: We're paid to keep the road clear while the gentleman meets his friends in the crypt. Two hundred septims, and we never see the friends. They come up the back way. The gentleman says nobody speaks of this, ever.

Fine by me. Except Ragnar swears that one of the friends walked right past him in the dark and he never heard a footstep. Ragnar's not right since. Keeps checking behind him. I'm starting to check behind me too.
Last night the gentleman left in a hurry and dropped a scrap of paper with a black hand on it. I burned it. Some things you don't want to be holding when the Jarl's guards come by.
place_lore.nirncraft.volunruud.rumour: Somebody's using Volunruud for secret meetings. Fine clothes, soft hands, Imperial accent. You don't go to a draugr tomb to sell a horse.
place_lore.nirncraft.volunruud.warrior_i:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
Here sleeps the warrior who would not kneel, and here his axe sleeps apart from him, lest the two of them wake together and remember their old quarrel with the world.
Whoever joins axe to hand, joins the warrior to his anger. Let them make sure their own anger is large enough to hold his.

^Copyist's remark
I have heard that someone has lately been holding meetings among these very carvings. One hopes they are not the sort of people to read old warnings as instructions.

place_lore.nirncraft.waterdancer_falls.f:
~She danced at the lip of the falling water,
~she danced where the rainbow is born,
~and the spray was her skirt, and the spray was her daughter,
~and she danced till the dawn, and the dawn.
place_lore.nirncraft.waterdancer_falls.h: A tall waterfall in Reaper's March whose spray throws a standing rainbow, and where, on still days, the spray appears to move in time with a tune you almost remember.
place_lore.nirncraft.waterdancer_falls.r: They say a dancer once leapt from the top of the falls and did not fall, and that her feet are still on the water. Look, at the right hour, and you may see ripples that are not from the stream.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest.apothecary_:
^REMEDIES FOR EVERY SEASON
^Penhallow's, at the Sign of the Mortar, by the Fish Bridge
Fevers broken, coughs quieted, boils lanced with a steady hand and clean steel. Tinctures of blessed thistle for the lungs. Salts of nightshade, carefully measured, for those whose sleep has fled. No charms. No curses lifted. No questions about the fen-sickness answered after dark.

Below, in a smaller and less steady hand: 'To whoever took the green-bound case from my cart on the Peryite road: keep the silver. Return the papers. There are forty years of cures in them, and one recipe I would rather no one ever read. Ask for me at the Mortar. I will not call the Watch.'
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest.hook: The jewel of the Iliac Bay: a merchant city of bridges, guildhalls and Breton courtesy, where the Knights of the Rose keep the peace and every honest counting-house keeps a second set of books.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest.merchant_le: Odile Marchand, cloth factor of the Lower Bridges

#Wayrest, 11th of Hearthfire
Dear Hassim,
Your dyed wool arrived, all forty bolts, and not one of them the colour you promised. I have sold them anyway, as 'Craglorn dusk', at a premium. The court ladies adore anything that sounds as if it came from a dangerous place. You owe me a dinner and an apology, in that order.

The bay crossing has doubled in price since the Saltreef business. The Knights of the Rose ride the docks every evening now, which is very good for my nerves and very bad for my smugglers. Send the next load overland by Bangkorai, and for pity's sake tell your drovers not to camp near the old shrines on the road. Two of Gaston's men did, last month. One came back. He has taken holy orders and will not say why.
Yours in profit,
Odile
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest.rumour: In Wayrest a man will bow to you, praise your boots and sell you a ship that sank last spring. Smile back, check your purse, and you'll do fine.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest.watch_notic:
^BY ORDER OF THE CAPTAIN OF THE WATCH
^Posted this 4th of Last Seed, 4E 201
Citizens are reminded that the old Daedric stones north of the city are NOT a feast-ground, a trysting place, nor a fit spot for wagers of courage. Three scorched circles have been found in the grass beside the shrine of the Prince of Ruin since Midyear, and one of them still had a boot in it.

Any citizen who sees torches on the north road after curfew is to report it at the Bay Gate, not to follow them. The Watch does not pay for funerals. The Watch does, however, pay five septims for a name. Discretion is assured; the Watch is, after all, Breton.

place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest_sewers.hook: The brick-vaulted drains beneath Wayrest, where the city's politeness runs out and its gutters begin.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest_sewers.rumo: There is a stretch of the Wayrest sewers where a ledger is said to be hidden, and the Sewer-Warden has never found it, and he has looked every day for thirty years.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayrest_sewers.ward:
^A report, in the form required by the Cormorant's house rule:
The water in the third arch has risen with the tide,
And something below it has opened its eye.
I have counted the bricks, and the bricks are all there,
But the count has been wrong since the Duchess's heir.

The overflow chamber, which was dry as a book,
Is now full of shining. I will not look.
The fox mask, the diadem, and the cold altar:
I have sealed the door and laid down the halter.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayward_pass.hook: A high pass on the Windhelm road where the Pale climbs into Winterhold. Travellers get lost in its fogs often enough that it earned its name honestly.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayward_pass.rumour: Wayward Pass? The road forks three times in the fog and only one fork goes anywhere. I've known men walk in at noon and come out at Nightgate Inn by midnight, going the wrong way.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayward_pass.sk4_no: Folio #28 (891, -1113): Field inspection recorded for Wayward Pass within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #28 for wayward_pass: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Wayward Pass are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.wayward_pass.waymar: Waymark 17: Wayward Pass. Bear north for Alftand and the glacier, which you will not want. Bear south for Nightgate Inn, which you will. Ironbind Barrow lies a short way southwest of this post; do not mistake its torches for the inn's.

The fog lies thickest in Frostfall and Sun's Dusk. If you cannot see your own hand, sit down where you are and wait. More travellers die walking in the fog than sitting in it.
B. S.
place_lore.nirncraft.weeping_giant.hook: An inn built under a toppled stone giant, whose cheek is wet at every hour and whose tears fall into a basin by the door.
place_lore.nirncraft.weeping_giant.rumou: The giant over the Weeping Giant inn weeps salt. Folk say it is the sea trying to get out.
place_lore.nirncraft.weeping_giant.threa: The tears stopped last night. The first time in a hundred and thirteen days. I sat with the cup beneath the cheek and waited, and none came, and I wept myself. I do not know why I wept. There was a lullaby in the wind and I did not recognise the tongue. It was the gentlest thing I ever heard. I did not want it to stop.
place_lore.nirncraft.weeping_giant.web.p: Day 112 of pouring. The tears do not stop. I collect them in a cup and pour the cup into the sea, and in the morning the cup is full again. The water tastes of rust and something sweeter. I asked a Direnni scholar. He did not laugh. He asked where the cellar drain leads.
place_lore.nirncraft.weeping_wamasu_fall: A high waterfall with the shape of a giant weeping creature carved into the rock behind its sheet.
The Weeping Wamasu has fallen quiet. The Argonians say it is losing its voice because the marsh has a cut in it.

~Hush, little river, the night is long.~Hush, little spring, I will sing you a song.~Hush, little fall, the tears are deep.~Hush, great mother, and go to sleep.~The world has wept enough, they say.~Close your eyes, and fade away.

~The falls once sang and now they sigh.~The wamasu weeps and the clouds go by.~A root is cut and a throat is sore,~a song unsung is a closing door.~We are the marsh and the marsh is we,~and nobody asked the old Hist tree.
A lone stone watchtower west of Whiterun, guarding the approach across the plains. Its guards have been jumpy since something with vast wings was seen over the hills.
The lads at the Western Watchtower saw something in the sky. Something big. Captain told them to keep it quiet, which is why everyone in Whiterun's heard about it.

Folio #37 (-289, 115): Field inspection recorded for Western Watchtower within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Report for the captain at Dragonsreach:
Night of the 24th. Clear sky. At the third hour Guardsman Brunolf saw a shape cross Secunda from south to north. He says it was too big for a bird and too fast for a cloud. He has been relieved of the watch and given a strong drink.

Night of the 25th. Same shape seen again by myself and by Guardsman Torsk. I have not been given a strong drink. I request one. I also request arrows, as we have nineteen between six men, and a second bell, as the first is cracked.

The giants at Bleakwind Basin have moved their mammoths to the far side of the basin. They are not afraid of us. They are afraid of something. Hreinn.
