place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_priory.hook: A grey-stone cloister with a bell tower and an orchard on the Colovian slopes, where a single clapperless bell hangs from the orchard wall.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_priory.rumou: The priory's bell rings once at night with no hand on it. The brothers say to leave it be.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_priory.web.p: Seven bells: Weynon, Sentinel's ridge, Bruma chapel, the Cloud Ruler cloister, Frostcrag, a small bell at the barrow, and Sancre Tor. A woman in grey took the Weynon clapper and left a donation. She says she keeps a vigil older than the Empire. I did not like her smile.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_stones.hook: A ring of weathered standing stones in the snowfields of the central Pale. Shepherds lead their flocks around it, never through, and nobody remembers why.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_stones.rumou: The Weynon Stones? Just old rocks. But my granda always walked around them widdershins, and my granda lived to ninety.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_stones.sheph:
~One for the fallen, two for the cold,
~Three for the lamb that never grew old,
~Four, five, six for the shepherd's lost sons,
~Seven and eight for the wolves and their runs,
~Nine for the stone that hums in the night,
~Walk round the ring and keep it in sight.

^Note from Brynja Stormquill
The shepherds' children skip around the ring singing this, always widdershins, never through. When I asked a girl why, she said, 'Because the ninth stone is listening.' When I asked what it was listening for, she ran away.
place_lore.nirncraft.weynon_stones.stone: Waymark 26: Weynon Stones. Nine stones in a broken ring, two fallen. Not Dwemer, not Nordic in any style I know. Older. The lichen on the north faces is thick as a fur.

Curious detail: the snow inside the ring melts a day earlier in spring than the snow outside it. The shepherds say the stones keep a fire under them. I put my ear to the largest stone and heard nothing, then something, then nothing. Recommend a College mage with better ears than mine.
place_lore.nirncraft.whistling_mine.fore:
THE LOWER GALLERY IS CLOSED.
The whistling is not the wind. The wind does not come down a dead-end shaft. The wind does not freeze a man's beard to the rock while he stands there with his pick. The wind does not have a face.

We broke into an ice pocket on the 3rd of Frostfall and something came out of it, long and white and bright as frost under the moon. We have three of them now, maybe four. The Jarl pays by the load and we have not raised a load in two weeks.
Any sellsword who clears the lower gallery gets the next month's ore money. I will sign that in front of a priest.
place_lore.nirncraft.whistling_mine.hook: An iron mine in the hills of eastern Winterhold, named for the wind that sings through its shafts. This winter the wind sings at night even when the air is still.
place_lore.nirncraft.whistling_mine.ore_:
Last Seed: 52 loads. Hearthfire: 47 loads. Frostfall, first week: 12 loads. Frostfall, second week: 0 loads.
Chalked underneath in another hand: Torbjorn taken by the Falmer at the Sightless Pit. Gunnhild frozen. Egil frozen. The rest of us drinking at the Frozen Hearth until someone fixes it.

Chalked underneath that, in a steadier hand: Skuli has posted a notice. Anyone who clears the lower gallery gets the next month's ore money. Most of us would pay it ourselves, just to sleep without hearing that whistle in our heads.
Chalked last: If you go down, take a torch, take a friend, and take your time. Egil didn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.whistling_mine.rumo: Whistling Mine always whistled. Now it screams. The miners quit after the third man froze solid at the ore face in the middle of a shift.
place_lore.nirncraft.whistling_mine.sk4_: Folio #21 (1689, -1333): Field inspection recorded for Whistling Mine within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #21 for whistling_mine: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Whistling Mine are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
Cut above a row of niches, each holding a body wrapped in furs gone stiff with frost: Here lie the ice-wardens of the white ridge. They kept the black ice from the hands of greed, and were buried with a sliver at their throats, that they might keep it still. Waken them only if you have come to give, not take. The wardens do not know the difference between a smuggler and a pilgrim. They have stopped caring.
Someone has scratched beneath it, in a hurry: Five of the niches are empty now. The slivers were taken from their throats. We should not have taken the slivers.
A Nordic tomb cut into the white ridge below Mortrag Peak. Its draugr wear stalhrim at their throats, and a smuggler's map says not all of their ice stayed buried.
White Ridge Barrow. The smugglers who cut stalhrim out there used it as a hiding hole. Then something in the deep rooms started taking its share.

Torvar thinks the stash is in the barrow. It was, until the dead started moving. I moved it. Stalhrim Source, west of the black ice, eleven paces past the split rock, under the slab with the Skaal hand cut into it. Ha. Let them blame the Skaal. If you are reading this, Torvar, I took my share and then some. If you are not Torvar, take it with my blessing; it is better than him having it.

Scrawled on the back in charcoal: Torvar, if you are reading the back too, you are even more of a fool than I thought. Do not go to the Glacial Cave again. The ice there is waking. I am done with ice. I am going to Windhelm to sell fish.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_deep_si: A roaring limestone sinkhole beside the White River where surface water vanishes into a dark subterranean chasm.
Log-drivers on the White River steer their rafts hard to the south bank so the current doesn't pull them into the Deep Sink.

Keep the guide-poles ready once you pass the limestone bluffs below the waterfall. A subterranean cavern swallows half the river channel here, and pale blind creatures have been seen crawling up the wet rocks on moonless nights.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_watch.b:
Right. New rules, since half of you were too drunk to stand watch on Middas.
One. Only ONE cask open at a time.
Two. The rest go to Grelka at Swindler's Den, and she pays us, and we buy food. Food, lads. Not more mead.

Three. The meadery is sending guards with its carts now. Good. Guards drink too. Leave a cask by the road with a sad face drawn on it. Works every time.
Four. The key to the store-room stays on my belt. That's not a rule, that's a warning.

Kolskegg.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_watch.h: A bandit cave on the White River south-east of Whiterun, with a lookout over the meadery road. Its band has developed a taste for Honningbrew mead and no taste at all for paying.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_watch.l:
#Turdas
Stood lookout all day. Saw a fox, two Honningbrew carts and the Stormcloak camp's smoke over the hills to the east. Kolskegg says they won't bother us, we're too small to matter. I don't like being too small to matter.

#Fredas
Kolskegg drank a whole cask and fell in the river. We pulled him out. He made us swear not to tell anyone. I am writing it down because I swore not to TELL. I am thinking of leaving. My mother is in Riverwood. She thinks I work at the mill.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_watch.r: White River Watch is where the stolen mead goes. You can hear the singing from the river some nights. Badly sung, too. Eirik at Honningbrew wants it stopped.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_river_watch.s: Folio #36 (348, 115): Field inspection recorded for White River Watch within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #36 for white_river_watch: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing White River Watch are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_rose_prison.h: A river-fort prison above the Stormhold gorge, its cells half-flooded and its last prisoner the only one who wanted to stay.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_rose_prison.r: Twelve went into the White Rose by boat at dawn and eleven came out, a scout says. The twelfth is an old man who has waited twelve years for someone to ask him a question.
place_lore.nirncraft.white_rose_prison.w:
#Day four thousand and some
I was convicted of a theft I did not commit. I was not angry for long. I have been listening ever since to the river, and I have learned the names of everything that passes. I do not wish to be freed. I wish to be asked.

If you are reading this, ask me anything. It has been a long time.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun.feud_lette: You looked at me in the market today and my father saw. He said nothing, which is worse. If your uncle hears what I think of the Empire, and mine hears what you think of Ulfric, there will be blood on the steps of Jorrvaskr and we will be the reason.

So I will not wave. I will not sit at your table in the Bannered Mare. But on Fredas, when the Companions train, I will be at the Gildergreen with a flower for Kynareth, and if a flower should go missing from my hand, I will not tell anyone who took it.

Burn this. I mean it. Burn it.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun.hook: The trading heart of Skyrim, built on a hill above the Tundra with Dragonsreach looming over the Gildergreen. Every road in the hold leads here, and every rumour too.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun.rumour: Whiterun's the only city in Skyrim where a Nord, a Khajiit and a Legionnaire can all buy the same loaf from the same baker. Jarl Balgruuf likes it that way, and the war doesn't.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun.sk4_note_6: Folio #7 (62, -68): Field inspection recorded for Whiterun within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun.steward_no:
^BY ORDER OF THE JARL
All farmsteads within a day's ride of the Plains District are to report any livestock taken from the open field, whether by wolf, giant or anything larger, to the guard captain at the main gate within two days of the loss.

Losses reported will be weighed against the grain levy of Hearthfire. Losses NOT reported will be assumed to have been sold privately, and will be taxed accordingly.

Further: the bell at the Western Watchtower is not to be rung for sport. The next fool who rings it will pay for the oil of every lamp lit in panic. Given this 3rd of Last Seed, 4E 201.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_imperial_c: A fortified Legion camp in the western Tundra, tents and palisades set to watch the road to the Reach. Its officers are short of men, short of patience and short one courier.

1. Patrols to walk the Rorikstead road at first and last light, in fours, never threes.
2. No soldier is to drink at the Frostfruit Inn in uniform. The innkeeper is sympathetic to the Empire. The patrons are not.
3. Any deserter caught is to be held for the provost at Whiterun, not hanged on the spot. We are short enough of men without hanging the ones we have.

4. ADDENDUM, 19th of Last Seed. Courier Decianus has not reached Whiterun. The dispatch case he carried holds troop dispositions for the Whiterun garrison. If those reach Windhelm, men will die. Tracks lead east from the road to the bandit hole called Swindler's Den. Any soldier, or civilian of good character, who recovers the case will be paid from my own purse.

The Legion camp out west lost a courier and a whole case of dispatches. The captain's been sending patrols up and down the road and swearing at the scouts. Somebody in Swindler's Den knows something, I'd wager.

Folio #29 (-1310, -156): Field inspection recorded for Whiterun Imperial Camp within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #29 for whiterun_imperial_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Whiterun Imperial Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Dear Mother,
The north is cold. They say it isn't cold yet, which is worse. The Nords in Rorikstead sell us cabbages at three times the price and smile while they do it.

We lost a courier last week, Decianus, the one who used to sing. The captain pretends it is about the dispatches, but I saw him sitting alone by the fire afterwards with the man's spare helmet.

I am well. I am fed. I have not had to fight anyone yet, except a mudcrab, and I won. Please send socks. Your loving son, Quintus.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_mammoth_bu: A painted stone circle and timber drying-rack on the open tundra where giants cure mammoth cheese and carved ivory.
Hunters out on the western plains give the Mammoth Butchery a wide berth; the giants there have two bull mammoths guarding the racks.

Folio #46 (-1500, -80): Field inspection recorded for Whiterun Mammoth Butchery within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #46 for whiterun_mammoth_butchery: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Whiterun Mammoth Butchery are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

Counted four carved tusks leaning against the painted boulder and three leather vats of fermented mammoth curd hanging from the cross-beams. Do not approach with drawn steel; leave a wheel of salt-brick on the flat stone and wait until the herdsmen move the bulls to water.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_siege_enca: A fortified ring of earthworks, timber mantlets, and catapult frames thrown up across the eastern approach to the plains.
Farmers east of the city say the soldiers at the Siege Encampment bought up every oak beam in the valley to build their mantlets.

Twelve seasoned ash beams for the throwing-arms and forty bundles of rawhide rope stored under the oiled canvas. From the eastern earthwork, Dragonsreach sits clear against the sky at twelve hundred paces.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stables.co:
To the captain of the guard at Whiterun gate,
On the 22nd of Last Seed I was riding west with the satchel for Rorikstead and the Imperial camp when four men came out of the rocks near Redoran's Retreat and pulled me off my horse. They took the satchel and my boots.

I am told this is not the guard's concern, since it happened outside the walls. I would remind the captain that one letter in that satchel was sealed by the Jarl's own steward, and that I said so to the robbers, loudly, before I thought better of it.

If the guard will not go, I will pay someone who will. Kjeld.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stables.fa:
^WHITERUN CARRIAGE
To Riverwood and the southern road: 10 septims
To Rorikstead: 10
To Solitude, Windhelm, Riften, Markarth: 20 each
To Dawnstar, Winterhold, Morthal, Falkreath: 20 each, and bring a cloak

Rules of the stand:
No livestock inside the carriage. That means goats. That means YOU, Lemkil.
The driver does not wait past the second bell.
The driver is not responsible for dragons.
Tips are welcome and encouraged and remembered.

The driver will take you as far as the road goes and no further.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stables.ho: The stables and carriage stand below Whiterun's gate, where every traveller in the hold eventually waits for a ride. The drivers know more gossip than the Jarl's court.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stables.ru: Want a carriage? Twenty septims to anywhere, and the driver will tell you three secrets on the way. Kjeld lost a whole satchel of letters to bandits last month, mind. Redoran's Retreat, he says.
place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stables.sk: Folio #14 (-24, 51): Field inspection recorded for Whiterun Stables within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.whiterun_stormcloak: A Stormcloak war camp in the hills east of the White River, where Ulfric's soldiers sharpen their axes and wait for the order to march on Whiterun.

#Second Seed
Joined up in Windhelm. They gave me an axe and a blue sash and told me I'm fighting for Skyrim. I've lived in Skyrim my whole life and never knew it needed fighting for.

#Last Seed
Camped above the White River. You can see High Hrothgar from here, white against the sky. The old sergeant says the Greybeards will never take a side. Lucky them. Some nights I watch the lights of Whiterun and think about how many people live behind those walls who've never done anything to me.
There's a Stormcloak camp past the river, near the Ritual Stone. They buy bread from the farms and pay in Windhelm coin. Fair enough, until the day they march.

Folio #39 (509, 140): Field inspection recorded for Whiterun Stormcloak Camp within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #39 for whiterun_stormcloak_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Whiterun Stormcloak Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
Hold the camp. Do not engage the Whiterun garrison unless attacked. Balgruuf has not chosen a side, and as long as he keeps his gates shut to the Legion we can wait.

Buy from the farms. Pay fair. A farmer who sells us bread today opens his gate to us tomorrow. Any soldier caught stealing from a Nord farm will be sent back to Windhelm in irons and I will deal with him personally.

Report any Legion movement on the western road. The Imperial camp near Rorikstead is short of men. Find out how short. Stone-Fist.
place_lore.nirncraft.whitewatch_tower.ho: A crumbling watchtower north-east of Whiterun, built to guard the road and now used to rob it. The bandits who hold it paint their shields red and count every traveller who passes.
place_lore.nirncraft.whitewatch_tower.ru: Whitewatch Tower used to keep the north road safe. Now the only thing it keeps is a tally of every purse it's emptied. Vantus Loreius has lost two hands on that road already.
place_lore.nirncraft.whitewatch_tower.sk: Folio #24 (182, -323): Field inspection recorded for Whitewatch Tower within Whiterun Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.whitewatch_tower.to:
#Hearthfire
Dunmer pilgrim, going to High Hrothgar: 8 septims and a nice cloak.
Farm cart from Loreius: 30 septims, one cabbage, one driver who talked back. He doesn't talk now.
Khajiit caravan: tried. They had more swords than us. Let them by. Not writing that down. Wrote it down anyway.

Note to the lads: Brattvar at Halted Stream wants two men a week for his mine. He pays in ore, not coin. I say no. If he wants men he can take them off the road himself, like we do.

Anyone who paints his shield and doesn't stand his watch gets thrown off the top. I'm not joking. Ask Svein. Oh wait. Ingjald.
I went up for a dare when I was twelve and found a ring of bone on the top step, white as new teeth. I put it in my pocket. All the way home I heard a woman singing behind me, and when I looked back the tower was lit green from top to bottom. My father took the ring back up the next morning and wept the whole way, though he never told me why. Leave her be. Or if you must go up, go up to help her, not to rob her.
A broken watchtower on the headland north of Fort Hraggstad. Long ago a sailor's widow kept a lantern burning at its top for a ship that never came home. Fishermen swear the lantern is still lit.
On foggy nights there's a green light at the top of Widow's Watch. The Legion lads from Hraggstad won't patrol under it. One of them did once, and he came back talking to someone who wasn't there.

~I wed you with a ring of whalebone white,
~You sailed with it upon your other hand.
~I keep the twin of it, and keep the light,
~And keep this tower, since I cannot keep the land.

~If any find my ring when I am gone,
~Carry it down to where the dark rocks meet
~The water at the Orphan's lonely stone,
~And give it to the sea, to make it sweet.
~Then I may sleep. Until then, I will burn
~My lantern for a sail that won't return.
place_lore.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep.hook: At place.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep, weathered stone and fresh tracks reflect the tensions of the rain-soaked moors and ancient cairns of Glenumbra, where Camlorn's cathedral clergy and the Beldama Wyrd keep uneasy watch over the barrow-dead.
place_lore.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep.rumou: Wayfarers passing place.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep report signs of moorland werewolf packs, barrow-wights, and Llugwych blood-courtiers operating under cover of the local boundary disputes.
place_lore.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep.v8_lo:
Intercepted Dispatch from place.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep

We have cached the extra lantern-oil and boundary-rolls behind the inner masonry at place.nirncraft.wilcliff_keep. As long as the local magistrates remain divided over the seasonal tolls, neither the garrison outriders nor the guild bailiffs will search this sector closely. Keep the watch-fires low until the courier arrives from the coast.

place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm.grey_quart: Galdrus Hlervu, for the families of the Grey Quarter

#To the Steward of the Palace of the Kings, 9th of Evening Star, 4E 200
We ask, again, for the watch to walk our streets after dark. Three doors were marked with soot this month. On the third night one of them burned.
We do not ask for charity. We pay our taxes in coin and our tolls in insults. We ask only that the men we pay to guard the city remember that the Grey Quarter is inside its walls.

Our grandparents spent their first winter in Skyrim at Refugees' Rest, east past Traitor's Post, sleeping in a tower with the wind for a blanket. Some of them are still there, in urns no one has visited for years. We would like not to join them before our time.
^Respectfully, and with diminishing patience.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm.hook: The City of Kings, oldest of the Nord cities, where Ulfric Stormcloak rules from the Palace of the Kings and the Dunmer of the Grey Quarter endure behind walls that never quite became home.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm.quartermas:
#Sun's Dusk, 4E 201
Issued: 40 cuirasses, blue, sized for boys who think they are men. 12 axes, 3 of them with handles that will not survive a winter. Salt fish, 9 barrels. Mead, not enough.
Missing: the payroll strongbox for the eastern pickets, 310 septims, last seen on the cart of Bjorlam Frost-Hand and two of his messmates. Cart found on the Hollyfrost road. Men not found.

Note to the captain: the scouts say smoke rises from the old cabin they call Traitor's Post. The name will amuse no one in the Palace. I recommend we let the name do our talking and send six men, not two.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm.rumour: Ulfric's guards will drink to Talos with you all night. Say one kind word about the Grey Quarter, though, and watch how fast the cups go empty.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm.unsent_let: Hjordis, a washerwoman of the Stone Quarter

Arnbjorn, my heart,
They say the Winterhold Stormcloak Camp is so cold the mead freezes in the horn. I hope you are drinking it faster than that. Your sister has had her baby, a loud girl with your chin, and we have named her Svana after your grandmother.

I washed the Jarl's linens again this week. You would laugh to see how ordinary they are. A king's sheets have the same stains as ours.
Come home when the war lets you. Come home even if it doesn't. I will not tell anyone you were afraid. I was afraid too, the whole time you were growing up.
^Your mother
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm_stables.ca:
#Frostfall, 4E 201
4th: a Breton scholar to Kynesgrove, asking about Mzulft the whole way. Overpaid. Left his gloves.
7th: two Dunmer to Darkwater Crossing, paying in old Morrowind coin. Accepted it. Told nobody.
9th: a man in silver-buckled leathers to Mixwater Mill, with chains in his pack. Did not ask. Did not like him.

#Frostfall, 4E 201
12th: Imperial courier, Riften road, asked me to forget his face. Done, for 30 septims.
15th: a widow from Darkwater, crying the whole way. Her husband went into Snapleg Cave. Took no fare. Some things a man doesn't charge for.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm_stables.ho: The stables and carriage stand below Windhelm's great bridge, where every rumour in Eastmarch passes through at a horse's walk, and some of them pay the fare.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm_stables.ru: Ask the carriage driver at the stables. He hears everything between Windhelm and Riften, and he forgets none of it, for the right price.
place_lore.nirncraft.windhelm_stables.sk: Folio #9 (1840, -532): Field inspection recorded for Windhelm Stables within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #9 for windhelm_stables: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Windhelm Stables are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.windstad.hook: A homestead plot on the northern edge of the Hjaalmarch marsh, overlooking the Sea of Ghosts. The last house here sank into the bog. The Jarl of Morthal is looking for someone stubborn enough to build another.
place_lore.nirncraft.windstad.old_owner_:
#Second Seed, 4E 168
Built the new byre on oak piles. My husband laughed and said the bog wouldn't take an oak pile in a hundred years. It took the old byre in three.

#Frostfall, 4E 171
The house leans. We can feel it in our beds. Every morning the door sticks a little worse. The marsh wants the house back. Grandmother said the marsh only gives back what is asked of it politely, so last night I went out and asked it, politely, to wait until the children were grown.
#Evening Star, 4E 171
It did not wait. We are going to Morthal. Let the next fool build on stone.
place_lore.nirncraft.windstad.rumour: The Jarl will sell you the Windstad land for a song. Lovely view of the sea, fine fishing. You just have to build on stone, and you have to not mind the old house that's still under the mud.
place_lore.nirncraft.windstad.steward_of: Thorvar Mist-Eye, Steward to the Jarl

To any person of good character and sufficient purse:
The Jarl of Hjaalmarch offers the freehold of the Windstad land, on the north coast between the Icerunner wreck and the High Gate ruins, for the sum agreed at Highmoon Hall. The buyer must undertake to build in stone, and to keep a light on the shore for the fishing boats.

The Jarl has asked me to add a personal note, which I do not fully understand: 'Whoever builds there will be happy for a while, and then they will be needed.' Make of that what you will. I usually do not try.
place_lore.nirncraft.windward_ruins.band:
Nirvel says we're merchants now, not bandits. Merchants get to sleep in a dry ruin and eat Dawnstar fish for free. I can get used to that.
But he keeps the coin in his own chest and only he has the key. When I asked for my share he said 'after the thaw'. Bandits pay out every week. Maybe merchants are worse than bandits.
Also, I dreamed of the black door too. Didn't tell Nirvel.

If the boss doesn't pay up by Sun's Dusk I'm taking my share myself and going to Windhelm. They say there's work there for a man with a club and no questions. Better than freezing in a ruin for a man who sells salt to widows.
place_lore.nirncraft.windward_ruins.hawk: Dream-ward sachets sold in Dawnstar, Frostfall: 146. At five septims each, 730 septims. Cost of nightshade, salt and sacking: 31 septims. Cost of a priest's robe to wear while selling: 12 septims, stolen, so nothing.

Note: the sachets do nothing. Of course they do nothing. Nothing in Mundus stops the dreams, and as long as the dreams go on, the fish-wives keep buying. Raise the price to eight when the snow closes the road.
Note: the Gull-Wife woman is asking questions. Have Brakk scare her off.
place_lore.nirncraft.windward_ruins.hook: A wind-scoured Nordic ruin southwest of Dawnstar. A pedlar of 'dream-ward' charms has been seen coming and going from it, and his trade is booming.
place_lore.nirncraft.windward_ruins.rumo: That fellow selling sachets to keep off the nightmares? Someone saw him camped in Windward Ruins with a whole crew. And a whole lot of coin.
place_lore.nirncraft.windward_ruins.sk4_: Folio #10 (-8, -1585): Field inspection recorded for Windward Ruins within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #10 for windward_ruins: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Windward Ruins are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold.collapse:
Dearest Hroar,
You ask me again to come south to Whiterun and I tell you again: no. My grandmother is under that water. So is her mother's house, and the shop where she sold candles, and the temple where she was married. If I leave, there is nobody left who remembers which rocks they were.

I walk the cliff every evening. The Jarl's men think I am mad, and perhaps I am. But on the lowest tide last Evening Star I heard the bell. I swear it on Kyne. Three strokes, slow, the way they rang it for the dead.
The College says the Collapse was a storm. A storm does not take half a city and leave one tower dry.

Come north if you love me. Bring warm boots.
Ysolde
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold.hearth_t:
#Frostfall, 4E 201
Room, two nights, the Argonian scholar from the College. Paid in coin that sparked when I bit it. Kept it anyway.
Mead, nine bottles, Legion courier bound for the camp west of town. On credit. Will never see that again.
Stew for the Dunmer from the wreck-camp, no charge. Mother would have wanted it.

Bread and salt fish for a stranger asking the way to Saarthal. Told him to stay away. He tipped me a whole septim to stop talking.
Broken stool, one. Stormcloak and Legion man disagreed about Talos. Both are paying.
Note: buy more candles. The nights are getting longer and so are the stories.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold.hook: What remains of the old capital of the north clings to a cliff above the Sea of Ghosts. Most of the city lies under the waves, and the survivors have long memories.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold.rumour: Winterhold? It was a great city once, before the sea took it. Now it's an inn, a Jarl, and a lot of people blaming the College.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold.sk4_note: Folio #2 (1417, -1749): Field inspection recorded for Winterhold within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #2 for winterhold: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Winterhold are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold_glacier_: A towering curtain of blue glacial ice and freezing meltwater plunging down the sheer cliff wall into the northern sea-canyon.
When the sun hits Winterhold Glacier Falls at noon, the ice-pillars crack like thunder all the way up to the College bridge.
The sub-glacial stream carves a fresh arch through the blue ice every summer thaw, washing ancient carved stones and Mammoth bones out onto the gravel bar below the town cliffs.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold_imperial:
1. No patrol is to go near Hob's Fall Cave or the sea caves below the cliffs, for any reason, including pursuit. This order replaces my order of last month, which said the same thing more politely.
2. Patrols travel in fours. Not threes. Never twos.

3. Any soldier found sleeping on watch will dig the latrines until Sun's Dawn.
4. Legionary Corvus is still missing. If anyone sees him, do not approach. Report his position and wait for an officer. Yes, even if he waves. ESPECIALLY if he waves.
A Legion camp pitched in the snow west of Winterhold, watching a Jarl who leans toward Ulfric. Its patrols along the coast keep going missing.
The Legion camp west of town lost another patrol on the coast road. The captain says Stormcloaks. The men say something worse.

Folio #12 (509, -1632): Field inspection recorded for Winterhold Imperial Camp within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #12 for winterhold_imperial_camp: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Winterhold Imperial Camp are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.

#18th of Frostfall
Saw Corvus on the beach below the lighthouse, three weeks after we buried him at sea. He was standing up to his knees in the water, watching the camp. His skin was blue as a Dunmer's ghost. Nobody believes me but Pell, and Pell saw him too.

#20th of Frostfall
Captain has doubled the watch. Pell has stopped sleeping. I keep thinking: we buried him at sea, and the sea runs into Hob's Fall.

#22nd of Frostfall
Pell's gone. His bedroll was wet with seawater this morning, and the tracks went down to the beach. The captain says desertion. I've started sleeping with my boots on and my sword under the blanket.
place_lore.nirncraft.winterhold_stormclo:
Mother,
We sit in the snow and watch the sea for a ship that does not come. The sergeant says the Winter War is late. The sergeant said that two weeks ago. We have bows without arrows and a boy from Dawnstar who keeps screaming in his sleep.

Ulfric will win this war, I know it. But I would like him to win it with dry socks. Send socks.
Talos guard you,
Hrodi

^Postscript
The Dawnstar boy says he dreams of a door on a hill and a woman behind it. The sergeant told him to dream of Ulfric instead. He tried. He says Ulfric was behind the door too.
A Stormcloak camp in the snowy hills where Winterhold meets Eastmarch, guarding the northern approach to Windhelm. Its soldiers are watching the coast for a lost supply ship.
The Stormcloaks camped south of the sea caves are waiting on a ship called the Winter War. Between you and me, they'll be waiting a long time.

Sergeant,
Found her. The Winter War is on the rocks northeast of Yngol Barrow, broken across the middle. Saw a few of the crew's tracks heading inland but no crew. Saw horkers on the deck and slaughterfish in the flooded hold.

Could not get to the lower hold. If the swords are still aboard, we will need a proper salvage party, or someone mad enough to swim for it. Legion scouts were watching the wreck from the ridge. We'd better be quick.
place_lore.nirncraft.witchmist_grove.gro:
~Leave milk at the water's edge and walk away.
~Leave bread at the root and do not look back.
~Take nothing from the grove that the grove has not given.
~The mist-mother counts her children every night, and she counts in a voice like yours.
^Cut by the first folk of Kynesgrove, who knew better than to build here.

Someone has left fresh offerings on the stone: a heel of bread, a cup of goat's milk gone to ice, and a child's wooden doll with a scrap of red ribbon tied around its waist. Under the doll, scratched with a hunting knife: 'Take this one instead. Give her back.'
place_lore.nirncraft.witchmist_grove.hoo: A misty hollow of hot springs and gnarled trees south of Kynesgrove, where a hunter built a lodge against good advice and the wisps have been dancing on its roof ever since.
place_lore.nirncraft.witchmist_grove.hun:
#Rain's Hand
Built the lodge between the two warmest pools. Best hunting in Eastmarch: elk come to drink every dawn and never think to look up. Kynesgrove folk say the grove belongs to someone. Kynesgrove folk say a lot of things.

#Last Seed
Lights over the water at night, blue and cold. My daughter Tova calls them pretty and tries to follow them. I have tied a bell to her door.

#Frostfall
The bell rang. Tova's bed is empty. The lights are dancing over the far pool and there is a tall pale shape among them, singing with my daughter's voice.
place_lore.nirncraft.witchmist_grove.rum: Witchmist Grove's pretty as a painting from the road. Go closer and the mist starts following you home. Sensible people stay on the road.
place_lore.nirncraft.witchmist_grove.sk4: Folio #19 (1813, -68): Field inspection recorded for Witchmist Grove within Eastmarch Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #19 for witchmist_grove: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Witchmist Grove are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolf_jarls_howe.hoo: A great Atmoran barrow under a hill of snow with a long ship buried whole as the dungeon's central room.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolf_jarls_howe.rum: The howe's ship is whole. They say you can hear her creak in the dark of the barrow.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolf_jarls_howe.thr: To my heirs: I have the crown of the foreign king beneath the keel of my ship and I will carry it to my own grave rather than let it go to any living man. It is a heavy thing. It weighs nothing. It does not shine. I will not look at it. Bury me on top of it, and do not ask why my sleep is so poor.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolf_jarls_howe.web: SHE SLEEPS TO CARRY US HOME. The word is the name of the hold, spoken as a promise. When the ice breaks, wake the ship. When the ship wakes, board her. Do not look back at the shelf. It was only ever a place to wait.

place_lore.nirncraft.wolfskull_cave.acol:
Master Ulvarr,
I have brought the third heart as you asked. I did not ask whose it was. I want you to know that I did not ask, so that you know I am obedient.

But I must tell you that the dead we raised from the Hall of the Dead in Solitude still have their names sewn into their shrouds. One of them was my uncle. He looked at me. I know you say they do not look, but he looked.
Please let me tend the fire instead of fetching. I am good at fires. I will be very good at fires.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolfskull_cave.hook: A cave in the hills south-west of Solitude, its mouth guarded by an old stone wall. Necromancers who revere the Wolf Queen meet here, and on certain nights green fire lights the ridge.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolfskull_cave.ritu: The Queen's bones lie elsewhere, guarded by fools. We do not need her bones. We need her name, spoken correctly, on the night of her death, by a choir of thirteen. We are nine. The difference will be made up with the dead of Solitude's Hall, which are plentiful and poorly guarded.

Requirements: four fresh hearts, a circlet of wolf teeth, the ash of a Septim pretender (substitute: any Imperial noble; the Jarl's steward has been suggested and is unpopular).
The green fire must be kept burning. It is visible from Solitude. Good. Let them look up and wonder.
place_lore.nirncraft.wolfskull_cave.rumo: Green lights over Wolfskull Cave again. My grandmother says they used to see them in her day too, and that the Wolf Queen's old servants never really left. I say my grandmother says a lot of things.

place_lore.nirncraft.woodhearth.dockhand:
Sister,
You asked if it's true about the Mandate-Breakers. It's true. There's a band of them out by the Namira shrine north-east of here. The Green Pact lets us eat what we kill in battle within three days, as you know, and nobody in Woodhearth would turn up their nose at a Maormer leg after a raid.

But these ones don't wait for battles. They don't wait three days. And they've started to say it's not the Pact they serve but the Lady of Decay, who says that all flesh is the same flesh. Two of the net-boys have gone. Their mothers are asking the Wardens. The Wardens are asking whether it's really any of the Wardens' business. That's how bad it's got.
place_lore.nirncraft.woodhearth.hook: A harbour city of Greenshade grown from a ring of living trees, where Bosmer, Altmer traders and Maormer spies all share the same docks and none of them share the same story.
place_lore.nirncraft.woodhearth.rumour: Woodhearth's wardens are jumpy. Somebody's been setting fires in the deep forest east of the city. In Valenwood you can kill a man and be forgiven by supper. Burn a tree and you're hunted for life.
place_lore.nirncraft.woodhearth.warden_n: Warden Ilthaer, of the Greenshade Watch

^FIRE IN THE GREEN
Three burns have been found in the forest north-east of the city, each a perfect circle, each at the dark of the moon. At the heart of the newest stands the shrine of the Prince of Ruin, its altar still warm.

Whoever lit these fires has broken the oldest law of Y'ffre and will answer to every hunter in Greenshade. Anyone who knows the names of these firebrands is to come to me at the Warden's bough. Anyone who knows them and stays silent is to consider whether they enjoy being alive.
place_lore.nirncraft.word_wall_dead_cron: On the cliffs beside Dead Crone Rock stands a curving wall of dragon script, its claw-marked words still faintly humming with power.
Old Nord wall up past Dead Crone Rock, covered in dragon scratches. They say it teaches a word that makes grown men run screaming. Useful, around crones.

A traveller who did not sign

My best attempt at the dragon script, worked out with a College primer and a great deal of guessing:
HERE THE DRAGON'S SERVANTS LAID THE BRAVE WHO DID NOT FLINCH, AND FEAR ITSELF WAS SET TO GUARD THEM, SO THAT THE LIVING WOULD STAY AWAY.

One word glowed as I read it, a word I think means 'fear' or 'dismay'. When I touched it I felt like a man at the edge of a cliff, about to fall. I left in a hurry. Whoever comes next: put your hand on the brightest word. You'll know which one.
place_lore.nirncraft.word_wall_lost_vall: An ancient Word Wall above the falls of Lost Valley Redoubt, its dragon script carved deep into the cliff. Hagravens and Forsworn guard the valley below.
There's a wall of dragon writing up past Bilegulch, over the Lost Valley falls. The Forsworn hold the valley, and the hagravens make their prayers to that wall like it might answer.

Charcoal rubbing of the central panel, with my notes. The script is the same as on the Bilegulch and Sunderstone mounds, which supports my view that all three were made by one dragon cult. One word recurs, carved deeper than the rest and in a separate hand, as if added in haste. The local Forsworn call it 'the word that walks through walls'.

I copied it twice. Each time, my hand passed through the paper for a moment, as though the paper had become smoke. I have decided not to copy it a third time. Further work on the mound below Bilegulch is assigned to my assistant, Ennis.
place_lore.nirncraft.word_wall_statue_to: A Dragon Wall of the old Nords on the shoulder of Mount Kilkreath, a stone's throw from Meridia's statue. Its claw-marked runes speak of the wind's fury.
There's a wall of dragon writing up by Meridia's statue. A scholar from Solitude spent a week up there copying it. Came down with frostbite and three new theories, none of which he'd explain.

The wall commemorates a warrior whose breath, the inscription asserts, could strike with the force of the storm. The three characters most deeply cut I render tentatively as fury, wind and strike(1). I am confident in the first and the third and moderately confident in the second, which may also mean 'drunken uncle'(2).

(1) My learned rival at the College of Winterhold renders the second as 'grip.' He is wrong, as usual.
(2) This is a joke. The Nords who carved this would not have laughed at it either.
Nota bene: the wall is warm to the touch at dusk. I recorded this and then removed it from my fair copy, as it is unscholarly. I record it again here because it is true.

place_lore.nirncraft.wreck_of_the_brineh:
Out of Solitude for Dawnstar and Winterhold.
Salted cod, 30 barrels.
Pine pitch, 12 barrels.
Mead, Black-Briar, 8 casks.
Fish (special), 3 barrels, marked with a red knot. Not to be opened by any crew. Captain's orders.

Nobody on this ship is a fool. A barrel of cod does not need three locks and a guard. The captain says the red-knot barrels are for a buyer at the Pale Imperial Camp. If that is fish, I am the Emperor.

^Last entry, smudged
Struck the rocks at the change of watch. Captain is in his cabin with the red-knot barrels and his crossbow and will not come out. I am taking the boat.
A merchant ship broken in two on the Pale coast west of Dawnstar. Her hold is half under water, and salvagers say not every barrel aboard her is what the manifest claims.
The Brinehammer ran onto the rocks with a hold full of 'salted fish'. Funny, fish that rattles like coin.

Lads,
We dive at low tide. Forget the cod, forget the pitch. Find the three barrels with the red knot. They're Legion pay, bound for the camp south of here, and nobody at that camp knows the ship went down yet.
If the Legion turns up, we're honest salvagers. If the horkers turn up, run. If anyone tries to keep a barrel to himself, he goes in the water. The Sea of Ghosts doesn't ask questions.

One more thing. Old Bull-Tusk's herd is back on the ice. Don't throw stones at the calves this time, Hrek. I'm not hauling you out of the water again.
Ulfgar

place_lore.nirncraft.wreck_of_the_icerun: A Hjaalmarch trading ship run aground in the ice off the northern marsh. Its furs and fish rotted long ago, but scavengers keep coming back for something in its hold.

The Icerunner hit the ice in a fog so thick the crew didn't see it till they were standing on it. Some walked to Windstad. Some didn't. The ones that didn't are still aboard, if you believe the fishermen.

From the Icerunner:
Furs, spoiled, 30. Worth nothing.
Salt cod, spoiled, 4 barrels. Worth less.
Captain's sword, rusted: sold at Morthal for 8.
Captain's charts: kept. Shows a cove north-east of Windstad nobody else has drawn.

Strongbox in the captain's cabin: locked. Can't shift it. Rolf of Pinemoon will want a cut if he hears. Don't tell Rolf. Come back with a crowbar and a cousin.
There is something in the lower hold that knocks back when you knock. Don't knock.
We struck the ice at the second bell. Fog so thick you could lean on it. Captain Sorrel ordered the boats out, but the ice took one and the other we needed for the wounded.

Five of us are walking to the old Windstad farm across the ice. Three are staying with the ship, too hurt to move. I have left them the last of the mead and promised to come back with a sledge.
If you find this and we have not come back, we are under the ice somewhere between here and the shore. Look for the wounded first. Their names are Brann, little Saffa and old Gotthelf.

place_lore.nirncraft.wreck_of_the_pride_: A Telvanni ship from Morrowind, run aground east of the College while fleeing the Red Year. Dunmer refugees still visit the wreck to mourn; others visit to loot.

^Translated in the margin by a College hand
The sky is red over Tel Vos. Mother says the mountain has woken and we must go on the ship with the mushroom-masters. We may take one bag each. I took my doll and Father's ancestor-urn, because Mother forgot it.

The sea is grey here and it bites. A Telvanni mage told the captain to sail through the ice instead of around it. The captain did as he was told. Then there was a great noise and the deck was tilted and everyone was screaming.
I hid the urn in the captain's cabin, in the chest with the spiral lock. If Father's ashes are lost he will have nowhere to go. Mother is calling. We are going over the side to the rocks.
The Pride of Tel Vos. A mushroom-wizard's ship full of refugees, broke up right there on the rocks. Some of the grey-skins in town were aboard as children.

Cargo of Master Ralvo Dren, for safekeeping in Skyrim until Morrowind is calm.
Soul gems, grand, 14. Soul gems, common, 60.
Books of the Master's private library, 3 crates (do NOT let the refugees burn these for warmth).
Passengers: 48 commoners, for which the Master has been paid in full.
Note: the passengers are not cargo and may be put ashore if the weight becomes inconvenient.

^Postscript, in a different hand
The Master's books went into the sea when we struck. The gems did not; I locked them in the hold and I have the only key. If the Master asks, tell him the commoners stole them. He will believe it. He always does.

place_lore.nirncraft.wreck_of_the_stride:
To my sister Ottilie in Anvil, if this bottle ever floats that far:
We hit the rocks in the dark. The captain is shouting about the Company's box. I have no box. I have a little sea-chest of my own, thirty years of wages in it, and I have dragged it up the beach and buried it in the shingle below the big black rock, about thirty paces inland from the bow, where the tide never reaches.

The wreckers are coming down the cliff with lanterns. I am going to swim for it. If I make Raven Rock, I will go back for the chest myself. If I do not, Ottilie, it is yours. Buy that little house by the lighthouse. Fennick.
The broken hull of the Strident Squall on the island's southern shore, picked over by wreckers and mudcrabs. The Company wanted its strongbox; the cook only ever wanted his savings.
The Strident Squall? The Company sent folk for the pay chest. Nobody went looking for Old Fennick's savings, though. He was the ship's cook, and he never trusted a strongbox in his life.

Everything off the Squall split even, after the lantern-man takes his tenth. Company goods go to the Orc at the Ramshackle Trading Post, who doesn't ask. Personal goods we keep. The Company will send someone for their box, so we leave the box, and we leave quickly when the sails come. Nobody digs on the beach. Somebody saw the cook digging. Somebody should have dug faster.

Addendum, in a different hand: The cook did not come back. Neither did the lantern-man, who went looking for the cook's hole on his own. The tide brought his lantern back. If anyone finds the big black rock, share, or swim.

place_lore.nirncraft.wreck_of_the_winter:
Captain was clever with the ice. We struck at the second bell. Mast went over, half the crew with it. Rest of us are on the rocks with the arrows, waiting for the sea to settle.
If you find this, the swords are in the lower hold, aft. If you're a Stormcloak, take them to the camp west of here. If you're a Legionary, I hope the slaughterfish find you.

Three of us left now. The captain went back aboard for the manifest he was meant to burn and the hull shifted and took him. We're walking inland at first light. Talos guide us to the camp before the cold does.
A Stormcloak supply ship that ran onto the rocks off the eastern Winterhold coast while carrying arms to Windhelm. Both sides would like to know what is left in her hold.
The Winter War went down with Stormcloak steel aboard. Ulfric's men want it back. The Legion wants it sunk deeper.

Captain,
You carry forty swords, sixty shields and a crate of arrows for the camp north of Windhelm. Run the coast close, without lights. The Imperial navy is thin this far north and their captains are lazy.

If you are boarded, the cargo goes over the side. If you are wrecked, burn the manifest. Skyrim will not forget a crew that dies with its cargo.
Skyrim would rather they lived, though. Don't be clever with the ice.

^Captain's note on the back
Aye, Galmar. Close and dark it is. The pilot says there's ice off the point by Yngol Barrow but I've run it a dozen times. We'll be at the camp by the third night.

place_lore.nirncraft.wrothgarian_mountai: A broken ridge where the sky is a permanent dusk and sharp peaks throw shadows that never change.
At noon the shadows on the Wrothgarian ridge fall the wrong way, and the sky there is the colour of permanent dusk.

Do not look at the shadow's tip at noon. It is a line, and it points to a place, and the place is a hammer. The Orcs who looked have not slept well since. The line crosses the Chief's hall and ends in the old forge beneath the city. I have built a cairn on it in the hope it will think twice.

place_lore.nirncraft.wynley_ruins.hook: A tumbled chapel-yard east of Camlorn whose broken tower still holds the oldest bell in Glenumbra, tolled once a year by the Company of the Peal.
place_lore.nirncraft.wynley_ruins.ringer:
^THE COMPANY OF THE PEAL
^Treble: Ysoldt Garrick (fifty years, deaf in the left ear, ringing true).
^Second: Pell the younger (talks while ringing; no one minds).
^Third: unfilled, since the Winter of Bells. Do not offer the rope to a stranger.
^Tenor: Brother Cael, who rings but does not speak.
Note: the third rope is never to be pulled. The bell rang it alone last Tirdas. The Archpriest says it was the wind. The wind in Camlorn, I may say, has never once rung a bell in the correct order.
place_lore.nirncraft.wynley_ruins.rumour: In Camlorn the bell-ringers have a code. It is not a secret. Every child knows it. That is what makes it so useful. At Wynley, they say, the old bell keeps the original.

place_lore.nirncraft.xal_haj_ei_shrine.h: A shrine in a hollow reed-forest, half-sunk in a pool, its walls carved with root-patterns.
place_lore.nirncraft.xal_haj_ei_shrine.r: The shrine in the reeds has gone grey. The keepers say the Root is in pain.
place_lore.nirncraft.xal_haj_ei_shrine.w: Root of the marsh, root of the sky, we are in pain and so are you. A cut is a cut, a tap is a tap, and no one asks the tree. We keep the shrine and we weep, because the shrine weeps. Forgive those who do not know, and those who do. Let the sap run clean.

place_lore.nirncraft.yngol_barrow.hook: The barrow of Yngol, son of Ysgramor, lost at sea on the voyage to Skyrim. His father raised it by the coast near Windhelm, and its halls are said to hold the prow of Yngol's ship.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngol_barrow.rumour: Yngol Barrow. Ysgramor's own son is in there. Well, his ghost. His body is still somewhere out in the Sea of Ghosts.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngol_barrow.shipwr:
To any brave heart passing through.
Old shipwrights in Windhelm say that when Ysgramor buried his son, he set a carving from the prow of Yngol's longship above the tomb, a sea-wolf's head in black oak. They say any new ship blessed by touching it will never founder on the Sea of Ghosts.

I am building a ship for my sons, who fish the ice-floes every spring. My husband was lost off Winterhold. I will not lose them too. Bring me the sea-wolf's head, or let me touch it once, and I will carve your name into the keel. I pay in honest Stormcloak coin.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngol_barrow.yngol_:
^Rendered from the old runes by a College hand
The sea took my son and gave me nothing back. I give him this hall instead, and the sea-wolf from his ship, and the songs of five hundred.
Let him guard this coast as I could not guard him.

^Beneath it, newer, in a Windhelm hand
Shipwrights come here before every launching, though the old rule says they should not. They touch the stone of the door and ask the son of the Harbinger to keep their keels whole. Some say he answers. Some say the sea answers instead. Both kinds come back.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngvild.fisher_plea:
To any sellsword who reads this at the Dawnstar docks.
My sister Ingrith took her skiff out past Hela's Folly on the 2nd of Frostfall to check the crab pots. She came back without the crabs and without her wits. She sits by the fire and says she has been invited to a wedding on the island, and that the bridesmaids are already waiting.

Last night she was gone from her bed. Her skiff was gone from the beach. The tracks lead down to the water and the water leads to Yngvild.
I have forty septims and my late husband's sword. Both are yours if you bring her home. If you cannot bring her home, bring me her wedding ring, so that I have something to bury.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngvild.hook: A sea cave on a lonely island off the Winterhold coast. Lights burn there at night, and the Dawnstar fishermen swear they have seen pale women walking on the water.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngvild.host_journa: My household grows. The last girl from Dawnstar arrived in a fine state, her eyes already half-dreaming. I suspect the nightmares in that town do half my work for me; the frightened sleep poorly, and the sleepless are easy to call.

The ghosts serve well, but they are cold company. I keep them in their best gowns and let them dance in the great hall. They do not complain. The living ones complain constantly, until they stop being living ones.
Must write to Hob's Fall again for more salts. The woman there drives a hard bargain for a College dropout.
place_lore.nirncraft.yngvild.rumour: Yngvild? Don't row past it after dark. My cousin did, and something sang to him from the rocks. He hasn't been right since.
Folio #10 (595, -1948): Field inspection recorded for Yngvild within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #10 for yngvild: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Yngvild are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
#THANKS LEFT AT THE WELL
From a salt-carrier: thanks, and a pinch of salt. From a mother with a sick child: thanks, and a ribbon, for the child lived. From a sword-singer, who did not leave his name: thanks, and a very small, very sharp knife, point downward.
A deep, cool spring in a bowl of the Yokudan desert, ringed with tamarisks and old cairns, where every caravan of the lost continent once stopped to drink and to give thanks.
The wellspring has never run dry, even in the great drought. The herders say it is because it is not fed by rain, but by something beneath the sand that has not yet decided to stop.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_overlook.ho: A small Nordic ruin on a rise above the Yorgrim river in the eastern Pale. A smuggler's crew once used it to watch the Windhelm road, and left something behind.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_overlook.ru: Yorgrim Overlook? Little ruin on a hill. Used to be smugglers there. They left in a hurry, and smugglers never leave in a hurry with full pockets.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_overlook.sk: Folio #18 (1180, -959): Field inspection recorded for Yorgrim Overlook within The Pale Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

Addendum #18 for yorgrim_overlook: All travelers, carters, and hold patrollers passing Yorgrim Overlook are instructed to report disturbed masonry, outlaw campfires, or missing mile-stones to the nearest hold watch-post before sundown.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_overlook.sm:
Brother,
The Legion found the road cache, so I have moved the Cyrodilic brandy money. It is near the Overlook, where we used to watch the sleds. From the old standing arch, walk toward Mount Anthor until the river is lost from view. Under the leaning pine, a stone with a fox scratched on it. The purse is beneath.

If the Legion catches me, deny you know me. If I die, the purse is yours. If you spend it all on mead at Nightgate Inn I will haunt you, and I will be very boring about it.
S.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_stead.hook: A stone-built steading above the frozen river valley where trappers trade white-fox pelts and tallow oil along the Dawnstar road.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_stead.rumou: Trappers at Yorgrim Stead say the ice on the river groans like a waking giant whenever the north wind shifts.
place_lore.nirncraft.yorgrim_stead.warde: Traded nine arctic fox skins and two jars of rendered horker oil to the courier riding between Dawnstar and Winterhold. Stay on the staked road past the Windward Ruins; snow-bears have been denning in the broken stonework.
place_lore.nirncraft.ysgramors_tomb.hook: The burial hall of Ysgramor, father of the Nords, on the windswept northern coast. Only the Companions may open its doors; everyone else simply stands outside and feels small.
place_lore.nirncraft.ysgramors_tomb.pilg: Father of the Nords, Harbinger of the Five Hundred, I have walked from Whiterun with my son's ashes in a clay jar. He died with a blade in his hand, as you would have wished, fighting the bandits at Valtheim. I cannot open your door, but I can leave him on your step.

Let him drink in your hall. Let him hear the old songs. Let him forgive me for saying he was too young to go.
I will come back in the spring, if I am spared.
place_lore.nirncraft.ysgramors_tomb.rumo: Ysgramor's own tomb, out on the coast. The Companions come and stand there sometimes, all grim and quiet. We fishermen give it a wide berth.
place_lore.nirncraft.ysgramors_tomb.sk4_: Folio #7 (1186, -2033): Field inspection recorded for Ysgramors Tomb within Winterhold Hold. Boundary cairns, road approaches, and way-markers were checked against the steward's winter ledger before the frost locked the high trails.

place_lore.nirncraft.ysgramors_tomb.ward:
The door opens for the Circle and the Circle alone. Not for gold, not for a fine sword, not for a scholar's letter of introduction from Cyrodiil, however many seals it bears.
The last grave-robber who forced it was found on the beach below, still holding his crowbar, his eyes full of frost. He had no wound on him at all.
The Harbinger keeps his own house. Leave your offering on the step, say his name once, and go back the way you came.

For three seasons the wardens at place.nirncraft.zthenganaz have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by clanless mountain raiders, Daughters of Wroth frost-hags, and Lyrezi peak-vampires. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.
